children.translated_text: There was the son of <s>Devabhrāṭ</s>, and then the son of <s>Subhrāṭ</s>;
<s>Daśajyoti</s>, <s>Śatajyoti</s>, and <s>Sahasrajyoti</s> came into being.
From those thousand lineages came kings such as the line of <s>Kuru</s>,
and a succession of families beginning with <s>Māndhātṛ</s>, <s>Rāma</s>, and <s>Nahuṣa</s>.
<s>Dvaipāyana</s>, with his mother's permission, in the field of his brother
begot three sons, like fires, headed by <s>Dhṛtarāṣṭra</s>.
<s>Pāṇḍu</s>, the younger brother of <s>Dhṛtarāṣṭra</s>, obtained in the forest sons born on his wives,
sprung from <s>Dharma</s>, <s>Vāyu</s>, <s>Indra</s>, and the <s>Aśvins</s>.
When their father had died and they were in the residence of the sons of <s>Dhṛtarāṣṭra</s>,
the fire of <s>Duryodhana</s>'s anger blazed up, fanned by the wind of gambling.
Angered by sufferings such as exile in the forest, they, in the great battle,

children.text: jahuḥ parasparaṃ kṣatraṃ niḥśeṣā yena bhūrabhūt ||
children.translated_text: destroyed one another's warrior order, so that the earth was left without remainder of it.
Those great chariot-fighters, slain in the field of <s>Samantapañcaka</s>,
being famed, reached heaven, equal to <s>Māndhātṛ</s> and <s>Nahuṣa</s>.
The son of <s>Vicitravīrya</s>, deeply grieved when his sons had been slain,
lamented before <s>Saṃjaya</s>, remembering the valor of the <s>Pāṇḍavas</s>.
Struck by the unstable essence of worldly life, wavering like passing waves,
<s>Saṃjaya</s> consoled the king as he spoke forth.
Having heard this summary from the <s>Sūta</s>, <s>Śaunaka</s> again asked;
and when questioned about the story of the field of <s>Samantapañcaka</s>, he spoke.

children.text: purā kṣatrakṣayaṃ kṛtvā bhargaśiṣyaḥ sa bhārgavaḥ
children.translated_text: Long ago, after bringing about the destruction of the warrior class, that <s>Bhārgava</s>, disciple of <s>Bharga</s>,
made five lakes of blood at <s>Samantapañcaka</s>.

children.text: tataḥ prabhṛti puṇyaṃ tanmunīnāṃ vacasā kila
children.translated_text: From then onward that place became holy, by the word of the sages, it is said;
there the great war of the <s>Kuru</s> and <s>Pāṇḍava</s> kings took place,

children.text: akṣauhiṇyo daśāṣṭau ca tatraiva nidhanaṃ gatāḥ ||
children.translated_text: and eighteen <s>akṣauhiṇīs</s> met their destruction right there.

children.text: ratho gajo narāḥ pañca trayo 'śvāḥ pattirucyate
children.translated_text: One chariot, one elephant, five men, and three horses are called a <s>patti</s> (small troop unit);
then come <s>senāmukha</s>, <s>gulma</s>, <s>gaṇa</s>, <s>vāhinī</s>, <s>pṛtanā</s>, and <s>camū</s>.
In sequence, an <s>anīkinī</s> too is formed, each being three times the preceding one;
the wise say that ten times an <s>anīkinī</s> is an <s>akṣauhiṇī</s>.
The <s>Bhārata</s>, joined with the <s>Vedas</s> and <s>Vedāṅgas</s>, removes impurity;
it is said to have eighteen books and to be adorned with many narratives.
Its hundred inner books, beginning with the accounts of <s>Pauṣya</s> and <s>Pauloma</s>,
were expanded through the three worlds by the pupils of <s>Vyāsa</s> and by <s>Śuka</s>.
The son of <s>Saramā</s>, beaten by the brothers of the <s>Pārīkṣita</s> king,
by <s>Bhīmasena</s> and the others, went to his mother for refuge.
Then the wife of <s>Kaśyapa</s>, in anger, cursed the innocent king,

children.text: adṛṣṭaṃ prāpsyasi bhayaṃ na cirāditi abravīt ||
children.translated_text: saying, 'Before long you will meet an unseen danger.'

children.text: tacchrutvā cakito gatvā muniṃ vavre purohitam
children.translated_text: Hearing that, terrified, he went and chose a sage as his priest;
then <s>Janamejaya</s>, together with his brothers, remained at ease.
Meanwhile a great sage named <s>Dhaumya</s>, also called <s>Lohadanta</s>,
tested his pupils and made them free of doubt through knowledge.
First the illustrious one commanded his pupil, the <s>Pāñcālya</s> <s>Āruṇi</s>,

children.text: kṣetre jalaṃ badhāneti sa ca gatvā tathākarot ||
children.translated_text: 'Dam the water in the field'; and he went and did so.
Because he placed himself in the breach of the water-flow and protected
the field, his venerable teacher became a giver of boons to him.
Since, when summoned by the teacher, he rose up after opening the field,
that sage became famous from that as <s>Uddālaka</s>.
When he had fulfilled his task and gone, then another, <s>Upamanyu</s>,
was assigned by the teacher to guard the cows, living on alms.

children.text: taṃ guruḥ pīvaraṃ dṛṣṭvā prāha kenāsi vartase
children.translated_text: Seeing him stout, the teacher said, 'By what do you live?'
And <s>Upamanyu</s>, with folded hands, replied, 'By alms.'
'Without reporting it to me, you, restrained in your vow, are not entitled to eat food;
a second begging obstructs others, and that is not proper for you.'

children.text: gavyaṃ kṣīraṃ kutaḥ svaṃ te vatsaphenaṃ tadeva ca
children.translated_text: 'How is cow's milk your own? And the calves' foam likewise?'
Thus forbidden by <s>Dhaumya</s>, that wretched one gave up that food.
Then, from eating arka leaves, in time he became blind;
fallen into a well, when called from afar by the teacher, he spoke:
'From eating arka leaves I have become blind and fallen into a well, lord;
I am here.' Hearing this, <s>Dhaumya</s>, filled with compassion, said:

children.text: vatsa stutvāśvinau dvau tvaṃ divyaṃ cakṣuravāpnuhi ||
children.translated_text: 'Child, praise the two <s>Aśvins</s>, and obtain divine sight.'
Hearing this, he praised those two with the <s>Aśvina-sūkta</s> and, through their boon, obtained

children.text: apūpaṃ gurave taṃ ca sāmṛtaṃ sa nyavedayat ||
children.translated_text: a cake containing nectar; and he offered it to his teacher.
Then, by his teacher's boon, he became possessed of knowledge and divine sight;
<s>Upamanyu</s>, purified in the fire of testing, shone like gold from the <s>Jambū</s> river.
Then the third, named <s>Veda</s>, was yoked like an ox to the burden;
through the teacher's satisfaction he was made a vessel for the whole wealth of knowledge.
Thereafter, in time, in <s>Veda</s>'s hermitage too there became a pupil,
named <s>Uttaṅka</s>, as if he were the very abode of splendors through austerity.

children.text: kadācidatha taṃ dhṛtvā śiṣyaṃ gehe jitendriyam
children.translated_text: Once, keeping that self-controlled pupil at home,
<s>Veda</s> went away to officiate at a sacrifice, for service connected with the rites.

children.text: kriyāmahīnāṃ tvaṃ kartā nirdiṣṭo guruṇā gṛhe
children.translated_text: 'You have been appointed by the teacher in the house as performer of rites left undone;
come to the teacher's wife in her season, as the teacher would,' the women of the teacher's household said to him.
But when he disregarded that and stood unmoving like a piece of wood,
the teacher returned and made him a vessel of his own knowledge.
When he said, 'I will bring the teacher's fee,' the teacher said to him:
'Child, let whatever is desired by my wife be given.'

children.text: uttaṅkena tataḥ pṛṣṭā kiṃ dadāmīti tadvadhūḥ
children.translated_text: Then, when <s>Uttaṅka</s> asked her, 'What shall I give?', that wife
said, 'Of King <s>Saudāsa</s>, also known as <s>Pauṣya</s>...'
He has a wife named <s>Damayantī</s>; ask her for the jeweled earrings for me.

children.text: mahyaṃ dehīti tacchrutvā pratiśrutya jagāma saḥ ||
children.translated_text: Hearing this, he promised and went away.
As he went along the road, he then saw a man mounted on a bull.
From him he heard, "Eat the dung of this bull."
At his words he ate it and went on to <s>Pauṣya</s>'s dwelling.

children.text: tatrāntaḥpuram āsādya kṣatriyāṃ na dadarśa saḥ ||
children.translated_text: There, after reaching the inner apartments, he did not see the royal lady.

children.text: tām adṛṣṭvā nṛpaṃ prāha tvadbhāryā kiṃ na dṛśyate
children.translated_text: Not seeing her, he said to the king, "Why is your wife not visible?"
Hearing that, <s>Pauṣya</s>, who was pleased and loved guests, said:

children.text: tvaṃ na paśyasi me jāyāmucchiṣṭastāṃ pativratām ||
children.translated_text: "You do not see my wife, that faithful wife of mine, because you are ritually impure from remnants."
Hearing this, <s>Uttaṅka</s> remembered the truth about his eating the cow-dung.
He said to him, "After eating it I did not rinse; I am ritually impure."
Then, sitting down and rinsing according to rule, he saw her.
She was a royal woman, embodied radiance, like <s>Lakṣmī</s>, devoted to her husband.
After he had told his own story and asked her, she gave him
those two divine earrings, adorned with a circle of light.
"<s>Takṣaka</s> constantly seeks these fine earrings, brahmin.
You must go carefully," she said to <s>Uttaṅka</s>.
Having received the beautiful jeweled earrings given by her,

children.text: pauṣyeṇāmantritaḥ śrāddhe dṛṣṭvānnaṃ taṃ śaśāpa saḥ ||
children.translated_text: he was invited by <s>Pauṣya</s> to a śrāddha; seeing the food, he cursed him.
"<s>Pauṣya</s>, this impure food has been offered to me by you.
You will become blind." When this had been said, <s>Pauṣya</s> replied to him:
"You will be cut off from your lineage, because you condemn food that is not spoiled."
Having said this and inspected that food, <s>Pauṣya</s> spoke to him again:
"Holy sir, the fault is not mine. It was brought with loosened hair;
the food, containing hair, is as good as impure. Therefore forgive me."
Hearing this, <s>Uttaṅka</s> said, "After becoming blind, you will regain sight.

children.text: vāraya pratiśāpaṃ me tvamapi kṣmābhṛtāṃ vara ||
children.translated_text: You too, best of kings, must avert my counter-curse."
<s>Pauṣya</s> said, "Brahmins have sharp speech and unsteady minds,
but kṣatriyas are otherwise; therefore I am not able to destroy a curse."
Then <s>Uttaṅka</s> said to <s>Pauṣya</s>, "Let what you said not harm me.
The curse you gave for condemning pure food is not really valid."
Having spoken thus, he quickly set out. While he was going on the road,
as he touched water, with his garments placed on the bank and covered,
<s>Takṣaka</s>, in the form of a mendicant, quickly stole the earrings.
Then he entered <s>Pātāla</s>, intent on searching for <s>Takṣaka</s>.
After praising the nāgas, he saw before him a marvel in the serpent abode:
two women there weaving a cloth with white and black threads,
and a wheel with twelve spokes, turned by six boys.

children.text: tataḥ puraṃdaraṃ stutvā hayārūḍhaṃ dadarśa tam
children.translated_text: Then, after praising <s>Puraṃdara</s>, he saw him mounted on a horse.
At his command he blew into the opening at that horse's rear.
As it was being blown, fire with smoke came out through the mouths of the channels
and made the serpent dwelling dark with smoke.
Then the frightened <s>Takṣaka</s> gave him those jeweled earrings.

children.text: te prāpya hṛṣṭastenaiva vājinā prayayau gurum ||
children.translated_text: Having obtained them, delighted, he went to his guru on that very horse.

children.text: dattvā te gurubhāryāyai guruṃ papraccha kautukāt
children.translated_text: After giving them to his guru's wife, out of curiosity he asked his guru

children.text: paṭaṃ cakraṃ vayasyaṃ ca naraṃ ca vṛṣavāhanam ||
children.translated_text: about the cloth, the wheel, the companion, and the man mounted on the bull.
Asked, the teacher said, "Son, the two women weaving

children.text: te hi dhātā vidhātā ca sāsāśrivalayākulam ||
children.translated_text: are <s>Dhātṛ</s> and <s>Vidhātṛ</s>; that cloth is crowded with dark and bright rings.

children.text: tatkālacakramṛtavaḥ kumārāḥ ṣaṭ ca te sthitāḥ
children.translated_text: That is the wheel of time, and the six boys standing there are the seasons.
The one mounted on the horse is <s>Parjanya</s>, and that horse is fire.
The bull is the elephant of the gods, and <s>Puraṃdara</s> is mounted on it.
Its dung is nectar; it was eaten by you, a fortunate man."

children.text: ityuttaṅkaḥ samākarṇya guroḥ prāpya varaṃ varam
children.translated_text: Hearing this from his guru and receiving an excellent boon, <s>Uttaṅka</s>
went, because of his hostility toward <s>Takṣaka</s>, to King <s>Janamejaya</s>.
Reaching <s>Hastināpura</s> and seeing <s>Janamejaya</s>,

children.text: provāca kṣatriyā rājannirvairā na padaṃ śriyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: he said, "O king, kṣatriyas without enmity do not attain the seat of royal fortune.
Your father <s>Parīkṣit</s> was burned by wicked <s>Takṣaka</s>.
It is fitting for you to make an effort to injure him."
Hearing these words of <s>Uttaṅka</s>, <s>Janamejaya</s> became
like fire enclosed by wind, with the smoke-like movements of his frowning brows.
Hearing this speech of the sūta, <s>Śaunaka</s>, born in the line of <s>Bhṛgu</s>,

children.text: papraccha svakulaṃ pūrvaṃ sa ca pṛṣṭo 'bhyabhāṣata ||
children.translated_text: asked first about his own family, and, being asked, he spoke.
<s>Pulomā</s> was the beloved wife of the eminent sage <s>Bhṛgu</s>;
the doe-eyed females of the ascetic grove, conquered by her glance, did not shine.

children.text: patyau snānāya niryāte pulomā nāma rākṣasaḥ
children.translated_text: When her husband had gone out to bathe, a rākṣasa named <s>Pulomā</s>
came up and saw <s>Pulomā</s> alone, adorned with beauty.

children.text: pṛṣṭena vahninā khyātā bhṛgorbhāryeti sa svayam
children.translated_text: When fire, questioned by him, declared, "She is <s>Bhṛgu</s>'s wife,"
that passion-stricken rākṣasa himself carried her off, heavy with pregnancy.
From her womb her son fell, blazing from anger like the fire at the end of time,
and by his brilliance the demon's chest became ashes in an instant.
From her tear-drop a river arose in the hermitage,
famous as <s>Vadhūsarā</s>, destroyer of the sins of the world.

children.text: tato bhṛguḥ samabhyetya jñātvā dṛṣṭyā ca tatpunaḥ
children.translated_text: Then <s>Bhṛgu</s> came, and, knowing that matter again by his insight,
he of fiery splendor quickly cursed fire, the whisperer in the ear.
Having incurred the state of eating everything through the great sage's curse, fire

children.text: adarśanaṃ gataḥ prāpa pratiṣṭhāṃ brahmaṇo varāt ||
children.translated_text: disappeared, and then, by <s>Brahmā</s>'s boon, regained his established place.
And because he had fallen, he came to have the name <s>Cyavana</s>; then by that maiden he had
a son named <s>Pramati</s>, and <s>Ruru</s> was his son.
Long ago, in the hermitage of <s>Sthalakeśa</s>, <s>Ruru</s> had as his wife <s>Pramadvarā</s>;
when his beloved had been bitten by a wicked serpent, he brought her back to life with half of his own lifespan.
His son was <s>Śunaka</s>; that one's son was <s>Śaunaka</s>, namely you.
After joyfully reviving that wife, <s>Pramadvarā</s>, <s>Ruru</s>
became, it is said, constantly bound to a single vow: the destruction of snakes.
Once a <s>Ḍuṇḍubha</s>, struck by him as he held a staff in his hand,
when questioned, spoke, curling his crooked body into coils:
"I was formerly a Brahmin named <s>Sahasrapāt</s>; through delusion, by me
a frightened Brahmin named <s>Khagama</s> was struck with a hooded snake.
Because of his curse I have come, for a long time, to this state of being a <s>Ḍuṇḍubha</s>;
and by that very man the ending of the curse was appointed at the sight of <s>Ruru</s>.

children.text: dīrghavairaṃ dvijo bhūtvā mā kṛthā bhujagānprati
children.translated_text: Having become a Brahmin, do not keep up a long enmity toward serpents.

children.text: kṣatriyasya vrataṃ dhairyaṃ dvijānāṃ bhūṣaṇaṃ kṛpā ||
children.translated_text: Steadfast courage is the vow of a kṣatriya; compassion is the ornament of Brahmins.

children.text: tathā hi vahninā dagdhāḥ sarpasatre bhujaṃgamāḥ
children.translated_text: Thus, when serpents were being burned by fire in the snake sacrifice,
by the victorious king descended from <s>Parīkṣit</s>, in anger over his father's killing,
they were then saved, out of compassion, by the Brahmin <s>Āstīka</s> himself."
Hearing this, the sages again asked <s>Sūta</s> about the story of <s>Āstīka</s>;
he said that a great Brahmin was born in the family known as the <s>Yāyāvaras</s>.
Known as <s>Jaratkāru</s>, a celibate student wandering in former days,
he saw his forefathers hanging from a clump of vīraṇa grass.
They were face downward over a great pit, their support being gnawed by a mouse;
asked about their lineage and names, they spoke to him:
"The thread of our meritorious descendants has been cut off by your celibacy.
We are your own fathers, attacked untimely by the mouse.
Then, because of their words, he again undertook marriage,

children.text: na mannāmnīṃ vinā bhāryāṃ bhajiṣyāmīti sarvadā ||
children.translated_text: always saying, "I shall not take a wife unless she has my own name."
Then in time, without asking for her, the self-controlled man obtained, as assigned by fate,
the sister of <s>Vāsuki</s> as his wife, one having the very same name.
From him she obtained a son named from the word "asti," because "there is a fetus" had been said:
<s>Āstīka</s>, the one who would avert the maternal curse from all the Nāgas.
Asked again by <s>Śaunaka</s> about the cause of the mother's curse
upon the Nāgas, <s>Sūta</s>, skilled in ancient tales, spoke:
By the boon of their husband <s>Kaśyapa</s>, O sage, the daughters of <s>Dakṣa</s>,
<s>Kadrū</s> and <s>Vinatā</s>, long ago bore wombs suited to birds and serpents.
When the sons of <s>Kadrū</s>, the snakes, first came forth from their eggs,
<s>Vinatā</s>, out of jealousy, broke open one of her two eggs.
Because the egg was broken before it was complete, thighless <s>Aruṇa</s> was born;

children.text: mātaraṃ kupito dāsyaṃ yāsyasīti śaśāpa saḥ ||
children.translated_text: angry, he cursed his mother, saying, "You shall go into slavery."
Then, in time, those two sisters saw a divine horse,
whose birthplace was the Ocean of Milk churned by <s>Mandara</s>.
When gods and demons, striving to carry off the amrita,
had formerly churned it with the mountain, the Ocean of Milk gave the adornment of <s>Caṇḍīśa</s>,

children.text: śaśāṅkaṃ kaustubhaṃ lakṣmīṃ sudhāṃ dhanvantariṃ tathā
children.translated_text: the moon, the <s>Kaustubha</s>, <s>Lakṣmī</s>, the nectar, <s>Dhanvantari</s>,
the elixir, and the king of horses to the gods.
Then <s>Viṣṇu</s> himself, in a woman's form, deceived the great Asuras

children.text: sudhāṃ jahāra sahasā taddattāṃ ca papuḥ surāḥ ||
children.translated_text: and suddenly carried off the nectar; the gods drank it when it was given to them.
Then, as <s>Rāhu</s>, in the form of one of the gods, was swallowing the elixir,
<s>Hari</s> cut off with his discus the head whose throat the amrita had reached.
Because he had been pointed out by the moon and the sun, from the killing of him that head

children.text: tapo ghorataraṃ cakre yena tāvatti parvasu ||
children.translated_text: performed very terrible austerity, by which it devours those two at the lunar junctures.

children.text: amṛtotthaṃ bhaginyau taṃ dṛṣṭvāśvaṃ dhavalaṃ pathi
children.translated_text: Seeing that white horse, born from the amrita, on the road, the two sisters
spoke freely to one another: "What color is he?"
<s>Vinatā</s> said, "White," while <s>Kadrū</s> said, "With a black tail."

children.text: paṇaṃ dāsyāya cakrāte vivādeneti te tataḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus, in their dispute, they made a wager whose stake was slavery.
Then <s>Kadrū</s>, her mind impure, said to her sons, the Nāgas:
"Sons, the horse of the gods is white; make his tail black."
Hearing this, the serpents did not do it, afraid of sin.
"In the spreading snake sacrifice, fire shall be your end."
In anger at their refusal, <s>Kadrū</s> thus cursed her sons.
Then, when the horse had been made black by the remaining serpents,
<s>Vinatā</s>, defeated by their childish trickery, went into slavery.
Then from the other egg arose <s>Garuḍa</s>, with a golden brilliance.
His boundless power was made manifest by the trembling mass of his own radiance;

children.text: stūyamānaḥ suraiḥ sarvaiḥ sa yayau māturantikam ||
children.translated_text: praised by all the gods, he went to his mother's side.
Bearing the splendor of a fire growing with abundant oblations of ghee,
<s>Tārkṣya</s> came upon his mother <s>Vinatā</s>, who was carrying <s>Kadrū</s> on her shoulder, defeated in the deceitful wager,

children.text: mātaraṃ vinatāṃ tārkṣyaḥ prāpya śuśrāva tatkathām
children.translated_text: and he heard that story.
At his mother's word, though hostile to serpents, he carried the serpents.
Having taken them near the chariot of the sun, where they fainted from intense heat,
<s>Kadrū</s>, seeing her own sons being carried by <s>Suparṇa</s>
and scorched by the rays of the sun, praised the lord of the winds.
Their torment from the heat was destroyed by the rain from the mass of clouds produced by him;
roaring, the serpents wandered over the earth, borne by <s>Tārkṣya</s>.
Then, hearing from the serpents that slavery would last until the amrita was brought,
<s>Tārkṣya</s>, undertaking that effort at once, asked his mother:
"Mother, for release from slavery, I am going straight to the amrita."
Command me quickly to gather the gods as food for myself.
She said: On the shore of the ocean there is a large lineage
of Niṣādas; through them you may obtain abundant satisfaction.
But among the Niṣādas there is a Brahmin there, and he must be protected by you.
When he clings in your throat, as if he were a heated fishhook,
as though scattering pain through your vital parts, you should recognize him as the Brahmin.
Though he lives among fishermen, he has not fallen from his own <s>dharma</s>.

children.text: aluptasaṃdhyaḥ satataṃ na hi jātyā tiraskṛtaḥ ||
children.translated_text: He never neglects the twilight rites, for he has not been cast down by birth.

children.text: svasti te 'stu vraja kṣipramiti māturgirā khagaḥ
children.translated_text: May it be well with you; go quickly. At these words of his mother, the bird
set out, agitating the ocean with the wind from the beating of his wings.
Having eaten the vast clan of servants dwelling on the ocean shore,
and having released from his throat the twice-born man who was caught there like a fishhook,
he went on and reached his father <s>Kaśyapa</s>, a treasure-house of splendors.
After bowing, he told him of his effort to bring away the nectar,

children.text: bhojanaṃ diśa me tāta na tṛpto 'smītyathābhyadhāt ||
children.translated_text: and then said: Father, give me food; I am not satisfied.
<s>Kaśyapa</s> said to him: Son, in this lake there are two mighty beings,
an elephant and a tortoise, standing there across many yojanas.
Long ago, through a quarrel that arose from the division of wealth, two merchants,
<s>Supratīka</s> and <s>Vibhāvasu</s>, by mutual curses came to this condition.
Eat those two. Hearing this, <s>Tārkṣya</s>, intent on stirring up commotion,
seized them with his two feet and went off with tremendous speed.
Coming to a forest of divine trees, he then reached a rohaṇa tree,
and, weary, sat down upon a golden branch.
The branch, a hundred yojanas wide, broke as soon as it was touched by his foot,

children.text: abhajyata munivyāptā cañcvādāya sa tāṃ yayau ||
children.translated_text: and it was crowded with sages; taking it in his beak, he flew away.
The lord of birds, afraid, held it because it was covered
with hanging <s>Vālakhilyas</s>, emaciated by austerity and facing downward.
He approached <s>Kaśyapa</s>, bearing the branch, the elephant, and the tortoise,
and, with mind bewildered, was distressed, asking: What should I do?
Then, entreated by <s>Kaśyapa</s> himself out of love for his son,
all the <s>Vālakhilyas</s>, devoted to austerity, left the branch and went away.
At his father's word, he dropped the branch on the Himālaya and, having eaten the meat,
went to the abode of <s>Śakra</s>, intent on carrying off the nectar.

children.text: tapasā vālakhilyānāṃ jāto jetā sa vajriṇaḥ
children.translated_text: By the austerity of the <s>Vālakhilyas</s> he had been born as the conqueror of the thunderbolt-bearer,
the Indra of all birds, the vehicle of <s>Hari</s>, and one favored with a boon.
Long ago, at <s>Kaśyapa</s>'s sacrifice, gods, siddhas, seers, and cāraṇas
unceasingly and unhindered carried the materials for the rite.
The slayer of <s>Vṛtra</s> came there himself, carrying a load of firewood
as large as a mountain, and saw the <s>Vālakhilyas</s>.
Seeing them, no taller than the tip of a thumb and emaciated by austerity,
their bodies oppressed by a burden no more than a strip of palāśa wood,
sinking like mountains in the water-filled ocean,

children.text: jahāsālpabalānindraḥ ko vā lakṣmyā na mādyati ||
children.translated_text: <s>Indra</s> laughed at their slight strength; who is not intoxicated by fortune?
Angered by his laughter, they performed a terrible sacrifice, praying:
May there be a mighty son of <s>Kaśyapa</s>, a conqueror of <s>Indra</s>.
Born from the power of that rite, he went forth to conquer the lord of the gods,
like a moving <s>Sumeru</s> surrounded by a hundred suns.
Entering heaven, he defeated the gods and was crowned with victory;
the hero conquered <s>Śakra</s> in battle and bewildered the immortals in battle.
After striking down <s>Viśvakarman</s> in the house of the guardians of the soma,
with a fearsome mass of dust raised by the beating of his wings,
he drove away the two serpent guards, then split open the cage,
and, proud in his strength, carried off the nectar protected by a whirling great wheel.
Without drinking it, he swiftly took up the jar of nectar
and set out; from afar the lord <s>Viṣṇu</s>, husband of <s>Kamalā</s>, saw him.
O lord of birds, I am pleased by this freedom from greed of yours;
choose a boon, said the blessed <s>Hari</s> to him.
May I become immortal without this nectar, and may I always stand above you:

children.text: varaṃ gṛhāṇa matto'pi tamityāha sa pakṣiṇam ||
children.translated_text: and the bird said to him: Accept a boon from me as well.
Hearing that, the blessed lord said: All this shall indeed come to pass.

children.text: vāhanaṃ me bhavānbhūyāttārkṣyaḥ prāha tathāstu me ||
children.translated_text: May you become my vehicle. <s>Tārkṣya</s> replied: So be it for me.
Having obtained the state of being <s>Viṣṇu</s>'s vehicle and a place above his banner,
as he went onward he was struck by the thunderbolt when the wielder of the thunderbolt came upon him.
Though struck by it, he felt no pain, and with a laugh he himself let fall

children.text: svayaṃ tatyāja māno 'stu vajrasyeti vihasya saḥ ||
children.translated_text: one wing a hundred yojanas long, saying: Let there be honor for the thunderbolt.

children.text: nirjitena surendreṇa sakhyaṃ kṛtvā jagāda tam
children.translated_text: Making friendship with the conquered lord of the gods, he said to him:
The nectar that I have set down for the serpents must be taken away by you.

children.text: uktveti gatvā bhujagāndattvā tebhyaḥ sudhāṃ khagaḥ
children.translated_text: Having said this, the bird went to the serpents, gave them the nectar,
and said: Drink this according to rule, freed from servitude.

children.text: sudhāṃ kuśeṣu saṃsthāpya snātuṃ yāteṣu bhogiṣu
children.translated_text: When the serpents had placed the nectar on kuśa grass and gone to bathe,
<s>Indra</s>, who had been instructed beforehand by <s>Tārkṣya</s>, quickly carried it away.
Seeing that they had been deceived and that the seat of kuśa grass was smeared with nectar,
the serpents licked it with the tips of their long tongues, and thereby obtained split tongues.
From then on, darbha grass attained purity for offerings to gods and ancestors,
and by <s>Śakra</s>'s word the serpents became food for <s>Tārkṣya</s>.
Thus I have told the cause of the maternal curse
upon <s>Śeṣa</s>, <s>Vāsuki</s>, <s>Karkoṭa</s>, <s>Takṣaka</s>, <s>Aila</s>, and the other serpents.
Then, by fierce austerity, having obtained boons from the Grandfather,
at his word <s>Śeṣa</s> bore the earth, together with its mountains and forests.
Then the serpents, headed by <s>Vāsuki</s>, abandoned through their mother's curse,
assembled and deliberated on a countermeasure to the snake sacrifice.
Some said, 'At that sacrifice all of us, gathered together,
will act by poisonous firebrands, or by the four kinds of expedients.'
Then <s>Elapattra</s>, best of the wise, said to <s>Vāsuki</s>:
'This curse, born from our mother's curse, is inevitable.
As a child lying in my mother's lap, I heard, concerning that curse,

children.text: kadrūraho na tīkṣṇeti devānāṃ bruvatāṃ giraḥ ||
children.translated_text: the words of the gods, who were saying, "Ah, <s>Kadrū</s> is not too harsh."
When the curious gods asked the four-faced one about the pacification of the curse,
he said, "The negligent biting serpents devoted to evil
will go to destruction in the snake sacrifice, those fierce bearers of poison;
but the son of a <s>Yāyāvara</s> will release the remaining ones who stand in <s>dharma</s> (righteous order).
He will be born again as the son of the serpents' own sister,
the famous <s>Astīka</s>, son of <s>Jaratkāru</s> by <s>Jaratkāru</s>."
I heard this long ago when I was a child, lord of serpents.'
Hearing this from <s>Elapattra</s>, <s>Vāsuki</s> cast off his fear.
Then after some time <s>Parīkṣit</s>, born in the line of <s>Pāṇḍu</s>,
the lord of the earth, wandered in the forest while following deer.
Seeing before him the sage <s>Samīka</s>, who was under a vow of silence, he said:
'Did you see on the path a deer marked by my arrow?'

children.text: iti pṛṣṭo yadā kiṃcinnovāca sa munistadā
children.translated_text: When the sage, though questioned in this way, said nothing at all,

children.text: śavaṃ bhujagamādhāya skandhe tasya yayau nṛpaḥ ||
children.translated_text: the king placed a dead snake on his shoulder and went away.
Then his son <s>Śṛṅgī</s>, very wrathful, saw his father

children.text: atha tattanayaḥ śṛṅgī mahākopī vilokya tam ||
children.translated_text: defiled by the outbreak of poison from the dead snake and covered with stinging insects.
With his hands and lips trembling, he cursed the doer of that deed:
'Within seven days the fire of <s>Takṣaka</s>, flashing with poison, will burn him.'
Hearing that, <s>Samīka</s>, ocean of compassion, sent a messenger
to the king, saying, 'This curse must be guarded against.'
Terrified by the sage's curse, <s>Parīkṣit</s>, by the counsel of his ministers,
arranged protection for himself with multitudes of spells, guards, and medicines.
When the seventh day had arrived, <s>Takṣaka</s>, impelled by fate,
set out for <s>Hastināpura</s> to strike down the king of the earth.

children.text: sa dadarśa puro vipraṃ kaśyapaṃ viṣamantriṇam
children.translated_text: On the way he saw the Brahmin <s>Kaśyapa</s>, skilled in poison-spells,
a poor man seeking wealth, who had come to protect <s>Parīkṣit</s>.
After hearing all his intention, the serpent said:

children.text: ahaṃ sa takṣako nāma mā jetuṃ kaḥ pragalbhate ||
children.translated_text: 'I am that one named <s>Takṣaka</s>; who is bold enough to conquer me?

children.text: taṃ rakṣasi narendraṃ cenmayā dagdhaṃ mahādrumam
children.translated_text: If you can protect that king, then revive this great tree
burned by me; I will know thereby your mastery of poison-spells.'
Having spoken thus, he instantly burned a banyan tree with the force of his poison.

children.text: saśākhapuṣpapatraṃ ca cakre mantreṇa taṃ dvijaḥ ||
children.translated_text: By his spell the Brahmin made it again complete with branches, flowers, and leaves.
Then <s>Takṣaka</s> offered wealth to him in return, saying, 'Turn back,'

children.text: prasādya pradadau bhūri prāpya vipraśca tadyayau ||
children.translated_text: and, after winning him over, gave much; the Brahmin received it and went away.

children.text: kāladaṣṭaṃ nṛpaṃ jñātvā yāte divyadṛśi dvije
children.translated_text: When the far-seeing Brahmin had gone, knowing the king to be bitten by Time,
<s>Takṣaka</s> sent serpents in the guise of ascetics to the king.

children.text: taṃ sametya mahīpālaṃ channāḥ svastīti vādinaḥ
children.translated_text: Those disguised ones approached the ruler, saying 'Blessings,'

children.text: phalāni ca dadustasmai puṣpāṇi ca kuśaiḥ saha ||
children.translated_text: and gave him fruits and flowers together with <s>kuśa</s> grass.
Seeing a very small insect come out from within one of those fruits,
the king said to the sages, reasonably, 'I honor the curse.
Let this worm named <s>Takṣaka</s> bite me for a moment, though falsely.'
While he was speaking so, <s>Takṣaka</s> wound himself around him before the ministers.
Then, with a ring of blazing flames of poison,
the lord of serpents reduced the king and his palace to ashes and went through the sky.
When that king had been burned, his son <s>Janamejaya</s>,
chosen for the kingdom by the best of ministers, took <s>Vapuṣṭamā</s> as his wife.
As that king enjoyed himself with that slender lady in a splendid garden,
after some time he heard from the circle of ministers what had happened to his father.
Scorched by the fire of anger, he undertook a countermeasure
against all the serpents in a snake sacrifice, entering it together with Brahmins.
In that sacrifice, where the sky was licked by rows of flames trembling and flaring,
serpents like elephants fell into the fire of the snake sacrifice.
As the serpents fell, dark with the smoke of their poison-fire
and gleaming for a moment with sparks, they seemed like masses of clouds in turmoil.
While the serpents were being burned in the king's snake sacrifice,

children.text: sureśaṃ śaraṇaṃ yāte mantrakṛṣṭe ca takṣake ||
children.translated_text: and while <s>Takṣaka</s>, drawn by the mantra, went to <s>Indra</s> for refuge,
the king said, 'Drag down <s>Takṣaka</s> together with <s>Indra</s>

children.text: iti bruvāṇe bhūpāle khaṃ prāpte ca śatakratau ||
children.translated_text: and cast him into the fire,' and <s>Śatakratu</s> had reached the sky.
At that moment, frightened, trembling, and with folded hands,

children.text: astīkaṃ vāsukiḥ prāha svasrīyaṃ rakṣa māmiti
children.translated_text: <s>Vāsuki</s> said to his sister's son <s>Astīka</s>, 'Protect me.'
Promising, 'So be it,' he went to the king <s>Janamejaya</s>'s
sacrificial ground and, announced by the doorkeepers, entered.

children.text: tato mantrabalāt traste takṣake vajriṇā saha
children.translated_text: Then, when <s>Takṣaka</s>, together with the wielder of the thunderbolt, was terrified by the power of the mantra,
and for a moment hung suspended at <s>Astīka</s>'s word, 'Stay!',
broad streams of fat, thick with the grease of the masses of burned serpents,
flowed in great volume toward the lord of rivers, the ocean.

children.text: astīko 'yaṃ nṛpaṃ prāpya svastipūrvāṃ stutiṃ vyadhāt
children.translated_text: This <s>Astīka</s>, having approached the king, made a praise beginning with a blessing.
Thus, when the auspicious praise had been uttered, that king was pleased with him,

children.text: dadau varaṃ tadvarācca sa rarakṣa phaṇīśvarān ||
children.translated_text: and granted a boon; and through that boon he protected the lords of serpents.
Then, by the words of <s>Astīka</s>, when the king's snake-sacrifice
had ceased, there was rejoicing among all the remaining <s>nāgas</s>.
After hearing the story of <s>Astīka</s>, the pure tale of the <s>Bhārata</s>,
<s>Romaharṣaṇi</s>, then questioned by <s>Śaunaka</s>, spoke.
The venerable son of <s>Satyavatī</s>, questioned by the <s>Pārīkṣita</s> king,
the lord, at the snake-sacrifice, urged <s>Vaiśampāyana</s> on.
That pupil, addressed by him, recited the <s>Mahābhārata</s>
during the intervals of the sacrificial session, after bowing to the imperishable Lord.
It is meritorious, purifying, life-giving, an <s>itihāsa</s> (ancient history), a divine tree,
with <s>dharma</s> as its root, <s>śruti</s> as its trunk, <s>smṛti</s> as its flower, and a great fruit.
Among the <s>Cedis</s> there was a king <s>Vasu</s>, a universal sovereign and friend of <s>Hari</s>;
by him a sacrifice for the worship of <s>Indra</s> was established on earth.
When his queen <s>Girikā</s> was in her fertile season, that ruler of men,
roaming in the hunt, remembered that long-eyed woman alone.
He emitted his seed, and quickly enclosed it in a leaf from a tree;
then, tying it to the throat of a hawk, he sent it to his beloved.
Pulled from the hawk by another bird, it fell into the waters of the <s>Yamunā</s>;
an apsaras fallen by a curse, having obtained the state of a fish, swallowed it.

children.text: babhūva garbhiṇī sātha kṛṣṭā kālena dhīvaraiḥ
children.translated_text: Then she became pregnant; in time she was caught by fishermen.

children.text: suravāravadhūḥ sā hi śāpān mātsyīṃ tanuṃ śritā
children.translated_text: For that heavenly courtesan had assumed a fish's body because of a curse;
named <s>Adrikā</s>, when she was cut open, she went to the abode of the gods.
When twins were born from her, <s>Vasu</s> took the boy,
who, called <s>Matsya</s>, as king established the <s>Matsya</s> country.
As his portion, the king gave the girl, <s>Gandhakālī</s>, to a fisherman,
by whose glance the quarters became like groves of blooming blue lotuses.
<s>Parāśara</s>, wishing to cross over, saw on the bank of the <s>Yamunā</s>
that fisherman's daughter, slowly reaching fresh youth.
Then, by the greatness of the future event, he was filled with desire; with a word

children.text: vidhāya dikṣu nīhāraṃ bheje tāṃ hariṇekṣaṇām ||
children.translated_text: he made mist in the directions and enjoyed that doe-eyed woman.
By the sage's boon, <s>Gandhakālī</s> did not lose her maidenhood,
and she became lotus-scented, pleasing his mind.
United with her in the boat, with her eyes like fresh lotuses,
he, bright as the sun, begot a son, a sun of knowledge.
This is the venerable <s>Vyāsa</s>, the dark son of <s>Satyavatī</s>,

children.text: yo jāta eva sarvāṅgavedavit prayayau vanam ||
children.translated_text: who, as soon as he was born, knowing the <s>Vedas</s> with all their limbs, went to the forest.

children.text: jātaḥ sa yamunātīre dvaipāyana iti smṛtaḥ
children.translated_text: Born on the bank of the <s>Yamunā</s>, he is remembered as <s>Dvaipāyana</s>;
and, after dividing all the <s>Vedas</s>, the mighty one attained the name <s>Vyāsa</s>.
As if indicating by his rays the science that teaches the three aims of life,
as he went he said to his mother, 'I should be remembered in times of danger.'

children.text: atha rāmahate kṣatre sambhūte viprataḥ punaḥ
children.translated_text: Then, when the warrior class had been slain by <s>Rāma</s> and had arisen again from brahmins,
the daityas, formerly crushed by the foe of <s>Pura</s>, descended to earth in partial forms.
The earth, oppressed by their burden, went to <s>Brahmā</s> for refuge,

children.text: trāṇaṃ nārāyaṇaṃ prāpa sendramaṃśena gāṃ gatam ||
children.translated_text: and obtained <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> as protector, who, along with <s>Indra</s>, had gone to earth in a partial form.
The gods, together with siddhas and gandharvas, intent on crushing the enemies of the gods,
descended after <s>Viṣṇu</s> himself in the lineages of many royal sages.
The fourteenfold creation had formerly been created by <s>Svayaṃbhū</s>;
in that creation, among human beings, gods and dānavas were born.
The great asuras, <s>Vipracitti</s>, <s>Hiraṇyākṣa</s>, <s>Prahlāda</s>, and others,
became, among men, <s>Jarāsaṃdha</s>, the <s>Caidya</s>, <s>Śalya</s>, and others.
A portion of the lord of the gandharvas became King <s>Dhṛtarāṣṭra</s>, ruler of men;
through the curse of <s>Aṇīmāṇḍavya</s>, <s>Dharma</s> became <s>Vidura</s>.
Born in a vessel, <s>Droṇa</s>, of the sage <s>Bharadvāja</s>, was a portion of <s>Bṛhaspati</s>;
<s>Droṇa</s> became very wise, the teacher of all bowmen,
and <s>Aśvatthāman</s> was a portion of <s>Rudra</s>; <s>Śāntanava</s> was a <s>Vasu</s>.
<s>Kṛpācārya</s> too was of <s>Rudra</s>; <s>Śakuni</s> was the <s>Dvāpara</s> age.
<s>Sātyaki</s> was a portion of the <s>Maruts</s>; so too were <s>Hārdikya</s> and <s>Drupada</s>.
<s>Suyodhana</s>, a portion of <s>Kali</s>, brought about the destruction of all kings;
the sons of <s>Pāṇḍu</s> were portions of <s>Dharma</s>, <s>Anila</s>, <s>Indra</s>, and the two <s>Aśvins</s>.
<s>Dhṛṣṭadyumna</s> was a portion of fire, and <s>Karṇa</s> a portion of the fierce-rayed sun;
the venerable <s>Vāsudeva</s>, crusher of enemies, was a portion of <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>.
After hearing of the descent of these portions, <s>Janamejaya</s> asked
about the vast lineage of the <s>Kurus</s>; and, when questioned, the sage spoke.
There was a protector of the earth, <s>Duḥṣyanta</s>, an ornament of splendor,
by whose shining fame, as though washed bright, dark women fell into doubt about themselves.
The wives of his enemies, robbed by his arrows of the painted leaf-marks on their cheeks,
he made lose, even by the bending of his brow, the charm of their own arched brows.
Once, that bowman entered the forest from delight in hunting,
threatening with arrows the deer whose eyes were like women's eyes.
After killing troops of lions, he came out from the midst of his army
and slowly reached the hermitage of <s>Kaṇva</s>, where the creepers trembled in a gentle wind.
There he saw the river <s>Mālinī</s>, garlanded with swans,
charming like a woman, with broad sandbanks for hips.
In that hermitage, where the blossoming trees were noisy with the sounds of restless swarms of bees,
he saw a maiden with long eyes.
It was as if clever <s>Manobhū</s>, burned by the fire of the eye,
had fashioned a woman's body in order to deceive the three-eyed god.
She had performed the proper hospitality and, delighted, spoke words of welcome.
Agitated by wonder and by love, he quickly asked:

children.text: kva sthito bhagavānkaṇvo muniḥ subhrūr mahāyaśāḥ
children.translated_text: Where is the blessed sage <s>Kaṇva</s>, O fair-browed one, the greatly renowned muni?
I have come to bow to him, worthy of worship by the dwellers in <s>Nandana</s>.
Hearing this from the lord of the earth, the hermit girl spoke,
her glance turned sideways, with lotuses set at her ears:

children.text: phalāni svayamādātuṃ sa niryātaḥ pitā mama
children.translated_text: My father has gone out himself to gather fruits.
Rest here for a little while; he will return before long.
Hearing that, the king said: A great wonder is connected with you.
Tell me this: how are you the daughter of that celibate ascetic?
Asked thus, the maiden said: Listen, if you are curious,

children.text: mama janmakathā pūrvaṃ kathitā muninā yathā ||
children.translated_text: to the former story of my birth, just as it was told by the sage.
Once, when the blessed sage <s>Kauśika</s> was practicing austerities,
an excellent apsaras was sent by the king of the gods to obstruct him.
She, fair-eyed and named <s>Menakā</s>, came to that forest,
and the young woman moved about gently, like a creeper struck by the wind.
Then the wind, impelled by the lord of <s>Śacī</s>, carried away her splendid garment,
as she possessed a lovely beauty like the tender shoots of young plantains.
Seeing her overcome by shame, the sage became desirous;
for, truly, the mind-born god is hard to restrain even for the great.
Then, courted by him herself as a lover, the full-breasted woman
entered into the play of love for more than a hundred years.
In due time she gave birth to me, like a flowering spray bearing a bud,
and, as soon as I was born, abandoned me on the lonely bank of the <s>Mālinī</s>.
There the blessed <s>Kaṇva</s> saw me covered by birds
and, an ocean of compassion, took me up; I became known by the name <s>Śakuntalā</s>.
Born from the sage <s>Viśvāmitra</s>, a treasury of austerity, in <s>Menakā</s>,
I have been reared by the sage <s>Kaṇva</s> as though I were his daughter.

children.text: iti tasyā vacaḥ śrutvā provāca pṛthivīpatiḥ
children.translated_text: After hearing her words, the lord of the earth spoke,
his mind swaying in the fresh, strong wind of love:
O young fawn-eyed girl, this man is under your control.

children.text: sāpatnye vasudhāvadhvā yogyā rājñaḥ sutā hyasi ||
children.translated_text: You are fit to be a king's wife, a co-wife of the bride Earth.
May the water-lily beds in my house be washed by the moonlight of your face,
lovely with playful smiles, even in the daytime.
When this was said, out of shame her glance
fell upon her budding breasts and bent down as far as the line of the three folds at her waist.
I am under my father's authority; when he comes, he will give me to you.
So she said, trembling, bashful, and charming in her syllables.
Your son will be the protector of the earth, O pure-smiling one.

children.text: bheje vivāhaṃ gāndharvaṃ rājā kṛtveti saṃvidam ||
children.translated_text: Having made this agreement, the king entered into a gandharva marriage.
She was rich with the springtime of youth, beautiful with clustered breasts,
shaken by the wind of passion, her lower lip trembling like a shoot.
Like a <s>mādhavī</s> creeper in a spring garden at dawn, she was covered with sprouts of horripilation;
the king, like a bee, kissed that spray of honey in the radiance of her smile.
Taking leave of her, who had been overcome by the arts of love-play, the king departed,
saying: For your sake I shall send an escort.
When the king had quickly gone, <s>Kaṇva</s> came back and saw <s>Śakuntalā</s>,
trembling and swaying like a lotus-bed from which an elephant has withdrawn.
Knowing her by divine sight to have had a fitting union,
the self-controlled sage was pleased and, requested by her, granted a boon to the king.
May there always be an unimpeded approach to <s>dharma</s> for the kings,
for those born in the lineage of <s>Duḥṣyanta</s>, thus the sage declared.
Then, in due time, pale-faced like the eastern quarter bearing the moon,

children.text: suṣuve sadṛśaṃ putraṃ sā skandamiva pārvatī ||
children.translated_text: she gave birth to a son like him, as <s>Pārvatī</s> gave birth to <s>Skanda</s>.
When born, he arose like a wish-granting tree radiant with full moons.
Powerful, he became <s>Sarvadamana</s>, because he subdued lordly beasts.
Taking her son, for whom the sage had performed rites appropriate to a kṣatriya,
<s>Śakuntalā</s>, with permission, set out for the city of <s>Duḥṣyanta</s>.
Followed by <s>Kaṇva</s>'s disciples, she reached <s>Hastināpura</s>,
and, approaching the king with her lotus face bent down in modesty, she said:

children.text: ayaṃ te tanayo rājanmayi jāto guṇādhikaḥ
children.translated_text: This is your son, O king, born from me and surpassing in virtues.
Fulfill, my lord, the truth pledged in <s>Kaṇva</s>'s hermitage.
Hearing this from <s>Śakuntalā</s>, the king spoke, though he remembered:

children.text: nāhaṃ tvāmeva jānāmi kuto nu tanayaṃ tava ||
children.translated_text: I do not know even you; whence, then, could your son be mine?
Having said this, the lord of the earth, with a frowning face,
did not accept the lotus-eyed boy being handed to him by the beautiful woman.
But she, a virtuous woman, was agitated by the shame of denial, anger, and trembling,
and she condemned the earth-lord's speech, stained with falsehood.
Alas, O king, you do not recognize your own son, who resembles you,
like a man of weak sight failing to see himself reflected in a mirror.
You ought not make a denial, though you know the truth, O great-minded one.
A king, O king, does not shine through contact with the dust of falsehood.
Truth belongs to beings of the highest nature; kindness belongs to those glorious in fame;
freedom from malice belongs to those of good conduct, and grace is the dwelling-place of fortune.
For one of innate and noble qualities, and likewise of renown,
what you say to me in the assembly is not fitting for you, O king.
Women, first the abode of affection and afterward the vessel of kindness,
surely do not deserve abandonment, for women are worthy of honor.
A wife is friend, kinsman, physician, servant, teacher, counselor, and refuge;
in every condition she brings rest to men.
Like a lamp arisen from a lamp, a son gives light in the next world.
Who, apart from you, would despise a son, a delight to the eyes?
With a son born from one's own heart, showering the nectar of heaven,

children.text: sukṛtenaiva putreṇa ko nāma na sukhī bhavet ||
children.translated_text: with a son who is one's very merit, who indeed would not be happy?
When the five witnesses dwelling inside the body, together with others,
laugh at the beginning of denial, who then is more shameless than he?
Having spoken thus, the proud woman wept aloud from the pain of humiliation,
adorning the surface of her breasts with a necklace of large drops of tears.
O king, in her you yourself have been born, like the sun in spotless water.
Accept your son; accept your lotus-eyed wife.
Such a speech issued from the sky, and when the king heard it,
he took up his son and made him lord of the <s>Bharatas</s>.
That son of <s>Śakuntalā</s>, the <s>Dauṣyanti</s> king who founded the <s>Bhārata</s> line,
the powerful one ruled the earth girdled by the seven seas.
Long ago, in the war between gods and asuras, <s>Śukra</s>, having obtained the <s>saṃjīvanī</s> science,
revived the <s>Dānavas</s>, his disciples, who had been slain by the gods.
When the armies of the daityas were inexhaustible, the gods conferred, and the slayer of <s>Vṛtra</s>
sent <s>Kaca</s>, the son of <s>Bṛhaspati</s>, to learn that science.
Then <s>Kaca</s> went to the city of <s>Vṛṣaparvan</s>, lord of the <s>Dānavas</s>,
approached <s>Śukra</s>, and for a long time remained under a vow there.
Accepted by him, that man, while performing a thousand-year vow of service,
pleased his daughter <s>Devayānī</s>.
Knowing that he had come to obtain the <s>saṃjīvanī</s> science, the <s>Dānavas</s>
consulted together and secretly killed him while he was occupied in guarding the guru's cows.
Her heart tender with affection for him, fair-eyed <s>Devayānī</s>

children.text: provāca pitaraṃ tāta kaco 'dyāpi na dṛśyate ||
children.translated_text: said to her father: Father, <s>Kaca</s> is still not seen today.
This lord of the day, beloved of the lotuses, has gone to his setting,

children.text: agopāścāgatā gāvo vyaktaṃ tāta hataḥ kacaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and the cows have come back without their herdsman; surely, father, <s>Kaca</s> has been killed.
Without obedient and skillful <s>Kaca</s>, the grandson of the sage <s>Aṅgiras</s>,
I cannot live. Saying this, she became tear-eyed.
Then, with divine sight, remembering the <s>saṃjīvanī</s> science in an instant,
<s>Kāvya</s> revived <s>Kaca</s> from afar, though he had been slain by the lords of the <s>Dānavas</s>.

children.text: āhūto guruṇābhyetya sa vṛttaṃ svaṃ nivedya ca
children.translated_text: Called by his guru, he came near, reported what had happened to him,
and then, sent out by <s>Devayānī</s> for flowers, went to the forest.

children.text: taṃ punardānavā hatvā dagdhaṃ niṣpiṣya nirjane
children.translated_text: Again the <s>Dānavas</s> killed him, burned him, and ground him up in a lonely place,
and gave him to the guru in liquor that had been sent as a courtesy.
Then <s>Devayānī</s> said: Father, <s>Kaca</s>, lotus-eyed,
whom I sent for flowers, is again not seen.

children.text: tataḥ śukraḥ kṣaṇaṃ dhyātvā devayānyā girā kacam
children.translated_text: Then <s>Śukra</s>, after meditating for a moment at <s>Devayānī</s>'s words,
revived <s>Kaca</s> inside his belly and heard from him what had happened.

children.text: tatraiva dattāṃ śukreṇa vidyāmāsādya tāṃ kacaḥ
children.translated_text: There itself, having obtained that science given by <s>Śukra</s>, <s>Kaca</s>
quickly split open his belly, came out, and revived him.
Then <s>Śukra</s> said: The twice-born man who, through delusion, drinks liquor
will go to a miserable state in hell, filled with darkness.
After gaining the science at length, and ready to go after taking leave of his guru,

children.text: devayānī kacaṃ prāha bhaja māmiti bhāminī ||
children.translated_text: <s>Devayānī</s>, the lovely woman, said to <s>Kaca</s>: Choose me.

children.text: kacaḥ provāca śukro me subhru mānyo guruḥ pitā
children.translated_text: <s>Kaca</s> replied: Fair-browed one, <s>Śukra</s> is my honored guru and father;

children.text: ahaṃ tasyoṣitaḥ kukṣau dharmeṇa tvaṃ svasā mama ||
children.translated_text: I have dwelt in his belly, and by <s>dharma</s> you are my sister.
Rejected by him, she, trembling and overcome with anger, said:
Because of your pride, the science of you who abandon one devoted to you will not bear fruit.
Hearing that, troubled <s>Kaca</s> said to the daughter of <s>Śukra</s>:
Since I have not departed from good conduct, I am not worthy of your curse.
That science will attain success among my disciples, for I possess <s>dharma</s>;

children.text: muniputro na te kaścidbhavitā svocitaḥ patiḥ ||
children.translated_text: no son of a sage will become a husband suited to you.
Having spoken thus, <s>Kaca</s> quickly departed from the house of <s>Śukra</s>,
and the gods came out to meet <s>Kaca</s>, who had returned after a thousand years.

children.text: te kacātprāpya tāṃ vidyāṃ tuṣṭāstasmai varaṃ daduḥ
children.translated_text: Pleased after receiving that science from <s>Kaca</s>, they gave him a boon,
by which he became of imperishable fame and a recipient of a share in sacrifice.
Meanwhile, in the grove of her own pleasure garden, lotus-faced <s>Śarmiṣṭhā</s>,
the daughter of <s>Vṛṣaparvan</s>, joyfully took her pleasure.
Attended by a thousand maidservants, languid with the intoxication of play,
she imitated the graceful sport of creepers shaken by the spring wind.
There too <s>Devayānī</s>, the full-breasted daughter of <s>Śukra</s>,
sporting with youth, the abode of the mind-born god, amused herself.
Then the husband of <s>Śacī</s>, arriving there by chance and coming up to those women,
became wind and, fond of a smile, made an exchange of their garments.
Then, when there was recognition through the pulling about of their own garments,
a quarrel arose between <s>Śarmiṣṭhā</s> and <s>Devayānī</s>.
Foolish girl, you, daughter of a poor beggar with outstretched hand,
despise me, the daughter of the giving lord of the daityas?
After saying this, <s>Śarmiṣṭhā</s> threw <s>Devayānī</s> into a well.
From those maddened by the intoxication of power, who can obtain welfare?
When the daitya princess had gone away, King <s>Yayāti</s>, son of <s>Nahuṣa</s>,
having gone out hunting, came by chance to that thicket.
There, seeking water, in that waterless well he saw
the daughter of <s>Śukra</s>, her face adorned with extraordinary beauty.
When she had told him her lineage and name, the lord of the earth lifted her up,
taking the rolling-eyed woman by the hand, like <s>Viṣṇu</s> once more lifting the earth.
When the king had gone from there, <s>Devayānī</s>, deeply distressed,

children.text: āhūya prāha pitaraṃ vṛttaṃ sā bāṣpagadgadam ||
children.translated_text: Having called her father, she told him what had happened, her voice choked with tears.
<s>Śukra</s> said to her, "How can a story of children's playful quarrels
be treated as authoritative by good people who wish to cross beyond endless enmity?
For even when there has been an offense, a good man must endure the fire of anger;
if it is not sprinkled with the waters of forgiveness, it may not be quenched even through many births.
When <s>Uśanas</s> had spoken thus gently, then that proud girl said:
"Who, except a beggar, falls from honor because of wretchedness?
Despised by her, father, I do not wish to live."
Going to <s>Vṛṣaparvan</s>, the daughter related what had happened.
Saying, "I am going away, abandoning the Daityas," he
rose to depart in anger, his garment slipping off in agitation.
Then the frightened lord of the Daityas fell at his feet,
his cheek for a moment touched by the tips of his swinging earrings.
"Let <s>Devayānī</s> be appeased; I have no anger,"

children.text: ityāha śukraḥ sādhūnāṃ kopo hi vinayāvadhiḥ ||
children.translated_text: said <s>Śukra</s>, "for the anger of good men lasts only until humility is shown."
Then <s>Vṛṣaparvan</s>, with folded hands, appeased the guru's daughter
and gave her his own daughter as a maid, attended by a hundred maidservants.
Having obtained <s>Śarmiṣṭhā</s> as a maid, the delighted daughter of <s>Bhṛgu</s>
said with a smile, "How are you the maid of a beggar's daughter?"
Then one day that young girl went to that same forest,
filled with jasmine buds and with winds moving through rows of mango trees.
Meanwhile King <s>Yayāti</s>, out of delight in hunting,
came again to that very region, lotus-eyed.
Seeing him as if he were a second <s>Manmatha</s>, <s>Devayānī</s>
heard his name and lineage and said, "I am under your power."
Then <s>Yayāti</s> said to that beautiful woman whose lineage had been told:
"I am a Kṣatriya, daughter of a sage; lovely-browed one, how can I seek you?
Who indeed is able to overstep the brilliance of the twice-born,

children.text: tejo laṅghayituṃ śaktaḥ ko nu nāma dvijanmanām ||
children.translated_text: whose weapon is more terrible than deadly poison and which has conquered the fire of dissolution?
I do not dare to marry you without your father's consent.

children.text: kāvyaḥ praṇetā dharmāṇāṃ pramāṇaṃ tadvaco mama ||
children.translated_text: <s>Kāvya</s> is a promulgator of dharmas; his word is authority for me."

children.text: atha rājño vacaḥ śrutvā pitaraṃ sā sulocanā
children.translated_text: Then, after hearing the king's words, the lovely-eyed woman
called her father and made known her own resolve for marriage.
Then, when <s>Śukra</s> said, "There is no fault," and himself gave her,

children.text: jagrāha nāhuṣo loke munīnāṃ hi girā sthitiḥ ||
children.translated_text: the descendant of <s>Nahuṣa</s> accepted her; for in the world order rests on the words of sages.
Having obtained <s>Devayānī</s>, accompanied by <s>Śarmiṣṭhā</s>, the king
went happily to his own city, where a fresh festival had been arranged.

children.text: tataḥ prāpa sutau devī devayānī narādhipāt
children.translated_text: Then Queen <s>Devayānī</s>, lotus-eyed, in due time

children.text: yaduṃ ca turvasuṃ ceti kāle kuvalayekṣaṇā ||
children.translated_text: obtained two sons from the king, <s>Yadu</s> and <s>Turvasu</s>.
Then one day <s>Śarmiṣṭhā</s>, with breasts like clusters, approached the king in her fertile season,
intent and full with the onset of fresh youth.
Standing in private near an aśoka grove, she spoke,
her jeweled anklets and girdle jingling as she trembled deeply:

children.text: sakhyāḥ patiḥ kṣitipate mama tvaṃ dharmataḥ patiḥ
children.translated_text: "O king, as my friend's husband you are, by dharma, my husband too.
Today I ask you in my fertile season; lord, let this earlier affection be fulfilled."

children.text: tacchrutvā bhūpatiḥ prāha dattvā śukraḥ sutāṃ purā
children.translated_text: Hearing that, the king said, "Long ago, when <s>Śukra</s> gave me his daughter,
he made me enter an agreement: '<s>Śarmiṣṭhā</s> is not to be enjoyed by you.'
His word, which I greatly fear, is an obstacle to that union.

children.text: pūrṇenduvadanāṃ subhru kastvāṃ na bahu manyate ||
children.translated_text: Yet who would not greatly honor you, full-moon-faced, lovely-browed one?"
Hearing this, the daughter of the Daitya king addressed the ruler,
tracing the ground with the tip of her foot, her eyes long:
"In marriage, among women, in joking speech, when life is at stake, and when wealth is lost,

children.text: na satyaṃ gaṇyate sadbhiḥ satyaṃ sākṣiṣu śasyate ||
children.translated_text: truth is not reckoned by the good; truth is praised in the case of witnesses."
Thus entreated, the king himself enjoyed that lotus-eyed woman,
whose cheek and lip-buds were mingled with drops of sweat.
Sporting secretly with that young doe-eyed woman, the king

children.text: druhyuṃ cānuṃ ca pūruṃ ca kālena prāpadātmajān ||
children.translated_text: in time obtained sons: <s>Druhyu</s>, <s>Anu</s>, and <s>Pūru</s>.
Then one day, in the garden, the daughter of <s>Bhṛgu</s> saw those princes of the king,
with faces like his and with the quarters smeared by their radiance.
Suspicious, she asked, "Whose children are you?"
The boys pointed from afar to the king as their father.
Then, seized by the fire of anger, <s>Devayānī</s>
went secretly to her father's house and reported all of that royal conduct.
As the king followed that very wife to soothe her,

children.text: śaśāpa kupitaḥ kruddho jarājīrṇo bhaveti tam ||
children.translated_text: the enraged sage, angry, cursed him: "Become worn out by old age."
Then, after hearing the curse, the king appeased the son of <s>Bhṛgu</s>,
who said, "By transferring your old age to a son, you will obtain youth."
Hearing this, he went to his own city and said to his sons in order:
"My sons, give me youth in exchange for old age."

children.text: te tamūcurgataprāṇo dhanyo na tu jarārditaḥ
children.translated_text: They said to him, "Blessed is the man whose breath has gone, but not one afflicted by old age;
for an old man, bearing the burden of the body, is the seat of every misfortune."
Rejected by the four sons beginning with <s>Yadu</s>, the king
cursed them so that they would not be fit for kingship and would have sinful lineages.
Then the king, receiving the youth bestowed by <s>Pūru</s>,
was happy for a thousand years, devoted to sensual enjoyment.

children.text: pūrṇe kāle nijaṃ rājyaṃ yauvanaṃ ca mahīpatiḥ
children.translated_text: When the time was complete, the king, pleased,
gave his own kingdom and youth to <s>Pūru</s> and became a forest-dwelling sage.
This royal lineage of <s>Pūru</s> is the Paurava line; from <s>Yadu</s> comes the Yādava line.
From his father's curse came the <s>mleccha</s> Śakas; the remaining ones were the Yavanas and others.
Then, by further tapas, the <s>Nāhuṣa</s> ascended to heaven
and dwelt in <s>Brahmā</s>'s world and in the assemblies of the guardians of the worlds.
Once, then, <s>Devendra</s> asked him in the course of a story:
'King, through what meritorious tapas do you shine? To whom are you equal?'
He replied, 'Among gods, siddhas, seers, gandharvas, kings, and serpents
I see no one equal to myself in tapas, nor even in fame.'

children.text: iti bruvāṇaṃ taṃ śakraḥ patetyāhoccayā girā
children.translated_text: As he was speaking thus, <s>Śakra</s> said to him in a loud voice, 'Fall!'
'By your contempt for all beings, that tapas of yours is exhausted, O king.
By great disdain, by exultation, anger, and amazement,
austerities come to destruction, just as fame does through very bad conduct.'
At <s>Śakra</s>'s words the king quickly fell from the abode of the gods,
his facial brightness ruined, and he begged for the company of the good.

children.text: satāṃ madhye patetyuktaḥ sa surendreṇa pārthivaḥ
children.translated_text: Told by the lord of gods, 'Fall among the good,' that king
fell head downward from heaven into the sacrificial ground of his daughter's sons.
<s>Pratardana</s>, <s>Vasumanas</s>, <s>Śibi</s> the <s>Uśīnara</s>, and <s>Aṣṭaka</s>

children.text: te nṛpaṃ sūryasaṃkāśaṃ patantaṃ taṃ vyalokayan ||
children.translated_text: saw that king, radiant like the sun, as he fell.
<s>Aṣṭaka</s> said to him, 'Divine one, who are you, with the brilliance of blazing fire?
A source of such splendors as these is surely not small.'
When thus questioned from nearby by <s>Aṣṭaka</s>, he gave his own name

children.text: uvāca janmavṛttāntaṃ pātanaṃ ca divo bhuvi ||
children.translated_text: and told the story of his birth and his fall from heaven to earth.
Then, questioned by his daughter's son about the truth of worldly existence, that all-knowing one,
not yet touching the ground, spoke from what he had experienced through the company of the good.
'A man, ascending to the mansion of the Thirty gods with merit as his provisions,
enjoys the divine fruit of good deeds, accomplished and skilled in the play of pleasures.
In time, when his merit is exhausted, he, like a lord whose wealth is spent,
is driven alone from heaven, as a sensual man is from a courtesan's house.

children.text: divaḥ patantaṃ taṃ ghorā rākṣasā gṛdhragomukhāḥ
children.translated_text: As he falls from heaven, terrible rākṣasas, vulture-faced and cow-faced,
devour him again and again as he is repeatedly produced, roaring loudly.
After being eaten by them for sixty thousand years and much tormented,
following his own karma, he goes, as mere consciousness, into union with a body.
Joined with the scent of latent impressions, the embodied one creeps into a womb,
like wind pervaded by sounds, together with the elements whose powers are unmanifest.
A sinful man and one who insults others is born among low wombs;

children.text: bhuvi puṇyaparo yāti punaḥ svargagatiṃ naraḥ ||
children.translated_text: on earth, a man devoted to merit again reaches the path to heaven.
First a householder, then a forest-dweller, and then one who has laid aside all rites,

children.text: nirvairo nirmamaḥ śāntaḥ prayāti paramaṃ padam ||
children.translated_text: free of hostility, free of possessiveness, and peaceful, he reaches the supreme state.'

children.text: yayātiriti dauhitraiḥ pṛṣṭaḥ sarvaṃ nigadya tat
children.translated_text: Thus questioned by his daughter's sons, <s>Yayāti</s> told all that,
and, touched by their merit, went to heaven accompanied by those very men.
Those five kings, mounted on divine aerial seats,
shone in the third heaven with mighty energy, like five risen suns.
Among them King <s>Śibi</s> the <s>Uśīnara</s> shone more brightly,

children.text: dānena tapasā kīrtyā satyena kṣamayā tathā ||
children.translated_text: through generosity, tapas, fame, truth, and likewise patience.
When the <s>Nāhuṣa</s> king of the earth had ascended to heaven again,
the lineage of <s>Pūru</s>, his son, became very extensive on earth.
Long ago <s>Vaivasvata Manu</s> had a son named <s>Iḍa</s>;
his son was <s>Āyu</s>, and <s>Nahuṣa</s> was born from <s>Āyu</s>.
<s>Yayāti</s>, son of <s>Nahuṣa</s>, was king; <s>Pūru</s> was his son.
<s>Janamejaya</s> was his son, and after him came <s>Prācīdhanvan</s>.
His son was <s>Saṃyāti</s>, and then there was one named <s>Śampāti</s>.
His son was <s>Sārvabhauma</s>; <s>Ārādhīra</s> was his own son.
His son was <s>Mahābhauma</s>, and after him came <s>Ayutanābha</s>.
<s>Akrodhana</s> was his son, and his son was <s>Devātithi</s>.
His offspring was the illustrious <s>Pada</s>; <s>Ṛkṣa</s> became his son.
Then there was one named <s>Matināra</s>; his son was <s>Taṃsu</s>.

children.text: nalinaśca taṃsoḥ sūnur duṣyantas tatsuto vibhuḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Nalina</s> was <s>Taṃsu</s>'s son, and powerful <s>Duṣyanta</s> was his son.
<s>Bharata</s> was his heir; <s>Abhimanyu</s> was the <s>Bhārata</s> king.
<s>Suhotra</s> was his son, and then <s>Hastin</s>, the maker of <s>Hastināpura</s>.
<s>Vikuṇṭha</s> was <s>Hastin</s>'s son, and after him came <s>Ajamīḍha</s>.
In the line of <s>Ajamīḍha</s> came <s>Saṃvaraṇa</s>; <s>Kuru</s> was <s>Saṃvaraṇa</s>'s son.
The <s>Kaurava</s> king <s>Abhimbā</s> came, and after him was <s>Parīkṣit</s>.
From <s>Parīkṣit</s> came <s>Bhīmasena</s>; <s>Pratīpa</s> was his son, O king.
From <s>Pratīpa</s> came the illustrious King <s>Śaṃtanu</s>, husband of <s>Satyavatī</s>.
<s>Vicitravīrya</s> was his son; after him came <s>Pāṇḍu</s>, lord of the earth.
<s>Arjuna</s> was <s>Pāṇḍu</s>'s heir, and <s>Saubhadra</s> was his son.
<s>Parīkṣit</s> was his son, and after him you are <s>Janamejaya</s>.
And this long-lived <s>Śatānīka</s> of yours is worthy of the lineage.
His son will be the illustrious king <s>Sahasrānīka</s>, performer of horse sacrifices.
This is the lineage of <s>Pūru</s>.'
Long ago in <s>Brahmaloka</s>, <s>Mahātithi</s>, a sacrificer of <s>Manu</s>'s line,
stayed in the place of the Four-faced One, together with royal sages.
There the embodied <s>Mandākinī</s> served the lotus-born Grandfather,
seated in the assembly, with a yak-tail fan white as a swan.
White with a garland of foam and with the edge of her garment like trembling waves,
the doe-eyed woman's cloth stirred when shaken by the breeze from her fan.
Seeing her, with bracelets and girdle jingling as she moved in agitation,
all the gods became embarrassed for a moment and lowered their faces.
But <s>Mahātithi</s>, seeing her with a splendor like the womb of <s>Rambhā</s>,
with an eye free from the fault of blinking, looked up.

children.text: tatkopādbrahmaṇā śaptaḥ sa papāta tato bhuvi
children.translated_text: Then, cursed by <s>Brahmā</s> because of that anger, he fell to the earth,
and thought, "May I become the son of King <s>Pratīpa</s> himself."
At that time <s>Gaṅgā</s>, returning from <s>Brahmaloka</s>,
saw the <s>Vasus</s>, their faces dejected, moving through the sky.
Asked by her about the reason for the curse, they, with their splendor gone, said:
"We have been cursed by <s>Vasiṣṭha</s>; we are falling to the surface of the earth.
Goddess, we shall become the sons of <s>Śaṃtanu</s>, son of <s>Pratīpa</s>;
out of compassion, you ought there to become our mother.

children.text: jātānasmāñjale kṣiptvā vimuktiṃ ca vidhatsva naḥ
children.translated_text: When we are born, cast us into the water and grant us release.
Who could endure human birth, painful and a dwelling-place of calamity?"
Hearing that, <s>Jāhnavī</s> said, "I will do all this.

children.text: kiṃ tu tasya nṛpasyaikaḥ putro 'stu bhavatā mataḥ ||
children.translated_text: But let one son of that king be agreed upon by you.
I cannot make fruitless the union for which I will go to him."
Hearing this speech of <s>Gaṅgā</s>, the delighted <s>Vasus</s> said:
"From an eighth part of each of us, of our strength, valor, virtues, and vigor,
goddess, a celibate son of yours will be born."
Having made this agreement, when they had gone to the earth,
King <s>Pratīpa</s>, ruler of the earth, was long engaged in muttering prayer on the riverbank.
From the sacred water there, <s>Gaṅgā</s> herself, rippling with beauty,
climbed upon his right thigh and said to him, "Enjoy me."

children.text: sa tāmuvāca nājñātāṃ nāvarṇāṃ na parastriyam
children.translated_text: He said to her, "Know, proud lady, that my vow is always this:

children.text: vrajāmīti vrataṃ viddhi mama mānini sarvadā ||
children.translated_text: I do not go to a woman unknown to me, of another class, or belonging to another man.

children.text: dakṣiṇāṅkopaviṣṭā ca tvaṃ snuṣā me bhaviṣyasi
children.translated_text: And since you have sat on my right lap, you will become my daughter-in-law;
this is the place for children, while the left is the place for a beloved."

children.text: iti rājño vacaḥ śrutvā tathetyuktvā trimārgagā
children.translated_text: Hearing the king's words, the three-pathed river said, "So be it,"
and departed, filling the bank with floods of radiance.
Meanwhile a son was born to the vow-observing <s>Pratīpa</s>:
because of <s>Brahmā</s>'s curse, <s>Mahābhīṣa</s> became <s>Śaṃtanu</s>, son of the king whose old age was peaceful.

children.text: taṃ yuvānaṃ tataḥ prāha sa kadācitsutaṃ nṛpaḥ
children.translated_text: Then one day that king spoke to his son when he was young:

children.text: gaṅgākūle purā putra divyā yoṣitsvayaṃ mayā ||
children.translated_text: "Son, on the bank of the <s>Gaṅgā</s> long ago a divine woman was by me

children.text: vṛtā snuṣeti vacasā tāṃ bhajasva samāgatām
children.translated_text: chosen by the words, 'You are my daughter-in-law'; when she comes, take her as your wife."
After saying this and giving him the kingdom, <s>Pratīpa</s> went away to practice austerity.
Then <s>Śaṃtanu</s>, an ornament of the expanse of the world and beloved of the people,
became the lord of kings, with disturbances pacified.
As he wandered on the sandy bank of the <s>Gaṅgā</s>, he plunged into an ocean of delight
in a bower where clusters of flowers danced gently, stirred by the wind.
He saw a divine woman whose face was like the <s>Kārttikī</s> moon,
clad in clear garments, white as foam of nectar, like a lotus.
Seeing her, whose broad hips were like riverbanks, who was filled with darting fish-like glances,
a stream of loveliness, full of the essence of the flavor of beauty,
the lord of the earth, his eyes opened wide with joy and wonder,

children.text: pituḥ smṛtvā vacaḥ prāha rambhoru bhaja māmiti ||
children.translated_text: remembered his father's words and said, "Lovely-thighed one, be mine."
Hearing him as he spoke with love, that river of the gods
regarded him as a beloved whose term would end when he refused to let her act as she wished.
Enjoying himself with that slender woman in a fresh garden, the king,
lotus-eyed, did not notice even the passage of time.
Then, one after another, she took the seven <s>Vasus</s> who had fallen through the curse, as soon as they were born,

children.text: jaghāna salile kṣiptvā noce kiṃcicca tāṃ nṛpaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and killed them by casting them into the water; the king said nothing to her.
When the eighth son was born and she was stopped by the king, she then said:
"You have fallen away from the agreement; farewell, lord of the earth, I am going.
Have you forgotten that refusal brings separation?
I, the three-pathed river, O king, became your beloved,
appointed to free the falling <s>Vasus</s> from <s>Vasiṣṭha</s>'s curse.
Long ago the eight <s>Vasus</s>, delighting in sport and accompanied by their dear friends,
wandered joyfully in <s>Vasiṣṭha</s>'s ascetic grove beside <s>Meru</s>.
There <s>Dyaus</s>, a <s>Vasu</s>, saw the great sage's sacrificial cow,
the fulfiller of every wish, roaming there, and spoke to his own wife:
'This lovely cow of the sage streams nectar.
Even a mortal with a body becomes immortal through her milk.'

children.text: vasubhāryā niśamyeti taṃ prāha dayitaṃ priyā
children.translated_text: Hearing this, the <s>Vasu</s>'s wife said to her beloved husband:
'In the mortal world there is a friend of mine, my very life outside my body:
<s>Ajirāvatī</s>, daughter of King <s>Uśīnara</s>.
For her sake I want the milk; take this <s>Surabhi</s> by force.'
Saying, 'So be it,' he, urged on and bewildered by love, stole the cow.

children.text: tejasā saha naśyanti strījitānāṃ hi buddhayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: For the minds of men conquered by women perish together with their splendor.
Because of anger at that, <s>Vasiṣṭha</s> came upon those <s>Vasus</s> and at once cursed them:
'By the fault of even one, a whole group incurs blame.

children.text: martyeṣu janma bhūyādvaḥ śāpaṃ śrutveti te tataḥ
children.translated_text: May birth among mortals be yours.' Hearing the curse, they then,
terrified, propitiated him, and he slowly said to them:
'For you this curse will have the womb as its limit and will last a year;

children.text: yo hartā dyaurastu ciraṃ manuṣyo 'yaṃ bhaviṣyati ||
children.translated_text: but <s>Dyaus</s>, who stole the cow, shall remain a human for a long time.'

children.text: iti śaptāvaśiṣṭena mocitāḥ sapta te mayā
children.translated_text: Thus cursed by <s>Vasiṣṭha</s>, those seven have been released by me.
O king, this long-lived son of yours is the eighth <s>Vasu</s>, <s>Dyaus</s>.

children.text: ityuktvā prayayau gaṅgā tūrṇamādāya taṃ śiśum
children.translated_text: Having spoken thus, <s>Gaṅgā</s> quickly departed, taking the child with her.
He became known as <s>Devavrata</s>, whose vow had been appointed by the gods.
Then in time, when he had acquired learning and become skilled in weapons and missiles,

children.text: jāhnavī taṃ narapateḥ punaretya sutaṃ dadau ||
children.translated_text: <s>Jāhnavī</s> returned and gave that son back to the king."
Delighted, <s>Śaṃtanu</s>, having obtained <s>Gāṅgeya</s> as a worthy son,
thought his own life fruitful after consecrating him as heir apparent.
Then once <s>Śaṃtanu</s> wandered through the woodland tracts near the bank of the <s>Kālindī</s>,
watching birds whose calls were sweetly humming.
There, smelling a divine fragrance akin to the scent of blooming lotuses,
he saw a maiden, as though she were a shining portion of beauty itself.

children.text: kāsīti pṛṣṭā sā tena provāca varavarṇinī
children.translated_text: When he asked her, 'Who are you?' that lovely woman replied to him,
'I am named <s>Satyavatī</s>, daughter of the lord of the fishermen.'

children.text: tataḥ smareṇa sahasā sa dhīro vivaśīkṛtaḥ
children.translated_text: Then, suddenly overpowered by <s>Smara</s>, though he was firm-minded,
he approached the fisherman-king and asked for that beautiful woman.

children.text: asyāṃ jāto rājyabhāgī sutaste yadi bhūpate
children.translated_text: 'If a son born from her is to share the kingdom, O king,
then I shall give her to you,' said the chief of the fishermen.
Hearing this, <s>Śaṃtanu</s> reflected on his son <s>Devavrata</s>, the bearer of the burden,
and, disregarding the fisherman's words, went back to <s>Hastināpura</s>.
There, assailed by <s>Manmatha</s>, with her alone fixed in his heart,
he found no sleep, thinking of her like a half-remembered song.
His son <s>Devavrata</s> himself, that ocean of fortitude, came to him in solitude, absorbed in thought,
and asked the cause of his grief and burning sorrow.

children.text: sutena pṛṣṭaḥ provāca tvamevaikaḥ suto mama
children.translated_text: Questioned by his son, he said, 'You alone are my one son;
for those who have only one son, fear arising from the extinction of offspring does not pass away.
Since a son worthy of the family, surpassing all in virtues, has been born in you,
for me, whose purposes are accomplished, another marriage would be an absurdity.'
Hearing those words, <s>Gāṅgeya</s>, through the speech of the ministers,
understood that his father's mind had been carried away by the fisherman's daughter.
He went to the fisherman-king who lived on the bank of the <s>Yamunā</s>,
and, after being honored, asked for the lovely-eyed maiden for his father.

children.text: kathaṃ tvayi sthite vīra dauhitro me nṛpo bhavet
children.translated_text: 'While you are still there, hero, how could my daughter's son become king?'
When the fisherman-king said this, the heroic son of <s>Śaṃtanu</s> replied:

children.text: nāhaṃ rājyaṃ kariṣyāmi satyo 'yaṃ samayo mama
children.translated_text: 'I shall not rule the kingdom. This agreement of mine is true.'
As <s>Gāṅgeya</s> said this, the fisherman-king spoke again:
'Truth-keeping one, this vow of yours is indeed imperishable,

children.text: tvatsutānāṃ tu vīrāṇāṃ rājyaṃ ko vārayiṣyati ||
children.translated_text: but who will prevent your heroic sons from taking the kingdom?'
Hearing that, <s>Devavrata</s> addressed the fisherman-king:
'Let your fear of my sons depart; I shall be a celibate.'
When the prince had spoken thus, the gods, raining flowers from the sky,

children.text: bhīṣaṇā te pratijñeyaṃ bhīṣmeti procire surāḥ ||
children.translated_text: declared, 'This vow is terrible,' and called him <s>Bhīṣma</s>.
Then <s>Gāṅgeya</s>, his mind free from doubt, quickly took her,
given by the fisherman-king, and went to <s>Hastināpura</s>.
Then the king, receiving <s>Satyavatī</s> handed over by his son,
heard of that vow and became shamefaced, his face bent down.

children.text: svacchandanidhanaṃ tasmai dadau tuṣṭaḥ pitā varam
children.translated_text: Pleased, his father gave him the boon of death at will;
what is not to be given to grateful men who help without even being asked?
Then in time <s>Satyavatī</s> gave birth to a royal boy,
like a bamboo creeper bearing a pearl, like the night of full moon bearing the moon.
When he, named <s>Citrāṅgada</s>, had reached youth,
<s>Satyavatī</s> bore another boy too, a protector of the earth.
When he, called <s>Vicitravīrya</s>, gradually reached full bodily growth,
