the king ascended to heaven by rows of sacrificial stairways.
Then young <s>Citrāṅgada</s>, consecrated by <s>Bhīṣma</s>,
a hero, was slain by a hostile gandharva also named <s>Citrāṅgada</s>.
Thereafter <s>Devavrata</s> gave the kingdom to <s>Vicitravīrya</s>;

children.text: āpatsvapi na sīdanti satāṃ satprakriyāḥ kriyāḥ ||
children.translated_text: the right practices of good men do not fail even in calamities.
To gain brides for him, the son of the river conquered the kings at a svayaṃvara
and brought away the daughters of the king of <s>Kāśī</s>.
Knowing that the eldest of them, named <s>Ambā</s>, had already chosen another even in her heart,
and desired <s>Śālva</s>, he released her, as though she were a flame.
<s>Vicitravīrya</s> too, constantly stirred by the waves of mature desire,
had his heart moistened by the pleasures of sport with <s>Ambikā</s> and <s>Ambālikā</s>.
Delighting in them, he was consumed by the wasting disease that preyed on him,
and the moonlike king went away somewhere, his disk marked by the twilight of his subjects' affection.
When <s>Vicitravīrya</s> had gone to the third heaven, <s>Satyavatī</s>,
burning with grief, spoke to <s>Gāṅgeya</s> in a voice choked with tears:
'This lineage of <s>Śaṃtanu</s> has been cut off by cruel-working Time.
What ought now to be done here, my son, you should consider.
In the field of <s>Vicitravīrya</s>, your brother who has gone to the gods,
establish the lineage, or else take a wife.'
Hearing this speech of <s>Satyavatī</s>, <s>Bhīṣma</s>, his understanding unshaken, said:

children.text: sādhūnāṃ maraṇaṃ śreyo na mātaḥ satyaviplavaḥ ||
children.translated_text: 'For good men, death is better, mother, not the betrayal of truth.
I remember that vow made at your marriage with single-pointed mind;

children.text: tyajanti jīvitaṃ kāle maryādāṃ na tu māninaḥ ||
children.translated_text: men of honor give up life when the time comes, but not their moral boundary.
Let some Brahmin come to us and establish the lineage;
of old, when the warrior class had been slain by <s>Rāma</s>, kings were born from twice-born men.
By the sage <s>Autathya</s> too, in <s>Sudoṣṇā</s>, beloved of <s>Bali</s>, lord of the earth,
a king named <s>Aṅga</s> was begotten.
And in a śūdra woman sent by that very woman,
the sage begot <s>Kukṣivat</s> and the others, eleven sons who became sages.'

children.text: bhīṣmasyeti vacaḥ śrutvā prāha satyavatī śanaiḥ
children.translated_text: Hearing these words of <s>Bhīṣma</s>, <s>Satyavatī</s> said softly,
'I have a kānīna son, a sage born from <s>Parāśara</s>.
The holy one, born on an island in the <s>Yamunā</s>, is known as <s>Dvaipāyana</s>.'

children.text: vedavyāsaṃ mahātmānaṃ taṃ smarāmi kulasya naḥ
children.translated_text: I remember that great-souled <s>Vedavyāsa</s> of our family;
surely, if entreated by me, he will make the splendor of the lineage sprout again.
As she was speaking thus, <s>Bhīṣma</s> respectfully said, "So be it,"

children.text: sasmāra tapaso rāśiṃ sā sutaṃ jñānabhāskaram ||
children.translated_text: and she remembered her son, that heap of tapas, that sun of knowledge.
The blessed one, dark as collyrium, came as soon as he was meditated upon,
with beard and eyes tawny from the mass of rays of his own brilliance.
His mother addressed him, omniscient, aware of the whole event,
and honored by the priest and by <s>Bhīṣma</s>, her breasts flowing from maternal affection:
"O sage, knower of <s>dharma</s> (righteous order), at my word, in the field of your brother <s>Vicitravīrya</s>,
beget offspring for the establishment of our lineage.
This kingless earth is like a boat without a helmsman;
for in a kingdom without a king the bounds of <s>dharma</s> (righteous order) sink down."
<s>Vyāsa</s> accepted his mother's words, saying, "So be it,"
and then <s>Satyā</s>, having told <s>Ambikā</s> what had happened, sent her to him.
She, the daughter of the king of <s>Kāśi</s>, approached that dark, tawny-eyed

children.text: saṃgamya taṃ munivaraṃ bhītā netre nyamīlayat ||
children.translated_text: best of sages, and in fear she closed her eyes.
Then, when the sage had come back from her presence, <s>Satyā</s> said to him,
"Will a son worthy of the lineage be born from her, O <s>Vyāsa</s>?"

children.text: iti pṛṣṭo muniḥ prāha tanayo 'syāṃ bhaviṣyati
children.translated_text: Asked in this way, the sage said, "A son will be born from her,
and he will have many sons; but because of his mother's fault he will become blind."
Saying, "What use is a blind man?" <s>Satyavatī</s> entreated the sage again,
and he approached <s>Ambālikā</s>. She too, seeing him blazing,
hard to look at like the fierce-rayed sun, unapproachable like a mountain,
became pale-faced, her mind shaken and overcome.
Then, returning to <s>Satyā</s>, the sage was questioned again and said,
"A son named <s>Pāṇḍu</s> will be born from this pale-faced woman."
Then <s>Ambikā</s> bore blind <s>Dhṛtarāṣṭra</s>, a treasury of intelligence,
and <s>Ambālikā</s> bore <s>Pāṇḍu</s>, white as the camphor of fame.
Again entreated by his mother, the sage produced a third son,
from union with a Śūdra woman appointed through <s>Ambikā</s>'s deception.

children.text: dharmo māṇḍavyaśāpena sa bālaḥ śūdratāṃ gataḥ
children.translated_text: That child was <s>Dharma</s>, who had entered Śūdra status through <s>Māṇḍavya</s>'s curse;
<s>Vidura</s> became Śūdra in role, for one's own conduct is a great lineage.
Long before, while the sage <s>Māṇḍavya</s> was practicing austerities,
city guards saw wealth left near him by frightened thieves.

children.text: maunavrataḥ sa taiḥ pṛṣṭo yadā novāca kiṃcana
children.translated_text: When he, keeping a vow of silence, said nothing at all after being questioned by them,

children.text: tadā taṃ caurasahitaṃ te ninyuḥ pārthivāntikam ||
children.translated_text: they brought him, together with the thieves, before the king.
The king, not knowing what had happened, in delusion set him upon an evil stake;

children.text: śūlasthaḥ sa tapastīvraṃ ciraṃ tepe mahātapāḥ ||
children.translated_text: fixed on the stake, that great ascetic practiced severe tapas for a long time.
Sages, becoming birds, spoke with grief to him as he was on the stake:
"Blessed one, as the result of what deed have you come to this state?"
He said, "The self itself experiences what it itself has done before."

children.text: tataḥ prasādayāmāsa taṃ jñātvā cakito nṛpaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then the king, alarmed when he learned the truth, appeased him.

children.text: ākṛṣyamāṇaṃ śūlāgraṃ yadā tasya na niryayau
children.translated_text: When the stake's point did not come out as it was being pulled from him,
he carried its cut-off tip inside his body and wandered about.
From that time onward he became known in the world as <s>Aṇīmāṇḍavya</s>.
Angry, he went to <s>Dharma</s>, who was seated there, and said,
"Of what deed is this impalement of mine the ripened fruit?"
Asked thus by the lord of sages, <s>Dharma</s> reflected and said to him,

children.text: pucche yatputtikā pūrvaṃ tvayā viddhā tṛṇāṅkuraiḥ ||
children.translated_text: "Long ago you pierced a little creature in the tail with blades of grass.
This is the ripened fruit of that deed." Hearing this, the sage said,
"Ah, for a slight offense an unbearably harsh punishment has been given to me by you,
O <s>Dharma</s>; therefore you will be born in a Śūdra womb.

children.text: mayā bālye kṛtaṃ hyetadbālā yasmād apātakāḥ
children.translated_text: For I did this in childhood, and children are not culpable,
up to the end of fourteen years: this is the established and honored rule."

children.text: evaṃ munīndraśāpena dharmo yātaḥ sa śūdratām
children.translated_text: Thus, through the curse of the lord of sages, <s>Dharma</s> went into Śūdra status,
and <s>Vidura</s> became far-seeing, wise, and a knower of <s>dharma</s> (righteous order).
When the blessed <s>Vyāsa</s> had disappeared, those delights of the <s>Kurus</s>,
full of great vigor, grew up amid the festivals of the subjects.
Among them the eldest was strong <s>Dhṛtarāṣṭra</s>, whose eye was wisdom,
but <s>Pāṇḍu</s>, like <s>Duṣyanta</s> and <s>Bharata</s>, bore the kingdom.
The son of <s>Ambikā</s> obtained <s>Gāndhārī</s>, daughter of mighty <s>Subala</s>,
king of <s>Gāndhāra</s>, and younger sister of <s>Śakuni</s>.
"You will obtain a hundred sons of vast strength and splendor":
such was the boon <s>Hari</s> himself, when propitiated, gave her.

children.text: viditvāndhaṃ patiṃ sā tu satī vrataparāyaṇā
children.translated_text: But when she learned that her husband was blind, that faithful woman devoted to vows
bound her eyes with a fine cloth, a very ground of humility.
Meanwhile King <s>Kuntibhoja</s> adopted <s>Kuntī</s>, daughter of <s>Śūra</s>
and younger sister of <s>Vasudeva</s>, as though she were his own child.

children.text: putrī ca mātuleyī ca gṛhe sā tasya kanyakā
children.translated_text: As both daughter and niece, that maiden grew up in his house,
performing due worship for guests, gurus, and twice-born men.
From the eminent sage <s>Durvāsas</s>, whom she had carefully propitiated, that virtuous woman
received a divine mantra for summoning the gods for the sake of sons.
Then one day, standing on the palace roof and endowed with fresh youth,
she summoned the thousand-rayed Sun in order to test the truth of the mantra.
As soon as he was meditated upon, the blessed one came visibly to that beautiful woman
and said, "Here I am," his restless, shining earrings swinging.
Hearing this, the embarrassed girl addressed him with folded hands,
<s>Kuntī</s>, also known as <s>Pṛthā</s>, her girdle jingling as she trembled.
For the sake of testing the sage's mantra, O blessed one, I meditated upon you.
Be gracious, ocean of compassion; forgive this childish impulsiveness.
Thus addressed by <s>Kuntī</s>, <s>Bhāskara</s>, whose sight is unfailing, said:
I have come for your sake; enjoy union with me, lovely-smiling one.

children.text: tvayā saha kuraṅgākṣi saṃgamo me prasādanam
children.translated_text: Doe-eyed one, union with you is the satisfaction of my favor;
there is no greater humiliation than an invocation made fruitless.
Your refusal of union with me will bring fault; otherwise it will bring welfare.

children.text: ityarthitā sā bahuśo raviṇā saṃgamaṃ yayau ||
children.translated_text: Thus entreated many times by <s>Ravi</s>, she entered into union.
Then, through the boon of the Thousand-rayed one, without losing her maidenhood,
she gave birth to a son, <s>Karṇa</s>, bright with golden earrings.
Abandoned by her in the water as an infant, from fear of relatives and from shame,
he was taken up by the charioteer <s>Adhiratha</s>, together with the gold.
Then he was raised by his wife <s>Rādhā</s>, together with that wealth;
because he had been obtained with riches, that splendid boy came to be named <s>Vasuṣeṇa</s>.
At the time of his worship of the Sun, there was nothing that he would not give,
for he was endowed with prowess and knowledge of every weapon and missile.
Then <s>Pāṇḍu</s>, the beloved, won that king's daughter <s>Kuntī</s>, lotus-eyed,
at her svayaṃvara, in the assembly of kings.
And the son of <s>Ambālikā</s> obtained <s>Mādrī</s>, the beauty-streaming daughter of the king of <s>Madra</s>,
with the bride-price given by <s>Devavrata</s>.
Sporting with those two women of restless eyes, the lord of the earth

children.text: prītyā ratyā ca sahito manobhava ivābabhau ||
children.translated_text: shone like <s>Manobhava</s> accompanied by <s>Prīti</s> and <s>Rati</s>.

children.text: sa jitvā dikṣu bhūpālānkaraṃ prāpya dhanurdharaḥ
children.translated_text: Then that archer conquered the kings in the directions and received tribute;
he attained equality with <s>Yayāti</s>, <s>Śaryāti</s>, <s>Nṛga</s>, and <s>Nābhāga</s>.
<s>Bhīṣma</s> brought the mixed-caste daughter of King <s>Devaka</s>
and gave her to <s>Vidura</s> for the increase of the lineage.
Meanwhile <s>Gāndhārī</s>, the faithful beloved of <s>Dhṛtarāṣṭra</s>, because of the fulfilled word,
carried her pregnancy for a pair of years.
Desiring sons, and after carrying the pregnancy for so long, she became jealous
and repeatedly struck her own belly with her fists.
Then the royal queen gave birth to a lump of flesh, compact like a stone,
as if it were made of sorrow and distress.
Then, at <s>Vyāsa</s>'s word, that lump was sprinkled with cold water;
from the pregnancy beaten by fists it became one more than a hundred.
Those portions, each only the size of a thumb-joint, were kept in jars of ghee;
separated, in time they became children of lovely brilliance.
The eldest of them was <s>Duryodhana</s>, and then came <s>Duḥśāsana</s> and the others,
with <s>Vikarṇa</s> and <s>Duḥśala</s> foremost; and <s>Duḥśalā</s> alone was a daughter.
And among the offspring of <s>Dhṛtarāṣṭra</s>, <s>Yuyutsu</s> too was born as a son.
When they were born, a dreadful succession of evil omens arose.
But <s>Pāṇḍu</s>, fond of hunting, an archer and hero, roaming in the forest,
struck with arrows a sage in the form of a deer, absorbed in mating.
As his life was ending in union with his beloved, the sage cursed him:
O king, may you too, like this, become the cause of my untimely death.
Thus cursed by the chief sage, <s>Pāṇḍu</s> was struck by the fire of grief.

children.text: tyaktvā rājyaṃ vane tasthau brahmacārī vadhūsakhaḥ
children.translated_text: Abandoning the kingdom, he stayed in the forest as a celibate, with his wives as companions;
with his two beloved wives he went to the ascetic grove of <s>Śataśṛṅga</s>.
His mind became clear with the nectar of tranquility and contentment.
Once, in a lonely place, troubled by thought, he said to <s>Kuntī</s>:
Even for a sacrificer, beautiful one, the path to heaven depends upon a son;
therefore produce for me a <s>kṣetraja</s> (field-born, legally begotten) son, princess.
In former times, kings born in a kṣatriya field from brāhmaṇas are heard of;

children.text: iti patyurvacaḥ śrutvā kuntī prāha sulocanā ||
children.translated_text: hearing her husband's words, lovely-eyed <s>Kuntī</s> said:
This is not proper for me, O king; even in thought I

children.text: na cintayāmi putro me tvatta eva bhaviṣyati ||
children.translated_text: do not consider anyone other than you. My son will come from you alone.

children.text: vyuṣitāśvaḥ purā rājā pauravo yajvanāṃ varaḥ
children.translated_text: Long ago there was a <s>Paurava</s> king named <s>Vyuṣitāśva</s>, best of sacrificers;
always devoted to his beloved, he wasted away through consumption.

children.text: taṃ vyasuṃ rājamahiṣī bhadrā nāma manaḥpriyam
children.translated_text: His royal queen, named <s>Bhadrā</s>, dear to his heart, did not abandon that lifeless beloved;
lamenting, she was intent on going with him, sharing his fate.
As that devoted wife embraced her beloved for a long time and grieved,
a voice born from the sky said to her: <s>Bhadrā</s>, with this lifeless man
unite in secret, fortunate one; you will obtain sons.
Hearing that command from the sky, the truthful woman did as instructed;
from the king she obtained three <s>Śālva</s> and four <s>Madra</s> sons.
Thus, O king, for chaste women whose thought is fixed on no other, the husband is the deity.
Hearing this speech of <s>Kuntī</s>, <s>Pāṇḍu</s> spoke again:
This is indeed so, just as you say; blessed are you, lotus-eyed one.
In former times women were unrestricted among men of their own varṇa and common to all;
therefore all people were without hostility.
<s>Auddālaka</s> <s>Śvetaketu</s>, in a secluded place, saw his mother
being drawn away by the hand by an unfamiliar twice-born man.
Angered, he established for women the rule of the vow to one husband.
But by the husband's command, there is no fault for them in union with another man.
In former times the chaste <s>Madayantī</s>, at the command of her husband <s>Kalmāṣapāda</s>,
obtained from <s>Vasiṣṭha</s> a son named <s>Aśmaka</s>.

children.text: rājño vicitravīryasya vayaṃ ca kṣetrajāḥ sutāḥ
children.translated_text: And we are <s>kṣetraja</s> sons of King <s>Vicitravīrya</s>;
therefore, beloved of the king, you ought to carry out my word.

children.text: ityākarṇya vaco bhartuḥ prāha kuntī natānanā
children.translated_text: Hearing her husband's words, <s>Kuntī</s>, her face bent down, said,
her sidelong eyes contracted with shame.
Formerly I propitiated the sage <s>Durvāsas</s> and obtained from him
a mantra flashing with abundant power, whose sure fruit is the summoning of the gods.
With this mantra, daughter, after summoning the best of the gods,
you will obtain sons as you wish; so the sage said to me.

children.text: sāhaṃ kaṃ devam āhvāya tvadājñākāriṇī vibho
children.translated_text: So which god shall I summon, obeying your command, lord,
so that, with a son in my lap, I may fulfill your intention?

children.text: iti rājñyā vacaḥ śrutvā prahṛṣṭaḥ pāṇḍurabravīt
children.translated_text: Hearing these words of the queen, <s>Pāṇḍu</s> rejoiced and said:
Among the dwellers in heaven, <s>Dharma</s> is the best, O woman of excellent face;
therefore summon <s>Dharma</s>, goddess, and obtain a son.
Hearing that, the royal queen, firm in her vow, meditated on the mantra;
united with <s>Dharma</s> in yogic form, she conceived.
Then in due time <s>Kuntī</s> gave birth to a son of great brilliance,
like the glory of victory giving birth to an empire, worthy of honor from all kings.
This is <s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s>, son of <s>Dharma</s>, eldest among those who uphold <s>dharma</s> (righteous order);
when he was born, such a speech of sky-going beings arose in the heavens.
Then <s>Pāṇḍu</s> said to his wife: Kings in whom strength is foremost are supreme;
summon the god <s>Māruta</s> and obtain a powerful son.
Hearing, "So be it," <s>Kuntī</s>, from <s>Samīraṇa</s>, the breath of the world,
obtained a second boy, born after the interval of a year.
That child, fallen from his mother's lap because of fear of a tiger,
with limbs compact as a thunderbolt, broke a stone into pieces.
This one, named <s>Bhīmasena</s>, has been born with terrible valor;
so <s>Sarasvatī</s>, deep in tone, thundered in the sky.
On the very day when mighty <s>Duryodhana</s>, son of <s>Dhṛtarāṣṭra</s>, was born,

children.text: tasmin eva sa kaunteyo bhīmakarmā vṛkodaraḥ ||
children.translated_text: that son of <s>Kuntī</s>, <s>Vṛkodara</s> of fearful deeds, was born as well.

children.text: tataḥ pāṇḍuḥ kṣaṇaṃ dhyātvā smṛtvā śakraṃ divaukasām
children.translated_text: Then <s>Pāṇḍu</s>, after thinking for a moment and remembering <s>Śakra</s>,
lord of the heaven-dwellers, again instructed his beloved for the obtaining of that god's son.
By fierce asceticism, together with his wife, <s>Pāṇḍu</s> himself
satisfied the lord of the gods within a year and obtained a vision of him.
Told directly by the foe of <s>Bala</s>, "I shall give you a son,"
he stood joyful and disciplined, intent on the increase of his own lineage.
Then, from <s>Śatakratu</s>, summoned by the mantra, <s>Kuntī</s> obtained

children.text: putraṃ hi tejasāṃ rāśiṃ devaṃ sūryamivāditiḥ ||
children.translated_text: a son, a mass of splendors, just as <s>Aditi</s> obtained the god <s>Sūrya</s>.
This is <s>Arjuna</s>, son of the lord of the gods, equal to him in valor;
so a voice came forth from the sky at the birth of <s>Vijaya</s>.
The women of heaven danced, and companies of <s>Gandharvas</s> sang;
at the birth of the son of <s>Jambhāri</s>, the dwellers in <s>Nandana</s> rejoiced.

children.text: tato bhartrārthitā kuntī mādrī mantraṃ dadau rahaḥ
children.translated_text: Then <s>Kuntī</s>, requested by her husband, gave the mantra secretly to <s>Mādrī</s>,
and said, "For you, this gives the fruit of one invocation."
Then, after reflecting, she made a single invocation of the two <s>Aśvins</s>;
who is able to set a limit to the cleverness of skilful minds?

children.text: suṣuve yamajau kāle tato mādrī tayoḥ sutau
children.translated_text: Thereafter, in due time, <s>Mādrī</s> gave birth to twin sons of those two,
like insight forming discernment from what is heard and half-heard.
With the syllable-garland of the names <s>Nakula</s> and <s>Sahadeva</s>,
those two boys, by their new arrival, made it as if moist with nectar.
In ascetic groves, among sages who performed vows suitable for royalty,
<s>Pāṇḍu</s> shone with those five sons as a mantra shines with its five limbs.
Meanwhile spring became the minister of victorious King <s>Manmatha</s>, the stage-manager of the new drama of broken love-play,
the moonrise over the milk-ocean made of the women of passion's quarter for doe-eyed women.
Under its power the <s>aśoka</s> tree, excited by the fall of the lotus feet of playful women with tinkling anklets and by fresh passion,
became thrilled in a succession of blossoms; there blessed bodiless <s>Anaṅga</s> was the authority.
When that childhood friend of <s>Manmatha</s> was opening forth, that teacher of play, the season whose matted locks were networks of bees,
<s>Mādrī</s>, her body intent on gathering flowers, wandered among the branches with eyes restless as young deer.
Then that moon among kings saw his beloved, moon-beautiful of face, a victory-banner of the flower-weaponed god,
and at the mere sight, his passion, made to leaf by spring, blossomed; <s>Madana</s> in him flowered, complete with arrows.
Then the wish-fulfilling tree of love for the joy of the Kurus, its foot planted on the slope of her hips, in the bed of passion, with eye-leaves rolling playfully,
bearing her shining breasts as fruits, performed all the sport of repose.
Though <s>Pāṇḍu</s>'s mind was restrained by the bond of the curse, he drank in his beloved with the shell-cups of his eyes;
for the command of King <s>Kāma</s>, contrary yet compliant, takes deepest hold on what is forbidden.
Then, gently addressed by her beloved, her lotus face sprouting moonlight-white rays moist with a smile,

children.text: roddhuṃ śaśāka na manaḥ prasṛtaṃ priyasya ko vā vidhātṛcaritaṃ parimārṣṭumīśaḥ ||
children.translated_text: she could not restrain his mind as it rushed forth; who can wipe away the deed of fate?
Wrapping her with the edge of his garment, and checking his mind because of the discipline meant to quiet the curse, he embraced her firmly,
though, as if in fear, the creepers forbade him with leaf-hands shaken by the confused humming of swarms of bees.
Embracing her, whose cheeks were full and bristling with horripilation, whose lovely eyes were long like opening blue lotuses,

children.text: unmādinīṃ sapadi madranarendraputrīṃ kelīpalāśaśayanaṃ vijane nināya ||
children.translated_text: he at once led the maddened daughter of the <s>Madra</s> king to a secluded bed of <s>palāśa</s> leaves for love-play.
Then, his half-closed eyes tasting the pleasure of touch,
the king gave up his life, brought under the power of the twice-born man's curse.
When he had gone to heaven, <s>Mādrī</s> suddenly entered the fire of grief,
as if to learn the strength of the funeral fire that was yet to come.
Then <s>Kuntī</s> came there, saw that, and heard the account of it;
grieving and with her mind set on dying, she said to <s>Mādrī</s>:
Blessed are you, <s>Mādrī</s>, for for you, with the delighted lord of the earth,
there was the festival of embrace, the lap of auspicious passion.
Rise up; protect the sons. I shall follow my husband.
Hearing this speech of <s>Kuntī</s>, the daughter of the <s>Madra</s> king said:
Noble lady, this lord of the earth, with his eyes fixed upon my face,
has gone to the abode of the gods as if unsated with pleasures.
How can I, a faithful wife, be able to abandon that loving husband,
the companion of delight to my eyes, when he has gone alone to the other world?

children.text: svaputranirviśeṣau tu pālyau me tanayau tvayā
children.translated_text: But my two sons should be protected by you as no different from your own sons.
Having said this, the wide-eyed woman fell at <s>Kuntī</s>'s feet.
Then, somehow entrusting <s>Pṛthā</s> with the care of the sons,
and at once arranging the beauty of her dress as though for a wedding,
<s>Mādrī</s> entered the fire, embracing the king.
Truly, in the burning heat of grief, the funeral fire is cold as snow.
When <s>Pāṇḍu</s> had gone to heaven, the sages dwelling on <s>Śataśṛṅga</s>
brought <s>Kuntī</s>, together with her sons, to <s>Hastināpura</s>.
Coming at once, they reported to the <s>Kurus</s> the account of <s>Pāṇḍu</s>,
the birth of his sons, and <s>Mādrī</s>'s following of her husband.
After placing the princes, as a deposit entrusted to <s>Dhṛtarāṣṭra</s>
and quickly to their grandsire as well, they went away to the ascetic forest.
When <s>Pāṇḍu</s>'s body had been ritually prepared by <s>Vidura</s> together with <s>Bhīṣma</s>,
with <s>Mādrī</s> as his companion, the townspeople fainted from that grief.
Then the blessed sage <s>Kṛṣṇadvaipāyana</s>,

children.text: vijane jananīṃ prāha satyāṃ satyanidhiḥ svayam ||
children.translated_text: himself a treasure of truth, met his mother <s>Satyavatī</s> and spoke to her in private:
The time whose happiness is now only to be remembered has passed; this tainted time has arrived.
The sin of the world grows like a wasting fever in an old man.
This earth, lovely only in the past and with the circle of her virtues destroyed,

children.text: na bhāti bhūḥ saṃkucitā padminīva himāhatā ||
children.translated_text: does not shine, shrunk like a lotus struck by frost.
Therefore, mother, resort to the ascetic forest together with your daughters-in-law;
when times have dried up their happiness, renunciation is an undecaying nectar.

children.text: iti vyāsavacaḥ śrutvā gatvā satyavatī vanam
children.translated_text: Hearing <s>Vyāsa</s>'s words, <s>Satyavatī</s> went to the forest,
and, together with her daughters-in-law, attained the supreme state through ascetic yoga.
Then that group of one hundred and one mighty princes of the king,
growing up together and mingled with the <s>Pāṇḍavas</s>, went on.
The eldest of them was <s>Duryodhana</s>, always of the same age as <s>Bhīma</s>;
in children's games he could not endure the son of the Wind, who was bold.
When they were intent on gathering fruit and had climbed trees, <s>Vṛkodara</s>
mounted the base of the tree and made them fall with his foot.
In water games, taking all of them swiftly in his arms,
he submerged them for a long time, so that in a moment they were nearly lifeless.
Then <s>Suyodhana</s>, defeated in the children's games along with his younger brothers,
adopted a crooked design, overwhelmed by the torment of anger.
At <s>Pramāṇakoṭi</s>, while <s>Bhīma</s> slept, he bound him, covered him with snakes,
and threw him into the water; the power of fools leads only to harm.
With utter ease he killed <s>Duryodhana</s>'s beloved charioteer,
with a backhand blow, his face crooked as he half-yawned in sleepiness.
Then <s>Vṛkodara</s> awoke and tore apart the snakes whose fangs had been broken by biting.

children.text: cicheda tadruṣā tasmai viṣānnaṃ kauravo dadau ||
children.translated_text: Angered at that, the <s>Kaurava</s> gave him poisoned food.
When the poison had been digested, the tree of anger among them grew;
its fruit appeared as the destruction of all the kings of the earth.
Again, in former times, when <s>Śaradvata</s>, son of <s>Gautama</s>, was practicing asceticism,
<s>Vṛtrahā</s>, afraid, sent a maiden of the gods to obstruct him.
Seeing her, named <s>Jalapadī</s>, with eyes like blooming lotuses,
that sage, his firmness shaken off by desire, emitted his seed.
From that seed, fallen on a clump of reeds, an excellent pair
was born in time, furnished with a black antelope skin and marked with arrows.
The boy and the girl, while their minds were set on hunting,

children.text: gṛhītau tau kṛpārdreṇa rājñā śantanunā vanāt ||
children.translated_text: were taken from the forest by King <s>Śantanu</s>, whose heart was softened with compassion.
Raised with kindness by the king and fit for brahmanical and divine vows,

children.text: kṛpaḥ kṛpī ca tau nāmnā loke khyātau babhūvatuḥ ||
children.translated_text: they became known in the world by the names <s>Kṛpa</s> and <s>Kṛpī</s>.
That <s>Kṛpa</s> became the teacher of the sons of <s>Pāṇḍu</s> and of the <s>Kurus</s>,
like <s>Jāmadagnya</s>, fully skilled in the knowledge of weapons and missiles.
Long ago <s>Bharadvāja</s>, seeing <s>Ghṛtācī</s>, a celestial beauty,
while walking in the sacrificial storehouse, placed his fallen seed in a jar.
From that was born the sage's son <s>Droṇa</s>, best of those who know the Veda,
who received the supreme fiery missile from the sage <s>Agniveśa</s>.

children.text: sa prāpa gautamīṃ bhāryāṃ kṛpasya bhaginīṃ kṛpīm
children.translated_text: He obtained as wife <s>Kṛpī</s>, the <s>Gautama</s> woman, sister of <s>Kṛpa</s>,
and in her he begot as his own son the hero <s>Aśvatthāman</s>.
When born, the strong one cried out loudly and loudly, like <s>Uccaiḥśravas</s>;
because he had the strength of a divine horse, he therefore became <s>Aśvatthāman</s>.
Then <s>Droṇa</s>, a householder with a son, desiring wealth,
went to <s>Rāma Jāmadagnya</s>, who tirelessly poured out riches.
<s>Bhārgava</s>, having given the earth to <s>Kaśyapa</s> and all his wealth away,
was going to the shore of the ocean when he addressed <s>Droṇa</s>, who had arrived.
Only my body remains; take the weapons as your teacher's fee.
For I am <s>Bhārgava</s>; I cannot bear to see the face of an afflicted man turned away.
Having said this, the mighty one gave him the lore of withdrawal, together with its secret vow,
and the whole <s>Dhanurveda</s> (science of archery), interwoven with the collection of vidyās and weapons.
After obtaining the divine weapons, he went to the king who had been his childhood friend,
to <s>Drupada</s> the <s>Pāñcāla</s>, son of <s>Pṛṣata</s>, seeking wealth.
For formerly, when he was a prince, he had spoken to him in childhood,
saying, as a matter of youthful desire, "When I have obtained the kingdom, I will give you half the kingdom."

children.text: tatsmṛtvā prāpya taṃ droṇo vayasyaṃ pārṣataṃ nṛpam
children.translated_text: Remembering this, <s>Droṇa</s> reached his friend, King <s>Pārṣata</s>,
and, simple-hearted, said, "Friend, give me that half of the kingdom."

children.text: taṃ prāha drupado brahmanmūrkho 'si bata mandadhīḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Drupada</s> said to him, "Brahmin, you are a fool, alas, dull-minded.

children.text: na lajjase kathaṃ rājā tava bhikṣābhujaḥ sakhā ||
children.translated_text: How are you not ashamed? How can a king be the friend of you, who live on alms?
A bond of friendship is fitting among men equal in honor, family, character,
wealth, knowledge, and mind; where the opposite holds, it is only for laughter."
Thus rejected by <s>Drupada</s>, <s>Droṇa</s> went to <s>Gajāhvaya</s>,
and, desiring the post of teacher to the <s>Kauravas</s>, stayed in <s>Kṛpa</s>'s house.
Meanwhile, those princes, delighting in play in a secluded place,
could not recover a ball that had fallen into a well, though they gathered closely around.
<s>Droṇa</s> pierced it with a handful of reeds arranged in a chain,
drew out the ball, and gave it to them as they were filled with wonder.

children.text: te tasya dṛṣṭvā tatkarma bhīṣmāyaitya nyavedayan
children.translated_text: Seeing that deed of his, they went and reported it to <s>Bhīṣma</s>;
then <s>Devavrata</s> made him the guru of all the princes.
Accepting those pupils, and kings from many regions as well,
he always showed affection for <s>Arjuna</s> greater than for his own son.
<s>Rādheya</s>, the charioteer's son, also entered his pupilship,
constantly competing with <s>Savyasācin</s> in the arts of weapons.
But <s>Arjuna</s> applied supreme effort to mastering archery;
eating at night when the lamp had gone out, he took his mouth as his lamp.
Thinking that everything could be accomplished by practice, he practiced in complete darkness,
so that he became skilled in striking a target by sound.
Hearing the twang of his bowstring, <s>Droṇa</s> came to him, delighted,

children.text: tamāha tvatsamaḥ śiṣyo nānyo mama bhaviṣyati ||
children.translated_text: and said, "No other pupil equal to you will be mine."
Then one day in private, to <s>Droṇa</s>, foremost of all bowmen,
came the illustrious son of <s>Hiraṇyadhanvan</s>, lord of the <s>Niṣādas</s>.
Wise <s>Ekalavya</s> said, "Teach me; I have come as your pupil."
But <s>Bhāradvāja</s>, recognizing, "This man is a <s>dāsa</s>," did not accept him.
He went away, made a clay image of <s>Droṇa</s>, and, full of faith, worshipped it constantly;
then he practiced weapons by himself, through which he became the best of bowmen.
Then once, when the <s>Pāṇḍavas</s> had gone out for training in the forest,
they saw a hound whose mouth had been filled with seven arrows.
Asking themselves, "Whose lightness of hand is this?" they searched for him,
and then saw <s>Ekalavya</s>, disciplined in his vows, the foremost of bowmen.
Questioned by them, he said with a smile, "I am <s>Droṇa</s>'s pupil."
When <s>Arjuna</s> heard that, he went to his teacher and said,
"Ah, you have a bow-bearing pupil better than I am."
Hearing this, <s>Droṇa</s> went to that son of the <s>Niṣāda</s> chief,
met him, and again spoke to him as he bowed with folded hands:
"If you are my pupil, quickly let a teacher's fee be given."
The <s>Niṣāda</s> prince said to him, "I am blessed; let it be accepted."
Then the guru asked him for his right thumb as the teacher's fee,

children.text: dadau ca taṃ nikṛtyāsmai nirvikārānano 'tha saḥ ||
children.translated_text: and he cut it off and gave it to him, his face showing no change.

children.text: pratiyāte tato droṇe yāti kāle dhanurbhṛtām
children.translated_text: After <s>Droṇa</s> had gone back, as time passed among the bowmen,
<s>Arjuna</s> became superior among thousands of royal princes.
Once the pot-born teacher set up a lofty bird as the target,
and said to his pupils, "What do you see here?"

children.text: te prāhurbhāsamakhilaṃ paśyāmaḥ svaṃ ca kārmukam
children.translated_text: They said, "We see the whole bird and our own bow."
"I see nothing except the bird's neck," said <s>Arjuna</s>.

children.text: tataḥ pārthaṃ pariṣvajya śaraṃ muñceti sādaram
children.translated_text: Then <s>Droṇa</s> embraced <s>Pārtha</s> and respectfully said, "Release the arrow."
And <s>Arjuna</s> cut off that bird's neck.
Then one day in the <s>Gaṅgā</s>, a powerful crocodile, like an elephant,
seized <s>Droṇa</s> by the thigh as he was preparing to bathe.
The circle of pupils, urged by him to rescue him at once,
looked this way and that and could not decide on the action to take.
The son of <s>Śakra</s> killed the crocodile with five arrows;
then the guru, pleased, gave him the <s>Brahmaśiras</s> weapon.
When all the sons of kings and royal men had acquired the science,
King <s>Dhṛtarāṣṭra</s>, on a stage constructed by craftsmen,
together with <s>Kṛpa</s>, <s>Bhīṣma</s>, and the others at their head, and with all the women of the inner palace,
went, at the guru's word, to see the princes' mastery of weapons.
Then <s>Droṇa</s>, moon-bright, entered the arena filled with spectators,
wearing two garments bright as the water of the <s>Gaṅgā</s>.
Together with <s>Aśvatthāman</s>, he shone, a treasury of brilliance,
like the three-eyed god himself with mighty <s>Skanda</s>.
Entering, those princes, through the lightness of their weapon-skill,
formed garlands of spectators at the edges, as if set down in a painting.
Then, their mighty circles of motion displayed through mutual rivalry,
<s>Bhīmasena</s> and <s>Suyodhana</s>, clubs in hand, entered.
The two proud men, with the ocean rising up, as it were, through the spectators' eager cries,
the son of <s>Droṇa</s>, at his teacher's word, restrained with his two arms.
<s>Vidura</s> described to the sightless <s>Dhṛtarāṣṭra</s>
that variety of their weapons, and also to <s>Kuntī</s> and the daughter of <s>Subala</s>.
Then, checking the tumultuous roar with a signal of his finger,
<s>Bhāradvāja</s>, his eyes widened with joy, spoke:
Now let <s>Pārtha</s> be seen, dearer to me than my own son;
I think even <s>Kārtavīryārjuna</s> would be ashamed in rivalry with him.
When the pot-born one had spoken thus, <s>Śvetavāhana</s> entered,
long-armed to the knees, heroic, dark in complexion, and lotus-eyed.
By the power of his divine weapons, creating fire, water, and wind,
he moved about in the arena, garlanded by the lotus-like glances of the city women.
Seeing the wondrous divine power of the crowned <s>Arjuna</s> there,
the <s>Kurus</s> too, greatly excited, displayed their training in weapons.
Then there arose outside a deep and solemn sound,
like the rumble of a rain-cloud, produced by the slapping of arms.
Because of it, among the spectators whose eyes were fixed on the doorway
and whose faces were lifted, wondering 'What is this?', there was a strange agitation of curiosity.
Then, resembling a golden palm tree, splendid, with a beautiful circular halo,
making the quarters tawny with the rays from the jewels of his shining armor,
like a second sun, a storehouse of mighty splendors,
<s>Karṇa</s>, lotus-eyed and foremost among bowmen, entered.
He bowed to <s>Kṛpa</s> and <s>Droṇa</s>, his earrings trembling with careless ease,
and, with disdain, performed a feat indistinguishable from <s>Arjuna</s>'s divine weapons.
Then <s>Suyodhana</s>, his body sprouting horripilation from the joy of seeing him,
first addressed him affectionately and formed a friendship with him.
Then, as <s>Karṇa</s> and <s>Pārtha</s>, whose enmity had arisen from persistent rivalry,
began a duel, a new excitement arose.
Seeing the two sons of <s>Śakra</s> and the Sun themselves ready to fight,
<s>Kuntī</s>, who knew the hidden matter of her son's story, fainted.
Seeing the two ready to fight, <s>Kṛpa</s>, the teacher of archery, said:

children.text: samaiḥ sakhyaṃ ca yuddhaṃ ca bhāratānāṃ kulavratam ||
children.translated_text: Friendship and battle between equals are the family rule of the <s>Bhāratas</s>.
<s>Arjuna</s>, heir of <s>Pāṇḍu</s> and ornament of the <s>Kuru</s> line,
ought not to fight with one whose family and conduct are unknown, and who is not a king.
Hearing this speech of <s>Kṛpa</s>, <s>Karṇa</s>, somewhat downcast,
proud though he was, scratched the ground, his eyes closing in shame.

children.text: tato duryodhanaḥ prāha guro yuktaṃ na bhāṣase
children.translated_text: Then <s>Duryodhana</s> said: Teacher, you do not speak rightly.
If excellence lies in virtues, what is the use of examining outward form?
By learning, strength of arm, austerity, fame, and prosperity,
men of achievement, endowed with virtues, create families worthy of name.
And as for what was said, 'He is not a king,' let the teacher hear my answer there.
Those glanced upon by Fortune quickly attain universal sovereignty.
This <s>Karṇa</s> has been made by me lord of the region of <s>Aṅga</s>;
for one with such a body, what wonder would there be even in kingship over the gods?
Having spoken thus, with jeweled pitchers, with parched grain, flowers, and water,
he consecrated him, placed a turban on him as he sat on a golden throne, and made him king.
Then, fanned by white yak-tail fans waved by the hands of beautiful women,
he shone like a lotus pond filled with royal swans.
On his head a white parasol, bright as the moon, shone,
as though his fame, wheeling in the sky, had playfully formed a circle.
Meanwhile the charioteer <s>Adhiratha</s>, worn out by old age and trembling, came in to see his son,
stumbling, his hand busy with a staff.
When he cried 'Son!' from afar, drenched with tears of joy,
<s>Karṇa</s>, bound with his new diadem, then bowed down to him.
Recognizing, 'This is a charioteer,' <s>Bhīma</s>, with a smiling face, said:

children.text: aho nu citraṃ rādheya spardhase savyasācinā ||
children.translated_text: Ah, what a wonder, <s>Rādheya</s>, that you compete with <s>Savyasācin</s>!
Be ready instead, well trained, for the duties of driving a chariot;
for a cat's imitation of a lion is not becoming.
Hearing this, <s>Karṇa</s> sighed and looked toward the sun;
and, springing up in anger at that, the hero <s>Suyodhana</s> said:
For a warrior whose power is bold in battle, who is heroic and strong,
wise and accomplished in learning, this is no time to investigate his roots.
Fire is born from water, and <s>Kārttikeya</s> too from Fire;

children.text: gūḍhaṃ hi mahatāṃ janma paricchettuṃ ka īśvaraḥ ||
children.translated_text: indeed, the birth of great men is hidden. Who has the power to determine it?

children.text: pārtha yūyaṃ yathā jātāḥ kiṃ tena kathitena vā
children.translated_text: And how you <s>Pārthas</s> were born, what need is there to tell that?
For everyone, it seems, is bold in pointing out another's faults.
When <s>Karṇa</s>, with earrings and armor, shines like the thousand-rayed sun,
whose mind could even be touched by the suspicion that he is merely human?
Or what is the use of these battles of words? If the fever of pride remains,
then let the arm be put to work with the fierce bow drawn into a circle.
When the people, agitated, heard this speech of <s>Duryodhana</s>,
the sun, kissing the peak of the western mountain, became deep red.
As the day, reddened by twilight, departed while a little darkness slowly spread,
it was flushed like a frown, as though angry in hostility toward the night-lotuses.
When lamps, like flower-buds adorning the ears of Lady Night,
had appeared on the royal road, making it golden-hued,
<s>Duryodhana</s> departed, playfully taking <s>Karṇa</s> by the hand.
together with his brothers, his jeweled bracelet ringing in excitement.
With affectionate eyes fixed on the lotus-face of <s>Dhanañjaya</s>,
<s>Bhīṣma</s>, <s>Droṇa</s>, <s>Kṛpa</s>, and the others went along with the <s>Pāṇḍavas</s>.
"Wonderful! <s>Bhīma</s> is astonishing; ah, <s>Arjuna</s> is a marvel,
and oh, <s>Duryodhana</s>!" So praising them, the people went away.
Then the teacher, in private, spoke to his pupils, beginning with <s>Arjuna</s>:
"A prince, the son of <s>Pṛṣata</s>, was formerly my friend.
In childhood he told me, 'I will give you half the kingdom.'

children.text: prāptarājyo mayā gatvā saralena sa yācitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: When he had obtained the kingdom, I went and guilelessly asked him for it.

children.text: na tulyo 'sīti me cakre nyakkāraṃ madaviplutaḥ
children.translated_text: Drunk with pride, he insulted me, saying, 'You are not my equal.'
For the great fire of anger against him, you, my pupils, are the rain-clouds.
Having said, 'All of you, make him bow,' the teacher slowly fell silent.
Then the princes, <s>Dhanañjaya</s> and the rest, went forth
and, having conquered <s>Drupada</s> with his followers at the head of battle,
quickly bound him, brought him back, and presented him to <s>Droṇa</s>.

children.text: sakhyaṃ punaḥ samādāya bhāradvājo mumoca tam
children.translated_text: The son of <s>Bharadvāja</s> renewed their friendship and released him.

children.text: sa hi droṇāya rājyārdham āhicchatrapuraṃ dadau ||
children.translated_text: For <s>Drupada</s> gave <s>Droṇa</s> half the kingdom, the city of <s>Ahicchatra</s>.

children.text: vinirjito raṇe rājā matvā droṇaṃ sudurjayam
children.translated_text: The king, defeated in battle, considered <s>Droṇa</s> very hard to overcome,
and fixed his desire on the birth of a son as a means of retaliation against him.
When <s>Duryodhana</s> learned that the sons of <s>Pṛthā</s>, rich in learning and valor,
had their virtues sung by the townspeople, he blazed with the fire of hatred.
With <s>Karṇa</s> and <s>Saubala</s> as his friends, he became consecrated to their humiliation;

children.text: babhūva viduro gūḍhaṃ tāndhiyaiva rarakṣa ca ||
children.translated_text: but <s>Vidura</s>, hidden from view, protected them by wisdom alone.
Seeing, from the people's affection, that the sons of <s>Pāṇḍu</s> were fit for the kingdom,
<s>Suyodhana</s> met <s>Dhṛtarāṣṭra</s> in private and said:
"Father, after winning over the subjects, <s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s>, with his younger brothers, seeks
the inheritance of <s>Pāṇḍu</s>, which has come within reach through effort, with a crooked mind.

children.text: na pauruṣeṇa na tyāgānna nītyā vā pṛthāsutāḥ
children.translated_text: Not by prowess, not by generosity, nor by policy, have the sons of <s>Pṛthā</s>

children.text: lokasya priyatāṃ yātāste puṇyaiḥ kiṃ tu kevalaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: become dear to the people; it is only through their merit.
When the <s>Pārthas</s> have obtained the kingdom, the rulers of the earth
will be under their control. Shame on us, father, living on their food!
A <s>caṇḍāla</s> beggar, marked by a broken bowl for leftovers, is fortunate;
not one whose crest bows down in begging among men of equal lineage.

children.text: te vayaṃ tava dāyādā māninaḥ pṛthivīpateḥ
children.translated_text: We are your heirs, high-spirited men, O lord of the earth;
we must not become despised. You should act so that this does not happen.
Better, amid rough places at the edge of a village overrun by packs of dogs,
is the praiseworthy life of a jackal than the life of one held in contempt.
Hearing this speech of <s>Duryodhana</s>, the son-loving
wise <s>Dhṛtarāṣṭra</s> reflected for a moment and began to speak:
"He, my younger brother <s>Pāṇḍu</s>, was elder in virtue;
the delighting of the subjects alone was the ornament of his kingship.
His son, beloved of the people, deserves the kingdom that is rightfully his;
for royal fortune born of the people's affection runs obediently after him.
The subjects, once honored by <s>Pāṇḍu</s> with gifts suited to their dignity,

children.text: na sahante prakṛtayaḥ pārthadrohaṃ na bāndhavāḥ ||
children.translated_text: and our kinsmen too, will not tolerate hostility toward the <s>Pārthas</s>."
Hearing his father's words, <s>Duryodhana</s> spoke again:
"Father, for just this reason every person is dependent on another.
At present wealth is in our hands; win over the subjects as <s>Pāṇḍu</s> did.
People always sell even their lives for riches as if they were straw.
For a little while, O king, send the <s>Pāṇḍavas</s> to <s>Vāraṇāvata</s>

children.text: visṛjya svāṃ śriyaṃ kartuṃ baddhamūlāṃ tvamarhasi ||
children.translated_text: to see the great festival, and you should make your own fortune firmly rooted.
<s>Bhīṣma</s>, our grandfather, I know, has adopted neutrality;
<s>Droṇa</s>'s son loves me, and because of him so do <s>Kṛpa</s> and <s>Droṇa</s>.
Only <s>Vidura</s>, concealed, is always a benefactor of the <s>Pārthas</s>;
he is a cause of suspicion for me, father. Let protection of our fortune be arranged."
Hearing that, the son of <s>Ambikā</s> accepted it, saying, 'So be it.'

children.text: bhavitavyatayā hanta buddhiḥ kasya na kṛṣyate ||
children.translated_text: Alas, whose understanding is not dragged away by destiny?
Then people set on by him praised, in the midst of the assembly,
the city of <s>Vāraṇāvata</s>, splendid with festivals day after day.
The king gradually perceived that the <s>Pāṇḍavas</s> were eager to see it,
and said, 'Go to see the great festival of the journey.'
Then the sons of <s>Pāṇḍu</s>, suspicious, took leave of their elders privately,
and, receiving their blessings, went to the city of <s>Vāraṇāvata</s>.
At that moment <s>Duryodhana</s> summoned the chief officer <s>Prarocana</s>
and spoke to him in secret, with joy and affection put forward first:
"Even fortunes, fickle as the sidelong glances of bold women,
remain long for kings through the careful employment of good ministers.
With you as my helper, I wish by stratagem to enjoy

children.text: bhoktumicchāmyupāyena tvaṃ hi me prathamā gatiḥ ||
children.translated_text: the earth with its thorns removed; for you are my foremost recourse.
Today, by the king <s>Vaicitravīrya</s>, the sons of <s>Pāṇḍu</s>
have been sent to <s>Vāraṇāvata</s> to see the great festival of the journey.
Going there with all speed, riding a mule,
secretly make for them a house of lac mixed with ghee.
When they have come to trust that place, together with <s>Kuntī</s>, then gradually
you must set fire to it at night, with the outer doors barred.
When <s>Duryodhana</s> had spoken thus, <s>Prarocana</s> was filled with joy;
promising, 'That shall be so,' he set out for <s>Vāraṇāvata</s>.
The citizens, with anxious minds, followed the departing sons of <s>Pāṇḍu</s>,
together with <s>Vidura</s>, censuring the lord of the earth.
When the circle of citizens had been turned back by the words of <s>Ajātaśatru</s>,
<s>Vidura</s>, though unasked, spoke as he was about to go back the opposite way:

children.text: yaḥ kāyakartanaṃ tīkṣṇaṃ vetti śastram alohajam
children.translated_text: "The man who understands the sharp, non-iron weapon that cuts the body,

children.text: śiśirapratipakṣaṃ ca kakṣaghnaṃ na sa hanyate ||
children.translated_text: and the enemy of cold, the burner of thickets, is not slain.
Even when the foe of cold has grown strong, there is no fear for those who dwell in a hole;
nothing is inaccessible to men with eyes, and there is no misfortune for the steadfast.
A traveler comes to know the country; he knows the directions by the stars.
A wise man, always master of his senses, is not overpowered by others."
Having said this, <s>Vidura</s> quickly departed, his eyes filled with tears;
<s>Kuntī</s> asked <s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s>, "What was that?"
"The burner of thickets is the blessed fire; the non-iron weapon is poison.
He said by those words, 'This must be understood,'" replied the righteous son.
Then all of them, adorned, entered <s>Vāraṇāvata</s>
on the eighth day under <s>Rohiṇī</s>, in the bright half of <s>Phālguna</s>.

children.text: tatra taiḥ pūjitāḥ pauraiḥ pūjayanto dvijottamān
children.translated_text: There, honored by the citizens and themselves honoring the best of brahmins,
they stayed happily for ten nights, while festivals had been arranged by <s>Prarocana</s>.
Then, at <s>Prarocana</s>'s word, a house made by skilled craftsmen,
constructed of lac and ghee, was entered by the <s>Pāṇḍavas</s>.
Entering it and smelling its odor, the son of <s>Dharma</s> said to <s>Bhīma</s>,

children.text: idaṃ mandiramāgneyaṃ śaṅke naḥ śatrubhiḥ kṛtam ||
children.translated_text: "I suspect that this house is incendiary, made for us by our enemies.
Let us live right here, our appearance unobserved, guarding against trickery;
otherwise our enemies will strike us down with arrows by a secret punishment."
Having said this, <s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s> remained there for a long time in suspicion,
constantly examining the paths with his younger brothers under the guise of hunting.
Meanwhile, a digger sent by <s>Vidura</s> came there secretly
at night and reported the whole hidden situation to the <s>Pārthas</s>.
He made a well-covered tunnel, hard to detect, like a creeping serpent,
with winding and counter-winding steps and a long subterranean exit.
Then <s>Bhīma</s>, knowing that <s>Prarocana</s> was preparing to burn them,
himself set fire to the house with <s>Prarocana</s> inside it.
There, as the seven-flamed fire grew in the house ringed by flames,
and the people were distressed, alarmed by the smell of lac, ghee, and resin,
a <s>Niṣādī</s> woman, accompanied by her five sons and led on by loud chatter,
had come there to eat; by fate's power she was burned there.

children.text: kiṃ na dagdhā vayaṃ sarve dagdhapāṇḍavadarśinaḥ
children.translated_text: "Why have we all not burned, seeing the <s>Pāṇḍavas</s> burned?
Sinful <s>Suyodhana</s>, whose king they had, is a ruined murderer.

children.text: diṣṭyā ca sānubandho 'sau svayaṃ dagdhaḥ prarocanaḥ
children.translated_text: And fortunately <s>Prarocana</s> himself has burned, together with his associates."
Thus, with voices choked by tears, the citizens cried out in the night.
But <s>Bhīmasena</s>, like <s>Garuḍa</s>, went out through the tunnel,
taking his mother on his shoulder and the <s>Pārthas</s>, with <s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s>, in his arms.
With the sons of <s>Mādrī</s> in his lap, mighty <s>Bhīma</s> set out,
as though making the earth play at swinging by the impacts of his feet.
Then, believing that the sons of <s>Pāṇḍu</s> had been burned, those led by <s>Bhīṣma</s>
performed the water rite for them, grieving and full of tears.
Then on a lightless road, measuring the directions by the stars,

children.text: bhīmo gaṅgāṃ samuttīrya viveśa viṣamaṃ vanam ||
children.translated_text: <s>Bhīma</s> crossed the <s>Gaṅgā</s> and entered a rugged forest.
Placing <s>Kuntī</s> there beneath a banyan tree with her sons,
he went to bring water to remove their exhaustion.
Quickly, with his own upper garment, from a lake pointed out by swans,
he took water, returned, and saw his sons asleep.
He said, "Fortunes are without substance, as tremulous as elephants' ears,
since even these men lie here in the forest, using their arms as pillows."
Saying this, <s>Bhīmasena</s>, making that moment his watch,
stood awake and vigilant, scanning the directions.
At that time, in that forest, there was a constant dweller there,
a rākṣasa named <s>Hiḍimba</s>, whose appearance was like a cloud at the end of an age.
With his eye tawny like a mass of lightning, he made the quarters tawny,
as if tearing the world apart with the cavernous flames of his fangs.
Smelling the scent of humans, with the corners of his mouth dripping,
the night-roamer joyfully spoke at night to his sister <s>Hiḍimbā</s>:

children.text: jāne cireṇa me diṣṭaṃ dhātrā bhojanamīpsitam
children.translated_text: "I know that after a long time the Creator has assigned me the food I desired;
this fragrance of mortals truly delights my belly.
Go, look at these men who are not far away, and bring them here;
for I am longing to drink blood up to my throat."
Hearing her brother's words, the rākṣasa maiden went
and saw the <s>Pāṇḍavas</s> asleep and <s>Vṛkodara</s> awake.
Seeing him, lotus-eyed and like <s>Manmatha</s> made visible,
she became filled with desire and assumed a very charming form.
She had breasts like clusters and a red lower lip like a fresh shoot;
with lovely shape she was like a creeper shaken by the breeze of dalliance.
The forest ground shone with her sidelong-glancing eyes,
as if with peacock feathers fallen from circles of dancing peacocks.
Approaching slowly, broad-hipped and sweet-spoken,
she spoke to the son of the Wind, her eyes turned sidelong:
"Who are you, standing in this deserted place like sons of gods?
For this is a terrible forest, occupied by a terrible rākṣasa."
My brother, named <s>Hiḍimba</s>, has set out here to kill you.

children.text: tamahaṃ māyayā pāpaṃ vañcayāmi bhajasva mām ||
children.translated_text: I will deceive that wicked one by magic; accept me.

children.text: iṅgitajña svayaṃ viddhi mama bhāvaṃ bhavadgatam
children.translated_text: You who understand signs, know for yourself the feeling of mine that is fixed on you.
Wake these people; I will protect them by carrying them through the sky to another forest.
For, through love for a husband, a woman's own family side is mere grass.
Hearing her words, the son of the Wind spoke:
I will not, beautiful-browed one, like a coward, as if out of fear,
suddenly wake my brothers from their happy sleep, nor my mother either.
Let that poor night-roamer come, ripened by Time.
Let him learn the utterly terrible pain caused by the machine of my arms.
While this conversation was taking place there between <s>Hiḍimbā</s> and <s>Bhīmasena</s>,
that rākṣasa himself arrived, his palate and tongue quivering with terror.
From the sounds rising from the clashing mechanism of his fangs,
with smoky outbursts of fire, the quarters became disturbed.
Seeing them asleep and <s>Vṛkodara</s> awake,
and his sister with her eyes fixed on his face, he said this:
Ah, wicked woman! Through affection for humans you have forgotten my command.
I know that you too, together with these men, have gone to the house of <s>Yama</s>.
Having spoken thus, with beard and hair terrible with flames of fire,
<s>Hiḍimba</s> rose up to swallow <s>Hiḍimbā</s>, like Death at the fatal hour.
<s>Bhīmasena</s> said to him, laughing as if in sport:

children.text: naināmarhasi hantuṃ tvaṃ mayi jīvati rākṣasa ||
children.translated_text: You do not deserve to kill her, rākṣasa, while I am alive.
This beautiful-smiling, lotus-eyed woman was given to me
by the blessed <s>Kāma</s> himself, who dwells within all beings.
Having spoken thus, <s>Bhīmasena</s>, swollen and agitated with anger,
dragged him by force and seized him with both arms, heavy as a mountain.
When battle began between the two, and the earth was shaking,

children.text: prabuddhā sahasā kuntī saha putrairdadarśa tat ||
children.translated_text: <s>Kuntī</s>, suddenly awakened together with her sons, saw it.
Then, learning what had happened from <s>Hiḍimbā</s>'s words, <s>Pṛthā</s>
became somehow troubled in mind through love for her son.
Then <s>Arjuna</s> came up and addressed the son of the Wind:

children.text: jahi naktaṃcaraṃ bhīma yāvatsaṃdhyā na dṛśyate ||
children.translated_text: Kill the night-roamer, <s>Bhīma</s>, before twilight is seen.
For the night, dark like an old grove of palmyras, has grown worn out;
before the cruel moment comes, destroy the rākṣasa.
Or else, <s>Bhīma</s>, with arrows sharpened like the fangs of death,
I will make this chief of rākṣasas remember the terror of <s>Rāghava</s>.
Hearing <s>Phalguna</s>'s words, <s>Bhīma</s> said loudly, "Not so,"
and whirled the rākṣasa around hundreds of times.
Throwing him down violently, he crushed him on the ground,
his hideous body clattering as joints, vital parts, and bones split apart.

children.text: sa tena balinā gāḍhaṃ pīḍyamāno niśācaraḥ
children.translated_text: Being tightly pressed by that mighty one, the night-roamer
roared like <s>Mahiṣāsura</s> of old when overcome by <s>Durgā</s>.
As the vault of heaven was filled with his great roar,
the dwellers in heaven feared that an untimely dissolution had begun.
Then, with the gurgling of a throat bursting in billows of blood,
that rākṣasa went to death together with the darkness of night.
As the night was dwindling, the sky, red with dawn,
seemed to be filled everywhere with whirlpools of blood.
Then morning appeared, hard to look upon like a piśāca,
with a tawny beard and mane of matted hair spread wide by ruddy rays.
When he had been killed, <s>Vṛkodara</s> did not welcome that sister of his;
red-eyed with anger, he said, "Shame on cruel rākṣasas!"
Then <s>Hiḍimbā</s>, full-breasted and afraid that her purpose would be broken,

children.text: prayayau śaraṇaṃ kuntīṃ bhīmo māṃ bhajatāmiti ||
children.translated_text: went for refuge to <s>Kuntī</s>, saying, "Let <s>Bhīma</s> accept me."
Urged by his mother through her words, and by the son of <s>Dharma</s>,

children.text: divā samāgamaḥ kārya iti tāṃ saṃvidābhajat ||
children.translated_text: <s>Bhīma</s> accepted her under the agreement that their meeting was to be by day.
With her, in lovely regions of divine forests,
and on the slopes of <s>Kailāsa</s>, moving as suited her power,
among the lofty white lotuses of the <s>Mānasa</s> lakes of <s>Himavat</s>,
and on the peaks of <s>Malaya</s>, delightful with sandalwood,
<s>Bhīma</s>, enjoying that young woman, a doe with pearl-necklace eyes,
obtained the splendor of <s>Manobhava</s>, attended by <s>Rati</s>.
Then <s>Hiḍimbā</s> bore a son, <s>Ghaṭotkaca</s>, with a fearsome face;

children.text: asūta māyināṃ sadyaḥ prasūtiḥ kila rakṣasām ||
children.translated_text: for rākṣasa women skilled in magic are said to give birth at once.

children.text: tataḥ samāmantrya yayau bhīmaṃ sā kṣaṇadācarī
children.translated_text: Then that night-roaming woman took leave of <s>Bhīma</s> and went away;
for the unions of sky-going beings last only until the birth of a son.
Saying, "I should be remembered in matters of need,"
<s>Ghaṭotkaca</s> too went to the northern quarter, lovingly greeted by the <s>Pārthas</s>.
Then the sons of <s>Pāṇḍu</s>, crossing forests and the territories of kings,
went on, hidden in matted hair and bark garments.
On the road they saw <s>Kṛṣṇadvaipāyana</s>, a mass of brilliance,
with the leaf-buds of their joined hands pressed to the surfaces of their foreheads.
When compassionate <s>Kṛṣṇadvaipāyana</s> reassured her that <s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s>

children.text: āśvāsitā tena kuntī dhṛtiṃ lebhe manasvinī ||
children.translated_text: would obtain full sovereignty, high-minded <s>Kuntī</s> regained firmness of mind.
At his word, they entered the broad city of <s>Ekacakrā</s>
and stayed in a brāhmaṇa's dwelling, like fires in the guise of twice-born men.
"You must remain here without revealing yourselves, moving in concealment.
I will return after a month," said the sage, and he departed from them.

children.text: bhikṣānnaṃ te samāhṛtya sadā mātre nyavedayan
children.translated_text: Gathering food by begging, they always presented it to their mother.

children.text: tato 'rdhaṃ bhīmasenāya sarvebhyo 'rdhaṃ dadau ca sā ||
children.translated_text: Then she gave half to <s>Bhīmasena</s> and half to all the others.
Then one day, while they were dwelling happily in the house of those Brahmins,
<s>Kuntī</s> heard a piteous cry that tore the heart.
Hearing it and filled with compassion, she spoke to <s>Bhīma</s>, who stood before her,
as the excellent Brahmin looked at his son and his daughter in front of him:
"Alas, in this insubstantial saṃsāra, for embodied beings bound by the machinery of karma,
unions with loved ones arise only to tear the heart when separation comes.
Today one person from my house has been assigned by the king to the rākṣasa.
I cannot bear to abandon anyone, and the wise man must protect himself as well.
How can I, pitiless, abandon my wife, faithful in conduct and of one mind with me,
a companion fashioned by fate?
And this girl, appointed by the creator for some husband,
the future mother of my daughter's son: how could I be able to abandon her?
This boy, not yet speaking clearly, is a stream of delight to the heart;
if I perish, he will surely perish too when his means of life is cut off.

children.text: iti bruvāṇaṃ taṃ bhāryā provāca dhṛtiśālinī
children.translated_text: As he was speaking thus, his steadfast wife said to him,

children.text: samayo vihito dhātrā mamāyaṃ nyāyataḥ prabho
children.translated_text: "Lord, this turn has been assigned by the creator to me according to justice;
and for women, to die before one's husband is the strength of their blessings."
Hearing that, the girl spoke to her parents in a gentle voice:
"A girl must inevitably be given away by her people to someone.
Therefore abandon me alone today, and may there be welfare for you.

children.text: pituḥ saṃtāriṇī kanyā loke hyasminparatra ca ||
children.translated_text: For in this world and the next, a daughter carries her father across."
Hearing that, even the little boy spoke, lifting a club in his hand,
as the gleam of his new teeth seemed to spill out the milk he had drunk:
"With this rākṣasa-stick I myself will kill him."
Hearing the child's indistinct words, the women of the house wept.
Hearing their pitiable lament, <s>Kuntī</s>, distressed in mind,

children.text: dvijaṃ bāṣpākulaṃ kuntī śucaḥ papraccha kāraṇam ||
children.translated_text: asked the tear-choked Brahmin the cause of his grief.
"Even staking my life as the price, I shall carry you across from sorrow.
Take courage and tell me," she said.
The Brahmin replied to her, "Mother, this sorrow has no remedy.

children.text: idaṃ no vihitaṃ dhātrā tatra tvaṃ kiṃ kariṣyasi ||
children.translated_text: This has been ordained for us by the creator; what can you do there?
Here there dwells a night-roamer, dreadful in form, named <s>Baka</s>.

children.text: vāreṇa bhuṅkte paurāṇāmekaṃ sa puruṣaṃ sadā ||
children.translated_text: By turns he always eats one man from among the townspeople.
The king of <s>Vetrakīyagraha</s> constantly sends to him
a man together with a buffalo, and also a cart of food.
The wicked king is strong in taking wealth, but weak in giving protection;

children.text: mastakasthaṃ hi maraṇaṃ prajānāṃ duṣkṛtī nṛpaḥ ||
children.translated_text: indeed such a king is death standing upon the heads of his subjects.
This turn has now come to me, a resident of the royal domain.

children.text: astu janmāntare mātaḥ svasti vā darśanaṃ punaḥ ||
children.translated_text: May we see one another again in another birth, mother. Farewell."
Hearing this, <s>Kuntī</s> said, "Let your fear of the rākṣasa depart.
I shall send my own son to this great eater."
Hearing that, the Brahmin covered his ears and immediately said,
"Even to hear such words is not fitting for people like me.

children.text: aho bata nṛśaṃsānāṃ dhuri māṃ cakravartinam
children.translated_text: Ah, mother, you are preparing to make me the emperor at the head of the cruel.
Let this cease; it is improper.
Who, except an outcaste, would kill an ascetic Brahmin,
a guest come home from a distant country, for the sake of protecting his own life?"

children.text: iti vipravacaḥ śrutvā kuntī provāca sasmitā
children.translated_text: Hearing the Brahmin's words, <s>Kuntī</s> said with a smile,
"Brahmin, my son is perfected in mantra; he need not be pitied by you.
By the power of his knowledge he will surely destroy that rākṣasa.
You, unaware of his might, have spoken only out of compassion."
Hearing this, the Brahmin became delighted, and confidence slowly arose in him;
regarding her as a goddess, he accepted it, saying, "So be it."
Then <s>Kuntī</s>, making <s>Vṛkodara</s> of vast valor know the whole affair,
sent him forth, ready for the Brahmin's need.
<s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s> too, learning of it and fearing disgrace, said,
"Mother, it is not fitting for you to give up your son in order to save others."
Hearing his words, <s>Kuntī</s>, knowing <s>Bhīma</s>'s prowess, said,
"I have done this, son; now <s>dharma</s> alone is our course."
Hearing this, the heroic <s>Dharmanandana</s>, lover of Brahmins,
praised his mother, who was intent on the Brahmin's business, and said:
"Mother, your thought, worthy of true courage, brings us the highest joy.

children.text: gūḍhaṃ prayātu bhīmaśca yathā na jñāyate paraiḥ ||
children.translated_text: But let <s>Bhīma</s> go secretly, so that he is not known by others."
By that command, <s>Bhīma</s> took the cart filled with food
and went to <s>Baka</s>'s forest, crowded with hundreds of palāśa trees.
While eating that food, he saw there the night-roamer,
with hair and eyes blazing upward, like a motionless forest fire.
The rākṣasa too, seeing him eating without fear,
was filled with anger and astonishment and spoke like a roaring cloud:
"Hey! Fool, how can you eat my food as if you had no fear?
Or rather, those who have made death certain do indeed abandon fear."
Saying, "You are not the one," the night-roamer, black as death,
struck <s>Bhīmasena</s> on the back with both hands, in contempt.
But he, still eating the food, unmoved like a great mountain,
looked at the demon calmly, as if in play.
Then that astonished rākṣasa came at <s>Vṛkodara</s> in anger,
and, suddenly uprooting a śāla tree, struck him with a crash.
<s>Bhīmasena</s> too, unconfused, after eating and rinsing his mouth according to rule,
uprooted a great tree and struck the night-roamer.
When battle began between the two, with the trees of the earth used up completely,
there arose a cracking roar, as if mountains were splitting apart.
Then <s>Bhīma</s>, seizing that man of fierce valor by the neck,
set his knee upon his back and bent him like a bow.
From the mouth of that rakshasa as he was being broken by <s>Bhīma</s>
there gushed up a stream of blood, garlanded with waves.
Then, when he had fallen lifeless upon the ground,
his terrified followers came together, having heard the full noise.
Reassured by <s>Bhīma</s> and made to keep to an agreement,
they abandoned their thorn-like oppression of the world and went away, grieving for their master.
Then, after <s>Bhīmasena</s> had gone, leaving the night-roamer on the road,
on the following day the townspeople assembled and saw <s>Baka</s> slain.
Delighted, they inquired whose turn it had been and, in amazement, questioned the brahmin.
He said, "The rakshasa was killed by someone perfected in mantras."
Then, when the world was free of its thorn and moved in happiness at will,
one day a guest, a twice-born man, came to the brahmin's house.
As he sat after eating and told stories,

children.text: kathāḥ pāṇḍusutāḥ svairaṃ papracchuḥ pṛthayā saha ||
children.translated_text: the sons of <s>Pāṇḍu</s>, together with <s>Pṛthā</s>, questioned him freely and with curiosity.
After narrating charming accounts of many lands,
at the end of his tale he said, "In <s>Pāñcāla</s> there is well-being; its king is prosperous.

children.text: drupado nāma sa purā droṇaśiṣyairjito raṇe
children.translated_text: Long ago that king, named <s>Drupada</s>, was conquered in battle by the pupils of <s>Droṇa</s>.
After giving half his kingdom to <s>Droṇa</s>, he burned inwardly with anger.
Though he had many sons, he desired a son fit for the killing of <s>Droṇa</s>,
and, bowing down, he served a sage on the bank of the <s>Jāhnavī</s>.
There he, a capable man, attended for a year upon two <s>Kāśyapa</s> brahmins,
named <s>Yāja</s> and <s>Upayāja</s>, strict in their vows, with many desired offerings.
Then once, when <s>Upayāja</s> was pleased, the king said to him,
"O twice-born one, through your power I desire a son who will kill <s>Droṇa</s>.

children.text: prāptaṃ tadvijito nidrāṃ na lebhe duḥkhito hyaham
children.translated_text: Since I suffered that defeat, distressed as I am, I have obtained no sleep.
I will give you a hundred million cows adorned with gold."
Hearing what was said by <s>Drupada</s>, <s>Upayāja</s> said to him,
"I, a brahmin, am not suited for base acts of this kind.
My younger brother <s>Yāja</s> should be appointed to this rite.
Once, when he was greedily eating a fruit that had fallen on impure ground,
I recognized him even from afar: 'This man is greedy.'"
Hearing that, <s>Drupada</s> approached <s>Yāja</s>, bowed, and said,

children.text: dehi droṇāntakaṃ putraṃ godhanaṃ te dadāmyaham ||
children.translated_text: "Give me a son who will bring an end to <s>Droṇa</s>; I will give you wealth in cattle."
Hearing this, <s>Yāja</s>, who understood the circumstance of that king,
and who sacrificed according to the Atharva-saṃhitā, duly performed the oblation.
Then from the midst of the fire there arose a crowned youth, clad in armor,
like a mass of flames, with sword and bow.
"This son, named <s>Dhṛṣṭadyumna</s>, has been born as the destroyer of <s>Droṇa</s>,

children.text: tava rājanniti tataḥ śuśrāva drupado divaḥ ||
children.translated_text: O king, for you"; then <s>Drupada</s> heard this from the sky.
Considering the command of fate impossible to transgress, and learning that story,

children.text: droṇaḥ sarvāsu vibudhaṃ taṃ cakre mānināṃ varaḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Droṇa</s>, best of proud men, made him learned in every discipline.
From the sacrificial pit there also arose his younger sister, a maiden,
like the presiding deity of the moon worshiped by brahmins at every lunar phase.
"This beautiful dark one, dark as the petal of a blue lotus, is <s>Kṛṣṇā</s>.
She has been born for the pacification of the earth's burden"; again the king heard this from the sky.
In time, lovely in her graceful movements, she became a flowering bower of <s>Madana</s>'s garden,
bearing breast-clusters, the charming spring splendor of youth's honey-season.
A very splendid great festival of her self-choice marriage
will take place in the city of <s>Pārṣata</s>, in an assembly of rulers of the earth.
Hearing this from the excellent brahmin, the sons of <s>Pāṇḍu</s> were disturbed,
and their hearts became troubled: "How has a destroyer of <s>Droṇa</s> been born?"
Then <s>Kuntī</s> said to them, "This country is not kind to those in need.
Sons, we, with our meager provisions, should go to the prosperous <s>Pāñcālas</s>."

children.text: iti māturgirā gantuṃ jātodyogeṣu teṣu tu
children.translated_text: When, at their mother's word, they had begun preparations to go,
the blessed sage himself, the son of <s>Satyavatī</s>, arrived.
That ocean of compassion asked after the welfare of the sons of <s>Pāṇḍu</s>,
and, omniscient, told them everything: "Long ago there was a sage's daughter.
By austerity that slender-waisted woman propitiated the boon-giver five times,
and asked <s>Candraśekhara</s>, 'Give me a husband.'
Hearing her speech repeated fivefold, the lord of <s>Girijā</s>
said, 'Good lady, you will have five husbands.'
She has now been born in the city of <s>Pāñcāla</s> as the daughter of <s>Drupada</s>.
When you have gone there, she will become your wife."
When <s>Vyāsa</s> had spoken thus and vanished, the <s>Pāṇḍavas</s> took leave of the brahmins,
set out, and reached the sacred ford called <s>Somaśrava</s> on the bank of the <s>Gaṅgā</s>.
There, at the beginning of evening, with women, one named <s>Citraratha</s>,
the lord of the gandharvas, sported, eager for water-play.
At the edges of his arms, adorned with bracelets, armlets, and jewels,
the waters, through their gleams, took on the splendor of a rainbow.
Again and again, upon the breasts of the doe-eyed women,
he made their pearl necklaces seem doubled by the streams of water scattered from his hands.
Those lotus-faced women of his, with jeweled girdles jingling,
where chattering birds along the bank repeatedly stirred the <s>Gaṅgā</s>.
For those fine-browed women, by their necklaces and smiles and leaf-like teeth,
and by their camphor earrings, the darkness was scattered as though its threads were broken.
The <s>Pāṇḍavas</s>, reaching that bank, saw him standing in that condition,
their way lit in front by <s>Pārtha</s>, who held a blazing firebrand in his hand.
He too, at the sight of them, quickly looked at his beloved women, their breasts covered with garments,

children.text: vilokya kāntāḥ krodhāndha uvācāgre sthitaṃ jayam ||
children.translated_text: and, blinded by anger, spoke to <s>Jaya</s>, who stood before him:

children.text: aho nu nirbhayā yūyaṃ yadakāṇḍe mahīmimām
children.translated_text: "Ah, how fearless you are, since at an improper time you have come to this ground,
my bed of sport; or perhaps delusion is at fault here.
The wandering of men who do not know place and time is surely for the daytime;
this moment, with the faces of the quarters hidden by darkness, belongs to beings who move through the sky.
I am named <s>Aṅgāraparṇa</s> and also called <s>Citraratha</s>;
I am king of the Gandharvas, and this grove on the bank of the <s>Gaṅgā</s> is mine."
Hearing that jealous speech of his, <s>Vijaya</s> replied:
"Ah, you speak boldly either from the madness of love or from delusion.
The <s>Gaṅgā</s>, moving through the three worlds and purifying all people,
is whose private playground, as though she were a channel in his own garden?
In bowing to gods, siddhas, and twice-born men, in satisfying cows,

children.text: puṇyāmbhasāṃ ca saṃsparśe kālaṃ ko vā parīkṣate ||
children.translated_text: and in touching holy waters, who ever examines the proper time?"
Hearing these words of <s>Arjuna</s>, he mounted his chariot and released an arrow,
his bow bent into a circle by the rod of his arm.
With an arrow <s>Phalguṇa</s> at once warded off his arrows,
and, a treasury of fiery brilliance, manifested the terrible Agneya weapon.
When the region of the sky became matted with flames from its radiance,
in a moment the chariot of <s>Aṅgāraparṇa</s> was reduced to ashes.
Then the son of <s>Pāṇḍu</s> seized him, chariotless and fallen on the ground,
dragging him by hair fragrant with the scent of mandāra blossoms.
A swarm of bees, risen from his scattered garlands, cried out
like compassion herself, babbling as a petitioner for his rescue.
When he had been captured, his wife sought refuge with <s>Dharmaja</s>,
frightened <s>Kumbhīnasī</s> by name, her girdle jingling from trembling.
Then <s>Dhanaṃjaya</s>, restrained by <s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s> out of compassion,

children.text: taṃ mumoca na vīrāṇāṃ viṣamastheṣu vikramaḥ ||
children.translated_text: released him; the valor of heroes is not directed against those in distress.
Then the Gandharva, his crest bowed before <s>Pārtha</s>, said:
"I have been conquered by you, hero; now my pride has been abandoned by me.
The name <s>Aṅgāraparṇa</s> has ended for me today, since my brilliance is gone,

children.text: yo 'haṃ citraratho yuddhe tvayā dagdharathaḥ kṛtaḥ ||
children.translated_text: for I, <s>Citraratha</s>, have had my chariot burned by you in battle.

children.text: gṛhāṇa cākṣuṣīṃ vidyāṃ prāṇadastvaṃ sakhā mama
children.translated_text: Accept the visual knowledge; you are the giver of my life and my friend.
By this knowledge, once given, everything is seen just as one wishes.

children.text: evameva na gṛhṇāmi mānī tvaṃ kṣatriyo yadi
children.translated_text: If, being a proud Kṣatriya, you will not take it merely as a gift,
then give me, with affection, this Agneya weapon.
I shall give you a group of five hundred Gandharva horses;
in time of battle even a hundred of them will always be inexhaustible."

children.text: ityuktvā sa dadau vidyāṃ pāvakāstraṃ vilokya ca
children.translated_text: Having spoken thus, he gave the knowledge and, after beholding the fire-weapon,

children.text: sakhyaṃ ca śāśvataṃ bheje jayinā savyasācinā ||
children.translated_text: entered into lasting friendship with victorious <s>Savyasācin</s>.

children.text: tataḥ kirīṭī gandharvaṃ prītaḥ papraccha nirvṛtam
children.translated_text: Then <s>Kirīṭin</s>, pleased, asked the satisfied Gandharva:
"Why did you fall into hostility toward us without cause?"
Hearing that speech of <s>Pārtha</s>, the hero <s>Citraratha</s> replied:

children.text: śṛṇu pārtha mayā yena yuṣmākaṃ dharṣaṇā kṛtā ||
children.translated_text: "Listen, <s>Pārtha</s>, for what reason I showed aggression toward you.
At night we overpower those who have no Brahmins set before them, no sacred fires, and no recitation,
for then we are born into an excess of increased strength.
My eagerness for battle arose especially in the presence of women;

children.text: kāntākaṭākṣahṛṣṭo hi na vetti maraṇaṃ janaḥ ||
children.translated_text: a man delighted by the sidelong glances of his beloved does not know death.
I have been conquered by you, <s>Arjuna</s>, through the highest brahmacarya;
otherwise, whence comes the power of Kṣatriyas without a purohita?
O <s>Tāpatya</s>, moon of the Kuru lineage, your valor,
joined with a mantra-knowing purohita, would conquer the three worlds."
Hearing that, the son of <s>Pāṇḍu</s> asked him with curiosity:
"How are we <s>Tāpatyas</s>? Tell me, king of the Gandharvas."

children.text: iti pṛṣṭaḥ sa pārthena provāca premanirbharaḥ
children.translated_text: Questioned thus by <s>Pārtha</s>, he spoke, filled with affection:

children.text: babhūva bhārate vaṃśe purā saṃvaraṇo nṛpaḥ ||
children.translated_text: "Long ago in the Bharata lineage there was a king named <s>Saṃvaraṇa</s>.
Seeing the mass of his fame, infatuated Vidyādhara women
found no rest even on the peaks of crystal mountains.
That king, once absorbed in hunting and roaming in a forest,
with his horse exhausted, slowly climbed a mountain peak on foot.
There, in a lovely grove of lotus-creepers with sweetly humming birds,
where the bodies of deer were stilled by the music of Kinnarī sport,
tawny with the pollen of puṃnāga, kesara, aśoka, and mango blossoms,
as though a second golden mountain had been fashioned by the creator,
he saw the whole treasury of the flower-bowed god's beauty,
a divine maiden, a stream of extraordinary loveliness and nectar.
