She was adorned with the gold of the radiance of her limbs, with the pearl-beauty of her smile,
with the jewel of her charming glance, and with youth itself.
Seeing that wide-eyed woman, even the heroic king
became a play-pavilion for amazement, passion, and trembling.
"Whose are you, moon-faced one? Who are you, lotus-eyed lady?

children.text: bhaja māṃ subhage nītaṃ kāmena tava dāsatām ||
children.translated_text: Favor me, fair one, whom Love has brought into servitude to you."
With his eyes acting like bees upon the lotus of her face,
the king, making flattering speech, somehow became talkative.
Hearing this, the young girl was ashamed, her lotus-face bent down;
after standing for a moment, she sprang up into the sky and vanished from sight.
When she, the daylight splendor for the lotus of the king's eyes, had gone,
he fell into the torment of separation, distressed like a <s>cakravāka</s> bird.
For whom does affection not arise from repeated meeting?
But an extraordinary person nourishes the heart merely by being seen.
Not seeing her, his lotus-face withered by sighs,
he wandered in the forest like a madman, bewildered by separation.
Loud with incoherent lament, he fainted and fell to the ground,
as if uprooted by violent <s>Manmatha</s> when he came upon him.
Seeing the king fallen, the maiden who was standing in the sky
came back again and spoke to him when he had regained consciousness.
"I am the daughter of <s>Tapana</s>, king, named <s>Tapatī</s>;
and you are celebrated in the three worlds as generous in every virtue.
But I desire marriage only when permitted by my father;
in childhood women depend on their father and are always subject to another's authority."
Having said this, restless-eyed <s>Tapatī</s> entered the sky,
making the directions bright as with hundreds of moons by the radiance of her teeth.
When she had come near and departed again, the king once more fell into burning torment,
as if first sprinkled with sandal-water and afterwards drenched with poison.
Then, when his ministers with their troops had arrived after searching the forest,
one great minister came near and saw him.
Seeing the universal monarch unconscious on the ground, he was alarmed;
slowly reviving him, he questioned him, and so learned that story.

children.text: tato mantrigirā rājā vaśiṣṭhaṃ śreyasāṃ nidhim
children.translated_text: Then, at the minister's word, the king meditated on <s>Vaśiṣṭha</s>, his own <s>purohita</s> (family priest), treasure of blessings,
and performed worship of <s>Bhāskara</s>.
Thereupon <s>Vaśiṣṭha</s>, with arms raised and fasting for twelve days,
went to <s>Tapana</s> and himself asked for <s>Tapatī</s>.
Blessed <s>Sūrya</s> said to him, "This has long been my own wish:
'I shall give this daughter to <s>Saṃvaraṇa</s>.'"
Having spoken thus, the lord of day joyfully gave <s>Tapatī</s>;
taking the maiden whom he had resolved to give, the sage presented her.
Then the king, married to that doe-eyed young woman,
took his pleasure on mountain-crests dark with networks of creepers.
Delighting with that slender woman and wearing a crest of mandāra blossoms,
he lived for twelve years in the regions of divine forests.
Without that moon among kings, the subjects were oppressed by famine
because no rain fell, and the splendor of their sacrifices disappeared.
Then the king, entreated by his ministers, entered his own city,
and at that very moment the earth became rich with grain.
From him, the sacrificer, a son named <s>Kuru</s> was born in <s>Tapatī</s>;
born in that lineage, you, <s>Pārtha</s>, have been called <s>Tāpatya</s> by me.
Hearing that, <s>Phalguṇa</s> said, "I wish to hear
the life of the great sage <s>Vaśiṣṭha</s>, the <s>purodhas</s> (chaplain) of that king."
Questioned thus by the son of <s>Kuntī</s>, the lord of the Gandharvas said to him,

children.text: śṛṇu prabhāvaṃ vīrasya tasya śāntātmano muneḥ ||
children.translated_text: "Listen to the power of that heroic sage, whose self was at peace.
Though able to burn the whole world with the fire of his anger,
he endured, like a deep ocean, the offense ordained by time.
Desire and anger themselves, skilled in causing the world's sport,
trembling with fear, performed the rubbing of his feet.
Long ago <s>Viśvāmitra</s>, son of <s>Gādhi</s> and a <s>Kauśika</s>, was a king;
following deer in the forest, he entered <s>Vaśiṣṭha</s>'s hermitage.
Then, invited by him, the king with his army and mounts
obtained divine enjoyments provided by that wish-granting cow.
That cow named <s>Nandinī</s>, delighting mind and eye,
<s>Viśvāmitra</s> asked the eminent sage for her, offering herds of cattle.
Though the king, as a petitioner, offered elephants with gold, horses,

children.text: arthināṃ na dadau hotā kāmadhenuṃ mahāmuniḥ ||
children.translated_text: and even his kingdom, the great sage, the sacrificer, did not give the wish-granting cow.
Then the king, maddened by the power of royal fortune, seized her by force,
while she looked piteously and was let go by the patient lord of sages.
As she was being carried off by him, she produced <s>Pahlavas</s> from her cry,
brave <s>Śakas</s> from her dung, and <s>Yavanas</s> too from her womb.
With eyes reddened by grief, she also produced <s>Daradas</s>, <s>Turuṣkas</s>, <s>Cīnas</s>, and <s>Mlecchas</s>;
struck down by them, <s>Viśvāmitra</s>'s army fled at once.
Knowing that he had been defeated by brahmanical power, hard to overpower, <s>Kauśika</s>
performed austerity for a long time to obtain it, scorching the immortals.
Meanwhile king <s>Saudāsa</s>, out of delight in hunting,
as he was traveling, saw <s>Vaśiṣṭha</s>'s son on a one-track path.
The king said to him, named <s>Śakti</s>, "Move aside."
He too at once said to him, "A Brahmin deserves precedence before a king."
Then <s>Saudāsa</s>, the <s>Pauṣya</s> called <s>Kalmāṣapāda</s>, became angry;
in rage he rushed at the sage's son like a <s>yātudhāna</s> (demon).
Struck by a blow in anger, the sage's son cursed him,
saying in a mind shaken by fear, "You will become an eater of men."
Cursed by him, that king went to his own city;
when a sage requested a meat meal from him, he went into the inner apartments.

children.text: smṛtvā tamardharātre ca nijaṃ sūdaṃ samādiśat
children.translated_text: Remembering him at midnight, he ordered his own cook:
"Quickly prepare a meal of meat for the Brahmin," he said.
To him, who said, "Whence could there be meat at midnight?"
the king said, "Give this Brahmin human flesh."
The cook too went to the execution ground, to those who were fixed on the tips of stakes,

children.text: māṃsaṃ kṣaṇena saṃskṛtya dadau viprāya bhojanam ||
children.translated_text: and, having quickly prepared their flesh, gave the Brahmin a meal.
But the Brahmin, seeing with divine sight and knowing that it was not fit to be eaten, became angry;
though loudly entreated, he said to him at once, "Become an eater of human flesh."
Then, through the repeated curse, that king was enveloped;
and the raksasa, ordered in that way by <s>Viśvāmitra</s>, commanded him:
"Eat all the sons of <s>Vasiṣṭha</s>," out of enmity.
Ordered by him, he made the king a raksasa of cruel conduct.
Possessed by the raksasa, he went to <s>Vasiṣṭha</s>'s hermitage
and said to <s>Śakti</s>, "This curse given by you has now arrived.
From you indeed I begin my meal of human flesh.
I am skilled at making a mouthful of the syllable Oṃ; where will you go?"
Having spoken thus, the terrible one, drenched with blood, ate him;
and after swallowing a hundred sons of <s>Vasiṣṭha</s>, he was still hungry.
Then, seeing the hermitage bereft of his sons, the sage
became scorched by grief, as though split open by a thunderbolt.
From the summit of <s>Meru</s> he cast off his body, and by a serpent he sought death;

children.text: śoke bandhuriva snigdhaḥ kuto vā labhyate budhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: but where is a wise man to be found, tender like a kinsman in grief?
He entered fire, but considered it like a mass of snow;
for those burned by the fire of grief, I think ordinary fire is useless.

children.text: viveśa jaladhiṃ kaṇṭhe sa baddhvā vipulāṃ śilām
children.translated_text: He entered the ocean, having tied a great stone around his neck;
even for great souls, the cruel calamity of separation is hard to cross.
Cast aside by the hand-like wave, he did not lose his life in the ocean;

children.text: duḥkhavyathāṃ na jānāti jaḍarāśiḥ kathaṃ tu vā ||
children.translated_text: for how could a mass of inert matter know the anguish of sorrow?
He bound himself tightly with ropes and threw himself into a river;
because of him it became without bonds, and that river became <s>Vipāśā</s>.
Another river, running away in a hundred streams, gained the name <s>Śatadrutā</s>.
Then the lord of sages ceased from the effort of dying.
One day in the hermitage he heard, from the daughter-in-law <s>Apaśyantī</s>,
the sound of study from his grandson who was situated in her womb.
Seeing that <s>Apaśyantī</s>, the wife of <s>Śakti</s>, and learning her story,
that best of steadfast men took hold of resolve and steadied himself.
King <s>Saudāsa</s>, possessed by the raksasa, came toward him with his daughter-in-law,
terrible and roaring like a cloud full of lightning, in order to kill him.
As he rushed on, the mantra-knowing sage, with a huṃkāra,
made the king's curse vanish, and the raksasa abandoned him.

children.text: muktaśāpaḥ sa bhūpālo muniṃ prahvo vyajijñapat
children.translated_text: Freed from the curse, the king bowed low and petitioned the sage:
"Long ago, in her fertile season, a young Brahmin was joined with his wife.
Before he had attained his own satisfaction, with my mind possessed by a raksasa,
I, sinful one, ate him while his eyes were fixed on his beloved alone.
His wife, helpless with grief and lamenting, cursed me:
'Your life shall last only until the moment of union with your beloved.'
Since this line of <s>Ikṣvāku</s> has been cut off while I have resorted to celibacy,

children.text: dehi me kṣetrajaṃ putraṃ kule nastvaṃ parāyaṇam ||
children.translated_text: give me a kṣetraja son; you are the refuge of our lineage."
Thus requested by <s>Kalmāṣapāda</s>, by <s>Saudāsa</s>,
the sage, directed by him, approached <s>Damayantī</s> with a detached mind.
She conceived the sage's embryo, which remained for twelve years;
in pain she struck it with a stone, and therefore her son was <s>Aśmaka</s>.
Meanwhile the wife of <s>Śakti</s>, at the proper time, gave birth to a son,
who had sung the Vedas with their ancillary sciences while staying in the womb for twelve years.
Because by him his grandfather, whose life was departing, had been sustained through firmness,
he therefore became known as <s>Parāśara</s>, a son equal to <s>Śakti</s>.

children.text: sa māturvacasā jñātvā pitaraṃ sānujaṃ hatam
children.translated_text: Learning from his mother's words that his father had been killed together with his younger brothers,
he, from anger, set his mind toward the destruction of the three worlds.
<s>Vasiṣṭha</s>, seeing his grandson enraged like the fire at the end of time,
spoke, his eyes softened with compassion toward all beings:

children.text: mā krudhaḥ putra sa pitā pūrṇāyuste divaṃ gataḥ
children.translated_text: "Do not be angry, son. Your father, his lifespan complete, has gone to heaven.

children.text: svakarmamuddhito lokaḥ ko hantā kaśca hanyate ||
children.translated_text: The world is borne along by its own karma; who is the killer, and who is killed?
Long ago King <s>Kṛtavīrya</s> filled the <s>Bhṛgus</s>, Brahmins who received the first shares,
with riches resembling the wealth of <s>Kubera</s>.
In time, kings of that lineage, impoverished and seeking wealth,
plundered the house of the <s>Bhṛgus</s> like cruel bands of robbers.
An effort toward unjust seizure of wealth is undertaken in a perverse way;
because truth contracts among the greedy, their riches too only contract.

children.text: haranto bhārgavadhanaṃ nirdhanā eva te nṛpāḥ
children.translated_text: Those kings, taking the wealth of the <s>Bhārgavas</s>, remained poor;
seeing that wealth in the wombs, they killed them from children down to embryos.
Then, as the <s>Bhārgavas</s> were being killed by the <s>Haihaya</s> kshatriyas,
one <s>Bhṛgu</s> woman, from fear, held her miscarried embryo in her thigh.
The child was born by splitting open her thigh, like another sun;
with his mere glance he suddenly stole the sight of the assembled kings.

children.text: abhyāse kṣatriyāḥ sarve prasādya brāhmaṇaṃ bhayāt
children.translated_text: All the kshatriyas, drawing near, propitiated the Brahmin out of fear;
regaining their eyes at his word, they departed with their valor broken.
That child-sage, named <s>Aurva</s>, hearing that the <s>Bhṛgus</s> had been killed,
great in austerity, set his mind on the destruction of all the worlds.
Seeing his fierce anger, blazing with the brilliance of a hundred fires,
The Pitṛs themselves restrained him, fearing that the world would be scorched.
The fire of anger that he had raised up to burn the worlds
was placed, at their word, in the submarine fire of the mare's mouth; for the worlds rest upon the waters.

children.text: ityaurvaḥ krodhajaṃ vahniṃ sa tatyāja mahāmuniḥ
children.translated_text: Thus the great sage <s>Aurva</s> abandoned the fire born of anger.

children.text: putra tvamapi kopāgniṃ tyaja mā vikriyā gamaḥ ||
children.translated_text: "Son, you too must abandon the fire of anger; do not undergo any change of mind."
At this speech of <s>Vasiṣṭha</s>, he desisted from destroying the three worlds;
but <s>Parāśara</s>, through a Rākṣasa-sacrifice, offered the Rākṣasas into the fire.

children.text: tataḥ sametya kṛpayā pulastyo munibhiḥ saha
children.translated_text: Then <s>Pulastya</s>, coming together with the sages out of compassion,
appeased him and saved the Rākṣasas, so that their race might remain established.
Because of that speech, <s>Parāśara</s> desisted from the sattra-sacrifice;
and he deposited the sacrificial fire that slew Rākṣasas in a tree on the northern Snow-mountain.
When this had been told by the king of the Gandharvas, the son of <s>Śakra</s>
heard it and said to him, "Tell us who should be our purohita."
"At the tīrtha called <s>Utkocaka</s>, the sage who is <s>Devala</s>'s younger brother
is <s>Dhaumya</s>; he is suitable for you," said <s>Citraratha</s>.
Then, taking leave of the Gandharva, the delighted sons of <s>Pāṇḍu</s> went
to <s>Dhaumya</s>'s hermitage, those fortunate men, by the path he had indicated.
Then the heroes bowed to him, whose heart and face were gracious,
and chose him as their beneficial purohita for the prosperity of imperial victory.
Then, full of eagerness, placing him in front and accompanied by their mother,
they went to the city of the <s>Pāñcālas</s> to see <s>Kṛṣṇā</s>'s svayaṃvara.
As they went with a company of Brahmins to the assembly of kings,
they saw the best of sages, <s>Pārāśarya</s>, a treasury of blessings.
Having bowed to him and received his permission, they entered the city,
crowded with troops of elephants, horses, and chariots belonging to great kings.
The heroes, living on alms and dressed as Brahmins,
settled their mother in a potter's house and themselves went to the svayaṃvara-ground.

children.text: adhṛṣyaṃ kārmukaṃ yatra rādhāyantraṃ ca pārṣataḥ
children.translated_text: There <s>Pārṣata</s> had set up an unapproachable bow and a target-device
as the valor-wager for the choosing of his daughter.

children.text: savyasācī sa cejjīvedvīro mama sutāṃ paraḥ
children.translated_text: His wish regarding that target was, "If the hero <s>Savyasācin</s> is alive,
then no other man shall possess my daughter."
Then all the kings entered the hall, attended by great sages
and by spectators eager for wonder, their jeweled earrings swinging.
Among them <s>Duryodhana</s> bore surpassing splendor,
white with the rays of his pearl necklace, like the moon among the stars.
On costly jewel seats and on golden lion-thrones
the kings sat down like immortals on the peaks of <s>Meru</s>.
There those foremost bearers of earth, with lovely bracelets and crests glittering with jewels,
shone, perfumed with sandalwood and aloe.
With white fly-whisks moving around them, bright like royal swans,
they looked like lotus ponds filled with tall white lotuses.
Then <s>Kṛṣṇā</s> appeared, clothed in a garment of clear radiance,
like the victory-banner of Love at the beginning of his conquest of the three worlds.
The circle of kings, reflected in the row of her toenails,
seemed to have set out to look at her face, bent down in bashfulness.
The pair of shafts of her thighs, soft as opening petals in the lotus-pond of beauty,
shone within the water of her clear garment.
She bore broad hips around which a tinkling girdle moved,
like the <s>Mandākinī</s> bearing a sandbank noisy with calling waterfowl.
She bore a line of hair, a young plantain of good fortune,
like the playful crest-plume's shadow of Love's peacock.
With her charming pair of breasts garlanded by drops of water,
she, a river of youth, shone like one with a pair of cakravāka birds.
Her lotus-face, whose bee was her sidelong glance and whose filaments were the radiance of pure teeth,
shone with her red lower lip as its petal.
Moving about playfully, she looked at the kings,
as they were fanned by Love with the fan of dalliance.
Then <s>Dhṛṣṭadyumna</s> spoke, restraining with his arm
the voices of the bards who adorned the kings victorious over enemies.
"O moon-like kings, radiant with fame white as heaps of camphor,

children.text: ayaṃ samājo bhavatāṃ kasya no nayanotsavaḥ ||
children.translated_text: which of you is not a festival for our eyes in this assembly?

children.text: na naḥ pragalbhate vāṇī yuṣmākaṃ guṇavarṇane
children.translated_text: Our speech does not grow bold in describing your virtues,
you whose fame is flawless nectar, a moonlight of marvels.
Here is the unapproachable bow, and here is the target, O beloveds of the earth;

children.text: kṛṣṇāṃ ca tatpaṇaprāpyāṃ dṛṣṭvā yuktaṃ vidhīyatām ||
children.translated_text: having seen <s>Kṛṣṇā</s>, obtainable by that wager, do what is fitting."
Having spoken thus, the prince addressed the proud kings;
then again he spoke to his sister, his words bright with the moonlight of his teeth's rays:
"O <s>Kṛṣṇā</s>, after bowing to the venerable sages and to the kings,
look upon them all with confidence; the striker of the target will be your husband.
This is the illustrious <s>Duryodhana</s>, a king, the crest-jewel of great kings,
whose proud friends enjoy royal fortune as though it were their own.
These are his heroic brothers, with <s>Duḥśāsana</s> at their head;
in the cage of their arms <s>Lakṣmī</s> shines like a sport-loving goose.
This is the illustrious lord of <s>Aṅga</s>, an ocean of nectar for hosts of suppliants;

children.text: karṇo vikarṇo nāmnāpi jāyate yasya śātravaḥ ||
children.translated_text: he is <s>Karṇa</s>, by whose very name his enemies become as if bereft of ears.
This mighty <s>Saubala</s> is the maternal uncle of the king of the Kuru line;
the fire of his valor rises up with the sighs of enemies sent away from home.
This is <s>Jayadratha</s> of <s>Sindhu</s>, armed with a bow and unmatched as a chariot-warrior.
the gods came to fear that the earth would be touched by the dust of whose army.
This lotus-petal-eyed one is <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, the slayer of <s>Keśin</s>,
a lotus-lake for the rows of bee-like eyes of sixteen thousand women.
And this is <s>Rauhiṇeya</s>, delight of <s>Revatī</s>, warder-off of enemies,
who always shines with the splendor of rut, like <s>Airāvaṇa</s>.
<s>Kṛtavarman</s>, <s>Aniruddha</s>, <s>Gada</s>, <s>Sātyaki</s>, <s>Uddhava</s>,
<s>Akrūra</s>, and <s>Cārudeṣṇa</s>: these are the bulls among the <s>Dāśārhas</s>.
This is <s>Virāṭa</s>, king of the <s>Matsyas</s>; this is <s>Sudakṣiṇa</s> of the <s>Kāmbojas</s>.
This Kaurava is <s>Somadatta</s>, the own brother of <s>Śantanu</s>;
and these are the sons of <s>Somadatta</s>: <s>Bhūri</s>, <s>Bhūriśravas</s>, and <s>Śala</s>.
This is <s>Śalya</s>, lord of the <s>Madras</s>, and king <s>Bhagadatta</s>.

children.text: ete cānye ca bhūpālāstvadarthaṃ subhru saṃgatāḥ
children.translated_text: These kings, and others too, have assembled for your sake, fair-browed one.

children.text: arhāḥ kulena kuntyā ca rādhābhettā tu te varaḥ ||
children.translated_text: They are worthy by lineage and family, but the man who pierces the target is your bridegroom.
When the prince of the <s>Pāñcālas</s> had spoken thus, the lordly kings
rose up toward the bow, their bows grasped as if in sport.
As they gazed at the pillars of their arms, charming with expansions of pride,
there arose among the rulers of the earth that agitation born from desire.
Crowded with the brilliance of tinkling bracelets, armlets, and bright necklaces,
and with their earrings swinging about, there was a certain confusion among them.
At that moment <s>Śauri</s> said to <s>Balabhadra</s>,
"Look at the sons of <s>Pāṇḍu</s>, hidden among the Brahmins.
Surely they have escaped from the lac house; now, their youth attained, they shine,
inwardly measuring the whole wretched gathering of kings by the pride of their arms."
While <s>Madhuripu</s> was speaking thus at ease, all the kings,
each saying "I first," crept toward the bow.
With the sky filled by gods drawn by the delight of seeing it,
the kings stood as if painted, their eyes fixed on <s>Kṛṣṇā</s>.
They could do no more than make the bow, heavy as a mountain,
their whole hope for obtaining <s>Kṛṣṇā</s>, yet their wishes were at once cut off.
Even in thought they considered the lifting of that bow very hard to bear,
as though their armlets and earrings had been crushed to powder by its pressure.
When the kings' courage had suddenly collapsed and their enthusiasm was broken,
and the necklaces of those proud men had grown dull with their hot sighs,
then the mighty-armed <s>Savyasācin</s> rose up from among the Brahmins,
as though lifting up the fallen honor and wealth of bowmen.
When he faced the bow, the embarrassed Brahmins said,
"Ah, what folly, worthy of a Brahmin, belongs to this reckless man!
That which was not held even by powerful men beginning with <s>Śalya</s>,
this young Brahmin, through delusion, wishes to string.
Now we shall be mocked or hated by the kings;
by the disgrace of even one man, the whole company perishes.
Or perhaps this man is capable and heroic, and he appears divine in form.

children.text: channānāṃ ko hi jānāti tejasaḥ sāraphalgutām ||
children.translated_text: Who knows whether hidden powers are substantial or worthless?"
While all were speaking thus, the <s>Pāṇḍava</s> drew the bow,
and, lovely as <s>Rāma</s>, at once struck the target and brought it down.
At the very moment when <s>Kirīṭin</s>'s arrow fell upon that target,
at that very moment Love's arrows entered <s>Kṛṣṇā</s>'s heart.
Then <s>Pārtha</s> became bright with flower-showers cast down by the gods;
the kings became dark, as if with swarms of bees rising from those flowers.
Then <s>Kṛṣṇā</s>, taking up a garland of flowers
made splendid by the blue lotuses that were the rays of her sidelong glances, approached <s>Dhanaṃjaya</s>.
<s>Drupada</s> too, his eyes blossoming with joy, together with his sons,
congratulated him, looking with jealousy at the kings.
Then the rulers of the earth looked for a moment at one another's faces,
as drops of sweat sprang up from the heat of the fire of humiliation.
They spoke, the beauty of their lips washed by the shadow of feigned smiles,
their accumulated anger revealed by their reddened lotus-eyes:
"Ah, by this earth-ruling <s>Drupada</s>, falsely humble and long-bearded,
the proud kings of the earth have been made ridiculous.
Having set the prowess of our arms upon the balance-scale of doubt,
this cheat has made this game of mockery for us.
By us, straightforward men, our fame, pure as crystal,
has itself been stained with the mud of contact with wicked people.
By the Brahmin who acted with excessive rashness, our anger has been stirred;

children.text: vadhyo 'yaṃ drupadaḥ kanyāṃ yo 'smai dātuṃ samudyataḥ ||
children.translated_text: this <s>Drupada</s>, who is ready to give his daughter to him, deserves to be killed.
How can we possibly endure an overturning of proper conduct?
A <s>svayaṃvara</s> (self-choice ceremony) fit for kings is not prescribed for Brahmins."
Having spoken thus, all the kings, with shining golden armor,
came together to kill the son of <s>Pṛṣata</s>, their faces crooked with frowns.
Seeing them furious with anger, <s>Drupada</s> went to the Brahmins
for refuge; they too, prepared for battle, rose up on every side.
Then <s>Vijaya</s>, laughing, held the Brahmins back from battle,
and, drawing that same bow, rushed upon the kings.
<s>Bhīmasena</s> too uprooted a broad-branched tree,
and, massive as a mountain, stood up before the ocean of kings.
Seeing that <s>Kirīṭin</s>'s form matched his might, <s>Karṇa</s>,
greatly enraged, approached and entangled him with arrows.
Then the straight and long arrows released from <s>Arjuna</s>'s arms

children.text: na sehe samare karṇaḥ khalaḥ sādhuguṇāniva ||
children.translated_text: <s>Karṇa</s> could not withstand in battle, like a wicked man unable to bear the virtues of the good.
Then <s>Karṇa</s>, apprehensive of <s>Phālguṇa</s>'s wealth of valor, said to him:
"Are you the <s>Dhanurveda</s> embodied, <s>Rāma</s> himself, <s>Śakra</s>, or a Brahmin?"
Hearing <s>Karṇa</s>'s words, <s>Dhanaṃjaya</s> laughed and said:

children.text: yudhyasva kiṃ tavānena na me jīvangamiṣyasi ||
children.translated_text: "Fight. What use is this to you? You will not go from me alive.
With arms tender as lotus fibers and with delicate heroism,
<s>Duḥśāsana</s> and the rest are enough in this battle for men like us."
Having spoken thus, from within the circle of his fierce bow
he quickly filled him with arrows, as the sharp-rayed sun fills with its rays.
Then mighty <s>Bhīmasena</s>, impetuous, conquered <s>Śalya</s> and <s>Duryodhana</s>,
and by his valor made them upon his arms like armlets.
When <s>Śalya</s>, together with the king, had been defeated by <s>Bhīma</s> in arm-to-arm combat,
the kings withdrew, apprehensive of Brahminical power.
When wise <s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s> had gone ahead with the twins,
then <s>Bhīma</s> and <s>Phālguṇa</s>, taking <s>Kṛṣṇā</s> afterward, went on.
Near a potter's house, in the dwelling of a <s>Bhārgava</s>,
those heroes reached their mother, who was staying inside the workshop.
Then <s>Bhīma</s> and <s>Arjuna</s> said to her, "Alms have been brought."

children.text: niśi kuntī ca tāvūce samaṃ saṃbhujyatāmiti ||
children.translated_text: And at night <s>Kuntī</s> said to the two of them, "Let it be enjoyed equally."

children.text: draupadīṃ ca puro dṛṣṭvā tato bhrājiṣṇubhūṣaṇām
children.translated_text: Then, seeing <s>Draupadī</s> before her, adorned with shining ornaments,
<s>Pṛthā</s>, stricken by the falsehood of her utterance, fell into remorse.

children.text: khinnā vilokya tāṃ kuntī mithaḥ saṃtatiśālinaḥ
children.translated_text: Seeing <s>Kuntī</s> distressed, they made an agreement among themselves,
and said, "<s>Kṛṣṇā</s> is indeed for all of us."
Then <s>Śauri</s>, companion of <s>Halāyudha</s>, recognized the sons of <s>Pāṇḍu</s> by signs of their prowess,
and joyfully approached to see them.
Entering secretly and seeing them, the sons of his paternal aunt,
<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, saying "I am <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>," grasped the feet of <s>Dharmaja</s>.
They embraced and conversed with <s>Śauri</s>, rejoicing together,
and after hearing one another's stories for a moment, they stood with eyes full of tears.

children.text: tato yathāgate yāte kṛṣṇe lāṅgalinā saha
children.translated_text: Then, when <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> had gone back as he had come, together with <s>Lāṅgalin</s>,
<s>Dhṛṣṭadyumna</s>, suspicious and wishing to learn his sister's circumstances, wandered about.
Concealed near the <s>Bhārgava</s>'s house, during the course of their conversation,
he heard the name "<s>Kṛṣṇā</s>" being called and stories proper to Kṣatriyas.

children.text: tataḥ sa hṛṣṭo drupadaṃ tamabhyetya samabhyadhāt
children.translated_text: Then, delighted, he went to <s>Drupada</s> and said to him:

children.text: tāta rājendravaṃśyena vṛtā sā bhaginī mama ||
children.translated_text: "Father, my sister has been chosen by a scion of a royal line.
The nāgavallī creeper has of itself climbed the areca tree;
nectar-rich moonlight has come together with the moonstone."

children.text: iti putravacaḥ śrutvā drupadaḥ svaṃ purohitam
children.translated_text: Hearing his son's words, <s>Drupada</s> sent his own priest
and had the sons of <s>Pāṇḍu</s> brought to his own residence.
From what had been arranged by clever royal servants for the king's test,
they selected and accepted a gift suitable for rulers.
<s>Kuntī</s>, taking <s>Kṛṣṇā</s> with her, then entered the inner apartments,
and the <s>Pārthas</s>, honored, sat down on jeweled seats.
Then <s>Pārṣata</s>, after honoring them as they sat after eating,
asked first about their lineage, though it was already indicated by their bearing.
Then <s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s> spoke in a voice deep as a cloud,
as if acting as the teacher of tāṇḍava dance for sportive peacocks:
"O king, qualities unmatched and proportionate to valor
belong to a person endowed with spirit, not to one of low birth.
Fond of your daughter, why do you suspect without due consideration?

children.text: rādhāvibhede sāmānyaḥ ko hi nāma pragalbhate ||
children.translated_text: Who, being ordinary, would ever have dared at the piercing of the target?
I am <s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s>, O king; this is <s>Bhīma</s>, this is <s>Arjuna</s>.

children.text: anena tatpuro rājñā yantraṃ bhūmau nipātitam ||
children.translated_text: By him, before you, O king, the mechanism was brought down to the ground."
Hearing <s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s>'s speech, as if sprinkled with nectar,
<s>Drupada</s>, his resolve fulfilled, obtained the splendor of joy.

children.text: muhūrtaṃ harṣaniḥsyandaḥ sthitvā śrutvā ca tatkathām
children.translated_text: After remaining for a moment while joy streamed forth, and after hearing their account,
the king of <s>Pāñcāla</s> spoke, condemning the sons of <s>Dhṛtarāṣṭra</s>:
"By fortune you have escaped from that lac house and from great danger;

children.text: diṣṭyā ca yuṣmatsaṃbandhaḥ prāptaḥ sukṛtinā mayā ||
children.translated_text: and by fortune, through my merit, kinship with you has been obtained by me.
Let <s>Śvetavāhana</s> take my daughter's hand according to rule."

children.text: tacchrutvovāca kaunteyo mātuḥ satyāṃ giraṃ smaran ||
children.translated_text: Hearing that, <s>Kaunteya</s>, remembering his mother's truthful words, said:

children.text: putryāstava vayaṃ sarve grahīṣyāmaḥ karaṃ nṛpa
children.translated_text: "All of us shall take your daughter's hand, O king.

children.text: mā viśaṅkasva dharmasya susūkṣmo hi gatikramaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Do not be doubtful; the movement of <s>dharma</s> is exceedingly subtle."
<s>Drupada</s> too, hearing that, spoke with his mind shaken:
"Ah, though you know <s>dharma</s>, you speak of a blameworthy act fit for the wicked.
Disregarding family custom, how can a man like me
undertake this act, which is cast out by the talk of the world?
Women are vowed to one husband, while men may have many wives;
how can you lightly abandon this condition as righteous?"

children.text: tacchrutvovāca taṃ pārtho mā rājanvimanā bhava
children.translated_text: Hearing that, <s>Pārtha</s> said to him, "Do not be troubled, O king.
We were commanded by our mother: 'Together this is to be enjoyed.'

children.text: tadatathyaṃ kathaṃ kartuṃ śaktaḥ satyadhano janaḥ
children.translated_text: How can a person whose wealth is truth make that untrue?
For truth is the root of the tree of <s>dharma</s> with its thousand branches."
When the king together with his son was dejected at <s>Kaunteya</s>'s words,
<s>Kuntī</s>, being questioned, came forward and told the lord of men that very thing.
Meanwhile there arrived the blessed sage, the creator of beings,
the son of <s>Satyavatī</s>, the cutter-off of all doubts,
honored there by them, whose crests touched the ground.
He had heard their separate doubt about <s>dharma</s> in connection with the marriage.
The best of sages said to him, "Do not make a useless doubt.
Listen to this matter, described here by <s>Vedhas</s> himself.
Long ago, when <s>Yama</s> was intent on the performance of a sacrifice, the whole world
was filled with the burden of creatures and oppressed because death had ceased.
Then <s>Pākaśāsana</s>, occupied with protecting the earth,
saw the four-faced god and went to the ground of <s>Yama</s>'s sacrifice.
There, in the <s>Jāhnavī</s>, he saw a row of golden lotuses
moving along with masses of waves, for a moment made to dance by whirlpools.
Then, out of curiosity, <s>Sahasrākṣa</s> followed it and saw a doe-eyed one,
a divine woman whose lotus-face was downcast with sorrow.
From the drops of her tear-water there was a garland of golden lotuses in the water;

children.text: tāṃ vilokya sa papraccha vismitaḥ śokakāraṇam ||
children.translated_text: seeing her, he was astonished and asked the cause of her grief.
She too, saying "You will know," went away with the gait of an elephant,
and <s>Śakra</s>, following her alone, saw on a mountain summit
a handsome man seated on a throne, accompanied by his beloved.
Seeing him playing with dice, <s>Vṛtrahā</s> spoke from pride:

children.text: aho nu jagatāṃ nāthaṃ mā dṛṣṭvāpi na kampase
children.translated_text: "Ah, though you have seen me, the lord of the worlds, do you not tremble?

children.text: vikalo 'pi puraḥ strīṇāṃ nūnaṃ śakrāyate janaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Surely even a powerless man plays the <s>Śakra</s> in front of women."
Hearing the words of <s>Śatamanyu</s>, the lord of <s>Girijā</s> laughed,
and with a mere fraction of his eye made him motionless in an instant, like a piece of wood.
Then, at the end of the dice-play, he spoke in private to that tearful woman,
making the world crystalline with the rays of his laughter:
"Touch this man at my command and release the proud one from the bond of my anger."
So instructed by him, the heavenly woman touched the thunderbolt-bearer, who had been made rigid.

children.text: spṛṣṭamātraḥ sa ca tayā papāta gatacetanaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The moment he was touched by her, he fell unconscious.
The beloved of <s>Umā</s> said to him, "Do not again show such pride.
Rise; split open the crest of the mountain and look into the cave."

children.text: iti śrutvā tathā kṛtvā sa dadarśa darīgṛhe
children.translated_text: Hearing this and doing so, he saw in the cavern-dwelling
four other <s>Purandaras</s>, equal in form, age, and dress.
Seeing them, <s>Śakra</s> trembled and became bewildered in mind,
fearing, "May I not become like these."
Then the blessed <s>Bharga</s> said to him, "For your task, let there be
a birth for the five of you in the human world, to quiet the burden of the earth."
Hearing the words of <s>Maheśvara</s>, they then made respectful añjalis,

children.text: ūcurdharmādayo devāḥ santu no janakā iti ||
children.translated_text: and the gods beginning with <s>Dharma</s> said, "Let us be the fathers."
<s>Śakra</s> also said, "Let my son be the fifth among them;

children.text: tvatprasādādahaṃ deva na patāmi svayaṃ kṣitau ||
children.translated_text: by your favor, O god, I myself shall not fall to earth."

children.text: evamastviti taṃ devaḥ prītaḥ provāca śaṃkaraḥ
children.translated_text: Pleased, the god <s>Śaṃkara</s> said to him, "So be it.
The angers of great souls end at humility; they do not remain fixed.
<s>Viśvabhuj</s>, <s>Dhṛtadhāmā</s>, <s>Śibi</s>, <s>Śānta</s>, and another, <s>Tejasvī</s>:

children.text: tejasvī veti te śakrā jātāḥ pāṇḍusutā bhuvi ||
children.translated_text: those <s>Śakras</s>, O <s>Śakra</s>, have been born on earth as the sons of <s>Pāṇḍu</s>.

children.text: tadarthaṃ sundarī jātā svargastrī saiva bhūtale
children.translated_text: For that purpose the same heavenly woman was born on earth as the beautiful woman;

children.text: kṛṣṇā tava sutā rājannatra mā vimatiṃ kṛthāḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Kṛṣṇā</s> is your daughter, O king; do not have any doubt about this.

children.text: etatsarvaṃ yathā vṛttaṃ paśya divyena cakṣuṣā
children.translated_text: See all this as it happened with divine sight."

children.text: ityuktvāsmai dadau vyāsaḥ kṣaṇaṃ dhyānamayīṃ dṛśam ||
children.translated_text: Having said this, <s>Vyāsa</s> gave him, for a moment, a vision made of meditation.
Then, seeing the truth, the king of <s>Pāñcāla</s> was delighted,
and, saying "I am blessed," he bowed and went out with the sage.
Then, when the best of sages had departed and an auspicious conjunction with <s>Puṣya</s> and the moon was honored,
after <s>Dhaumya</s> had duly offered into the fire, preceded by mantras,
the sons of <s>Pāṇḍu</s>, one after another, took the hand of <s>Kṛṣṇā</s>,
honored by all the <s>Pāñcālas</s>, who gave abundant jewels and garments.
While that renowned and very wealthy festival was taking place,
<s>Kṛṣṇa</s> sent wealth with many horses and elephants to the sons of <s>Pṛthā</s>.
Then, when the kings learned that <s>Kṛṣṇā</s> had been obtained by the sons of <s>Pāṇḍu</s>,

children.text: vismayaṃ ca prakopaṃ ca saṃtāpaṃ ca prapedire ||
children.translated_text: they fell into astonishment, anger, and distress.
Hearing of the rise of the <s>Pāṇḍavas</s>, those led by <s>Duḥśāsana</s>
said, "Alas, misery!" condemning the ordinance of fate.
Then the delighted <s>Vidura</s> approached <s>Dhṛtarāṣṭra</s>

children.text: uvāca diṣṭyā tvatputraiḥ prāptā kṛṣṇā balāditi ||
children.translated_text: and said, "By good fortune, <s>Kṛṣṇā</s> has been won by your sons through strength."
Hearing that from the wise man, the king of the <s>Kurus</s> was pleased,

children.text: kṛṣṇāṃ duryodhanenaiva prāptāṃ mene saha śriyā ||
children.translated_text: and thought that <s>Kṛṣṇā</s> had been won by <s>Duryodhana</s> himself, together with fortune.
Again the <s>kṣattṛ</s> addressed him: "O lord, by your brother's sons,
freed by fate from the lac house, it has been won by the sons of <s>Kuntī</s>."
Then he, concealing his expression and outwardly displaying joy,

children.text: uvāca putrābhyadhikā diṣṭyā jīvanti te mama ||
children.translated_text: said, "By good fortune those dearer than my own sons are alive."
At that moment <s>Suyodhana</s> came with his ministers,
and, after <s>Vidura</s> had gone, spoke to his father, overcome by anger:
"Ah, those enemies who have made enmity have been forgotten by you,
since, through delusion and simple honesty, you are setting out to make an alliance with them.
With wealth, moon-white umbrellas, and the splendor of chowries,
you will surely be mocked in a kingdom where trust is impossible.

children.text: cauraṃ dviṣṭaṃ vadhūṃ yātāṃ śatruṃ vitrāsitaṃ kṛtam
children.translated_text: A thief, a hated man, a wife who has gone away, or an enemy who has been frightened:

children.text: punaḥ saṃgṛhya yaḥ śete sa taireva prabodhyate ||
children.translated_text: whoever takes them back and sleeps is awakened by those very ones.

children.text: viśvāsaṃ śaṅkite śatrau mā kṛthāḥ saralāśayaḥ
children.translated_text: Do not place trust in a suspected enemy, O straightforward-minded one.
O king, a kingdom full of many deceits is said to be enjoyed by stratagems, not by battles."
I know that these princes can now be conquered by stratagems;
but if they are neglected, then even in mere intention they will be hard to conquer.

children.text: śrūyate draupadī teṣāṃ sarveṣāṃ mahiṣī matā
children.translated_text: <s>Draupadī</s> is heard to be regarded as the wife of all of them;

children.text: saiva tadbhedanopāyo jīvitaṃ hi kaleḥ striyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: she herself is the means for dividing them, for women are the very life of strife.
Let them be killed secretly this very day by clever and sharp men of mine;
for a desire whose time has passed only nourishes remorse.
When <s>Duryodhana</s> had spoken thus, the hero born from the Sun
spoke, making a row of filaments in his lotus-face with the rays of his teeth:
Even when they have been properly devised with effort by intelligent men,
stratagems do not succeed at all without regard for fate.
When an enemy is proud, has made enmity, and has shown the substance of his valor,

children.text: ko hi daivaṃ samuddiśya vilambeta vadhe ripoḥ ||
children.translated_text: who indeed, pointing to fate, would delay in killing him?
Though the <s>Pārthas</s> have been worn down by you through many kinds of efforts,
they turn back with great energy; what else can this be except fate?
Devices, plans, and deceptions are said to be only the wasting of time;
for victory without peril has one clear measure alone: valor.
O lord of the earth, kill the sons of <s>Pāṇḍu</s> in battle this very day;
for when they are protected by <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> and the others, in time they will be impossible to defeat.
A fire whose flame can be measured by a fist is brought to rest with water;
when it has grown, afterward it is seen only by those below it, scorched.
Hearing this, the son of <s>Ambikā</s>, deluded by affection for his son,
thought, "So it is," and became filled with uncertainty.
He summoned the elders headed by <s>Bhīṣma</s>, skilled in policy,
and asked for a decision on what was right and wrong in his son's plan.
Then the great-hearted grandsire, who saw impartially, said:
O king, even now I think no distortion has come upon us.
After giving them half the kingdom, with no vulnerable opening discerned by enemies,
one should enjoy prosperity that is clear and free from reproach.
Through compassion, with their forces, through affection for kin, and through noble lineage,
rulers, truly, shine in restraint and conciliation.
When the son of <s>Gaṅgā</s> had spoken thus, the son of <s>Bharadvāja</s> said:
O king, <s>Śāntanava</s> has spoken what is best for the welfare of your family.

children.text: prāptakālaṃ vacaḥ pathyaṃ pramādī na śṛṇoti yaḥ
children.translated_text: The heedless man who does not listen at the proper time to salutary speech whose time has come,

children.text: dhikchandaṃ sa cireṇaiva naṣṭaśrīkaḥ śṛṇoti saḥ ||
children.translated_text: alas for his desire, hears it only much later, when his fortune has been destroyed.
Let this present enmity among kinsmen be covered over by sound policy;
for when a split in a family is laid open, its powers depart at once.
Hearing this, <s>Karṇa</s>, his face slightly contracted,

children.text: uvāca bata jīvanti nijaiḥ puṇyaiḥ kṣitīśvarāḥ ||
children.translated_text: said, "Ah, kings live by their own merits.
Ministers strengthened by uncommon honor
and by gifts do not desire their lord; if that is so, what else is surprising?
Or rather, the trust of kings in those who live at court is entirely false;
only the conjunction of fortune brings prosperity even to one who is disabled.
There was a lord of the earth famous as <s>Ambarīṣa</s>,
disabled, deprived of his faculties, his life perceptible only by his breaths.
His minister <s>Mahākarṇi</s>, covering the whole realm,
formed the intention of seizing the kingdom, deluded by greed.
Then, by unseen men arisen from the king's merit,
that minister was forcibly killed; so royal splendors follow fortune."
Hearing this, <s>Droṇa</s> said, "Son of a charioteer, surely the <s>Kurus</s> are destroyed,

children.text: kuravaḥ karṇa darpāndhāḥ sarvajño 'tra tvameva ca ||
children.translated_text: O <s>Karṇa</s>; blind with pride, you alone are all-knowing here."
Then the very wise <s>Vidura</s> addressed <s>Dhṛtarāṣṭra</s>:

children.text: aho nu nāsti te rājanbheṣajaṃ vyasanāmaye ||
children.translated_text: Alas, O king, there is no medicine for you in this disease of disaster.
What <s>Bhīṣma</s> and <s>Droṇa</s> say is for your good and fitted to sound policy;
that effortless nectar, alas, whom would it not please?
By <s>dharma</s> (right order), the <s>Pāṇḍavas</s> are equal to your own sons;
O protector of the earth, you should not take away their inheritance.
With mighty <s>Bhīmasena</s> and with <s>Vijaya</s> the archer,

children.text: ko hi sarvasvamādāya vītaśaṅkaḥ sukhaṃ vaset ||
children.translated_text: who, after taking all their property, could live happily free from fear?
Let the anger caused by provocation be drawn away by conciliation
from the heart of the straightforward hero <s>Ajātaśatru</s>.
Let them be brought here today, conciliated for the fortune of the family;
let there be joy for the crowds of citizens eager to see them.
<s>Karṇa</s> is simple, and <s>Duryodhana</s>, bewildered by new sovereignty, is a child;

children.text: nṛśaṃsaḥ śakunisteṣāṃ kuto nu svahite matiḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Śakuni</s> is cruel. How could they have any thought for their own welfare?
Awakened by these words of <s>Vidura</s>, <s>Dhṛtarāṣṭra</s>

children.text: uvāca sādhu yuṣmābhiruktaṃ kīrtyai kulasya naḥ ||
children.translated_text: said, "You have spoken well, for the fame of our family.
Go, <s>Vidura</s>, and quickly bring the sons of <s>Kuntī</s> with their retinue;
my mind longs for the nectar of union with them."
By the command of the king, <s>Vidura</s>, with swift conveyance,

children.text: yathoktaṃ dhṛtarāṣṭreṇa hṛṣṭaḥ sarvaṃ nivedya saḥ
children.translated_text: joyfully reported everything exactly as <s>Dhṛtarāṣṭra</s> had said,
and said to the <s>Pāṇḍavas</s>, "Come to <s>Nāgapura</s>."
Then, at the words of the king of <s>Pāñcāla</s> and of <s>Keśava</s>,
the sons of <s>Pāṇḍu</s>, with their followers, went to <s>Hastināpura</s>.
Then, from the minds of the citizens streaming with the nectar of joy at seeing them,
there arose a certain eagerness to count their fame.
They, with jewel-bound crowns and lovely armlets and earrings,
shone like moving, fully formed <s>Rohaṇa</s> mountains.
Then, entering the capital and bowing to the grandsire,
they approached <s>Dhṛtarāṣṭra</s> together with <s>Kṛpa</s> and <s>Droṇa</s>, and paid homage.
After they had stayed there happily for some time, with their needs fulfilled,
they went to <s>Khāṇḍavaprastha</s> at the command of <s>Āmbikeya</s>.

children.text: uddiṣṭaṃ tatra rājyārdhaṃ te prāpya vyavasāyinaḥ
children.translated_text: There, receiving the half of the kingdom assigned to them, those resolute men
built a very wealthy city with a network of varied gateways.
There, in that place resembling heaven and lovely with gardens like <s>Nandana</s>,
those guardians of the worlds, whose fame was renowned in all directions, rejoiced.
Then one day, while he was seated in the assembly there together with his younger brothers,

children.text: svayaṃ yudhiṣṭhiraṃ draṣṭum āyayau nārado muniḥ ||
children.translated_text: the sage <s>Nārada</s> came of his own accord to see <s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s>.
The sons of <s>Pāṇḍu</s> bowed to him, whose mass of radiance had tawny-lit the quarters,
and honored him with rich jeweled seats and other offerings.
The glorious one asked after the health of <s>Dharmanandana</s> and his younger brothers,
and with blessings made <s>Draupadī</s>, who had come to bow to him, blessed.
Then, after dismissing her, the sage spoke to the <s>Pāṇḍavas</s> in private:
"By good fortune you are well, and prosperity has embraced you again.
Since you are attached to a single wife and are united with one another,
you must live without resentment; for women are the root of division.
The two <s>asuras</s> <s>Sunda</s> and <s>Upasunda</s>, who had conquered the host of immortals,
became unconquerable through asceticism, strengthened by a boon from <s>Prajāpati</s>.
There was no fear for those two strong-armed warriors from any beings,
as they ranged continually on the battlefields, except division between themselves.
Then <s>Vidhi</s>, having deliberated with the gods on a means of splitting them,
created a lovely celestial woman named <s>Tilottamā</s>.
Taking from all jewels one flawless sesame-grain portion after another,
she was swiftly fashioned by <s>Viśvakarman</s> at <s>Brahmā</s>'s command.
Then, for the sake of the gods' work, she went slowly to entice the Daityas,
after circumambulating the gods, walking with the gait of an elephant.
On seeing her, <s>Śaśiśekhara</s> at once became four-faced,
and <s>Śakra</s> became thousand-eyed, while the sages became hundred-faced.
Knowing that those two lords of the <s>asuras</s> were seated in a grove of the <s>Vindhya</s>,
the slender-waisted woman went there and began gathering flowers.
Her body, bent with graceful play, with the edges of its vine-like form loosened,
at times showing the charming illusion of soft cries caused by the descent of bees,
at times restless with the movement of her fine garment shaken by a gentle breeze,
shone beautiful as the very expanse of Love's enjoyment divided into parts.
When those two, intoxicated with liquor, saw the deer-eyed woman,
they fell into division, saying, 'She is mine alone, she is mine alone.'
Then, with maces raised, maddened by the fury of battle in combat,
they were shattered by one another's blows and lost their lives.
Thus, O king, women are the place of division, calamity,
and defeat; therefore one should approach them with apprehension.
The division of brothers must be guarded against by you with effort, O king;
this service of a single woman is a vow on the edge of a sword.
Hearing what had thus been told by <s>Nārada</s>, the sons of <s>Pāṇḍu</s>,
fearing division among themselves, made an agreement concerning their wife:

children.text: kṛṣṇayā saṃgataṃ bhrātā bhrātaraṃ yo vilokayet
children.translated_text: 'The brother who should see another brother together with <s>Kṛṣṇā</s>
shall live for twelve years as a forest-dweller, serving sacred <s>tīrthas</s>.'
Having taken up this agreement in the presence of the sage <s>Nārada</s>,
the heroes guarded the earth with arms like the lordly serpents' coils.
Then, when the divine seer had departed, one day the son of <s>Śakra</s>
heard from afar the cry of a Brahmin lamenting in distress:
'By wicked robbers, stronger than I, a weak man,

children.text: hriyate godhanaṃ me 'dya pārtho rakṣatu māṃ tataḥ ||
children.translated_text: my wealth in cattle is being carried off today; let <s>Pārtha</s> protect me from that.'
Hearing the twice-born man's outcry, <s>Arjuna</s> quickly,
eager for his bow, said at once, 'You must not be afraid.'
As he went to the armory, he learned that <s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s> was stationed there,
together with <s>Draupadī</s>, and became troubled with anxious thought.

children.text: apyāyudhārthī saṃsmṛtya pratijñāṃ na viveśa saḥ
children.translated_text: Though he needed his weapons, he did not enter, remembering the vow;

children.text: brahmasvavipralopaṃ ca na sehe mānināṃ varaḥ ||
children.translated_text: yet that best of honorable men could not bear the plundering of a Brahmin's property.
'On this side lies the breach of my agreement; on that, a greater loss of <s>dharma</s>,'
he reflected, and became distressed through doubt between truth and <s>dharma</s>.

children.text: ito me vanavāso 'stu dvijopekṣāṃ tu na kṣame
children.translated_text: 'Let exile in the forest be mine in this case; but I cannot endure neglect of a twice-born man.'

children.text: iti praviśya jagrāha sa niścityāyudhaṃ nijam ||
children.translated_text: Having decided thus, he entered and took up his own weapon.
Then <s>Pārtha</s>, treasure-house of fame, cut the band of robbers to pieces with arrows,

children.text: brāhmaṇāya dadau pārtho godhanaṃ yaśasāṃ nidhiḥ ||
children.translated_text: and gave the wealth in cattle back to the Brahmin.
Then <s>Arjuna</s> approached <s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s> and said with folded hands,
'O king, because the agreement has been broken, farewell; I am going to the forest.
You should permit me, who have set out to serve sacred <s>tīrthas</s>.
O king, as your younger brother, O <s>Dharmarāja</s>, I cannot endure falsehood.'
Hearing that unwelcome speech, the king, with tears in his eyes, said to him:
'Long ago, O <s>Pārtha</s>, we made the agreement about seeing one another.

children.text: na manyustvayi bhrāturme na cāhaṃ darśitastvayā
children.translated_text: There is no anger toward you from me, your brother; nor was I seen by you.
Since you are guiltless according to my statement, you ought not abandon us.'
Hearing that, the capable son of <s>Śakra</s> said to the king:
'How could a person like me practice <s>dharma</s> by means of a pretext?'
Having said this and taken leave of the king, the son of <s>Pāṇḍu</s> set out,
accompanied by disciplined expounders of sacred knowledge who knew the ancient histories.

children.text: sa gatvā puṇyatīrthāni sevamānaḥ saha dvijaiḥ
children.translated_text: He went to holy <s>tīrthas</s>, visiting them together with Brahmins.
Having reached <s>Gaṅgādvāra</s>, he himself descended to bathe.
There a daughter of the lord of nāgas, seeing him in the form of <s>Manmatha</s>,
born in the family of <s>Airāvata</s>, drew him away, bewildered by desire.

children.text: ulūpī nāma sā kāntā nivedyāsmai nijaṃ kulam
children.translated_text: That lovely woman, named <s>Ulūpī</s>, declared her own lineage to him,
and said to him there, after he had performed the fire rite, "Enjoy me."
Hearing the desire-filled words of that woman with restless eyes,
broad-eyed <s>Pārtha</s>, after reflecting for a moment, spoke.
"O fair-browed one, when you yourself approach as a nectar-stream for the eyes,

children.text: bhajamānaṃ svayaṃ subhru kastvā na bahu manyate ||
children.translated_text: wreathed in waves of beauty, who would not hold you in great esteem?
But I have been consecrated to <s>brahmacarya</s> for twelve years,
and I wander among holy <s>tīrthas</s>; this condition rests on my elder's word."
Hearing these words of <s>Arjuna</s>, the daughter of the serpent-lord
spoke, her breasts dappled by the rays of her eyes lowered in shame.
"Lotus-eyed one, this course of mine is contrary to maidenly conduct,
since I speak even before you like a bold woman.
Lord, I know the whole true account of your vow,
but if one says, 'This applies to your former household,' what use is any further statement?

children.text: rakṣa vā samayaṃ nātha jīvitaṃ vā prayaccha me
children.translated_text: Either preserve your vow, lord, or give me my life.

children.text: yoṣidvadhe ca satye ca cintyatāṃ gurulāghavam ||
children.translated_text: In the killing of a woman and in truth, consider which is weightier and which lighter."
Hearing this from the gazelle-eyed woman, he, affectionate to one who sought his love,
entered into that great festival of union, the essence of playful love.
Then on the next day, after taking leave of that young woman with downcast face,
accomplished <s>Pārtha</s> rose up from the water and went on to the <s>tīrthas</s>.
The <s>Pāṇḍava</s> went to the side of <s>Himavat</s>, and saw the slope of <s>Agastya</s>,
the holy mountain of <s>Vasiṣṭha</s>, and <s>Bhṛgutuṅga</s> as well.
At many sacred <s>tīrthas</s>, that pure-hearted man, restrained in his vow,
gave to Brahmins hundreds of thousands of cows, lands, gold, and houses.

children.text: hiraṇyabindostīrthe ca snātvā prācīṃ diśaṃ yayau
children.translated_text: After bathing at the <s>tīrtha</s> of <s>Hiraṇyabindu</s>, he went to the eastern quarter;
having reached the river <s>Utpalinī</s>, he came to <s>Naimiṣāraṇya</s>.

children.text: nandāmaparanandāṃ ca kauśikīṃ ca gayāṃ tathā
children.translated_text: He passed <s>Nandā</s>, <s>Aparanandā</s>, <s>Kauśikī</s>, and <s>Gayā</s>,
then the <s>Aṅgas</s> and <s>Vaṅgas</s>, and went to the shore of the ocean.
After seeing Mount <s>Mahendra</s>, he went to the city of <s>Maṇipūra</s>,
and stayed there, respectfully honored by King <s>Citravāhana</s>.
There <s>Phalguṇa</s>, his eyes opening wide with joy, saw his daughter,
named <s>Citrāṅgadā</s>, endowed with beauty.
Seeing that moon-faced, slender woman with curving eyes,
even though unpracticed in asking, he requested her from <s>Citravāhana</s>.
When asked by him, that king too, delighted, with joined palms, said:

children.text: dhanyo 'smi pārtha yasya tvaṃ svayaṃ saṃbandhamīhase ||
children.translated_text: "Blessed am I, <s>Pārtha</s>, since you yourself seek kinship with me.
But in our family, by the boon of <s>Śambhu</s>, for the preservation of succession,
the line proceeds only by a single-son sequence; a second offspring is not found.

children.text: seyamekaiva me jātā kanyāpi tanayo yathā
children.translated_text: This one alone has been born to me; though a daughter, she is as a son.

children.text: asyāḥ suto me bhavitā rājye vaṃśavivardhanaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Her son will be mine, increasing the lineage in the kingdom.
Take this daughter of mine for the bride-price of giving the son."
Thus, by that very agreement, he gave her to the son of <s>Pāṇḍu</s>.
Sporting there with her whose eyes were like those of a frightened doe,
he passed three years, each charming with spring.
Then, remembering the agreement, <s>Arjuna</s> took leave of her and departed;
on the southern coast of the ocean he reached the five <s>tīrthas</s>.
There, while bathing at one of them, the hero forcibly pulled up
a very powerful crocodile, like an elephant, fastened to his knee.
Drawn up by him with force, in a moment it became a woman,
her form blooming with the radiance of gleaming divine ornaments.
Questioned by <s>Pārtha</s>, she said, "We are five celestial women.
Having obstructed an ascetic, we became crocodiles through his curse.
'A hero will pull you up and bring about the appeasement of the curse';
when we begged him, he declared this release from the curse.
You yourself are that eminent hero, foretold to us long ago by <s>Nārada</s>.
Today, lord, through heaps of our merit, you have come to this earth.
From this curse, this great danger, I have been carried across by you.
Ocean of compassion, you should rescue the other four as well."
Thus requested by that heavenly woman, the son of <s>Śakra</s>
lifted them from the curse and went again to the city of <s>Maṇipūra</s>.
There, long delighting in the playful sports of <s>Citrāṅgadā</s>,
he wandered in groves of young mango trees, like <s>Smara</s>.
In due time <s>Pārtha</s> begot on her a lotus-eyed son,
named <s>Babhruvāhana</s>, as <s>Maghavan</s> begot <s>Jayanta</s>.

children.text: mātāmahāya taṃ dattvā sa yātaḥ paścimāṃ diśam
children.translated_text: Giving him to his maternal grandfather, he went to the western quarter;
having reached the <s>tīrtha</s> of <s>Prabhāsa</s>, that restrained giver stayed there.
Seeing his dear friend serving that <s>tīrtha</s>, <s>Acyuta</s>

children.text: prītiṃ bheje samabhyetya sahasā tena saṃgataḥ ||
children.translated_text: felt joy, came eagerly, and suddenly met with him.
The two embraced one another, their eyes expanded with joy,
asked each other about their own adventures, and remained filled with affection.

children.text: tatastau rathinau gatvā dṛṣṭvā raivatakaṃ girim
children.translated_text: Then the two chariot-warriors went and saw Mount <s>Raivataka</s>;
joyful, the two heroes entered <s>Dvārakā</s>, crowded with festival.
Honored by <s>Balabhadra</s> and the other foremost <s>Vṛṣṇis</s>,
<s>Arjuna</s> enjoyed himself there with <s>Pradyumna</s> and the rest.
Then <s>Raivataka</s>, adorned with the great festival of pilgrimage...
The Vṛṣṇis, all richly adorned, went together with their beloved women.

children.text: teṣāṃ madhye babhau sragvī kirīṭī bhogakuṇḍalaḥ
children.translated_text: In their midst <s>Kirīṭin</s> shone, garlanded, crowned, and wearing coiled earrings,
like another god of love who had come there to seek her out.
When that throng of women had gone there to the great festival,
<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>'s younger sister, the maiden <s>Subhadrā</s>, graceful in form, shone forth.
Dark, with hands like tender shoots, swarming with bee-like sidelong glances,
and bearing the flowers of smiles, she possessed youth like spring itself.
The doe-eyed girl shone with a necklace white as the moon,
like a stream of fresh youth encircled by a band of foam.
<s>Arjuna</s> saw her, rich in the charm of the abode of love,
as though she were making her own ear-lotus with a mere portion of her glance.
By the spread of her own radiance she made her ornaments seem doubtful,
like the cool-rayed moon-goddess born from the womb of nectar.
Seeing her, a flowering spray on the fortune-tree, moist with playfulness,
<s>Arjuna</s> became the target for showers of arrows from the flower-armed god.
His neck trembled and rolled with wonder born from seeing her,
and he said, "Ah, the graceful beauty of this restless-eyed girl!
It is indivisible, unbounded, uncommon, unsurpassed.
Ah, is it something to be tasted by the eyes, or an elixir for the others?"
Thinking thus with longing, even that steadfast hero again and again became
as if a play-ball for the tremors of love's fever.
Then, while the whole crowd of people was absorbed in the great festival,
the heroic chariot-warrior <s>Jiṣṇu</s>, with <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>'s approval, carried her off.
Then, learning that she had been carried off, all the Vṛṣṇis gathered together
and were shaken, armed for battle, like fires eager to burn.
When their battle-effort began, with golden armor fastened on, horses saddled,
and great bows strung and raised,
as <s>Lāṅgaladhvaja</s>, trembling with anger, reviled <s>Bībhatsu</s>,
his hue like a rainbow made from the gleam of his swinging earrings,
as <s>Ugrasena</s>, heated by fierce, terrible warmth, breathed hard,
and as <s>Sāmba</s>, looking up into the sky, suspected <s>Śambara</s>,
as <s>Cārudeṣṇa</s>'s arm shone with a drawn sword,
and <s>Sāraṇa</s>, eager for heroes, was swift to kill in battle,
as <s>Aniruddha</s> too was armed and <s>Kṛtavarman</s> was altered by fury,
as <s>Akrūra</s> turned cruel and <s>Gada</s> stood with his mace raised,
<s>Hari</s>, remaining silent for a moment, his face unchanged,
said, "At a moment of joy, what is this turmoil of anger among you?
A maiden must inevitably be given to some man endowed with virtues.
Tell me, in this world, who has virtues greater than <s>Arjuna</s>?
For him, the jewel among protectors of the earth, kingship itself is a small price.

children.text: ākhaṇḍalabhuvā tena saṃbandhaḥ kasya na priyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Who would not delight in kinship with him, the son of <s>Ākhaṇḍala</s>?
He is an archer, quick-handed, mighty-armed in battle.
For whom would enmity with <s>Arjuna</s>, with <s>Arjuna</s> himself, bring the fortune of victory?
Let wealth first be sent to him, <s>Subhadrā</s>'s husband,

children.text: preṣyantāṃ draviṇaṃ pūrvaṃ pakṣo 'yaṃ pratibhāti me ||
children.translated_text: with maidservants, horses, chariots, and elephants. This course seems good to me."
Through <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>'s counsel the Dāśārhas quickly abandoned
their anger, as snakes abandon poison when they reach the ground of reflection.
Meanwhile <s>Śvetavāhana</s>, with the wedding performed and his vow for the full time completed,
went eagerly to <s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s>'s presence.
Seeing <s>Arjuna</s> arrived together with <s>Subhadrā</s>,
<s>Dharmasuta</s>, his mind filled with joy, thought the whole world too small.
Then, after bowing to the king and <s>Bhīma</s>, and being greeted by the twins,
he appeased <s>Kṛṣṇā</s>, who was fierce with the hidden poison of jealousy.

children.text: prauḍhā cābhyarthitā tena sā prītimadhikāṃ yayau
children.translated_text: Mature and entreated by him, she came to even greater affection;
for among proud women love increases after the anger born of intimacy.
<s>Subhadrā</s> too approached, bowed at <s>Pṛthā</s>'s feet,
and with affection bowed to <s>Drupadā</s>, who spoke kindly.
Before <s>Pāñcālī</s>, whose eyes widened with affection, <s>Keśava</s>'s sister
shone as a loving woman, like <s>Prīti</s> standing before <s>Rati</s>.
There even the women, with unwinking eyes, drank in <s>Subhadrā</s>,
whose face was the full moon and who was the fire-stick of Love, for a long time.
Then, when <s>Haladhara</s> had taken leave of the <s>Pārthas</s> and gone with his retinue,
<s>Keśihā</s> himself stayed right there out of affection for <s>Arjuna</s>.
<s>Subhadrā</s>, full of love and delighting with <s>Kirīṭin</s>,
in due time gave birth to a lovely lotus-eyed son.
Though still a boy, he was spirited, and so he was remembered as <s>Abhimanyu</s>.
Equal in valor to the two <s>Kṛṣṇas</s>, he grew into a very mighty one.

children.text: sa pituḥ sarvavidyāsu mātulasya ca saṃgamāt
children.translated_text: Through association with his father in all the arts, and with his maternal uncle,
he became heroic also in the sciences, beloved and beautiful as the full moon.
<s>Kṛṣṇā</s> too, in time, bore sons one after another to the sons of <s>Pāṇḍu</s>,
rich in great qualities and equal to <s>Pṛthu</s> in valor.
<s>Prativindhya</s> was the king's son, and <s>Sutasoma</s> was the son of the Wind-god's son;
from <s>Arjuna</s> came <s>Śrutakarman</s>, renowned on earth for his deeds.
From <s>Nakula</s> came <s>Śatānīka</s>, and <s>Śrutasena</s> from the youngest.
Thus these five sons of <s>Pāñcālī</s> became powerful.
While <s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s>, foremost among the bearers of earth, protected the earth,
people became slack in their regard for the deeds of <s>Rāma</s> and the others.
Kings, like elephants maddened by the scent of royalty, clung to the post of his command,
and, brought under control by his splendor, constantly breathed hot sighs.
The greedy were won over by gifts and honors, and the subjects were won over by protection.
and honored people, won over by humility, came to serve his fame.
Through his virtues, prosperity, and generosity, that prosperity was made bright as nectar,
and the people's affection for those two always increased toward him.
Then one day the son of <s>Śakra</s>, together with <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>,
went to the bank of the <s>Yamunā</s>, eager for sport in the water.
There, on a bank where birds called in bowers of moist vañjula creepers,
where the young wind stirred the shoots of the reed-like trees,
that lotus-eyed beloved of <s>Hari</s>, with beloved women such as <s>Subhadrā</s>,
freely sported with streams of water turned into garlands.
The water, with rainbows born from the rays of the jewels on his armlets,
shone as if fallen from clouds of the rainy season.
Then, coming up with <s>Murāri</s> and entering a garden pavilion,
he sat comfortably and listened to the songs of the doe-eyed women.
Amid jokes and playful banter, with yak-tail fans made of the rays of his teeth,
he seemed to cool his beloved women, wearied by their games.
Then a certain Brahmin arrived, filled with a mass of his own splendor,
like <s>Parameṣṭhin</s>, his form tawny as if with pollen from the lotus of his garment.
Seeing him, as if majesty embodied or the golden mountain walking,
the two <s>Kṛṣṇas</s> rose from their jeweled seats with joined palms.

children.text: sa copasṛtya śanakaiḥ svastivādaṃ vidhāya ca
children.translated_text: He approached slowly, uttered words of blessing,
and said, "I am a Brahmin who eats much, yet I am hungry from scant food.
I have come to you two, having heard that you are generous." After hearing the Brahmin's words,
<s>Pārtha</s> and the <s>Vārṣṇeya</s> said, "Name the food that is dear to you."
Then the Brahmin spoke again, making his real form visible:
"I am <s>Pāvaka</s>; I wish to burn this <s>Khāṇḍava</s> forest.
<s>Takṣaka</s> lives here, a beloved friend of <s>Śakra</s>.

children.text: tatprītyā guptamindreṇa praveṣṭuṃ nāsti me gatiḥ ||
children.translated_text: Because it is guarded by <s>Indra</s> out of affection for him, I have no way to enter.
Therefore I ask for the forest, freed from the masses of clouds sent by <s>Śakra</s>,
held back by nets of arrows released from your arms.
Thus the dark-tracked Fire asked <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> and <s>Arjuna</s> there,
and saying, "Good," they armed themselves for what he desired.
There was a king named <s>Śvetakī</s>, delight of the <s>Ikṣvāku</s> line,
whose fire blazed continually in a twelve-year sacrificial session.
His officiating priests, wearied by the extensive rites and many sacrificial enclosures,
went away with their eyesight destroyed by the dense smoke of ghee.
Abandoned by his priests, he propitiated <s>Śaṃkara</s> through asceticism;
then, in the twelve-year sacrifice appointed for him by the three-eyed god,
the Fire obtained sluggishness from unbroken streams of ghee.
With dimmed radiance and weakened, he fell into loss of appetite through that torpor.
Commanded by <s>Brahmā</s>, he came to burn <s>Khāṇḍava</s>, rich in living beings,
thinking, "The sluggishness produced by ghee is calmed only by forest fare."
With this intention, the Fire then blazed forth in <s>Khāṇḍava</s>.
But again and again <s>Pākaśāsana</s> quickly, with hail-bearing clouds,
brought him to extinction; because of that he remained ill for a long time.

children.text: tataḥ kālena sa prāpya naranārāyaṇau bhuvi ||
children.translated_text: Then, in time, he encountered <s>Nara</s> and <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> on earth.
Delighted, and instructed by the four-faced god for stopping the obstruction of rain,
<s>Pārtha</s> said to him, "Lord, I do indeed possess divine weapons,
but I have no bow fit for the task, suitable for battle.
With an ordinary chariot here, and with arrows that run out,
even though equipped, I am merely ready for your work.
And for the stout strength of <s>Murāri</s>'s mighty arm
there is no weapon equal to his prowess and capable of your task."
Hearing <s>Arjuna</s>'s words, <s>Anala</s> said, "I will give them,"

children.text: sasmāra varuṇaṃ devaṃ sa ca dhyātaḥ samāyayau ||
children.translated_text: and remembered the god <s>Varuṇa</s>; when meditated upon, he came.
Prompted by Fire, he then gave <s>Gāṇḍīva</s> to the son of <s>Pāṇḍu</s>,
along with two inexhaustible quivers and a chariot like a city.
In it broad, tall horses with the speed of wind
shone, moon-white, like autumn clouds in the sky.

children.text: sudarśanaṃ ca kṛṣṇāya cakraṃ kaumodakīṃ tathā
children.translated_text: He also gave <s>Sudarśana</s>, the discus, and <s>Kaumodakī</s> to <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>,
and, after taking leave of <s>Kṛśānu</s>, the lord of the waters departed.

children.text: somena rājñā vijitaṃ purā yena jagattrayam
children.translated_text: With that bow King <s>Soma</s> had formerly conquered the three worlds;
obtaining it, <s>Arjuna</s> shone like <s>Tripurāri</s>.
Then <s>Dhanaṃjaya</s> mounted the chariot, which resounded like the great elements,
gleaming with the brilliance of gold and jewels, and bearing a terrible monkey-banner.
He said to Fire, "Be ready; enter <s>Khāṇḍava</s>."
As the son of <s>Pāṇḍu</s>, together with <s>Janārdana</s>, spoke joyfully,
the seven-rayed Fire went with those two to the great forest.
Then <s>Dhūmaketu</s> himself quickly blazed up in <s>Khāṇḍava</s>.
With flame-tossed tongues, as if terrifying the world,
the sky became darkened with smoke and filled with crests of fire.
The quarters, beyond comparison even with rākṣasas whose beards and hair are blazing,
appeared all around with flames slanting across them.
As if with freshly melted golden waves of <s>Meru</s>,
when that forest was seized in a moment by <s>Citrabhānu</s>,
all the trees became like blossoming kiṃśukas and aśokas.
Then a crackling roar arose, striking against the sky,
terrible, like the breaking of knots at the start of the cosmic egg's bursting,
in some places forming heaps, in some places playing among the creepers.
In places the spreading tongues of the fire's flames reached the peacocks,
with swarms of scorched, crackling insects, as the swiftly drying fire advanced.
In the thickets it quickly obtained them like full offerings of sesame,
while the severed tips of the fire's flames clung to the courtyard of the sky.
They produced the illusion that golden aerial cars of sky-going beings were moving about.

children.text: tataḥ pravṛtte bhūtānāṃ medasā vimale tale ||
children.translated_text: Then, when the pure ground began to be covered with the fat of creatures,
the world, with smokeless circles of flame, seemed to have become golden.
Then there arose a terrible cry of "kaha-kaha" from the eater of oblations,
like the lament of the quarters being licked by his flames.
Clusters of sparks from the fire wandered about with flickering brilliance,
as if they were the souls of burned beings traveling through the sky.
The forest-dwellers, their bodies half scorched, fled away,
and hosts of beings cried out, fearing the fire of cosmic dissolution.
The maned crests of the lions became encircled by flames,
as if marked with sprays of blood from the bursting temples of rutting elephants.
For a moment the huge-bodied leaders of elephant herds, as they burned,
wandered about as if covered with broad seals of gold.
Cut down on every side by <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> and <s>Arjuna</s> with circles of arrows,
all the forest creatures, their paths blocked, fell into the fire.
Then, hearing that <s>Khāṇḍava</s> was burning, the lord of the gods
came himself, surrounded by clouds, and saw it.
The sky was crowded with lightning and clouds, and the forest was covered with flame and smoke;
each became a fitting comparison for the other, terrifying to beings.
As the creatures were being struck down by <s>Kirīṭin</s> with the <s>Gāṇḍīva</s>,
<s>Takṣaka</s>, out of fear, had already gone away to <s>Kurukṣetra</s>.
His beloved serpent-wife, terrified, swallowed his son,
named <s>Aśvasena</s>, and fled, betrayed by the tail that remained outside.
But the <s>Pāṇḍava</s>, seeing that tail, cut it off,
skillfully, with a broad-edged arrow, greatly angered by the deception.
"May you have no secure standing in the future," <s>Arjuna</s> cursed him.
And <s>Vāsudeva</s> approached <s>Pāvaka</s>, who had surged forth.
Then the lord of the winds, with streams of rain as thick as arms,
seemed to set up a mass of crystal pillars in the sky.
But the rain released by <s>Ākhaṇḍala</s> was blocked in a moment by <s>Savyasācin</s>
with a net of arrows, and it ceased under the heat of the fire.
Then <s>Śatamanyu</s>, enraged, together with the gods who had lifted their weapons,
covered <s>Dhanaṃjaya</s> with a shower of divine missiles.
Swiftly warding off those missiles with counter-missiles, <s>Śvetavāhana</s>
fought all the gods, filling the sky with arrows.
Then <s>Pārtha</s> reduced to sesame-sized fragments, with his arrows,
the peak of Mount <s>Mandara</s>, its rocks kindled with flame, which <s>Śakra</s> had hurled.
When the host of gods had been conquered by <s>Arjuna</s>, the lord of the gods,
seated on <s>Airāvaṇa</s>, shone as if painted in a picture, from astonishment.

children.text: tamuvāca nabhovāṇī śakra mā sāhasaṃ kṛthāḥ
children.translated_text: A voice from the sky said to him, "<s>Śakra</s>, do not act rashly.

children.text: takṣakaste suhṛnnātra sthito yuddhena kiṃ vṛthā ||
children.translated_text: <s>Takṣaka</s>, your friend, is not present here; what is the use of fighting in vain?

children.text: naranārāyaṇau devau kṛṣṇau te viditau dhruvam
children.translated_text: Surely you know that these two dark heroes are the gods <s>Nara</s> and <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>.

children.text: etau na jetuṃ samare śakyau śakraśatairapi ||
children.translated_text: These two cannot be conquered in battle even by hundreds of <s>Śakras</s>."
Hearing this, <s>Śakra</s> departed, his neck bent in shame,
yet delighted when he saw his son superior to his own might in battle.
Then the blessed <s>Pāvaka</s> swallowed the forest-dwellers,
the <s>bhūtas</s>, <s>yakṣas</s>, <s>daityas</s>, <s>rākṣasas</s>, and serpents, their bodies shattered by torrents of <s>Arjuna</s>'s arrows.
Having made them his morsels, he regained his health,
as if announcing his joy with flames that were no longer disturbed.
Then from the house of <s>Takṣaka</s>, <s>Maya</s>, lord of the <s>daityas</s>, rose up;
as he fled in terror, the fire, with long arms of flame, rushed after him swiftly.
It crept forward, shaking the world with its heavy, furious roars,
and looked like smoky <s>Kṛtānta</s>, a black serpent.
<s>Maya</s>, seeing the angry fire pursuing him from behind,
and the wielder of the discus ready to strike, cried to <s>Jaya</s>, "Protect me!"

children.text: taṃ pārthaḥ śaraṇaṃ yātaṃ rarakṣa karuṇānidhiḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Pārtha</s>, a treasury of compassion, protected him when he came for refuge;
it is not the conduct of great souls to turn away from rescuing the afflicted.
Thus <s>Maya</s> and <s>Aśvasena</s> were released from that great danger,
and four <s>Śārṅgaka</s> birds were protected by <s>Agni</s> himself.
Long ago there was a celibate sage named <s>Mandapāla</s>,
into whose mind the sacred sciences, knowers of revelation, entered of themselves.
In time he gave up his body and went to the abode of the gods,
but, being without a son, he did not obtain the worlds won by asceticism.
At the command of the gods he went to the earth for the sake of sons,
and, uniting with a bird-wife, he obtained four sons.
When his sons were in <s>Khāṇḍava</s>, that great sage
knew that the danger from fire had arrived and praised <s>Pāvaka</s>.
The blessed <s>Anala</s>, pleased by that hymn, did not burn them,
though their mother had abandoned them from fear and they had to remain by themselves.
After sparing the young <s>Śārṅgika</s> sons of <s>Mandapāla</s>,
the lord of the gods then came together with them, amazed by that deed.

children.text: astrāṇi pārtha dāsyāmi kāle te rudradarśinaḥ
children.translated_text: "<s>Pārtha</s>, I shall give you weapons at the proper time, when you have seen <s>Rudra</s>;
there will be imperishable affection between you and <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, the son of <s>Pāṇḍu</s>."
Having granted this boon to the two of them, he departed, pleased, to heaven.
Then, having addressed <s>Vahni</s> and being satisfied, <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> and the <s>Pāṇḍava</s>
went to the region they desired, which had attained the splendor of a golden mountain.
And the two <s>Kṛṣṇas</s>, descending from their chariots on the bank of a cascade,
found rest amid breezes from young plantain leaves.
Because of King <s>Śvetaketu</s>, who had sacrificed for many years,
<s>Pāvaka</s>, ceaselessly drinking ghee, had fallen into heaviness.
Through the valor of <s>Jiṣṇu</s> and the power of the enemy of demons,
he cast it off by burning <s>Khāṇḍava</s>, and became fit for oblations.

children.text: iti hutabhugakāṇḍe prauḍhapārtheṣu pakṣānilabahulavilāsaḥ khāṇḍavaṃ nirdadāha
children.translated_text: Thus, in the section on the Fire-eater, when <s>Pārtha</s> had grown mighty, with abundant play of winds from wings, he burned <s>Khāṇḍava</s>;
and, violently distressing the world, he checked <s>Ākhaṇḍala</s>'s rain with masses of <s>Vijaya</s>'s arrow-canopy.
Having bowed to <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> and to <s>Nara</s>, the best of men,
to the goddess <s>Sarasvatī</s> and to <s>Vyāsa</s>, one should then proclaim <s>Jaya</s>.
At <s>Abhimanyu</s>'s wedding, gathered with many kinsmen,
the <s>Pāṇḍavas</s> entered <s>Virāṭa</s>'s jewel-bright assembly hall.
With the foremost <s>Vṛṣṇis</s> and <s>Pāñcālas</s> seated on golden thrones,

children.text: babhāse sā sabhā vīrair dyaur ivāmaraśekharaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: that assembly shone with heroes like heaven with the chiefs of the immortals.
There <s>Janārdana</s> and <s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s>, seated on one throne,
made the hall lovely with their own rays, like beryl and gold.
When <s>Ajātaśatru</s>, after a long time, stood as a friend rich in prosperity,
the lotus-petal eyes of the kings came into bloom.
