Then the dark-cloud-hued <s>Acyuta</s>, a cloud flashing with the rays of the <s>Kaustubha</s>, spoke,
as though making the peacocks in the palace gardens dance.
He shone, the quarters tinged by the gleam of his clear teeth,
as if scattering rays of the <s>Pāñcajanya</s> that had been drunk in.
"What is known to these lion-like kings is nevertheless being said again;
it is the outburst of a force of anger long stored within.
In this assembly of kings, the offenses of the <s>Kauravas</s> cannot be counted,
and the seizure of <s>Kṛṣṇā</s>'s hair stands displayed as their banner.
Even so, when a goal can be achieved by conciliation, good men do not approve punishment.

children.text: ko hi hastāvaceyeṣu padmeṣu paraśuṃ kṣipet ||
children.translated_text: Who would throw an axe at lotuses that can be plucked by hand?"
Hearing this, the plough-bearer, white as <s>Kailāsa</s>, spoke,
casting out, with the rays of his teeth, what seemed a digit of the moon from the milk-ocean:
"What this kinsman of the worlds, <s>Kamalā</s>'s lord, has said,

children.text: tadeva matamasmākaṃ kva vinā sāma siddhayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: that alone is our view. Where are successes without conciliation?
Who, after killing enemies who could be brought round by conciliation, would make fame,
the mirror for the adornment of fortune, stained by sighs of remorse?
Splendor obtained by the killing of one's own kin does not shine, even when it has arisen,
like a severed nose stuck on with flesh taken from one's own cheeks.
Fortune won by cruel action, after standing like a flame of fire,
afterwards quickly departs, producing darkness with the collyrium of defilement.
Blessed are the sons of <s>Kuru</s> rejoicing in the houses of <s>Ajātaśatru</s>,
and the sons of <s>Pṛthā</s> delighting in <s>Hastināpura</s> of the Kaurava lord.
Blessed are they who, in the garden of kinsmen's houses, unconstrained with one another,
after meals go to the private chambers, witnessed by the jests of lovely women.
Innocent women, wine, secret music on the lute, and sweet songs,
a gathering with friends and relatives: these are the fruit of the wish-granting tree of merit.
For men whose treasuries and allies are exhausted, who hate the opening moves of policy,
and who are mounted upon death, bloodshed in battle comes first."
When <s>Rauhiṇeya</s> had spoken thus, <s>Sātyaki</s>, true in valor,
his earrings dancing on cheeks trembling about a face contracted with anger,
then spoke, while on his chest, where a pearl necklace rolled over sword-scars,
he again and again tossed up his white upper garment:
"Ah! This smooth speech is uttered by one whose honor has fallen far away.
How could words harsh with attack come from men whose pride is wretched?
When men's minds grow affectionate toward an enemy whose only remedy is slaughter,
that is extreme cowardice in those whose proud swords have not been wearied.
Men fond of battle do not listen to words of those who seek peace under the pretext of welfare,
with their standing hidden by fear and their syllables scarcely touching the lips.
The proud are gentle before friends and bowed in love toward high-spirited women,
but they are hard in crushing enemies, swollen with courage.
For those who have not drawn sword or bow and have forgotten notorious offenses,
fortune gained by conciliation arranged through begging is a bracelet for a severed hand.
A royal serpent whose <s>hālāhala</s> poison of anger has been abandoned through ministers' counsel
is killed by enemies, if cowards are his authorities.

children.text: rūḍhasnehāḥ parārtheṣu na te śāmyanti kauravāḥ
children.translated_text: The <s>Kauravas</s>, deeply attached to others' goods, will not grow calm
until <s>Gāṇḍīva</s> comes under the pressure of the staff-like arm of the <s>Pāṇḍava</s>.
Until, by the sidelong glances of battle-fortune, those men are pierced
with feathered arrows reaching to the ear, they will not take on redness.
These arrows of mine, thirst born from the heat of the fire of anger,
will not find satisfaction without drinking the blood from the breasts of the <s>Kauravas</s>.
<s>Bhīṣma</s>, <s>Droṇa</s>, and <s>Kṛpa</s>, covered with the dust of shame flashing from their endurance of <s>Kṛṣṇā</s>'s humiliation,
surely desire a bath in a river of blood.
Having spoken thus, <s>Sātyaki</s> at once became a face of knitted brows,
bearing the form of an ocean from which <s>Kālakūṭa</s> poison had arisen.
Then, while the kings' heads were eager to taste those words,
<s>Drupada</s> too, turning toward <s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s>, began to speak:

children.text: hariryadāha rāmaśca sa evādya satāṃ kramaḥ
children.translated_text: "What <s>Hari</s> and <s>Rāma</s> have said: that indeed is now the way of good men.

children.text: sātyakiḥ śauryasadṛśaṃ dhanyaṃ kiṃ vā prabhāṣatām ||
children.translated_text: Let <s>Sātyaki</s> say something blessed and worthy of his valor.
When easily accomplished measures are being praised, the wise become unable to define them;
but that fire of anger will not be extinguished without the weapons of the enemies' beloved women.

children.text: rājñā dūtā visṛjyantāṃ kṛtakaṃ sāma cārthyatām
children.translated_text: Let messengers be sent by the king, and let a feigned conciliation be requested.
Having placed his feet in two positions, he should consider and then resort to one.
Let <s>Dhṛṣṭaketu</s> be brought, and king <s>Senābindu</s>,
and <s>Bhagadatta</s>, that ally of <s>Indra</s> in the battle with the demons,
and <s>Śalya</s>, who is like a thorn to the enemy, and <s>Jayatsena</s> of <s>Magadha</s>,
the five <s>Kekaya</s> brothers, and <s>Yudhāmanyu</s> and <s>Uttamaujas</s>.

children.text: ityuktvā drupado rājā virarāma dhiyā nidhiḥ
children.translated_text: Having spoken thus, king <s>Drupada</s>, a treasure-house of intelligence, fell silent.
With <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>'s approval, messengers were dispatched, and they went to the kings.
Then, at <s>Murāri</s>'s word, <s>Drupada</s> addressed his own priest, who was not weak,
an embodied mass of vigor with visible form:
"Best of twice-born men, go and ask that lord of the Kauravas for conciliation
without obstruction, before his army comes to fullness.

children.text: vaktuṃ tvameva jānīṣe vicitraṃ laghu sāravat
children.translated_text: You alone know how to speak in a varied way, briefly and with substance."
Sent by the king of the <s>Pāñcālas</s>, he went to the <s>Kurus</s>.
When he had gone, <s>Madhuripu</s>, with the other heroes of the <s>Vṛṣṇis</s>,
took leave of the sons of <s>Pāṇḍu</s> and the <s>Mātsya</s> king, and went to <s>Dvārakā</s>.

children.text: atṛptā darśane tasya pārthāḥ saṃstambhya mānasam
children.translated_text: The <s>Pārthas</s>, still unsated with the sight of him, steadied their minds
and, on their kinsman's advice, set about gathering forces.
Meanwhile <s>Dhārtarāṣṭra</s> and <s>Śvetāśva</s>, eager for battle,

children.text: jagmatuḥ keśavaṃ tulyaṃ sāhāyyaṃ yācituṃ raṇe ||
children.translated_text: went to <s>Keśava</s> equally, to ask for aid in war.
The two reached <s>Dvārakā</s>, whose mansions glittered with jewels
and which shone on all sides with ministers, like the city of the Kaurava.
They entered <s>Śauri</s>'s inner apartment, the pleasure-house of <s>Śrī</s>,
pervaded by rays from blue gems like streaming plumes of incense-smoke.
There they saw <s>Keśinisūdana</s> asleep
on a clear crystal couch, like another Ocean of Milk.
As he slept gently, the Kaurava sat there at his head,
while <s>Phalguṇa</s> sat in front at his lotus feet.
Then the Lord awoke and first saw <s>Dhanaṃjaya</s>,
his joined hands touching his crown, blazing with tremendous splendor.
After receiving his salutation and asking <s>Savyasācin</s> about his welfare,
he also saw <s>Suyodhana</s>, whose shoulder was resting near the pillow of the couch.
When the two entreated him, "May you be our ally in war,"
the god turned around and spoke with his face toward the Kaurava:
"You arrived first, while <s>Śvetavāhana</s> came last;
but because he was seen first, <s>Pārtha</s> shall choose me.
There is an <s>akṣauhiṇī</s> of the <s>Vṛṣṇis</s>, and I am a non-combatant, O king.
Knowing the two shares as equal, take the <s>akṣauhiṇī</s> as you wish."
Thus addressed by <s>Śauri</s>, the delighted <s>Suyodhana</s>, smiling, said, "So be it,"
thinking the <s>Vṛṣṇi</s> army to be the greater share.
Taking that army, guarded by <s>Kṛtavarman</s> and the others,
and permitted by <s>Keśava</s>, he went to <s>Hastināpura</s>.
<s>Arjuna</s> too, having obtained <s>Hari</s>, who had renounced battle by his word,
and was bound by a vow to serve as charioteer, thought he had gained the earth.
Then <s>Śvetavāhana</s>, after taking leave of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>,
went to <s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s>'s presence, accompanied by a small but swift-footed retinue.
Meanwhile the Kaurava carried off <s>Śalya</s>, who had come to aid the son of <s>Dharma</s>,
with hidden honors and banquets made to seem equal.
By many kinds of dancing and singing, garlands, jewels, choice garments,
and royal services, all arranged in various ways along the roads,
he was first served by him and accepted his alliance;
then, with his neck bent crooked by shame, he went sorrowfully to the son of <s>Dharma</s>.
Honored respectfully by <s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s>, he then described
how he had been carried off by the lord of the Kauravas through deceptive hospitality.
After hearing from <s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s> about <s>Kṛṣṇā</s>'s suffering at the dice-game,
the exile, and the other sorrows of those men, the king of <s>Madra</s> spoke at the end of the tale:

children.text: purā triśirasaṃ śakraḥ sutaṃ tvaṣṭuḥ prajāpateḥ
children.translated_text: "Long ago <s>Śakra</s> had the three-headed son of <s>Prajāpati</s> <s>Tvaṣṭṛ</s>,
who was practicing fierce austerity, killed, because he feared that vow.
Then, angered, <s>Tvaṣṭṛ</s> again created a son named <s>Vṛtra</s>,

children.text: tapasā yena vijitāḥ surāḥ śarma na lebhire ||
children.translated_text: by whose ascetic power the conquered gods found no peace.
In battle, having lightly swallowed the heroic wielder of the thunderbolt,
he stood with unchanged face, consecrated to the destruction of the gods.
Through a destiny appointed by the Creator, when his face was bent down in a yawn,
the lord of the Thirty, his limbs contracted, suddenly came out.
Then <s>Balanisūdana</s>, taking refuge in <s>Viṣṇu</s>, conqueror of the enemies of the gods,
obtained counsel on the means for killing him.

children.text: sāmnā sakhyaṃ samādāya sa vṛtreṇa tarasvinā
children.translated_text: By conciliation he made friendship with mighty <s>Vṛtra</s>,
and constantly pondered a hidden opening for bringing him down.
Then, when he was absorbed in twilight meditation, <s>Śakra</s>, with <s>Viṣṇu</s>'s permission,
killed mighty <s>Vṛtra</s> with foam that had the thunderbolt within it.
When he had been killed, <s>Śakra</s> was overcome by terrible <s>brahmahatyā</s> (the sin of killing a brahmin),
and, his heart whirling in distress, he found no confidence anywhere.
His self overturned by sin, he went to an exceedingly vast lake,
and, dwelling in the tender fibers of lotuses, he became filled with remorse.
Then King <s>Nahuṣa</s>, occupying <s>Śakra</s>'s station and greater than <s>Vāsava</s>,
was surrounded by the gods together with siddhas and sages in the vacant abode of the gods.
Deluded by his new sovereignty, he solicited <s>Śacī</s>.
Fools, having obtained a great station, pursue their own destruction.

children.text: sā satī balinā tena yācyamānā punaḥ punaḥ
children.translated_text: That faithful woman, repeatedly importuned by that powerful one,

children.text: guruṃ bṛhaspatiṃ patyuḥ prayayau śaraṇaṃ śacī ||
children.translated_text: <s>Śacī</s> went for refuge to her husband's guru, <s>Bṛhaspati</s>.
Going there at his word, and approaching from afar what had been pointed out,
she saw the lord of the <s>Maruts</s> hidden inside that lake.
Seen by his beloved while he was in distress, he sighed in sorrow,
and, knowing the course of events, spoke to her whose eyes were blurred with tears:
"That arrogant, very wrathful <s>Nahuṣa</s>, an elephant among kings,
cannot be destroyed by force, lotus-eyed one.

children.text: gatvā tvaṃ yuktimāsthāya brūhi taṃ manmathāntaram
children.translated_text: Go, adopt a stratagem, and with a pretext of love tell him:
'Mount a carriage of the Seven Sages and come to me at your pleasure.'"
Thus instructed by her husband, <s>Paulomī</s>, moving secretly,
quickly came to <s>Nahuṣa</s> and made that very agreement with him.
Then <s>Nahuṣa</s>, king of the gods, made the sages his chariot and set out;
in his haste he touched <s>Agastya</s> with the tip of his foot, saying, "Crawl on!"
Then, fallen by the curse of that great sage in anger,
he attained serpent-hood itself, from which you formerly released him.
At the guru's word, <s>Purandara</s> cast off his brahmanicide
among rivers, women, trees, and mountains; then, restored to health, he was free from distress.
There, entreated by the gods and made stainless by the guru's word,
<s>Indra</s>, regaining his own kingdom, rejoiced together with his beloved.
Those who hear this tale of <s>Indra</s>'s victory when undertaking victory
obtain victory without fail; therefore I have told it to you."
Hearing what was thus spoken by the king of <s>Madra</s>, the victory-seeking
<s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s> bowed with humility and calmly replied:
"Though you have taken refuge with the Kuru side, accomplish this task:
continually disparage the charioteer's son's splendor and bring about its destruction."
Then <s>Śalya</s> promised, "So be it," and set out toward the Kurus,
displaying a world-girdling array with masses like rows of elephants' temples.
Meanwhile <s>Garuḍadhvaja</s> came to the sons of <s>Pāṇḍu</s>,
as did <s>Sātyaki</s>, <s>Cekitāna</s>, and <s>Jayatsena</s> the <s>Māgadha</s>.
The <s>Kekayas</s>, <s>Dhṛṣṭaketu</s>, and King <s>Kuntibhoja</s> came too,
making the earth impassable with their vast armies.
Those forces, with elephants as crocodiles and unchecked waves of weapons,
entered the ocean of <s>Pārtha</s>'s army and seemed to become hard to distinguish.
As the armies of the <s>Pāṇḍavas</s> and of their enemies gradually increased,
that resolute priest entered the assembly of the Kuru king.
He entered the assembly attended by <s>Bhīṣma</s>, <s>Karṇa</s>, <s>Kṛpa</s>, <s>Droṇa</s>, <s>Śalya</s>, and <s>Bāhlika</s>,
a cave of lion-like kings, and received honor.
After asking after everyone's welfare, and after obtaining in proper order his turn to speak,
the brahman spoke, his mind fearless through the flash of eloquence:
"As the earth came by succession to <s>Dhṛtarāṣṭra</s> and <s>Pāṇḍu</s>,

children.text: tannāma viditaṃ loke yathā cātmā tathātmajaḥ ||
children.translated_text: that is known in the world; and as one's self is, so is one's son.

children.text: bhavadbhiḥ svecchayā dattāmapi pārthaḥ kṛśāṃ śriyam
children.translated_text: Even the slight prosperity given by you at your pleasure, <s>Pārtha</s>
brought to fullness, as the bright fortnight fills out the digit of the moon.

children.text: yathāsya sā hṛtā naiva tadvaktuṃ matameti naḥ
children.translated_text: How that same prosperity was taken from him, we do not think it fitting to say;
for those who have not forgotten insults do not lack power.
The term of forest-dwelling is complete, and the concealed residence has been passed through.
Let a livelihood be arranged for us by our grandsire and uncles, according to our own share."

children.text: iti yaudhiṣṭhiraṃ vipraḥ saṃdeśaṃ vinivedya saḥ
children.translated_text: Having delivered this message from <s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s>,
the brahman, knowing the signs of kings, fixed his gaze on their faces.
Then the wise son of <s>Śantanu</s>, filled with joy, said:

children.text: diṣṭyā śamārthinaḥ pārthā diṣṭyā necchanti saṃgaram ||
children.translated_text: "Fortunately the <s>Pārthas</s> seek peace; fortunately they do not desire battle.
Fortunately the great chariot-warriors have not entered the fire of <s>Gāṇḍīva</s>;
fortunately all the kings of the earth have been forgotten by Death."
As <s>Gāṅgeya</s> was speaking thus, <s>Karṇa</s> spoke in anger,
his tree-like arms restless as the tucked edge of his garment slipped in agitation:
"If the <s>Pāṇḍavas</s>, conquered and pitiable, are begging,
why, grandfather, is your joy filled with such a deep roar?
The <s>Pāṇḍavas</s> are always raised high by your praises;
yet in every land there are great chariot-warriors a thousand times their equal."
Hearing <s>Karṇa</s>'s words, <s>Bhīṣma</s> said with a smiling face:

children.text: aho nu vallabho mantrī hitamābhāṣase prabhoḥ ||
children.translated_text: "Ah indeed, a beloved counselor! You speak what is beneficial for your lord.

children.text: na śaktāḥ samare sthātuṃ na cecchanti śamaṃ khalāḥ
children.translated_text: The wicked are unable to stand in battle, yet they do not wish for peace;
surely, fallen from both positions, their sole practice is slander.
It is strange, <s>Rādheya</s>, that you do not wish for friendship, though his valor
was seen by you yourself in the <s>Ghoṣayātrā</s> and at the cattle raid."
When <s>Gāṅgeya</s> had spoken thus, the king whose eye was wisdom
reflected, and then spoke humbly, after seeking the grandsire's approval:

children.text: amīṣāṃ bhūmipālānāṃ kṛtsnasya ca kulasya naḥ
children.translated_text: "The son of <s>Śantanu</s> has spoken the true welfare
of these rulers of the earth and of our whole family, for he sees the future.
Go, <s>Saṃjaya</s>; approach the righteous king <s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s>
and speak to him in my words, in the way by which he desires friendship.
For even after reflecting, I see no fault at all in him."
That wise son of <s>Dharma</s> should be addressed by you with whatever is fitting.
Thus instructed by <s>Vaicitravīrya</s>, the noble-minded son of <s>Gāvalgāni</s>
went to the sons of <s>Pāṇḍu</s>, accompanied by the priest.
In a swift chariot he came to the <s>Pāṇḍavas</s>, worn down by calamity,
and, reaching them gradually, entered the assembly hall.
Approaching <s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s>, together with <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, <s>Bhīma</s>, and <s>Dhanaṃjaya</s>,
and with the <s>Cedi</s>, <s>Sṛñjaya</s>, <s>Pāñcāla</s>, <s>Matsya</s>, <s>Māgadha</s>, and <s>Kekaya</s> chiefs,
to the assembly that shone, its faces like ornaments gleaming with their own radiance,
<s>Saṃjaya</s> bowed, proclaiming his own name.
After asking about the welfare of the family of kinsmen, the king then said:
"Do the foremost of the <s>Kurus</s> remember us, together with our wives?
Tell me, <s>Saṃjaya</s>: against the fire of hostility, grown great, with the waters of appeasement,
is the king intent on remedy? For an undertaking headed by conciliation is best.
Surely he does not begin a course of action by which, scorched by regret,
he would again and again with his sighs dim the pearl necklace of his fame?
Seeing his own fortune, broad with masses of rutting elephants,

children.text: api vīkṣya na tādṛśi vetyāyūṃṣi vahantyasau ||
children.translated_text: does he not understand that lives do not last in such a condition?
Does the son of <s>Ambikā</s>, looking on us with the feeling of kinsmen,
not stand by his son's words, which portend the sole destruction of the family?"
Hearing these clear and sweet words of the king,
<s>Saṃjaya</s> said, "The lord of the <s>Kauravas</s> acts rightly in every respect.
The <s>Kurus</s>, wearing forbearance like the necklace of a noble bride, are free from guilt;
they will remain so, if without war you will come to satisfaction.
Great men do not praise war, a cage of uncertainty;
even victory gained here through the destruction of friends and kinsmen is defeat.

children.text: athavā manyunā vyāpto vartase yadi niṣkṛpaḥ
children.translated_text: Or, if you are overcome by anger and live without pity,
then why were the restraints of forest dwelling endured in vain?

children.text: yadi dharmaḥ pramāṇaṃ te na syātsaralacetasaḥ
children.translated_text: If <s>dharma</s> (righteous order) were not your authority, you of straightforward mind,
then all the <s>Kurus</s> would already have ceased to exist through the wrath of <s>Bhīma</s> and <s>Arjuna</s>.

children.text: sarvakṣayaphale yuddhe vibhūtyai mā kṛthā matim
children.translated_text: Do not set your mind on prosperity in war, whose fruit is the destruction of all;
the fortunes of men like you shine when ornamented only by freedom from greed."
When <s>Saṃjaya</s> had spoken thus, the son of <s>Dharma</s> replied,
revealing, with the brightness of his teeth, what seemed his own clear intention:
"When have you ever heard from us speech that seeks war?
Frightened by the destruction of the world, you should not speak to us in this way.
Our own fortune must not be abandoned, and our kinsmen must be protected;
in this matter, unsteady as a swing, <s>Janārdana</s> is our authority."
When <s>Dharmarāja</s> had spoken, the lord of <s>Kamalā</s> said:
"Now, <s>Saṃjaya</s>, war depends on you people, or on me.
If the <s>Kaurava</s> would act properly toward these <s>Pāṇḍavas</s>,
who desire no war and ask for only five villages,
but if it is otherwise, then by masses of arrows released from <s>Gāṇḍīva</s>
you will see your own army made fierce by the dance of headless trunks."

children.text: iti śaurervacaḥ śrutvā sānujasya ca bhūpateḥ
children.translated_text: Hearing the words of <s>Śauri</s> and of the king together with his younger brothers,
<s>Saṃjaya</s>, having received permission, quickly went back toward the <s>Kurus</s>.
He went to <s>Hāstinapura</s>, to the palace of <s>Dhṛtarāṣṭra</s>,
and at day's end, weary from the road, entered after being announced by the doorkeeper.
After reporting to him the welfare of the mighty <s>Pāṇḍavas</s>,
he said, "I shall speak their message in the morning," and went to his own house.
When he had gone, the king, suspicious, sleepless, and troubled by remorse,
summoned <s>Vidura</s> and asked what would be good for himself.
"Today <s>Saṃjaya</s> has gone to the heroic sons of <s>Pāṇḍu</s> and returned;

children.text: jāne naitadvacaḥ prātaḥ sabhāyāṃ kiṃ nu vakṣyati ||
children.translated_text: I do not know what speech he will deliver in the assembly tomorrow morning."
Hearing this, the chamberlain said, "O king, why are you distressed?
What misfortune has come upon you, though you are intelligent and learned?
One whose aim is unfulfilled does not obtain sleep, like a lover with an unattainable woman,
or a weak man overcome by the strong, or a thief whose reckoning has changed.
No one dissatisfied over another's wealth can set his mind at rest;
for wakefulness is hard to ward off for those scorched by deep craving.
Men of auspicious character, free from the joy and anger born of conflict,

children.text: cintājvareṇa spṛśyante na hi nāma manīṣiṇaḥ ||
children.translated_text: wise men, indeed, are not touched by the fever of anxiety.

children.text: vikāro lakṣyate yena na saṃpatsu vipaścitā
children.translated_text: That by which no alteration is seen in the wise amid prosperity,
and by which one crosses difficulties: that they call wisdom.
The dreadful state that houses every doubt and is a great abode of misfortune,
that spreads darkness and is terrible: learned men do not resort to it.
Judgment in counsel, courage in fear, and boldness in practical dealings:
this is the proper mark of learning; parrot-like recitation is something else.
Love of virtues, humility, discernment, and association with good people,
and lack of confusion in affairs: this is the nature of the wise.
One who, even without livelihood, does no improper act; even when strong, feels no arrogance;

children.text: na duḥkhito 'pi saṃtāpaṃ bhajate yaḥ sa paṇḍitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and even when suffering, does not give way to torment: he is a learned man.
One who infers by his insight and speaks what is fitting in an assembly,

children.text: anindyaṃ kurute yaśca sa vidvāniti gaṇyate ||
children.translated_text: and who does what is blameless, is counted a wise man.
Skilled in helping others and unable to endure another's distress,
wise men with pleasant speech are said to be rare in this world.
Shame on those fools who, by intoxication, anger, greed, delusion, and mind-born impulses,
are made to dance as they please, always like mechanical dolls.
What use are those without discernment, falling at every step

children.text: āyāso jīvitaṃ yeṣāṃ nidhanaṃ ca priyāśiṣaḥ ||
children.translated_text: for whom life is weariness, and death a cherished blessing.
A fool who thinks himself omniscient, a man without wealth who has grand pretensions,
a powerless man harsh with anger: by whom is such a deluded man not mocked?
Those who slander without cause, and those who look only for faults,
who would not cast away those wicked, disreputable men like owls?

children.text: vṛddhiṃ yadyāti sahasā mūḍhānāṃ viddhi tadgatam
children.translated_text: If prosperity comes suddenly to fools, know that it is going toward its end;
at the time of its extinction, the flame of a lamp grows large.
Speech stained by falsehood, a mind stained by meanness,
and a glance stained by envy do not belong to men who are not evil-hearted.
Abandon a son who destroys the family; do not fall away from your own <s>dharma</s>.
For the good there is nothing dearer than <s>dharma</s>, and nothing at all dearer than truth.
Long ago the daitya <s>Virocana</s> and <s>Sudhanvan</s>, son of <s>Aṅgiras</s>,
went together to the mansion of the divine maiden <s>Keśinī</s>.
When a golden seat was set down there for those two, who were full of rivalry,

children.text: vayaṃ śreṣṭhā iti mitho vivādaḥ samajāyata ||
children.translated_text: a mutual dispute arose between them: 'We are the superior ones.'
Then those two, filled with jealousy, made their lives the stake
and came to see <s>Prahlāda</s>, <s>Virocana</s>'s father.
After the matter had been reported by them, he saw the case as touched by doubt;
<s>Prahlāda</s> said to his son, 'I cannot take away the truth.'
When the daitya king had spoken thus, <s>Sudhanvan</s> praised his truthfulness,
and, pleased with him, voluntarily released the son whom he had won.
Rejecting even his own son, whose life had been wagered by himself,
<s>Prahlāda</s>, adorned with truth, preserved the boundary of <s>dharma</s>.
Fortune has humility as its ornament; the mind has straightforwardness as its ornament;

children.text: vāṇī ca satyābharaṇā na hi nāmākṛtātmanām ||
children.translated_text: and speech has truth as its ornament. These are certainly not for uncultivated souls.
O guardian of the earth, you ought not abandon truth for the sake of the earth,
for truth alone is the provisions for the perilous road of <s>saṃsāra</s>.
In whatever way the minds of men are intent on the good,
in just that way, at every step, they bring forth every kind of prosperity.
An assembly without elders is ruined, and elders who speak unrighteousness are ruined;
<s>dharma</s> is ruined when deprived of truth, and truth when it rests on deceit.
The terrible act, painful even in another birth, is seen by those who look to the future;
the wise do not perform an action that produces later remorse.
Long ago <s>Atri</s>, in the form of a swan, was questioned by the <s>Sādhyas</s>, O lord of the earth,
and he said: 'The steadfast, who have conquered anger, are the vessel of prosperity.

children.text: na giro marmabhedinyaḥ sabhrūbhaṅgāśca no dṛśaḥ
children.translated_text: Words that pierce vital spots, glances with knitted brows,
and harsh changes of manner do not arise in those whose minds are stainless.
The duty that is done simply because it ought to be done is completed concisely;
for such people there is no rope-long chain of one attachment following another.

children.text: na sevyā dhanino nīcā nānugamyā madoddhatāḥ
children.translated_text: Low men who are rich should not be served, nor should men swollen with pride be followed;

children.text: na kāryāḥ suhṛdo lubdhā nākṣepyā balaśālinaḥ ||
children.translated_text: greedy men should not be made friends, and the powerful should not be insulted.
O king, out of affection for <s>Suyodhana</s>, do not set your mind on sin;
for after death a darkness not of this world hangs over one.

children.text: anāgateṣu doṣeṣu yo na jānāti saṃvṛtim
children.translated_text: A man who does not know the remedy for faults before they arrive,

children.text: vyasane saṃnipatito vivaśaḥ sa karoti kim ||
children.translated_text: when he has fallen helpless into calamity, what can he do?'
When <s>Vidura</s> had spoken thus, the king sighed and said,

children.text: jayaṃ dharmānujaṃ jāne kiṃtu tyājyo na me sutaḥ ||
children.translated_text: 'I know that victory follows <s>dharma</s>, yet my son is not to be abandoned by me.
Who is able to overstep what the Creator has ordained?
What has been decreed by destiny will truly not fail to happen.

children.text: purā na mṛtyurastīti śrutaṃ gūḍhaṃ vaco mayā
children.translated_text: Long ago I heard the hidden saying, "There is no death."

children.text: kathaṃ tadapi me kṣattaḥ saṃśayaṃ chettumarhati ||
children.translated_text: Explain that too to me, O <s>Kṣattṛ</s>, so as to cut away my doubt.'
Hearing this, <s>Vidura</s> said, 'I am a śūdra; how could I have the power,
outside the Veda, to speak the secret of those who know secrets, hidden in <s>śruti</s>?
Let <s>Sanatsujāta</s>, lord of yogins, eternal though still a boy,
my son, come here today and answer your question.'
Having said this, <s>Kṣattṛ</s> remembered him, entering meditation;
and as soon as he was meditated upon, he came and, when questioned, spoke to the king:

children.text: krodho 'ntakaḥ sarvamidaṃ nihanti ya eṣa puṃsāṃ vadanādudeti
children.translated_text: 'Anger is the ender: it destroys all this when it rises from men's mouths,

children.text: vimohakāmāñjalinā janaughaṃ pibannaśeṣaṃ maraṇaṃ na mṛtyuḥ ||
children.translated_text: drinking up the whole multitude of people with handfuls of bewildering desire. Death is not the real death.
The inner death of men is the fully grown group of the six enemies; <s>Śamana</s> is not death.

children.text: janmaiva mṛtyuḥ sa yato 'sti tasmiñjanmanyapete na hi mṛtyurasti ||
children.translated_text: Birth itself is death, because death exists in it; when birth has departed, death does not exist.

children.text: jayanti viprā maraṇaṃ na nāma śuṣkakriyāmātraniṣaṇṇacittāḥ
children.translated_text: Brahmans conquer what is called death, not those whose minds rest merely on dry ritual acts.

children.text: chandāṃsi tatraiva nivārayanti na tīrthasevā na tapo na yajñaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The Vedic metres stop at that very point; neither service at sacred fords, nor austerity, nor sacrifice suffices.
Those who worship the faultless abode of bliss, beyond grief and joy and beyond the three <s>guṇas</s>,
for them immortality is self-awareness; but anger comes upon fools as death.
Anger, craving, grief, thirst, pride, greed, fault-finding, disgust, jealousy,

children.text: kāmo vivitsā ca vimohayuktā doṣā nṛṇāṃ dvādaśaghoramṛtyuḥ ||
children.translated_text: desire, inquisitiveness joined with delusion: these twelve faults are men's terrible death.
Austerity, vows, sacrifice, and observances are a binding discipline; liberation comes through realization of the supreme imperishable.
That supreme imperishable is not established anywhere among desired objects; it is beyond stars, sun, fire, and water.

children.text: yacchukrato brahmamahatprakāśaṃ yāte mṛte dyaur vidiśo diśaśca
children.translated_text: That bright, great Brahman-light, by which heaven, the intermediate quarters, and the quarters shine when it goes forth,

children.text: yat prāṇito rājati khe vivasvānsanātano yogivaraiḥ sa mṛgyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: that by which <s>Vivasvān</s>, made animate, shines in the sky, is the eternal one sought by the best yogins.

children.text: janmanyudaste yadupaiti mṛtyuḥ pṛṣṭe ca śukroccaritaḥ prakāśe
children.translated_text: When birth has been cast away, that to which death comes, and in the light uttered by <s>Śukra</s> when questioned...
Visible to the lords of yogins, they attain immortality; therefore, O foremost of the Kurus, death does not exist.
Having spoken thus, he of radiant form, with a face like rays of nectar,
<s>Sanatsujāta</s> respectfully took leave of the king and disappeared.
Then, at dawn, into the great assembly furnished with jeweled seats
<s>Dhṛtarāṣṭra</s> entered, together with <s>Bhīṣma</s>, <s>Kṛpa</s>, <s>Droṇa</s>, and the others.
Then kings such as <s>Bhagadatta</s>, their valor sung by bards, entered,
their garments tinged tawny by their crests and diadems.
On the floor of the assembly, dark with emerald pillars, they shone
like graceful royal swans in the true shade of a lotus grove.
Their claw-like hands gleamed with rays from the jewels of flashing bracelets;
they were lions among kings, with broad white turbans seeming like manes.
Then, with yak-tail fans gliding to his ears, slow with intoxication,
the splendid <s>Suyodhana</s>, drunk with pride, entered like a lordly elephant.
When those kings, resplendent with shining crowns, had mounted golden seats,
like gods seated upon the peaks of <s>Meru</s>,
<s>Saṃjaya</s> entered before the Kuru king and sat down,
smiling, again and again looking over the gathering of earth-ruling kings.

children.text: pratyāgataḥ pāṇḍavebhyaḥ kiṃ nu vakṣyati saṃjayaḥ
children.translated_text: 'What indeed will <s>Saṃjaya</s>, returned from the <s>Pāṇḍavas</s>, say?'
Thus some strange excitement of curiosity arose among the rulers of the earth.
<s>Dhṛtarāṣṭra</s>, after reflecting for a moment, then addressed <s>Saṃjaya</s>, who wished to speak,
and asked about <s>Pārtha</s>'s message, as if he had gained eyes in his ears.

children.text: pūrvaṃ gāvalgane brūhi kimāha sa dhanaṃjayaḥ
children.translated_text: First, O <s>Gāvalgani</s>, tell me: what did that <s>Dhanaṃjaya</s> say,
whose glory <s>Agni</s>, satisfied at <s>Khāṇḍava</s>, sings like a bard?
At the slaughter of the <s>Kālakeyas</s>, among the peacocks of heaven's gardens,
the sound of whose <s>Gāṇḍīva</s> became the teacher of a fierce dance?
Thus questioned by the king, <s>Saṃjaya</s> replied:

children.text: śrūyatāṃ suhṛdāṃ madhye kirīṭī māṃ yadabhyadhāt ||
children.translated_text: 'Listen, among friends, to what <s>Kirīṭin</s> said to me.
In the presence of the grandsire, of <s>Droṇa</s>, of <s>Kṛpa</s>, and of <s>Kṛtavarman</s>,
of <s>Drauṇi</s>, of the lord of <s>Madra</s>, of <s>Śakuni</s>, and of <s>Bāhlika</s>,
of the counselor, of the charioteer's son, and of all the rulers of the earth,
and in front of his father, make <s>Suyodhana</s> hear this:
If you do not give up the kingdom of compassionate <s>Dharmarāja</s>,
then this heavy arm of mine, devoted to the <s>Gāṇḍīva</s>, will be upon you.
In a battle-whirlpool of blood, hard to cross, rising up
from the split frontal globes of maddened elephants broken by his mace, you will see <s>Bhīma</s> in battle.
Like two advancing buffaloes amid masses of dust raised by chariots,
the twins will carry out Death's sport among your armies.
Tearing apart your trembling, dust-covered battle-lines,
<s>Dhṛṣṭadyumna</s> will accomplish the requital for <s>Kṛṣṇā</s>'s wrath.
With his bow as a flame, encircled by the sparks of flashing arrows,
<s>Śikhaṇḍī</s> will become a comet in the dense forest of foes.
When the close formation of great chariot-warriors is broken by <s>Sātyaki</s>'s arrows,
the Kuru armies, put to flight, will surely scatter into a thousand parts.
The arrows of <s>Saubhadra</s>, falling upon the lotus-faces of heroes,
will plainly become witnesses to the widowhood of Kuru women.

children.text: sthāsyanti te kathaṃ nāma yeṣāṃ yuddhamupasthitam
children.translated_text: How, indeed, will those men stand, when battle has come upon them
with the <s>Caidya</s>, <s>Kuntibhoja</s>, <s>Matsya</s>, and <s>Drupada</s>?

children.text: drakṣyanti me rathe dṛptaṃ kuravaḥ kapikuñjaram
children.translated_text: The Kurus will see on my chariot the proud mighty monkey,
who bears a wonder fashioned by <s>Viśvakarman</s> among the hosts of beings.

children.text: ghoraḥ kahakahaḥ śabdaḥ śrūyate yasya garjitaḥ
children.translated_text: The terrible 'kaha-kaha' sound of his roar is heard,
like the fire at the end of an aeon yawning as it longs to burn.
The charioteer of that chariot is the Blessed Lord himself, <s>Kaiṭabhasūdana</s>.
That chariot is coming swiftly; let it be checked, if it can be checked.
When you see <s>Karṇa</s>'s chariot shattered like your own cherished ambition,
O <s>Suyodhana</s>, you will remember the beneficial words of kinsmen and friends.
When <s>Phalguṇa</s>'s message had thus been reported by <s>Saṃjaya</s>,
there arose on the cheeks of the rulers of the earth a gleam of horripilation.
Then <s>Bhīṣma</s> took up speech deep as a roaring cloud,
as though filled by those faces reflected in the jeweled walls.
O <s>Duryodhana</s>, you do not understand the dreadful calamity that has arrived.
I think the lords of the earth have been marked by the sidelong glance of Time.
Who could dare to look upon <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> and <s>Arjuna</s> in one chariot,
portending the destruction of the worlds, like two suns risen together?
These two are <s>Nara</s> and <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>; petitioned by the gods sent by <s>Viriñci</s>,
<s>Pārtha</s> and <s>Govinda</s> have been born to quiet the burden of the earth.
The <s>Kālakhañjas</s>, together with the <s>Paulomas</s>, dwellers in <s>Hiraṇyapura</s>,
were slain by <s>Pārtha</s> in his incarnation as <s>Nara</s>: so says <s>Nārada</s>.
After repeatedly hearing <s>Karṇa</s>'s words, sweet to the ear,
this delusion of pride has been born in you, by which the earth will perish.
Rogues who say what is pleasant remain only during the prosperities of kings;
but when the wind of disaster falls, they go off like cotton to the quarters.
By the very men through whom a foolish lord is thrown into the crisis of bad policy,
by those very men, standing far away, he is mocked: 'This one is stupid.'
Those bees of the lotuses of fortune, enjoyers of the sandalwood of kingship,
those peacocks of the forest of pleasure, are not seen when the end comes.

children.text: haniṣyāmi raṇe pārthāngiraṃ karṇo bravīti yat
children.translated_text: As for <s>Karṇa</s>'s saying, 'I will kill the <s>Pārthas</s> in battle,'

children.text: dṛṣṭaṃ taddhopayātrāyāṃ gograhe ca svayaṃ tvayā ||
children.translated_text: you yourself saw what that amounted to in the <s>Ghoṣayātrā</s> and at the cattle raid.
When the son of <s>Śantanu</s> had spoken thus, <s>Vaikartana</s>, breathing hard, replied.
At this moment it is not fitting for me to say what would be worthy of my own forbearance.

children.text: kiṃ kurmaḥ samarārambho na syādyadi mahīpateḥ
children.translated_text: What can we do? If the king's undertaking of battle were not at hand,
who would endure such harsh speech, cutting into the vital parts?
Having said this, in agitation he made the jeweled pavement with the tip of his foot,
deeply scratched, as if it had been rubbed by the edge of a whetstone.

children.text: yadā tvayā virahitaṃ sainyaṃ rājño bhaviṣyati
children.translated_text: "When the king's army will be without you,
then, <s>Bhīṣma</s>, I shall fight," said the king of <s>Aṅga</s>, and he went out.
Then <s>Dhṛtarāṣṭra</s>, after reflecting, again said to <s>Saṃjaya</s>:
"Does the righteous king, the son of <s>Dharma</s>, desire peace with the <s>Kauravas</s>?

children.text: yoddhārastatra ke prāptāḥ kiyacca vipulaṃ balam
children.translated_text: Who have arrived there as fighters, and how great is the vast army?"
Questioned thus by <s>Vaicitravīrya</s>, <s>Saṃjaya</s> replied:
"That steadfast <s>Dharmarāja</s>, <s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s>, does desire peace,

children.text: vīro yuddhaṃ ca yenāsya vipulo balasaṃgrahaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and he is a hero whose great gathering of forces is also ready for war.
Having said this, <s>Saṃjaya</s>, his heart bewildered, fell into a faint;
and after a moment he recovered and spoke again to the king:
"That army of the sons of <s>Pāṇḍu</s>, hard to enter because of its maddened elephants,
dense with showers of weapons and missiles, whom indeed would it not bewilder?

children.text: bhuvi santi gajā naiva hayāśca vanakuñjarāḥ
children.translated_text: I thought: 'On earth there are no elephants, nor horses, nor forest elephants;
there are no elephants and no chariots at all there.'
<s>Sātyaki</s>, <s>Drupada</s>, <s>Śaibya</s>, <s>Śikhaṇḍī</s>, the five <s>Kekayas</s>,
<s>Cekitāna</s>, <s>Jayatsena</s>, <s>Yudhāmanyu</s>, and <s>Uttamaujas</s>,
<s>Dhṛṣṭadyumna</s>, <s>Virāṭa</s>, <s>Dhṛṣṭaketu</s>, and <s>Ghaṭotkaca</s>,
the son of <s>Arjuna</s> and the sons of <s>Draupadī</s>: these heroes stand there, eager to fight."
Hearing this, <s>Vaicitravīrya</s>, distressed, spoke again:
"For my sons, there will be fear from <s>Bhīma</s>, and from no one else.
I seem already to see my sons' destruction come again in battle,

children.text: paśyāmīva punaḥ prāptaṃ putrāṇāṃ nidhanaṃ raṇe ||
children.translated_text: their arms and chests split open by the blows of <s>Bhīmasena</s>'s mace.
What more? When the circle of the sky is blocked by <s>Arjuna</s>'s arrows,

children.text: hatā api na śakṣyanti manye gantuṃ divaṃ nṛpāḥ ||
children.translated_text: I think the kings, even when slain, will not be able to go to heaven."
As the son of <s>Ambikā</s> was speaking thus, proud and angry <s>Suyodhana</s>,
looking with enthusiasm upon the lion-like kings in the assembly, said:
"It is not fitting to utter what is improper; self-praise is indeed blameworthy.
On what grounds do you think the sons of <s>Pāṇḍu</s>, equal in lineage to your sons, superior?
They have seven <s>akṣauhiṇīs</s> (army divisions); I have eleven standing ready.
Why then, without reflecting, do you fear defeat?
Even hundreds of thousands of blazing <s>akṣauhiṇīs</s>, with weapons as their very mind,

children.text: gajastho bhagadatto vā tulyaṃ manye raṇe na vā ||
children.translated_text: I do not consider equal in battle to <s>Bhagadatta</s> mounted on his elephant.

children.text: yeṣāṃ śāntanavo goptā droṇaśca sasuto yudhi
children.translated_text: Those whose protector is the son of <s>Śantanu</s>, and <s>Droṇa</s> with his son in battle,

children.text: teṣāṃ śaṅkāspadaṃ sākṣādapi manye na vajrabhṛt ||
children.translated_text: for them I do not think even <s>Vajrabhṛt</s> himself a cause for anxiety.
<s>Bṛhadbala</s> is to be counted, and <s>Śalya</s>, <s>Saindhava</s>, and <s>Bāhlika</s> too;
let a match among the <s>Pārthas</s> be sought for these leaders of my army."
When <s>Dhārtarāṣṭra</s> had spoken thus, <s>Vidura</s>, sorrowful, said:
"Alas, through enmity among kinsmen the <s>Bhārata</s> family is ruined.
Once, before the eyes of a snare-living hunter, two strong birds bound in a net
quickly went through the sky, carrying the net with them.
The hunter too followed them for a long way, watching the sky,
expecting that through mutual division they would fall to the earth.
Then, after they had suffered long, a quarrel arose, with beaks and claws as weapons;

children.text: saha jālena patitau gṛhītau tena dhīmatā ||
children.translated_text: they fell together with the net and were seized by that clever man.
So, through division among the <s>Kurus</s>, this destruction has arrived.
What more is to be said? The great festival of the night of death is near."
When <s>Vidura</s> had spoken thus, the sage <s>Pārāśarya</s> himself
came forward and, out of compassion, spoke to <s>Gāndhārī</s> and <s>Suyodhana</s>:

children.text: putra dattvā nijaṃ rājyaṃ pārthebhyo rakṣa jīvitam
children.translated_text: "Son, give your own kingdom to the <s>Pārthas</s> and save your life.
Do not quickly become, in your own family, the banner of the terror of destruction.

children.text: kimanyatra śṛṇoṣi tvaṃ dhṛtarāṣṭraḥ śṛṇotu te
children.translated_text: Why listen elsewhere? Listen, and let <s>Dhṛtarāṣṭra</s> hear this from you:
certainly prosperity is there where the god <s>Janārdana</s> is.
Know his power, reported by <s>Saṃjaya</s>."
Having said this, the sage quickly vanished while the kings looked on.
Then, questioned by the king, the son of <s>Gāvalgaṇa</s> spoke:
"O king, <s>Madhuripu</s> himself has risen up for the sake of the <s>Pāṇḍavas</s>.
The wise recount his wondrous deeds;
this whole moving and unmoving universe exists by his mere wish.
He is <s>Vāsudeva</s>, dwelling in the heart; he is <s>Viṣṇu</s> through his mastery;
he is <s>Janārdana</s> from crushing foes, and <s>Dāmodara</s> from self-restraint."
When <s>Saṃjaya</s> had said this, the king whose eye was wisdom
praised the god in his mind and bowed to <s>Garuḍadhvaja</s>.
Meanwhile the son of <s>Dharma</s> spoke in the presence of <s>Hari</s>,
reflected in the <s>Kaustubha</s>, as if lovingly entering his heart:
"O lord, soul of the universe, whatever is said before you
plainly becomes repetition, even if it has not been spoken.
So when <s>Saṃjaya</s> came and said much in a few words,
the mind of <s>Ambikā</s>'s son has still not become clear, even today.
Out of affection for his son, he does not desire peace by giving back our own kingdom.
How is it right for us to overlook our lawful property?
In the forest, even on a corpse abandoned by jackals, its belly hollowed out by worms,
people set their concern; but not upon one bereft of wealth."
A man without wealth is alone even though he has a family, and unknown even though born in a noble house;
even if learned, he is indeed regarded as lacking proper conduct.
Through wealth a man, though low-born, obtains noble birth; though worn out by age, he obtains youth;
and though a fool, he obtains a flowering of brilliance.
Wealth is always weightiest, because it is the root of <s>dharma</s> (righteous order) and desire;

children.text: dāne viṣayabhoge ca dhanahīnaḥ karoti kim ||
children.translated_text: what can a man without wealth do in giving or in enjoying objects of pleasure?
A sinner is never free from poverty, and a poor man is never free from sin;
I think there is only a difference of name between sin and poverty.
The poor are simply poor; but one whose sovereignty has fallen away is pitied,
for at his suffering this world sighs and looks upward.

children.text: kathaṃ nu kṣatriyo bhūtvā rājyaṃ nijabhujārjitam
children.translated_text: How indeed, after becoming a kṣatriya, could one abandon a kingdom won by one's own arms
and, with downcast face, accept prosperity assigned by <s>Virāṭa</s>?
"This virtuous man once possessed fortune, but now he has fallen from it"—

children.text: iti dattaṃ kṛpāviṣṭairbhuñjate na hi māninaḥ ||
children.translated_text: the proud do not enjoy what is given by people filled with pity in such words.
Greedy <s>Suyodhana</s> will not give the kingdom without battle;
who, being himself lord, would willingly abandon fortune ripened into enjoyment?
Fie on war, full of much exertion, unrestrained, and doubtful to the mind,
where victory is purchased with the lives of friends, kinsmen, and servants.
You ought to act so that King <s>Dhṛtarāṣṭra</s> gives without war
our own share of the kingdom to us.
Let him give us <s>Kuśastūla</s>, then <s>Āmandī</s>, and also the place called <s>Vāraṇa</s>,

children.text: ekaṃ cānyamapi jñātaṃ grāmānpañca dadātu naḥ ||
children.translated_text: and one other known village as well: five villages in all.
When <s>Dharmarāja</s> had spoken thus, the foe of <s>Kaiṭabha</s> said:
"So it is, lord of men; the good commend peace.
I myself will go there for the welfare of all kings;

children.text: jāne mama vaco rājā kuruvṛddhaḥ kariṣyati ||
children.translated_text: I know that the aged Kuru king will do as I say.
But if he too, from delusion caused by love for his son, should go on the wrong path,
we, who walk in true <s>dharma</s> (righteous order), shall not be blameworthy among families."
Hearing this, the son of <s>Kuntī</s> again said to <s>Keśava</s>:

children.text: gamanaṃ tatra te kṛṣṇa na mahyamabhirocate ||
children.translated_text: "Your going there, <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, does not please me.
<s>Suyodhana</s> is petty and sinful, surrounded by still more dreadful friends,
by whom great calamities have been brought down for our sake."
To the king speaking thus, <s>Madhusūdana</s> said:

children.text: mā kṛthāḥ saṃśayaṃ rājanmayi nāsau pragalbhate ||
children.translated_text: "Do not entertain doubt, king; that man will not be bold against me.
The armies of the Kuru king, swallowed by my anger,
will not exist for even a moment if they do what is improper."
When <s>Viśvaksena</s> had spoken thus in vehemence, <s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s>
replied: "The Blessed One himself is the authority in a matter of doubt.
When you have arisen out of compassion for the worlds, O abode of the universe,
who can take on the weight of instructing you in a message, O teacher of the world?

children.text: gamyatāṃ tatra kuntī tu samāśvāsyā tvayā prabho
children.translated_text: Go there; but <s>Kuntī</s> is to be consoled by you, lord.
When you have returned successful and unharmed, we shall see you again."
When the king had spoken thus, <s>Bhīma</s>, <s>Phalguna</s>, and likewise <s>Nakula</s>,
anxious about the destruction of the world, spoke to the husband of <s>Kamalā</s>:
"Blessed one, among the kings say such things to <s>Suyodhana</s>
that, free from agitation, he may desire peace together with us."
Hearing what his elder brothers had said, <s>Sahadeva</s> spoke:

children.text: kṛṣṇāṃ tattadbravīthāstvaṃ yathā saṃdhirna no bhavet ||
children.translated_text: "You should speak of <s>Kṛṣṇā</s> in such a way that there may be no treaty for us.

children.text: vikāraṃ ko hi vismṛtya parākramadharo naraḥ
children.translated_text: For what man who possesses valor, forgetting an injury,
deserves honor with a mind blunted against retaliation?"
When <s>Sahadeva</s> had spoken thus, <s>Kṛṣṇā</s>, whose eyes were like black antelopes,
made a rainy day out of her tears and said to <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>:
"After seeing me dragged in that way by <s>Duḥśāsana</s> in the assembly,
look, <s>Mādhava</s>: the <s>Pāṇḍavas</s>, free from enmity, desire peace.
Having passed the time of concealment, I think these men do not remember the enemy's humiliation,
like those released from dwelling in the womb.
If I have been forgotten by them through greed, exile, or wretchedness,
then will not <s>Dhṛṣṭadyumna</s> fight with <s>Duḥśāsana</s> and his companions?
What more is there? When you have gone and entreated him, <s>Duryodhana</s> may make peace;

children.text: vismartavyā tu neyaṃ me veṇī manyuniketanam ||
children.translated_text: but this braid of mine, the abode of anger, must not be forgotten.
Having spoken thus, her eyes clouded as if by smoke from the rising fire of grief,
she produced, with a flood of tears, the semblance of a severed garland of pearls.
"Soon, <s>Kṛṣṇā</s>, you will see the women of kṣatriyas whose enemy families have been slain,
their bracelets freshly broken." Thus he then spoke to her.
Then, after taking leave of the sons of <s>Pṛthā</s> at a moment sacred to <s>Mitra</s>,
at sunrise on a day at the beginning of winter, with serene mind,
under <s>Revatī</s>, auspicious and noble, happy together with <s>Sātyaki</s>,
<s>Garuḍadhvaja</s> set out in a chariot roaring like a cloud.
As he went, winds blew with the faces of the quarters covered by irresistible dust,
and with a roar; the earth also trembled.
The sages, <s>Bhārgava</s> and others, came up to him as he was going and said:
"Out of curiosity we shall see you seated in the Kaurava assembly."
Reaching <s>Bṛhatkūla</s> at the end of the day and letting down his conveyance,
he, attended by about a thousand followers, then spent one night.
Then <s>Dhṛtarāṣṭra</s>, learning through messengers that <s>Hari</s> had arrived,
joyfully spoke in person to <s>Bhīṣma</s> and the others and to his son, full of smiles:
"The blessed foe of <s>Kaiṭabha</s>, the god, the destroyer of <s>Kāliya</s>...
This report is well known on earth: "He will come to us."
Taking abundant jewels, and also elephants, horses, and chariots,
let the ministers, by my command, go out on the road to welcome <s>Hari</s>.
As the king was saying this, while the Grandfather praised him,
and while <s>Vidura</s> reflected for a moment, <s>Duryodhana</s> laughed and said:
Father, <s>Keśava</s> truly deserves worship greater than this,
but he will think that we are frightened by the beginning of war.
That wise one alone is the refuge of the <s>Pāṇḍavas</s>.
I shall bind him and then meet them; this is my hidden desire.
When he heard that displeasing speech, as the king, <s>Ambikā</s>'s son, trembled,
<s>Bhīṣma</s> said, "This family of the <s>Bharatas</s> is surely no more.
Your son is a moth, a single herald of evil omens.
It will not turn out thus once he has encountered <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, whose deeds are dark and terrible."
Having spoken thus, <s>Bhīṣma</s>, terrible with his frown and showing the play of the fire of anger,
went out sighing, his garment loosened by agitation.
Then at daybreak the foe of <s>Kaṃsa</s>, glorious and shining with the <s>Kaustubha</s>,
entered the city of the Kuru king like an ocean of jewels.
On the royal road, crowded with elephants and horses, where lofty mansions were caressed by rows of lotus-eyes beautiful with eager gazing,
and adorned with canopies of gems and gold, the nectar-lovely body of <s>Kaiṭabha</s>'s foe shone forth.
The faces of the women on the balconies, eager for a momentary sight of <s>Lakṣmī</s>'s lord,
their radiance divided by windows adorned with vaidūrya jewels, gained the beauty of clusters of lotuses covered with a net of moss.
On seeing <s>Rukmiṇī</s>'s beloved, like an autumn sky kissed by auspicious conch and moon-disks,
starred with necklaces, the minds of the women rose up and sported.
With the foremost ray of the <s>Kaustubha</s> as a young shoot, and adorned by the palāśa-like light of his body,
with the radiance of his conch as blossoms, he seemed at every step to plant a tree of beauty.
Coming to the broad gateway with its jeweled arch, darkened by circles of restless bees
mingling with the temples of dark elephants, he quickly entered to see <s>Dhṛtarāṣṭra</s>.
After the king's priest had arranged and offered due honors to him with respect,
he reached <s>Ambikā</s>'s son with his attendants and said, "The discussion will be tomorrow."
Then <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> quickly greeted the elders of the Kuru family and went to <s>Vidura</s>'s dwelling, satisfied by devotion alone.

children.text: sutakuśalakathābhiḥ svairamāśvāsya kuntīṃ punaraviśadudagraṃ dhāma duryodhanasya ||
children.translated_text: Freely comforting <s>Kuntī</s> with talk of her sons' welfare, he again entered <s>Duryodhana</s>'s lofty mansion.

children.text: bhoktuṃ tena nimantritaḥ praṇayitāṃ mithyā dadhānena sa bhuktiḥ prītipuraḥsarā vipadi kā prauḍhoktirityabravīt
children.translated_text: Invited to dine by him, who falsely displayed affection, he said, "A meal is preceded by love; what use is proud speech in misfortune?"

children.text: kṣatturmandirametya nirvṛtipadaṃ bhuktvā priyārho 'nayattenaivākhiladharmanītividuṣā kurvankathāḥ śarvarīm ||
children.translated_text: Going to the house of the chamberlain <s>Vidura</s>, a place of joy, he ate what was worthy of a friend and spent the night in conversation with him, who knew all <s>dharma</s> (righteous order) and policy.
Then, in the assembly attended by <s>Bhīṣma</s>, <s>Kṛpa</s>, <s>Droṇa</s>, <s>Śalya</s>, and the king of <s>Sindhu</s>,
<s>Śauri</s> approached, with <s>Suyodhana</s> going before him.
Entering and passing through the cloud of the courtyard, filled with the rainbow-like brilliance of royal crowns,
he shone like the sun.
Then he beautified the assembly, smiling with the white turbans of all the kings
and furnished with couches studded with jewels, gold, and pearls.
Seeing the lotus-eyed one, whose chest bore the <s>Śrīvatsa</s>, as he approached,
the Kuru elders rose, and so did thousands of other kings.
Meanwhile great seers headed by <s>Nārada</s> arrived,
as though served by fire stretched out from their own radiance.
When seats and arghya had been given to them, <s>Hari</s> then took his seat,
which, reflecting all the worlds in its jewels, was like another universe.
With his foot placed on the top of a blue-jewel footstool, he shone,
as if displaying once more the majesty of his battle with <s>Kāliya</s>.
With his feet resting on the splendor of the blue rays of the jeweled pavement, he appeared
as though asked by a visible brow to rebuke all visible forms.
With the radiance of his toenails he made again, as it were, the heavenly river,
clear as a spotless garment, foaming splendidly, and flowing to the ocean.
He shone with a broad necklace of stars,
as if attended by rows of stars out of affection for the full moon of his <s>Pāñcajanya</s> conch.
Pervaded by the glow of his heated-gold armlets,
he surpassed, by his body, the beauty of a mountain of sapphire enjoying the early sunlight.
With his dark arms, made noble by the beauty of his yellow garment,
he bore the semblance of vaidūrya pillars bound at their ends with gold.
With sprouts of rays from pearl-smiling armlets,
he appeared sprinkled with sloughed skins from his familiarity with reclining on the serpent <s>Śeṣa</s>.
Bearing a circle of radiance, together with the <s>Kaustubha</s>, red as young leaves,
he shone as though fashioning the lotus from which the four-faced <s>Brahmā</s> arose.
With masses of red rays from the corners of his eyes,
he repeatedly made blooming lotus-ponds, eager for <s>Kamalā</s>'s caress.
At his ears he bore the pearl-bright reflection of his earrings,
like a small, pure row of the inhabitants of <s>Śvetadvīpa</s>.
With circles of ruby-rays from his crown, spreading in the sky,
he seemed to create a discus to protect <s>Mitra</s> from fear of <s>Rāhu</s>.
He bore a white turban like the loud laughter of splendor,
like the embodied sound of a conch rolling through the universe.
Striking the sapphire pillars with the lustres of his body...
He seemed to be cutting down once again the forest of <s>Bāṇa</s>'s arms.
Reflected in the crystal walls of the assembly hall, he shone
as if entering the guardians of the quarters, whose forms were bent down by his own power.
The kings, with unwinking eyes, looked upon the lord of <s>Lakṣmī</s> seated in the assembly,
and, as if by their merit, for a long time attained a state equal to that of the gods.
Then, on that assembly floor, silent like the ocean after the churning had ended,
while the rulers of the earth were eager, wondering, 'What will he say?', the teacher of the world
took up a voice slow with the drum-sound of an embodied tāṇḍava,
and full of the majestic roar of a great cloud.
For a moment the white masses of rays from his teeth seemed to announce

children.text: haṃsā iva vimānena śrotuṃ prāptaṃ caturmukham ||
children.translated_text: that four-faced <s>Brahmā</s>, like swans, had come in an aerial car to listen.
Let <s>Vaicitravīrya</s>, <s>Bhīṣma</s>, and <s>Droṇa</s> consider
what we, alarmed at the destruction of the world, say here.
A beneficial word is first spoken fearlessly and with affection,
so long as it has not grown blunted by rejection in the assemblies.
In the empire of virtues, it is lineage that is established as the foundation;
indeed, the fortunes of good men shine when adorned by pride in their family.

children.text: bharatasya kuroḥ pūrvaṃ jāto 'si nṛpa satkule
children.translated_text: O king, you were born long ago in the noble line of <s>Bharata</s> and <s>Kuru</s>;
how have you taken to the wrong road through delusion caused by affection for your son?

children.text: tṛṣṇāmukhaṃ sukhaṃ duḥkhaṃ tyajyatāṃ mahatāṃ kule
children.translated_text: Pleasure, with craving as its mouth, is pain; in the family of the great let it be abandoned.
For the transformations of worldly existence that bring forgetfulness do not overpower the mighty.
For men whose heads are bowed with discipline, whose minds are full of compassion,
and whose dust of enmity is pacified, the night is not fruitless.
For good men whose minds are trusting through affection, who desire wealth without greed,
and who are devoted to siding with the good, the worlds are friends.
The blazing prosperities of the greedy, from whom the circle of kinsmen has withdrawn,
agitate the heart like flames of a cremation fire.
Whatever is not enjoyed as one's own by kinsmen together with friends,

children.text: svayogyamāsasampūrṇaṃ na gehaṃ pakkaṇaṃ hi tat ||
children.translated_text: though fit for oneself and abundantly full, is not a house but an outcaste hamlet.
The enjoyment of wealth by relatives, the enjoyment of doe-eyed women by beloveds,
and the enjoyment of good sayings by the learned are always fresh youth.
A mind adorned with discernment, beauty increased by virtues,
and fortune surrounded by friends and relatives are the marks of meritorious deeds.
For sinful men who are hostile to friends and kin and who make a dull hoard,
wealth has a brilliance that lasts only a moment, like that of clouds.
He whose friends are good men, and whose enemy is even a son if that son is uncontrolled,
adorns the world as spring adorns a forest.
For those whose jeweled crown is humility, whose gemmed earrings are sound śāstra,

children.text: tyāgaśca kaṅkaṇaṃ yeṣāṃ kiṃ teṣāṃ jaḍamaṇḍanaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: and whose bracelet is generosity, what need have they of dull ornaments?
This destruction of kings, of brothers, has arisen;
if neglected, it will burn the worlds like fire from the rubbing together of bamboos.
The abandonment of the ever-devoted, cruelty toward one's own people,
and conflict with the powerful are the first sprouts of calamity.
Fame is nectar in an ocean of nectar, and <s>Lakṣmī</s> is a lotus in a lotus-bed;
when this circle of kings is destroyed, what good remains except remorse?
Are these upholders of the earth to be slain for the seizure of another's property?
For what reason is a grove of mango and campaka trees burned by anyone?
Prosperity obtained by killing the strong, arising together with disaster, leads to sorrow,
like the festival of poor men held out of rivalry with their neighbors.
For kings intent on the effort of conquest, resources are the root;
the gathering of kinsmen together with friends is called wealth.
Therefore who is more worthy of honor than that righteous <s>Ajātaśatru</s>, bound by affection,
whose command is respectfully received upon the heads of heroes?
Without depending on <s>Bhīmasena</s>, who would enjoy mature sovereignty,

children.text: bhīmasenamanāśritya ko nu prauḍhāṃ śriyaṃ bhajet ||
children.translated_text: with elephant-temple breasts, a sword for her braid, and a fly-whisk for her smile?
Even today, in the houses of the inhabitants of <s>Hiraṇyapura</s>,
the dense, proud sound of the <s>Gāṇḍīva</s> is quieted only by a conch.

children.text: śatakratubhuvā tena śaṅkitaḥ ko nu rājate
children.translated_text: Who indeed can shine when he is feared by that son of <s>Śatakratu</s>,
for whose essence of valor <s>Tripurāntaka</s> is the measure?

children.text: prajñānayana tāṃ satyāṃ kuru rājannito diśam
children.translated_text: O king, with wisdom as your eye, make that true direction your course from here;
rulers who go that way are born again in the form of strength.
After hearing that speech of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, beneficial to the <s>Bhāratas</s>, clear and spoken by <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>,
honored in mind by the assembly, <s>Bhārgava</s> spoke.
'As you say, Blessed One, it is true, if the <s>Kaurava</s> listens;
if he is negligent in attending to the welfare of the kings, he commits an offense.
Long ago there was a king named <s>Dambhodbhava</s>, a royal elephant blinded by pride;
seeking battle, he roamed the whole world like pride embodied.
That king reached <s>Badaryāśrama</s> and challenged <s>Nara</s> and <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> to battle;

children.text: ayācata raṇaṃ mūḍhā na hi śāmyantyapātitāḥ ||
children.translated_text: fools do not grow calm unless they have been struck down.
Then, shattered by fierce reed-arrows from <s>Nara</s>'s bow-staff,
but protected by him out of compassion, he became free from pride.
Thus pride is truly a thunderbolt; when it comes upon the lord of the <s>Kauravas</s>,
O king, it makes the moon of his own fame wane into the dark fortnight.'
After hearing the words of <s>Jāmadagnya</s>, the sage <s>Kaṇva</s> also said,
'O king, in this lineage of <s>Bharata</s> you have become a comet of destruction.
Long ago <s>Mātali</s>, charioteer of the lord of the gods,
wandered over the earth to find a suitable husband for his daughter <s>Guṇakeśī</s>.
Then, having by chance met the divine seer <s>Nārada</s>,
and being told, "We two shall go together," he entered <s>Pātāla</s> as his companion.'
Then, having entered <s>Pātāla</s> and seen the god <s>Umāpati</s>,
he saw the splendid dwelling of the <s>Daityas</s>, <s>Dānavas</s>, and serpent chiefs,
<s>Rasātala</s>, filled with divine beings shining with their own radiance.
"This lotus-eyed one is <s>Puṣkara</s> by name, the son of <s>Varuṇa</s>;
he obtained beloved <s>Jyotsnāvalī</s>, though opposed by those who approved his daughter.
From here came that bow <s>Gāṇḍīva</s>, stretched and powerful, from the waters,
which had been obtained by king <s>Soma</s>, glorious in conquering the three worlds.
This charming canopy of the lord of waters, streaming with clear, pure cascades,
is made of moonstone, like a bathing pavilion belonging to Fortune.
Here is the fire that feeds on water; here the gods placed the nectar under guard.
Into this the moon enters when waned, and, waned though it is, grows again.
From here the blazing horse-head rises up at the lunar junctures.
This is that great blazing rod, within which is the fire of Time.
And this is <s>Hiraṇyapura</s>, belonging to the mighty <s>Daityas</s>,
where the <s>Nivātakavacas</s> dwell together with the <s>Kālakhañjas</s>.
And this is the world of the <s>Sauparṇas</s>, where these sons of <s>Garuḍa</s>,
all radiant like <s>Meru</s>, shine as men bearing the mark of <s>Śrīvatsa</s>.
This is the world of the <s>Surabhīs</s>, where the mothers of the <s>Rudras</s>,
the four wish-giving cows, sustain all the directions.

children.text: iyaṃ bhogavatī nāma bhogināṃ subhagā purī
children.translated_text: This fair city of the serpents is called <s>Bhogavatī</s>;
there the best of serpents, headed by <s>Vāsuki</s>, shine.
This lovely serpent, a very embodiment of <s>Kandarpa</s>, is named [<s>Sumukha</s>].
His father, named <s>Dikcara</s>, was eaten by <s>Vainateya</s>.
Hearing this, <s>Mātali</s> was pleased; seeing that lotus-eyed one
as fit for his daughter, he regarded him as a son-in-law.
Then <s>Nārada</s>, at <s>Mātali</s>'s word, approached <s>Āryaka</s>,
the serpent king who was <s>Sumukha</s>'s grandfather, and spoke to him:
"<s>Mātali</s>, dear friend of the king of the gods in battles,
wishes to give his daughter <s>Guṇakeśī</s> to your grandson.
Hearing that, <s>Āryaka</s> said, "This alliance is praiseworthy for us;

children.text: sumukhasya vayaḥ kiṃ tu pratijñāto garutmatā ||
children.translated_text: but <s>Sumukha</s>'s life-span has been pledged by <s>Garutmān</s>."
When <s>Āryaka</s> had spoken so, <s>Mātali</s> himself said:

children.text: vṛta eva mayā putryai sumukhaḥ sadṛśo varaḥ
children.translated_text: "<s>Sumukha</s> has indeed been chosen by me as a suitable bridegroom for my daughter.
Let him see the lord of the gods; he will arrange this one's welfare."
Having said this, <s>Mātali</s>, followed by <s>Nārada</s>, took him along,
went to heaven, and saw <s>Indra</s> standing together with <s>Upendra</s>.
Then, when <s>Mātali</s>'s affair had been reported by <s>Nārada</s>,
<s>Viṣṇu</s>, full of compassion, spoke affectionately to <s>Śakra</s>:
"<s>Śakra</s>, <s>Mātali</s> is your charioteer; his daughter's husband must be protected.
Let nectar be given to this one; by a boon let him be made a god."
Thus addressed by <s>Viṣṇu</s>, <s>Śakra</s> made him immortal by his word.
Then the serpent, having obtained life, gained <s>Guṇakeśī</s>.
When the serpent-destroyer learned that event, he was angry,
and, shattering the quarters with the wind from his wings, he came to heaven.
That hero spoke to the wielder of the thunderbolt and to <s>Viṣṇu</s> in the presence of the gods:

children.text: kathaṃ me vṛttivicchedo bhavadbhyāṃ krīḍayā kṛtaḥ ||
children.translated_text: "How has the cutting off of my livelihood been done by you two as a sport?
Surely this is an insult, because I am <s>Viṣṇu</s>'s servant.
I too am a giver of boons, and by my own will I became the vehicle of him who chose me.
I too have slain <s>Daityas</s>; I too was born from <s>Kaśyapa</s>.
By what, then, have I become inferior, reduced to being your petitioner?
With the edge of my wing I bear the three worlds together with <s>Viṣṇu</s>."
As he spoke thus in arrogance, <s>Viṣṇu</s> laughed and said to him:

children.text: savyetaraṃ vaha sakhe bāhuṃ me balināṃ vara
children.translated_text: "Friend, best of the strong, bear my other arm.

children.text: satyamitāṃ tataste 'haṃ jāne vāṇīṃ dhṛtiṃ tathā ||
children.translated_text: Then I shall know this speech of yours to be true, and your firmness as well."

children.text: ityuktvāsya bhujaṃ skandhe nidadhe sa hi līlayā
children.translated_text: Having said this, he playfully placed his arm on <s>Garuḍa</s>'s shoulder.
Under that heavy teacher, whose lesson removed pride, he fell down.
Blood poured from his mouth, his wings drooped, and he was utterly stunned.
Protected by the Lord, who was softened with compassion, he regained his composure.
Thus pride leads to humiliation, and bad conduct only to destruction.

children.text: duryodhana vṛthā darpaṃ mā kṛthā vyasanodayam ||
children.translated_text: <s>Duryodhana</s>, do not vainly make pride arise, the source of calamity.
Their masses of matted hair are white with fame, and their nails make them fearsome;
indeed, great king, <s>Bhīma</s> and <s>Dhanaṃjaya</s> are man-lions among kings."
Hearing these words of <s>Kaṇva</s>, he sighed, his face turned aside,
and, touching his thigh shaped like an elephant's trunk, he accepted evil policy.
With a sidelong glance he looked at <s>Rādheya</s>'s chest, uneven with hidden blows,
as though with the deceptive steps of Fortune, and considered him obliquely.
With the rays of a feigned smile making other yak-tail fans,
<s>Suyodhana</s> spoke while scratching the footstool with his foot:

children.text: yāce vadāmi viharāmi harāmi śatrūnpremṇā bhaje nanu parāniti mūḍhavāñchā
children.translated_text: "I beg, I speak, I play, I destroy enemies, and surely I lovingly serve others: such is foolish desire.

children.text: daivaṃ hi janmalikhitālikapaṭṭalekhāṃ dṛṣṭvā muhurmuhurudeti śubhāśubheṣu ||
children.translated_text: For fate, seeing the tablet of the forehead inscribed at birth, rises again and again in good and evil things."
When the son of <s>Dhṛtarāṣṭra</s> had spoken so, <s>Nārada</s>, dejected, said,
though he was a connoisseur of playful arts and curious only about quarrels:
"For men blinded by obstinacy and hard to restrain, trees poisonous with the anguish of sorrow
spring up in the heart from seeds of misconduct sown by themselves.

children.text: gālavākhyo muniḥ śiṣyo viśvāmitraṃ guruṃ purā
children.translated_text: Long ago a sage named <s>Gālava</s>, a pupil of <s>Viśvāmitra</s>,
said again and again to his teacher, "I will give you a teacher's fee."
Though he was refused many times, when he kept saying that very thing,
Then <s>Viśvāmitra</s>, angered by his insistence, said to him:
"Give me eight hundred horses, pure with right-turning marks,
with dark ears and with the brightness of snow, jasmine, and the moon."
Hearing that, <s>Gālava</s> considered horses of that kind hard to obtain,
and within days he became little more than bones, absorbed in anxiety and grief.

children.text: sa vayasyaṃ samabhyetya garuḍaṃ patatāṃ varam
children.translated_text: He went to his friend <s>Garuḍa</s>, the best of flyers,
reported that matter to him, and grieved, troubled by remorse.
Then <s>Tārkṣya</s> said to him, "Mount me, sage; search the quarters,
and obtain those dark-eared horses for your guru's purpose."
Thus addressed by the king of birds, <s>Gālava</s> mounted him,
and set out, faint with agitation and with his eyes half closed.
Seeing many different wonders and serpents ranging in the sky,

children.text: pūrvaṃ pūrvā diśaḥ prāpa devānāṃ pūrvamālayam ||
children.translated_text: he first reached the eastern quarter, the gods' first abode.
Then he went to the south, once presented by <s>Yama</s> as a guru's fee,

children.text: dakṣiṇāṃ ca tataḥ prāyātpitaro yatra somapāḥ ||
children.translated_text: where the ancestors who drink soma dwell.

children.text: paścimāṃ ca tato gatvā paścādyatra raviḥ karān
children.translated_text: Then, going to the western quarter, where afterward the sun,
having released its rays at the end of the day, enters the ocean,
and taking the northern quarter, by which one crosses beyond sin,
where holy <s>Viṣṇupada</s> is, and also <s>Marutta</s>'s sacrificial ground,
after wandering through those quarters, the eminent one reached a lofty mountain.
After a long time <s>Garuḍa</s> and <s>Gālava</s> sat down on its summit.

children.text: tataḥ siddhāṃ dadṛśatuḥ śāṇḍilīṃ nāma bhāsurām
children.translated_text: Then they saw a radiant perfected woman named <s>Śāṇḍilī</s>.
Received there with hospitality by her, they ate and fell asleep.
Then <s>Garuḍa</s>, sleepless, pondered a desire:
"A sage's wife of this kind would be fit for <s>Brahmā</s>'s abode,

children.text: viṣṇoḥ śakrasya vā dhāmni dhyātveti virarāma saḥ ||
children.translated_text: or for the dwelling of <s>Viṣṇu</s> or <s>Śakra</s>." Having thought this, he stopped.
Then at dawn his wings had fallen loose, and his claws and face were withered;
he became like a heap of sodden flesh, exceedingly distressed.
Afterward, when he had told his lineage and bowed down, full of compassion,

children.text: sapakṣaṃ śāṇḍilī cakre taṃ dṛśā balavattaram ||
children.translated_text: <s>Śāṇḍilī</s> made him winged again and stronger by her glance.
Then, taking leave of her, <s>Gālava</s> departed with <s>Tārkṣya</s>.
Distraught by worry over his guru's purpose, he did not regain steadiness.
As he was traveling on the road, the sage <s>Viśvāmitra</s> happened to arrive
and, smiling, spoke to him, whose face was lowered in shame:

children.text: kva te mahyaṃ pratijñātāḥ śyāmakarṇā hayāstvayā ||
children.translated_text: "Where are the dark-eared horses that you promised me?"
After <s>Kauśika</s> had spoken thus and gone away, to <s>Gālava</s>, deeply sorrowful,

children.text: uvāca garuḍo dhyātvā tasya kāryasya niścayam ||
children.translated_text: <s>Garuḍa</s> spoke, after reflecting on the resolution of his task:
"Everything is obtained by wealth; and that divine wealth <s>Śakra</s> and <s>Kubera</s>,

children.text: divyaṃ premṇā mudā yuktau rakṣataḥ pṛthusaṃcayau ||
children.translated_text: joined with affection and joy, guard as vast stores.
The dark-eared horses are obtained only with riches.
There is one king, <s>Yayāti</s>, a lord with countless followers."

children.text: ityuktvā garuḍo gatvā yayātiṃ muninā saha
children.translated_text: Having said this, <s>Garuḍa</s> went with the sage to <s>Yayāti</s>
and asked for horses from him, though all his wealth had been spent on sacrifices.
Requested by him, he said, "I have a daughter who may be given for bride-price.
Her name is <s>Mādhavī</s>; let him give her and obtain the horses."
After speaking thus, the king gave the maiden out of fear of disappointing a supplicant.
<s>Gālava</s> took her, dismissed <s>Garuḍa</s>, and went away.

children.text: haryaśvaṃ nāma sa nṛpaṃ vīraṃ matimatāṃ varam
children.translated_text: He addressed a king named <s>Haryaśva</s>, a hero and foremost among the wise:
"O king, this maiden should be taken by you for a bride-price.
For her give dark-eared horses, and receive this king's daughter.
After she has borne one son, I will give her back to you again."

children.text: iti saṃvidamādāya sa tāṃ jagrāha vājibhiḥ ||
children.translated_text: Having made this agreement, he accepted her together with the horses.
Then in time, in her, as <s>Vāsava</s> begot <s>Jayanta</s>,
he begot a son named <s>Vasumanas</s>, endowed with wealth and strength.
Then the sage took <s>Yayāti</s>'s daughter back from him
and, with the very same agreement, went to King <s>Divodāsa</s>.
When a son named <s>Pratardana</s> had been born, the sage again
took her back and, seeking the remaining horses, went and reached the lord of birds.
He said to him, "I have obtained six hundred horses.
Out of friendship, think of a way for me to obtain the remainder."
When the despondent sage had asked this, the son of <s>Vinatā</s>

children.text: uvāca ṣaṭ śatānyeva pṛthivyāṃ santi vājinām ||
children.translated_text: said, "Only six hundred horses exist on earth.
Long ago a thousand dark-eared horses, through <s>Ṛcīka</s>'s ascetic power,
were obtained from <s>Varuṇa</s> for the sake of a marriage-price.
In the course of so much time, of those horses, in a certain royal sea,
four hundred were carried away by the current of the <s>Vitastā</s>.
Therefore only six hundred horses exist on the surface of the earth.
Give this maiden to your guru, friend, as completion of the horses."
When <s>Garuḍa</s> had spoken thus, <s>Gālava</s> gave those horses

children.text: dattvā kanyāṃ ca tāṃ prādādgurave tanayāvadhi ||
children.translated_text: and offered that maiden to his guru for a term ending with the birth of a son.
Then <s>Viśvāmitra</s> begot in her a fourth son, <s>Aṣṭaka</s>,
equal to <s>Indra</s>, and gave her back to <s>Gālava</s> himself.
Then <s>Gālava</s>, his auspicious task accomplished, gave <s>Yayāti</s> his daughter,
lotus-faced and, by a boon, not deprived of her virginity.
Then <s>Yayāti</s> held a <s>svayaṃvara</s> (self-choice ceremony) for that daughter.
It was arranged in an assembly of moving and unmoving beings.
There <s>Mādhavī</s> considered gods, siddhas, seer-kings, and earthly kings,
and, with her mind set on sacred fords and austerity, chose a secluded forest as her chosen spouse.
There, feeding on sprouts of grass and practicing celibacy together with the deer,
Terrified, she wandered about, as if from fear of people's suspicion.
Then, in time, <s>Yayāti</s>, a performer of sacrifices, reached the abode of the gods,
but, his merit exhausted through contempt for all beings, he fell from heaven.
As he was falling, his daughter's sons, <s>Aṣṭaka</s> and the others, by their own merit,

children.text: punarāropitaḥ svarge putryā ca tapasā tayā ||
children.translated_text: and that daughter by her austerity, raised him up again to heaven.
<s>Gālava</s>, through excessive insistence, came to an unhappy alteration of state,
and <s>Yayāti</s> too, through excessive pride, fell to the surface of the earth.
When <s>Nārada</s> had related this, <s>Dhṛtarāṣṭra</s>, to <s>Suyodhana</s>,
and <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, <s>Bhīṣma</s>, <s>Droṇa</s>, and <s>Gāndhārī</s> spoke these words:
"Understand this speech, meant for <s>Duryodhana</s>'s good, for the prosperity of your own family.
Do not, through delusion, enter the fire of the <s>Pārthas</s>' anger like a foolish young moth.
Make peace with the sons of <s>Pāṇḍu</s>, and with those lords of earth
whose power is increasing, enjoy the earth and drink deep of fame."
Hearing this, the son of <s>Dhṛtarāṣṭra</s>, filled with fierce anger, said:
