"Things that must come to pass do indeed come to pass and cannot be turned back.

children.text: jayo vā saṃśayo lakṣmyā vadho vā svargado yudhi
children.translated_text: Victory, or uncertainty regarding fortune, or death in battle that grants heaven:
I do not see either one of these alternatives as wholly pure.
High-spirited men, untrained in bowing and worth the price of the earth,

children.text: ta eva praṇatāḥ śatrau labhante na varāṭikām ||
children.translated_text: when they have bowed to an enemy, do not obtain even a cowrie.
The proud <s>Pāṇḍavas</s>, their arrogance roused, devoted to enmity upon the earth,
shall not have a share from me even the size of a needle's point, much less anything more."
Having spoken thus, the <s>Kaurava</s>, fixed in his resolve to seize <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>,
went out, consulted with <s>Karṇa</s> and the others, and entered again.
Knowing that intention of theirs, <s>Sātyaki</s>, best of the wise,
calmly reported it to <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, whose deeds are unstained.
Then, filling that assembly as if with matted locks that were flames of the fire of anger,
the foe of <s>Kaiṭabha</s> displayed a terrible body.
In his body, made of all the gods and radiant with shining splendor,
the kings were bewildered when they saw that fierce form of his.
<s>Adhokṣaja</s>, after displaying that endless, immeasurable cosmic form
to all the sages, took leave of them all and departed.
With a chariot that roared like a cloud and bore the bright emblem of <s>Garuḍa</s>,
he went to <s>Vidura</s>'s dwelling and entered to see <s>Kuntī</s>.

children.text: taṃ bhrātuḥ putramāyātaṃ pariṣvajya hariṃ pṛthā
children.translated_text: <s>Pṛthā</s> embraced <s>Hari</s>, her brother's son, when he had arrived,
and, after hearing of her sons' welfare, she spoke with tearful eyes:
"<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, the compassionate son of <s>Dharma</s> is to be addressed by you with my words:

children.text: ārjavaṃ brahmasulabhaṃ na te kṣatriya śobhate ||
children.translated_text: 'Straightforwardness, suitable for a Brahmin, does not befit you, a <s>kṣatriya</s> (warrior).
Though you are a king, you beg for your own wealth with words of the highest worth.
Do you not know the sinful <s>Kauravas</s> and their sinful allies?
For Brahmins of the eight-kapala rite, ignorant of ultimate reality
and turned away from worldly dealings, such dullness may be excusable.
Long ago <s>Vidurā</s> spoke to her own son, a king defeated by enemies
and averse to making an effort: patience is no ornament for a king.
He who, forgetting anger, endures insult from offenders
is, in the world, a little son of <s>Dharma</s> only to fill up the count of men.
Better a tree with thorns than a <s>śamī</s> of simple disposition;

children.text: spṛhaṇīyā varaṃ vandhyā na mātā śāntatejasām ||
children.translated_text: better a barren woman than the mother of sons whose fire has grown calm.
Thus addressed by his mother <s>Vidurā</s>, a king named <s>Saṃjaya</s>
became eager in the effort for victory and destroyed his enemies.
The blessed bearer of the <s>Gāṇḍīva</s> should be addressed with what is suitable for his protection;
but incitement is of no use for the hero <s>Bhīma</s>.'
Taking leave of her as she was speaking thus, toward the sons of <s>Pāṇḍu</s>
the <s>Garuḍa</s>-bannered one went, with horses urged on by <s>Dāruka</s>.
When he had departed, the terrified <s>Dhṛtarāṣṭra</s> then asked <s>Saṃjaya</s>,
having learned through spies of the actions of the foe of <s>Kaiṭabha</s>:
"I have heard, <s>Saṃjaya</s>, that as the politic foe of <s>Kaṃsa</s> was going,
some private counsel took place with <s>Rādheya</s>.

children.text: ekastvaṃ dhīmatāṃ dhuryo yadi jānāsi kathyatām
children.translated_text: You alone are foremost among the wise; if you know it, let it be told."
Asked thus by the king, <s>Saṃjaya</s> replied:
"I heard the secret words of <s>Karṇa</s> and <s>Keśava</s> as they spoke.
After honoring <s>Karṇa</s> again and again, <s>Janārdana</s> said this:
'By the god <s>Ravi</s>, the eye of the three worlds, you were born in <s>Kuntī</s>.
You, <s>Karṇa</s>, are a son of <s>Pāṇḍu</s>, a <s>kṣetraja</s> (legally begotten son), elder brother of <s>Dharmaja</s>.
Therefore come; abandon the <s>Kauravas</s> and join your own brothers, the sons of <s>Pāṇḍu</s>.
Together with them, enjoy the earth as <s>Śakra</s> does with the immortals.'
Hearing this respectfully, the hero <s>Karṇa</s> spoke to <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>:
'Blessed one, I know in full the origin of myself.

children.text: kiṃ tu bhuktaṃ ca pītaṃ ca visrabdhaṃ yasya mandire
children.translated_text: But in the house of the one whose food and drink I have enjoyed in trust,
of <s>Duryodhana</s>, that mighty friend, how could I, by betrayal,
I, <s>Karṇa</s>, son of the thousand-rayed sun, O <s>Acyuta</s>,
desire royal fortune stained by the reproach of treachery to a friend?

children.text: kirīṭinā mayi hate bhīmena ca suyodhane
children.translated_text: When I have been slain by <s>Kirīṭin</s> and <s>Suyodhana</s> by <s>Bhīma</s>,
<s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s> will certainly obtain the whole earth.

children.text: matkathāṃ naiva vācyo 'sau jñātvā māṃ bhrātaraṃ hi saḥ
children.translated_text: He must not be told my story, for if he knows me to be his brother,
he will not accept the entire kingdom, though it is attainable and his own.
In this war ordained by fate for the destruction of the field of <s>kṣatriyas</s> (warriors),
you will see the <s>Pārthas</s>, O <s>Vaikuṇṭha</s>, heroic and possessed of victory.'"
In a dream he was eating rice pudding with ghee, clothed in white garments;
I saw <s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s> mounted upon a heap of bones.
In a palace of a thousand supports, surrounded by his brothers,
that same man appeared again, wearing pure garlands and filled with great courage.
The glorious <s>Vṛkodara</s> was seen standing on the peak of a very high mountain,
and <s>Kirīṭin</s>, your ally, was seen on the head of a white elephant.
The lord of the <s>Kauravas</s>, with his followers, wearing red garlands and unguents,
was seen by me going toward the southern quarter, riding on a donkey.
And <s>Drauṇi</s>, <s>Hārdikya</s>, and <s>Gautama</s> were seen with white turbans.
Apart from them, surely <s>Kṛtānta</s> will move among us.
As such dreadful evil omens are seen, <s>Keśava</s>,

children.text: tathā jāne na naḥ śeṣo gāṇḍīvena bhaviṣyati ||
children.translated_text: so I know that no remnant of us will be left by <s>Gāṇḍīva</s>.
When <s>Karṇa</s>, modest and restrained, had said this privately,
the Blessed Lord whose banner bears <s>Garuḍa</s> took leave of him and departed.
When <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> had gone, <s>Vidura</s> approached <s>Kuntī</s>, who loved her son,
and told her of <s>Duryodhana</s>'s crooked conduct.
Though the son of <s>Dhṛtarāṣṭra</s>, intent on dying, has been conciliated many times,

children.text: asmadvaco na gṛhṇāti pathyaṃ bāla ivāturaḥ ||
children.translated_text: he does not accept our wholesome word, like a sick child.
Since <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> has gone away dishonored, when the battle between <s>Kurus</s> and <s>Pāṇḍavas</s>

children.text: dhruvaṃ pravṛtte nikhilā pṛthivī na bhaviṣyati ||
children.translated_text: has surely begun, the whole earth will cease to be.
Hearing what <s>Vidura</s> said, <s>Kuntī</s>, her heart disturbed by anxiety,
went to <s>Karṇa</s>, who was absorbed in recitation on the bank of the <s>Bhāgīrathī</s>.
He was standing in worship of the rising <s>Bhāskara</s> until the heat reached his back;
waiting for him, she remained there, afflicted by the fatigue of the intense heat.
At the end of his recitation, <s>Karṇa</s> looked at her, folded his hands,
and said, "I am <s>Rādheya</s>, the charioteer's son. What may I do?"

children.text: sā taṃ babhāṣe vātsalyāt kanīnastvaṃ suto mama
children.translated_text: Out of affection she said to him, "You are my son, born when I was an unmarried girl.
Your father is the thousand-rayed one, not a charioteer, O man of broad splendor.
Join <s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s>, your modest brother,

children.text: bhuṅkṣva vīra mahīṃ kṛtsnāṃ mā pāpānkauravānbhaja ||
children.translated_text: and enjoy the whole earth, hero; do not follow the sinful <s>Kauravas</s>."
Thus entreated by his mother, great-hearted <s>Karṇa</s> heard that very statement
spoken from the sky by the god <s>Ravi</s> himself in visible form.
Bowing, he said to <s>Kuntī</s>, "Mother, I know that what you have said is true;
but I am not able to abandon my loyalty to aged <s>Adhiratha</s>.
From my birth his loving hopes have been fostered in me;
how could they suddenly become vain, like the friendship of low men?

children.text: bahiścaraṃ jīvitaṃ ca na tyājyo mama kauravaḥ
children.translated_text: The <s>Kaurava</s> is my life moving outside me, and he must not be abandoned;

children.text: sarvāvasthāsu yasyāhaṃ bandhuḥ svāmī guruḥ suhṛt ||
children.translated_text: in every condition I am his kinsman, lord, teacher, and friend.
At no time, mother, will I kill your sons, except <s>Arjuna</s>.

children.text: na haniṣyāmi mā te 'stu praṇayo 'yaṃ vṛthā mayi ||
children.translated_text: Let this affection of yours toward me not be fruitless.

children.text: mayā hate phalgune vā hate pārthena vā mayi
children.translated_text: Whether <s>Phalguna</s> is killed by me, or I am killed by <s>Pārtha</s>,
you will still be the mother of five sons. What else is there to consider?"
When <s>Vaikartana</s> had spoken thus, <s>Pṛthā</s>, her mind trembling again and again,
took leave of him and secretly went to <s>Vidura</s>'s house.
Then the Blessed Lord, the slayer of <s>Kaiṭabha</s>, reached the <s>Pāṇḍavas</s>
and reported the hard, dangerous intention of the <s>Kauravas</s>.
Then, in the armies of the sons of <s>Pāṇḍu</s>, there arose an eager stir,
swollen with courage and energy, a tumult at the beginning of victory.
With <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>'s approval, the <s>Pāṇḍavas</s> appointed the heroic, mighty-armed <s>Dhṛṣṭadyumna</s>,
born from the fire, as commander of the army.
Then, when he had been consecrated, rejoicing and possessed of great power,
<s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s> set out for <s>Kurukṣetra</s> with vast forces.
As that ocean of kings moved forward eagerly,
there arose a roar produced by the collision of masses of troops.
With clusters of moist dust raised by elephants, horses, and chariots,
the front seemed like a mass of smoke from a fire against enemies that was about to blaze.
The kings, their jewel ornaments shining as they were touched by the rays of the sun,
moved about like heaps of golden arrows.
As bards sang of them by names marked with fame and valor,
the heroes thought that even the gods were not hard to conquer.
The dust of elephant vermilion, stirred up by the wind of their flapping ears,
made the surface of the sky seem filled with whirlpools of blood.
Then the sons of <s>Pāṇḍu</s>, together with <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, reached <s>Kurukṣetra</s>
and arranged the stations of the kings on the bank of the river <s>Hiraṇvatī</s>.
The lords of men respectfully occupied the camps, ringed by moats,
which had been indicated by <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> and <s>Arjuna</s>.
When the <s>Pāṇḍava</s> was encamped at <s>Kurukṣetra</s> together with the kings,
the distressed earth resounded with the noise of conches and drums.
Meanwhile the lord of the <s>Kurus</s>, surrounded by thousands of kings,
marched out, making the earth seem filled with banners and parasols.
The glorious one, drawing eleven <s>akṣauhiṇīs</s> after him, shone
like the thousand-rayed sun drawing its rays, or like the ocean drawing rivers.
In his army, crowded with mountain-like elephants, swords shone
like serpents pressed by the earth and risen from openings of the underworld.
Seeing the kings, and accompanied by <s>Droṇa</s>, <s>Karṇa</s>, <s>Kṛpa</s>, and others,
he approached <s>Devavrata</s> respectfully and addressed him:
"May you, a powerful hero like another <s>Kārttikeya</s>,
be lord of our armies at this great commencement of battle."
Thus requested by the <s>Kaurava</s>, the grandfather spoke:
"Here I am, your general; I shall fight the sons of <s>Pāṇḍu</s>."
"Every day I shall put down this bow only after the killing of ten thousand warriors;

children.text: na cāpametadityetāṃ viddhi me yudhi saṃvidam ||
children.translated_text: otherwise I shall not lower this bow. Know this to be my agreement in battle."
When <s>Gāṅgeya</s> had spoken thus, and <s>Dhārtarāṣṭra</s> reverently
consecrated him, the whole world trembled with the crash of thunderbolts.
Then, having reached <s>Kurukṣetra</s>, at <s>Duryodhana</s>'s command, slowly
the kings occupied rich camps that had been assigned to them.

children.text: śrutvā yudhiṣṭhiro bhīṣmaṃ kṛtaṃ senāpatiṃ paraiḥ
children.translated_text: When <s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s> heard that <s>Bhīṣma</s> had been made commander by the enemy,
he spoke to all the kings and to his younger brothers in the presence of <s>Hari</s>:

children.text: pūrvaṃ bhīṣmeṇa no yuddhaṃ bhaviṣyati mahaujasā
children.translated_text: "First our battle will be with mighty <s>Bhīṣma</s>,
before whom even <s>Jambhāri</s> would not count for us in battle.
The women of the gods sing of his conduct, noble in valor.

children.text: yattā bhavantastiṣṭhantu śakyate na sa helayā ||
children.translated_text: Stand intent; he cannot be dealt with lightly.
In battle he is a treasury of firmness, the foremost bearer of the yoke among all bowmen."
Having spoken so, the wise king, with <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>'s approval, appointed
seven lords over the seven armies, seven men with the prowess of <s>Śakra</s>:
the <s>Mātsya</s> king, <s>Drupada</s>, <s>Śaineya</s>, <s>Dhṛṣṭaketu</s>, and <s>Śikhaṇḍin</s>;
the <s>Māgadha</s> and <s>Pārṣata</s> too became commanders of that army.
And <s>Dhṛṣṭadyumna</s> became the master of those swift heroes;
above him <s>Pārtha</s>, protected by <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, became the overseer.
Meanwhile <s>Haladhara</s>, regarding <s>Bhīma</s> and <s>Suyodhana</s> as equal,

children.text: priyau śiṣyau sadā matvā śanaistaṃ deśamāyayau ||
children.translated_text: as two dear pupils alike, slowly came to that region.
He took leave of <s>Dharmarāja</s>, together with his younger brothers and <s>Janārdana</s>,
and, his mind averse to a war of kinsmen, the noble one went to see the sacred fords.
When he had gone, <s>Rukmī</s>, son of <s>Bhīṣmaka</s>, came to the <s>Pāṇḍavas</s>;

children.text: rukmī nāma kare yasya māhendravijayaṃ dhanuḥ ||
children.translated_text: in his hand was the bow <s>Māhendravijaya</s>.
Splendid, surrounded by an akṣauhiṇī, and conqueror of all kings,
he approached, excited with arrogance, and said to <s>Savyasācin</s>:
"I shall give you help in this terrible battle;
I shall kill <s>Bhīṣma</s> and <s>Droṇa</s>, if you are afraid, <s>Phalguna</s>."
Hearing this, <s>Arjuna</s>, unagitated, gave an answer with a smile:
"Ah, you wander over the earth as a rescuer of the frightened.
In the destruction of the <s>Nivātakavacas</s>, or in the victory over the <s>Gandharvas</s>,

children.text: gograhe vā sakhā kaścitko bhavenme bhavadvidhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: or in the seizure of the cattle, what friend like you could I have had?"
Told by <s>Kirīṭin</s>, with disdain, "Go back as you came,"
he went from there, blind with pride, and addressed <s>Duryodhana</s> in the same way.

children.text: tenāpi māninā tyaktaḥ sa jagāma nijāṃ purīm
children.translated_text: Rejected by that proud man as well, he went to his own city.
When he had departed, a vast beginning of battle arose between the two armies.
At this time king <s>Dhṛtarāṣṭra</s>, loving his sons,
asked <s>Saṃjaya</s> about the movements of the <s>Kuru</s> and <s>Pāṇḍava</s> armies.

children.text: sa tena pṛṣṭaḥ provāca saṃniviṣṭe baladvaye
children.translated_text: Asked by him, he said: "When the two forces had been drawn up,
<s>Suyodhana</s> commanded <s>Ulūka</s>, the son of <s>Śakuni</s>:
'Go, ally of the <s>Kauravas</s>, and tell the son of <s>Kuntī</s> in the assembly of kings:
Do not delay in battle, taking refuge in long postponement.
Give all your wealth to your loved ones and arrange meetings with those dear to you;
the battle with the son of <s>Śaṃtanu</s> stands near you, not far away.'
Thus addressed by <s>Duryodhana</s>, the descendant of <s>Subala</s> went
and said that very thing to <s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s>, elder brother of <s>Bhīma</s> and <s>Arjuna</s>, among the kings.
Then <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> and <s>Dhanaṃjaya</s>, their eyes copper-red with anger, said to him:
"<s>Ulūka</s>, tomorrow <s>Suyodhana</s> will see that he is ripe for Time.
And he who thinks <s>Gāṅgeya</s> his refuge in this battle
will see that very man cut apart by arrows released from <s>Gāṇḍīva</s>."
Thus sent back with an answer by the two of them, the son of <s>Gāndhāra</s>
went and reported it to <s>Dhārtarāṣṭra</s> in the midst of the kings.
Then, asked by <s>Suyodhana</s> about the number and rank of chariot-warriors, the grandsire
spoke, causing the beauty of thrilled excitement to rise on the faces of the heroes:
"Hear, in this array of armies, among the enemy's men and our own,
the distinctions between mahārathas and rathas among all the heroes in battle.
You, O king, are an excellent ratha, together with your brothers as rathas;
men like me are not bold enough to speak of their own merits.
<s>Hārdikya</s> is a heroic atiratha, and the king of <s>Madra</s> is equal to him.
<s>Bhūriśravā</s>, lord of a troop, is foremost among the best rathas.

children.text: rathaḥ sudakṣiṇo rājā saindhavo dviguṇo rathaḥ
children.translated_text: King <s>Sudakṣiṇa</s> is a ratha; the <s>Saindhava</s> is a double ratha.
<s>Vinda</s>, <s>Anuvinda</s>, and <s>Nīla</s> are renowned as the finest of chariot-warriors.

children.text: suśarmā sānujo vīro ratho vīrataro mama
children.translated_text: Heroic <s>Suśarmā</s>, with his younger brother, is a ratha, very heroic in my judgment;
so too are your son <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s> and your brother <s>Duḥśāsana</s>.
The heroic king <s>Daṇḍadhāra</s> is famed as an excellent ratha;
the great heroes <s>Ugrāyudha</s> and <s>Bṛhadbala</s> are excellent rathas.

children.text: śāradvataḥ kṛpo vīro yūthapānāṃ tu yūthapaḥ
children.translated_text: Heroic <s>Kṛpa</s>, son of <s>Śaradvat</s>, is a troop-leader among troop-leaders.
The king of <s>Gāndhāra</s>, <s>Śakuni</s>, your maternal uncle, is a ratha.

children.text: rudrasya tejasā yukto drauṇiḥ śataguṇo rathaḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Drauṇi</s>, endowed with <s>Rudra</s>'s energy, is a hundredfold ratha.
And <s>Droṇa</s>, leader of hosts of rathas, is a triple ratha.
<s>Satyaśravas</s> is a noble ratha; <s>Vṛṣasena</s> is a mahāratha.
<s>Jalasaṃdha</s> is an excellent ratha; the <s>Māgadha</s> is remembered as an atiratha.
Heroic <s>Bāhlika</s> is equal to him; <s>Satyamān</s> is an excellent ratha.
<s>Alabuṣa</s>, lord of rākṣasas, is famed as the best of rathas.
<s>Bhagadatta</s> of <s>Prāgjyotiṣa</s>, many times superior, is a lord of rathas."
<s>Vṛṣaka</s> and <s>Acala</s>, the two brothers, sons of <s>Gāndhāra</s>, are chariot-warriors.
Sensitive, intent on conciliation, and deprived of his armor and earrings,

children.text: puruṣaḥ katthano nīcaḥ karṇa eva rathottamaḥ ||
children.translated_text: that man, boastful and low, <s>Karṇa</s> alone is an excellent chariot-warrior.
Hearing this, <s>Karṇa</s>, his eyes reddened with anger, breathed like a serpent

children.text: uvāca bata vṛddho 'pi bhīṣma bālāyase dhiyā ||
children.translated_text: and said, "Alas, <s>Bhīṣma</s>, though old, you are childish in understanding.
From delusion, from causeless hatred, or from pride, words that tear the vitals,

children.text: satataṃ pāpa kaṭukaṃ bhāṣamāṇo na lajjase ||
children.translated_text: harsh and sinful, are what you constantly speak, wicked man; are you not ashamed?
When great battles are at hand, by those who know policy
even cowards are made into soldiers with words of false praise.
In this great royal task that must be borne, the contempt for great men
which you show makes me know that you have been set by the enemies as a divider.
I do not think it strange that this enumeration of chariot-warriors is spoken;

children.text: śauryaṃ tejaśca śūrāṇāṃ vacasā gaṇyate katham ||
children.translated_text: but how can the valor and splendor of heroes be measured by speech?
If king <s>Duryodhana</s> endures it because of the weight of the undertaking,
what has that to do with us, that we should endure insult?
I shall conquer the vast army of the <s>Pārthas</s> that has arrived.

children.text: uccaiḥ kṛto 'si mithyaiva kiṃ kurmo bhīṣma bhūbhujā ||
children.translated_text: You have merely been raised high in vain by the king, <s>Bhīṣma</s>; what can we do?
Or else, when the enemy has been conquered by me, the fame will come to you.

children.text: ahate tvayi gāṅgeya tasmādyotsye na pāṇḍavaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: Therefore, while you are unharmed, <s>Gāṅgeya</s>, I shall not fight the <s>Pāṇḍavas</s>."
When the son of the charioteer had spoken thus, the hero <s>Śāntanava</s> said,

children.text: viśrānte yudhyamāne vā kā nāmāsyā raṇe tvayi ||
children.translated_text: "Whether you are resting or fighting, what place at all is there for you in battle?
In this affair of the king, long pondered and now at hand,
discord is being restrained by us; for that reason, <s>Karṇa</s>, you are not killed.
Speaking thus, <s>Śāntanava</s>, questioned again by the <s>Kaurava</s>,
described the strength and weakness of the chariot-warriors in the <s>Pāṇḍava</s> army.

children.text: svayaṃ yudhiṣṭhiro rājā yamau ca balināṃ varau
children.translated_text: King <s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s> himself, and the twins, foremost among the strong,
will move through your army as great chariot-warriors of great energy.
<s>Bhīma</s> is a chariot-warrior eight times over, a hero commanding a hundred chariots;
and what sort of chariot-warrior <s>Phalguna</s> is is known to all heroes.
The five sons of <s>Draupadī</s> are chariot-warriors, and so is <s>Uttara</s>, son of <s>Virāṭa</s>.
<s>Abhimanyu</s> is equal to his father, and also to the foe of the gods.
<s>Sātyaki</s>, whose valor is true, is foremost among hosts of chariots;
and the heroes <s>Yudhāmanyu</s> and <s>Uttamaujas</s> are, in my view, two chariot-warriors.
The aged <s>Virāṭa</s> and <s>Drupada</s>, whose strength has been seen, are great chariot-warriors;
and <s>Dhṛṣṭadyumna</s> and <s>Śikhaṇḍī</s> are famed on earth as surpassing chariot-warriors.
<s>Kṛtavarmā</s>, however, is a half-chariot-warrior; the son of <s>Dhṛṣṭadyumna</s> is a child.
<s>Dhṛṣṭaketu</s>, <s>Kṣatradeva</s>, <s>Jayanta</s>, <s>Citrajit</s>, and <s>Jaya</s>,
<s>Kuntibhoja</s>, <s>Cekitāna</s>, and the five heroic <s>Kekayas</s>,
together with <s>Śaibya</s> and the king of <s>Kāśi</s>, are all regarded as excellent chariot-warriors.
<s>Śaṅkha</s> and the other sons of <s>Matsya</s>, and king <s>Vārakṣema</s>,
<s>Citrāyudha</s>, <s>Satyadhṛti</s>, and <s>Senābindu</s> the <s>Paurava</s>,
<s>Purajit</s>, <s>Candrasena</s>, and <s>Śreṇimān</s> are great chariot-warriors;
<s>Rocamāna</s> is equal to them, and so is <s>Vasudāna</s> together with his son.
The hero <s>Satyajit</s>, son of <s>Drupada</s>, I consider a chariot-warrior eight times over.
<s>Ghaṭotkaca</s> is many times greater, a foremost chariot-warrior among leaders of troops;
but the other heroic kings, the sons who delight <s>Pāṇḍu</s>, are half-chariot-warriors.
All these I shall fight, though they are guarded by the bearer of the <s>Gāṇḍīva</s>,
even with weapons raised, except for <s>Śikhaṇḍin</s> alone, who has the form of a woman.
Long ago, for the sake of my brother <s>Vicitravīrya</s>,
I carried off at their svayaṃvara the three daughters of the king, lord of <s>Kāśi</s>.
<s>Ambā</s>, <s>Ambikā</s>, and <s>Ambālikā</s>, those ravishers of kings,

children.text: rathe me yudhyamānasya latā iva cakampire ||
children.translated_text: trembled like vines in my chariot while I was fighting.
Then, seeing me depart after I had conquered all the kings of the earth,
the eldest of them, lotus-eyed and named <s>Ambā</s>, said:

children.text: sālvarājo mayā pūrvaṃ manasā dayito vṛtaḥ
children.translated_text: "Previously king <s>Śālva</s> was chosen by me in my heart as my beloved.
Hero, you should not carry me off by force, unwilling and helpless as I am."
Hearing this, I at once abandoned her, as though she were blazing,
with the thought of avoiding a stain upon the <s>Bhārata</s> family.

children.text: sā gatvā sālvanṛpatiṃ saṃkalpaṃ vinivedya tam
children.translated_text: She went to king <s>Śālva</s>, made that intention known to him,
and said, "Lord, accept me, who have come of my own accord out of love."
Thus addressed by her, whose eyes were like those of a young deer, the lord of <s>Śālva</s>,

children.text: hṛtānyeneti tāṃ mānī na jagrāha kulodgataḥ ||
children.translated_text: proud and high-born, did not accept her, saying, "You were taken by another."
By fate she had fallen from both sides; going in grief to a forest of ascetics,
she asked the sages for renunciation, telling them her own story.
Then her maternal grandfather, the royal seer <s>Hotravāhana</s>, who was staying there,
was distressed on hearing her tale and said:
"Daughter, on <s>Mahendra</s> mountain dwells <s>Rāma</s>, scion of the <s>Bhṛgu</s> family,
an ocean of compassion; go to that mighty one for refuge.

children.text: śiṣyo hi tasya vacasā guroḥ śantanunandanaḥ
children.translated_text: For <s>Śāntanunandana</s>, his pupil, at his teacher's command,

children.text: grahīṣyati parityaktāmapi tvāṃ mā śucaṃ kṛthāḥ ||
children.translated_text: will accept you, though you have been cast away. Do not grieve."
When this had been said, <s>Kṛtavrata</s>, the eldest disciple of <s>Jāmadagnya</s>,
came by chance to that region frequented by sages.

children.text: sa śrutvā pūjitaḥ kanyākathāṃ tāṃ hotravāhinīm
children.translated_text: Honored there, he heard from <s>Hotravāhana</s> that story of the maiden
and said, "Tomorrow morning <s>Rāma</s> himself will come to this forest."
When <s>Kṛtavrata</s> had spoken thus and that day had passed,
in the morning the glorious <s>Rāma</s> himself appeared, radiant.
After bowing to him, honored by the best of sages and seated on an adorned seat,
The princess, tearful, went for refuge to that ocean of compassion.
Hearing her story, he, whose heart was straightforward, said:

children.text: putri madvacasā bhīṣmo na tvāṃ tyakṣyati gauravāt ||
children.translated_text: "Daughter, out of respect <s>Bhīṣma</s> will not reject you when I speak.
I myself will go to the field of the <s>Kauravas</s>,
and, after instructing the son of <s>Śāntanu</s>, I shall arrange what is favorable to your desire."
Having said this, <s>Bhārgava</s>, accompanied by his pupils, took her with him
and went to <s>Kurukṣetra</s>, filling the quarters with masses of radiance.
Knowing that the sage, honored by the dwellers in heaven, had come in person,
I at once went out to meet him, placing the household priest before me.
When <s>Rāma</s>, with his followers, saw me come and had received my worship,

children.text: uvāca bhīṣma kanyeyaṃ hṛtā tyaktā ca kiṃ tvayā ||
children.translated_text: he said, "<s>Bhīṣma</s>, why was this maiden carried off and then abandoned by you?
Released by you and rejected even by wicked <s>Śālva</s>,
take this high-spirited woman, at my word, for your brother's sake."
Hearing this command of my teacher, that ocean of compassion,
I said, "This woman, tainted in feeling, is not fit for our family.

children.text: svayaṃ yātāṃ sālvapatiṃ tena tyaktāṃ ca madbhayāt
children.translated_text: She herself went to the lord of <s>Śālva</s>, and he rejected her from fear of me.
How can I, at your word, take her as a stain upon the family?
Be gracious, blessed one; it is not proper for you to say this now."
When I had addressed him so, <s>Rāma</s>, agitated with anger, said:
"Having been my pupil, <s>Bhīṣma</s>, how do you despise me through delusion?
Destruction stands before you, breaker of my command.
Ah, born of a new royal line, you do not know me,
me who twenty-one times destroyed the <s>kṣatriyas</s> (warrior class), the destroyer of the <s>Hehayas</s>."
Hearing those words of his, uttered again and again,
I replied, my body wet with the sweat of a slight rising anger:
"The wise call a teacher one who instructs people in the conduct of the good;
but scripture says that even he, if he has taken to a wrong path, is to be abandoned.
You are now ready to direct me in a matter removed from <s>dharma</s> (right order);
you deserve the points of my arrows in a battle over <s>kṣatriya</s> conduct.
All those <s>kṣatriyas</s> whom you killed before were cowards;
I think no man like me had been born then.
Fight as you wish, hero, accompanied by pupils and kings.
I stand ready, my bow my only companion, to cut down your pride."
When I had spoken thus, my proud teacher, the fiery son of <s>Bhṛgu</s>,
rose up at <s>Kurukṣetra</s>, a hero facing battle.
When he had mounted a divine chariot, his blazing weapons and splendor shining,

children.text: yuyutsuṃ jāhnavī devī mātābhyetya jagāda mām ||
children.translated_text: the goddess <s>Jāhnavī</s>, my mother, came to me as I wished to fight and said:
"Son, do not enter into hostility with the son of <s>Bhṛgu</s>,
the fire at the root of the <s>kṣatriya</s> race, while I ask this favor of you toward him."
Though addressed even by my mother, I did not abandon the vow of my family;

children.text: vīrā bhayapraṇāmeṣu bharatā na hi śikṣitāḥ ||
children.translated_text: for heroes of the <s>Bharatas</s> have not been trained in bows born of fear.
With my bow drawn, I bowed to that teacher of all archers,
and for a moment I stood motionless, wishing for the first fall of his arrow.
Then, while the sky was encircled by rings of flame from the circle of his weapons,
for a moment I became invisible amid the masses of arrows.
Then, filling the ten directions with the sound of my conch,
I fought in battle against <s>Rāma</s>, the cessation-point of <s>kṣatriya</s> prowess.
As I fought with him, unshaken, for three days,
all the gods honored my valor, raining flowers.
Again and again I was sustained by the <s>Vasus</s> in the form of Brahmins and by <s>Jāhnavī</s>,
my mind stunned by the descent of the weapon of <s>Jāmadagnya</s>.
Then, with a host of great weapons, I conquered in battle, with effort,
<s>Bhārgava</s>, the pupil of <s>Pinākin</s>, whose purpose had grown slack.
Thereupon he withdrew from that crushing clash of battle, amazed,
and, with his neck somewhat bent, said to the daughter of the king of <s>Kāśi</s>:

children.text: durjayo yudhi gāṅgeyaḥ kiṃ karomi nṛpātmaje
children.translated_text: "The son of <s>Gaṅgā</s> is hard to conquer in battle. What can I do, princess?
The <s>kṣatriya</s> race is exceedingly cruel; it does not honor me as teacher.

children.text: adhunā kṣattriyaḥ śiṣyo mayā varjya iti bruvan
children.translated_text: Now a <s>kṣatriya</s> pupil is to be avoided by me,"
said <s>Rāma</s>, and went to <s>Mahendra</s>; I entered my own city.
Then the daughter of the lord of <s>Kāśi</s>, tormented by the fire of anger and grief,
performed still more terrible austerity in the hermitages of the great seers.
"May another birth come to me, dishonored as I am, for the killing of <s>Bhīṣma</s>."
With this intention, at sacred fords, she gradually became one who took no food.
Seeing her emaciated by fierce austerity, the divine river said to her:
"At the end of your body, crooked in conduct, you will be in the land of <s>Vatsa</s>,
known as the river <s>Tumbī</s>, frequented by terrible creatures."
Thus addressed by the heavenly river, in time she steadfastly worshiped <s>Vṛṣabhadhvaja</s>,
the boon-giving lord, and obtained the boon she had in mind.
In time she was born, by the will of the Lord, to <s>Drupada</s>,
a king who desired a son and practiced fierce austerity, first as a daughter.
"This girl will become a man," the blessed Lord declared;
therefore the king proclaimed her as his son.
Given the name <s>Śikhaṇḍin</s>, that girl, a false little son,
took as wife <s>Sulocanā</s>, daughter of the lord of <s>Dāśārṇa</s>.

children.text: sā yauvanavatī dṛṣṭvā śayyāyāṃ tāṃ śikhaṇḍinīm
children.translated_text: When that young woman saw <s>Śikhaṇḍinī</s> on the bed

children.text: striyaṃ duḥkhārditā pitre dūtyā sarvaṃ nyavedayat ||
children.translated_text: to be a woman, she was stricken with grief and reported everything to her father through a messenger.
The king of <s>Dāśārṇa</s>, <s>Hiraṇyavarman</s>, learning that his daughter
had been given to a false son, came to fight <s>Drupada</s>.
When that very vast, impetuous army was drawing near,
<s>Drupada</s>, filled with anxiety, could not reach a decision about what should be done.

children.text: viṣaṇṇaṃ pitaraṃ dṛṣṭvā mātaraṃ ca śikhaṇḍinī
children.translated_text: Seeing her father despondent, and her mother too, <s>Śikhaṇḍinī</s>,
thinking herself the cause, went alone to the forest.
There, afflicted by grief, fasting, and protected by <s>Sthūṇākarṇa</s>,
in that forest she saw a great mansion encircled with jewels.

children.text: praviśya sahasā tasthau nirāhārā ciraṃ śucā
children.translated_text: Entering suddenly, she remained there for a long time, fasting in sorrow.
And the <s>yakṣa</s> (nature-spirit), seeing her and hearing her story, spoke:
"Receive the sign of a man, given by me, O slender-waisted one;

children.text: gatvā trāyasva pitaraṃ nijaṃ rūpaṃ prayaccha me ||
children.translated_text: go and rescue your father, and then give me back my own form.
When your purpose has been accomplished, before long you will again become a woman."

children.text: iti saṃvidamādāya visṛṣṭā tena sā yayau ||
children.translated_text: Having made this agreement and been released by him, she went away.

children.text: dattaṃ vinimayāttena sā rūpaṃ prāpya pauruṣam
children.translated_text: Taking from him through exchange the form that he gave, she gained masculinity,
and, reaching her own city, reported her story to her father.
The lord of <s>Dāśārṇa</s>, delighted when he saw his son-in-law well pleased,
summoned <s>Drupada</s>, bestowed much wealth, and departed.
Meanwhile the lord of wealth himself went to <s>Sthūṇākarṇa</s>'s house;

children.text: yāto dadarśa strīrūpaṃ taṃ hriyā nodgataṃ puraḥ ||
children.translated_text: there he saw him in female form, not coming forth before him because of shame.
Then <s>Kubera</s>, having learned the story, spoke to him:

children.text: strīrūpa eva pāpa tvaṃ narastvastu śikhaṇḍinī
children.translated_text: "Remain female in form, wicked one; but let <s>Śikhaṇḍinī</s> be a man.
By my word, let this exchange last as long as that one lives."
Having said this, when <s>Vaiśravaṇa</s> himself had gone away in anger,
the son of <s>Drupada</s>, his purpose achieved, approached that <s>yakṣa</s>.
He had come, in his honesty, to give back his own form, being truthful;
but seeing <s>Śikhaṇḍin</s>, the <s>yakṣa</s> said with a downcast face:

children.text: gaccha pāñcālya nedaṃ me strīrūpaṃ yujyate svayam
children.translated_text: "Go, O <s>Pāñcālya</s>; this female form of mine does not suit me.
Because of the lord of wealth's curse, I have lost my form, and you have been protected."

children.text: iti yakṣavacaḥ śrutvā śikhaṇḍī svapuraṃ yayau
children.translated_text: Hearing these words of the <s>yakṣa</s>, <s>Śikhaṇḍin</s> went to his own city,
skilled in every missile and weapon, with valor equal to a <s>yakṣa</s>.

children.text: evaṃ na strī na puruṣaḥ strīpūrvo drupadātmajaḥ
children.translated_text: "Thus the child of <s>Drupada</s>, formerly a woman, is neither woman nor man;

children.text: varjyo yudhi mayā nityamiti me kṣatriyavratam ||
children.translated_text: he must always be avoided by me in battle: this is my <s>kṣatriya</s> (warrior) vow.
One who is fleeing, has laid down weapons, has loosened hair, or is without armor,

children.text: strīpūrve śaraṇaṃ yāte na śūraḥ śantanoḥ sutaḥ ||
children.translated_text: one who was formerly a woman or has sought refuge, is not one whom the son of <s>Śantanu</s> will strike."
When <s>Bhīṣma</s> had said this at night in the assembly of kings,
<s>Duryodhana</s> bowed to his grandsire in the morning and said:
"In how much time can the ocean-like army of the sons of <s>Pāṇḍu</s>

children.text: śaktaḥ kṣapayituṃ kiṃ vā droṇaḥ karṇaḥ kṛpo 'thavā ||
children.translated_text: be destroyed by you, or perhaps by <s>Droṇa</s>, <s>Karṇa</s>, or <s>Kṛpa</s>?"
Thus addressed by the king of the <s>Kurus</s>, the son of <s>Śantanu</s> said with a laugh:
"Constantly displaying great weapons, I am able to destroy that army in a month."
When he had said this, the teacher also said the same.
<s>Kṛpa</s> said, "in two months," and <s>Drauṇi</s> said, "in ten days;"
<s>Karṇa</s> promised the destruction of the foe in five days.

children.text: tato vihasya sotprāśaṃ bhīṣmaḥ karṇaṃ vigarhayan
children.translated_text: Then, laughing with mockery, <s>Bhīṣma</s> censured <s>Karṇa</s>,
and did not approve, describing the great strength of <s>Savyasācin</s>.
Meanwhile the son of <s>Dharma</s> addressed <s>Śvetavāhana</s>:
"O <s>Pārtha</s>, I think the battle-lines of the <s>Kuru</s> king are boundless;

children.text: kālena kiyatā tāsāṃ kṣayaṃ phalguṇa manyase ||
children.translated_text: in how much time, O <s>Phalguṇa</s>, do you think their destruction can be achieved?"
Asked thus by the king, the son of <s>Śakra</s> spoke:
"I will be the fighter, <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> the charioteer, and the mighty <s>Gāṇḍīva</s> the bow.

children.text: astraṃ pāśupataṃ ghoraṃ priyaṃ devasya dhūrjaṭeḥ
children.translated_text: There is the terrible <s>Pāśupata</s> weapon, dear to the god <s>Dhūrjaṭi</s>;
what reliance can there be on mortals, when something equal to this is raised?"
When <s>Kaunteya</s> had said this, from the warriors' delight,
the bodies of the kings became like jackets clearly bristling with gooseflesh.
At that moment, at the king's command, <s>Kṛpa</s>, the son of <s>Somadatta</s>, the lord of <s>Madra</s>, <s>Bhagadatta</s>, <s>Jayadratha</s>, and the others,

children.text: agresaraṃ tripathagātanayaṃ vidhāya yuddhāṅgaṇaṃ viviśurāśu vimuktadhāma ||
children.translated_text: placing the son of <s>Tripathagā</s> at their head, quickly entered the battlefield, their splendor released.

children.text: puṇye bhārgavabhinnabhūpanidhane kṣetre tataḥ kaurave kaunteyasya samantapañcakataṭe senāniveśo babhau
children.translated_text: Then, on the holy <s>Kuru</s> field at the bank of <s>Samantapañcaka</s>, where kings had been slain by <s>Bhārgava</s>, the camp of <s>Kaunteya</s> shone
with weapons like flames from the jewels on <s>Śeṣa</s>'s heads, agitated by the earth's surface rubbed and shaken by masses of swift, tall horses and elephants.

The lords of the <s>Karṇāṭas</s>, <s>Aśvakas</s>, and <s>Karūṣikas</s>, the lords of <s>Matsya</s>, <s>Aṅga</s>, and <s>Vaṅga</s>, the <s>Śailas</s>, <s>Saindhavas</s>, <s>Sālvas</s>, <s>Mālavas</s>, <s>Śakas</s>, and kings of <s>Prāgjyotiṣa</s>,

children.text: suhmakrāthakirātacīnayavanā gauḍetraparyantajāḥ kṛcchreṇa kṣitipālalakṣanibiḍaṃ tatrāntaraṃ lebhire ||
children.translated_text: the <s>Suhmas</s>, <s>Krāthas</s>, <s>Kirātas</s>, <s>Cīnas</s>, <s>Yavanas</s>, <s>Gauḍas</s>, and those born at the borders scarcely found room there, crowded as it was with hundreds of thousands of kings.
Having bowed to <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> and to <s>Nara</s>, the best of men,
to the goddess <s>Sarasvatī</s> and to <s>Vyāsa</s>, then one should proclaim the <s>Jaya</s>.
When kings from the world visible to men, pervaded as far as the sun's rays,
had gathered at holy <s>Kurukṣetra</s>, the sacred abode,
when the armies had become one in the battle of <s>Kuru</s> and <s>Pāṇḍava</s>,
and the quarters, with only old men and children left, had gone empty,
when dreadful omens had appeared everywhere,
and the two armies, with their banners, came within sight of each other,
<s>Hṛṣīkeśa</s> and <s>Dhanaṃjaya</s> joyfully blew their conches,
and at the deep sound of those conches the worlds trembled.

children.text: viṣamastho na hantavyo na ca senāvinirgataḥ
children.translated_text: "One who is in a disadvantaged position is not to be killed, nor one who has gone out from the army,

children.text: na nivṛtte raṇe ceti maryādāṃ cakrire nṛpāḥ ||
children.translated_text: nor when he has turned away from battle": so the kings established the rules.
Meanwhile <s>Pārāśarya</s>, lord of sages, came near
and addressed <s>Dhṛtarāṣṭra</s>, who was distressed and had gone into the palace.
In this complete gathering of heroic earth-protecting kings,
a terrible destruction of the <s>kṣatra</s> (warrior power), O king, has arrived.

children.text: divyaṃ gṛhāṇa nayanaṃ svayaṃ yuddhaṃ vilokaya
children.translated_text: Receive divine sight; behold the battle yourself.
When the sage had said this, the king, his mind troubled, replied:
Blessed one, I cannot bear to see the slaughter of my kinsmen,
and, since what is destined must inevitably happen, I am not able to prevent it.
When the king had spoken thus, the boon-giving sage
made <s>Sañjaya</s> divine-eyed and again addressed the ruler of the earth:

children.text: ayaṃ te nikhilaṃ yuddhaṃ kathayiṣyati saṃjayaḥ
children.translated_text: This <s>Sañjaya</s> will tell you the whole battle;
nothing will be unknown to him, for he will have divine sight.
Death yawns wide for the kings, <s>Dhṛtarāṣṭra</s>, because of your bad policy,
for evil omens are seen, whispering ruin in the ear.

children.text: saureṇa pīḍitā gāḍhaṃ rohiṇī jvalitā diśaḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Rohiṇī</s> is sorely oppressed by <s>Śani</s>; the quarters are blazing.
Births are inverted, and the sun is covered by a headless trunk.
The sky is filled with flesh-eating creatures; clouds rain blood.
What more? Alas, the earth, queen of kings, will no longer be.
Fire with its flame turned to the right, and likewise serenity of mind,
these are clear signs of victory; where <s>dharma</s> (righteous order) is, there victory is.
Hundreds may be conquered by one, while one may not be conquered even by hundreds;
this edge of the sword is unsteady, and certainty is not to be reckoned here.
When the lord of sages had spoken thus and quickly disappeared, the king
asked <s>Sañjaya</s> about the arrangement of the continents, and, being asked, he spoke:
O king, in the broad disk of the cool-rayed moon, shaped like a mirror,
the whole spacious island <s>Sudarśana</s> is reflected.
On one side it has the shade of a pippala tree, and on the other the form of a hare.
In this circular island, encircled by the salt ocean,
a tall golden mountain stands in the middle like the pericarp in a lotus.
Other mountains lie on both sides of that mountain,
beginning with <s>Himālaya</s>, touching east and west.
To the south are <s>Himavān</s>, <s>Hemakūṭa</s>, and <s>Niṣadha</s>;
to the north are mighty <s>Śṛṅgavān</s>, <s>Nīla</s>, and <s>Śveta</s>.
Between these mountains, variegated with jewels, are the lands called <s>varṣas</s>.
<s>Bhārata-varṣa</s> is the land of action; the others are lands of enjoyment.
In <s>Harivarṣa</s> and the lands beginning with it, the creation of beings is like <s>Smara</s> in beauty;

children.text: sthānaṃ sukṛtināṃ yatra vikhyātā gaṇḍikā iti ||
children.translated_text: there is the abode of the meritorious, famed as <s>Gaṇḍikā</s>.
Likewise, below <s>Meru</s> lies <s>Jambūkhaṇḍa</s>; from its flowing fruit
the bright river <s>Jambū</s> was born, producing <s>jāmbūnada</s> gold.
The northern <s>Kurus</s>, drinking that very water, become free from death.
This island is named from that tree which touches heaven.
Having spoken thus, <s>Sañjaya</s> went to the battlefield at <s>Kurukṣetra</s>,
and, returning to <s>Dhṛtarāṣṭra</s>, reported the destruction of his own warriors.
Listen, O king: after the son of <s>Śantanu</s> had slain countless feudatory chiefs,
he made the victory of the sons of <s>Pāṇḍu</s> doubtful.
When the armies had been mutually arrayed by the elephant-like kings
in the two formations called <s>Vajra</s> and <s>Sūcīmukha</s>, by <s>Gāṅgeya</s> and <s>Arjuna</s>,
in that field of <s>kṣatriya</s> destruction, where all <s>kṣatriyas</s> had assembled,
with <s>Duryodhana</s> fiercely enraged and proud of his vast army,
when the ocean of troops had risen up at the conch-blast of <s>Gāṅgeya</s>,
and at the conch-sound of the sons of <s>Pṛthā</s>, following <s>Pāñcajanya</s>,
when the expanse of the world was filled, as though the quarters were thundering,
glorious <s>Vijaya</s>, whose charioteer was <s>Acyuta</s> and who was the refuge of the whole army,
saw among the <s>Kuru</s> forces his teachers, relatives, and kinsmen.
Thinking that they had become like moths in the fire of his own valor,
he, distressed and full of compassion, said to <s>Govinda</s>:

children.text: aho bata vimūḍhānāṃ rājyaleśe sukhāya naḥ
children.translated_text: Alas! For us bewildered men, for the pleasure of a mere scrap of kingdom,
O <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, this violent undertaking proceeds even to the killing of kinsmen.
Having abandoned the praise of good conduct and overstepped the standing of our family,
how could one like us enjoy prosperity obtained by the killing of teachers?
Having spoken thus, <s>Bībhatsu</s>, his eyes filled with tears, out of pity, in the chariot
dropped <s>Gāṇḍīva</s> from his hand and sat down despondent.
Seeing him overpowered by grief, <s>Madhusūdana</s> said:
At this untimely moment, what is this cowardice of yours, you whose very substance is courage?
An energetic, proud <s>kṣatriya</s> buys fame even with his life.

children.text: nijāṃ kulasthitiṃ pārtha na dharmyāṃ hātumarhasi ||
children.translated_text: O <s>Pārtha</s>, you must not abandon your own righteous family station.

children.text: saṃyuktaṃ vā viyuktaṃ vā nityaṃ dehena dehinam
children.translated_text: Whether the embodied self is joined to the body or separated from it,
what knower of truth grieves in this display of universal illusion?
Just as pleasure and the other states of the body arise from time to time in their due forms,
so too bodies arise for this embodied one who truly exists, while they themselves lack true being.
The one who endures the contacts of objects and senses, perishing things that give joy and sorrow,

children.text: sahate yo viluptātmā nirvāṇaṃ tasya śāśvatam ||
children.translated_text: with the self unconfounded, has everlasting <s>nirvāṇa</s> (release).
For this unborn, ancient, indestructible embodied self,
the imagining of a body is like the replacement of worn-out leaves.
For this embodied one, whose nature is manifest and unmanifest at beginning, middle, and end,

children.text: sata evāsya satataṃ na virāmaḥ śarīriṇaḥ ||
children.translated_text: there is always being itself; there is no cessation.
Therefore, abandoning this disgraceful shrinking, broad-minded one,

children.text: jayājayau samaṃ matvā viśa svargonmukho raṇam ||
children.translated_text: regarding victory and defeat alike, enter the battle with heaven before you.
Having adopted yogic understanding, free from the bondage of action,
experience the state beyond the <s>guṇas</s>, devoid of dry Vedic rites.
For the wise, this alone is the purpose in all the Vedas,
as, when reservoirs are full, for those who carry water.
Unattached, renouncing the fruit, perform the action that is always prescribed,
offering it only to the supreme Lord; for bargaining belongs to those who seek fruit.
When your understanding, freed from delusion, reaches calm,
then you will be fulfilled, indifferent to the meanings heard in scripture.
As he was speaking thus, <s>Pārtha</s> asked the Blessed Lord
about the marks of one whose wisdom is steady and who is absorbed in concentration; he replied as follows.
'There is no other than the Lord; I am full of my own bliss':
one who has cast off every intention is called a man of steady wisdom.
Like a tortoise drawing in its limbs, he abides with desires withdrawn into their refuge;
because he is free from meditation on sense-objects, that man of steady mind does not perish.
By hard austerities the sense-objects merely dry up, but not the taste for them,
for those who are without disdainful detachment and do not always see the inner self.
He who sleeps among beings in their waking time and is awake amid darkness
becomes unshaken like the great ocean and attains the state of <s>brahman</s>.
Hearing this, <s>Arjuna</s>, his mind troubled, said to <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>:
'How, speaking in this way, do you yoke me to this terrible battle?
After saying yourself, Lord, that understanding is better than action,
you praise action suited to the foolish, bewildering me.'
When the white-horsed one said, 'Tell me what is best,' <s>Keśava</s> replied:
'A twofold foundation, through wisdom and action, has been taught by me for <s>Sāṃkhya</s> and <s>Yoga</s>.
A person is not freed from action by not beginning it, nor by abandonment;
his hearing and the other senses run forcibly toward their own activities.
Even when the organs of action are restrained, people remember everything with the mind;
false in conduct, inwardly attached, they are workers with a controlled appearance.

children.text: śreyo hyakarmaṇaḥ karma na yajñaḥ karmaṇā vinā
children.translated_text: Action is better than inaction, for there is no sacrifice without action;
those who eat the remains of sacrifice are trees of merit, while others are mere enjoyers.
Even while established in action, when a human being reaches freedom from attachment,
satisfied in the state of delighting in the self, then he turns away from duties.
By action alone <s>Janaka</s> and others in ancient times attained perfection;
therefore do not turn away from duty; let the world follow you.
Even for me, though I have done all that must be done, this action protects stability;
otherwise the world would perish, loosed from my authority.
An ordinary person is not a vessel for teachings fit for the all-knowing when he lacks respect;
therefore one should not urge such people on, like lame men set moving at speed.
Fight, calmly renouncing all actions in me;

children.text: taranti hi tamo ghoraṃ nityaṃ manmatavartinaḥ ||
children.translated_text: for those who continually follow my view cross over the terrible darkness.
Do everything suited to your nature, devoted to your own <s>dharma</s>,
abandoning attachment and aversion, born from what is dear and not dear.'
Hearing this, <s>Arjuna</s> said: 'Driven by what does a powerless creature
commit evil, as if forcibly brought under control?'

children.text: iti pṛṣṭo hṛṣīkeśo jagāda jagatāṃ patiḥ
children.translated_text: Asked thus, <s>Hṛṣīkeśa</s>, lord of the worlds, spoke:
'It is by this, arising from the quality of passion, giver of joy, grief, and the rest,
by desire, whose companion is anger, whose habit is the destruction of the world,
by this strong, terrible enemy, by egoism.
As water is covered by moss, as the stainless sky by dust,
so the self is covered by impurity, like the risen sun by a cloud.
Its seat is the cage of the senses, joined with mind and understanding;

children.text: yasya taṃ duḥsahaṃ śatruṃ kāmarūpa vināśaya ||
children.translated_text: destroy that unbearable enemy in the form of desire.

children.text: sūryeṇāptaḥ purā matto yogo 'yaṃ manunā tataḥ
children.translated_text: Long ago this <s>yoga</s> was received from me by the Sun, and then by <s>Manu</s>;
that very teaching, lost through time, has been declared by me to you today.
You are witness to many births, my devotee and also my companion,

children.text: na tatsmṛtipathaṃ yātaṃ kiṃtu te prāktanaṃ vapuḥ ||
children.translated_text: but that has not entered the path of your memory, because your former body is gone.

children.text: ahaṃ tu nityadharmasya sthitaye guptaye satām
children.translated_text: But I, for the establishment of eternal <s>dharma</s> and the protection of the good,
come into being age after age for the destruction of the wicked.
This action does not cover me, the maker of <s>dharma</s> who is himself unmade;
you too, unattached and without desire, should perform the action proper to your lineage.
The distinction among action, inaction, and wrong action is hard to know:

children.text: svocitaṃ phalahīnaṃ ca viruddhaṃ ceti bhedataḥ ||
children.translated_text: they are divided as what is proper to oneself, what is without fruit, and what is contrary.
Whoever, through renunciation of the fruit of action, perceives inaction in action,
and whoever knows action in sinful inaction, that person is wise.
One whose actions are burned by the fire of knowledge, eternally blissful and without dependence,
free from expectation and ego, a sacrificer, is dissolved in <s>brahman</s>.
Having offered a <s>brahman</s>-made oblation into the fire of <s>brahman</s> by an offering that is <s>brahman</s>,
one devoted to the sacrifice of the breaths goes to <s>brahman</s> through concentration on <s>brahman</s>.
Some offer the senses into the fire of restraint, and sense-objects into the fire of the senses;
having offered those actions into the fire of the self's <s>yoga</s>, they go to the highest goal.
Others too, sacrificers through gifts, austerity, <s>yoga</s>, recitation, and knowledge,
after holding, here in the channels, the restraint of breath, exhalation, and the rest,
spotless, surrender all knowledge;
eating the nectar left from sacrifice, they go to the supreme abode.
When such knowers are served by you with reverent prostration,
they will effortlessly make you one who sees the whole in your own self.
Burned clean of sin by the fire of knowledge, you will become pure;
in time, for those who have faith, knowledge becomes clear of itself.'
Fools who partake of doubt perish, but not those whose doubt has been cast away;
therefore, as a knower, cut off doubt, stand up, and rise for glory.
Hearing that, <s>Pārtha</s> again asked <s>Madhusūdana</s>:
"Tell me, O <s>Janārdana</s>, which is better, renunciation or <s>karmayoga</s> (the discipline of action)?"
Questioned in this way, <s>Śauri</s> said: "Both of these lead to liberation,
but <s>karmayoga</s> is superior to renunciation; such is my view.
Even while hearing, even while speaking, even while touching, in their own duties,

children.text: saktā api na sajanti paṅke ravikarā iva ||
children.translated_text: though engaged, they do not cling, like rays of the sun in mud.
Whatever is enjoined for human beings as merit and demerit
is just this: when knowledge is covered by ignorance, there is this latent impulse toward action.
Those whose ignorance has been driven away by knowledge reach the supreme state;

children.text: brāhmaṇe vā śvapāke vā vibudhāḥ samadṛṣṭayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: the wise look equally upon a brāhmaṇa and upon a dog-cooker.
For those detached from external pleasure, which is perishable and gives birth to sorrow,
the supreme light becomes clear through delighting in inner happiness.
Having cast off outward contacts, fixing the gaze between the brows,
and holding the breath and downward breath equal within the nostrils, they strive for liberation.
Free from desire, passion, pride, hatred, fear, and anger,
free from envy, one finds peace from egoism and the darkness of ignorance.

children.text: kriyāvān aphalākāṅkṣī nijaṃ karma karoti yaḥ
children.translated_text: One who is active, without longing for the fruit, performs his own action;
having passed beyond the state of one wishing to ascend, he is mounted in yoga and free from envy.
Firm and satisfied with knowledge, he sees the self by the self,
steady in seat and form, like an ocean without waves.
Looking at the tip of the nose, with mind at peace, he reaches me through <s>samādhi</s> (concentration),
when his food and other activities are disciplined and his mind is always unwavering.
The yogin who has abandoned desires certainly attains the self;
restraining the mind, they see it wherever it flows.

children.text: ātmānaṃ māṃ ca sarvatra mamātmani tathākhilam
children.translated_text: They see the self and me everywhere, and likewise everything in my self.
This restless mind is restrained only by detachment,
and by powerful practice, like a violently rushing wind.
Hearing this, <s>Kaunteya</s> again asked <s>Keśava</s>:
"O god, because of the mind's fickleness, what is the fate of one fallen from yoga?"
Questioned again in this way by <s>Arjuna</s>, the Blessed Lord replied:
"Even one fallen from yoga will become a person who has done good;

children.text: ciraṃ bhuktvā sukhaṃ divyaṃ sa kalyāṇapuraḥsaraḥ ||
children.translated_text: having long enjoyed divine happiness, he is led onward by auspicious merit.

children.text: bhogināṃ yogināṃ vāpi sambhūto mahatāṃ kule
children.translated_text: Born either in the family of enjoyers or of yogins, among the great,
the wise man regains, through later births, what was practiced before.
Yoga surpasses austerity and knowledge; therefore become a yogin, O <s>Arjuna</s>.

children.text: mayi nyastamanā nityaṃ bhaktyā māṃ vetti mānava
children.translated_text: A human being whose mind is always placed in me knows me through devotion.
I, of eightfold form, am all; I am the living being in what moves and does not move.
The wise know me as the cause of creation, maintenance, and destruction.

children.text: sarve matprāṇitā bhāvā mayi sarvaṃ pratiṣṭhitam ||
children.translated_text: All states of being are impelled by me; everything is established in me.

children.text: devīṃ māyāṃ dadhānaṃ māṃ na jānāti vimohitaḥ
children.translated_text: The deluded person does not know me as bearing divine <s>māyā</s> (cosmic illusion);

children.text: ye tu jānanti māṃ māyāṃ bhavanti kṛtinaḥ sadā ||
children.translated_text: but those who know me and <s>māyā</s> are always successful.

children.text: arthī jijñāsurārto vā jñānī vā māṃ prapadyate
children.translated_text: The seeker of gain, the seeker of knowledge, the distressed, or the knower may take refuge in me;
but I am constantly within reach of the knower, who is dear to the dear one.
Those devoted to no other deity, faithful and free from doubt,
worship me, desiring liberation, thinking, '<s>Vāsudeva</s> is all.'
They know me as what is called <s>brahman</s> (ultimate reality), <s>adhyātma</s> (the inner self), and action, together with <s>adhibhūta</s> (the material domain),
and also together with <s>adhidaiva</s> (the divine domain) and <s>adhiyajña</s> (the sacrifice-principle), even at the departure from the body.
When <s>Acyuta</s> had spoken thus, the son of <s>Śakra</s> said:
"What is this <s>brahman</s>, O Blessed Lord, and what is called <s>adhiyajña</s>?"
Questioned in this way, <s>Hṛṣīkeśa</s> spoke to <s>Śvetavāhana</s>:
"The imperishable is the supreme <s>brahman</s>; the state of the self is <s>adhyātma</s>.
Action, unattached, producing worldly existence, and the condition belonging to perishable things is <s>adhibhūta</s>.
Here I myself am <s>adhidaiva</s>, and I, the all-pervading one, am also <s>adhiyajña</s>.
Those who remember me at the time of death, having become intent on me, enter me alone.
For the state at the end of life is equal to the disposition of people in another birth.
Those who remember the seer, the ancient one, the ruler, subtler even than the subtle,
eternal, beyond darkness, and shining like the sun,
placing the breath between the brows and piercing the aperture of <s>brahman</s>,

children.text: omityekākṣaraṃ brahma japanto yānti te param ||
children.translated_text: reciting <s>om</s>, the one-syllabled <s>brahman</s>, they go to the supreme goal.
The creation of beings, beginning with <s>Brahmā</s>, revolves like a wheel;

children.text: paraṃ māṃ pratipannāste na bhavanti bhave punaḥ ||
children.translated_text: but those who attain me, the supreme, do not come again into becoming.

children.text: vairañce 'smin ahorātre bhavanti na bhavanti ca
children.translated_text: In this day and night of <s>Vairañca</s>, beings come to be and cease to be;
but the one Blessed Lord, unmanifest, does not perish.
The luminous day, bright and northward-leading, is solely for liberation.
Listen also, O <s>Phalguṇa</s>, to this royal secret, purifying and fruitful.
One without faith, brought under the power of <s>saṃsāra</s> (worldly wandering), does not attain me.

children.text: sarvakartari bhūtāni mayi santi na teṣvaham
children.translated_text: All beings exist in me, the doer of all; I am not in them.

children.text: lokāḥ sthitā na sthitāśca mayi vyomnīva vāyavaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Worlds are both established and not established in me, like winds in the sky.
This <s>prakṛti</s> (primordial nature), presided over by me, gives birth to what moves and does not move.
Those of stained and fruitless vision do not know me as unattached.

children.text: sarvaṃ sarvagataṃ yajñaṃ vedyaṃ bījaṃ bhavābhavam
children.translated_text: The virtuous know me as everything, all-pervading, sacrifice, the knowable, the seed, and existence and non-existence,
as the cause of all causes.
Those devoted to the religion of the three Vedas, troubled by the gain and loss of heavenly enjoyment,
do not attain me, being bound by the snare of dry ritual action.
Those worthy ones who have me alone as refuge, who are constant and worship no other,
even if born from other wombs, come by themselves to that state."

children.text: bhūyo 'pi me śṛṇu sakhe prītyā yatpratibodhyase
children.translated_text: Listen again, my friend, with affection, to that by which you are being instructed by me.

children.text: na tattvenāmaragaṇā munayo vā vidanti mām ||
children.translated_text: Neither the hosts of immortals nor even the sages know me in truth.
Whatever preeminent thing, endowed with majesty, you see in this moving and unmoving world,

children.text: tadahaṃ sarvabhūtātmā na hi kiṃcinmayā vinā ||
children.translated_text: that am I, the self of all beings; for there is nothing apart from me.
I am <s>Viṣṇu</s>; I am the sun, the moon, and <s>Maghavan</s>.
I am <s>Śaṃkara</s> and the lord of wealth; I am fire and also the guru of the gods.
I am the imperishable; I am time; I am victory, and I am prosperity as well.
Hearing this, <s>Pārtha</s> said, "I know you as everything, O <s>Acyuta</s>;

children.text: kiṃtu viśvamayaṃ rūpaṃ draṣṭumicchāmi te vibho ||
children.translated_text: yet I wish to see your form made of the universe, O <s>Vibhu</s>."
Thus addressed by the son of <s>Pāṇḍu</s>, the blessed slayer of <s>Kaiṭabha</s>
displayed the universal form by the power that manifests the universe.
In the body of him who possessed endless thousands of heads, eyes, and arms,
of him who is the abode of the world, the universe was seen absorbed.
Seeing that splendor, which filled the sky with a radiance surpassing the sun and fire,
<s>Pārtha</s>, thrilled with horripilation, spoke to him with joined palms:
"I see you, your vast body pervaded by an exalted host of gods,
you by whose boundless form everything is filled.
Crowded with <s>Brahmā</s>, <s>Rudra</s>, the <s>Maruts</s>, fire, chief sages, and serpents,
I cannot bear to look upon that very body, without any end.
I see heroes headed by <s>Bhīṣma</s> and <s>Droṇa</s> entering your mouths,
terrible with fangs, like the mouths of time at the destruction of an age.
Who are you, with this terrible form of total destruction,
suddenly risen by yourself to burn up all the worlds?"
When <s>Kaunteya</s> had spoken thus, <s>Madhusūdana</s> said:
"I am the ender of kings, consecrated for the destruction and upheaval of the world.
Kill the heroes at the front of the <s>Kuru</s> army, already slain before by me,
and obtain fame and fortune, fitting for your lineage.
Hearing the words of <s>Kāliya</s>'s foe, <s>Pārtha</s>, with joined palms,
bowed down and spoke with a trembling mind and a faltering voice:
"The worlds rejoice in your fame, and in the praise sung by <s>Siddhas</s> and <s>Cāraṇas</s>;

children.text: dīptyā dravanti rakṣāṃsi sthāne tava janārdana ||
children.translated_text: the demons flee from your brilliance. This is fitting, O <s>Janārdana</s>.
Again and again I bow to you, the abode of the world, the universal form, O <s>Adhokṣaja</s>,

children.text: anantaṃ śāśvataṃ dhāma sarvātmānaṃ punaḥ punaḥ ||
children.translated_text: the endless, eternal abode, the self of all.
Forgive that, since you love those who bow to you,

children.text: ukto 'si kṛṣṇa govinda yādaveti purā mayā ||
children.translated_text: you were formerly addressed by me as 'friend,' '<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>,' '<s>Govinda</s>,' and '<s>Yādava</s>.'
Having seen this great, fierce form, O blessed lord,
I see the entire world as if mounted upon a wheel.

children.text: prasīda darśaya vibho vapuḥ saumyaṃ tadeva me
children.translated_text: Be gracious, O <s>Vibhu</s>; show me that same gentle body.

children.text: śāntiṃ me yāti sahasā nānyathā vyathitaṃ manaḥ ||
children.translated_text: My distressed mind will suddenly come to peace in no other way."
Thus propitiated by the bowing wearer of the diadem, <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>
then showed his own form, that same four-armed one.

children.text: devā api na paśyanti mamedaṃ sarvagaṃ vapuḥ
children.translated_text: "Even the gods do not see this all-pervading body of mine";
having said this, the lord of <s>Kamalā</s> reassured <s>Kaunteya</s>.
Then <s>Arjuna</s> said to <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, "Those devotees who worship you,
and those who worship the unmanifest imperishable: which of them are the greater yogins?"
Asked thus by <s>Pārtha</s>, <s>Hari</s>, having granted favor, said:
"My devotees, endowed with faith, are in every way the greater yogins.
But attainment of me comes only with difficulty through service of the unmanifest imperishable;
the path of the subtle and the gross is painful, even for knowers of reality to attain.
My devotees, however, attain the supreme state very quickly;
therefore keep your mind on me always, devoted to nothing else.

children.text: vaśe yadi na te cittam abhyāsena gṛhāṇa tat
children.translated_text: If your mind is not under your control, seize it through practice.
If you are unable even in that, then be one who constantly performs my work for your own good.
Or, devoted to me, undertake renunciation of the fruits of actions.
For knowledge is higher than mere practice, and meditation here is better than knowledge.
Renunciation of fruit is better than meditation, and from that peace is superior.
One who hates none, an ocean of compassion, equal in pleasure and pain, tranquil,

children.text: udāsīnaḥ śucirdakṣaḥ kṣamī bhaktaḥ priyo mama
children.translated_text: indifferent, pure, capable, and patient: such a devotee is dear to me.
The body is called the <s>kṣetra</s> (field); the wise know me as the <s>kṣetrajña</s> (knower of the field).

children.text: kṣetraṃ tatsavikāraṃ tu māyā bhūtādi ca sthitam ||
children.translated_text: That field, together with its modifications, is established as <s>māyā</s> and the elements and so forth.
For peaceful knowers who have seen its faults, there is no delusion.
The abandonment of honor, hypocrisy, pride, and anger, and service to the guru,
and constant non-attachment to what is perishable: this is knowledge; anything else is ignorance.

children.text: jñeyaṃ tu manmayaṃ brahma śuddhaṃ sadasatoḥ param ||
children.translated_text: But what is to be known is Brahman, consisting of me, pure, beyond being and non-being.
It has hands and faces everywhere, every form, and is free from affliction.
<s>Prakṛti</s> (nature) and <s>puruṣa</s> (person): this is the union of field and knower of the field.

children.text: prakṛtiḥ karaṇe heturbhoktā tu puruṣaḥ smṛtaḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Prakṛti</s> is the cause in the instruments of action, while <s>puruṣa</s> is remembered as the enjoyer.
Whoever sees the separate existence of beings as resting in one place,

children.text: tatsaṃgamācca vistāraṃ sa yāti brahma śāśvatam
children.translated_text: and their expansion from that union, goes to the eternal Brahman.
The supreme self is beyond the <s>guṇas</s> (qualities), imperishable because it is eternal;

children.text: bhautike 'pi sthitaḥ kāye sarvavyāpī na lipyate ||
children.translated_text: though situated even in a material body, it is all-pervading and is not stained.
Listen again to this complete knowledge, honored by the gods,
the yoga by which, in this womb of Brahman, embodied arising comes about.
Born from that, the three <s>guṇas</s>, beginning with <s>sattva</s>, shine forth;
through their variety embodied beings wander in saṃsāra without cease.

children.text: sattvaṃ prakāśakaṃ jñeyaṃ yadutthaiḥ stambhakaṃ rajaḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Sattva</s> is to be known as illuminating; <s>rajas</s> is binding through what arises from it.
For <s>tamas</s> is a covering, from which delusion, negligence, and the like arise.
Through the constant intermixture of these, and through distinctions of deficiency and excess,

children.text: guṇadoṣāśca dṛśyante te te kila śarīriṇām ||
children.translated_text: various virtues and faults are indeed seen among embodied beings.
My devotees, whose minds are tranquil and who have entered the state of liberation while living,
free from these <s>guṇa</s>s (qualities), enjoy imperishable happiness.
The aśvattha tree of existence has its root above and rises up to the abode of <s>Brahmā</s>;
it has many branches in other worlds and sprouts in manifold objects of sense.
For those awakened by <s>guṇa</s> and action, it brings forth auspicious and inauspicious fruits;
whoever knows it as spread upon the ground of innate nature is a knower of the Veda.
Cutting it with the axe of nonattachment, they go to my state,
free from delusion, stainless, and beyond sun, moon, and fire.
The living being, a portion of that, moves everywhere in this world of living beings;
like the wind taking up fragrance, it carries away the impressions of the senses.
The wise see that being, of such a kind, though joined with the <s>guṇa</s>s in all states, as beyond <s>guṇa</s>s,
the supreme life of all the worlds.
Though I enter into the creation of beings, I am imperishable and eternal;
those who are filled with me and steadfast worship me as <s>Puruṣottama</s>.

children.text: abhīḥ sattvaṃ śucirjñānaṃ damo dānaṃ tapaḥ kratuḥ
children.translated_text: Fearlessness, sattva, purity, knowledge, self-restraint, giving, austerity, and sacrifice,
nonviolence and other virtues arise from the divine endowment.
By hypocrisy, pride, intoxication, anger, harshness, ignorance, and fickleness
the demonic endowment is indicated, increasing delusion and grief.

children.text: yukto 'pi satataṃ divyasaṃpadā mā śucaḥ sakhe
children.translated_text: You are constantly joined with the divine endowment, so do not grieve, friend;
those who have entered a demonic disposition resort to a demonic womb.
A person, bound by <s>guṇa</s>s such as sattva, is known by his actions;
for the mind, food, and conduct of embodied beings correspond to their <s>guṇa</s>.
Having heard this, <s>Phalguna</s> then again said to <s>Acyuta</s>:
"Lord, I wish to know the true nature of renunciation and abandonment."
When the son of <s>Pāṇḍu</s> had spoken thus, the Blessed Lord replied:
"They declare renunciation to be the abandonment of the fruit of desired acts.
The abandonment of the fruits of all actions is called <s>tyāga</s> (abandonment);

children.text: matkarma na parityājyaṃ tyājyaṃ tu vidhigarhitam ||
children.translated_text: action done for me should not be abandoned, but what is condemned by rule should be abandoned.
Abandonment of obligatory action through delusion is called tāmasa;
abandonment through fear of hardship and pain is remembered as rājasa and fruitless;
but abandonment by those who act without attachment is regarded as proper to sattva.

children.text: karma kartā ca buddhiśca trividhā guṇabhedataḥ
children.translated_text: Action, the agent, and understanding are threefold according to the distinction of <s>guṇa</s>;

children.text: dhṛtiḥ sukhaṃ ca traiguṇyāttrividhaṃ dehināṃ matam ||
children.translated_text: steadfastness and pleasure too, through the three <s>guṇa</s>s, are considered threefold among embodied beings.

children.text: yathoktasevī niḥsaṅgaḥ kuru karma nijaṃ sakhe
children.translated_text: Follow what has been taught; unattached, perform your own action, friend.
Devoted to me and intent on praising me, you will attain the supreme state.

children.text: idaṃ bhaktāya te jñānamupadiṣṭaṃ mayā svayam
children.translated_text: This knowledge has been taught by me myself to you, my devotee;
whoever hears it will cross beyond the sufferings of <s>saṃsāra</s>.
Has your delusion been destroyed? Has this been heard by you?"
When <s>Keśava</s> had spoken thus, the son of <s>Śakra</s> said:
"Blessed Lord, I am free from delusion; I shall carry out your command."
Having said this, the hero drew <s>Gāṇḍīva</s>, eager for battle.
Then, as he looked upon <s>Pārtha</s> eager to fight,
there arose among the armies a joyful roar, slow and deep as thunderclouds.
Then, while the armies of the kings first rang with the clanging of swords striking the armor of fine warriors,
the son of <s>Dharma</s>, putting aside armor, bow, and arrows, eagerly advanced toward <s>Devavrata</s>.
"Shame, shame on the king, mean in conduct, merely called a man, a coward, falsely named <s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s>!
This man goes to his enemies with joined palms to beg." So the heroes, stunned by his gesture, spoke separately.
But he too, of spotless fame, approached <s>Bhīṣma</s> and the others, bowing before the <s>Dhārtarāṣṭra</s>s who had staked their bodies;
with his crown touching their feet, he bowed openly and received a blessing that would conquer the whole earth.
And when the mṛdaṅgas and trumpets of the battlefield were struck, <s>Yuyutsu</s>, virtuous and devoted solely to the virtues of the <s>Pārtha</s>s,

children.text: abhyāyayau tava sutaḥ svakurūnnirasya dhāvanti tulyaguṇameva nṛṇāṃ manāṃsi ||
children.translated_text: your son came over, abandoning his own <s>Kuru</s>s; men's minds run only toward equal virtue.
In this drama of battle, at the mouth of great destruction, with its front guarded by bands of swords,
before <s>Arjuna</s> he seemed to recite a prologue with loud bow-twangs, scattering handfuls of flowers of fame.
Meanwhile, where many disturbed sparks had arisen from the collision of the tips of the crowns in the circle of kings,
the victorious, lofty row of hundreds of arrows from <s>Gāṅgeya</s>, the pupil of the sage who was disciple of the trident-bearer, blazed up.
Hearing <s>Bhīma</s>, whose terrible roar made all the worlds tremble as the elephants of the quarters drew in their motionless ear-flaps in terror,
a fearsome roar like a storm-cloud at the end of the age, fear appeared among the warriors.

children.text: atha bhīmaṃ samabhyāyāt svayaṃ rājā suyodhanaḥ
children.translated_text: Then King <s>Suyodhana</s> himself advanced against <s>Bhīma</s>,
together with heroic brothers, shaking his broad bow.
Then, when battle began and was hard to discern because of showers of arrows,
the illustrious son of <s>Śantanu</s> himself charged at <s>Dhanaṃjaya</s>.
<s>Kṛtavarman</s> attacked <s>Sātyaki</s>, and <s>Bṛhadbala</s> attacked <s>Abhimanyu</s>;
<s>Duḥśāsana</s> attacked <s>Nakula</s>, and <s>Durmukha</s> attacked <s>Sahadeva</s>.
<s>Śalya</s> likewise attacked <s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s>, and the teacher attacked the son of <s>Drupada</s>;
<s>Somadatta</s> attacked the prince of <s>Virāṭa</s>, and <s>Bāhlika</s> attacked the lord of <s>Cedi</s>.
<s>Alumbusa</s> attacked the heroic <s>Ghaṭotkaca</s>, foremost of rākṣasas,
the son of <s>Droṇa</s> attacked <s>Śikhaṇḍin</s>, and the lord of <s>Prāgjyotiṣa</s> attacked the <s>Matsya</s> king.
<s>Kṛpa</s> attacked the king of the <s>Kekaya</s>s, and <s>Jayadratha</s> attacked <s>Drupada</s>;
and mighty <s>Vikarṇa</s> attacked <s>Sutasoma</s>, the son of <s>Bhīmasena</s>.
<s>Cekitāna</s> attacked <s>Vikarṇa</s>, and <s>Saubala</s> attacked <s>Prativindhya</s>;
and <s>Śatāyu</s> attacked brave <s>Irāvat</s>, the son of <s>Phalguṇa</s>.
The two <s>Avanti</s> kings, <s>Vinda</s> and <s>Anuvinda</s>, attacked the renowned <s>Kuntibhoja</s>;
and the <s>Kaurava</s> <s>Vīrabāhu</s> attacked <s>Uttara</s>, son of <s>Virāṭa</s>.

children.text: anye ca vīrā rājāno rājasiṃhāḥ prahāriṇaḥ
children.translated_text: Other heroic kings too, lion-like rulers and fierce strikers,
rich in courage and spirit, rushed upon him together with their armies.
From their hands came masses of rays from jeweled bracelets,
and golden-feathered arrows made the horizon seem filled with fire.
Then, amid the fierce dust and the press of elephants, horses, and chariots,
a tumultuous battle of heroes began, with all bounds broken.
Then, with the heads of heroes repeatedly falling and bounding up,
the fortune of battle seemed to be playing an eager game of ball.
Thereafter, as the <s>Pāṇḍava</s> armies were repeatedly torn apart
by arrows released from <s>Bhīṣma</s>'s bow, a great cry arose.
Then heroic <s>Abhimanyu</s>, grandson of the son of <s>Śatamanyu</s>, came forward
and charged at <s>Bhīṣma</s> while all the kings looked on.
With force he fought <s>Bhīṣma</s>, who was accompanied by <s>Kṛtavarman</s> and the others,
using arrows, and he cut down his banner.
When the golden palm-standard had fallen, the grandsire grew enraged,
and, showering divine missiles, swiftly rushed upon <s>Saubhadra</s>.
Then great chariot-warriors headed by <s>Vṛkodara</s>, roaring aloud,
surrounded <s>Śantanu</s>'s son on every side, together with his followers.
<s>Bhīṣma</s>, too, pierced <s>Sātyaki</s>, and with the point of an arrow
tore from the chariot the golden lion on the banner of the Wind-god's son.
Meanwhile, delighted <s>Uttara</s>, son of <s>Virāṭa</s>, mounted a rutting elephant
as tall as a mountain peak and fought the king of the <s>Madra</s>s.

children.text: sa kuñjarendraḥ śalyasya pādena caturo hayān
children.translated_text: That lordly elephant, roaring with the sound of a cloud,
dragged away <s>Śalya</s>'s four horses with its trunk and killed them with its foot.

children.text: tato madrādhipaḥ kruddhaḥ śaktiṃ śaktimatāṃ varaḥ
children.translated_text: Then the enraged lord of <s>Madra</s>, foremost among wielders of spears,
in agitation hurled a blazing spear at <s>Uttara</s>, who was raining arrows.
His heart split by it, <s>Uttara</s> dropped his weapon and fell,
like a karṇikāra blossom fallen from the mountain-peak of the great elephant.
Seeing <s>Uttara</s> slain, his younger brother <s>Śaṅkha</s>, in anger,
came at <s>Śalya</s> and made his body bristle with arrows.

children.text: tasya śalyo 'tha gadayā vidārya dalaśo ratham
children.translated_text: Then <s>Śalya</s> split his chariot to pieces with a mace,
and roared so that the quarters seemed to be shattered.

children.text: śaṅkho hatāśvaḥ sahasā phalguṇasya rathaṃ yayau
children.translated_text: With his horses killed, <s>Śaṅkha</s> suddenly went to <s>Phalguṇa</s>'s chariot;
then <s>Bhīṣma</s>, destroyer of kings, plunged into the <s>Pāṇḍava</s> army.
As the troops of the <s>Matsya</s>s, <s>Kekaya</s>s, <s>Pāñcāla</s>s, and <s>Cedi</s>s everywhere
were split apart by <s>Bhīṣma</s>'s arrows, the sun went to the western mountain.
Then, when the battle had ceased, the kings
went to their camps, praising <s>Bhīṣma</s>'s vast valor.
At day's end, his army shattered and his heart afflicted with grief, the son of <s>Dharma</s>
brooded over the destruction of his own forces and over <s>Bhīṣma</s>'s valor.
In the midst of the kings, overcome with pity, he said to <s>Govinda</s>:
"As I am being worn away in battle, austerity is truly better for me.
Enough of this war for me, O <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, which brings about the destruction of the earth.

children.text: ko mucyeta raṇe prāpya bhīṣmaṃ bhīṣmaparākramam ||
