children.translated_text: Who could escape in battle after meeting <s>Bhīṣma</s>, whose valor is terrible?"
To the king who was speaking thus, <s>Madhusūdana</s> replied:
"Your victory is certain, O king, since <s>Dhanaṃjaya</s> is your warrior.
<s>Sātyaki</s>, <s>Drupada</s>, <s>Śaibya</s>, <s>Śikhaṇḍin</s>, the five <s>Kekaya</s>s,
and wrathful <s>Saubhadra</s> in battle could kill even hosts of enemies."
When <s>Janārdana</s> had spoken in this way, they discussed among themselves

children.text: mithaḥ kathayatāṃ teṣāṃ sā jagāma vibhāvarī ||
children.translated_text: the fierce prowess of <s>Bhīṣma</s>, and that night passed away.
Then, when the thousand-rayed sun had risen, the sons of <s>Pāṇḍu</s>
formed the crane battle-array with great energy, and the others also formed an array.
Thereafter, when a fierce battle had begun, terrifying to the timid
and shaking the heart, the palm-bannered one was seen in the command of battle.
With deep and steady fury, avoiding ordinary men,
he swiftly cut off the heads of kings alone.
When the battle-array had been tossed by <s>Bhīṣma</s>, like the ocean stirred by wind,
the white-horsed one, with <s>Acyuta</s> as his charioteer, rushed angrily against him.
As he came on, <s>Bhīṣma</s> quickly filled him with arrows,
as did all the other great chariot-warriors headed by <s>Droṇa</s> and <s>Duryodhana</s>.
<s>Pārtha</s>, too, with his shafts, made the <s>Kuru</s> army on every side
seem torn into a thousand pieces by the wide winds of their feathered arrows.
Then, urged on by <s>Duryodhana</s>, <s>Śantanu</s>'s son himself,
as if reproaching his own <s>kṣatradharma</s> (warrior duty), rushed at <s>Dhanaṃjaya</s>.
As the two fought there for a long time without distinction between them,
the ten directions were blocked by their net of arrows and could not be seen.

children.text: na dadarśa tayoḥ kaścidantaraṃ kṣipatoḥ śarān
children.translated_text: No one perceived any interval between the two as they shot arrows,
like two roaring clouds powerful with torrential streams of rain.
Then heroes headed by <s>Droṇa</s> fought
with those led by <s>Dhṛṣṭadyumna</s>, so that the gods in heaven thrilled with wonder.
Then <s>Bhīmasena</s> entered the army of the <s>Kaliṅga</s>s,
and, felling elephants, made the earth impossible to cross.
Through streams of bloody fluid that arose from the temples of rutting elephants split open by <s>Bhīma</s>,
the horses, moving with difficulty, went on up to their throats.
Having slain the elephant-host of the attacking <s>Kaliṅga</s>s,
he killed King <s>Ketumant</s> together with his foot-followers.
At the roar of <s>Bhīmasena</s>, who had exterminated the <s>Kaliṅga</s>s,
the earth trembled with a sound deep as thunderclouds.
Then <s>Bhīṣma</s> came up, saw that the army had been split apart,
made <s>Bhīma</s> chariotless, and struck down the horses of <s>Śaineya</s>.
<s>Abhimanyu</s>, with sharp arrows, struck down brave <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>,
the valor-marked and swift-handed son of <s>Duryodhana</s>.
Seeing his son fallen within reach of destructive <s>Saubhadra</s>,
King <s>Duryodhana</s> himself rushed forward with his followers.
Seeing his son surrounded by Kuru heroes, <s>Arjuna</s>
at once advanced against the foes, making <s>Gāṇḍīva</s> whirl in a circle.
Because of that wondrous warrior's quickness, his arrows from every side
cut off the heads of heroes like fruits from trees.
When the armies, with chariots and horsemen shattered, were torn apart
by arrows driven from the fierce <s>Gāṇḍīva</s> by the son of <s>Ākhaṇḍala</s>,
and when the sky was filled, as if with blood, by the red of evening,
at the end of the day the grandsire ordered the withdrawal from battle.
On the next day, seeing the <s>Gāruḍa</s> formation arranged by <s>Bhīṣma</s>,
the sons of <s>Pāṇḍu</s> made the half-moon as their counter-formation.
Then, when the battle began, shattering the courage of the timid,
the earth seemed, through the dust, to have climbed into the sky.
When the mass of dust was suddenly stilled by streams of blood,
there arose a dreadful clash of kings, watched by the thirty gods.
In battle, with heroes headed by <s>Bhīṣma</s> and <s>Droṇa</s>, and with those headed by <s>Phalguṇa</s>,
they appeared locked together like immortals with primeval gods.
As the showers of weapons of the enemies, massed together on every side,
were checked by <s>Arjuna</s> with a great net of arrows,
the two heroes <s>Bhīmasena</s> and <s>Ghaṭotkaca</s>, unshaken in the Kuru formation,
entered and threw the enemy army into confusion.
The wrathful son of <s>Dhṛtarāṣṭra</s> rushed at those two in fury,
making the quarters red with the crest-jewels of the gathered kings.
The heroes in his train, struck down by arrows from <s>Haiḍamba</s>,
trembled like trees overtaken by a mighty wind.
The terrible rising shower of blazing arrows
sent by <s>Duryodhana</s> was quickly cut apart by <s>Vṛkodara</s>.
Then the <s>Kaurava</s>, pierced in the chest by a broad shaft
released by <s>Bhīma</s> and sunk deep, fainted in great distress.
When he was carried away by his charioteer in a chariot with its banner disordered,
that whole army fled while <s>Droṇa</s> and <s>Bhīṣma</s> looked on.
Although restrained by great chariot-warriors, in that scattered ocean of troops
King <s>Suyodhana</s> regained courage and quickly advanced again.
Seeing the army repeatedly routed by <s>Pārtha</s>, <s>Sātyaki</s>, and <s>Saubhadra</s>,
he approached the grandsire and spoke to him:
"See my army torn apart by enemies who strike their mark,
while you, out of pity for the sons of <s>Pāṇḍu</s>, have taken to neutrality.
It would be enough for you, with <s>Droṇa</s> as helper, to stand in the front,
if, by the force of my ill fortune, you did not have compassion for the <s>Pārtha</s>s."
Hearing this said by <s>Suyodhana</s>, the son of the celestial river
spoke, the surface of his cheeks washed by the nectar of a slight smile:
"You have been told many times, O king, that the <s>Pāṇḍava</s>s are unconquerable;

children.text: yattu śakyaṃ mayā kiṃcidvṛddhenādya karomi kim ||
children.translated_text: yet whatever little can be done by me, an old man, I shall do today."
Having spoken thus, the great-armed one drew his bow to the measure of a palm tree,
and, as the day was growing dim, advanced against the foes all at once.
Then, by arrows risen from <s>Bhīṣma</s>'s chariot and bright as sunbeams,
many divisions, torn apart like darknesses, went to destruction.
On lances, on parasols, and on the bodies of kings,
arrows marked with <s>Bhīṣma</s>'s name fell, bringing them to final nonexistence.
Again and again, by his arrows, massed like dense ranks, whose nocks and heads could not be seen,
the army of the <s>Pāṇḍava</s>s became invisible.
Even while avoiding him as he fought in battle with blazing weapons,
all the kings saw thousands of <s>Bhīṣma</s>s in the quarters.
As the circles of kings became moths in the fire of <s>Bhīṣma</s>,
three elephants at a time were split by each single arrow.
When the army of the vigorous <s>Pāṇḍava</s>s had been divided into a thousand fragments,
<s>Acyuta</s> brought <s>Phalguṇa</s>'s chariot near the son of <s>Gaṅgā</s>.
Then, by the radiant arrows of <s>Bhīṣma</s>, for <s>Savyasācin</s>
there was for a moment, as for a lion, a beautiful golden cage.
Though the movement of his arrows was blocked, the son of <s>Śatamanyu</s>,
with <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> as charioteer, fought by moving with effort along varied courses.
The grandsire, delighted, praised the more-than-human steadiness
of him who stood firm in valor, saying, "Well done, my son!"
Those two dark ones, standing in one chariot and pierced by his heron-feathered arrows,
shone, sprinkled with blood, like two blooming red aśoka trees.
Then, by unbroken arrows released from <s>Bhīṣma</s>'s bow,
which overran the expanse of the world, the ten directions could not be seen.
When <s>Bhīṣma</s>, like the fire of time, had risen with broad flames of arrows,
The <s>Pāṇḍava</s> army fled, pursued from behind by the enemy.
When the foremost warriors had been broken, <s>Kaiṭabhāntaka</s> said:
“Where now are you, whose wealth is honor, in this battle of boundless fame?
Abandoning the conduct of your lineage, you have fallen into this cowardice.”
Having spoken thus and seeing them still fleeing, <s>Keśava</s>
addressed the brave <s>Sātyaki</s>, who was fighting with effort:

children.text: tiṣṭhantu yāntu vā sarve sātyake pṛtanāgragāḥ
children.translated_text: “Let all the leaders of the army stand or go, O <s>Sātyaki</s>;

children.text: eṣa svayaṃ nihanmyadya sānugaṃ śantanoḥ sutam ||
children.translated_text: I myself today will kill the son of <s>Śantanu</s>, together with his followers.”
Having said this, <s>Kaṃsāri</s> himself raised <s>Sudarśana</s>, whose edge was like the disk of the blazing sun,
and descended from the front of the chariot.
When he was angry, his radiance was like the terrible fire at the end of an aeon;

children.text: na rūpaṃ sehire draṣṭuṃ surā api divi sthitāḥ ||
children.translated_text: even the gods standing in heaven could not bear to look upon his form.
With his staff-like arms whirling in fury and his yellow garment flashing,
he assumed the splendor of a blue mountain covered with moving clouds at twilight.
Seeing him coming like <s>Antaka</s>, consecrated for the destruction of the world,
the steadfast son of <s>Śantanu</s>, shaking his bow, said:
“Come, come, Blessed <s>Viṣṇu</s>, conqueror of the enemies of the gods;
cut off my head with your discus, the fire that burns away the afflictions of existence.
By you, from whose navel-lotus the self-born one arose,
by you, the dwelling-place of the world, if I am slain, let this person attain blessedness.”
When the son of the sacred river had spoken thus with bowed head,
<s>Arjuna</s> quickly descended from his chariot and followed <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>.
Pressing down by force upon the feet before the enemy of <s>Kāliya</s>,
he said, “Lord, restrain this anger fit for the destruction of the universe.
I will destroy all the enemies in battle; by truth I swear this to you.”
Having appeased him in this way, <s>Pārtha</s> made him mount the chariot again.
Then, with the sound of the <s>Gāṇḍīva</s> and the roar of the <s>Pāñcajanya</s>,
the two <s>Kṛṣṇas</s> made the circles of kings seem like dark rain clouds.
Then <s>Śalya</s>, <s>Bhūriśravas</s>, <s>Śala</s>, and those headed by <s>Bhīṣma</s>, with arrows packed without gaps,
covered <s>Phalguṇa</s> with showers of weapons.
Cutting through that great rain of weapons at once, the <s>Pāṇḍava</s>
deployed the <s>Māhendra</s> weapon, capable of destroying all worlds.
When that great weapon, blazing with fiery power, was suddenly unleashed,
the <s>Kuru</s> army trembled as if scattered by a fierce wind.
As the troops were being swiftly slain by the bearer of the <s>Gāṇḍīva</s>,
a river of blood flowed, rising from the bodies of men, elephants, and horses.
Ghosts frequented that river, whose sheets of foam were umbrellas, whose water-birds were moving yak-tail fans,
and which was mottled with hair as with water-moss.
While that terrible destruction of kings, a festival of battle, was taking place,
the quarters, as twilight came on, seemed filled with blood.
When the fierce-rayed sun, fresh in the color of blood, had gone to its setting,
it seemed like a lump of flesh swallowed by the terrible demon of darkness.
Their bows and armor shattered, their chariots and banners scattered,
the <s>Pāṇḍavas</s>, wounded by weapons, made their withdrawal.
Again at dawn the <s>Kurus</s> and <s>Pāṇḍavas</s>, enraged, marched out,
roaring with great energy at the front of the <s>vyāḍa-vyūha</s> (battle formation).
Then, when the battle began, portending the destruction of the earth,
the heroes led by <s>Saubhadra</s> fought the warriors headed by <s>Bhīṣma</s>.
Then <s>Bhīṣma</s>, filling the spaces between the quarters with torrents of hundreds of arrows,
passed beyond the other great chariot-warriors and rushed upon <s>Arjuna</s>.
While those two heroes were fighting evenly and swiftly,
<s>Abhimanyu</s> alone fought the heroes headed by <s>Droṇa</s>.
Having cut apart the armor, standards, and chariots of those great chariot-warriors,
he quickly made a heap of severed kings’ heads fall.
Seeing <s>Saubhadra</s> surrounded by all those beginning with <s>Droṇa</s>,
<s>Dhṛṣṭadyumna</s>, lord of the army, came up and cut down the <s>Kauravas</s>.

children.text: sa hatvā cāmaraṃ śūraḥ pauravyatanayaṃ nṛpam
children.translated_text: That hero killed <s>Cāmara</s>, the king and son of <s>Pauravya</s>,
and tore from <s>Saṃyamani</s>’s body his head with its earrings disordered.
Meanwhile, with vast elephant forces, the lord of elephants,
ordered by <s>Duryodhana</s> against <s>Bhīma</s>, rushed forward with mace in hand.
Then <s>Bhīmasena</s>, with impetuous force, descended from his chariot against the elephants,
and, roaring, struck them down with heavy blows of his mace, mighty in dense assault.
Struck by the blows of the mace, like mountains split by the thunderbolt,
the maddened elephants fell, and the earth trembled as if frightened.
When the elephant army had been slain by fearsome <s>Bhīma</s>,
all those beginning with <s>Duryodhana</s>, enraged, charged at him.
Then <s>Vṛkodara</s>, stunned by the impact of <s>Suyodhana</s>’s arrow,
recovered and angrily entered the enemy army in his chariot.
As he rose up like <s>Kṛtānta</s>, enraged for the destruction of the universe,
fourteen younger brothers of the <s>Kuru</s> lord, encountering him, went to destruction:
<s>Senāpati</s>, <s>Suṣeṇa</s>, <s>Jayasaṃdha</s>, <s>Sulocana</s>,
<s>Bhīma</s>, <s>Ugra</s>, <s>Bhīmaratha</s>, <s>Bhīmabāhu</s>, and <s>Alolupa</s>,
together with <s>Sama</s>, <s>Vivitsu</s>, <s>Kaṭaka</s>, <s>Durmukha</s>, and <s>Duṣpradarśana</s>.
Having slain these, he made the army of the <s>Kauravas</s> into a thousand fragments.
<s>Bhagadatta</s>, with his followers, charged at him on the maddened elephant <s>Supratīka</s>,
whose cry was deep and terrible.
With sharp arrows like rays from that sun of splendor rising over the elephant like an eastern mountain,
he and the enemy host, inflamed with anger, were struck from close at hand.
Then, pierced in the heart by his arrow, which split a vital spot,
Clinging to the flagstaff, <s>Bhīma</s> stood utterly unconscious.
Then <s>Ghaṭotkaca</s>, enraged on seeing his father distressed,
rushed at <s>Bhagadatta</s> and deployed a terrible illusion.
Then, mounted on <s>Airāvaṇa</s> and accompanied by maddened elephants of the quarters,
he pressed hard upon <s>Supratīka</s> with blazing showers of weapons.
As that lordly elephant was being pierced and roared,
at its sound all the elephants stood clustered together, shrinking back.
Seeing the lord of <s>Prāgjyotiṣa</s> locked in combat with <s>Ghaṭotkaca</s>,
<s>Bhīṣma</s>, together with heroes such as <s>Droṇa</s>, rushed to that place.
Seeing <s>Ghaṭotkaca</s>, death-like, roaring, and terrifying,
<s>Bhīṣma</s>, best of the wise, judged that warrior of fierce valor unconquerable at twilight,
and ordered the withdrawal of his fine armies,
by which the <s>Kaurava</s>s seemed to have escaped from the mouth of death.
Then at night the Kuru king approached the grandsire
and, distressed, asked the reason for the victory of the sons of <s>Pāṇḍu</s>.
The son of <s>Śantanu</s> said to him, "O king, you have always been told

children.text: devena viṣṇunā guptā na jeyāḥ pāṇḍavā iti ||
children.translated_text: that the <s>Pāṇḍava</s>s, guarded by divine <s>Viṣṇu</s>, cannot be conquered.
Long ago, for the calming of earth's burden, <s>Svayaṃbhū</s>, in an assembly of sages,

children.text: prādurbhūtaṃ svayaṃ viṣṇuṃ tuṣṭāva sahasāṃ nidhim ||
children.translated_text: praised <s>Viṣṇu</s> himself when he appeared, the storehouse of powers:
"Victory to you, lord of the universe, soul of the universe, <s>Viśvaksena</s>, treasury of nectar,
solid bliss of undiminished consciousness, radiant with the uniform light of awareness.
Homage to you, maker of the creation, preservation, and destruction of the world,
to the great <s>Trivikrama</s>, possessing the three guṇas and the three forms.
Homage to you whose arms are splendid with the brilliance from the edge of your fierce discus,
destroyer of the darkness of demons, cleaver of delusion.

children.text: avatīrṇā bhuvaṃ nātha dānavā ye hatāstvayā
children.translated_text: O lord, those proud demons who, having descended to earth,
were slain by you: enter a human body for their destruction."

children.text: iti stutāḥ padmabhuvā devo nārāyaṇaḥ prabhuḥ
children.translated_text: Thus praised by the lotus-born one, the god <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, the lord,
descended to earth together with <s>Nara</s>, to calm earth's burden.
He is this blessed <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, born as the delight of the <s>Yādava</s>s,
and <s>Nara</s> is the steadfast <s>Vijaya</s>, foremost of all bowmen.
These two gods, <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> and <s>Arjuna</s>, cannot be conquered even by the thirty gods;

children.text: iti jñātvā śamaḥ putra kriyatāṃ pāṇḍunandanaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: knowing this, my son, make peace with the sons of <s>Pāṇḍu</s>.
Then at dawn, those standing at the fronts of the makara and hawk formations,
with <s>Bhīṣma</s> and <s>Bhīma</s> at their heads, made battle with the sons of <s>Pāṇḍu</s>.

children.text: hatānāṃ hanyamānānāṃ ghnatāṃ ca samare mithaḥ
children.translated_text: Of men slain, being slain, and slaying one another in battle,
of heroes falling there, there arose a tumultuous roar.
By <s>Bhīma</s>, <s>Phalguṇa</s>, <s>Saubhadra</s>, the <s>Matsya</s> prince, <s>Sātyaki</s>, and the <s>Pārṣata</s>s,
and by those led by <s>Bhīṣma</s>, the two armies, split apart, fell into danger.
In that fierce battle, where headless trunks danced and maddened vetālas crowded together,
the dreadful combat became a festival for spirits.
As bowmen repeatedly shot up a net of arrows into the sky,
when the sun was covered, the kings' mass of weapons became useless.
Seeing <s>Sātyaki</s> engaged with the hero <s>Bhūriśravas</s>,
<s>Sātyaki</s>'s sons, bow in hand, rushed upon that place.
As they charged, pouring down a full rainy day of arrows,

children.text: bhūriśravāḥ śirāṃsy ārād uccakarta śitaiḥ śaraiḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Bhūriśravas</s>, from close by, cut off their heads with sharp arrows.
When they had been killed, the angry <s>Dhanaṃjaya</s>, with his weapon blazing,
with <s>Hari</s> as charioteer, made a slaughter of the Kuru armies.
When a fourth of a hundred thousand unretreating kings had been slain,
the army was withdrawn at day's end by the wielder of the <s>Gāṇḍīva</s> bow.
Again at dawn the Kurus and Pāṇḍavas, armored for battle, set out
with the hard-to-discern divisions of their two formations, the krauñca and the makara.
Then <s>Bhīmasena</s>, suddenly crushing the enemy force,
entered it, fiercely enraged, together with the son of <s>Drupada</s>.
When the formation had been split by those two, the angry sons of <s>Kuru</s>
quickly surrounded them with hostile elephant corps.
In battle, from the bodies of elephant-riders crushed by the blows of <s>Bhīmasena</s>'s mace,
there arose a terrible confusion as they fell.
As the armies were fighting with strong-armed <s>Bhīma</s>,
King <s>Suyodhana</s> himself, with his followers, rushed at him.
Seeing <s>Bhīma</s> covered by the <s>Kaurava</s>s with showers of arrows,
the <s>Pārṣata</s> bewildered them with the mohana weapon.
When <s>Droṇa</s> himself came up and neutralized the mohana weapon with the jñāna weapon,
<s>Bhīma</s> swiftly charged the Kuru lord.
"Blind with pride, where will you go now alive while I am alive?
Having said this, they covered him with hundreds of arrows swift as thunderbolts.
Then, by arrows fallen from <s>Bhīma</s>'s bow, his chariot-banner was cut away,
and, torn open in the chest, he fell into a faint, his mind distressed.
Meanwhile, as the kings were being slain by <s>Bhīṣma</s>'s arrows,
there arose a terrible crush, a battle-festival for death.
As the heroic sons of <s>Draupadī</s> fought with the <s>Kaurava</s>s,
a dreadful battle went on, destroying elephants, horses, and chariots.
Then the son of <s>Śantanu</s> ordered the withdrawal of the armies,
when the sun, wrapped in the dust of kings, had gone to setting, red as blood.
On the next day, when <s>Bhīṣma</s> himself had arranged the maṇḍala formation,
<s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s> formed the hard-to-break vajra formation.
Then, when the terrible battle between <s>Bhīṣma</s> and <s>Pārtha</s> had begun,
<s>Virāṭa</s> rushed upon <s>Droṇa</s>, the most weighty of all bowmen.
<s>Droṇa</s>, covering him with a shower of arrows as he showered arrows in return,
roared with a bow-twang like thunder and struck down his chariot.

children.text: sa hatāśvaṃ samutsṛjya rathaṃ putrasya saṃbhramāt
children.translated_text: Abandoning that chariot whose horses had been killed, in alarm
he mounted the chariot of his son <s>Śaṅkha</s>, whose troops had been slain and who had taken up his bow.
Then <s>Droṇa</s>, seeing father and son standing in one chariot,
sent at <s>Śaṅkha</s> a terrible arrow like the staff of death.
With his heart pierced by it, he fell, sprinkled with blood,
like a blossoming <s>kiṃśuka</s> tree torn from a mountain by the wind.
Then, after <s>Droṇa</s> had assailed <s>Śikhaṇḍin</s>, who was raining shafts, with arrows,
and when <s>Śikhaṇḍin</s>, his horses killed, had climbed onto <s>Sātyaki</s>'s chariot,
<s>Alambusa</s>, the lord of rākṣasas, cruel in deed, rushed at him.
As that lord of rākṣasas fought by illusion and roared,
<s>Sātyaki</s>, in anger, turned him back with the fierce <s>Raudra</s> weapon.
When he had been conquered by the <s>Śaineya</s>, <s>Irāvān</s>, son of <s>Arjuna</s>,
whose valor equaled that of <s>Jambhāri</s>, advanced against <s>Vinda</s> and <s>Anuvinda</s>.
Then, as <s>Ghaṭotkaca</s> came on, terrifying like <s>Kṛtānta</s>,
<s>Bhagadatta</s>, foremost of kings, checked him with a lordly elephant.
Having struck back the heroic <s>Haiḍamba</s>, he then attacked the army of the <s>Pāṇḍava</s>s
and proudly churned it up, as a great elephant churns a lotus pond.

children.text: mādrīsutau tataḥ śalyaṃ vidhāya virathaṃ śaraiḥ
children.translated_text: Then the two sons of <s>Mādrī</s>, making <s>Śalya</s> chariotless with arrows,
turned him away in battle while the circle of kings looked on.

children.text: svayaṃ yudhiṣṭhiro rājā nṛpaṃ jitvā śrutāyudham
children.translated_text: King <s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s> himself, after defeating King <s>Śrutāyudha</s>,
plunged into the <s>Kaurava</s> army and turned it back with arrows.
When <s>Gautama</s>, teacher of bowmen, had been defeated by <s>Cekitāna</s>,
<s>Bhīṣma</s> made a slaughter of kings, and elsewhere <s>Arjuna</s> did the same.
Seeing <s>Śikhaṇḍin</s>, at <s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s>'s command, rushing upon <s>Bhīṣma</s>,
the king of the <s>Madra</s>s checked him with divine weapons.
As the unretreating rulers were being slain by <s>Bhīṣma</s>,
and the <s>Trigarta</s>s by <s>Pārtha</s>, the sun went down.
When the world was covered with darkness and the battle was flooded with blood as with liquor,
the kings went to their camps like heedless <s>vetāla</s>s.
The next morning, when <s>Bhīṣma</s> had again arranged the ocean formation,
the son of <s>Drupada</s> formed the great <s>śṛṅgāṭaka</s> battle array.
When the armies were being split open by arrows loosed from <s>Bhīṣma</s>'s bow,
<s>Vṛkodara</s> alone faced him in anger.
Quickly killing the charioteer of the son of <s>Śantanu</s> with arrows,
he also made <s>Droṇa</s>'s chariot have its banner wildly shaken.
Then <s>Bhīma</s>, having found his mark, killed seven younger brothers of <s>Duryodhana</s>,
who were raging with pride, as a lion kills elephants.
After slaying those men, <s>Bahvāśin</s>, <s>Kuṇḍadhāra</s>, <s>Viśālākṣa</s>, <s>Sudurjaya</s>,

children.text: mahodaraṃ maṇḍitakaṃ sunābhaṃ ca nihatya tān ||
children.translated_text: <s>Mahodara</s>, <s>Maṇḍitaka</s>, and <s>Sunābha</s>,
he routed the <s>Kaurava</s> army and roared, making the quarters resound,
like <s>Rudra</s> arisen for the destruction of all the worlds.
Then the valiant <s>Irāvān</s> entered the <s>Kuru</s> host.
<s>Ulūpī</s>, the nāga maiden, had borne him as the first-born to <s>Phalguna</s>.
Because <s>Arjuna</s> had formerly said to him in the city of the gods, "You yourself must aid me in battle,"
he came to that battlefield.
Borne by steeds of the underworld with trappings of jewels and gold,
he made the field with his arrows like another serpent-world.
Going against the vast <s>Gāndhāra</s> forces, warriors on horses,
he slew the seven sons of <s>Śakuni</s>, men of mighty valor.
Then, ordered by <s>Duryodhana</s>, the illusion-working lord of rākṣasas,
<s>Alambusa</s>, fierce in battle, advanced against <s>Irāvān</s>.
Then <s>Irāvān</s>, with his sword, at once cut off the rākṣasa's

children.text: sa niṣaṅgaṃ dhanurdīptaṃ nanāda balināṃ varaḥ ||
children.translated_text: quiver and blazing bow, and the best of the strong roared.

children.text: tato māyāṃ samāśritya mahatīṃ mohanīṃ nṛṇām
children.translated_text: Then, resorting to a great illusion that bewildered men,
those two of terrible valor entered the sky and fought.
As the rākṣasa was being struck by <s>Irāvān</s>'s own floods of weapons,
a terrible cry arose, frightening all living beings.
Then serpents, born of serpent-women, made an alliance with him,
the foremost of hooded snakes spreading their hoods and spitting sharp poison.
Then the rākṣasa, greatly enraged, assumed the form of <s>Garuḍa</s>;
after devouring all the serpents, he took back his own terrible body.
Then, while <s>Irāvān</s> was bewildered by illusion, the enemy rākṣasa with his sword
took from his body his head with its earrings.
When the son of <s>Dhanaṃjaya</s> was slain, <s>Haiḍamba</s>, overwhelmed with anger,
roared so that the earth shook together with its mountain ranges.
Seeing him rushing on, King <s>Duryodhana</s> himself
fought that great master of illusion together with all his own forces.
<s>Vidyujjihva</s>, <s>Vegavant</s>, <s>Mahāraudra</s>, and <s>Pramāthin</s>,
terrible night-roaming followers of <s>Haiḍimba</s>, he slew.
Then a spear launched by <s>Ghaṭotkaca</s> at the lord of the <s>Kuru</s>s
was intercepted in front by the lord of the <s>Vaṅga</s>s with a great elephant.
When that elephant had fallen and <s>Suyodhana</s> had been saved,
the flesh-eater made a slaughter of the armies of men.
Then <s>Bhagadatta</s>, after routing the army of the <s>Pāṇḍava</s>s,
with the elephant <s>Supratīka</s> he made <s>Ghaṭotkaca</s> fight.
Hearing that his son had been killed, the enraged son of <s>Śatamanyu</s>,
made the earth impassable with the heads of kings.
<s>Bhīma</s> too, scorched by anger when his brother's son had fallen,
sent the heroic younger brothers of <s>Suyodhana</s> to the abode of <s>Yama</s>.
<s>Anādhṛṣṭi</s>, <s>Kuṇḍalin</s>, <s>Kuṇḍabhedin</s>, and <s>Sulocana</s>,
<s>Virāṭa</s>, <s>Dīrghabāhu</s>, <s>Subāhu</s>, and <s>Kanakadhvaja</s> also:
having slain these men, he made the <s>Kaurava</s> army crowded with hundreds of headless trunks,
a delight to frenzied vetālas, at the close of day.
Then, when bows and armor had slipped away, and chariots and elephants were broken,
the great chariot-warriors made the armies withdraw from the battle.
Then at night king <s>Suyodhana</s>, together with his followers,
summoned <s>Karṇa</s> and considered the defeat of the sons of <s>Pṛthā</s>.
The son of <s>Vikartana</s> said to him, "Friend, let my advice be carried out.
Make the son of <s>Gaṅgā</s> lay down his weapons; I shall conquer the <s>Pāṇḍavas</s>.
This old man is inactive, and he is partial to <s>Dhanaṃjaya</s>;
you have placed an excessive burden on him, entirely without reflection."
Hearing these words spoken by <s>Karṇa</s>, as though impelled by hundreds of acts through joy,
he rose and went with his brothers to <s>Bhīṣma</s>'s camp.
The spaces of the quarters were made tawny by the rays of thousands of jeweled lamps;
at night it shone like a mountain with its forests of blazing herbs.
The lamps before him, surpassed by the radiance of jeweled earrings, armlets, and crowns,
seemed dull and ashamed.
Looking with a sidelong glance at the bowing kings,
who were announced by name and noble valor by circles of staff-bearing attendants,
he shone, with a snow-bright necklace swaying as he walked,
like <s>Manmatha</s> adorned with a net of billows of nectar.
The illustrious king reached the bright camp of the son of <s>Śantanu</s>,
and, seeing him lying on a jeweled couch, bowed to him.
Honored by him as king and having taken a seat,
<s>Duryodhana</s>, after reflecting for a moment, addressed his grandfather:
"This arm of yours, fond of the bow and conqueror of the son of <s>Bhṛgu</s>,
is, in my opinion, sufficient for conquering the three worlds.
If the <s>Pāṇḍavas</s> are to be protected by you out of compassion or gentleness,
then permit battle-hardened <s>Karṇa</s> to fight."
Thus addressed by the <s>Kuru</s> king, as if struck in a vital spot,
he said, "You will see in the morning," and, sighing, looked at the ground.
The <s>Kaurava</s> too took leave of him and went to his own camp,
mottling the quarters with ornaments flashing in the light of lamps.
Then at dawn, when <s>Bhīṣma</s>, together with <s>Droṇa</s>, <s>Drauṇi</s>, and the others,
had arranged the all-auspicious <s>vyūha</s> (battle formation), standing at the head of the array,
while the sons of <s>Pāṇḍu</s> roared in their armies and counter-formations,
the heroic <s>Abhimanyu</s> tore apart the front of the <s>Kuru</s> army.
Like the risen summer sun, hard to behold because of hundreds of arrow-rays,

children.text: na sehire taṃ bhūpālā māninaḥ saṃhatā api ||
children.translated_text: the proud kings could not endure him, even though they were gathered together.
Then, urged on by <s>Duryodhana</s>, <s>Alambusa</s>, lord of rākṣasas,
rushed against him, bearing an illusion that could bewilder the three worlds.
At his great roar, which seemed to announce the dissolution of the world,
many warriors suddenly fell, their lives gone.

children.text: draupadeyaiḥ puraḥ prāptaiḥ sa vidhāya raṇaṃ kṣaṇam
children.translated_text: After fighting for a moment with the sons of <s>Draupadī</s>, who had come before him,
<s>Abhimanyu</s> then made the rākṣasa's body all one surface with arrows.
Then the son of <s>Subhadrā</s>, with the fiery power of the solar weapon,
cut through the dark illusion fashioned by that rākṣasa, after it had been pierced by arrows.
Then in battle, <s>Drauṇi</s> and the others, engaged with those led by <s>Sātyaki</s>,
made the sky crowded with the fires of divine weapons.
<s>Arjuna</s>, approaching <s>Droṇa</s>, who was unbearable with his mass of great weapons,
created a bewildering agitation of the worlds with the <s>Vāyavya</s> weapon.
And when the fire had been extinguished by <s>Drauṇi</s>, who had launched the mountain weapon,
<s>Dhanaṃjaya</s> filled the <s>Kuru</s> army with nets of arrows.
When the elephant ranks had been split by the terrible blows of <s>Bhīma</s>'s fearsome mace,
a river of blood flowed, garlanded with foam made of banners.
While that dreadful, chaotic battle was going on,
severed heads danced to rhythms beaten by vetālas.
<s>Bhīṣma</s>, unbearable with broad flames of arrows, with brave warriors as his fuel,
blazed like a fire consecrated by the mantra of his bowstring's twang.
The arrows swiftly driven by his arms entered the kings,
like birds at evening entering great trees full of dense shade.

children.text: khadyotā iva vṛkṣeṣu śalabhā iva śāliṣu
children.translated_text: Like fireflies among trees, like locusts among rice-plants,
<s>Bhīṣma</s>'s arrows fell upon the lords of men like swans upon lakes.
With the severed yak-tail fans and turbans of kings strewn over them,
<s>Bhīṣma</s> made the quarters in battle bright with his own fame.
Spreading the earth with the heads of kings, gleaming as if with horripilation,
he made them seem like pleasure lotus-ponds for the goddess of battle.
The sparks of fire born from the scraping of helmets against arrows

children.text: rājñāṃ hatānāṃ bhīṣmeṇa jīvā iva nabhaścarāḥ ||
children.translated_text: seemed like the sky-faring souls of kings slain by <s>Bhīṣma</s>.
With his dense net of arrows, swallowing the world on every side,
he made all the armies imagine an untimely night.
When the <s>Pāṇḍava</s> force had been split apart, its armor, chariots, and standards cut down,
when the elephant divisions were broken and only remnants of kings remained,
When they had gone, shamelessly casting away their bows, <s>Keśava</s>
said to <s>Arjuna</s>, "Kill <s>Bhīṣma</s>, true to his pledge, in battle."
Then <s>Dhanaṃjaya</s>, sighing, his lotus face downcast,
again and again condemning the <s>kṣattradharma</s> (warrior's duty), ran toward his grandfather.
Seeing the bearer of the <s>Gāṇḍīva</s> with bow raised, raining arrows,
when the army had quickly turned back, the warriors fought again.
Seeing <s>Phalguṇa</s> covered by arrows fallen from <s>Bhīṣma</s>'s bow,
the enemy of <s>Kaṃsa</s>, leaving the chariot, rushed at him with his arms as weapons.
Seeing <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> himself, enraged, rushing toward him, <s>Bhīṣma</s>
spoke, thinking himself blessed, his form adorned with horripilation:
"I am foremost among the fortunate, O blessed lord, best of the fulfilled,

children.text: yasya tvaṃ jagatāṃ nātho vadhāya svayamudyataḥ ||
children.translated_text: for you, lord of the worlds, have yourself risen up to kill me."
When the son of <s>Gaṅgā</s> had spoken thus, <s>Dhanaṃjaya</s> quickly from the chariot
descended and then brought <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> back again to the chariot.
Then, when the <s>Kuru</s> forest was strewn with showers of <s>Arjuna</s>'s arrows,
the son of <s>Śantanu</s> again made a destruction of kings.
In that terrible confusion, when the circle of excellent warriors was broken,
at day's end the sons of <s>Pāṇḍu</s> made a withdrawal.
Then at night, in a lonely place, <s>Dharmarāja</s>, distressed,

children.text: jagāda rājakaṃ dṛṣṭvā bhinnaṃ bhīṣmeṇa duḥkhitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: spoke to <s>Janārdana</s>, seeing the royal force shattered by <s>Bhīṣma</s>:
"Look, <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>: by the awakened submarine fire that is the son of <s>Gaṅgā</s>,
my boundless ocean of an army has been reduced to a small remnant.
Before <s>Bhīṣma</s>, whose bow is drawn into a circle and whose brilliance is that of hundreds of suns,
even <s>Akhaṇḍala</s> would truly become an object of humiliation.

children.text: alaṃ rājyena me tāvaditi vādini dharmaje
children.translated_text: Enough, then, of kingship for me." When the son of <s>Dharma</s> spoke thus,
<s>Śauri</s> said, "I myself shall fight the son of <s>Śantanu</s>.
Your business is not something I may leave undone; I have now cast aside my pledge.
In battle I shall strike down <s>Bhīṣma</s> while the rulers of the earth look on."
Hearing these words of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, the eldest <s>Pāṇḍava</s> said:
"I would not, out of desire, make you a speaker of falsehood, O <s>Acyuta</s>.
Going from here, I shall ask <s>Bhīṣma</s> on earth the means of victory,
for earlier, out of affection, he joined me to his blessing."

children.text: iti niścitya kṛṣṇena bhrātṛbhiśca sahāśu kṛt
children.translated_text: Having resolved this, with <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> and his brothers, quickly,
<s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s>, moving secretly, went to <s>Bhīṣma</s>'s camp.
He, with his younger brothers and friend, bowed to the grandfather, that mass of valor,
and asked the means of victory; and he, when questioned, said to him:

children.text: na taṃ paśyāmi lokeṣu vīro māṃ vijayeta yaḥ
children.translated_text: "I do not see in the worlds that hero who could conquer me,

children.text: jayalābhe ca yuṣmākaṃ mayi jīvati kā kathā ||
children.translated_text: and while I live, what talk can there be of your obtaining victory?

children.text: na viśastrena saṃtraste na strīpūrve mameṣavaḥ
children.translated_text: My arrows do not fall upon one without weapons, one terrified, or one who was formerly a woman;
therefore have me killed by <s>Śikhaṇḍin</s>, who is a <s>klība</s> (impotent one)."
When <s>Devavrata</s> had spoken thus, the king, his face bent down with shame,

children.text: akāma iva duḥkhena yayau svaśibiraṃ nṛpaḥ ||
children.translated_text: went to his own camp in grief, as if unwilling.
Then in the morning, when the armies had been arrayed and the excellent warriors faced one another,
the heroes headed by <s>Śikhaṇḍin</s> charged the enemy army.
Then, when the circle of kings was shaken by rows of <s>Bhīṣma</s>'s arrows,
<s>Śikhaṇḍin</s>, brandishing his bow and fierce with anger, addressed him:
The son of <s>Śantanu</s> said to him, "Strike as you please, O <s>Pārṣata</s>;
<s>Bhīṣma</s>'s shafts do not fall upon a person who was formerly a woman."
Approaching him as he spoke thus, with his bow bent into a circle,
<s>Śikhaṇḍin</s>, sighing in anger, said to the son of the river:
"I know you as the conqueror even of <s>Bhārgava</s>, possessing great power;

children.text: yudhi yudhyasva vā mā vā na me jīvangamiṣyasi ||
children.translated_text: fight in battle or do not fight, you shall not go away alive from me."
Having said this, the <s>Pārṣata</s> filled him with a net of arrows,
advancing while guarded from behind by the bearer of the <s>Gāṇḍīva</s>.

children.text: bhīṣmo 'pi tam anādṛtya viddhvā kṛṣṇārjunau śaraiḥ
children.translated_text: But <s>Bhīṣma</s>, disregarding him and piercing <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> and <s>Arjuna</s> with arrows,
entered the <s>Pāṇḍava</s> army like a fire in a forest of royal bamboos.
Then, with heroes headed by <s>Dhṛṣṭadyumna</s> and the impetuous <s>Kauravas</s>,
there arose a dreadful assault, with the faces of the quarters covered by dust.
Then the heroes beginning with <s>Droṇi</s>, at <s>Droṇa</s>'s command,
protecting <s>Bhīṣma</s> in battle, fought <s>Dhanaṃjaya</s>.
Then the son of <s>Śantanu</s>, with arrows heavy as thunderbolts,
churned up the splendor variegated by rays from the kings' crest-jewels;
and, making slaughter in battle as if it were the sport of Time,
troubled in mind, he spoke to <s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s> even from afar:

children.text: vadhāya kuru kaunteya yatnaṃ me nṛpatikṣayāt
children.translated_text: "Make an effort, O son of <s>Kuntī</s>, for my death, because of this destruction of kings.
I am deeply despondent, my son, because of this terrible deed."
When the son of <s>Gaṅgā</s> had spoken thus and slackened his bow,
the <s>Sṛñjayas</s>, together with the <s>Pāñcālas</s> and <s>Somakas</s>, charged at once.
Then the heroes of the <s>Kuru</s> army, blocking the great chariot-warriors of the <s>Pāṇḍavas</s>,
fought duels in order to protect <s>Bhīṣma</s>.
Then, even by the arrows of the son of <s>Gaṅgā</s>, though released without effort,
there proceeded a very terrible destruction of kings' lives.
At <s>Phalguṇa</s>'s urging, <s>Śikhaṇḍin</s>, his bow drawn in a circle to his ear,
rushed at him with the prowess of <s>Khaṇḍaparaśu</s>.
Then, seeing the army driven on by <s>Duryodhana</s> himself,
while that destruction of his own warriors was going on, the grandfather
launched a terrible divine weapon and rushed against <s>Dhanaṃjaya</s>,
and then, when <s>Śikhaṇḍin</s> had come before <s>Arjuna</s> and stood in front...

children.text: vimānā iva gāṅgeyo mahāstraṃ saṃjahāra tat
children.translated_text: Then <s>Gāṅgeya</s> withdrew that great weapon, like a celestial chariot,
while the kings fought on, longing for the world of <s>Brahmā</s>.
And as tens of thousands of heroes fell beneath <s>Bhīṣma</s>'s arrows,
the <s>Vasus</s> approached him, as he was tearing apart the enemy army, and said:
"<s>Bhīṣma</s>, this is the time for laying down arms, the time we desire for you."
Then, when his effort slackened, the three worlds became serene.
All the warriors, led by <s>Arjuna</s>, filled him with arrows;
and as his shafts were swiftly cut down by <s>Kirīṭin</s>,
<s>Śikhaṇḍī</s> sent against him a row of arrows with golden feathers.

children.text: śaikhaṇḍīṃ śaramālāṃ tāṃ śairīṣīm iva peśalām ||
children.translated_text: <s>Bhīṣma</s> laughing received that garland of <s>Śikhaṇḍī</s>'s arrows,
delicate like a line of śirīṣa blossoms, and held his bow still for a moment.
Then the chariot-guards of <s>Bhīṣma</s>, assigned by <s>Duryodhana</s>,
<s>Phalguṇa</s> bewildered with a net of arrows and covered them over.
As he was being pierced by close-packed arrows released from <s>Gāṇḍīva</s>,
<s>Bhīṣma</s> said with a smile to <s>Duḥśāsana</s>, who stood at his side:
"These are not the arrows of <s>Śikhaṇḍin</s>, which split masses of stone;

children.text: viśanti mama marmāṇi bilaṃ viṣadharā iva
children.translated_text: they enter my vital points like venomous snakes entering a hole.
These, hard as the thunderbolt and able to cut through the <s>Nivātakavacas</s>,
are terrible, body-piercing arrows, proven in the battle with the <s>Kirātas</s>."
Having spoken thus, the mighty one hurled a spear at the son of <s>Pāṇḍu</s>.
And the son of <s>Śakra</s> quickly split it into three with arrows.
Then, when all his weapons had been cut down by the wielder of <s>Gāṇḍīva</s>,
in a moment <s>Bhīṣma</s> became hard to see, covered with arrows without gaps.
While the heroes fought in confusion, as if possessed by spirits,
in that dreadful tumult, when the two armies could no longer be distinguished,
in the afternoon <s>Bhīṣma</s>, like another thousand-rayed sun, fell from his chariot,
that treasure-house of radiance, his body not touching the ground because of the arrows.
When that hero, the banner of all bowmen, had fallen,
the hearts even of the great heroes trembled.
Then, when the battle had ceased and the cry of lamentation touched the sky,
the grandsire, his self undiminished, assumed his own divine condition.
As the world trembled, a bodiless voice spoke:
"<s>Bhīṣma</s>, rich in yoga, wait for the season of the sun's northern course.
All-knowing one, hold your life-breaths in your heart, for your death is at your own will."
Hearing this, <s>Suravrata</s> entered the supreme yoga.
Then sages, released by the river of the gods in the form of swans,
came to him and told <s>Bhīṣma</s> that very same matter.

children.text: sthito 'smīti ca gāṅgeyo nigadya yaśasāṃ nidhiḥ ||
children.translated_text: "I remain," said <s>Gāṅgeya</s>, treasure-house of fame,
and, lying on the bed of arrows, he comforted all the frightened <s>Kurus</s>.
Then, when the <s>Kauravas</s> and <s>Pāṇḍavas</s> had come again and bowed down,
the bull of the <s>Kurus</s>, honoring them, spoke with eyes full of tears:
"Let support be arranged for my head, which is hanging down."
Hearing this, when cushions had been brought by the kings,

children.text: jagrāha śāsanāttasya tribhiḥ pārthaḥ śaraiḥ śiraḥ ||
children.translated_text: at his command <s>Pārtha</s> supported his head with three arrows.
<s>Bhīṣma</s>, pleased with that deed, then praised <s>Dhanaṃjaya</s>.
And he said to the <s>Kaurava</s>, "Make peace with the <s>Pāṇḍavas</s>."
Then, when the night had passed and the kings were seated,
<s>Bhīṣma</s>, attended by hosts of sages, asked for water.
When the kings had brought clear water in jars bright with jewels and gold,
<s>Arjuna</s> discharged the cloud-weapon.
Refreshed by the water that arose from it, <s>Gāṅgeya</s>
with delighted heart respectfully honored him as an incarnation of <s>Nara</s>.
When the great chariot-warriors had gone after taking leave of the son of the river,
<s>Karṇa</s>, worshiping him with joined hands, sought to win his favor.
The grandsire, serene in spirit and free of anger, said to him:
"Choose peace toward the sons of <s>Pṛthā</s>; those heroes are your brothers.
Hearing this, <s>Vaikartana</s>, his face bowed, said:
"I know everything, lord; yet this must inevitably be.
But for <s>Duryodhana</s>'s sake, as his friend and guardian of his honor,
permit me, father, as I set out for battle."
Speaking thus, he was permitted by <s>Bhīṣma</s>, and
he went to the army of the <s>Kuru</s> princes in a chariot thundering like a cloud.
Then for the bulls of the <s>Kurus</s>, eager for the king of <s>Aṅga</s>, their pride and regard broken by their vow to humble the enemy,
the army, fitted with its lord as they hastened, became like forests shaken by rows of driving winds.
Having bowed to <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> and to <s>Nara</s>, the best of men,
and to the goddess <s>Sarasvatī</s> and <s>Vyāsa</s>, then one should utter <s>Jaya</s>.
Hearing that <s>Suravrata</s> had been felled, <s>Dhṛtarāṣṭra</s>, deeply afflicted,
again and again mourned that foe-subduer, that mass of glory.
Then <s>Saṃjaya</s>, having come back after seeing the renewed battle,
when asked by the son of <s>Vicitravīrya</s>, described the slaughter of heroes.
Then, when <s>Bhīṣma</s> had been felled, O king, the <s>Kurus</s> were deeply distressed;

children.text: abdhau bhagne pravahaṇe vaṇijaḥ patitā iva ||
children.translated_text: they were like merchants fallen into the sea when their ship has broken apart.
They saw <s>Karṇa</s>, who had come, as the longed-for refuge in battle,
like men sold in foreign lands seeing an affectionate kinsman in distress.
Then <s>Duryodhana</s>, an ocean of firmness, restrained his grief,
and, with <s>Karṇa</s>'s consent, made <s>Droṇa</s> commander of the armies.
Consecrated by him according to rule, the preceptor of all bowmen,
that powerful hero shone like another <s>Mahāsena</s>.
For the aged one, his umbrella, bright with his own fame, shone
like the splendid disk of the moon rising from the ocean of milk.
Wearing golden armor, he blazed with rays and shone
as if attended by divine weapons that had arrived at the time for action.
Leader of all warriors, equal in abundant splendor,
he was as though <s>Dhanurveda</s> embodied, the final scripture of destruction.
He shone with his golden chariot, red horses, and banner,
like the sun upon <s>Meru</s>, attended by streams of twilight.
On his chariot his golden water-pot glittered,
like his martial heat drawn back and condensed into glory.
Grey up to his ears, dark in hue, the foremost bearer of the bow among all bowmen,

children.text: dadau varaṃ śriyā juṣṭaḥ sa rājñā svayamarthitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and attended by fortune, he granted the boon that the king himself requested.
I shall take King <s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s> alive in battle
and deliver him, once <s>Arjuna</s> is slain, while all rulers look on.
Accepting this word of his guru, the king stood with folded hands,
and, having it proclaimed through his own armies, made a festival of trumpet-sound.
But the son of <s>Dharma</s>, learning of this, together with the wielder of the <s>Gāṇḍīva</s>,
arrayed the <s>krauñca-vyūha</s>, armed himself, and set out to fight.
When <s>Droṇa</s> had formed the tightly packed <s>śakaṭa-vyūha</s>,
a great battle began, cutting down the bodies of heroes.
Then upon the armies of the <s>Sṛñjaya</s>s, <s>Pāñcāla</s>s, and <s>Matsya</s>s fell
unbearable arrows marked with <s>Droṇa</s>'s name, carrying bodies away.
As the armies were being split apart, and elephants and horses were falling,
even the chariots were swept away by the torrents of waves of blood.
The enraged heroes, led by <s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s>, rushed angrily against <s>Droṇa</s>,
but <s>Drauṇi</s>, <s>Karṇa</s>, <s>Kṛpa</s>, and the others furiously held them back.
Then <s>Abhimanyu</s>, dragging <s>Paurava</s> from his chariot by the hair,
struck him down with his sword while all the bowmen looked on.
In anger at that, the hero rendered <s>Jayadratha</s>, who had come at him sword in hand,

children.text: śalyaṃ ca virathaṃ vīro vidadhe balināṃ varam ||
children.translated_text: and <s>Śalya</s>, the best of the strong, bereft of their chariots.
Then <s>Śalya</s>, mace in hand, ran on foot against <s>Saubhadra</s>,
and <s>Bhīma</s> checked him with his own mace, the slayer of heroic hosts.
Between those two there arose a terrible mace-battle, bewildering men,
filled with sparks of fire scattered by their mutual blows.
Moving in circles like two intoxicated elephants,
they rushed eight steps forward and struck one another with their maces.
Seeing both of them fallen, their minds reeling in stupor born of heavy blows,

children.text: tau dṛṣṭvā patitau vīrāḥ saṃnipetuḥ prahāriṇaḥ ||
children.translated_text: the attacking heroes rushed together.
When the lord of the <s>Madra</s>s had quickly been carried off by <s>Kṛtavarman</s> on his chariot,
<s>Bhīmasena</s>, rallying himself, tore open the <s>Kuru</s> army.
Then the <s>Pāṇḍava</s>s saw the sons of <s>Draupadī</s> covered with the arrows
of <s>Dṛṣasena</s>, son of <s>Karṇa</s>, and rushed against him.
Then <s>Droṇa</s> himself, on his golden chariot, entered the <s>Pāñcāla</s> force
and with his arrows scattered it into a thousand fragments.
Piercing great chariot-warriors headed by <s>Śikhaṇḍin</s> and <s>Sātyaki</s>,
he looked for <s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s>, bringing destruction upon the kings.
<s>Yugaṃdhara</s>, <s>Vyāghradatta</s>, and King <s>Siṃhasena</s>
he sent to the house of death with arrows terrible as thunderbolts.
'Stand! I am standing. Fight! You are slain!' again and again,
such was the battle of the rulers fighting before <s>Droṇa</s>.
Hearing the clamor of his own troops as they fought with <s>Droṇa</s>,
the white-horsed one, <s>Arjuna</s>, quickly came to that place.
That hero, cutting down the <s>Kuru</s> army with a net of weapons,
made it a river of blood whose whirlpools carried off elephants.
Then, oppressed by <s>Pārtha</s>'s arrows, the foremost <s>Kuru</s>s
ordered the withdrawal of the armies when the hot-rayed sun had set.
At night, when all the kings had settled in their camps,
the teacher, as if ashamed, spoke to <s>Duryodhana</s>.
I told you plainly, O king, that I would seize <s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s>
when he was separated from the left-handed archer; for <s>Dhanaṃjaya</s> is hard to conquer.
As the teacher spoke thus in embarrassment before the king's assembly,
the king of the <s>Trigarta</s>s, who had made enmity with the diademed one, spoke.
We, with the companies of <s>Saṃśaptaka</s>s, with <s>Mālava</s>s and <s>Tuṇḍila</s>s too,
and with striking heroes from the <s>Madraka</s>s, <s>Kāmboja</s>s, and <s>Lalita</s>s,
with thirty thousand chariots, will summon <s>Pārtha</s> and take our stand apart;
we shall fight him, and by our good deeds we swear this as truth.
When this had been said, the <s>Trigarta</s>s made their oath with fire as witness,
and at dawn the heroic kings, headed by <s>Suśarman</s>, set out.
The vault of the sky was swallowed by dust raised by their horses and asses,
and with roars announcing dissolution they issued their challenge to <s>Phalguna</s>.
Seeing them stationed on level ground in a half-moon formation,
<s>Pārtha</s>, thus summoned, addressed <s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s>.
Let the noble one permit me to go to the slaughter of the <s>Trigarta</s>s;
these men, full of eagerness for battle, desire to fight me.

children.text: ayaṃ te satyajidvīraḥ pāñcālyaḥ pravaro rathaḥ
children.translated_text: Here is your brave <s>Satyajit</s>, a <s>Pāñcāla</s> and a foremost chariot-warrior;
when <s>Droṇa</s> advances, he will protect you, with valor equal to <s>Śakra</s>'s.
Having said this, the monkey-bannered one, whose fierce <s>Gāṇḍīva</s>-twang rang like bells through the edges of the quarters,
went against them, furious like a cloud of the end-time deluge.
They too, seeing the <s>Pāṇḍava</s> coming toward them, were filled with delight.
with their arrows they quickly made him look like a blossoming <s>śāla</s> tree.
Then <s>Dhanaṃjaya</s> blew his conch, like the foam of the ocean of valor, the loud laugh of battle's splendor,
and like the sprout of the tree of his own fame.
By its great sound, which produced fear, that army
became one whose elephants had turned back and whose horses stood motionless.
Then with a net of arrows that carried off the fish of life,
<s>Pārtha</s> surrounded the <s>Trigarta</s> army on every side.
Then, with the gapless arrows released by the bands of <s>saṃśaptaka</s>s,
when the expanse of the world was covered, an untimely night arose.
Then the son of the wielder of the thunderbolt deployed the great <s>Tvāṣṭra</s> weapon,
by which they, alarmed, saw thousands of <s>Arjuna</s>s.
With a broad-headed arrow drawn to the ear he cut from the body of mighty <s>Sudhanvan</s>
the head encircled by the flashing radiance of its crown.
Shaking away with the lovely wind-weapon the shower of weapons sent by him,
he made the earth invisible with heaps of those heads.
With parasols, banners, and chariots cut down, with arms and warriors' faces falling,
<s>Pārtha</s> made a terrible battle, a slaughter of the <s>Trigarta</s>s.
At this moment, when <s>Droṇa</s> had formed the <s>Vainateya</s> array,
the sons of <s>Pāṇḍu</s> advanced with a half-formed battle array.

children.text: tataḥ pravṛtte saṃgrāme kṣaye caiva mahībhujām
children.translated_text: Then, when battle had begun and the destruction of kings as well,
<s>Dhṛṣṭadyumna</s> and the others fought against those headed by <s>Droṇa</s>.

children.text: rajobhiḥ pihite vyomni dikṣu ruddhāsu sāyakaiḥ
children.translated_text: When the sky was covered by dust and the directions were blocked by arrows,
a terrible battle took place, without distinction and without bounds.
Then, when <s>Droṇa</s> rushed forward, wishing to seize the <s>Dharmarāja</s>,
a terrible tumultuous cry of the armies arose for a moment.
To ward off the hero, blazing like the fire at the end of time, the foremost of all bowmen,
<s>Satyajit</s>, whose valor was true, came forward.

children.text: yudhyamānaṃ tato hatvā vṛkaṃ rājasutaṃ guruḥ
children.translated_text: Then the guru slew the fighting prince <s>Vṛka</s>,
and with arrows he made <s>Satyajit</s> like the sun with rays scattered about.
Then for a moment <s>Satyajit</s>, with arrows marked with golden names,
brightly filled <s>Droṇa</s> as fireflies fill a tree.
Then the preceptor, with a broad-headed arrow, took from the body of valorous <s>Satyajit</s>
his head, whose earrings danced in a fierce <s>tāṇḍava</s>.
When <s>Satyajit</s>, foremost of all bowmen, had been struck down,
and the son of <s>Dharma</s> had fled, the army broke apart.
After carrying off <s>Śatānīka</s>, the attacking younger brother of <s>Virāṭa</s>,
and the kings <s>Dṛḍhasena</s>, <s>Kṣatradeva</s>, and <s>Vasudāna</s>,
while slaying the <s>Rukmaratha</s>s, <s>Cedi</s>s, <s>Matsya</s>s, <s>Pāñcāla</s>s, and <s>Sṛñjaya</s>s,
he made, with eddies of blood, a stream for the garden of <s>Kṛtānta</s>.
When the <s>Pāṇḍava</s> force had fled, oppressed by <s>Droṇa</s>'s arrows,
those headed by <s>Karṇa</s> and <s>Duryodhana</s> honored the son of <s>Bharadvāja</s>.
When the army had been turned back again by strong-armed <s>Bhīma</s>,
the assembled rulers of the earth rushed in anger upon <s>Droṇa</s>.
<s>Bhīma</s> came with horses the color of deer, and <s>Sātyaki</s> with crystal-bright horses;
and the army-chief <s>Dhṛṣṭadyumna</s> came with horses bright as doves.
<s>Nakula</s> and <s>Sahadeva</s> came with horses bright as parrots and partridges,
<s>Abhimanyu</s> with tawny ones, and the <s>Pāṇḍya</s>s with horses bright as snow,
while King <s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s> himself came with horses shining like ivory and having black tails.
But others, with varied colors and with variegated armor, garments, and banners,
surrounded <s>Droṇa</s> in battle and made the world consist of arrows.
The king born from <s>Dharma</s> had a banner with <s>Nanda</s> and <s>Upananda</s>, sounding like drums,
fashioned by a divine mechanism, and it shone brightly.
Golden-bright images of <s>Dharma</s>, <s>Anila</s>, <s>Indra</s>, and the <s>Aśvin</s>s, belonging to the sons of <s>Draupadī</s>,
shone as they fought in the tumult.
Seeing <s>Droṇa</s> surrounded by kings with cruel intent,
<s>Duryodhana</s> and the other heroes charged at the warriors headed by <s>Bhīma</s>.
When those led by <s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s> were engaged in duels with those headed by <s>Śalya</s>,
in the ranks gleaming with the festivity of battle,

children.text: kṛtabāhau subāhau ca hate vīre yuyutsunā
children.translated_text: after the heroes <s>Kṛtabāhu</s> and <s>Subāhu</s> had been slain by <s>Yuyutsu</s>,
and after the king of <s>Vaṅga</s>, together with his elephant, had been felled by <s>Bhīmasena</s>,
when the <s>Kaurava</s> force had fled and its proud warriors had been killed,
and the worlds were lightless with masses of dust-darkness,
<s>Supratīka</s>, urged on by <s>Bhagadatta</s>, resembling a cloud of dissolution,
and wild with rut, plunged into the army of the sons of <s>Pāṇḍu</s>.
His body had as its measure the mass of <s>Airāvata</s>, who stands in the house of <s>Jambhāri</s>
as an ally in the battle against the <s>Daitya</s>s.

children.text: śaśiśubhrairnakhair udyād ekapāt sa kṣaṇaṃ babhau
children.translated_text: With moon-white nails, raising one foot, he shone for a moment
as if bitten by hundreds of <s>Śeṣa</s>s angry at the crushing of their own earth.
Thinking, 'Here is the source of all splendors, beginning with moon and sun,'
he seemed like the eastern mountain attended by rows of stars.
As if thinking, 'This strength is useless without winning battle against the elephants of the quarters,'
he breathed out with broad hissing sighs, languid with rut.
As if thinking, 'Let these quarters come to helplessness through the heat of my prowess,'
he fanned again and again with the flaps of his ears.
With resounding noises like fierce kettledrums, loud as the drum of <s>Caṇḍīśa</s>,
he moved on, slightly opening his eyes in disdain.
Going over the earth adorned with the faces of heroes cut off by <s>Bhagadatta</s>'s weapons,
and seeing them at every step, he remembered lotus ponds.

children.text: sa vāhinīṃ pāṇḍavānāṃ praviśya nibiḍaṃ gajaḥ
children.translated_text: That elephant, having entered the dense army of the <s>Pāṇḍavas</s>,
crushed elephants, horses, and chariots and made it muddy with fat.
The armies of the enemies of the <s>Kauravas</s>, being trampled by the lordly elephant,
suddenly contracted, like prosperities under the force of pride.
When that elephant, equal to <s>Mandara</s>, had overrun the ocean of the army,
there appeared sprays of swords, like the poison <s>Kālakūṭa</s>.
Curling the tip of his trunk, he charged at <s>Vṛkodara</s>,

children.text: ākṛṣṭaṃ pāśahastena yena taṃ menire janāḥ ||
children.translated_text: so that people thought him already drawn in by one with a noose in his hand.

children.text: saṃśaye patitaṃ bhīmaṃ dṛṣṭvā tūrṇaṃ yudhiṣṭhiraḥ
children.translated_text: Seeing <s>Bhīma</s> fallen into danger, <s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s> at once
attacked <s>Bhagadatta</s> together with all the kings.
Although surrounded by those heroes, he killed the king of <s>Dāśārṇa</s>
and with <s>Supratīka</s> violently tore up <s>Sātyaki</s>'s chariot.
Then, at the terrible hissing of that spray-flinging elephant,
the frightened horses carried <s>Bhīmasena</s> and the others far away.
That army, harried by <s>Bhagadatta</s> mounted on his elephant,

children.text: janatā kunṛpeṇeva na lebhe śaraṇaṃ kvacit ||
children.translated_text: found no refuge anywhere, like a people oppressed by a bad king.
As elephants were falling and chariots too were shattering,
there arose a tumultuous noise with the cries of 'alas!' from the terrified.
Hearing the cries of his own men, the son of <s>Indra</s>, with the thunderbolt-weapon,
slew the <s>Trigartas</s> with their followers and then rushed upon <s>Bhagadatta</s>.
Seeing the bearer of the <s>Gāṇḍīva</s> bow coming swiftly like <s>Tārkṣya</s>,
the enraged lord of elephants, urged on by <s>Bhagadatta</s>, charged.
As he came on like <s>Antaka</s>, <s>Keśava</s>, with a leftward turn
made his fury futile by means of the chariot and again stood before him.
The lord of <s>Prāgjyotiṣa</s>, after piercing <s>Pārtha</s> with a thousand arrows,
released the <s>Nārāyaṇāstra</s>, and <s>Keśava</s> caught it.
As he quickly protected <s>Arjuna</s>, that weapon of the foe of <s>Kaiṭabha</s>
fastened on his chest and took on the appearance of a golden garland.
When that blazing, radiant great weapon had come to futility,
<s>Arjuna</s>, embarrassed, twanged his bow and said to <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>:
"Surely I am unfit for battles, since you took hold of the weapon."
Hearing this, the bearer of <s>Garuḍa</s> on his banner honored <s>Pārtha</s> and said:
"Long ago, at the word of the Earth, I, bearing four forms,
gave this, my own weapon, to <s>Naraka</s>, the son of <s>Bhūmi</s>.
That king obtained it, unfailing, from that daitya;
I have taken back that divine weapon. Now kill this king."
When <s>Janārdana</s> had spoken thus, <s>Savyasācin</s>
quickly filled <s>Bhagadatta</s>, together with his elephant, with upward-facing arrows.
Mounted on an elephant with the bulk of a great mountain, the lord of <s>Prāgjyotiṣa</s>, with his arrows,
made the sky a place from which the nearby heavenly chariots of immortals fled.
Then <s>Pārtha</s>, with a nārāca drawn back to his ear,
pierced the lord of elephants through both frontal globes to the tail and threw him into confusion.
Split by <s>Phalguna</s>'s arrow, that mountain-like elephant, as it fell,

children.text: jaghāna mahatīṃ senāṃ patitāḥ pātayanti yat ||
children.translated_text: struck down a great army; for the fallen make others fall.
Then <s>Bhagadatta</s>, enraged and pierced in the heart by the diademed one with a crescent-headed arrow,
dropped goad, bow, and arrows and became lifeless.
When that hero, the crest of all kings, had fallen,
the knot of hope for victory in the <s>Kuru</s> armies became slack.
When the <s>Kaurava</s> army had fled, the two sons of <s>Subala</s>, <s>Vṛṣaka</s> and <s>Acala</s>,
the two <s>Gāndhāra</s> leaders among bowmen, fought <s>Dhanaṃjaya</s>.
The two, showering arrows, were struck together by a single arrow of <s>Pārtha</s>,
and, sewn together as if they had become a <s>Bhāruṇḍa</s>, he made them fall with delight.
Seeing his two younger brothers slain, <s>Śakuni</s>, trembling with anger,
deployed a vast illusion and charged at <s>Savyasācin</s>.
Surrounded on all sides by weapons, cruel beings, and darknesses,
<s>Pārtha</s> did not tremble in battle, even before his hundreds of illusions.
With the solar weapon he cut through that illusion, which deluded the timid,
and launched arrows at him; <s>Śakuni</s> fled in fear.
Then, when the son of <s>Subala</s> had gone, thinking the world was made of <s>Arjuna</s>,
the <s>Kuru</s> army, routed by terror, found no refuge.
Then <s>Droṇa</s>, with his armies, wishing to seize <s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s>,
attacked the <s>Pāñcālas</s>, striking off the faces of heroes.
As the armies were being slain by the thousand by the red-horsed one,
the bride Earth trembled as if drunk with the wine of blood.

children.text: tūrṇaṃ praharata droṇaṃ tūrṇaṃ rakṣata saṃgare
children.translated_text: "Quickly strike <s>Droṇa</s>; quickly protect him in battle"--
such a great cry arose among both the <s>Pāṇḍavas</s> and their enemies.
Then, when the <s>Pāñcālas</s> and the <s>Sṛñjayas</s> had broken everywhere,
<s>Nīla</s>, lord of <s>Māhiṣmatī</s>, fought the <s>Kuru</s> army.
As he burned the armies with divine weapons, fiery in splendor,
<s>Drauṇi</s>, a treasure of courage and the lone bowman, went out to meet him.
Then the preceptor's son, while he showered arrows hard as thunderbolts,

children.text: chattraṃ dhvajaṃ kārmukaṃ ca bhallaiścicheda nirvyathaḥ ||
children.translated_text: calmly cut off his parasol, banner, and bow with broad-headed arrows.
Quickly descending from his chariot, <s>Nīla</s>, of brilliant valor,

children.text: kṛpāṇena śiro hartuṃ drauṇeḥ śyena ivāpatat ||
children.translated_text: swooped like a hawk to take <s>Drauṇi</s>'s head with his sword.
The son of <s>Bhāradvāja</s>, with a broad-headed arrow, cut off his lovely head,
bright with earrings, like the moon joined with a pair of stars.
When <s>Nīla</s> had been slain and the circle of the <s>Pāṇḍavas</s>' fine warriors had broken,
<s>Pārtha</s>, after killing the <s>Saṃśaptakas</s>, returned at speed to the battle-ground.
Then, as the enemy army was being split apart by <s>Bhīma</s>, <s>Phalguṇa</s>, <s>Saubhadra</s>, the <s>Matsya</s> king, the <s>Caidya</s> king, and others,
a tumultuous roar arose.
Then, with <s>Karṇa</s> and the others against those warriors
there was a terrible crush of battle, terrifying all the worlds.
In that boundless battle, hard to cross because of eddies of blood,
seeing the <s>Kuru</s> army broken, <s>Karṇa</s> fought <s>Pārtha</s>.
With the fire-weapon he made <s>Arjuna</s> and also <s>Sātyaki</s> and the rest
seem like mountains tawny from the dreadful burning of the quarters.
Then <s>Dhanaṃjaya</s> and the others, having struck down that fierce weapon with their weapons,
made <s>Karṇa</s>, with hundreds of arrows, like a dense cane thicket.

children.text: śatruṃjayaṃ vipāṭaṃ ca vīraṃ cāvarajaṃ śaraiḥ
children.translated_text: With arrows he struck down <s>Śatruṃjaya</s>, <s>Vipāṭa</s>, <s>Vīra</s>, and another younger brother;
the ape-bannered one sent <s>Karṇa</s>'s younger brothers to the city of <s>Yama</s>.
Then all the great chariot-warriors of the <s>Kauravas</s>, headed by <s>Droṇa</s>,
came to <s>Karṇa</s>'s side, hard to withstand with their blazing masses of weapons.
Those best of bowmen, locked in combat with <s>Sātyaki</s> and the others,
made a terrible battle, destroying elephants, horses, and chariots.
Then, when the strong-armed warriors had been pierced by showers of <s>Arjuna</s>'s arrows,
at the end of the day the kings turned back, sorely afflicted.
Then in the morning <s>Duryodhana</s> came to the preceptor and spoke,
deeply distressed as he described the prowess of the <s>Pāṇḍavas</s>:
"Ah! Even though you promised me, a man without merit,
the hero has come to futility in the seizing of <s>Dharmaja</s>.
Men like you, powerful, affectionate to your dependents, high-born, and famous,

children.text: vṛthā manorathaṃ kartuṃ śikṣitā na bhavadvidhāḥ ||
children.translated_text: are not trained to make another's desire fruitless."
Hearing what <s>Suyodhana</s> said, the jar-born one replied:
"O king, the <s>Pāṇḍava</s> is hard to seize, guarded by the wielder of the <s>Gāṇḍīva</s> bow.
Even so, today I shall do what is in your interest, as far as I have power.
Let the <s>Saṃśaptakas</s> go again and draw <s>Phalguṇa</s> away from the chariot."
When the teacher had spoken thus, the bands of <s>Saṃśaptakas</s> again
summoned <s>Arjuna</s> and, eager to fight, led him to the southern quarter.
Then <s>Droṇa</s>, the disciple of <s>Rāma</s>, consecrated for the destruction of kṣatriyas,
formed the <s>cakravyūha</s> (wheel formation), hard to pierce as the wheel of worldly existence.
In that host of enemies, a multitude of princes shone
with standards clear as the river of heaven adorning their ranks.
In its very center stood the prosperous king <s>Suyodhana</s> himself,
surrounded by a great elephant division and by all the great chariot-warriors.
<s>Droṇa</s>, together with <s>Jayadratha</s>, stood at the mouth of the formation,
along with thirty brothers of <s>Duryodhana</s>, splendid as gods.
Seeing that boundless army and the formation held by mighty warriors,
<s>Dharmanandana</s> reflected, while his army was being torn open by <s>Droṇa</s>.
Considering <s>Saubhadra</s> in battle equal in valor to the foe of <s>Kaṃsa</s>,
he addressed him in the presence of the kings, as one capable of conquering the three worlds:
"<s>Abhimanyu</s>, your father has gone against the <s>Saṃśaptakas</s>.
Therefore you, rich in those virtues, are able to bear this burden.
<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, <s>Arjuna</s>, <s>Raukmiṇeya</s>, or you, with the valor of the thunderbolt-bearer:
there is no bold fifth man for breaking the <s>cakravyūha</s> (wheel formation)."
Hearing this, <s>Saubhadra</s>, his eyes blossoming with joy, said:
"By your command, I shall split the formation today and enter it.
Let the great chariot-warriors follow me, for I do not know how to come out."
When <s>Arjuna</s>'s son had spoken thus, the kings headed by <s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s>
said, "So be it," and <s>Saubhadra</s> urged on his charioteer.
That hero, whose boyhood had just fallen away, was like a three-year-old lion.
At the front of battle he thought the whole multitude of kings insignificant.
Lovely, wearing golden armor, with sword fastened on, and adorned,
the hero seemed like a young god who had come down to earth out of curiosity.
His form was still very tender, but his valor was fully mature.
With his arrows he made <s>Droṇa</s>'s army resemble a heaving ocean.
Then, when a battle had begun that could bewilder even the great,
<s>Saubhadra</s>, of sharp valor, split the formation and entered it.
In speed, elegance, and wondrous skill, he seemed one man become many.

children.text: dṛṣṭvā praviṣṭaṃ taṃ sarve kuruvīrāḥ samādravan
children.translated_text: Seeing him entered, all the <s>Kuru</s> heroes rushed together at him:

children.text: ayaṃ gṛhīto yāto 'yaṃ hato 'yaṃ hantyayaṃ bahūn ||
children.translated_text: "Here he is seized! There he has gone! Here he is slain! There he kills many!"
Such was the cry of the kings around <s>Abhimanyu</s>'s chariot.
With heads still bearing jeweled crowns, with hands holding spears, swords, and arrows,
with bodies in golden armor, and with arms wearing armlets and bracelets,
with horses cut down and with elephants whose frontal globes were split,
falling without cease, he covered the earth.
Seeing their army being struck down by the attacking <s>Saubhadra</s>,
<s>Drauṇi</s>, <s>Karṇa</s>, <s>Kṛpa</s>, and the others rushed angrily at him.
Those heroes showering arrows he turned back with his own arrows;
then <s>Saubhadra</s> took the head of the king of <s>Aśmaka</s> with a broad-headed shaft.
Then, when the <s>Kuru</s> army was broken, <s>Droṇa</s>, <s>Karṇa</s>, and <s>Kṛpa</s> again,
along with <s>Drauṇi</s>, <s>Hārdikya</s>, <s>Gāndhāra</s>, <s>Śara</s>, <s>Śalya</s>, and <s>Bṛhadbala</s>,
<s>Bhūri</s>, <s>Bhūriśravas</s>, <s>Citra</s>, <s>Duḥśāsana</s>, and <s>Suyodhana</s>,
and other kings came up and showered him with arrows.
Covered by their swift, sharp arrows, the son of <s>Arjuna</s>
appeared lovely like a <s>karṇikāra</s> tree in springtime.
Before that son of <s>Pārtha</s>, as before <s>Kumāra</s>, the demons
were defeated in battle by the powerful one's power and fled away.
After swiftly killing the younger brother of the king of <s>Madra</s>, a man of terrible valor,
he killed the heroic brother of <s>Karṇa</s>, who roared like a cloud.
Conquering them one by one in order, and again and again in masses,
he brought destruction upon the kings, with <s>Karṇa</s> and <s>Duḥśāsana</s> at their head.
While he stood within the enemy army, kings in every direction
saw thousands of his golden bows because of his swiftness.
When the array of elephants, horses, and chariots had been torn open by his arrows,
a river of blood spread forth, marked by chowries and turbans like pale smiles.
When headless trunks rose up and the circle of fine warriors was broken,

children.text: dadhmau pārthasutaḥ śaṅkhaṃ diśaḥ śakalayan iva
children.translated_text: the son of <s>Pārtha</s> blew his conch, as if shattering the quarters.
Meanwhile, when the sons of <s>Pāṇḍu</s> were striving to enter the battle formation,
king <s>Jayadratha</s>, proud through the boon of <s>Bharga</s>, held them back.
Formerly, after being defeated by them in the abduction of <s>Kṛṣṇā</s>,

children.text: varaṃ tapaḥ kṛśo lebhe tajjayaṃ phalguṇaṃ vinā
children.translated_text: he, emaciated by austerity, had received from <s>Maheśvara</s> a boon to conquer them, apart from <s>Phalguṇa</s>.
He shone as he checked the sons of <s>Pāṇḍu</s> together with their followers,
like a mountain on the shore checking the stirred-up surges of the great ocean.
Bearing on his banner a golden boar bright as fire,
the <s>Saindhava</s> burned the <s>Pāṇḍava</s> army with <s>Rudra</s>'s energy.
When the sons of <s>Pāṇḍu</s> had been forcibly blocked by him alone,
<s>Abhimanyu</s>, entering among the kings, cut down a forest of heads.
Putting to flight heroic <s>Vṛṣasena</s>, the son of <s>Vaikartana</s>,
he carried off the head of the king of <s>Kāmboja</s>, its turban loosened.
In that terrible crush, when the quarters were blocked by dust,
the kings could be detected only by the rays of their jeweled ornaments.
Then the heir of <s>Vijaya</s>, like a lion seizing a rutting elephant,
seized king <s>Satyaśravas</s>, whose might was unequaled.
When that best of rulers had fallen under <s>Abhimanyu</s>'s control,
<s>Rukmaratha</s>, the son of <s>Śalya</s>, rushed at him with a roar.
With the <s>Gāndharva</s> weapon he suddenly reduced those princes,
whose fires of anger were marked by the smoke of their frowns, to only fame remaining.
When by him a hundred princes, equal in age and dress, had been slain,
it was like a forest of plantain trunks broken by a frenzied elephant.
As the circle of kings fled, <s>Suyodhana</s>, his pride broken,
bowed low in shame and sighed, torn by <s>Saubhadra</s>'s arrows.
Then <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, the son of <s>Duryodhana</s>, resembling <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>,
came up to <s>Abhimanyu</s> and sent forth a line of arrows.
<s>Saubhadra</s> fought that prince, a tender shoot of the creeper of fortune
and a bower of the tree of enjoyment, as an equal for a moment.
His face, attended by rows of pearls like lines of stars,
he cut from the base of the neck with a broad arrow, like the moon from the sky.
Then the lord of the <s>Kauravas</s>, enraged when his beloved son had fallen,
rushed against heroic <s>Saubhadra</s> together with all the great chariot-warriors.
With arrows he rapidly drove off the king, <s>Vaikartana</s>, <s>Droṇa</s>, <s>Drauṇi</s>, <s>Hārdikya</s>, and <s>Gautama</s>,
and he struck down <s>Vṛndāraka</s>.
Then, as the lord of <s>Kosala</s> charged at him in anger,
he cut off <s>Bṛhadbala</s>'s head, its earrings thrown into confusion, with a broad arrow.
Then attacking <s>Karṇa</s> with arrows terrible as thunderbolts,
he brought him to the balance-point of doubt, as if with sprouts of death's fangs.
After felling the attacking princes who were <s>Karṇa</s>'s companions,
he killed <s>Mārttika</s>, <s>Bhoja</s>, and also <s>Kuñjaraketana</s>.
Then, with a shaft, he made the son of <s>Duḥśāsana</s> turn his back,
and, making <s>Śalya</s> chariotless, he bewildered him with nets of arrows.
Having killed <s>Śatruṃjaya</s>, <s>Meghavega</s>, <s>Candraketu</s>, <s>Suvarcas</s>,
and <s>Sūryabhāsa</s>, he brought about the destruction of those <s>Gāndhāras</s>.
Driving off <s>Śakuni</s>, his whole body broken and drenched with blood,
he made heaps of head-fruits in the mango-groves of kings.
With a net of gold-shafted arrows, as if competing with his father,
he made the <s>Kaurava</s> army resemble blazing <s>Khāṇḍava</s>.

children.text: sa babhau bimbito rājñāṃ khaḍgeṣu kavaceṣu ca ||
children.translated_text: Reflected in the kings' swords and armor,
he alone shone as if, for the destruction of the world, he had assumed the universal form.
Seeing him burn many troops with hundreds of arrow-flames,
<s>Rādheya</s>, deeply pierced, came to the preceptor and said:
"Though a boy, his conduct is not boyish; this son of the son of <s>Vajrin</s>,
whose courage is like <s>Kākutstha</s>'s, is destroying the entire army.
A stratagem must be devised here; if he is ignored, he is unconquerable.
For in this battle the victorious fortune of the <s>Kauravas</s> depends on you."
Hearing this, <s>Droṇa</s> smiled and spoke to the son of the charioteer:
"True, the son of <s>Arjuna</s> is killing the army in a moment.

children.text: asya dhairyamamaryādaṃ dṛṣṭvā prauḍhaṃ ca vikramam ||
children.translated_text: Seeing his boundless firmness and mature valor,

children.text: romāñcakañcukaḥ kāyaḥ kasya nāma na jāyate
children.translated_text: whose body would not become sheathed in horripilation?
With bow, with sword, with chariot and armor,
or with a wheel, he cannot be conquered in battle even by the shining gods.
Therefore an effort must be made to destroy all his weapons,
if it can be done by you while he is within the enemy circle."

children.text: tato droṇaḥ samābhāṣya karṇena sahito yayau ||
children.translated_text: Then, after speaking, <s>Droṇa</s>, joined by <s>Karṇa</s>, went out
against <s>Saubhadra</s>, who had routed the army, together with all the great chariot-warriors.
He, with his bow drawn into a circle, met those heroes as they rushed upon him,
and with arrows made them turn back, as a mountain turns back the currents of rivers.
Then <s>Karṇa</s>, from the side, cut through his bent bow,

children.text: rathaṃ jaghāna hārdikyaḥ sārathiṃ tasya gautamaḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Hārdikya</s> struck his chariot, and <s>Gautama</s> struck his charioteer.
When he was chariotless and his bow was cut, <s>Droṇa</s> and the others charged at him.
The hero took up a blazing sword and a shield studded with many stars,
and, moving in circles, became hard to make out.
As he moved through the air in manifold motion, like the thousand-rayed sun all around,

children.text: patitaṃ menire mūrdhni tulyaṃ sarve mahārathāḥ ||
children.translated_text: all the great chariot-warriors thought him equally fallen upon their heads.
With a razor-headed arrow <s>Droṇa</s> split in two the sword with which he was striking,
jagged with pearls clinging to the fronts of split elephant temples.
When his sword had been cut away, he took up a wheel, bearing the mark of valor,
and with that wheel he wrought destruction among the circles of kings, seeming to wield a discus-weapon.
Then all those great chariot-warriors, <s>Droṇa</s> foremost, joined together,
and, fearing annihilation, shattered that wheel into sesame-sized pieces with arrows.
Then, with golden armlets and mace in hand, like another <s>Bhīma</s>,
he killed the heroic <s>Kālikeya</s>, son of <s>Subala</s>.
After killing seventy-seven sons of the king of <s>Gāndhāra</s>,
he felled ten Brahmavasātīya kings with his mace.
Having crushed the chariot of the <s>Kekaya</s>, he made the elephant corps
look like a circle of mountains split apart by the fall of a thunderbolt.

children.text: rathaṃ dauḥśāsaneḥ sāśvaṃ sa niṣpiṣya sasārathim
children.translated_text: He crushed the chariot of <s>Dauḥśāsani</s>, together with its horses and charioteer,
and with his elephant-slaying mace he rushed at that mace-bearing foe.
Moving in circles, the two struck at one another,
their maces crowded with sparks of fire born from dreadful impacts.
Struck by heavy blows, those two mighty-armed warriors fell down.
The great chariot-warriors struck the fallen son of <s>Subhadrā</s> from afar with arrows.
With all his limbs covered in arrows and his disordered hair scattered,
<s>Dauḥśāsani</s> rose and struck him on the head with his mace.
When that hero fell, like a young mango tree before the winds,
the whole garden of the world became troubled and bereft of beauty.
Even when they saw him stilled, that forest fire for the bamboo-grove of warriors,
the kings' hearts were bewildered, thinking that he might rise again.
Seeing the moon-faced prince fallen upon the ground,
the women of the gods and <s>Vidyādhara</s>s in the sky shed tears.
A boy, his bow cut away, exhausted, and deprived of his vehicle,
has been killed by all the great chariot-warriors: such was the cry in heaven.
Then the delighted <s>Kuru</s>s, having gained their target on every side, roared aloud,
and the defeated troops fled to the son of <s>Dharma</s>.
When lotus-eyed <s>Saubhadra</s> had fallen in battle,
