the red-rayed sun, as if stricken with grief, sank into the cave of the western mountain.
Then <s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s> and the others, seeing him killed face to face in battle,
grieved out of affection for the blameless son of the son of <s>Jambhāri</s>.

children.text: samāyayau tato jiṣṇuḥ śibiraṃ vimanā iva
children.translated_text: After that <s>Jiṣṇu</s> came to the camp, as if downcast in mind;
for generally the mind itself first tells of good and evil to come.
He looked at his own army, its splendor ruined and its faces lowered,
and at his brothers, as if pierced in their vital parts by poisoned iron arrows.
Longing in heart to see the son who had been away for the day,
he anxiously questioned them, as though they had been struck mute by grief:
'Surely my son has not entered the wheel-formation devised by <s>Droṇa</s>,
and been brought to death by the <s>Kuru</s>s, who fight deceitfully?

children.text: praveśaṃ śikṣito vyūhe mayā bālo na nirgamam
children.translated_text: The boy was taught by me how to enter the formation, but not how to get out.
Surely that lotus-eyed hero has been slain by sinners.'
Having spoken thus, <s>Dhanaṃjaya</s>, boiling in the fire of grief,
heard the account of his son and, from bewilderment, became like a post.
'That hero has entered a body made of fame, firm for an aeon,'
said <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>; addressed in this way, he regained consciousness and spoke:
'Ah, was there no one to protect my son, gone into the midst of enemies,
there in the middle of you, whose taking up of weapons was in vain?
Where shall I again see that beloved son, a garden of every virtue, with the valor of <s>Rāma</s>,
so dear, desired like something gained in a dream?
Clearly, surrounded by foes as he fell, my son remembered me,

children.text: svasrīyaḥ keśava tvāṃ vā luptadhairyo 'thavā na saḥ
children.translated_text: or you, O <s>Keśava</s>, as your sister's son; or perhaps he did not, his courage unbroken.
<s>Subhadrā</s> is slain, bereft of the son who rained nectar,
who possessed unsurpassed beauty, virtue, and valor.
I think the women of the gods regard that beloved moon-faced one
as a new <s>Manmatha</s> who has arrived in heaven.

children.text: pariṣvajasva hā putra kva yāto 'si vihāya mām ||
children.translated_text: Embrace me! Alas, my son, where have you gone, leaving me behind?'
After saying this, he fell to the ground like a palm tree torn up by the roots.

children.text: pratilabhya punaḥ saṃjñāṃ śrutvā hetuṃ jayadratham ||
children.translated_text: Regaining consciousness again and hearing that the cause was <s>Jayadratha</s>,
his ocean of grief drunk up by the fire of rage at his son's destruction, he said:
'I shall kill the sinful <s>Saindhava</s>, even if he is protected by the gods,
before the hot-rayed sun has set, while all the kings look on.
Those who commit treachery against their gurus and those who revile good men,

children.text: viśvastānghnanti ye svairaṃ nikṣepaṃ bhakṣayanti ye
children.translated_text: those who freely kill people who trust them, and those who consume a deposit entrusted to them,

children.text: nindanti ye striyaṃ bhuktvā ye ca śāstrārthavarjitāḥ ||
children.translated_text: those who, after enjoying a woman, speak ill of her, and those who are devoid of the meaning of <s>śāstra</s>,

children.text: ācaranti niṣiddhaṃ ye vihitaṃ ca tyajanti ye
children.translated_text: those who do what is forbidden and abandon what is enjoined,

children.text: lokān vrajeyaṃ tattulyānhanyāṃ yadi na taṃ yudhi ||
children.translated_text: may I go to worlds equal to his, if I do not slay him in battle.
If <s>Jayadratha</s> has not been slain before the whole day is ended,
then I shall enter the fire, to quiet the stain of falsehood and disgrace.
Whether on earth, in heaven, in the underworld, or in a cave of <s>Meru</s> or <s>Mandara</s>,
even if he is standing there, my arrows, unimpeded, will tear him apart.
Having spoken thus, his eyes copper-red with anger, together with <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, the enemy of <s>Kāliya</s>,

children.text: dadhmau śaṅkhaṃ mahī yena cakampe sakulācalā ||
children.translated_text: he blew his conch, by which the earth, with all its mountains, trembled.
At this moment, learning through spies what <s>Arjuna</s> had said,
the frightened <s>Saindhava</s> came to <s>Duryodhana</s> and reported it to him.
The <s>Kaurava</s>, taking him along, approached <s>Droṇa</s> with his followers
and told him of <s>Savyasācin</s>'s dreadful vow concerning the <s>Saindhava</s>.
<s>Jayadratha</s> says, 'For one day, unseen,

children.text: gacchāmi pārthivāḥ sarve māṃ vā rakṣantu saṃhatāḥ ||
children.translated_text: I will go away; or let all the kings together protect me.'
When <s>Duryodhana</s> had spoken thus, the son of <s>Bharadvāja</s> said to him,
'Tomorrow I shall form a great battle array, hard for even the gods to break.
I shall check the heroic <s>Dhanaṃjaya</s> with arrows
as he comes seeking the <s>Saindhava</s>, like a shore-mountain checking the ocean.'
When the red-horsed one had spoken thus, the foremost <s>Kuru</s>s rejoiced
and thought <s>Pārtha</s> already slain by the fire of his broken vow.
Thinking, 'This very night, in anger, he could destroy the entire army by himself,'
the <s>Kuru</s>s, out of fear of <s>Arjuna</s>, remained standing awake.
Meanwhile, to console <s>Subhadrā</s>, who was babbling, tormented and burned by grief for her son,

children.text: subhadrāṃ yājñasenīṃ ca śauriḥ sāntvayituṃ yayau ||
children.translated_text: and also <s>Yājñasenī</s>, <s>Śauri</s> went.
Comforted by <s>Keśava</s>, <s>Subhadrā</s>, her voice choked with tears,
lamented again and again, clasping to her neck her fainting daughter-in-law.
'Alas, my son, delight of my eyes, nectar-rayed moon of my house,

children.text: kva nu te padmapattrākṣaṃ drakṣyāmi vadanaṃ punaḥ ||
children.translated_text: where shall I see again your lotus-petal-eyed face?

children.text: iyaṃ te matsyaduhitā navoḍhā mahiṣī priyā
children.translated_text: This daughter of <s>Matsya</s>, your newly wedded and beloved queen,
resolved to die, is held back because of the precious burden in her womb.

children.text: nāthe pitari kṛṣṇe ca bhīme ca balināṃ vare
children.translated_text: When your father, <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, and <s>Bhīma</s>, best of the strong, were your protectors,
how do you lie in battle, covered with dust, like one without a protector?
My little son, attain the destiny of those devoted to brahman, generous,
sacrificing, meritorious, and attached to vows of good conduct.'
Having consoled her, who was loud with such lamentation, <s>Mādhava</s>
quickly went to the sleepless wielder of the <s>Gāṇḍīva</s>.
At <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>'s command, intent on recitation, on a pure bed
prepared according to rule, the son of <s>Śakra</s> then obtained sleep.
In a dream, moving through the sky and joined with <s>Viṣṇu</s>, he saw,
after ascending a divine mountain, the god whose crest bears the crescent moon.
Seeing him, the friend of <s>Govinda</s> bowed, with folded hands,
and, filled with joy, praised with devotion the boon-giving, most excellent lord.
Homage to <s>Bhava</s>, who brings about the arising and increase of the worlds;
homage to <s>Śarva</s>, who removes all the poison of evil deeds.
Homage to <s>Rudra</s>, who dispelled the fear of <s>Indra</s> routed by the lord of the demons;
homage to <s>Śiva</s>, the terrible one, to <s>Śrīkaṇṭha</s>, the skull-bearer.
To the fierce one, the abode of blessings, half-female, whose seed is drawn upward,
covered with serpents, worthy of service, partless and yet bearing the lunar digits, homage.
To him of the three guṇas, the three-eyed one, <s>Tryambaka</s>, the triple form,
to the wish-fulfilling tree of resolve, to you, trident-bearer, homage.
Thus praised in the dream, <s>Rudra</s> showed <s>Pārtha</s>
the bow and missile, in the form of a great serpent, together with their proper place.
Seeing that great missile, the <s>Pāśupata</s>, which he had obtained before, <s>Jaya</s>
and receiving the mantra from <s>Caṇḍīśa</s>, awoke with his purpose accomplished.
Then at dawn <s>Dhanaṃjaya</s> reported that to <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>,
and, delighted, considered the whole burden of his vow to be light.
Then, bathed, having performed the necessary rites and having offered into the fire,
the <s>Kuru</s>s and <s>Pāṇḍava</s>s went out with great ardor to the battlefield.
Then <s>Droṇa</s> arranged a battle array in the form of a cart, furnished with a broad wheel,
vast and formidable in display, protected by ten million fine warriors.
And in its middle he made a great-petalled lotus, with kings as its filaments,
and tens of thousands of horses, chariots, and elephants as its pericarp.
Inside that, putting those headed by <s>Kṛtavarman</s> into a needle-array,
he stationed <s>Jayadratha</s>, surrounded by heroes, in the noose of the needle.
When the armies had thus been arrayed by the wondrous-working preceptor,
the wielder of the <s>Gāṇḍīva</s>, with blazing banner, appeared at the front of the army.
The kings could not endure to look at the splendor

children.text: sehire na mahīpālā draṣṭuṃ tejo mahaujasaḥ ||
children.translated_text: of that mighty one, like the fierce-rayed sun with a thousand arrow-rays.
Then, when the world trembled and was crowded with hundreds of evil omens,

children.text: śvetāśve syandane kṛṣṇau śubhrau śaṅkhau pradadhmatuḥ ||
children.translated_text: the two <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>s blew their bright conches on the white-horsed chariot.
At their sound, which made masses of wind collide,
all beings thought the untimely beginning of universal dissolution had come.
Then, when the two oceans of armies swiftly met each other,
the battle became a wave of whirling swords dark as serpents.
Then <s>Pārtha</s>, covering the earth with the heads of heroes
and with ornamented arms, entered <s>Droṇa</s>'s army.

children.text: sa praṇamya guruṃ vṛddhamanumānya prasādya ca
children.translated_text: Having bowed to the aged preceptor, honored him, and won his favor,
he covered him, who had first discharged arrows, with blazing nets of shafts.
Then, intent on <s>Jayadratha</s> and with <s>Acyuta</s> as his charioteer, he swiftly...
After circumambulating <s>Droṇa</s>, he entered with the speed of the wind.
When <s>Śvetavāhana</s>, by his quickness, had left <s>Droṇa</s> behind and entered,
the two wheel-guards, <s>Yudhāmanyu</s> and <s>Uttamaujas</s>, also entered.
Then, like the agitation of the ocean stirred up when <s>Mandara</s> was churned,
there arose a tremendous roar from the battle-array as it was being torn open.
As he advanced, intent on his aim, crushing elephants before him,
the fallen faces of kings looked like forests of lotuses.

children.text: vṛto gato hato labdho hantyeṣa patitā vayam
children.translated_text: "He is surrounded! He has gone! He is slain! He is caught! He is killing! We are fallen!"
Such a terrible cry arose wherever <s>Dhanaṃjaya</s> went.
As he swiftly entered, longing to kill the king of the <s>Sindhu</s>s,
the sound of his chariot was deep like the roar of a cloud at the end of the world.

children.text: ajayyaṃ samare droṇaṃ tyaktvā dhīmati phalguṇe
children.translated_text: When the wise <s>Phalguṇa</s> had abandoned <s>Droṇa</s>, unconquerable in battle,
and had entered like a cloud raining arrows, the forest of the <s>Kuru</s>s trembled.
Then he defeated the heroes led by <s>Kṛtavarman</s>, who had rushed quickly against him,
and the son of <s>Śatamanyu</s> struck down the <s>Yavana</s>-<s>Kāmboja</s> force.
Then <s>Droṇa</s>, coming up behind, checked <s>Dhanaṃjaya</s> in battle with a <s>brahmāstra</s>,
and made the sky matted with a network of flames.
With a <s>brahmāstra</s> itself the son of <s>Śakra</s> at once destroyed that weapon,
avoided his teacher, and went with the speed of thought toward the army of the <s>Bhoja</s>s.
After turning the <s>Bhoja</s> away, as <s>Savyasācin</s> was proceeding onward,
king <s>Śrutāyudha</s>, son of the lord of waters, rose up against him.
Though pierced by the ten thousand arrows he released, <s>Pārtha</s>, an ocean of steadfastness,
slew his horses and chariot and brought about the loss of all his weapons.

children.text: varuṇena purā pitrā sa dattāmādade gadām
children.translated_text: He took up the mace formerly given to him by his father <s>Varuṇa</s>,
which, if hurled in delusion at one not fighting, returns and kills that very man.

children.text: sa tayā keśavaṃ mūḍho mṛtyudūtyeva ghorayā
children.translated_text: With that terrible mace, like a messenger of death, the foolish, mighty warrior
struck <s>Keśava</s>; but <s>Acyuta</s> did not move.
Coming back against him, he, the lord of men, was crushed by that same mace,
and fell with his armor broken, like a great mountain struck by the thunderbolt.
When the hero <s>Śrutāyudha</s>, son of the river <s>Varṇamāyā</s>,
had been killed, the chariot of <s>Pārtha</s> moved on with its momentum unbroken.
As the monkey-bannered chariot went forward with the tips of its standards shaken high by victory,
its smiling crown-ornament shone, lengthened by its speed.
Tawny with the splendor of <s>Gāṇḍīva</s>, as if with a circle of lightning,
king <s>Sudakṣiṇa</s> the <s>Kāmboja</s>, devoted to the <s>Kuru</s>s, attacked.
<s>Arjuna</s> swiftly cut the bow of that showerer of missiles,
and cut apart the spear he had released, which rang with dense bells.
Then that king, his body shattered by the torrent of <s>Pārtha</s>'s arrows,
fell, marked by a golden garland, like a <s>Vidyādhara</s> from the sky.
When the heroic <s>Kāmboja</s> had been killed and the ocean of the army was breaking,
king <s>Śrutāyu</s>, together with <s>Acyutāyus</s>, rushed at <s>Pārtha</s>.
Struck by <s>Śrutāyu</s> with a lance and by the other with a spear,
and likewise by thousands of arrows, the ape-bannered hero fainted.
Then, regaining consciousness, <s>Dhanaṃjaya</s> invoked the weapon of <s>Śakra</s>,

children.text: sāśvasūtau saputrau ca kathāśeṣau cakāra tau ||
children.translated_text: and made the two of them, together with their horses, charioteers, and sons, a mere remnant of story.
The <s>Pāṇḍava</s> slew the <s>Aṅga</s>s, <s>Vaṅga</s>s, <s>Kaliṅga</s>s, and the southerners,
and with swift arrows struck down a vast elephant division.
Felling with arrows the army of <s>Darada</s>s, <s>Turuṣka</s>s, <s>Cīna</s>s,
and other <s>mleccha</s>s, he made a dreadful river of blood.
Cutting off the head of the lord of the <s>Ambaṣṭha</s>s, bright with the jewel in its crest,
the hero whose charioteer was <s>Acyuta</s> entered with his course unchecked.
Then the lord of the <s>Kaurava</s>s came up to <s>Droṇa</s> and said:

children.text: ācārya paśya pārthena bhūbhujāṃ kadanaṃ kṛtam ||
children.translated_text: "Teacher, see the slaughter of kings that <s>Pārtha</s> has made.
How indeed could wretched <s>Pṛthā</s>'s son, O hero, have passed beyond you,
if your simple-hearted concern for your pupil were not present?
Today <s>Jayadratha</s>, whom you had easily granted safety,
has been placed by you yourself into the maw of time, terrible with gaping jaws.
For what ordinary man will check the bearer of the <s>Gāṇḍīva</s>,
ranging through my armies, when even you have disregarded him?"
When the <s>Kuru</s> king had spoken thus, the son of <s>Bharadvāja</s> said to him:
"Young <s>Pārtha</s>, with the speed of <s>Tārkṣya</s>, has passed beyond me, an old man, and come in.
At the gate of the formation I have held back <s>Bhīma</s>, <s>Sātyaki</s>, and the <s>Pārṣata</s>;
if I go after <s>Bībhatsu</s>, they will enter.

children.text: idaṃ tu te karomyadya hitaṃ lokeṣu duṣkaram
children.translated_text: But today I shall do for you this beneficial thing, difficult in the worlds,
by which in battle you will become unconquerable even for the gods.

children.text: ghore vṛtraraṇe rudraḥ surendrāya dadau purā
children.translated_text: In the terrible battle with <s>Vṛtra</s>, <s>Rudra</s> formerly gave to the lord of the gods

children.text: divyaṃ mantramayaṃ varma durbhedyo yena so 'bhavat ||
children.translated_text: a divine armor composed of mantra, by which he became hard to pierce.
That very armor, joined with mantra and received by me from my teacher's mouth,
I shall bind on you with a <s>brahmasūtra</s>, for the destruction of your enemies."
Having spoken thus, with mantra he bound on the <s>Kuru</s> king,
who was setting out to conquer <s>Arjuna</s>, a radiant golden cuirass.
When the lord of the <s>Kaurava</s>s had put on the divine armor from his teacher,
he advanced powerfully against <s>Pārtha</s> with divisions of elephants, horses, and chariots.
At this moment in the battle, at the front of the formation,
stood <s>Dhṛṣṭadyumna</s> and the others facing <s>Droṇa</s>, <s>Śalya</s>, <s>Śala</s>, and the rest,
along with the <s>Pāṇḍava</s>s, the sons of <s>Draupadī</s>, the <s>Rākṣasa</s> <s>Ghaṭotkaca</s>,
<s>Sātyaki</s>, <s>Drupada</s>, the <s>Matsya</s>, <s>Kuntibhoja</s>, and the <s>Kekaya</s>s.
Other heroic kings too rushed together and gathered there.
the heroes most skilled in divine weapons, against <s>Jalasandha</s> the king,
<s>Duḥśāsana</s>, <s>Vikarṇa</s>, <s>Citrasena</s>, and <s>Viviṃśati</s>,
<s>Alāyudha</s>, lord of the rākṣasas, <s>Alambuma</s>, and <s>Alambusa</s>,

children.text: bāhlikaṃ śakuniṃ droṇiṃ vṛṣasenaṃ ca gautamam
children.translated_text: <s>Bāhlika</s>, <s>Śakuni</s>, <s>Droṇi</s>, <s>Vṛṣasena</s>, and <s>Gautama</s>,
and again and again other great chariot-warriors emerging from within the battle-formation,
showered them with gold-feathered arrows marked with their own names.
There, in front of their chariots, they made a ground difficult to cross with whirlpools of blood.
Those heroes, noble in valor, with terrible showers of weapons,
made the quarters beautiful in their fury, fierce with the dance of headless trunks.
At that moment the one with white horses, entering the <s>Kuru</s> army,
made it white with rows of fallen enemy kings like royal swans.
With the arrows released from <s>Arjuna</s>'s arm and moving swiftly,
that chariot, driven by <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, went two krośas forward.
Those horses, equipped with golden harness, seemed to plunge into the sky;
with the webs of radiance stretched out by their speed, they made the quarters put forth shoots.
"An elephant is slain; a chariot is cut apart; this king has fallen" -
such was the noise there wherever <s>Arjuna</s>'s arrows moved.
Then <s>Vinda</s> and <s>Anuvinda</s>, the two <s>Avanti</s> princes, attacked the <s>Pāṇḍava</s>
and made him, together with <s>Keśava</s>, invisible beneath many showers of weapons.

children.text: tayoḥ pārtho rathau hatvā chittvā ca dhanuṣī śaraiḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Pārtha</s> slew their chariots and cut their bows with arrows;
then he took their two heads, by which the earth seemed to have two moons.
After killing those two mighty princes along with their armies,
<s>Arjuna</s>, seeing his own horses distressed, spoke to <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>:
"<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, the horses are afflicted and weary, wounded by the weapons and arrows of the foes.
Free them, remove the embedded shafts, and give them water to drink, lord."
Having spoken thus, he quickly descended; going on foot,
he alone fought all the kings who had come, thinking, "This is the opportunity."
Then, from the networks of <s>Pārtha</s>'s missiles and from their missiles in masses,
the sky became dreadful with flames issuing from their friction.
When <s>Arjuna</s> had quickly made a house-like cage of arrows,
and clear water had arisen from the earth split open by that missile,
<s>Kṛṣṇa</s> turned the horses around, drew out the shafts from them, and let them smell the ground;
after giving them water to drink, he yoked them again, delighted.
Those steeds carried the two <s>Kṛṣṇas</s>, their speed now doubled,
as if they were mounting the sky in a wish to conquer the horses of <s>Śakra</s>.
Then, when only a little of the day remained, the <s>Kaurava</s> army
trembled swiftly under the arrows of <s>Savyasācin</s>, who longed for the <s>Saindhava</s>.
When the kings had fled and the massed forest of elephants was broken,
the <s>Kaurava</s> lord came up, wearing armor fastened by <s>Droṇa</s>.
Seeing him, of great energy, approaching with a vast army,
the foe of <s>Kaiṭabha</s> spoke to the destroyer of the <s>Nivātakavacas</s>:

children.text: ayaṃ sa kartā darpāndho nikārāṇāṃ sthavīyasām
children.translated_text: "Here is that man, blinded by pride, the author of very great outrages.
The root of all misfortunes has arrived; kill this thorn of his family."
When the lotus-eyed one had spoken thus, the two heroes, <s>Jiṣṇu</s> and <s>Suyodhana</s>,
looked at one another for a moment and fought like <s>Indra</s> and <s>Namuci</s>.
Sent forth by the <s>Kuru</s> king, a line of arrows with white feathers
entered the crowned warrior like a row of swans entering <s>Krauñca</s> mountain.
Seeing the arrows of the wielder of the <s>Gāṇḍīva</s> rendered fruitless against <s>Suyodhana</s>,
<s>Govinda</s>, filled with great astonishment, said, "What is this?"
<s>Dhanaṃjaya</s>, the radiance of his lips washed by a smile, said to him,

children.text: jñātaṃ kṛṣṇa mayā yena pāpo 'yaṃ pratibhāṃ śritaḥ ||
children.translated_text: "I know, <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, by what means this wicked man has taken refuge in power.
His armor has been bound on by the teacher through a spell, and is like a thunderbolt.
I know the whole countermeasure for destroying this completely."
Having said this, he discharged a great divine missile to cut away the armor;
but <s>Droṇa</s>'s son shattered it from afar with a great missile.
"A divine missile cannot be used twice," said the son of <s>Pāṇḍu</s>;
then he made <s>Suyodhana</s> deprived of chariot, charioteer, and bow.
With arrows he then made ceaseless target-practice on his two hands,
which were beyond the reach of the armor; by this he turned him away.
Then all the great chariot-warriors, headed by <s>Drauṇi</s>,
rushed furiously upon <s>Pārtha</s>, with varied armor and banners.
There were <s>Karṇa</s>'s son with the peacock-banner, the <s>Madra</s> king with the plough-emblem,
and the illustrious king <s>Suyodhana</s> himself with the jeweled-serpent banner.
<s>Bhūriśravas</s> had a sacrificial-post banner, and around them were warriors with many other banners;
the kings, bearing weapons blazing with gold, fought terribly.
As they rushed on swiftly, <s>Dhanaṃjaya</s>, light-handed in battle,

children.text: cicheda bāṇairmarmāṇi chattrāṇi ca dhanūṃṣi ca ||
children.translated_text: cut their vital points, parasols, and bows with arrows.
With arrows he stripped off their armor and made their bodies, like lotus-hearts,
reddened by blood as if crimson with the young sunlight.
As the heroes and all the kings were being struck down by <s>Jiṣṇu</s>,
Time, with sword-wielding arms whirling, seemed to dance at his own festival.
Meanwhile <s>Droṇa</s>, standing at the mouth of the formation, rushed swiftly
at the son of <s>Dharma</s>, who was surrounded by great chariot-warriors, wishing to seize him.
After reducing the <s>Matsyas</s>, <s>Pāñcālas</s>, <s>Cedis</s>, <s>Sṛñjayas</s>, and <s>Kekayas</s>
to a scant remnant, he made the king chariotless with arrows.

children.text: hatāśvaṃ kṛttacāpaṃ ca dṛṣṭvā sarve yudhiṣṭhiram
children.translated_text: Seeing <s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s> with his horses slain and his bow cut,

children.text: hṛto hṛto nṛpa iti sphāratāraṃ pracukruśuḥ ||
children.translated_text: all cried out in a deep, ringing voice, "The king is taken! He is taken!"
Then the son of <s>Pāṇḍu</s> hurled a life-taking spear.
And with the <s>Brahmāstra</s> <s>Droṇa</s> instantly reduced it to ashes.
With all his weapons cut away and pierced by arrows terrible as thunderbolts,

children.text: saha devarathenāśu muktvā droṇaṃ yayau nṛpaḥ ||
children.translated_text: the king quickly escaped <s>Droṇa</s> and departed with his divine chariot.
When the son of <s>Dharma</s> had fled, the son of <s>Bhāradvāja</s>, blazing with anger,
burned the <s>Pāṇḍava</s> army with hundreds of flame-like clusters of arrows.
Then <s>Bṛhatkṣatra</s> the <s>Kekaya</s>, leader of the <s>Pāṇḍava</s> army,
struck down King <s>Kṣemadhūrti</s>, who was following <s>Droṇa</s>.
The great chariot-warrior <s>Dhṛṣṭaketu</s> made the <s>Trigarta</s> hero <s>Vīradhanvan</s>
headless, and in an instant turned him into a headless trunk.
In battle <s>Sahadeva</s> killed <s>Nirapatya</s> and <s>Hātamitra</s>,
and <s>Sātyaki</s> struck down the prince <s>Vyāghradatta</s>.
Seeing the army being pierced by the enemy, the son of <s>Bhāradvāja</s>
made the <s>Pāṇḍu</s> forces into nothing but heaps of heads.
Then the rakṣasa (demon) <s>Alambusa</s>, brother of <s>Baka</s>, engaged <s>Bhīmasena</s>,
and after fighting him with hundreds of arrows, he killed that army by māyā (illusion).
Seeing the river of blood set flowing by the rakṣasa (demon),
skilled <s>Bhīma</s> cut through that māyā (illusion) with the <s>Tvāṣṭra</s> weapon and swiftly defeated him.
That rakṣasa (demon) came again to kill <s>Bhīmasena</s>,
but huge-bodied <s>Ghaṭotkaca</s> barred the huge-bodied foe.
Leaving his chariot from his chariot, he roared like Time against Time,
seized <s>Alambusa</s> swiftly, crushed him, and made him lifeless.
When the rakṣasa (demon), mighty as <s>Jambha</s>, had been slain by <s>Ghaṭotkaca</s>,
terrible fear arose in the battle among all the kings.
Meanwhile the son of <s>Dharma</s>, not hearing
the sound of distant <s>Kirīṭin</s>'s conch, became somehow apprehensive.
Frightened by <s>Abhimanyu</s>'s fate and despondent, loving his brother,

children.text: uvāca sātyakiṃ matvā sa dhuryaṃ sarvadhanvinām ||
children.translated_text: he spoke to <s>Sātyaki</s>, regarding him as the foremost of all bowmen:

children.text: sātyake paśya bandhūnāṃ gurūṇāṃ suhṛdāṃ tathā
children.translated_text: O <s>Sātyaki</s>, see: for kinsmen, teachers, and friends alike,
and for the pride of your arms, this fitting time has come.

children.text: sa te guruḥ sakhā bandhuḥ kirīṭī śatrumadhyagaḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Kirīṭin</s>, your teacher, friend, and kinsman, is in the midst of enemies;

children.text: na jñāyate praṇaṣṭe 'tra śaṅkhaśabde kathaṃ sthitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: now that the sound of his conch has vanished, it is not known how he stands there.
Apart from you, radiant in conduct and foremost among men of valor,
on whom, O bearer of burdens, can this unbearable burden be placed?
For those who give the earth to worthy recipients and protect one who has sought refuge,
and for those who give up their lives for a friend's sake, the same fruit is heard of.

children.text: dhanyā bhavadvidhā eva kriyate yaiḥ sthiraṃ yaśaḥ
children.translated_text: Blessed indeed are men like you, by whom lasting fame is made
with their own lives, trembling like plantain leaves shaken by the wind.
When you have gone to see <s>Arjuna</s>, the fear born from <s>Droṇa</s>'s attempt to seize me
will certainly not arise for me, guarded by <s>Bhīma</s> and <s>Pārṣata</s>.
When <s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s> had spoken thus, <s>Sātyaki</s>, an ocean of courage,
made himself ready, saying, 'So be it,' eager to pierce the enemy army.
Clad in golden armor and wearing a garland, mounted on a chariot with white horses,
splendid, with a blazing lion-banner and a bow rumbling like thunderclouds,
generous, joyful after offering to the sacred fire, he took leave of the king and his younger brother,
entrusted his protection to <s>Bhīma</s>, adorned himself with auspicious ornaments, and went.
He came upon the son of <s>Bhāradvāja</s> like swift <s>Vainateya</s>,
and for a moment made the serpent-like kings tremble and reel.
Then a terrible battle arose between the preceptor and <s>Yuyudhāna</s>,
bewildering all the worlds, like the battle of <s>Skanda</s> and <s>Tāraka</s>.
Wise <s>Sātyaki</s>, thinking <s>Droṇa</s> unconquerable, said:

children.text: guro śiṣyaṃ tavānveṣṭuṃ phalguṇaṃ prasthitasya me
children.translated_text: Teacher, I have set out to seek your disciple <s>Phalguṇa</s>;
with so little of this day remaining, you ought not obstruct me.
Hearing this and drawing his bow, the pot-born one said:

children.text: na praveṣṭuṃ tvayā śakyaṃ mayi jīvati sātyake ||
children.translated_text: You cannot enter while I am alive, O <s>Sātyaki</s>.
As he was speaking thus, <s>Śaineya</s>, with the speed of mind and wind,
deceived him with his chariot and entered the enemy host that had challenged him.
Proceeding onward, after defeating in battle unconquerable warriors headed by <s>Kṛtavarman</s>,
he struck down fierce mlecchas (foreigners), <s>Kirātas</s>, and <s>Kāmbojas</s>.
As all the sons of <s>Pāṇḍu</s>, with their followers, strove to break the front of the formation,
<s>Kṛtavarman</s>, rich in archery, came out and checked them all.
And as <s>Sātyaki</s>, a thunderbolt to fine warriors, entered swiftly,
breaking masses of elephants and blocking the quarters with arrows,
<s>Sātyaki</s> scattered with arrows the shower of weapons released by him,
and cut <s>Jalasaṃdha</s>'s bow, which resembled <s>Śakra</s>'s weapon.
Angry, with his bow and missile cut away, after expending every weapon,
he then drove his elephant on fiercely and rushed at <s>Sātyaki</s>.
As he rushed on swiftly, <s>Śaineya</s>
cut off his two sandal-anointed arms and quickly took his head with its jeweled crown.
When he had been slain, that lordly elephant, tormented by <s>Yuyudhāna</s>'s arrows,
fled with its armor dangling and crushed the <s>Kaurava</s> army.
Rending the <s>Māgadha</s> army as he entered, the bull of the <s>Vṛṣṇis</s>
fought without confusion against the heroes headed by <s>Duryodhana</s>.
Then, after making all the fine warriors turn away, he
cut off the handsome head of the proud king <s>Sudarśana</s>.
He struck down <s>Śabaras</s>, <s>Yavanas</s>, <s>Bhojas</s>, <s>Barbaras</s>, and <s>Tāmraliptikas</s>,
and <s>Śakas</s>, <s>Muṇḍas</s>, and <s>Kuvindas</s>, while from afar felling rutting elephants,
and after killing various bands of bandits whose valor was cruel,
Karabhakuṭṭāka made the earth muddy with the mire of brains.
Then <s>Duḥśāsana</s>, pierced by <s>Sātyaki</s> with sharp arrows,
quickly left the battle and went to the side of <s>Bhāradvāja</s>.

children.text: taṃ dṛṣṭvā vihvalaṃ droṇo babhāṣe pārśvavartinam
children.translated_text: Seeing him distraught, <s>Droṇa</s> said to him as he stood nearby:

children.text: ko 'yaṃ te saṃbhramo vīra gatvā rakṣa jayadratham ||
children.translated_text: "Hero, what is this panic of yours? Go and protect <s>Jayadratha</s>.
Ah! Seeing your army broken by <s>Sātyaki</s>'s arrows,

children.text: kṛtavairaśca mānī ca yoddhavye vidruto 'si kim ||
children.translated_text: though you have made enmity and are proud, have you fled when there is fighting to be done?
This deed done by the <s>Śaineya</s> is, to be sure, superhuman;
the two heroes, <s>Bhīma</s> and <s>Pārtha</s>, will do many times more than this.

children.text: naiṣā sabhā sā pāñcālīṃ yatra tvaṃ kṛṣṭavānasi
children.translated_text: This is not that assembly hall where you dragged <s>Pāñcālī</s>;
these are fields of fame and valor, attainable only by staking one's life.
Even now let peace with the sons of <s>Pāṇḍu</s> be pleasing to you;
the arrows of <s>Arjuna</s> have not yet made an end of the heroes.
Fight swiftly, then, with no back turned toward the enemies;
for an army whose leaders are broken falls apart even while it is being held back."
Thus addressed by the golden-charioted one, he looked at the ground in embarrassment;
as he slew, he became a helper of Death at the destruction of the world.
In battle he killed <s>Vīraketu</s>, <s>Sudhanvan</s>, king <s>Citraketu</s>,
and likewise the hero <s>Citraratha</s>, all <s>Pāñcāla</s>s.
Then <s>Dhṛṣṭadyumna</s>, enraged, pierced <s>Droṇa</s> with arrows that split every ornament,
and, unshaken, tore open the army with his shafts.
When the teacher, heavily covered with arrows, had fallen into a faint,
the son of <s>Pṛṣata</s>, sword in hand, rushed upon him, preparing to kill him.
Then <s>Droṇa</s>, regaining consciousness, with arrows falling close at hand,
filled him with bamboo shafts, some a kiṣku in measure and some a span long.
Covered by them as if by scorpions, <s>Dhṛṣṭadyumna</s> turned away;
torn from behind by the teacher with broad arrows, he retreated.
Then the red-horsed one, furious, tore through the army of the <s>Pāṇḍava</s>s
and filled the earth with the heads of kings.
Then <s>Sātyaki</s> met <s>Duḥśāsana</s> as he came on, showering arrows,
and made him armor-cut, chariotless, bannerless, and arrowless.
He had been abandoned by the fleeing <s>mleccha</s>s, who had been shattered by blows;
but guarding <s>Bhīma</s>'s vow, <s>Sātyaki</s> did not kill him as he went away with face averted.
Meanwhile the mighty son of <s>Śiśupāla</s>, riding a golden chariot, entered the <s>Pāñcāla</s> army
and launched a blazing attack against <s>Droṇa</s>.

children.text: tasya tūrṇaṃ śitairbāṇairguruḥ kṛtvā yudhi kṣayam
children.translated_text: The teacher quickly brought him to destruction in battle with sharp arrows,
and struck his face, whose turban was sprinkled by rays from the jewel in his crest.
When <s>Dhṛṣṭaketu</s> had been killed, the mighty son of <s>Jalasaṃdha</s>,
showering arrows, in a moment became like a moth in the fire of <s>Droṇa</s>.
Having killed the well-armored son of <s>Dhṛṣṭadyumna</s> with swift arrows,
<s>Droṇa</s> slew the <s>Pāñcāla</s>s as <s>Bhārgava</s> slew the <s>Hehaya</s>s.
When the armies of <s>Pāṇḍu</s>'s sons were broken in that dreadful great battle,
the distressed people censured the teacher, cruel in his armor.
After the <s>Śaineya</s> had long since gone in, <s>Dharmaja</s>, anxious again,
approached <s>Bhīma</s> as the sun hung low and addressed him:

children.text: yathā na śrūyate bhīma śaṅkhaśabdaḥ kirīṭinaḥ
children.translated_text: "Since, <s>Bhīma</s>, the sound of the conch of the diademed one is not heard,
I think that all the great chariot-warriors have done something to him.
Without that hero, your younger brother, the sun that destroys the darkness of the enemies of the immortals,
how can I bear to live, <s>Bhīma</s>?
A terrible, unbearable roar of <s>Pāñcajanya</s> is heard;
I know that <s>Mādhava</s>, in anger at <s>Arjuna</s>'s death, has prepared to fight.
Therefore go, hero, and learn the news of <s>Savyasācin</s>.
Struck by faintness, I see the quarters overrun by darkness."
When <s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s> had spoken thus, <s>Vṛkodara</s> said to him:
"King, you should not entertain anxiety in vain about <s>Dhanaṃjaya</s>.
Who, indeed, would dare in battle to take on the burden of the wielder of the <s>Gāṇḍīva</s>,
who brings widowhood to the wives of the enemies of the gods?
Even so, today I take your command upon my head
and follow <s>Jiṣṇu</s>'s path, tearing through the <s>Kuru</s> army."
Having spoken thus, the son of the Wind, in a chariot sounding like a cloud,
his armor adorned with gold, rushed forth like the king of birds.
Mounting a golden chariot, with gold-feathered arrows
he filled the <s>Kuru</s> forest as if with serpents shining with jewels.
Then, as he wished to enter, the teacher came up to him and said:

children.text: mām anirjitya kaunteya bhettuṃ śakyā na vāhinī ||
children.translated_text: "Son of <s>Kuntī</s>, without defeating me, the army cannot be broken through.

children.text: tvadvidhaiḥ kururājasya saṃrambhaṃ mā kṛthā vṛthā
children.translated_text: By men such as you the anger of the <s>Kuru</s> king should not be stirred up in vain."
Having spoken thus, <s>Droṇa</s> covered the <s>Pāṇḍava</s> with showers of arrows.
Pierced by that net of arrows, <s>Vṛkodara</s> said:

children.text: yathā tvaṃ manyase droṇa nedānīṃ no gururbhavān ||
children.translated_text: "As you think, <s>Droṇa</s>, you are not now our teacher.
<s>Arjuna</s> honors those who are worthy of honor; I am <s>Bhīma</s>. Look at me!"
Having spoken thus, he hurled at him a mace heavy as a thunderbolt.
By that mace the chariot, abandoned by <s>Droṇa</s>, was shattered to pieces;
when <s>Droṇa</s> had withdrawn for a moment, he attacked the lord of the <s>Kaurava</s>s together with his younger brother.
<s>Bhīma</s> filled him, as he showered dreadful arrows, with arrows of his own.
Then he killed the <s>Kaurava</s>s whose faces had been cut off by razor-headed shafts:
<s>Vṛndāraka</s>, <s>Dīrghanetra</s>, <s>Suṣeṇa</s>, <s>Durvimocana</s>,
<s>Raudrakarman</s>, <s>Abhaya</s>, <s>Citrakānti</s>, and <s>Sudarśana</s>.
Having struck them down, while their army was shattered by his mace, he made a loud clap of his palms.

children.text: vidrutaṃ svabalaṃ dṛṣṭvā taṃ droṇaḥ punarādravat ||
children.translated_text: Seeing his own force routed, <s>Drona</s> rushed at him again.
With a chariot whose sound was deep like the rumble of a rain-cloud out of season,
the battle of <s>Drona</s> and <s>Bhima</s> quickly became terrible.
It became a cause for remembering the battle of the <s>Bhargava</s> and the <s>Kakutstha</s>.
Then the cruel-handed <s>Vrikodara</s> climbed down from his chariot.
Lifting up the teacher's chariot with his two arms, he hurled it far, far away.
Its wheels, banner, horses, yoke, and pole were broken and scattered.
<s>Drona</s>, with the stride of <s>Garuda</s>, leapt down from it and got away.
Then, finding an opening, tearing through excellent elephants,
and crushing the battle-throngs, the son of the Wind entered.
As he felled the faces of kings, <s>Maruti</s> again and again recalled
the lotus-pond of <s>Kubera</s>, whose lotuses had their stalks cut down.
Advancing after conquering the <s>Bhoja</s>s and <s>Kamboja</s>s, the elder brother of <s>Vijaya</s>
swiftly entered <s>Karna</s>'s agitated army, himself unagitated.
While <s>Satyaki</s> was crushing the heroes of <s>Karna</s> as he fought,
he heard the twang of the bow and roared, overwhelmed with delight.
Recognizing his roar from afar, <s>Krishna</s> and <s>Dhanamjaya</s>
blew their two conches, whose sound was like the milk-ocean churned by <s>Mandara</s>.
With that sound, rich in the clang of striking against the edges of the quarters,
and causing terror, the worlds trembled.
Hearing the equal conch-blast of the two <s>Krishna</s>s, <s>Yudhishthira</s>
rejoiced and thought that <s>Arjuna</s> had crossed over the ocean of enemies.
Seeing the army being broken by mighty-armed <s>Bhima</s>,
<s>Karna</s> advanced in anger, making the world consist of arrows.
The son of the Wind struck him with arrows as he came on, roaring,
and turned him away, his banner, chariot, and bow cut apart.
When <s>Radheya</s>, the foremost of the steadfast, had been broken in battle,
<s>Suyodhana</s>, his pride faded, came up to <s>Drona</s> and said:
"If <s>Arjuna</s>, your dear pupil, has passed beyond you,
then how have <s>Yuyudhana</s> and <s>Vrikodara</s> entered by force?
What else is this? Truly the hostility of fate is expanding against us,
when you, an ocean of valor, have gone beyond your limit."
Thus addressed by the <s>Kuru</s> king, the pot-born one spoke:

children.text: sainyaṃ puraśca paścācca gṛhītaṃ dhāryate katham
children.translated_text: "How can an army held from both front and rear be maintained?
Though guarded here with effort, it is being split open in front.
All the <s>Panchala</s>s and <s>Srinjaya</s>s are entering unchecked.
The gate of the army here must be guarded by me with every effort.
Are you, together with all these great chariot-warriors headed by <s>Karna</s>,
not enough to hold back <s>Partha</s>, <s>Satyaki</s>, and <s>Bhima</s>?
In what remains of this day's last moment, go and protect <s>Jayadratha</s>.
Now victory and defeat in the dice-game of battle are staked on him alone."
So instructed by his teacher, the king went and, with all his men,
made the two <s>Panchala</s> princes, the wheel-guards of the diademed one, chariotless.
Meanwhile <s>Karna</s> again came against <s>Vrikodara</s>
and with gold-fletched arrows made him resemble a blazing fire.
Then, pierced by feathered arrows loosed from <s>Bhima</s>'s arms, arrows that could split mountains,
the son of the charioteer, his weapon and chariot cut away, left the battle.
Then, when the <s>Kuru</s> force was broken, <s>Karna</s>, proud and recovered,
again rushed in his chariot against the roaring son of the Wind.
As the dreadful battle between <s>Karna</s> and <s>Bhima</s> went on for a long time,
there was destruction of men, elephants, and chariots by masses of arrows.
Then <s>Bhima</s> cut the son of the charioteer's bow, tall as a palm-tree,
and struck his thunder-sounding chariot, together with his hopes.
Seeing <s>Karna</s> chariotless but still fighting with effort,
<s>Durjaya</s>, ordered by the <s>Kuru</s> king, rushed at him.
As that heroic younger brother of <s>Duryodhana</s> came on, showering arrows,
<s>Bhima</s> killed him and, roaring, filled <s>Karna</s> with arrows.
Mounting another chariot, the son of the charioteer
attacked <s>Vrikodara</s> with a bow bristling with broad arrow-flames.
His body torn by those arrows, the son of the Wind trembled with anger.

children.text: gurvīṃ gadāṃ visṛjyāsya niṣpipeṣa rathaṃ javāt ||
children.translated_text: He hurled a heavy mace at him and swiftly crushed his chariot.

children.text: bhuvi sthitaṃ śarairbhinnaṃ karṇaṃ dṛṣṭvā suyodhanaḥ
children.translated_text: Seeing <s>Karna</s> standing on the ground, pierced by arrows, <s>Suyodhana</s>
angrily ordered his younger brother <s>Durmukha</s> to protect <s>Karna</s>.
As that <s>Kaurava</s>, hard to withstand like a thunderbolt of weapons, rushed on with speed,
<s>Bhima</s> knocked him from his chariot, his heart pierced through by arrows.
Mounting <s>Durmukha</s>'s chariot, <s>Karna</s>, afflicted by the fire of grief,
sent against <s>Bhima</s> arrows blazing as if unbearable.
Then the arrows loosed from <s>Bhima</s>'s arms, like snakes with hissing breaths,
pierced the king of <s>Anga</s> through and entered the underworld.
Deeply wounded, he fled in a chariot whose banner shook with speed,
as if uprooting the courage of the <s>Kuru</s> armies.
Then five younger brothers of <s>Duryodhana</s> rushed at <s>Bhima</s>:
<s>Jagaduh</s>, <s>Shalya</s>, <s>Durgrāhya</s>, together with <s>Durdarshana</s> and <s>Dushprabha</s>.
As those men fought, shining with costly ornaments,
he felled them with arrows, like a great wind felling clouds with rainbows.

children.text: hateṣu teṣu rādheyo dhunāno vipulaṃ dhanuḥ
children.translated_text: When they had been killed, <s>Radheya</s>, shaking his great bow,
again fought <s>Bhima</s>, unbewildered even at the great hour of doom.

children.text: tasya bhīmo dhanuśchittvā rathaṃ ca guruvikramaḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Bhīma</s>, of mighty valor, cut his bow and chariot,
and, roaring, made the weapons fall from the hands of the heroes.
When <s>Rādheya</s> was in a difficult position, <s>Suyodhana</s>
quickly sent seven younger brothers to help him.
<s>Citrākṣa</s>, <s>Citravarman</s>, <s>Citrabāṇa</s>, <s>Śarāsana</s>,
<s>Upacitra</s>, <s>Sacitra</s>, and <s>Cārucitra</s>, all together,
just as they came on, wearing matching ornaments and garments, were turned back;
made dead by arrows discharged from <s>Bhīma</s>'s arm, they fell upon the earth.
Seeing those heroes fallen like planets whose merit was exhausted,
<s>Karṇa</s>, his eyes filled with tears, took up another chariot.
Fighting with fury made greater by anger, <s>Vṛkodara</s>
unshaken, filled him with shafts swift as thunderbolts.
Seeing <s>Karṇa</s> covered by arrows fallen from <s>Bhīma</s>'s bow,
the <s>Kaurava</s> lord appointed seven younger brothers to protect him:
<s>Citrāyudha</s>, <s>Śatrusaha</s>, <s>Śatru</s>, and likewise <s>Śatruṃjaya</s>,
<s>Citrāsu</s>, <s>Citrasena</s>, and <s>Vikeśa</s>; he sent those men swiftly.
The son of the wind uprooted those heroes, facing him and pierced by arrows,
from the fronts of their chariots, like trees from mountains.
When those princely sons, rich in valor, had been slain,
a destruction of men quickly arose through the arrows of <s>Bhīma</s> and <s>Karṇa</s>.
Pierced by <s>Bhīma</s>'s arrows, the son of <s>Adhiratha</s> mastered his pain,
and, making his bow into a circle, made the sky consist of arrows.
Then <s>Karṇa</s>'s arrows, astonishing to behold,
as if become one through speed, deprived <s>Bhīma</s> of horses, charioteer, bow, and banner.
As the chariotless <s>Bhīma</s> approached in rage,
<s>Vaikartana</s>, roaring like the fire of dissolution, cut off all his weapons.
Then, his weapons exhausted, the son of the wind sent elephants and horses
against the son of the charioteer, but he cut them apart with arrows.

children.text: viṣamasthaṃ raṇe karṇo na jaghāna vṛkodaram
children.translated_text: In battle <s>Karṇa</s> did not kill <s>Vṛkodara</s>, who stood at a disadvantage,

children.text: vīraḥ kuntīvacaḥ smṛtvā satyaśīlā hi sādhavaḥ ||
children.translated_text: remembering <s>Kuntī</s>'s words; for good men are truthful in conduct.
Touching him, as it were, with his bow, he spoke with a roar:
"Fool, untrained in weapons, do not again fight with great warriors.
Ho, mighty-armed one, this battlefield is not suited to you;
crusher of heaps of flesh and bone, you shine in kitchens.
Or rather, for that body of yours, fit for carrying loads, you beast,
well-fed pack animals that find their living in the forest are suitable."
As <s>Rādheya</s> was saying this, <s>Kaṃsāri</s>, seeing from afar
that <s>Bhīma</s> had fallen into distress, reported it to <s>Phalguṇa</s>.
Then, in the counting of a moment, a swift row of arrows,
resembling streaks of gold and fallen from <s>Gāṇḍīva</s>, entered <s>Karṇa</s>.
As if violently filled with flames transferred from the <s>Khāṇḍava</s> fire,
<s>Rādheya</s>, enveloped, fled, his victorious banner-cloth shaken.
When <s>Vṛkodara</s>, heated by anger, had mounted <s>Sātyaki</s>'s chariot,
<s>Pārtha</s> sent a nārāca arrow at <s>Karṇa</s> along the path of the sky.
As that terrible arrow, equal to a thunderbolt and dreadful to all kings, approached,
<s>Drauṇi</s>, unseen from afar, quickly cut it apart with feathered arrows.
Then <s>Arjuna</s> filled the son of <s>Droṇa</s> with hundreds of arrows;
he too, pierced by those shafts, entered into the clash of armies.
Then, with the rays of gold-backed arrows
and of bows, making the royal host seem to roar in an arrangement of fury,
<s>Dhanaṃjaya</s> tore it open and reached the needle-formation,
where wicked <s>Jayadratha</s> sat protected by great chariot-warriors.
Meanwhile <s>Alambiṣa</s>, whose forest of warriors was licked by arrow-flames,
rushed roaring with a deep sound against <s>Sātyaki</s>.
As that excellent king came on, filling the quarters with arrows,
truthful in courage, <s>Sātyaki</s> checked his great army.
Covered by garlands of arrows with golden feathers from the two of them,
the quarters seemed to put forth shoots, as if sprinkled with heroic rasa.
Then <s>Sātyaki</s> quickly cut off his head with a bhalla arrow,
as it gathered a glow stained by the red jewel of his crown.
After slaying the hero <s>Alambiṣa</s>, foremost among excellent strikers,
<s>Sātyaki</s> killed five hundred princely sons.
As he was destroying the <s>Kuru</s> army in battle, blazing in valor,
the heroic <s>Bhūriśravas</s> himself, banner of heroes, charged at him.
The thunder of those two with splendid bows, clouds on a stormy day of arrows,

children.text: garjitaṃ cakitāḥ sarve rājahaṃsā na sehire ||
children.translated_text: all the frightened kings, like royal swans, could not endure.
With masses of sparks arisen from the mutual friction of their arrow-impacts,
the two shone like mountains swarming with jeweled insects.

children.text: chittvā parasparaṃ cāpaṃ syandanaṃ sampramathya ca
children.translated_text: Cutting each other's bows and smashing each other's chariots,
the two heroes, bearing sword and shield, fought for a long time.
Because their bodies could not be seen for speed as they moved in varied circles,
the warriors, with the battle brought to a halt, became spectators of the two.
Then the son of <s>Somadatta</s> dragged <s>Sātyaki</s> by his garlanded hair,
struck him on the chest with his foot, and threw him down.
Seeing him raise his sword to cut off <s>Sātyaki</s>'s head,
the slayer of <s>Kaiṭabha</s>, alarmed, suddenly said to <s>Pārtha</s>:
"Look at the bull of the <s>Vṛṣṇis</s>, sent by <s>Dharmarāja</s> for your sake,
exhausted in battle and fallen under the enemy's power: <s>Sātyaki</s>."
Surely, for brave warriors, victory and defeat are in every way impermanent,
if even this <s>Sātyaki</s> has reached a condition fit for a coward.
Here is <s>Bhūriśravas</s>, his valor unbroken, swiftly raising his sword,

children.text: samudyataḥ śiro hartuṃ śiṣyasya tava sātyakeḥ ||
children.translated_text: about to take the head of your disciple <s>Sātyaki</s>.
When <s>Janārdana</s> had spoken thus, the ape-bannered one
cut off with a broad arrow the arm of <s>Bhūriśravas</s>, which was turned toward the blow.
When that pillar-like arm had been cut from afar by the crowned warrior, unseen,
the people thought that <s>Sātyaki</s> had fallen out of the mouth of Death.
As that staff-like arm fell to the ground, with the ringing of its rows of bracelets,
it seemed to threaten <s>Kaunteya</s> with very shrill roars.
When that arm, a tethering-post for the elephants of royal victory and a resting place for the earth,
the pillar of the palace of prowess, had fallen to the ground,
releasing the mass of <s>Sātyaki</s>'s hair that had been drawn by its left hand,
<s>Yūpaketu</s>, of no small resolve, said to <s>Dhanaṃjaya</s>:

children.text: aho vīravrataṃ pārtha kīdṛśaṃ darśitaṃ tvayā
children.translated_text: "Ah, <s>Pārtha</s>, what sort of warrior's vow have you shown,
since my arm was struck down by deceit while I was engaged in battle with another?
Or rather, this is just what befits you, since <s>Janārdana</s> is your counselor;
skill in crooked warfare has arisen in your heart through greed for gain."
Having spoken thus, he made a bed of arrows with his left hand,
sat down, and, entering within, accompanied by the functions of touch,
offered the fire of his life into the arrows, his gaze fixed between his brows,
and placed his radiance in his head, beyond moon, sun, and fire.
Then <s>Bībhatsu</s> spoke to the kings, who were loud with blame:
"<s>Sātyaki</s>, confused and in deadly danger, was protected by me.

children.text: hantā śiṣyasya sakhyuśca kṛttahastaḥ kṛto yadi
children.translated_text: If I made the killer of my disciple and friend into one whose hand was cut off,

children.text: tatra kiṃ nāma manyadhvaṃ nirdoṣā yūyamāhave ||
children.translated_text: what fault do you find in that, you who are blameless in battle?
The single <s>Abhimanyu</s> was killed unfairly by all the kings,
exhausted, with his bow and sword cut away; what indeed do they not say against us?"
When <s>Kaunteya</s> had spoken thus, then <s>Sātyaki</s>, having regained consciousness,

children.text: yayāce praṇataḥ pūrvaṃ raṇaṃ prāyajuṣo ripoḥ ||
children.translated_text: first bowed and asked for battle from the foe who was undertaking a fast unto death.
With his sword he carried off the face of that sacrificial-minded hero, that treasure-house of fame,
a face that seemed to smile with the gleams of its strings of pearls.
Though <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> and the kings were hastily restraining him,
when <s>Sātyaki</s>, not understanding the situation because of anger, had killed him,
a cry of 'Shame!' rose from all the heroes and filled the sky,
while the gods in heaven praised the conduct of the son of <s>Somadatta</s>.
For <s>Somadatta</s>, having once been defeated by him in great anger,
propitiated through austerity the god <s>Rudra</s>, the destroyer of <s>Tripura</s>,
and obtained as his son <s>Bhūriśravas</s>, conqueror of <s>Sātyaki</s>,
the crest-jewel of all heroes, generous and performer of many sacrifices.
When that hero had fallen, the white-horsed one, eager to kill <s>Jayadratha</s>,
quickly entered the dense circle of kings.
As the sun was about to become the crest-jewel of the western mountain,
<s>Pārtha</s> saw the <s>Saindhava</s>, guarded by all the great chariot-warriors.
Drawing the <s>Gāṇḍīva</s> back to his ear from afar,
with his anger-reddened glance he seemed to burn that foe, terrible to approach.
Then, when the army was tossed about like an ocean turning back,
there arose a great cry, 'The Sindhu king is slain, slain!'
Then <s>Karṇa</s>, <s>Kṛpa</s>, <s>Drauṇi</s>, <s>Duḥśāsana</s>, and <s>Suyodhana</s>,
together with all the kings, fought against <s>Dhanaṃjaya</s>.
After quickly making them, with arrows, deprived of armor, chariots, and banners,
<s>Jiṣṇu</s>, causing the faces of kings to fall, rushed at the <s>Saindhava</s>.
<s>Jayadratha</s> too, seeing <s>Vijaya</s> with <s>Acyuta</s> as his charioteer,
drew out those arrows again and again and filled him with shafts.
Then, at the end of the day, <s>Madhuripu</s> said to <s>Savyasācin</s>,

children.text: chinddhi sindhupateḥ kṣipraṃ śiro divyena patriṇā ||
children.translated_text: "Quickly cut off the head of the Sindhu lord with a divine feathered arrow.
<s>Vṛddhakṣatra</s>, his father, granted this boon: whoever
makes his head fall on the earth, that man's own head too will fall in the same way.
His father is standing in austerity near <s>Samantapañcaka</s>;
therefore make the enemy's head fall in his lap, and from there let it go to the ground."
When <s>Śauri</s> had spoken thus, <s>Jiṣṇu</s> swiftly cut off the Sindhu's head
and with an arrow set it down in the lap of his father, who was absorbed in twilight meditation.
As <s>Vṛddhakṣatra</s>, unaware of the matter, threw that head from his lap to the ground,
his own head suddenly fell before him.
When that hero had fallen through a deed astonishing to the three worlds,
<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, together with the wielder of <s>Gāṇḍīva</s>, roared, making the quarters resound.
Then, when the formation was broken, the army of the Kuru king
reeled like a ship on the ocean, whirled about by eddies under great winds.

children.text: bhīmo nanarda taṃ nādaṃ hataṃ matvā jayadratham
children.translated_text: <s>Bhīma</s> roared that roar, thinking <s>Jayadratha</s> slain;
delighted, <s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s> took up the sound with many instruments.

children.text: akṣauhiṇīḥ sapta hatvā hataḥ pārthena saindhavaḥ
children.translated_text: "After seven akṣauhiṇīs had been slain, the <s>Saindhava</s> has been killed by <s>Pārtha</s>;

children.text: nūnaṃ na durgaṃ daivasya kiṃcidityūcire janāḥ ||
children.translated_text: surely nothing is difficult for fate," people said.
Then, when an indiscriminate battle had begun amid the destruction of kings,

children.text: droṇaṃ kṛpaṃ ca vidadhe śarairjiṣṇuḥ parāṅmukham ||
children.translated_text: <s>Jiṣṇu</s> made <s>Droṇa</s> and <s>Kṛpa</s> turn away with arrows.
And <s>Sātyaki</s>, the hero, mounted his own chariot, its tongue and side-pieces split by terrible arrows,

children.text: āruroha rathaṃ vīro vitīrṇaṃ hariṇā nijam ||
children.translated_text: which had been given by <s>Hari</s>.
Considering also the insult to <s>Māruti</s>, the son of <s>Śatamanyu</s>
again made a vow concerning the killing of <s>Karṇa</s>'s son <s>Vṛṣasena</s>.

children.text: tato yudhiṣṭhiraṃ prāpya tau ca sātyakiphalguṇau
children.translated_text: Then, after reaching <s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s>, those two, <s>Sātyaki</s> and <s>Phalguṇa</s>,
gladly congratulated each other's valor and told what had happened.
Then <s>Dharmanandana</s>, embracing the two <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>s,
praised <s>Viṣṇu</s>, lord of the worlds and cause of victory.
Then King <s>Suyodhana</s>, his eyes troubled with tears, came to <s>Droṇa</s>

children.text: ūce tvayā kṛtāśvāso nihataḥ sa jayadrathaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and said, "Relying on you for assurance, that <s>Jayadratha</s> has been slain."
Hearing this, <s>Droṇa</s> said, "Consecrated now only for destruction,
I shall not put off my armor, O king, without first killing your enemies."
When the preceptor had spoken thus, all the followers of <s>Duryodhana</s>
stood resolved in the battle-sacrifice where lives were the oblations.
Then, when the sun, whose light makes lotuses bloom, had gone to its setting,
as if drawn down like a red parasol by the floodwaters crimson with twilight,
and when the sky was filled with stars, bright and trembling,
like the life-breaths of kings slain in battle while shaking with anger,
and when the heavens were covered with darknesses black like a forest of swords,
like elephants burned by divine weapons as they went to heaven,
<s>Duryodhana</s> and the others, their crowns, armlets, golden arrows, and bows flashing,
made a terrible battle against their enemies.
At the roars of <s>Arjuna</s>'s bowstring and the lion-cries of <s>Māruti</s>,
and at the thunder of <s>Droṇa</s>'s bow, the earth trembled.
For the kings of the <s>Kurus</s> and <s>Pāṇḍavas</s>, fighting without rest,
the night appeared like <s>Kālarātrī</s> herself come in person.
Darkness gained fullness upon swords and elephants,
while it gained poverty upon parasols and fans.
In that festival for vultures and spirits, the earth became frightful,
as if rent apart by darkness moving with unceasing pride.
It became a festival in which vetālas beat time, breaking sudden courage,
and where headless trunks, with uplifted arm-staffs, made a tumultuous dance.
The flames of weapons striking helmets and mail appeared
like tawny beards and manes of hosts of darkness-demons.
There <s>Droṇa</s>, consuming the circle of kings with floods of great missiles,
cut off the head of <s>Śini</s>, blazing with its jeweled crown.
<s>Bhīmasena</s> too, leaping from chariot to chariot,
quickly slew with his fist the vigorous prince of <s>Kaliṅga</s>.
When he was struck by that fist in battle, his bones fell to the ground,
like the fruit of a long-ripe tree struck by a stone in the month of <s>Phālguna</s>.
Having swiftly destroyed the family of <s>Kaliṅga</s>, <s>Vṛkodara</s>
tore apart the two princes <s>Dhruva</s> and <s>Jaladhāra</s>.
After making <s>Karṇa</s> turn away, heroic <s>Bhīma</s>
struck down and crushed underfoot <s>Duṣkara</s>, the arrogant younger brother of <s>Duryodhana</s>.
Then <s>Sātyaki</s>, having slain <s>Śala</s>, the son of <s>Somadatta</s>,
made him, stricken with grief for his son, turn away with arrows.
As <s>Sātyaki</s>, raining arrows, tore through the <s>Kuru</s> army,
<s>Aśvatthāman</s> rushed at him, filling the quarters with arrows.
Seeing him destroying the armies like another <s>Rudra</s>,
<s>Ghaṭotkaca</s>, with doubled zeal at midnight, charged at him.
The quarters were completely filled by his great roar;
then it seemed a wonder that they did not split apart in pieces.
In battle, against radiant <s>Aśvatthāman</s>, whose fierce arrows were like rays,
<s>Ghaṭotkaca</s> shone forth, displaying the gaping onset of <s>Rāhu</s>.
The brilliance of the divine arrows released by <s>Drauṇi</s> in battle

children.text: na kūṇitāni netrāṇi rātrau bhūtāni sehire ||
children.translated_text: was such that living beings at night could not bear it with uncontracted eyes.
Alone, <s>Drauṇi</s> fought an akṣauhiṇī of rākṣasas
subject to the son of <s>Hiḍimbā</s>, smashing their shore-like weapons.
After cutting down the discus, bright as the fire of time, that delighted <s>Ghaṭotkaca</s> had hurled,
he slew <s>Añjanaparvan</s>, that son of his, who had terrible valor.

children.text: tato vimohinīṃ māyāṃ drauṇiḥ kruddhasya rakṣasaḥ
children.translated_text: Then <s>Drauṇi</s> cut through the bewildering magic of the furious rākṣasa
and killed the younger brothers of <s>Dhṛṣṭadyumna</s> with arrows in battle.
Having slain the sons of <s>Kuntibhoja</s> and thousands of attackers,
<s>Drauṇi</s>, raging like death, killed many princes.
Meanwhile <s>Bhīmasena</s>, with his mace that slays heroes,
quickly crushed the crowned head of the lord of <s>Bāhlīka</s>.
Then, enraged, he slew ten younger brothers of <s>Duryodhana</s>:
<s>Vīrabāhu</s>, <s>Dṛḍharatha</s>, <s>Nāgadanta</s>, and <s>Ayobhuja</s>,
<s>Pramāthin</s>, <s>Virajas</s>, <s>Suhasta</s>, and also <s>Sudṛḍha</s>;
after killing these seven <s>Gāndhāras</s>, he slew the sons of <s>Subala</s>.
As <s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s> himself was killing the <s>Kaurava</s> army in battle,
<s>Droṇa</s> too fought him with the Aindra, Vāruṇa, and Vāyavya weapons.
Then, when the guru launched a brahmāstra in order to seize him,
<s>Dharmaja</s>, without agitation, checked that very brahmāstra with a brahmāstra.
Seeing his army, together with its followers, being trampled by the sons of <s>Pāṇḍu</s>
like a lotus-pond by elephants, <s>Suyodhana</s> said to <s>Karṇa</s>,
"<s>Karṇa</s>, listen in battle to the cries of the swift armies,
as they are being slaughtered by the victorious sons of <s>Pāṇḍu</s>.
In this tumult, with no light, when a dire crisis has arisen,
you alone, O hero, are the refuge of splendor and our final resort."
Thus <s>Rādheya</s>, personally entreated with affection by the king,
spoke, as if casting a shower of arrows into the armies of <s>Pāṇḍu</s>.
With <s>Bhīṣma</s>, crest-jewel of all bowmen, lying on the hero's bed,
O king, this burden has come in due course to me alone; what is there to say?
Today in battle I shall bring down the diademed one, robber of heroes' vows, even if he were <s>Hara</s>,
with the spear given by <s>Vāsava</s>.
When the son of the charioteer had spoken thus, <s>Kṛpa</s> said with a laugh,

children.text: loke satyam avīre 'smin ekastvaṃ vīratāṃ gataḥ ||
children.translated_text: In this world devoid of heroes, truly you alone have attained heroism.

children.text: aho nu mithyā rādheya kathitena tavāmunā
children.translated_text: Ah, <s>Rādheya</s>, by this false statement of yours
the ears of all heroes have constantly been deafened.
From where have you come, mighty one, as if you had not heard the news,
that when the lord of <s>Sindhu</s> was slain, you did not act then?

children.text: dṛṣṭasārā vayaṃ sarve tava pāṇḍusutasya ca
children.translated_text: We have all seen the real worth of you and of the son of <s>Pāṇḍu</s>.

children.text: balānusāraṃ yudhyasva vṛthā ślāghāṃ tu mā kṛtāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Fight according to your strength; do not make empty boasts.
When the son of <s>Śaradvat</s> had spoken thus, <s>Vaikartana</s> said in anger,
Heroes thunder fruitfully, like clouds of the rainy season.

children.text: tvaṃ tu vṛddha nirācāro mohādevaṃ prabhāṣase
children.translated_text: But you, old man, bereft of proper conduct, speak so from delusion.
For who, taking refuge with another side, praises others like a panegyrist?
Brahman in name only, if out of hatred you speak so again,
I shall cut off your harsh tongue with this sword.
Seeing his maternal uncle enraged by <s>Karṇa</s> in his fury,
<s>Drauṇi</s>, angered, drew his sword and rushed at him.
As he came on like <s>Rudra</s>, capable of destroying the three worlds,
the king himself, together with <s>Gautama</s>, restrained him with words of policy.
Then, after appeasing <s>Droṇa</s>'s son and <s>Karṇa</s>, the <s>Kuru</s> king, intent on battle,
entered the <s>Pāṇḍava</s> army with all the great chariot-warriors.
By arrows of <s>Karṇa</s>, released from a bow drawn back to the ear,
<s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s>'s army was scattered on every side.
The cloud that was <s>Pārtha</s> approached that fierce fire of <s>Karṇa</s>, terrible with arrow-flames,
and covered it with streams of arrows.
Then in a moment <s>Karṇa</s>, his bow, chariot, and banner cut down by <s>Arjuna</s>'s arrows,
mounted <s>Kṛpa</s>'s chariot, his hopes shattered.
Seeing heroic <s>Duryodhana</s> fighting with his enemies,
<s>Drauṇi</s>, hard to check in battle, struck down the <s>Pāñcāla</s> army.
Slain by thousands by the son of <s>Droṇa</s>, the fire in the forest of kṣatriyas,
the surviving <s>Pāñcāla</s>s fled in all directions.

children.text: dhṛṣṭadyumnaṃ tato jitvā vīraṃ hatvāsya cānugān
children.translated_text: Then, after conquering <s>Dhṛṣṭadyumna</s> and killing his followers,
<s>Drauṇi</s> made the battlefield resemble the pleasure-garden of Death.
King <s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s> himself, together with <s>Bhīma</s> and <s>Arjuna</s>,
routed the <s>Kaurava</s> army and reduced it to a mere remnant, as after <s>Droṇa</s>.
Then <s>Sātyaki</s>, unbewildered, fought <s>Somadatta</s> as he came on with great valor,
as <s>Kumāra</s> fought <s>Tāraka</s>.
Pierced by hundreds of his arrows, <s>Sātyaki</s> steadied his pain,
and with an arrow like a thunderbolt split him open and felled him.
Then, in the battle of <s>Droṇa</s> and <s>Arjuna</s>, hard to endure because of masses of divine missiles,
the night shone like <s>Kālarātrī</s> clothed in red garments.
Then, by those headed by the diademed one and by those urged on by <s>Drauṇi</s> and <s>Kṛpa</s>,
there arose a fearsome roar from the armies as they were being broken.
Then, at <s>Duryodhana</s>'s command, in the dense darkness,
the heroes fought with continuous lamps fastened to the bodies of elephants and horses.
Those two armies at once shone all around with masses of lamps,
as if with the splendors of slain kings, gone into fragments.
Those troops gleamed with lamps reflected in their swords,
like forests blazing with clusters of night-shining herbs.
The radiances of the kings' jeweled ornaments, brightened by the lamps,
appeared like golden streaks on a touchstone of darkness.
Then, when those lamps were destroyed in the press of battle,
midnight reached its youth, as if through the removal of its enemies.
Then, when an indistinguishable battle rich in valor had begun,
and the lord of the <s>Kaurava</s>s himself, with his attendants, had been defeated by the son of <s>Dharma</s>,
<s>Karṇa</s> held back <s>Sahadeva</s>, though he had come into Death's road,

children.text: na jaghāna raṇe karṇaḥ smarankuntīvaco muhuḥ ||
children.translated_text: and did not kill him in battle, repeatedly remembering <s>Kuntī</s>'s words.
Then the heroic son of <s>Karṇa</s>, <s>Vṛṣasena</s>, entered the enemy army,
his rows of weapon-flames licking up the forest of kṣatriyas.
When the heroes had been routed by <s>Vṛṣasena</s>'s arrows,
the enraged son of <s>Drupada</s>, in anger, tore apart the <s>Kuru</s> army.
While the dreadful battle went on before the eyes of the son of <s>Bhāradvāja</s>,
<s>Dhṛṣṭadyumna</s> killed the heroic king <s>Drumasena</s>.
Then, at <s>Duryodhana</s>'s word, <s>Droṇa</s> and <s>Karṇa</s>
made lotus-ponds on the earth with the severed heads of kings.
Having conquered those headed by <s>Dhṛṣṭadyumna</s> and destroyed the leaders of the forces,
<s>Karṇa</s> routed the <s>Pāṇḍava</s> army and wrought destruction among kings.

children.text: taṃ karṇaṃ sāyakāneva kirantaṃ tejasāṃ nidhim
children.translated_text: That <s>Karṇa</s>, treasure-house of splendor, scattering arrows,

children.text: na sehire pare draṣṭuṃ raṇe tapanasaṃbhavam ||
children.translated_text: the enemies could not bear to look upon in battle, the son of the Sun.
As the armies were being broken by battle-skilled <s>Karṇa</s>,
the entire hope of victory of the sons of <s>Pāṇḍu</s> grew thin.
Then, at <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>'s word, in the black night, <s>Ghaṭotkaca</s>
swiftly struck at <s>Karṇa</s>, descending like <s>Kṛṣṇā</s>'s anger.
When he rose up, with blazing beard, tongue, and eyes,
the armies split into a hundred parts, as if struck down by his might.
At that time he, cloud-dark and fierce with the lightning of his frown,
<s>Partha</s> filled <s>Karna</s> with broad arrows falling in hundreds of streams.
He had mounted a four-hundred-cubit chariot whose body was like heated gold,
beyond comparison with a blue mountain set on fire on every side.
Bearing a radiant bow ten cubits in girth,
he was like a forest fire blazing around a great śāla tree.
With his broad crown flashing and his bright gold armlets shining,
he seemed to be breaking apart a peak lodged on a mountain of darkness.
His roar, harsh with loud laughter, seemed to belong to the powers of darkness;
and when men saw him, blazing with grotesque flames, the wounded cried out in pain.
When the enemy armies fled and the kings, fit only for pleasure, scattered,
only the mountain-like <s>Radheya</s> received that autumn storm-cloud of his attack.
Then, to protect the king of <s>Anga</s>, the strong son of <s>Jaṭāsura</s>,
<s>Alambusa</s>, after addressing the lord of the <s>Kaurava</s>s, came forward.
Then a terrible combat arose between that striker
and <s>Ghaṭotkaca</s>, who rained weapons, missiles, rocks, and fire.
As those two fought by manifesting wondrous stratagems made of māyā,
hundreds of warriors lost their lives from their mighty roars.
Then the son of <s>Bhima</s> rushed from his chariot against <s>Alambusa</s>'s chariot,
embraced him with both arms as if he were a friend, and crushed him tighter and tighter.
As he was being squeezed, from the openings of his channels there burst forth
spurts of blood, smoky, flaming with fire, and roaring aloud.

children.text: tato bhuvi viniṣpiṣya rāviṇaṃ taṃ ghaṭotkacaḥ
children.translated_text: Then <s>Ghaṭotkaca</s> crushed that howling one upon the ground,
tore off his head with speed, and went up to <s>Duryodhana</s>.
He said to him, 'This night-roving kinsman of yours has been killed by me.
Let the head of your dear one fall again, lowest of kings.'
Saying this, the night-rover rushed at <s>Karna</s>, roaring,
like agitated Time itself, whipped up by a fierce wind.
Then, when the dreadful battle between <s>Radheya</s> and the rākṣasa had begun,
the gods in heaven remembered the battle of <s>Rama</s> and <s>Ravana</s>.
Though pierced by the rākṣasa with arrows as thick as pillars,

children.text: viddho 'pi rakṣasā karṇo na cacāla mahāśayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: blazing like firebrands, great-hearted <s>Karna</s> did not move.
Then the rākṣasa, split open by <s>Karna</s>'s great arrows
released in anger, hurled a fiery discus at <s>Karna</s>.
Seeing that wide, thousand-spoked wheel making the sky tawny with its brilliance,
<s>Karna</s> swiftly cut the discus into pieces with his rushing arrows.
Then <s>Ghaṭotkaca</s>, in anger, created a deluding māyā,
crushed charioteer, banner, and broad chariot, and entered the sky.
In that sky, made a cremation ground, with dimmed fires and crowded with stars like bones,
there appeared for him millions of maddened vetālas.

children.text: muhurgajo muhuḥ siṃhaḥ kṣaṇaṃ meghaḥ kṣaṇaṃ giriḥ
children.translated_text: Now an elephant, now a lion, for a moment a cloud, for a moment a mountain,
he assumed a vast body made of all beings and rained down huge rocks.

children.text: bhuvo vahniṃ divaḥ śastraṃ digbhyo rākṣasamaṇḍalam
children.translated_text: Sending fire from the earth, weapons from heaven, and hosts of rākṣasas from the quarters,
he fought <s>Vaikartana</s> among the <s>Kuru</s> armies.

children.text: tato vidhūya tāṃ māyāṃ karṇo divyāstratejasā
children.translated_text: Then <s>Karna</s>, shaking off that māyā with the splendor of a divine missile,
burned the <s>Pandava</s> army and pierced the rākṣasa with arrows.
After killing <s>Hidimba</s>'s attendant yātudhānas by the thousand,
<s>Karna</s>, foremost among bowmen, shone with the valor of <s>Rama</s>.
The son of <s>Bhima</s> hurled at <s>Karna</s> a sixty-four-wheeled thunderbolt,

children.text: bhaimaḥ sasarja karṇāya svayaṃ rudreṇa nirmitām ||
children.translated_text: terrible with the tongue of Time and fashioned by <s>Rudra</s> himself.
Launched by the lord of the rākṣasas and able to crush masses of mountains,
that thunderbolt, with a great roar, reduced the son of <s>Adhiratha</s>'s chariot to ashes.
Then the son of the charioteer mounted another chariot
and killed other flesh-eaters with faces like piśācas.
Chariotless, a fire of anger, his eyes ringed with flame,
<s>Ghaṭotkaca</s>, master of great māyā, vanished again.
At that moment the rākṣasa lord, dear friend of <s>Baka</s>,
<s>Alāyudha</s>, with <s>Suyodhana</s>'s permission, came against <s>Bhima</s>.
He stood in a deeply thundering chariot yoked with a hundred horses
that had elephant ears and the appearance of piśāca faces.
<s>Bhima</s> received him, heavy with furious roaring,
as an unshaken hero perfected in spells would receive a risen vetāla.
Assailed by the dreadful rākṣasa, who rained rocks, weapons, and missiles,
<s>Bhima</s> sent forth his mace, intending to kill him.

children.text: tāṃ gadāṃ gadayā rakṣo hatvā jāmbūnadāṅgadām
children.translated_text: The rākṣasa struck that gold-armleted mace with his own mace,
and, roaring with the deep sound of an untimely thundercloud, entered the sky.
Seeing <s>Bhima</s> engaged at night with <s>Alāyudha</s>, a fighter of stratagems,
<s>Krishna</s> was for a moment troubled by uncertainty.
Then, at <s>Sauri</s>'s word, that hero, foremost in fierce deeds,
<s>Ghaṭotkaca</s>, leaving <s>Karna</s>, advanced against <s>Alāyudha</s>.
As the two raged in the sky, their collision thundered like clouds,
and fire was violently stirred up by the grinding of rocks and weapons.
Both were dreadful with beards and matted hair tawny like funeral-pyre fire;
sparks born from the grinding of their teeth seemed to whirl about.
And <s>Ghaṭotkaca</s> swiftly cut off <s>Alāyudha</s>'s head,
which was adorned with earrings resembling fire-pits.
Having killed him, the terrible, mighty son of <s>Hidimba</s> roared fiercely,
quickly approached <s>Karna</s>, and battered him with showers of rocks.
And <s>Vaikartana</s> too, after destroying the battle-line of the sons of <s>Pritha</s>,
Bewildered by <s>Ghaṭotkaca</s>, he covered him with nets of arrows.
Then the night-roamer, after striking down <s>Karṇa</s>'s chariot with a missile,
took up an illusion that enchanted the three worlds and entered the sky.
With firebrands, weapons, trees, stones, and mountains too,
that great-roaring one struck the army of the <s>Kauravas</s>.
At midnight, while all the heroes were fighting against the rākṣasa,
the kings fled, their chariots and elephants shattered.
In that exceedingly terrifying slaughter of all warriors,
<s>Karṇa</s>, unshaken in battle, filled the sky with arrows.
As the stones in the sky were being pierced by <s>Karṇa</s>'s shafts,
a crackling sound arose from them, bristling with masses of flame.
Then iron clubs, swords, śataghnīs, darts, and mallets,
together with tridents, maces, discuses, bhusuṇḍīs, arrows, and tomaras,
hurled at <s>Karṇa</s>'s face by the rākṣasa, the poison-fighter,
made the Kaurava army seem slain by hundreds of Deaths.
And when the army had fled, descending into streams of blood,
while <s>Rādheya</s> remained unsupported, endowed with courage,
the siddhas, gods, and seers in the sky departed after saying, 'May it be well!',
and the whole world trembled because of the illusion of the lord of rākṣasas.
Then the <s>Kaurava</s> approached the hero <s>Karṇa</s> as he fought,
and spoke, distressed and worn out by terror at the destruction of all:
'Why is the spear meant for <s>Arjuna</s>'s killing being held by you to no purpose?
At this midnight, who among us can escape this one and later win?'
Hearing this, <s>Rādheya</s> took the great-radiant weapon given by <s>Śakra</s>,
long preserved and dependent upon the killing of a single hero,
and released into the sky that tearer of hosts of daityas,
by the splendor of whose mass of flames the sky seemed to be parted with a hairline.

children.text: tejasvino rākṣasasya dṛḍhaṃ vakṣo vidārya sā
children.translated_text: Tearing open the firm chest of the powerful rākṣasa,
it went blazing to the third heaven, like another life-force.
Then, his illusion burned away, the son of <s>Hiḍimbā</s>, shaped like <s>Mandara</s>,
fell with his heart split open and crushed the Kuru army.
When the brave <s>Ghaṭotkaca</s>, equal in valor to the Ten-necked one, was slain,
the delighted <s>Kurus</s> honored <s>Karṇa</s> as equal to <s>Rāma</s>.
Then, when <s>Karṇa</s> was bereft of the spear, the slayer of <s>Kāliya</s> roared,
and, while the <s>Pāṇḍava</s> army was dejected, he danced filled with joy.
As he danced, his arms, with the yellow garment swirling, shone
like trees shaken by the wind, with masses of quivering filaments.
Grieving over the killing of the son of <s>Hiḍimbā</s>, <s>Pārtha</s> reproached him and said:
'What is this delight of yours at a time for grief, <s>Janārdana</s>?'
Hearing this, <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> said, '<s>Karṇa</s> is conquered now, my friend.
The life of the son of <s>Hiḍimbā</s>, whose mind was made restless by anxiety,
and the spear from <s>Karṇa</s>'s staff-like arm have gone together for your victory.
<s>Ekalavya</s>, <s>Jarāsaṃdha</s>, <s>Śiśupāla</s>, and the others
were formerly slain by me with my powers, since I knew of this battle in advance.
In just this way, <s>Karṇa</s> in battle could not be conquered even by the gods;
how much less, O <s>Pārtha</s>, when he had the terrible spear given by <s>Vāsava</s>?
Though constantly deluded by me, <s>Karṇa</s> did not release the spear at you,
even though he was urged on every night by the wicked <s>Kauravas</s>.'
When the <s>Dāśārha</s> had spoken thus, tormented by the accomplished killing of the hero,
the <s>Kurus</s> and <s>Pāṇḍavas</s>, blinded by anger, fought without distinction.
When the son of <s>Hiḍimbā</s> had been slain, King <s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s>, scorched by grief,
though consoled by <s>Keśava</s>, angrily rushed upon <s>Karṇa</s>.
Followed by all the kings, he entered the Kuru army.
Approaching him, lord <s>Vyāsa</s> addressed <s>Dharmarāja</s>:
'Fortunately the world has not been made Arjuna-less by the son of <s>Adhiratha</s> with his spear.
Now, hero, fight without fury and without agitation.
Four days from now the kings will be no more.

children.text: dharmavīra tyaja krodhaṃ sadā dharmānugo jayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: O hero of <s>dharma</s> (righteous order), abandon anger; victory always follows <s>dharma</s>.'
When <s>Vyāsa</s> had spoken thus and disappeared, <s>Bhīma</s>, <s>Arjuna</s>, and <s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s>
made terrible battle with <s>Droṇa</s>, <s>Karṇa</s>, <s>Kṛpa</s>, and the others.
That death-night of heroes was a festival for yakṣas and rākṣasas;
though it had three watches, for the rulers it became as though it had a thousand watches.
Then, when the army was overcome with sleep and the wounds made by weapons had grown quiet,
the white-horsed one, treasure-house of fame, saw it and spoke out of compassion:
'At this lightless moment all the great chariot-warriors are exhausted;
let them take rest for a moment, their eyes closed by sleep.'
When this was said, all the soldiers, praising <s>Dhanaṃjaya</s>,
seated on elephants, chariots, and shoulders, cast off their fatigue for a moment.
With chariots, elephants, and horses motionless, and parasols and chowries still,
those armies became unmoving, their soldiers' weapons laid in their laps.
Then the moon rose: the ivory hilt of the sky's sword-belt, a swan on the river of radiance,
a conch at the ear of the elephant that is the world, splendid as the ornamenting mirror of the women of the quarters.
Then, for all the heroes who had fallen facing battle,
the cool-rayed one filled heaven with his rays as though with their fame.
With the frost-necklace-bright rays of the nectar-shining moon,
the kings for a moment seemed to be fanned, as if with chowries.
The moon sprouted upon the arrows and thickly put forth shoots upon the swords;
it blossomed upon the kings' necklaces and bore fruit upon the conches.
Reflected in the rivers of blood, the moon
shone with a reeling red radiance, as if from the liquor of twilight.
Then, when the time of night had waned and the army was consumptive like a king with wasting disease,
the blessed lord of day rose, copper-red with blood.
