Tormented by the barbed words of <s>Duryodhana</s>, the pot-born one,
then in anger burned even those who did not know weapons with divine missiles.
When battle began again, without limit, in a destruction of the world,
there was a great tumult of joy among those being slain by <s>Droṇa</s>.
At that untimely end of an age, the sky-goers said,
"Is <s>Rudra</s>, in this body, preparing to destroy the worlds?"
The heroes of the <s>Cedis</s>, <s>Somakas</s>, <s>Pāñcālas</s>, <s>Matsyas</s>, <s>Kekayas</s>, and <s>Sṛñjayas</s>,

children.text: na śarma lebhire vīrāḥ pīḍitā droṇasāyakaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: oppressed by <s>Droṇa</s>'s arrows, found no safety.
Then <s>Virāṭa</s> and <s>Drupada</s>, covering <s>Bhāradvāja</s> with sharp arrows,

children.text: saṃchādya cakratuḥ kṣipraṃ vismayaṃ tava dhanvinām ||
children.translated_text: quickly caused amazement among your bowmen.
But then <s>Droṇa</s>, having killed the sons of <s>Pṛṣata</s>, men of vast valor,
cut away the necks of <s>Virāṭa</s> and <s>Drupada</s> alike with two broad-headed arrows.
When the armies of the <s>Matsyas</s> and <s>Pāñcālas</s> were broken, the son of the wind
rushed upon <s>Droṇa</s>'s division together with <s>Dhṛṣṭadyumna</s> and the others.
Then <s>Karṇa</s>, <s>Saubala</s>, <s>Hārdikya</s>, <s>Duḥśāsana</s>, and the others
fought <s>Bhīma</s>, the son of <s>Pṛṣata</s>, <s>Saineya</s>, <s>Phalguna</s>, and the rest.
In that furious clash of all the heroes,
there came a river of surging, waving gore, garlanded with billows.
Seeing <s>Droṇa</s> making slaughter of the <s>Pāñcālas</s>, <s>Cedis</s>, and <s>Matsyas</s> in battle,
the enemy of <s>Kaṃsa</s> spoke to the son of <s>Pāṇḍu</s>.
"This disciple of <s>Jāmadagnya</s> has become a great fire for the kṣatriyas,
with flames of divine missiles impossible to endure; who among us can withstand him?
The armed guru, fighting with his whole being, is unconquerable;
I think he has set out this very day to make the world devoid of <s>Pāṇḍavas</s>.

children.text: putraṃ tu nihataṃ śrutvā dhruvameṣa na yotsyate
children.translated_text: But when he hears that his son has been slain, surely he will not fight.
Therefore, resorting to stratagem, let policy for victory be established."
Hearing this, while <s>Arjuna</s> stood with his ears covered and his face cast down,
and while the Pāṇḍava king was mute, having somehow consented,
<s>Bhīma</s>, having killed with his mace a rutting elephant named <s>Aśvatthāman</s>,
loudly made <s>Droṇa</s> hear before him that his son had been killed.
Though the deeply unpleasant statement was uttered by the ashamed <s>Bhīma</s>,

children.text: durjayaṃ tanayaṃ matvā droṇo mene na tattathā ||
children.translated_text: <s>Droṇa</s>, thinking his son hard to conquer, did not believe that it was so.
Then, entering among the <s>Pāñcālas</s> with the desire to kill <s>Dhṛṣṭadyumna</s>,
he slew sixty thousand chariots of heroic warriors.
With a brahmāstra, <s>Droṇa</s>, of terrible valor,
angrily burned tens of thousands of <s>Cedis</s>, <s>Pāñcālas</s>, and <s>Matsyas</s>, like another <s>Rudra</s>.
Slaying brave <s>Prabhadrakas</s> and attacking <s>Somakas</s>,
he moved about, out of pride, like a youth of four hundred years.
Then the seers approached him as he was committing deeds most cruel
and restrained him from that dreadful massacre of world-destruction.

children.text: munisaṃghe gate vyomnā droṇo bhīmavacaḥ smaran
children.translated_text: When the company of sages had gone through the sky, <s>Droṇa</s>, remembering <s>Bhīma</s>'s words,
with doubtful mind asked truthful and valiant <s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s>.
Earnestly urged by <s>Govinda</s> for the pacification of world-destruction,
<s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s> said that very thing, and softly added, "the elephant."
The horses that had carried <s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s> without touching the earth
at once became earth-going, made heavy by untruth.
Then, as if pierced in his vital places by poisoned nārāca arrows,
<s>Droṇa</s>, having resolved on his own death, became like a painted figure.
To him <s>Dhṛṣṭadyumna</s>, his tongue like a blazing flame, quickly said:

children.text: aho nu brāhmaṇo bhūtvā piśitāśīva niṣkṛpaḥ
children.translated_text: "Ah! Though you are a brahmin, like a flesh-eater, without pity,

children.text: karoṣi kaluṣaṃ karma nihate 'pi priye sute ||
children.translated_text: you commit a stained deed even when your beloved son has been slain."

children.text: tacchrutvā sahasā droṇastyaktvā cāpaṃ saha krudhā
children.translated_text: Hearing that, <s>Droṇa</s> suddenly abandoned his bow along with his anger,
granted fearlessness to all, became silent, and beheld the inner light.
From the fall of the three coverings of his aggregate of six sheaths,
the light, issuing from the aperture of <s>Brahman</s>, entered the sky.
Meanwhile <s>Dhṛṣṭadyumna</s>, dragging him by the hair,
blinded by anger and agitated, though restrained by the sons of <s>Pāṇḍu</s>,
cut off with his sword the head of the guru, whose weapon had been withdrawn
and whose splendor had passed into its abode, while all the kings cried shame.
When the heroic guru of all bowmen, whose chariot was golden, had been slain,
all the great chariot-warriors of the <s>Kauravas</s>, bewildered, fled.
Seeing the Kuru army broken, the son of <s>Droṇa</s>, anxious,
asked the tear-eyed <s>Suyodhana</s>, "What is this?"
When he, with face downcast from grief, was unable to speak the dreadful news,
<s>Gautama</s>, prompted by him, reported to him the killing of his father.

children.text: śrutvā sa vaiśasaṃ ghoraṃ chadmanā vihitaṃ gurau
children.translated_text: Hearing of that dreadful atrocity done by deceit against the guru,
by the cruel <s>Pāñcālya</s>, he blazed up with the fire of anger.
As he breathed hard from fury, like Death wishing to burn everything,
his rage became exceedingly terrifying to all beings.
Grinding hand against hand, he said with tear-filled eyes,
"Ah, even my father was subjected to seizure by the hair.
Having caused the guru to be killed, that lying king, acting like a heron,

children.text: mayi jīvati kaunteyaḥ kathaṃ prāpsyati medinīm ||
children.translated_text: how will <s>Kaunteya</s> obtain the earth while I am alive?"
Today, when the sons of <s>Pāṇḍu</s>, together with their king, have been burned by my anger,
the heroes will remember <s>Bhārgava</s>, the destroyer of kṣatriya lineages.
Today, making <s>Pārṣata</s> a victim offered to the fire of my wrath,
I am set on making the earth empty of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> and <s>Pārtha</s>.
Long ago my father gave me a weapon declared by <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>.
With that, let the sky-roamers today behold the worlds destroyed by me.

children.text: ityuktvā saṃdadhe dīptaṃ tadastraṃ niyataḥ śuciḥ
children.translated_text: Having spoken thus, restrained and purified, he fitted that blazing weapon,
by which the three worlds trembled, wavering like leaves of an aśvattha tree.
Then <s>Drauṇi</s> roared with a sound like the ocean churned by Mount <s>Mandara</s>,
so that all the quarters seemed to break into fragments.
Then, seeing his own army distressed, <s>Śvetavāhana</s>,
breathing hard and troubled with remorse, said to the son of <s>Dharma</s>:
"The guru has been slain by a disciple, through deceit and from greed for power."
While the son of the lord of the gods was loud with such lamentation over the guru,
the son of the Wind, his eyes copper-red with anger, spoke:
"Surely, <s>Pārtha</s>, as a kṣatriya you ought not speak like a sage.
In battle, who takes account of justice toward an enemy who has done terrible harm?
When this heroic arm of mine, devoted to the mace, is here,

children.text: tvayi kṛṣṇe ca kiṃ nāma drauṇiślāghābhinandyate ||
children.translated_text: and when you and <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> are here, why should <s>Drauṇi</s>'s boasting be applauded?"
When <s>Bhīmasena</s> had spoken thus, <s>Pārṣata</s> said to <s>Arjuna</s>:
"A mere kinsman of brahmins, standing in evil action and bringing about the end of worlds, was killed by me.
He by whom ordinary men without armor were killed with a brahmāstra
was to be slain by every means, like an asura, as a thorn to the universe.

children.text: tvayā hataḥ kathaṃ bhīṣmaḥ sa ca prāgjyotiṣeśvaraḥ
children.translated_text: How was <s>Bhīṣma</s> killed by you, and likewise that lord of <s>Prāgjyotiṣa</s>,
your father's friend? What use is this? The ways of heroes are hard to fathom."
Hearing <s>Dhṛṣṭadyumna</s>'s words, <s>Arjuna</s>, with a sidelong, crooked glance,
sighed, scorched by anger, and said, "Fie, fie!"
When the son of <s>Dharma</s> bowed his head in shame and the kings had fallen silent,
<s>Sātyaki</s>, burning with anger, addressed <s>Dhṛṣṭadyumna</s>:

children.text: bata pāpa vayaṃ sarve ye gurughnaṃ puraḥ sthitam
children.translated_text: "Alas, sinner, all of us who speak calmly to the killer of the guru
standing before us; you ought to be killed with all effort."
When the <s>Śaineya</s> had spoken thus, the son of <s>Drupada</s> said:

children.text: aho nu paradoṣajño nirdoṣa iva bhāṣase ||
children.translated_text: "Ah, you know another's fault and speak as if you were faultless.
<s>Bhūriśravas</s>, having undertaken a fast to death, his arm cut off by the crowned one,
O cruel man of fallen conduct, by whom other than you was he struck down?
You should not say this, O king; otherwise, with sharp arrows
I shall make you, who will not turn back from arrogance, submit to teachers of discipline."
As those two, speaking thus in fury, were intent on killing each other,
<s>Bhīmasena</s>, with his younger brothers, restrained them at <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>'s word.
Then, after a moment, when the ocean of the <s>Kuru</s> king's army surged around,
the ten directions, covered by the weapon of <s>Droṇa</s>'s son, could not be seen.
By the blazing circles of weapons issuing from the <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> weapon,
the army of the <s>Pāṇḍavas</s>, being slaughtered, was reduced to a few survivors.
In that dreadful slaughter of warriors, filled with hundreds of flames born from clashing weapons,
King <s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s> was terrified.
Looking toward <s>Kirīṭin</s> and those headed by <s>Pārṣata</s>, he said:
"Let everyone flee from here; a great danger has arisen.
<s>Jiṣṇu</s> has adopted neutrality, angered by the death of the guru,
by whom the boy <s>Abhimanyu</s> was deceitfully struck down, though he was only a child, by an elder;
by whom those great chariot-warriors headed by <s>Satyajit</s> were slain,
and who gave divine, impenetrable armor to <s>Duryodhana</s>.

children.text: kriyatāṃ nādhunā yuddhaṃ svasti pārthāya dhīmate
children.translated_text: Let there be no battle now. May wise <s>Pārtha</s> be safe.

children.text: evaṃ vahniṃ pravekṣyāmi drauṇiṃ kālaṃ saheta kaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus I shall enter the fire; who can endure <s>Drauṇi</s>, who is death itself?"
When the king of <s>Dharma</s> had spoken thus, <s>Keśava</s>, raising his arms,
cried aloud to the kings, who were blazing with the weapon's splendor:

children.text: bho bhoḥ śastraṃ parityajya rathebhyo vrajata kṣitim
children.translated_text: "Ho, ho! Abandon your weapons and go down from the chariots to the ground.

children.text: astreṇānena hanyante na viśastrā bhuvi sthitāḥ ||
children.translated_text: By this weapon, those standing unarmed upon the earth are not killed."
As the foe of <s>Kaiṭabha</s> spoke thus with urgent agitation,
<s>Bhīma</s> said to the kings, "You should be fearless.
Here I am, armored, taking up my mace, famed like the appointed time,
risen up to kill <s>Drauṇi</s>; let the <s>Kurus</s> and <s>Pāṇḍavas</s> behold it."
As the son of the Wind came roaring on, <s>Droṇa</s>'s son,
laughing and saying, "This man is a fool," filled him with nets of arrows.
Then, as they were being burned on every side by the <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> weapon,
the kings descended from their mounts and cast their weapons away.
Upon <s>Bhīmasena</s>, standing on his chariot and fighting without confusion,
the circle of the weapon's rows of flame fell together as one mass.
Seeing <s>Bhīma</s> in an instant hidden by a mass of swiftly rushing tongues of fire,
<s>Arjuna</s> released the <s>Vāruṇa</s> weapon.
Struck on all sides by the fires of the <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> weapon, that weapon
was rendered useless in a moment, as if it had not been launched in the sky.
As <s>Vṛkodara</s> remained amid the terrible peril of the great weapon,
the two <s>Kṛṣṇas</s> quickly got down from the chariot and dragged him with their arms.
Taking the hero's weapon by force and quickly bringing him from the chariot to the ground,
the two heroes, <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> and the <s>Pāṇḍava</s>, wondrously radiant and pleased, stood there.

children.text: astre tataḥ svayaṃ śānte prasanne bhuvanatraye
children.translated_text: Then, when the weapon had subsided of itself and the three worlds were calm,
<s>Duryodhana</s> said to <s>Drauṇi</s>, "Let the weapon be used again."
Having said, "A divine weapon must not be employed twice," the troubled son of <s>Droṇa</s>
brought about the destruction of the <s>Pāñcālas</s>, <s>Matsyas</s>, and <s>Kekayas</s> with his arrows.

children.text: sa sātyakiṃ pārṣataṃ ca jitvā vidrāvya vāhinīm
children.translated_text: After defeating <s>Sātyaki</s> and the <s>Pārṣata</s>, and putting the army to flight,

children.text: jaghāna pauravaṃ vīraṃ rājānaṃ ca sudarśanam ||
children.translated_text: he killed the heroic <s>Paurava</s> and King <s>Sudarśana</s>.
When the armies of <s>Pāṇḍu</s>'s sons were broken, <s>Drauṇi</s> rushed after them,
but <s>Dhanaṃjaya</s> himself, enraged, checked him with showers of arrows.
Then <s>Drauṇi</s>, intent on destruction, brought forth the terrible fiery weapon,
whose sky was ringed with flames, for the ruin of the worlds.
Then all the best of kings, as though covered with golden armor,
fell to the ground, pervaded by the brilliance of the great weapon.
Seeing an <s>akṣauhiṇī</s> burned by that weapon, <s>Dhanaṃjaya</s>, surrounded by fire,
brought forth the fierce <s>brahmāstra</s> in order to pacify it.
When that weapon had vanished and <s>Keśava</s> and <s>Arjuna</s> were released,
the angry son of <s>Droṇa</s>, seeing them, said, "Shame on these weapons!"
Meanwhile there came the sage <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, thousand-rayed with knowledge, a bridge across the boundless ocean of Vedic nectar,
a royal swan on the lake of <s>Sarasvatī</s>'s mind, <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> and yet not dark.

children.text: rathaṃ samutsṛjya tamugrakarmā praṇamya papraccha gurostanūjaḥ
children.translated_text: Leaving his chariot, that man of fierce deeds, the guru's son, bowed to him and asked,
"Blessed lord, why have the divine weapons gone fruitless against <s>Pārtha</s> together with <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>?"
Questioned in this way by him, who was agitated with anger, the lord of sages said to him,
"These two heroes, <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> and <s>Arjuna</s>, are the seers <s>Nara</s> and <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>.
Long ago <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, after practicing austerity for sixty thousand years,
pleased the wielder of the <s>Pināka</s> and obtained equality with him.

children.text: sa eṣa durjayaḥ kṛṣṇaḥ svayaṃ liṅgārcanavrataḥ
children.translated_text: This <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> is unconquerable, himself vowed to the worship of the <s>liṅga</s>.
And you too, <s>Drauṇi</s>, are a portion of <s>Rudra</s>; therefore do not fall into agitation."
Hearing these words of <s>Vyāsa</s>, the guru's son became calm in anger,
bowed in thought to <s>Rudra</s>, and regarded the two <s>Kṛṣṇas</s> as gods.
Then, when the withdrawal of the armies had been arranged by the <s>Kurus</s> and <s>Pāṇḍavas</s>,
<s>Pārtha</s>, turning back from the battle, saw <s>Vyāsa</s> on the road.
Bowing to him, he asked, "Blessed lord, before me in battle
I saw a man with a trident in his hand, blazing with fiery splendor.
From that trident-bearer issued countless shining circles of spears,
and I saw the <s>Kuru</s> army being burned by them on every side.
He was terrible, like another <s>Rudra</s>, touching the earth for half a krośa."
Asked thus by <s>Dhanaṃjaya</s>, the delighted <s>Dvaipāyana</s> replied,
"That god is the enemy of <s>Tripura</s>, the crusher of <s>Gajāsura</s>,
<s>Rudra</s>, burner of Death, able to dissolve the three worlds.

children.text: yaṃ namaskṛtya varadaṃ rājante divi devatāḥ
children.translated_text: The gods in heaven shine after bowing to him, the giver of boons;
with smiling face he once paralyzed the pillar-like arm of <s>Jambhārāti</s>.

children.text: smaraharamasurāriṃ taṃ smara smerakāntiṃ haramajaramajayyaṃ śāśvataṃ viśvarūpam
children.translated_text: Remember him, the destroyer of <s>Smara</s>, enemy of the asuras, <s>Hara</s> of smiling radiance, ageless, unconquered, eternal, of universal form;
the uneven-eyed one, without a superior, tranquil, sovereign, the Lord, whose wall of splendor expands like a garland of young suns;
the destroyer of the solar eye, the breaker of <s>Dakṣa</s>'s consecration, being and non-being, undivided, apprehended by purity of nature;
<s>Śiva</s>, unmoving, inconceivable, crested with the young moon, foremost in the gaming assembly of the mountain-lord's daughter."

children.text: ityāgrahāt paramam āgrahamindrasūnoḥ prītyā vidhāya munimaulimaṇau prayāte
children.translated_text: Thus, when the crest-jewel among sages had lovingly satisfied the deep insistence of <s>Indra</s>'s son and departed,

children.text: bhūpāḥ praviśya śibirāṇi dināvasāne cakruḥ kathāḥ pravaravīrakathānubaddhāḥ ||
children.translated_text: the kings entered their camps at day's end and told stories bound up with the tales of the foremost heroes.
Having bowed to <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> and to <s>Nara</s>, the best of men,
and to the goddess <s>Sarasvatī</s> and <s>Vyāsa</s>, one should then proclaim the <s>Jaya</s>.
When <s>Droṇa</s> had been slain on <s>Kurukṣetra</s>, <s>Saṃjaya</s> came again
and reported to the king the astonishing battle of <s>Karṇa</s> and <s>Pārtha</s>.
Then <s>Duryodhana</s>, delighted by <s>Drauṇi</s>'s words, made <s>Karṇa</s>,

children.text: cakre drauṇigirā hṛṣṭaḥ śūraṃ senāsu nāyakam ||
children.translated_text: valiant and endowed with firm resolve, the commander of the armies.
Consecrated with jewel-made pitchers, that treasure-house of fame
became for the <s>Kuru</s> king a shower of nectar upon his hopes.
Having formed the <s>makara</s> battle-array, he stood amid the enemy hosts,
while the alert <s>Pāṇḍavas</s> formed a half-moon array.
Then, when the terrible battle began, crowded with sparks of fire from the clash of weapons and missiles,
a tremendous tumultuous roar arose.
Then <s>Bhīma</s>, mounted on an elephant, in battle killed the king of <s>Kulūta</s>,
who was seated on a fierce, rutting, four-tusked elephant.
Then elephants, pierced by arrows released to the ear and shot from <s>Karṇa</s>'s bow,
fell like mountains whose wings had been cut off.
<s>Pārtha</s>, <s>Sātyaki</s>, the <s>Pāñcālas</s>, the sons of <s>Draupadī</s>, and <s>Śikhaṇḍin</s>,
together with leaders such as <s>Kṛpa</s> and <s>Drauṇi</s>, made that day seem utterly unprecedented.
<s>Pārtha</s>, after slaying the <s>Saṃśaptakas</s>, sent the two brother-kings,
<s>Daṇḍādhāra</s> and <s>Sadaṇḍa</s>, with his arrows to the city of <s>Daṇḍādhāra</s>.
Then the <s>Pāṇḍya</s>, tearing apart the <s>Kuru</s> army of earthly kings,
cut off the heads of fighters with broad-headed arrows whenever he found his mark.
He did not endure rivalry with <s>Bhīṣma</s>, <s>Droṇa</s>, and <s>Arjuna</s>, born from the fever of pride,
for he always considered himself superior in strength.
By that lord of the southern region, whose fame was the smile of <s>Karṇāṭī</s> women,
whose weapon was sharpened by the eyes of <s>Lāṭī</s> women, the army was oppressed with arrows.
By <s>Drauṇi</s>, by the Sūta's son, by <s>Saubala</s>, and by <s>Kṛpa</s>...
Even though she was being restrained, the army of the Kuru king fled.
Approaching him swiftly, <s>Drauṇi</s> found him pouring down arrows like thunderbolts,
and, unconfused, fought him as the foe of <s>Jambha</s> once fought <s>Śambara</s>.
Then <s>Drauṇi</s> cut off his head, a lotus whose bees were his playfully restless eyes,
with its swinging earrings, using a broad-headed arrow.
When the hero named <s>Pāṇḍya</s>, the crest-jewel of kings, had been slain,
the army of <s>Pāṇḍu</s> no longer shone, like night without the moon.
Then, when weapons were deeply embedded and the warriors seemed to drink the showers of missiles,
when the heroes in battle seemed possessed and fought on unchecked,

children.text: miśrībhūteṣu bhūpānāṃ ratheṣu ca gajeṣu ca
children.translated_text: when the kings' chariots and elephants were all mixed together,
and the people had lost sight of one another because of the dense dust,
<s>Nakula</s> slew a great mleccha king, a cruel fighter,
rākṣasa-like in conduct and skilled in every weapon.
In that dense melee, <s>Karṇa</s>, remembering <s>Kuntī</s>'s words,
did not kill truthful and valiant <s>Nakula</s>, though he had come within reach of death.
Then the <s>Pāñcālas</s> and <s>Sṛñjayas</s>, scattered by heroes headed by <s>Karṇa</s>,
found no protection, nor did the Kurus from <s>Arjuna</s> and the others.
When the heroes had been slain, when others were broken, and when standards and chariots had been cut apart,
when foot-soldiers were crushed by close-packed masses of deeply wounded, bleeding elephants,
when the roads were crowded with headless trunks hurled about in an untimely tāṇḍava (wild dance),
and when broad rivers of blood drowned elephants and horses,
then, when only remnants of the armies survived and were exhausted, the <s>Kurus</s> and <s>Pāṇḍavas</s>,
their bows slack, made the withdrawal as the day ended.
Then at dawn, when the two armies were armed and had drawn near each other,
<s>Karṇa</s>, looking over the army of <s>Pāṇḍu</s>, spoke to <s>Duryodhana</s>:
"Today I shall become free from debt toward your favor and affection,
and toward the honor and wealth you gave me; in battle I shall reach satisfaction.
Today, by killing the wielder of <s>Gāṇḍīva</s>, the very essence of your enemies,
I shall make fruitful this long-cherished resolve of yours.
For good men, praising their own virtues is blameworthy in every way in this world;
yet, when the time for action has come, people do not praise muteness.
I surpass <s>Pārtha</s> in knowledge and in valor;
this much alone is his advantage, that priceless <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> is his charioteer.
<s>Śalya</s> is known to all kings as superior to <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>;
with him as charioteer I am confident I can conquer <s>Jiṣṇu</s>."
When the son of <s>Vikartana</s> had spoken thus, the delighted king <s>Suyodhana</s>
approached the king of <s>Madra</s> and humbly said the same thing.
Then the lord of <s>Madra</s>, angry, his garment disordered by agitation,
looked resentfully at <s>Rādheya</s> and addressed the lord of the <s>Kauravas</s>:
"Ah, king, straightforwardness serves only for insult,
since after long alliance you have spoken of me for service as a charioteer.
Am I not able to kill all the <s>Pāṇḍavas</s> in battle,

children.text: nṛpaṃ māṃ sūtaputrasya sūtaṃ kartuṃ yadicchasi ||
children.translated_text: that you wish to make me, a king, the driver of a sūta's son?"
After he had spoken thus, <s>Śalya</s> suddenly set out with his attendants to kill him;
but the Kuru lord appeased him and began to speak:
"King of <s>Madra</s>, you should not become angry where anger is out of place;
for you are greater than <s>Govinda</s>, and therefore we ask this of you here.
Our foes have appointed <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, who is greater than <s>Arjuna</s>, as his charioteer;
since you are greater than <s>Karṇa</s>, do not be obstinate about serving as charioteer.
Long ago, when the three worlds were troubled by daityas strengthened by boons from <s>Prajāpati</s>,
who dwelt at will in silver, iron, and golden cities,
and when the worlds were being oppressed, the gods, led by <s>Śakra</s>,

children.text: purā pinākinaṃ devaṃ śaṃkaraṃ śaraṇaṃ yayuḥ ||
children.translated_text: went for refuge to the god <s>Śaṅkara</s>, the bearer of <s>Pināka</s>.
Then the lord of the universe, entreated by the gods for the protection of all,

children.text: sarvadevamayaṃ kṛtvā rathaṃ viṣṇuṃ ca sāyakam ||
children.translated_text: made a chariot composed of all the gods and made <s>Viṣṇu</s> his arrow.
Armed for battle, he said to the gods, 'Let a charioteer be arranged for me,
someone whose power exceeds my own, by whose aid I shall slay the dānavas.'

children.text: tataḥ śakramukhā devā vicārya suciraṃ dhiyā
children.translated_text: Then the gods, headed by <s>Śakra</s>, reflected for a very long time with their intelligence,
and appointed <s>Brahmā</s>, maker of the universe, as his charioteer.
When <s>Hara</s>'s chariot had been taken up by him, with the syllable oṃ as the goad,
<s>Hara</s> burned the daityas, united in one city, with the fire of his arrow.
Thus even <s>Dhātā</s> himself once became <s>Rudra</s>'s charioteer;
therefore you too should not show contempt for <s>Karṇa</s>.
The good regard the fulfillment of a friend's affection as the fruit
of lordship, noble birth, virtues, and valor."
When <s>Duryodhana</s> had spoken thus, the king of <s>Madra</s>, smiling,
said, "I shall be a charioteer who speaks as he pleases."
Then, with white horses of his own choosing, like <s>Mātali</s>,
on <s>Karṇa</s>'s beautiful chariot fitted with heated gold,
<s>Śalya</s> lightly took up the well-trained cluster of reins,
like the elder brother of <s>Garuḍa</s> in heaven for the radiant Sun.
Seeing <s>Karṇa</s>, bow in hand and eager to fight, with <s>Śalya</s> as his charioteer,
the Kuru king, together with his followers, thought victory was already in his grasp.
As the Kuru armies roared with the sounds of conches and kettledrums,
<s>Karṇa</s> twanged his bowstring and addressed the king of <s>Madra</s>:

children.text: adya śakraḥ sutaṃ dṛṣṭvā mayā nihatamarjunam
children.translated_text: "Today, seeing his son <s>Arjuna</s> slain by me, <s>Śakra</s>

children.text: divyāstreṣu dṛśaḥ śaṅke sāsūyaṃ kṣipati kṣaṇāt ||
children.translated_text: will, I think, at once cast jealous glances upon the divine weapons.
Today, when <s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s> sees <s>Pārtha</s> split apart by my arrows
while they are grieving over the futility of the effort to kill <s>Bhīṣma</s> and <s>Droṇa</s>.
As <s>Karṇa</s>, the son of <s>Rādhā</s>, was speaking thus, the lord of the <s>Madras</s> said:
"Do not, son of a sūta, make false prattle like a child.
In the former battle with the <s>Gandharvas</s>, when you, wise as you are, had fled,
the <s>Kauravas</s> were protected by that hero of the three worlds.
In that fight over the cattle, when proud men had taken up their weapons,
he suddenly carried off the whole row of garments from men like you.
He defeated <s>Ākhaṇḍala</s> together with his followers in the <s>Khāṇḍava</s> forest.

children.text: taṃ samutsahase jetuṃ karṇa karṇo 'si kiṃ na vā ||
children.translated_text: Do you now dare to conquer him, <s>Karṇa</s>? Are you really <s>Karṇa</s>, or not?
Thus, again and again, <s>Rādheya</s> was suddenly struck by <s>Śalya</s> as if by a dart.
Restraining his anger, he said to him, "You will see."
Then, eager for battle with <s>Savyasācin</s> amid the troops arranged in battle formation,
<s>Karṇa</s>, foremost among the finest chariots, asked the soldiers:
"Where is that enemy of <s>Jayadratha</s>, the hero whose banner bears the monkey?
Without him these arrows of mine are wasting away in their eagerness.
To the man who quickly brings <s>Arjuna</s> into the path of my eyes,
I shall give splendid garments and ornaments,
chariots, rutting elephants, cows, gold, and cities,
lovely women and whatever other wealth he desires."
Hearing this, the king of <s>Madra</s> spoke with mockery:
"<s>Rādheya</s>, laughter born from your conduct may turn into grief.
Like a man about to die, childless, with wealth long accumulated,
why, through delusion and without reflection, do you wish to throw it away among others?
You yourself will see <s>Arjuna</s> coming, like a white-maned beast of prey under control,
and you will be like a frightened deer before the claws of his arrows.
Hearing this, the angered <s>Karṇa</s>, his face darkened by a frown, said:

children.text: nirguṇastvaṃ na jānīṣe na māṃ na ca dhanaṃjayam ||
children.translated_text: "You are worthless; you know neither me nor <s>Dhanañjaya</s>.
I alone know <s>Arjuna</s>, the rival in combat of <s>Pinākin</s>,

children.text: sa ca māṃ vetti tattvena tvaṃ mithyā tu pragalbhase ||
children.translated_text: and he knows me truly; you merely speak bold falsehoods.

children.text: ayaṃ mitropadhiḥ śatruḥ kenāpi preṣito 'si naḥ
children.translated_text: You are an enemy under the guise of a friend. Have you been sent to us by someone?
Or else, since you were born in a vile country, this crookedness of yours is no wonder.
The <s>Madrakas</s> are of contemptible conduct, devoid of truthfulness, character, and straightforwardness;
people in the world who know all the <s>Vedas</s> declare them bereft of honor.
The women of <s>Madra</s> are shameless, going to all men, confused by greed, delusion, and pride;
those ignoble women of <s>Madra</s> are your sisters and mothers."
When the king of <s>Madra</s> had been addressed in fury by <s>Rādheya</s> in this way,

children.text: uvāca mūḍha bahuśo hitamuktaṃ na budhyase ||
children.translated_text: he said, "Fool, though good advice has repeatedly been spoken, you do not understand it.
When your pride has slipped away and you have been defeated by <s>Savyasācin</s>,
you will remember these words of beneficial instruction, grieving and full of regret.
Long ago, on the ocean shore, there lived a very wealthy merchant,
rich in children, protected by the king, and free from disturbance.
The sons of that man had a crow that always ate their leavings,
fat-bodied, intimate with the wealthy boys, and loved like a son.
Then once there arrived swans traveling to <s>Mānasa</s> lake.
Filled with rivalry, the crow said, 'You are not equal to me in speed.',
'I know a full hundred descents, with distinctions of plunging and flying upward.',
'From flights equal to mine and yours, your swiftness will be known.',
Thus the royal swans were challenged by that eater of leavings.
Though summoned, they laughed inwardly and, being noble, said nothing.

children.text: ekastu haṃso jaladhau vrajāva iti saṃvidā
children.translated_text: But one swan, saying by agreement with the crow, 'Let us go over the ocean,'
shot forth with a smiling face like an arrow, together with him.
As the crow went through the sky over the ocean beside that wind-swift bird,
after only half a krośa he became frantic, his wings drooping like hands.
Then, his pride broken, he was set down on the shore by that very compassionate swan.
Spitting blood, after a long time he regained consciousness, having learned the difference between birds.
So too you, <s>Rādheya</s>, surrounded by the <s>Kauravas</s>,
will become bereft of pride when you meet <s>Arjuna</s> in battle."
Hearing this heart-piercing tale told by the king of <s>Madra</s>,
the heroic <s>Vaikartana</s>, though greatly angry, spoke without changing expression:

children.text: yuṣmadvidhānāṃ vacasā jāyate na bhayaṃ mama
children.translated_text: "Fear does not arise in me from the words of men like you.
See <s>Arjuna</s> struck down by me in battle, <s>Śalya</s>.

children.text: lakṣyābhyāse mayā vatsaḥ purā bāṇena dāritaḥ
children.translated_text: Long ago, while practicing at a target, a calf was pierced by my arrow,
hidden by a clump of trees, the calf of a twice-born man's homa-cow.
By that curse, my chariot wheel will bring about my end at the last moment.
This is the single weak point in me; otherwise I am hard to conquer.

children.text: tvaṃ tu kevalayānena nṛpeṇa vāhinā vṛtaḥ
children.translated_text: But you, chosen by the king together with the army merely for driving the chariot,

children.text: mayā svayaṃ saṃnikarṣe dvijihvaḥ kuṭilo vṛtaḥ ||
children.translated_text: have been placed by me close at hand, double-tongued and crooked as you are.
You are lord of the ill-conducted <s>Madrakas</s>, dwellers in a sinful land,
devoid of sacred places and proper customs; what more can be said?

children.text: abhakṣyaṃ bhuñjate nityam apātavyaṃ pibanti ye
children.translated_text: Those who constantly eat what should not be eaten and drink what should not be drunk,

children.text: agamyāsu ramante ca te madrāstava bāndhavāḥ ||
children.translated_text: and who consort with women who should not be approached, those <s>Madras</s> are your kinsmen.
Where women are common to all, and twice-born men eat everything,
where the <s>Madras</s> are joined with every sin, there you are king."
When <s>Karṇa</s> had spoken thus, the king of <s>Madra</s> also replied:
"<s>Karṇa</s>, you are king of the <s>Aṅgas</s>, sinners guilty of abandoning their maternal uncles.

children.text: vikrīyante sadā yatra dārāḥ putrāśca mānavaiḥ
children.translated_text: There wives and sons are always sold by men.
Being leader in that country, you do not deserve to speak to me in this way."
When the king of <s>Madra</s> had said this, those horses were urged onward.
as if tearing the earth, as if having grown wings, they flew upward.
Then <s>Jiṣṇu</s>, with white horses and <s>Acyuta</s> as his charioteer, was seen,
ahead of all the armies, intent on destroying the enemy.
Then, when the life-taking battle of the heroes had begun,
and the sound of twanging bows was covered by the blasts of war-drums,
<s>Śalya</s> said to <s>Rādheya</s>, who was eager for battle with <s>Dhanaṃjaya</s>,
"Look at the bearer of the <s>Gāṇḍīva</s> bow, breaking the Kuru army.
These <s>Saṃśaptakas</s>, tormented by hundreds of rows of <s>Pārtha</s>'s arrows,
are staying hidden in the huts made from heaps of slain elephants.
Look: the strings of pearls of the kings whose throats were cut by <s>Arjuna</s>'s arrows
have fallen like garlands of tears from the goddess of fortune.
When this had been said by the lord of <s>Madra</s>, the king said with joy, "Where will <s>Dhanaṃjaya</s> go?
He has come within the range of my arrows."
Then, when the hollow of the world was filled with the arrows of the son of <s>Vikartana</s>,
the <s>Pāṇḍava</s> army trembled like a great forest in the winds.
Again and again making heroes headed by <s>Dhṛṣṭadyumna</s> lose their chariots,
<s>Karṇa</s> slew ten thousand heroes in a moment.
When the army of the <s>Cedis</s>, <s>Māgadhas</s>, and <s>Pāñcālas</s> was broken, <s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s>,
followed by great chariot-warriors, himself rushed against <s>Rādheya</s>.
"Favorite of kings, this is not a battle of words, where you may boast."
Having said this, the son of <s>Dharma</s> filled <s>Karṇa</s> with arrows.
Then <s>Karṇa</s> slew with arrows the king's two great chariot-warrior wheel-guards,

children.text: hatvā śarairunmamātha dhvajaṃ cāpaṃ cakarta ca ||
children.translated_text: tore down his banner, and cut apart his bow.
Then <s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s> hurled a sharp-pointed spear,
terrible as the fang of Death and roaring aloud, at that Vṛtra among charioteers.

children.text: bhittvā vaikartanaḥ śaktiṃ tāṃ ghaṇṭākrandinīṃ muhuḥ
children.translated_text: The son of <s>Vikartana</s>, shattering that bell-shrieking spear again and again,
cut away the king's golden armor with arrows.
For a moment he covered him, whose armor was cut, with swift arrows,
and struck down his horses, white as teeth and with black tails.
Seeing the son of <s>Dharma</s> flee, the angry <s>Vṛkodara</s>
turned <s>Karṇa</s> back with arrows dreadful as thunderbolts.
The heroic younger brothers of <s>Duryodhana</s>, who had come at their brother's command,
<s>Bhīma</s> made, with broad arrows, dwellers in the city of the dead.
<s>Nanda</s>, <s>Upananda</s>, the unconquerable <s>Durdharṣa</s>, <s>Dhanurgrāha</s>, the mighty-armed <s>Mahābhuja</s>,
<s>Jarāsaṃdha</s>, <s>Śrutarvan</s>, <s>Durdina</s>, and <s>Saniṣaṅgin</s>,

children.text: pāśahastaṃ kavacinaṃ krodhaṃ ca sa mahābhujam
children.translated_text: <s>Pāśahasta</s>, <s>Kavacin</s>, and also <s>Krodha</s>, the great-armed one
slew; then, entering the army, he crushed the elephant division.
Then <s>Sātyaki</s>, the <s>Pāñcālas</s>, the sons of <s>Mādrī</s>, and <s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s>
fought those headed by <s>Karṇa</s> in that destruction of excellent warriors.
As the ocean of troops was being split apart by heroes headed by <s>Vṛṣasena</s>,
there arose the fierce sound of the <s>Gāṇḍīva</s>, striking the sky.
When <s>Dhanaṃjaya</s>, having slain all the <s>Saṃśaptakas</s>, turned back,
the Kuru army suddenly seemed to whirl in eddies.
When the circle of kings headed by <s>Suśarman</s> had been broken by <s>Pārtha</s>'s weapons,
<s>Karṇa</s> enacted the play of Death among the <s>Pāṇḍava</s> forces.
Having slain seven tens of thousands of powerful lordly elephants,

children.text: tāvantyeva rathānāṃ ca cakre bhūmibhujāṃ kṣayam ||
children.translated_text: and just as many chariots, he brought destruction upon the kings.
He slew <s>Vyāghraketu</s>, <s>Jaya</s>, <s>Śaṅku</s>, <s>Rudra</s>, supreme <s>Ugrāyudha</s>,
<s>Siṃhasena</s>, <s>Rocamāna</s>, <s>Śukta</s>, <s>Citrāyudha</s>, and <s>Hari</s>,
<s>Devāpi</s>, <s>Jiṣṇukarman</s>, <s>Śalabha</s>, and the two <s>Citradaṇḍakas</s>,
and other kings, and he carried out the slaughter of the <s>Pāñcālas</s>.
Then, as they were being slain by <s>Karṇa</s> and split into a thousand pieces,

children.text: babhūva pāṇḍave sainye ghoro vyatikaro navaḥ ||
children.translated_text: a new and terrible confusion arose in the <s>Pāṇḍava</s> army.
By <s>Karṇa</s>, by the son of <s>Droṇa</s>, by <s>Kṛpa</s>, by <s>Kṛtavarman</s>,
by the crowned <s>Arjuna</s>, by the son of <s>Pṛṣata</s>, by the <s>Śaineya</s>, and by <s>Śikhaṇḍin</s>,

children.text: kupitena ca bhīmena te sene pravidārite
children.translated_text: and by the enraged <s>Bhīma</s>, the two armies, thoroughly torn apart,
became scattered, their armor and weapons shattered.
<s>Phalguṇa</s>, with a divine weapon itself, conquered <s>Drauṇi</s>, who was raining divine weapons,
and saw the great chariot-warriors being slain by <s>Karṇa</s>.
Astonished at <s>Karṇa</s>'s valor, the enemy of <s>Madhu</s> said to him,
"Look, son of <s>Kuntī</s>, at the army burned by the fire of <s>Karṇa</s>'s weapons.
Look: the son of the charioteer has been marked by the glance of Death,
when, swollen with pride, he looked at me with a sidelong glance as I served as charioteer.

children.text: kṣaṇena nikhilāṃ syūtāṃ tāṃ senāṃ kurute nṛpaḥ
children.translated_text: In a moment this king makes that whole army pierced through;
look at the quarters covered without a gap by his net of arrows."
Having said this, <s>Keśava</s> quickly, with his deep-roaring chariot,
brought the son of <s>Śakra</s> near the chariot of <s>Bhīmasena</s>.
Then, from <s>Bhīma</s>'s words, <s>Dhanaṃjaya</s> thought of <s>Dharmarāja</s>,
who, pierced by <s>Karṇa</s>'s arrows, had slowly gone to the camp.
Sighing, deeply distressed, like a lion struck by the palm,
he went with the foe of <s>Kāliya</s> to see his brother.
He saw the son of <s>Dharma</s> lying there, pierced by arrows
with golden feathers, marked with <s>Karṇa</s>'s name, his armor cut apart.
<s>Keśava</s> and <s>Arjuna</s>, having bowed to his feet and sat down,
remained for a moment distraught, their bodies scorched by anxiety.
<s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s>, thinking that he had come after killing <s>Karṇa</s>,
rose, freed from pain, joyful, and filled with vast wonder at the victory.
"By the fire of whose weapons our armies have for the most part been utterly destroyed

children.text: sa diṣṭyā samare pārtha tvayā karṇo nipātitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: "By good fortune, O <s>Pārtha</s>, <s>Karṇa</s> has been felled by you in battle.

children.text: vīrāḥ sa vidviṣāṃ hantā dhaureyaḥ sarvadhanvinām
children.translated_text: That hero, the slayer of his enemies, the leader of all bowmen,
the pupil of <s>Rāma</s>, <s>Vaikartana</s>: tell me, how was he killed by you?"
Thus questioned by the king, <s>Śvetavāhana</s> replied:
"While I was fighting for a long time with <s>Drauṇi</s>, whose splendor was like <s>Rudra</s>'s,
and with the <s>Saṃśaptakas</s>, an obstruction arose to my felling of <s>Karṇa</s>.
Having stationed mighty-armed <s>Bhīmasena</s> against the opposing army,
I came, O lord, to see you, wounded by blows.
Now, with your permission, I shall make the refuge of the <s>Kauravas</s>,
<s>Karṇa</s>, remain only as a story, with arrows drawn back to the ears."
As <s>Bībhatsu</s> spoke thus, he was pained by his frustrated intention,
and <s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s>, covered with arrows and heated with anger, said:
"Having laid a huge burden upon <s>Bhīmasena</s>, O bowman,
you have gone away after seeing <s>Karṇa</s>'s true valor.

children.text: mithyaiva kuntyā garbhe tvaṃ kṣatriyavyañjano dhṛtaḥ ||
children.translated_text: It was falsely indeed that you, only the semblance of a kṣatriya, were borne in <s>Kuntī</s>'s womb,
like a straw arrow, merely filling out the number of sons.
For thirteen years hopes concerning you have been formed,
and all have gone to futility, like favors bestowed on a base man.

children.text: ka eva nāma jānīte karṇādbhīto dhanaṃjayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Who indeed would have known that <s>Dhanaṃjaya</s>, frightened by <s>Karṇa</s>,
would depart from battle, though bound to such a rule?
Give this <s>Gāṇḍīva</s> to some man of heroic power,
who will remove from us the terror of <s>Karṇa</s> in battle."
Hearing this, <s>Bībhatsu</s> was as if struck in his vital spots,

children.text: etadgirā dadau khaḍge kruddhaḥ sāśrulavā dṛśaḥ
children.translated_text: and, angry, with tears in his eyes, he put his hand to his sword.

children.text: taṃ kopasaṃkaṭo ghore duḥkhāgnau ca nirantare ||
children.translated_text: Seeing him fallen into the dreadful constriction of anger
and into an unceasing fire of grief, all-pervading <s>Govinda</s> addressed him:

children.text: jāne te hṛdgataṃ pārtha yena dolāyase muhuḥ ||
children.translated_text: "I know what is in your heart, O <s>Pārtha</s>, by which you waver again and again.

children.text: gāṇḍīvaṃ vitarānyasmai tvāṃ brūyādyaḥ sa te dhruvam
children.translated_text: Whoever should say to you, 'Give the <s>Gāṇḍīva</s> to another,' that man for you is surely
to be killed: such, O man of proper conduct, is your famous vow.

children.text: tadarthamasi kopāndho nihantuṃ kiṃ svid agrajam
children.translated_text: For that reason, blinded by anger, are you about to kill your elder brother?
Or, from fear of breaking your vow, do you look at the sword against yourself?
Listen: in this matter you are bewildered by truth alone.
Firm in a vow of mere truth, you do not know <s>dharma</s> and <s>adharma</s>.
Sometimes falsehood becomes <s>dharma</s>, and truth becomes <s>adharma</s>,
because of a difference in action; wise men must examine that with understanding.

children.text: dharmo 'pi gahanaḥ sūkṣmo jñāyate na yathā tathā
children.translated_text: Even <s>dharma</s> is deep and subtle, and is not known in just any way.

children.text: purā babhūva vipine balāko nāma lubdhakaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Long ago, in a forest, there was a hunter named <s>Balāka</s>.
Once, when a dreadful creature was destroying herds of cattle and groups of brahmins,
he suddenly killed it with an arrow and attained the world of <s>Śakra</s>.
Formerly there was a brahmin named <s>Kauśika</s>, who had made a vow of speaking truth.
Asked by bandits where some wealthy men who had fled had gone,
he, truthful in speech, pointed out those men, who were refuges of virtue and compassion.
After seeing them, the bandits quickly killed them out of desire for their wealth.
And <s>Kauśika</s> too, in time, fell and went to hell.
Thus, O <s>Pārtha</s>, the working of truth and <s>dharma</s> is profound.
Therefore, with regard to your elder brother the king, <s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s>, steadfast in <s>dharma</s>,
you ought not, through delusion, to think anything improper."
Hearing this, <s>Pārtha</s> drew his sword and was intent on killing himself;
to him, pierced by the breaking of his vow, <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> spoke again:
"A guru is in every way killed by insult,
and oneself is killed by self-praise in an assembly of elders.
Protect your vow and cast off the ignorance born of anger.
Therefore, for this killing today, desist, O <s>Phalguṇa</s>."
When the <s>Dāśārha</s> had spoken thus, <s>Dhanaṃjaya</s> said, 'So be it,'
and said to <s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s>, "You are cowardly, careless, and cruel."
"All the assembled <s>Daityas</s> and <s>Dānavas</s> were slain by me alone;
I am the foremost of bowmen," he said of himself as well.
Then, when the son of <s>Dharma</s>, in grief, was about to go to the forest,
<s>Hari</s> carefully pacified him, taking hold of his feet.
And <s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s>, with tears in his eyes, restrained <s>Pārtha</s>, who had fallen at his feet,
embracing him tightly, while his flood of anger melted away.
Then, after performing purification, the two heroes, <s>Dharmarāja</s> and <s>Dhanaṃjaya</s>,
mounted their chariots, armed, and went to the battlefield.
Then, with kings whose faces had been cut off by volleys of <s>Arjuna</s>'s arrows

children.text: kṣaṇaṃ babhūva patitaiḥ sā kabandhamayīva bhūḥ ||
children.translated_text: and had fallen, for a moment the earth seemed filled with headless trunks.
Meanwhile <s>Bhīmasena</s>, after killing <s>Duryodhana</s>'s younger brothers,
came upon <s>Duḥśāsana</s>, who was fighting with terrible might.
Crushing his chariot with his mace, together with its horses, weapons, and standard,
the husband of <s>Hiḍimbā</s> forcibly dragged him away, shattered, in battle.
Then <s>Vṛkodara</s>, remembering the terrible humiliation of his beloved,
possessed by a rage like that of a rākṣasa, drank the warm blood.
Seeing that dreadful deed of <s>Bhīma</s>, all the great chariot-warriors,
terrified, with swords and bows slipping down and eyes closed, trembled.
Proud in the streaming blood, his cheeks and face bristling, made utterly unrestrained by frenzy, his sequence of steps staggering,
the son of the Wind shone, his fearsome bright mace whirling in terrifying flourish, his mind intent on binding his beloved's hair.
And when <s>Duḥśāsana</s> too had been slain by that unprecedented manner,
even the bodies of great beings bristled with horripilation.
Meanwhile, in the army of the <s>Pāṇḍavas</s>, tormented by <s>Vṛṣasena</s>'s arrows,
there arose the din of elephants and horses falling down.
Even the gathered kings, protected by <s>Bhīma</s> and <s>Sātyaki</s>,

children.text: na sehire raṇe dīptaṃ karṇasūnoḥ parākramam ||
children.translated_text: could not withstand in battle the blazing valor of <s>Karṇa</s>'s son.
He fought <s>Sātyaki</s>, <s>Bhīmasena</s>, the two sons of <s>Mādrī</s>, the crowned <s>Arjuna</s>,
<s>Dhṛṣṭadyumna</s>, and other kings, matching each hero.
As though smiling at that astonishing fighter, <s>Arjuna</s>
cut off his arms and his head, beautiful like lotuses.
When <s>Vṛṣasena</s> had been slain in front of <s>Karṇa</s> by the bearer of the <s>Gāṇḍīva</s>,
he remembered, with tearful eyes, <s>Saubhadra</s>, who had been killed by many.
Then, with the fire of anger, whose rising smoke was his frown, fed by the ghee of wrath,
<s>Karṇa</s>, burning within, rushed upon <s>Dhanaṃjaya</s>.
When the battle between those two, rehearsed in hundreds of hopes, had begun,
the sky became crowded with gods and siddhas who had come out of curiosity.
In that battle of <s>Karṇa</s> and <s>Arjuna</s>, while each hoped for the victory of his own son,
a dispute suddenly arose in heaven between the Sun and the lord of the gods.
Asked by the gods, who had taken two sides, <s>Vṛṣāṅka</s> and <s>Kamalodbhava</s>
declared firmly what had long been settled: "Where <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> is, there is victory."
Then the deep-roaring conches of <s>Karṇa</s> and the crowned <s>Arjuna</s>
were blown by <s>Śauri</s> and <s>Śalya</s>, and by them the three worlds shook.
Then <s>Vaikartana</s> sent against the <s>Pāṇḍava</s> showers of arrows
whose pale feather-tips seemed marked by their own fame.
Struck by <s>Pārtha</s>'s banner, <s>Karṇa</s>'s standard trembled,
and one third of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>'s glance entered <s>Śalya</s> like a spear.
Then, as the quarters were continually being filled with <s>Arjuna</s>'s arrows,
the soldiers of the <s>Kauravas</s> stood back beyond the fall of the shafts.
Then the monkey-bannered one cut off the faces of the great chariot-warriors,
the protectors of <s>Rādheya</s>'s chariot, who had been assigned by <s>Duryodhana</s>.
Then <s>Karṇa</s>, unshaken, repeatedly cut apart
the mass of arrows being discharged by the crowned one's hand at the grip of the bow.
Then <s>Bhīma</s> and <s>Acyuta</s>, greatly astonished, said to <s>Pārtha</s>,

children.text: durjayaḥ samare karṇaḥ sthiro yudhyasva phalguṇa ||
children.translated_text: "<s>Karṇa</s> is hard to conquer in battle; stand firm and fight, <s>Phalguṇa</s>.
The fury you had, hero, in the <s>Kairāta</s> encounter, at <s>Khāṇḍava</s>,
or even in the killing of the <s>Kālakeyas</s>, take up now something greater than that."
Hearing this, <s>Vijaya</s>, his bracelets ringing as they shook,
drew the <s>Gāṇḍīva</s> tight and filled the sky with divine weapons.
With the <s>Bhārgava</s> weapon, <s>Karṇa</s> destroyed that shower of weapons from the crowned one,

children.text: taṃ ca bhīmaṃ ca kṛṣṇaṃ ca karṇo bāṇairapūrayat ||
children.translated_text: and filled him, <s>Bhīma</s>, and <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> with arrows.
Then, because of the streams of <s>Karṇa</s>'s arrows and <s>Arjuna</s>'s weapons on every side,
there was a vast slaughter among the armies of the <s>Pāṇḍus</s> and <s>Kauravas</s>.
Then <s>Karṇa</s> launched at <s>Savyasācin</s> a blazing serpent-faced weapon,
terrible with great coils and splendid with scattered sandal paste.
When that serpent had been released, <s>Śalya</s> said to the lord of <s>Aṅga</s>,
"This serpent, sent by you, will not reach <s>Pārtha</s>'s throat.
If you think it fit to be aimed again, <s>Rādheya</s>,
then either you are deaf, or you are always deaf to words meant for <s>Karṇa</s>'s good."
Thus addressed by <s>Śalya</s> in a way that diminished his vigor, the son of the Sun,
pure in resolve, said, "<s>Karṇa</s> does not aim twice."
Seeing that extremely dreadful, fiercely poisonous serpent, fallen from <s>Karṇa</s>'s bow,
rushing down, <s>Hari</s> made his body heavy as <s>Mandara</s>.
Then, when the four horses had gone down to the earth on their knees,
the snake seized the tip of the lowered crown of the crowned <s>Arjuna</s>.
When the piece of the crown fell, laughing loudly with pearls and jewels,
that serpent, cheated and hissing, entered the earth.
Then, piercing <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> and <s>Arjuna</s> with arrows like the staff of Time,
<s>Karṇa</s>, shooting them as far as the ear, roared again and again with laughter.
Then the son of <s>Śakra</s>, in anger, cut apart <s>Karṇa</s>'s armor,
which shone with divine jewels, and filled his body with arrows.

children.text: khāṇḍave kṛtavairaṃ taṃ khaṃ vrajantaṃ mahoragam
children.translated_text: <s>Pārtha</s> cut down with six arrows that great serpent, which had borne enmity from <s>Khāṇḍava</s>,

children.text: chittvā ṣaḍbhiḥ śaraiḥ pārthaḥ karṇaṃ punaratāḍayat ||
children.translated_text: as it was going through the sky, and then struck <s>Karṇa</s> again.
When the <s>Brahmā</s> weapon had been destroyed by <s>Vaikartana</s>, <s>Arjuna</s>
brought forth the <s>Śakra</s> weapon to counter him, crowded with hundreds of thunderbolt-missiles.

children.text: hatvā tamastraṃ rādheyo jyāṃ cicheda kirīṭinaḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Rādheya</s> destroyed that weapon and cut the bowstring of the crowned one,
but in an instant <s>Dhanaṃjaya</s> fitted a new bowstring.
Then <s>Arjuna</s> set upon the bow the <s>Raudra</s> weapon, bristling with masses of blazing flames,
by which the sky became terrible with the dreadful burning of the quarters.
Meanwhile, at that moment, by force of fate, the earth itself
seized the chariot wheel of the king of <s>Aṅga</s> in the battle.
Then, as he was trying to lift up that wheel, standing in distress,

children.text: uvāca karṇaḥ kaunteyaṃ muhūrtaṃ kṣamatāṃ bhavān ||
children.translated_text: <s>Karṇa</s> said to <s>Kaunteya</s>, "Please wait a moment.
When I have lifted this wheel, release your great weapon, <s>Phalguṇa</s>.

children.text: vyasanasthe viśastre ca nahi śūrā bhavādṛśaḥ ||
children.translated_text: For heroes like you do not strike one who is in difficulty and without a weapon."
Hearing this, the destroyer of <s>Kāliya</s>, laughing, said to <s>Karṇa</s>,

children.text: diṣṭyādya karṇa jānīṣe dharmaṃ vīravrate sthitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: "By good fortune, <s>Karṇa</s>, today you know <s>dharma</s> (righteous order), established in a hero's vow.

children.text: bahubhirnihato bālaḥ saubhadraḥ kiṃ nu vismṛtaḥ
children.translated_text: Have you forgotten how the boy <s>Saubhadra</s> was killed by many?
Count also that which you said to <s>Kṛṣṇā</s> in the assembly.
In the acts of giving poison and fire, you, whose <s>dharma</s> had been cut away, remembered it then;
surely the courses of <s>dharma</s> belong to base kings only when they are in distress.
When <s>Janārdana</s> had spoken thus, <s>Vijaya</s>, as if blazing with anger,
destroyed the brahmāstra prepared by <s>Karṇa</s> with a brahmāstra.
The king of <s>Aṅga</s> countered the fiery missile released by <s>Arjuna</s> with a watery one;
having checked weapon with weapon, he halted, his wheel swallowed up.
Then the son of <s>Akhaṇḍala</s> tore away with an arrow <s>Karṇa</s>'s standard, shining with gold,
like his lofty desire itself.
Then, taking up the añjalika arrow, adorned with gold,
he consecrated and drew it, its black mouth like the fang of death.
"If <s>Rudra</s> and the other teachers of weapons are pleased by my austerity,
then may I strike down my enemy with this," said <s>Arjuna</s>, and he released it.
At once pierced by it in the throat adorned with a necklace,
<s>Rādheya</s> fell like a golden palm tree cut down by a saw.
When <s>Karṇa</s>, the bearer of the burden among bowmen and leader of the <s>Kaurava</s> army, was slain,
<s>Śalya</s> quickly went away, planting a barb in their hearts and faces.
Seeing the king of <s>Madra</s> arrive in an empty chariot,
the kings said, "<s>Duryodhana</s> is slain; <s>Karṇa</s> lives."
When the king of <s>Aṅga</s> had fallen under <s>Arjuna</s>'s arrows,
<s>Duryodhana</s>, his senses stunned, knew nothing, like a body without its head.
Then a radiance, with trembling rays, rose from <s>Karṇa</s>'s body and entered the disk of the sun;
because of it, for a moment the sky became crowded with flame-clusters, while the heavenly cars were scattered through its spaces.
Having bowed to <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, and also to <s>Nara</s>, the best of men,
to the goddess <s>Sarasvatī</s> and to <s>Vyāsa</s>, then one should proclaim the victory.

children.text: evaṃ jambha ivendreṇa hate karṇe kirīṭinā
children.translated_text: Thus, when <s>Karṇa</s> had been slain by the diademed one, as <s>Jambha</s> was by <s>Indra</s>,
<s>Saṃjaya</s>, returning once more, reported the battle to the king.
"O king, when <s>Vaikartana</s> was slain, the crest-jewel of all heroes, the wish-granting tree of petitioners,
the maker of night for every hope,
and when his own life, as it were, had gone somewhere away with him,

children.text: duryodhano nirucchvāso mene śūnyā diśo daśa ||
children.translated_text: <s>Duryodhana</s>, distraught and breathless, thought the ten directions empty.
He moved among the chariot-warriors, eager to fight the <s>Pāṇḍavas</s>,
like a man gone to the other world in another body.

children.text: tato drauṇigirā kṛtvā śalyaṃ senāpatiṃ nṛpaḥ
children.translated_text: Then, at <s>Drauṇi</s>'s word, the king made <s>Śalya</s> commander of the army,
and for the sake of the kingdom he entered battle, the abode of the gods.
There were then ten thousand chariots, with some additional ones, and just as many elephants,

children.text: lakṣyadvayaṃ dvayānāṃ ca tisraḥ koṭyaḥ padātinām ||
children.translated_text: two hundred thousand of the two-horse divisions, and thirty million foot-soldiers.
This was the remainder of the <s>Kuru</s> king's army in the battle;
and the force remaining after slaughter among the <s>Pāṇḍavas</s> was half of that.
In that dreadful battle, that arena of the destruction of kings,
where foot-soldiers, chariots, and elephants rolled in the mud of brains,
where lotus-like faces were scattered, and broken chariot-wheels were like waterfowl,
where flocks of royal swans had fallen loose, and fragments of swords were confused with lotuses,
where the remaining gore was slippery with the mire of hair like water-weeds,
it was as if a lake had been churned by the elephant of untimely death.
Marked by the drooping ears of excellent horses, covered with broken bows,
and quivering with pieces like plantain trunks, it was like a forest struck by thunderbolts.
Filled with limbs like blue lotuses, and made manifest by the wine of powerful spears,
it was like the garden of <s>Kāla</s>, crowded with skull-cups.
When the battle began again, <s>Śalya</s>, <s>Hārdikya</s>, <s>Saubala</s>,
<s>Kṛpa</s>, <s>Drauṇi</s>, and <s>Suyodhana</s> entered the <s>Pāṇḍava</s> army.
<s>Pārtha</s>, the <s>Pārṣata</s>, the <s>Śaineya</s>, the sons of <s>Draupadī</s>, and <s>Śikhaṇḍin</s>
struck down the forces of the <s>Trigartas</s>, the <s>Gāndhāras</s>, and <s>Kapinātha</s>.
In that battle without bounds, the great chariot-warriors, as if intoxicated,
fought terribly in anger, their bands of kinsmen and friends slain.

children.text: satyasenaṃ suṣeṇaṃ ca citrasenaṃ ca karṇajam
children.translated_text: <s>Nakula</s> slew the heroes <s>Satyasena</s>, <s>Suṣeṇa</s>, and <s>Citrasena</s>, sons of <s>Karṇa</s>,
whose valor was equal to <s>Karṇa</s>'s.
Then the <s>Pāṇḍu</s> army, being trampled by mighty <s>Śalya</s>
like a lotus-pond by an elephant, trembled with a roar.
Seeing the army being struck down by <s>Śalya</s>, the barb of his enemies,
<s>Bhīma</s>, mace in hand and terrible in anger, rushed upon him.

children.text: sa hatvā gadayā tasya rathaṃ rathaśatacchidaḥ
children.translated_text: With his mace he smashed the chariot of that breaker of a hundred chariots,
and, raising his staff, stood before the one who was about to die, like <s>Kāla</s>.
The king of <s>Madra</s> too, taking up a mace with golden armlets,
fought <s>Bhīma</s> in anger, terrible in strength and lifted up by pride.
Moving in circles, the two rushed against each other
and struck each other with maces whose many blows cast up sparks.
When both of them had fainted and quickly fallen to the ground through stupor,
the <s>Kurus</s> and <s>Pāṇḍavas</s>, with their followers, rushed up in fury.
When the two suddenly regained consciousness and stood again as before,
the heroes headed by <s>Duryodhana</s> fought those headed by <s>Pārtha</s>.
As the kings fought, longing for the world of <s>Brahmā</s>,
<s>Suyodhana</s> slew <s>Cekitāna</s>, the best of rulers.
Then the enraged king of <s>Madra</s>, alone and by force, held back the sons of <s>Pāṇḍu</s> with their followers,
while he was praised by sky-roaming beings.
Calmly cutting apart with arrows the shower of weapons released by them,
<s>Śalya</s>, in a moment, made them invisible with feathered shafts.
When the army had been covered with a net of arrows by the ruler of <s>Madra</s>,
the enraged son of <s>Dharma</s> slew two thousand chariots.
Seeing his followers slain by the king, <s>Śalya</s>, in battle, then made <s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s>
filled with hundreds of arrows, like an aśoka tree.
When the son of <s>Dharma</s> was afflicted, <s>Nakula</s>, trembling with anger,
and <s>Bhīma</s>, <s>Sātyaki</s>, and the others showered <s>Śalya</s> with arrows.
Then, covering the belly of the world with the darkness of his arrows,
<s>Śalya</s>, roaring like a cloud, tore up the army of the sons of <s>Pṛthā</s>.
In that battle, when all was confused, <s>Jiṣṇu</s> fought with <s>Drauṇi</s>;
<s>Bhīmasena</s> fought <s>Duryodhana</s>, and <s>Nakula</s> fought the son of <s>Subala</s>.
Then <s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s>, against <s>Śalya</s>, whose kings had all been destroyed,
cutting away all his weapons, reduced his chariot to bits.
Mounting another chariot, the king of the <s>Madras</s>, blazing with anger,
left the son of <s>Dharma</s> with his bow, chariot, and banner cut away.
Then <s>Bhīmasena</s>, seeing the king bewildered and without a chariot,
cut apart the chariot of the <s>Madra</s> king, together with all its weapons.
Then <s>Śalya</s>, sword in hand, slaying chariots and elephants,
moved about with unseen body, in courses like the stride of <s>Garuḍa</s>.
Then, wrapped with a blazing red band,
inlaid with glittering jewels, like the row of teeth of Death,
as if saying, "The Kuru army has this as its end; whence could there be such a battle?"
crying out through its clusters of bells, with a thunderbolt's sound,
<s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s>, best of the powerful, with the valor of <s>Ṣaṇmukha</s>, hurled the blazing thousand-slaying
spear at the <s>Madra</s> king.

children.text: sa tayā bhinnahṛdayaḥ papāta kṣmābhṛtāṃ varaḥ
children.translated_text: With his heart split by it, that best of earth-lords fell,
streams of blood pouring from the openings of his ears, nose, and mouth.
When <s>Śalya</s> was slain, the last support of the <s>Kauravas</s>' hope was gone,
and all their chariot-warriors fled, their pride and wishes shattered.
Then <s>Śalya</s>'s younger brother, angry and named <s>Vicitrakavaca</s>,
advanced against <s>Dharmarāja</s>, who was tearing open the army.
As he rained arrows, the son of <s>Dharma</s> cut off his head, shining with bright variegated jewels,
like the lofty peak of <s>Rohaṇa</s> mountain.
When he was slain, the bannered army was breaking and had no protector;
turning back, <s>Kṛpa</s>, <s>Drauṇi</s>, and <s>Hārdikya</s> quickly came on.
With the <s>Cedis</s> and <s>Pāñcālas</s> roaring, having found their targets,
those great chariot-warriors fought for a moment, as though they had become many.
Then, out of wrath at their lord's death, the remaining <s>Madras</s> rushed upon <s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s>;
killing them, he made the earth devoid of <s>Madras</s>.
Then <s>Bhīma</s>, mace in hand and skilled in works of destruction,
crushed all the mlecchas and made the battlefield almost empty.
Then, when the hero <s>Satyarāja</s> had been brought down by <s>Sātyaki</s>,
<s>Duryodhana</s> himself came up and fought the sons of <s>Pāṇḍu</s>.

children.text: na ratho na gajo nāśvo na yodhaḥ pāṇḍaveṣvabhūt
children.translated_text: Among the <s>Pāṇḍavas</s> there was no chariot, no elephant, no horse, no warrior
that was not covered with <s>Duryodhana</s>'s arrows marked with golden names.
The herd of elephants trembled as he showered iron arrows,
again and again with the sharp bowstring sounds and the jingling of jewels and gold.
As <s>Duryodhana</s> fought, while his enemies found their marks,
<s>Drauṇi</s>, <s>Hārdikya</s>, <s>Suśarman</s>, <s>Kṛpa</s>, and the son of <s>Subala</s> came up.
In the dreadful turmoil of battle, as those warriors fell thickly,
the world became lightless when the sun was covered with dust.
In the unbearable dust, able to withstand the blows of great elephants' flanks,
no distinction at all could be made, as if the end of a kalpa had arrived.

children.text: kva drauṇiḥ kva ca gāndhāraḥ kva ca rājā suyodhanaḥ
children.translated_text: "Where is <s>Drauṇi</s>? Where is the <s>Gāndhāra</s>? Where is king <s>Suyodhana</s>?"
Such a great cry arose everywhere in the army of the <s>Pāṇḍus</s>.
At that moment, when the field of sight had passed into a whirl of dissolution,
the son of the Wind killed the remaining younger brothers of <s>Duryodhana</s>.
<s>Mahābāhu</s>, <s>Bhūribala</s>, <s>Jaitra</s>, <s>Durdarśana</s>, <s>Śala</s>,

children.text: sunādaṃ ca sa hatvā tānunnanāda kṣayocitān ||
children.translated_text: and <s>Sunāda</s> too: after killing those fit for destruction, he roared aloud.
Then, in the thinned-out battle, the hero <s>Sātyaki</s> seized me,
saying in haste, "This <s>Sañjaya</s> has been caught by me."
Then <s>Arjuna</s>, after killing <s>Suśarman</s> with his son and his foot-soldier retinue,
made the army of the oath-bound warriors utterly vanish with his arrows.
In that dice-game called battle, casting arrow-dice again and again,
<s>Sahadeva</s>, with a crescent-headed arrow, carried off <s>Śakuni</s>'s head.
After killing <s>Ulūka</s>, his son, the son of <s>Mādrī</s>
slew the army of the <s>Gāndhāras</s>, remembering the period of exile.
Then, when the army had been completely destroyed, weary and bereft of his vehicle,
king <s>Suyodhana</s> withdrew from battle and went away on foot.
In that great battle, with only <s>Kṛtavarman</s>, <s>Kṛpa</s>, and <s>Drauṇi</s> left,
the whole field of beings and ghouls had in a moment gone to extinction.
When, at <s>Dhṛṣṭadyumna</s>'s command, the <s>Śaineya</s> was preparing to kill me,
the venerable <s>Vyāsa</s>, a treasury of compassion, protected me.
Then, at the end of the day, afflicted with grief, I set out toward <s>Suyodhana</s>;
I saw the emperor, hard-hearted as a thunderbolt, going away.
He, walking on foot, saw me, his neck bent crooked with shame,
and said, "<s>Sañjaya</s>, tell the king, my father:

children.text: tena karṇena suhṛdā taiśca vīrairvinā kṛtaḥ
children.translated_text: bereft of that friend <s>Karṇa</s> and of those heroes,
your son, deprived of <s>Duḥśāsana</s> and the others, has entered a lake."
After saying this to me, he stilled the water by daitya magic,
and entered the broad lake, filled with the mature fire of grief.

children.text: taṃ stambhitorusalile sarasi praviṣṭaṃ jñātvā girā mama gurostanayaḥ kṛpaśca
children.translated_text: Knowing from the words of my teacher's son and of <s>Kṛpa</s> that he had entered a lake whose broad waters had been made motionless,
<s>Bhoja</s> too came to him, whose feet had been touched by the crest-jewels of kings and who was the abode of <s>Lakṣmī</s>'s play, and they grieved.

children.text: akṣauhiṇīparivṛto 'tha visṛjya gehaṃ rātrau yuyutsumakhilaiḥ saha rājadāraiḥ
children.translated_text: Then the son of <s>Dharma</s>, surrounded by an <s>akṣauhiṇī</s> battle-array, left his dwelling at night with <s>Yuyutsu</s> and all the royal women,
and together with <s>Dhanaṃjaya</s>, <s>Bhīma</s>, and the others, he pondered over <s>Duryodhana</s> as if over the remainder of a debt.
The rows of moonbeams from the nails of whose lotus feet shone like garlands on the heads of kings,

children.text: so 'pyeka eva kururājasutaḥ padātiryāto dhigasthiravilāsavikāsi daivam ||
children.translated_text: even that son of the <s>Kuru</s> king had gone alone on foot. Fie on fate, blooming in unstable sport!

children.text: yasyā vaśādbata natonnatabhāñji bhāvacakrāṇi hanta viśarārudaśāṃ viśanti
children.translated_text: By whose power, alas, the wheels of conditions, sharing in low and high states, enter a state of ruin,

children.text: saṃkrandanāni yativibhramamudritāni tasyai namo 'stu satataṃ bhavitavyatāyai ||
children.translated_text: to that destiny be constant homage, whose cries of lamentation are stamped with the semblance of ascetic restraint.
Having bowed to <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, and to <s>Nara</s>, the best of men,
to the goddess <s>Sarasvatī</s> and to <s>Vyāsa</s>, then one should proclaim the <s>Jaya</s>.
Then the heroes headed by <s>Drauṇi</s>, three chariot-warriors, came together
and spoke, with words sharp as arrows, to the honor-prizing king who had entered the lake.
"O king, rise up; in battle kill the enemy, O bowman.
Together with us, this is the time for valor, the birthplace of fame."
Hearing this, the lord of the <s>Kurus</s> praised their courage

children.text: ūce prātaḥ samāśvāsya mama kṣatrocitā gatiḥ ||
children.translated_text: and said, "In the morning, once I have recovered, my course will be what befits a <s>kṣatriya</s> warrior."

children.text: iti teṣāṃ samālāpaṃ śrutvā jñātvā suyodhanam
children.translated_text: When the hunters heard this conversation and recognized <s>Suyodhana</s>,
greedy for wealth, they reported it to <s>Bhīmasena</s>.
At <s>Bhīmasena</s>'s word, King <s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s>, together with his army,
accompanied by <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> as foremost among them, swiftly came to that place.
Seeing the sons of <s>Pṛthā</s> arrived with roaring elephant and chariot divisions,
<s>Gautama</s> and the others went away, fearing the disclosure of the king.
Then, at <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>'s word, the son of <s>Dharma</s>, that best of kings,
addressed <s>Suyodhana</s>, who was standing within the water.
"O king, O hero, your fame, beautiful like silver, camphor, and the lord of night,

children.text: aho vīra yaśaḥ śubhraṃ bhavatā malinīkṛtam ||
children.translated_text: pure and bright, has alas been stained by you.
After causing kings, the household-abodes of royal fortune, to be slain in battle,
how, proud man, intent only on protecting your life, are you not ashamed to live?

children.text: uttiṣṭha yuddhe svāṃ lakṣmīṃ tridivaṃ vā samāpnuhi
children.translated_text: Rise up. In battle obtain your own royal fortune, or heaven.

children.text: lābhaḥ samo hi vīrāṇāṃ vijayo nidhanaṃ nu vā ||
children.translated_text: For heroes the gain is the same, whether victory or death."
Hearing this speech of <s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s>, <s>Duryodhana</s>, filled with the poison of anger,
spoke from the water, breathing like an elephant.
"This is just as you say: royal fortune and death are the same to me.

children.text: bandhusvajanahīnā tu lakṣmīḥ kasya manaḥ spṛśet ||
children.translated_text: But whose heart would prosperity touch when it is bereft of relatives and one's own people?
Like an army without heroes, like an assembly without wise men,

children.text: svajanena vinā lakṣmīḥ kasya prīṇāti mānasam ||
children.translated_text: whose mind does prosperity please when it is without one's own people?

children.text: sa karṇaḥ suhṛdāmagryaḥ sa guruḥ sa pitāmahaḥ
children.translated_text: That <s>Karṇa</s>, foremost of friends, that teacher, that grandsire,
without them, ah, what hermitage of what good sage could make one forget?
For those separated from relatives and friends, prosperities are mere mockeries,
like varied garlands of pictured beauty for the blind.
Enjoy the earth once enjoyed by me, now devoid of jewel-like heroes,
like an old woman whose ornaments have been cast off by dispassion."
Hearing this, the son of <s>Pṛthā</s> spoke to the son of <s>Dhṛtarāṣṭra</s>:
"By good fortune, O lord of the earth, you are peaceful and fond of the ascetic grove.

children.text: sūcyagramapi na tyājyaṃ pāṇḍavānprati te bhuvaḥ
children.translated_text: Not even a needle-point of land was to be given up by you to the <s>Pāṇḍavas</s>;
today you wish to give the whole earth. What a marvel!

children.text: uttiṣṭha yuddhamekena tavāstu vijitaḥ sa cet
children.translated_text: Rise up. Let there be combat with one man; if he is defeated by you,

children.text: jitāḥ sarve tvayā rājanmā pralāpaiḥ kṛśo bhava ||
children.translated_text: all have been defeated by you, O king. Do not grow feeble with rambling words."
Hearing this speech of <s>Pārtha</s>, the king rose up in anger,

children.text: sāvalepaṃ vacaḥ śrutvā na sahante hi māninaḥ ||
children.translated_text: for proud men cannot endure speech uttered with contempt.
With golden armlets and mace in hand, like <s>Sumeru</s> furnished with peaks,

children.text: utthitaḥ sa babhau rājā daṇḍadhāra ivāparaḥ ||
children.translated_text: the king, risen up, shone like another bearer of the staff.
At <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>'s word, <s>Vṛkodara</s>, armored and mace in hand,
stood before him, intent on reckoning the insults to <s>Kṛṣṇā</s>.
Meanwhile <s>Haladhara</s>, as the <s>Kurus</s> and <s>Pāṇḍavas</s> were being destroyed,
distressed by fear for the ruin of his kinsmen, had slowly come from a pilgrimage to tīrthas.
Then, coming to <s>Kurukṣetra</s>, he saw those two armed with maces,
watching the battle of his two pupils and as if listening to their words to one another.
Honored by the sons of <s>Pṛthā</s>, headed by <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, he, radiant as a hundred moons,
sat down, clad in blue, like <s>Himavān</s> accompanied by a rain cloud.
Hearing this in the middle of the story, <s>Janamejaya</s>
respectfully asked <s>Vaiśampāyana</s> about the pilgrimage of <s>Halabhṛt</s>.
He said: "When the war of the <s>Kuru</s> and <s>Pāṇḍava</s> kings had begun,
<s>Pralambahā</s>, fearing destruction, took leave of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> and set out.
<s>Rāma</s>, who grants every desire to brahmins, departed under <s>Puṣya</s>,
and, reaching the <s>Sarasvatī</s>, then came to <s>Prabhāsa</s> by way of <s>Śayana</s>.
There <s>Tārā</s>, distressed by the moon-lord whose mind was attached to <s>Rohiṇī</s>,
reported him to her father; by his curse he became wasted away.
When the hare-marked moon was in a moment diminished by consumption because of the curse,
the gods, alarmed by fear of universal destruction, then directed him there.
Laughing, he quickly went to that <s>Prabhāsa</s>, and there too he attained fullness.
There, after bathing at <s>Bhāradvāja</s>, he went on to <s>Tritakūpa</s>.
There, in ancient times, King <s>Trita</s>, neglected by his two brothers,

children.text: sa cakre mānasaṃ yajñaṃ tato devāḥ samabhyayuḥ ||
children.translated_text: performed a mental sacrifice; then the gods came together to him.
Then, by a boon, that well became one that grants the fruit of drinking soma.
At that place on the bank of the <s>Sarasvatī</s>, <s>Rāma</s> bathed reverently.

children.text: tato vinaśanaṃ puṇyaṃ prāpa yatra sarasvatī
children.translated_text: Then he reached the holy <s>Vinaśana</s>, where the <s>Sarasvatī</s>,
hostile to Śūdras, cowards, and poets, disappeared, she who destroys the wicked.
From there the strong one went to <s>Bhūmika</s>, where the companions of the Apsarases,
the divine <s>Gandharvas</s>, sport with the amusements of dancing and song.
He also came to <s>Durgasrotas</s>, the holy <s>Śaṅkha-tīrtha</s>, and <s>Dvaitavana</s>,
and to <s>Nāgadhanvan</s>, where the dwelling of <s>Vāsuki</s> is.

children.text: viveśa naimiṣaṃ rāmo yatra prācī sarasvatī
children.translated_text: <s>Rāma</s> entered <s>Naimiṣa</s>, where the <s>Sarasvatī</s> flows eastward,
and where there is the sight of the sages who dwell in <s>Naimiṣāraṇya</s>.
He went to <s>Saptasārasvata</s>, where the sage <s>Caṅkaṇaka</s>,
seeing vegetable sap flowing from his own limb, began to dance.
As that sage danced violently, the excellent forest with its playmates,
and, through the power of his austerity, the whole world too, began to dance.
Then, entreated by the gods, the Lord came to him, and when he had shown him a wonder,
ashes issued from his own hand, and by that the sage was freed from pride.
Pleased by his praise, the mighty <s>Śaṃkara</s> granted him increase of ascetic power,
and his own presence at the <s>Saptasārasvata-tīrtha</s>.
<s>Bala</s> reached <s>Kapālamocana</s> and the <s>Auśanasa</s> <s>tīrtha</s>,
where the sage <s>Mahodara</s> was freed from a terrible grip on his thigh.
In former times, the head of a demon cut off by the arrows of <s>Rāghava</s>
had, they say, stuck to the thigh of <s>Mahodara</s> and kept crawling there.
Though he had plunged into all the <s>tīrthas</s>, only there did he regain health.
Then, reaching the hermitage of <s>Uttaṅka</s>, he came to <s>Pṛthūdaka</s>.
There, after being defeated by <s>Vasiṣṭha</s>, who had stolen his cow through brahmanical power,
the sage <s>Kauśika</s>, born in the royal warrior line, attained brahmanhood.

children.text: tatra rāmo dadau bhūri dhanaṃ vārṣṇeyanandanaḥ
children.translated_text: There <s>Rāma</s>, delight of the <s>Vārṣṇeyas</s>, gave abundant wealth.
Then, in a grove of the <s>Sarasvatī</s>, where <s>Indra</s>, after killing <s>Namuci</s>,
was afflicted by brahma-slaying and freed, he slowly reached that dreadful place.
Then he reached <s>Soma-tīrtha</s>, where sacrifice had been performed by the nectar-rayed Moon.
There the great Asura named <s>Tāraka</s> had been slain by the six-faced <s>Skanda</s>.
After bathing at <s>Skandābhiṣeka</s>, he then came to <s>Vahni-tīrtha</s>.
There <s>Agni</s>, lost because of <s>Bhṛgu</s>'s curse, became restored and content again.
The elder brother of <s>Acyuta</s> then came to the <s>Kaubera</s>, <s>Indra</s>, and <s>Yāmuna</s> <s>tīrthas</s>.
Having reached the hermitage of <s>Devala</s>, the sage <s>Jaigīṣavya</s>, skilled in true yoga,

children.text: yatra sarvagataṃ brahma devalāya jagau muniḥ ||
children.translated_text: there taught <s>Devala</s> the all-pervading <s>brahman</s>.
Then <s>Halāyudha</s> came to the <s>Sārasvata</s> <s>tīrtha</s>.
There, in former times, from the sight of an Apsaras, semen had fallen into the water.
By that the <s>Sarasvatī</s> obtained a son from the sage <s>Dadhīca</s>.
When the heap of <s>Dadhīca</s>'s bones had become the weapon of great <s>Indra</s>,
during a drought that son, maintained by her with fish as food,
the wise son <s>Sārasvata</s>, remembered the Vedas.
Then, when study had been forgotten by all the foremost sages,
who were wasted by famine, he became their teacher at their request.

children.text: tasmiṃstīrthe balaḥ snātvā yayau yatra purā vapuḥ
children.translated_text: After bathing at that <s>tīrtha</s>, <s>Bala</s> went to the place where, in former times,
<s>Sanatkumārī</s> was intent on abandoning her body through austerity in order to reach heaven.

children.text: nāradaḥ prāha nodvāhaṃ vinā svargo bhavediti
children.translated_text: <s>Nārada</s> said, "Heaven is not attained without marriage."
So she gave her body, to be enjoyed for a day, to the son of <s>Gālava</s>.

children.text: kṛtvā lalitamākāraṃ tridivaṃ ca yayau tataḥ
children.translated_text: Then, making herself into a graceful form, she went to the third heaven.

children.text: tatra snātvā ca dattvā ca plakṣaprasravaṇe tathā ||
children.translated_text: There he bathed and gave gifts, and likewise at <s>Plakṣaprasravaṇa</s>.
Viewing the <s>tīrthas</s> slowly, he reached <s>Kārapavana</s>.
There he heard from <s>Nārada</s> of the destruction of kings at <s>Kurukṣetra</s>.
Then, questioned by <s>Dhṛtarāṣṭra</s>, <s>Sañjaya</s> described the battle
of <s>Bhīmasena</s> and of the proud <s>Kaurava</s>, fought without chariots.
Going on foot to <s>Samantapañcaka</s>, <s>Suyodhana</s>
stood unmoving; in calamity the courage of the great grows still greater.
Then <s>Duryodhana</s> said to <s>Dharmaputra</s> and his followers,
"Let you all sit down and watch us two as we fight."
Hearing this, <s>Ajātaśatru</s>, together with the <s>Pāñcāla</s> soldiers,
the friend of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, sat down surrounding <s>Halāyudha</s>.
Then the son of <s>Kuru</s>, his belt fastened tight, challenged
swift <s>Bhīma</s>, mace in hand, as the war of words began.
Then a row of sparks arose from the blows of their maces,
creating the appearance of whirling gold ornaments amid the confusion.
When the sky was filled with gods eager to see the battle,
there arose among the women of heaven a wondrous excitement of curiosity.
In attack, avoidance, release, the royal turn, and the turning back,
in running, standing still, leaping, and counter-leaping,
the two bold heroes moved in beautiful circles,
and with great speed struck each other's flanks with a ringing crash.
Then <s>Bhīma</s>, shaking his mace that sounded like a thunderbolt,
whirled it around, producing a terrible rumbling roar.
Then <s>Bhīma</s> swiftly launched that mace, heavy as a mountain.
