Though struck, he remained unshaken, and <s>Bhīma</s> again released his mace.
Again it was rendered futile by the king and fell, shaking the earth.
Then <s>Bhīma</s> was struck on the broad chest by the <s>Kaurava</s>.
For a moment he perceived nothing at all, his mind confused by fainting.
Then, while the army of the <s>Pāñcālas</s> and <s>Sṛñjayas</s> was troubled with uncertainty,
<s>Bhīma</s> slowly recovered and struck the king on the side.
Struck by the heavy blow, the lord of the <s>Kauravas</s> fell down;
but rising quickly, he struck <s>Bhīma</s> and made him fall to the ground.
Then a shower of flowers, cast down by the gods and white with fame, descended,
together with a series of cries of 'well done,' upon the head of the son of the <s>Kuru</s> king.
Then, when <s>Bhīmasena</s> had risen and quickly wiped away the blood,
<s>Arjuna</s> asked <s>Hari</s>, 'Which of these two is the better fighter?'
He said, '<s>Bhīma</s> is strong, and his valor is terrible; what need is there to say it?
Yet in the instruction of mace-fighting and in prowess in battle,
the painstaking lord of the <s>Kurus</s> appears to be superior to <s>Bhīmasena</s>.
Therefore <s>Bhīma</s> is not able to bring him down by a fair battle according to <s>dharma</s>.

children.text: māyayā nihatā daityā māyāvadhyā hi māyinaḥ
children.translated_text: Demons have been killed by trickery, for tricksters are fit to be killed by trickery.
So let <s>Bhīma</s>, by trickery, contrive the breaking of his thighs.
Otherwise the king is hard to conquer. For thirteen years

children.text: eṣa lokabhayaṃ bhīme vidhāya gadayā śramam ||
children.translated_text: this man has made <s>Bhīma</s> toil with the mace and has caused fear among people.
<s>Suyodhana</s>, skilled in exercise, moves upward with speed.
When an opening is seen in this great mountain-like one, breaking him is easy.'
When <s>Janārdana</s> had spoken thus, <s>Bhīma</s> hurled
that dreadful mace; the <s>Kuru</s> king too leapt over it and struck him.
Then <s>Bhīma</s>, holding back his pain while his body reeled for a moment,
marked the opening and sent against him his mace adorned with golden bracelets.
Like a she-serpent amid the splendid illusion of golden ornaments worthy of the flower-arrowed god,
it fell upon the king's pair of thighs.
Then <s>Duryodhana</s>, his thigh-joints shattered and broken by the crushing fall of the mace, whose crash was like a thunderous, terrible cloud,

children.text: duryodhano 'tha nipapāta divaṃ vilokya vajrāvapātahatapakṣa ivādrirājaḥ ||
children.translated_text: fell down looking toward heaven, like the king of mountains whose wings had been struck by the fall of a thunderbolt.
When this great lord of the earth fell to the ground, his footstool reddened by masses of rays from the crown-jewels of kings, lords of akshauhinis,

children.text: asminmahīparivṛḍhe patite ca bhūmau kairninditaṃ na bhavabhaṅgurabhaṅgi janma ||
children.translated_text: who did not condemn birth, fragile and crooked with the breaking of worldly existence?
When that lord of eleven armies had fallen upon the earth,
the bride Earth, with restless rivers for her girdle, trembled.
The world became filled with a hundred fearful evil omens,
and beings who move in the sky praised that battle and went away.
Then <s>Bhīma</s>, counting up the insults done by the lord of the <s>Kurus</s>,
touched with his foot that head, the dwelling-place of the play of royal fortune.
Seeing that universal emperor fallen,
the earth seemed to weep over him with pearl-tears from necklaces cut by his trembling mace and armlets.
<s>Dharmarāja</s>, restraining <s>Bhīma</s> as he roared,
said to <s>Suyodhana</s>, 'King, this destruction of your friends is from your own misconduct.'

children.text: dṛṣṭvā śiraḥ padā spṛṣṭaṃ bhīmena jagatībhujaḥ
children.translated_text: Seeing the head of the king touched by <s>Bhīma</s>'s foot,
the one marked with the palm-tree banner, fierce with anger and loud with rage, spoke:
'Who, unless he were a beast, would touch with his foot the head

children.text: śiro vyājahatasyāsya kaḥ spṛśed apaśuḥ padā ||
children.translated_text: of this man, slain by treachery, whose glory scorched his enemies and whose splendor was taken by foes?'
After saying this, he was ready to burn <s>Bhīma</s> with the fire of anger,
but the enemy of <s>Kaṃsa</s> calmed him with many humble words.
As <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> said, 'You are the effect of the crimes of poison, dice, and fire,'
<s>Duryodhana</s>, checking his fierce pain, replied to him:
'Cowherd boy, I have been deceived by you when you made a signal for the fools.
Those heroes headed by <s>Bhīṣma</s> were brought down by you only through pretexts.
I have enjoyed pleasure with friends, sported with beloved women, and offered sacrifice with the foremost twice-born priests.

children.text: vadhaḥ kṣatrocitaḥ prāptaḥ ko 'nyo 'sti sadṛśo mayā ||
children.translated_text: I have obtained a death proper to a <s>kṣatriya</s>; who else is equal to me?

children.text: bhrūbhaṅgena nivāsitā vanabhuvaṃ śuṣyanmukhāḥ śatravo dṛṣṭā śrīḥ svayamarpitāgryasuhṛdāmuṣṇīṣahārasmitā
children.translated_text: With a mere frown I made my enemies, their faces dried up, dwell in the forest; I saw Fortune herself, smiling with turbans and necklaces, given to my best friends.

children.text: saṃgrāme 'pyaparāṅmukhasya nidhanaṃ dikṣu prarūḍhaṃ yaśaḥ kartavyaṃ spṛhaṇīyam anyad ucitaṃ yuktaṃ kimastyāyuṣaḥ ||
children.translated_text: I have died in battle without turning my back, and my fame has grown throughout the directions. What other enviable, fitting duty of life remains?'
Hearing these words of his, the proud <s>Pārthas</s>, as if ashamed,

children.text: nṛpaiḥ saha yayuḥ pārthā nādayanto rathairjayam ||
children.translated_text: went away with the kings, making the chariots sound out victory.
Then <s>Madhusūdana</s> first had <s>Phalguṇa</s> descend,
and afterward he himself got down from the chariot; then that chariot burst into flame.
'This chariot had been burned by the weapons of <s>Droṇa</s> and <s>Karṇa</s>, and was blazing intensely,'
the destroyer of <s>Kāliya</s> said when the astonished <s>Pārtha</s> asked about it.
Hearing this dreadful account from <s>Sañjaya</s>, the king, overwhelmed by stupor,
lamented for his sons, repeatedly remembering the words of <s>Vidura</s>.
Then, when <s>Kṛṣṇamuni</s> had arrived at the house of the <s>Kurus</s>, <s>Hari</s>,
sent by <s>Ajātaśatru</s>, approached the king and <s>Gāndhārī</s> and said:
'Though he was begged, the <s>Kaurava</s> did not desire peace, because of his own bad policy.

children.text: na ca dharmāccyutāḥ pārthāstena tena padaṃ ruṣaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The <s>Pārthas</s> did not fall away from <s>dharma</s>; therefore there is no ground for anger.
Your sons today are the sons of <s>Pāṇḍu</s>, radiant like gods.
And it was said before by you two yourselves: where there is <s>dharma</s>, there is victory.'
When the <s>Vṛṣṇi</s> hero had thus appeased them and gone,

children.text: munāvāśvāsya yāte ca śeṣaṃ papraccha saṃjayam ||
children.translated_text: and when the sage too had consoled them and gone, <s>Ambikā</s>'s son asked <s>Sañjaya</s> the rest.
He said, 'Then your son, trembling on the ground,
said to me, "Look! I have been brought down by the cook through trickery."
Meanwhile <s>Drauṇi</s>, <s>Hārdikya</s>, and <s>Gautama</s> came up,

children.text: dadṛśuḥ kauravapatiṃ nītaṃ kālena tāṃ daśām ||
children.translated_text: and saw the lord of the <s>Kauravas</s> brought by Time to that condition.'
Then the teacher's son, in anger, crushing one hand with the other,
breathing hard, made a vow to destroy his enemies without remainder.

children.text: atha vīraṃ tamāliṅgya cakre senāpatiṃ nṛpaḥ
children.translated_text: Then the king embraced that hero and made him commander,
for even at the end the proud do not let their self-assertion grow slack.
<s>Droṇa</s>'s son roared with a sound like the clouds of dissolution,
and in that night the king, afflicted by pain, entered a grievous state.
Then <s>Gautama</s>, <s>Hārdikya</s>, and the teacher's son entered the great forest,
considering inwardly the wave-like instability of royal fortune.
Having bowed to <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> and to <s>Nara</s>, the best of men,
and to the goddess <s>Sarasvatī</s> and to <s>Vyāsa</s>, one should then proclaim the Jaya.
When the sun, the abode of heat and beloved of lotuses, had gone to its setting,
the earth became covered with darkness like hair disheveled by grief.
When the day had been brought to its end by Time and the funeral fire of twilight had grown quiet,
the sky was filled with stars as if with bones left behind.
The dark night, fresh with grief and spreading the collyrium of darkness,
bore a row of trembling, bright star-tears.
In that dreadful face of night, in a forest dense with fearful beings,
when <s>Kṛpa</s> and <s>Kṛtavarman</s> had fallen asleep from exhaustion,
the lone <s>Drauṇi</s>, meditating on <s>Duryodhana</s>'s killing and filled with the hālāhala poison of wrath,
pondered his vow to destroy the enemies.
At that moment he saw, perched high on the top of a banyan tree,
a flock of crows being slaughtered by an owl.
Seeing the crows, brought there by the force of Time, struck down by the owl,
<s>Drauṇi</s> thought of that very policy for killing the <s>Pāṇḍavas</s>.

children.text: krudhā krūrāṃ dhiyaṃ kṛtvā kṛpabhojau vibodhya saḥ
children.translated_text: Making his mind cruel with anger, he awakened <s>Kṛpa</s> and <s>Bhoja</s>,
and spoke, breathing long, as if he were being burned by anger.
"The king of thousands of kings, alone and in a perilous condition,
has been struck down by <s>Bhīmasena</s> through deceit while we were alive.
Though we carried weapons, we merely saw him on the ground in vain,
like utter cowards, incapable of avenging the falling of tears.
Taking account of place and time, an enemy must be killed by every means.
Therefore today I shall kill the <s>Pāṇḍavas</s> with their followers while they sleep."
Hearing this sinful proposal to kill men asleep, <s>Kṛpa</s>, his mind contracted,
and filled with compassion, rebuked and addressed his sister's son:
"Shame on this vile battle, in which an inactive man is killed.
Glorious heroes do not strike, even against one whose courage is broken.

children.text: bhavānahaṃ ca bhojaśca kartāraḥ prātareva tat
children.translated_text: You, I, and <s>Bhoja</s> shall be the doers of that deed tomorrow morning,
by which we will never again suffer the pain of <s>Duryodhana</s>'s killing.
United in battle, we are sufficient even for the gods.
We shall enter the forest of our enemies like blazing fires."
When <s>Gautama</s> had said this, and <s>Kṛtavarma</s> agreed,
<s>Drauṇi</s>, sighing with tear-filled eyes, spoke again:
"When clever men go about practicing deceit, those who answer with comparable illusion
may touch the boundary of <s>adharma</s>, but they do not partake of its fruit.

children.text: arjunena hataḥ karṇaḥ sa ca śāntanavo yathā
children.translated_text: <s>Karṇa</s> was killed by <s>Arjuna</s>, and so too was the son of <s>Śantanu</s>.

children.text: tatkiṃ na viditaṃ loke śeṣaṃ vaktuṃ na pāryate ||
children.translated_text: Is that not known in the world? The rest cannot be spoken.
Now farewell to <s>dharma</s>; I have folded my hands to it.
For the moment I cannot endure this defeat, which tears my vital parts."
Having spoken thus, <s>Drauṇi</s>, resolved on a terrible purpose,
went by chariot through the darkness to the camp of the <s>Kauravas</s>' enemies.
Since, at <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>'s command, the <s>Pāṇḍavas</s> had earlier gone to another camp
together with <s>Sātyaki</s> and the warriors, without their attendants,
<s>Drauṇi</s>, rushing swiftly past <s>Kṛpa</s> and <s>Bhoja</s>,
reached the camp gate and saw a great being.
It had tawny beard, matted hair, and eyes, like a mass of flames,
like a heap of darkness, resembling a mountain of collyrium.
It was wondrous, with a thousand heads and eyes and a thousand feet,
its body wearing serpents as sacred thread, armlets, and bracelets,
terrifying even to fear itself, like the divinity of Death.
Seeing it, <s>Drauṇi</s>, dreadful in fury and unconquerable in valor,
a mountain of firmness, sent his whole array of weapons against it.
Those weapons, suddenly blazing with splendor,
came upon that great expanding being and perished.
Then <s>Drauṇi</s> looked on in amazement as, from the rays of that form,
thousands of discus-weapons issued forth.
In a moment his weapons had been swallowed by that being, and he was tormented by deep remorse.
Distressed, he himself condemned the impure deed he had begun.
Then he descended from the chariot and, intent in worship, approached <s>Tripurāntaka</s>,
the trident-bearing lord, for refuge, his mouth resounding with hymns to him.
When he was prepared there to give himself as an offering to <s>Rudra</s>,
a golden altar filled with flames appeared before him.
The sky was quickly filled with terrible <s>gaṇas</s> arising from it,
with faces and bellies of many creatures and blazing with many weapons.
Then, in the great fire blazing on the altar, <s>Droṇa</s>'s son
offered himself in devotion to the three-eyed god and threw himself in.
Then the blessed <s>Andhakasūdana</s>, pleased, came himself
and said to him, "Rise, best of the <s>Āṅgirasas</s>; you are my very own portion.
For the establishment of the foe of <s>Kaiṭabha</s>, this much has been done by me..."

children.text: ātmānaṃ viddhi me kṛṣṇaṃ sa me bahumataḥ sadā ||
children.translated_text: Know <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> to be my very self; he is always held in high honor by me.
But the <s>Pāñcālas</s> have been ripened by Time; there is no protection for them anywhere.
Take this sword; with it split them open without hesitation.

children.text: ityuktvā bhairave dīptaṃ khaḍgaṃ dattvā tirohite
children.translated_text: When the terrible one had spoken thus, given him the blazing sword, and disappeared,
then <s>Drauṇi</s>, hard to look upon because of his transformation, entered the camp.

children.text: dvāri bhojakṛpau dhṛtvā vidrutānāṃ vadhāya saḥ
children.translated_text: Keeping <s>Bhoja</s> and <s>Kṛpa</s> at the gate to kill those who fled,
he entered and saw <s>Dhṛṣṭadyumna</s> on a fine bed.
He was like a blazing lion, with rays from his starry necklace for claws,
as if gazed at in wonder by the lamps with their wavering flames.
He was surrounded by many soldiers, exhausted from the crush of many battles and bewildered by sleep,
their mounts freed from their trappings.
Seeing him, and burning with the flame of anger as he remembered his father,
<s>Drauṇi</s> said, "Get up, wretch, killer of your guru," and touched him with his foot.
Awakened suddenly by him, and seizing a weapon in confusion,
the son of <s>Drupada</s> recognized the son of <s>Droṇa</s> and trembled.
<s>Drauṇi</s> swiftly dragged him up by his garlanded hair,
threw him down, and, pressing his throat hard, made him helpless.
As he was being crushed in fury, his face fouled with vomited blood,
he grew angry and writhed, clawing and biting at <s>Drauṇi</s>'s feet.

children.text: śastreṇa chinddhi māṃ tūrṇaṃ mā padeneti gadgadam
children.translated_text: With his voice choked in his throat and broken by his breath, he said indistinctly,
"Cut me down quickly with a weapon, not with your foot."
The son of <s>Droṇa</s> said to him, "Sinner, you shall be killed by feet.
There are no weapon-purified worlds for sinful killers of gurus."
After saying this, he battered him to pieces with blows of his feet.
When he was killed, the people woke at the sound of that crushing.
Then, seeing <s>Drauṇi</s> marked with splashes of enemy blood,
the <s>Pāñcālas</s> and the <s>Draupadeyas</s> thought, "This is Death himself."
With eyes still red from sleep, as they brought weapons to one another,
there arose a great noise from them crying, "Armor! Armor!"

children.text: kva gajaḥ kva rathaḥ kvāśvaḥ kva cāpaṃ kva śilīmukhāḥ
children.translated_text: "Where is the elephant? Where is the chariot? Where is the horse? Where is the bow? Where are the arrows?"
As they spoke this way, <s>Drauṇi</s> angrily cut them down with his sword.
With harsh valor he killed <s>Uttamaujas</s> by trampling on his throat,
and he crushed <s>Yudhāmanyu</s>, who held a mace and cried out.

children.text: tataḥ khaḍgena śūrāṇāṃ śirāṃsi bhuvi pātayan
children.translated_text: Then, making the heads of heroes fall to the earth with his sword,
he made sport for the night of death with them, as if they were balls.
As the sons of <s>Kṛṣṇā</s>, the <s>Draupadeyas</s>, rushed at him,
he calmly made them, with his sword, fit mouthfuls for Death.
When brave <s>Prativindhya</s> was killed and <s>Sutasoma</s> was struck down,
and when <s>Śrutakīrti</s>, <s>Śatānīka</s>, and <s>Śrutavarman</s> were cut down,
<s>Śikhaṇḍī</s>, drawing his curved bow, filled <s>Drauṇi</s> with arrows.
But the son of <s>Droṇa</s>, enraged, cut him in two with his sword.
As the <s>Prabhadrakas</s> were slain in anger by the teacher's son,
the <s>Matsyas</s>, <s>Sṛñjayas</s>, and <s>Pāñcālas</s> saw Death close at hand.
Seeing him black, clothed in red, with red garlands and unguents,

children.text: hasantaṃ vīkṣya taṃ vīrāḥ saṃhāraṃ menire sphuṭam ||
children.translated_text: and laughing, the heroes clearly thought him to be destruction itself.
In the dense darkness, at the gate, <s>Bhoja</s> and <s>Gautama</s>
brought about the destruction of heroes, chariots, elephants, horses, and soldiers.
Thus, having killed an akṣauhiṇī and being smeared with fat and blood,
<s>Drauṇi</s>, terrible in conduct and like <s>Bhairava</s> in form, went out.

children.text: sa gatvā sahitastūrṇaṃ hārdikyena kṛpeṇa ca
children.translated_text: Then, quickly going together with <s>Hārdikya</s> and <s>Kṛpa</s>,
he saw King <s>Suyodhana</s> on the ground, his strength broken.
With the tip of his mace he repeatedly warded off the circle of flesh-eaters,
and in pain that pierced his vital parts he was biting the earth.
They quickly wiped away the blood vomited from his mouth,
and rained nectar upon him with the story of the total destruction of the <s>Pāñcālas</s>.
Though only a little life remained in him, when he heard this he turned his neck
and praised them with indistinct words swallowed at their ends.
With effort he embraced <s>Drauṇi</s>, whose eyes were filled with tears,
and softly said, "May we meet again in heaven."

children.text: aṅge vidhāya dayitāṃ sa gadāṃ sadaiva bhuktāṃ ciraṃ vasumatīmavagūhya dorbhyām
children.translated_text: Having placed his beloved mace against his body, and having long enjoyed the earth, he clasped her with his arms;
then the hero, his life-breath rising with force as far as his ears, slowly became the beloved of heavenly women.
Meanwhile, when the night had passed and the enemies had been destroyed,

children.text: jajñire pāṇḍavāḥ karma dāruṇaṃ drauṇinā kṛtam ||
children.translated_text: the <s>Pāṇḍavas</s> learned of the terrible deed done by <s>Drauṇi</s>.
When <s>Kṛṣṇā</s> heard that her sons, who had escaped that great danger,
and her younger brothers together with the <s>Pāñcālas</s> had been killed, she fell unconscious on the ground.
Slowly regaining consciousness, that fair-eyed woman, lamenting,
tore apart the hearts of the <s>Pārthas</s>, already shaken by grief.
"Until I have seen the head of wicked <s>Drauṇi</s>
cut off by arrows, until then this handful of life is mine."
Having said this, <s>Draupadī</s>, in sorrow, looked at <s>Vṛkodara</s>.
Out of anguish she said nothing more, resolved upon death.
Then <s>Bhīma</s>, struck in the heart by the spear of his beloved's grief,
mounted his chariot and set out, desiring to kill the son of <s>Droṇa</s>.
As he went, like the fire of Time wishing to burn the worlds,
his frown for a moment made on his forehead the likeness of a garland of smoke-clouds.
Fierce was <s>Drauṇi</s>, sheltered by <s>Rudra</s>, and enraged was the son of the Wind.
<s>Hari</s> said to the <s>Pāṇḍavas</s>, "Therefore let us go after him."
Then those led by <s>Kirīṭin</s> went forth together with <s>Sātyaki</s>,
all the chariot-warriors, the remaining sons of <s>Pāṇḍu</s>, eager for battle.
Then, when they reached <s>Drauṇi</s>, because of the sin of slaughtering men who were asleep,
they saw him with his radiance ruined and his rites abandoned, and they became agitated with anger.
When <s>Bhīmasena</s>, with <s>Nakula</s> as his charioteer, rushed against <s>Drauṇi</s>,
he, on foot and smeared with ghee, stood for a moment on the bank of the <s>Sarasvatī</s>,
and took up the <s>brahmaśīrṣa</s> weapon to make the world devoid of <s>Pāṇḍavas</s>.
To destroy it, the skillful <s>Pārtha</s> too released a <s>brahmāstra</s>,
by which the quarters were filled and rippled with the terror of trembling.
At that moment, together with <s>Nārada</s>, there came in person
the sage, the holy son of <s>Satyavatī</s>, the beneficent lord who cherishes beings.
Fearing destruction, he spoke to <s>Droṇa</s>'s son and to <s>Jiṣṇu</s>:
"In this collision of divine weapons, the world, its heroes slain, will burn.

children.text: pārtha saṃhara divyāstraṃ tvaṃ ca drauṇe girā mama
children.translated_text: <s>Pārtha</s>, withdraw the divine weapon; and you too, <s>Drauṇi</s>, by my word,
do not let these worlds become sharers in an untimely dissolution."
When the sage had spoken thus, <s>Arjuna</s> quickly withdrew his weapon;
but <s>Drauṇi</s>, though skilled in launching the weapon, was not able to withdraw it.
Then, while the world was blazing and the circle of the gods was distressed,
<s>Drauṇi</s> made the weapon fall into the womb of <s>Abhimanyu</s>'s wife.
Again, to ward that off, desiring the continuation of his son's line,
<s>Pārtha</s>, angrily reviling <s>Droṇa</s>'s son, released that weapon.
Then <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> said to <s>Jiṣṇu</s>, who was despondent at the destruction of his lineage:

children.text: mā śuco dhairyajaladhe na te vaṃśo vinaṅkṣyati ||
children.translated_text: "Do not grieve, ocean of steadiness; your line will not perish.
When he is born, I shall bring back to life this child, even though burned by the weapon's power,
the son of <s>Saubhadra</s>, the infant who is in <s>Uttarā</s>'s womb."

children.text: iti bruvāṇe govinde pārthāstre jvalite bhuvi
children.translated_text: As <s>Govinda</s> was speaking and <s>Pārtha</s>'s weapon was blazing upon the earth,
<s>Vyāsa</s>, together with the divine seer, addressed <s>Droṇa</s>'s son:
"Give up your crest-jewel; save the jewel that is your life from the great weapon.

children.text: aśaktaśca pramādī ca jānīṣe na yathocitam ||
children.translated_text: You are powerless and reckless, and you do not understand what is proper.
For a thousand years you will wander, foul with disease and self-contained,
a sign of famine, miserable, in desolate places."
Thus cursed, the guru's son spoke angrily to <s>Vyāsa</s>:
"Fallen into calamity, why have I been thrown by you into danger?

children.text: yatra yatra bhaviṣyāmi tatra tatra mamānugaḥ
children.translated_text: Wherever I shall be, there and there, following me,
you too, sage, by my counter-curse, will always be present."
After saying this, he handed over the crest-jewel as an offering for the weapon,
and <s>Droṇa</s>'s son departed; the sage too went away with the sage.

children.text: tataḥ praśānte brahmāstre pāṇḍavāḥ saha śauriṇā
children.translated_text: Then, when the <s>brahmāstra</s> had been calmed, the <s>Pāṇḍavas</s>, together with <s>Śauri</s>,
took the crest-jewel and presented it to <s>Yājñasenī</s>.
Having thus appeased <s>Pāñcālī</s>, the grief-stricken sons of <s>Pāṇḍu</s>
found no peace, as they brooded on the terrible slaughter of the <s>Pāñcālas</s>.
When this had been told by <s>Sañjaya</s>, the king, <s>Ambikā</s>'s son, heard it,
and, stunned by delusion and with the fire of grief sunk within him, fell unconscious for a moment.
Reviving him with streams of cool water, <s>Sañjaya</s>
and the ministers spoke to him as he grieved for his dear sons, his senses shaken:
"The wise are not touched by the bewilderments of worldly existence,
which gleam like dream and illusion and end in grief and delusion.
Those whose minds are not deluded are not bewildered by sons, wealth, and wives,
which are like shadow-playthings made by a divine magician.
This destruction of kinsmen through bad policy was neglected by you yourself;
now that it has happened, you should not indulge grief here in vain.
Good people are not confused by states born from power,
formed by the splendor of illusion and ending finally in nonexistence.
In a world sealed by its own karma, in the ocean of dissolution that is destiny,

children.text: kalayāmi na kālasya kaśca tāvati vartate ||
children.translated_text: I do not reckon that anyone remains even so much as a particle before Time.
With such words through the mouth of <s>Sañjaya</s>, they repeatedly told the king, broken by fierce delusion
and seeing the limit of the bad policy he himself had made, the tale of worldly existence, unstable like the flapping ear of a playful young elephant.
Having bowed to <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> and to <s>Nara</s>, the best of men,
and to the goddess <s>Sarasvatī</s> and to <s>Vyāsa</s>, one should then proclaim victory.
Then <s>Gāndhārī</s> and King <s>Dhṛtarāṣṭra</s>, their minds distraught,
went as if longing to see their sons who had been slain.

children.text: tatra tau vilapantau ca kṣipantau ca tanuṃ bhuvi
children.translated_text: There, as the two were lamenting and casting their bodies upon the ground,
the holy <s>Pārāśarya</s> came up and looked upon them.

children.text: sa dīnaṃ patitaṃ bhūmau hataputraṃ nareśvaram
children.translated_text: With compassion, he, together with <s>Vidura</s> and <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, addressed the wretched king,
who had lost his sons and had fallen upon the earth:

children.text: abhāvaḥ prākca paścācca dehināṃ satataṃ sthitaḥ
children.translated_text: "Nonexistence stands constantly before and after embodied beings;
in their intervening transformations, how can you rightly feel attachment?
In this boundless ocean of becoming, all creatures
come to be and cease to be, like bubbles on water, through the conjunction of karma.
It is true: <s>Suyodhana</s> was born for the pacification of the earth's burden.

children.text: sa ca yātastathā kṛtvā kastvaṃ tasya sa kastava ||
children.translated_text: He too has gone after doing that; who are you to him, and who is he to you?
King, do not grieve amid this great destruction;
not even a tiny particle of those who have gone returns back with their attendants.
This effort, born from the calamity of grief, leads only to weariness;
now let attachment, the root of the trees of sorrow, be restrained."

children.text: namaḥ kālāya yaḥ ko 'pi vidyate mṛtyunā vṛtaḥ
children.translated_text: Homage to <s>Kāla</s> (Time), by whom whatever body exists, enveloped by death,
comes of itself to old age among embodied beings.
Your sons were swallowed by Time through their own offense;
therefore you should not be angry with the sons of <s>Pāṇḍu</s> on account of guilt.
They, the resolute ones ever devoted to <s>dharma</s> (righteous order), were wounded by you in the matter of <s>dharma</s>;

children.text: pāṇḍavā bhrātaraṃ smṛtvā kāluṣyaṃ teṣu mā kṛthāḥ ||
children.translated_text: remembering your brother, do not place any stain upon the <s>Pāṇḍavas</s>.

children.text: gāndhārīṃ brūhi sahasā mohe majjati no yathā
children.translated_text: Speak quickly to <s>Gāndhārī</s>, lest she sink into delusion;
she herself said before: victory is founded on <s>dharma</s>.

children.text: iti teṣāṃ girā kṣipraṃ samohaṃ kauraveśvaram
children.translated_text: At their words the <s>Pārthas</s> quickly came to see the lord of the <s>Kauravas</s>, still filled with delusion,
their necks and heads bent low with shame.
Then the king, whose eye was wisdom, embraced <s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s>,
and afterward the illusory <s>Bhīma</s>, fashioned by <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>'s stratagem.
That image of the son of the Wind came near; in hatred he squeezed it with his two arms,
and it was reduced by him to fragments; everyone was astonished.
Then the son of <s>Dharma</s> bowed to the aged faithful wife,
<s>Gāndhārī</s>, whose eyes, like her husband's, were always covered with cloth.
When <s>Dharmanandana</s> had fallen down at her feet,
the fire of anger in her gaze burned the pair of his big toes.
Then the beloved wives of the slain lords of the earth, stricken with grief,
and <s>Gāndhārī</s>, surrounded by her daughters-in-law, went toward the middle of the battlefield.
There the daughter of <s>Subala</s>, bewildered and lamenting piteously,
tearfully spoke to <s>Keśava</s>, the faithful wife endowed with divine sight:
Look, <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>: these noble women mourn my sons, slain in battle,

children.text: śocanti yāḥ purā dṛṣṭā na sūryeṇa na cendunā ||
children.translated_text: women who before were seen neither by the sun nor by the moon.
See my heroic son, surrounded by women of the inner apartments like apsarases,
struck down face to face, his thighs broken.
And see this bride of <s>Suyodhana</s>; seeing the earth, with elephants and horses slain,
like a rival wife, she has fallen into a swoon.
Slowly regaining consciousness, she wipes away the dust for a long time,
and the queen of the king of kings questions her beloved:
Taking your jewel-clad mace upon your lap as though it were me,

children.text: dorbhyāṃ ca bhuvamāliṅgya kathaṃ supto 'si bhūpate ||
children.translated_text: and embracing the earth with your arms, how are you asleep, O king?
You are not enclosed on a golden couch, on a bed of pleasure;
how, O lord of men, does a jackal drunk with blood sleep here?
Here lies <s>Duḥśāsana</s>, your dear and handsome younger brother,
whose blood was drunk by <s>Bhīma</s> as if by a demon.

children.text: ayaṃ te dayitaḥ putro lakṣmaṇaḥ śatruṇā hataḥ
children.translated_text: Here is your beloved son <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, slain by the enemy;

children.text: sajīva iva vaktuṃ tvaṃ nātha kiṃcitsamīhate ||
children.translated_text: as though alive, he seems to wish to say something to you, lord.
Like two fallen ivory pillars of the gateway to Love's women's quarters,
those straight thighs seem to have been struck down by Time the tusker.
Here is your fitting diadem, long comfortably resting on your head,
brilliant, now fallen here and touched by the wasting of its splendor.
By your two feet, wet with blood as they moved through battle,
the constantly drunk radiance of royal crest-jewels seems to have been vomited out.
When you, a guardian of the world, have gone to heaven out of delight in <s>Nandana</s>,
only your fame, as though proud of its good fortune, follows after you.
On what other arm, gleaming with jeweled bracelets and white as camphor,
should the earth go to the bliss of resting upon <s>Śeṣa</s>?

children.text: yaḥ sa kaṅkaṇajhāṅkārair vyajanair vijito nṛpaḥ
children.translated_text: That king who was once fanned by yak-tail fans ringing with bracelets,
is now still being fanned by the wind from carrion birds' wings.
See the women of the <s>Kauravas</s>, pulling away <s>Duryodhana</s>'s bride as she cries out thus;
fallen on the ground, they roll about.
Over there <s>Subhadrā</s>, loving her child, wipes the dust from her little son <s>Saubhadra</s>,
as though ready to give him her breasts.
And this <s>Uttarā</s>, placing her husband's moon-like face in her lap,
washes it with streams of tears and questions him:
Ah lord, after saying all those tender words of love,

children.text: bhūmimāliṅgya kiṃ śeṣe priyāmadya vihāya mām ||
children.translated_text: why do you lie embracing the earth today, leaving me, your beloved?
You are the son of the wielder of <s>Gāṇḍīva</s>, the son of <s>Cakrapāṇi</s>'s sister,

children.text: tvaṃ śakrasadṛśaḥ śaurye kathameko hataḥ paraiḥ ||
children.translated_text: equal to <s>Śakra</s> in valor; how were you alone slain by enemies?
This lovely face of yours is like the lotus of <s>Kamalā</s>;
surely a blessed company of heavenly women will drink it in, smiling.
Because he is bodiless, <s>Anaṅga</s> had no proper ground for comparison with you;
today, beloved, by the slaying of your body, he has been made complete by you.
As you go to the third heaven, I suspect that, mistaking you for the moon,
the row of stars creates the illusion of a pearl necklace at your throat.
I, a new bride, was once asked by you for answering speech;

children.text: tvāṃ svayaṃ bhāṣyamāṇāṃ māṃ kathaṃ na pratibhāṣase ||
children.translated_text: now that I myself am speaking to you, why do you not answer me?
Where has your courtesy gone, fit to be counted among the whole multitude of virtues,
that, attached to the women of heaven, you neglect me?
In this beauty of yours, impossible for the Creator to make again,

children.text: prahṛtaṃ tvaccharīre yair dhik tān dagdhavilocanān ||
children.translated_text: shame on those burnt-eyed men who struck your body.
For you, who were equal to the Flower-armed god, surely your weapons became flowers in battle;
otherwise how could the heroes have withstood you?
The wives of <s>Virāṭa</s> are forcibly drawing away this young daughter as she laments in this way,
and, weeping, they go to her husband's side.
King <s>Virāṭa</s> lies slain with his younger brother, his son, and his ministers,
surrounded on the earth by daughters-in-law as if in heaven by hosts of apsarases.
This lovely-armed woman, seeing her husband's face cut by <s>Droṇa</s>'s arrows,

children.text: vilokya tāraṃ krośantī ruddhā sakhyeva mūrcchayā ||
children.translated_text: cries out loudly, checked by fainting as if by a friend.
Look: the women of the household mourn <s>Karṇa</s>, whose limbs have been torn away by flesh-eaters,
embracing him again and again, the refuge of the <s>Kauravas</s>.

children.text: nāmni saṃkīrtite yasya prāpurnidrāṃ na śatravaḥ
children.translated_text: At the mere uttering of whose name his enemies could not get sleep,

children.text: sa tvamadya hataḥ śeṣe dhikkālasya durantatām ||
children.translated_text: that very you now lie slain. Alas for the irresistible cruelty of Time!
<s>Jambhāri</s> himself became a beggar for whose armor and earrings;
how has truthful <s>Karṇa</s> been reduced by birds to mere remains?
The creation of the ruined Creator is by nature wholly incoherent:

children.text: kṛtvā yaḥ śakratulyatvaṃ na cakre kalpasākṣiṇam ||
children.translated_text: having made him equal to <s>Śakra</s>, he did not make him a witness of an aeon.
Thus <s>Karṇa</s>'s women, their ornaments scattered, cry aloud,
and the mothers of <s>Vṛṣasena</s> tear at the fullness of their breasts.

children.text: paśya jāmātaraṃ kṛṣṇa hataṃ mama jayadratham
children.translated_text: Look, <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, at my son-in-law <s>Jayadratha</s>, slain;

children.text: bālā śociti matputrī na ca jānāti śocitum ||
children.translated_text: my daughter, still a girl, grieves, and does not even know how to grieve.
Here is <s>Śalya</s>, slain in battle, whose valor was a thorn to his enemies;
see how he has now become a thorn to the women of the inner chambers.
Look: crows drag the tongue of this king of <s>Madra</s>,
the tongue with which he caused the slaughter of <s>Rādheya</s>'s spirit in battle.

children.text: paśya droṇasya samare vahneḥ śāntārciṣo yathā
children.translated_text: Look: for <s>Droṇa</s> in battle, like a fire whose flames are quenched,
the funeral rite is being performed by brahmins, after they drive away the clustered worms.
Here lies the hero <s>Bhūriśravas</s>, son of <s>Somadatta</s>, slain;
the warrior, his arm cut off by <s>Kirīṭin</s>, is mourned by his queen.
On the great sacrificial post of the battle-sacrifice, your arm was the arm like a sacrificial-post banner;

children.text: nikṛte jiṣṇunā manye yaśo nirlūnam ātmanaḥ ||
children.translated_text: when it was cut off by <s>Jiṣṇu</s>, I think my own fame was shorn away.
As your arm, a tethering post for the elephant-cow of Fortune and lordly serpent bearing the earth's burden,
is dragged away by jackals, its row of bracelets seems to cry out.
In moonlit mansions, women whose ornament was love for you
were once embraced by this arm, adorned with the ornaments of dalliance.
When this arm, a wish-granting tree for petitioners, has been cut off,
who else, hero, will become the weighty initiator of widowhood for the wives of enemies?
What powerful seizer of the throats of doe-eyed women by force
will now make the bud of an armlet's radiance into an ear-ornament?
Speaking such delirious lamentations, the bewildered woman addresses her lotus-like lord,
her own excellent, greatly renowned <s>Bhūriśravas</s>.
Look: <s>Śakuni</s>, hater of salutary counsel, is being devoured by jackals,
he of inauspicious conduct, like a wealthy man by courtesans.
The earth was quickly destroyed before by this man with petty dice that went to the ear;
now from this side it has been destroyed by <s>Kirīṭin</s> with arrows.
Here are the beloved wives of <s>Sudakṣiṇa</s>, king of the <s>Kāmbojas</s>;
by their lamentation they split even the hearts of stones.
These delicate women mourn prince <s>Bṛhadbala</s>, bright as the moon,
pierced through by the arrows of <s>Saubhadra</s>.
These sons of <s>Dhṛṣṭadyumna</s>, adorned with shining golden garlands,
slain by <s>Droṇa</s>, gleam like fallen <s>Vidyādharas</s>.
The <s>Kekayas</s>, <s>Dhṛṣṭaketu</s>, <s>Jayatsena</s> of <s>Magadha</s>,
and the aged king <s>Drupada</s>, together with ministers, sons, and kinsmen;
<s>Alāyudha</s>, <s>Alambusa</s>, <s>Bhagadatta</s>, <s>Śrutāyudha</s>,
<s>Vinda</s> and <s>Anuvinda</s> of <s>Avanti</s>, <s>Jalasaṃdha</s>, and <s>Sulocana</s>;
these foremost kings and thousands of other heroes have been slain,
yet, surrounded by their beloved women, they seem as if they had regained life.
Because, though able, you ignored them, <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, out of desire,
or out of hatred, or for the destruction of all, though omniscient, and in mere sport,

children.text: ṣaḍviṃśe vatsare prāpte vṛṣṇīnāṃ samare mithaḥ
children.translated_text: therefore, when the twenty-sixth year has come, in a mutual battle among the <s>Vṛṣṇis</s>,
there will be for you too a vast destruction of kinsmen.
For you too there will be some improper cause of death.
Having said this in a voice piercingly pitiful, the daughter of <s>Subala</s> wept.
Smiling, <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, whose own will creates dissolution and arising, said to her,
'This was ordained long ago by fate; what you have spoken is only repetition.
Do not grieve in vain over this destruction that was bound to happen.
O daughter of a <s>kṣatriya</s>, I am indeed the inevitable slayer of foes.'
When <s>Dāśārha</s> had spoken thus, <s>Dhṛtarāṣṭra</s> asked <s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s>

children.text: gatiṃ papraccha vīrāṇāṃ parimāṇaṃ ca saṃkṣaye ||
children.translated_text: about the destination of the heroes and the measure of the slaughter.
<s>Dharmarāja</s> answered him with words sweet in propriety:
'Twenty thousand, and six crores with six more,
heroes worthy of being counted, were slain in this battle.

children.text: aprahṛṣṭā hatā ye ca te gandharvapuraṃ gatāḥ ||
children.translated_text: And those who were slain without exultation have gone to the city of the <s>Gandharvas</s>.
Those who turned their backs from fear have attained the state of <s>Yakṣas</s>;
but those who stood with their courage unbroken have taken refuge in <s>Brahmā</s>'s world.
Those who were killed on foot or from their mounts have gone to the side of <s>Meru</s>.
By the grace of the sage <s>Lomaśa</s>, I see this with divine sight.'
Having spoken thus, the son of <s>Dharma</s> quickly ordered
funeral rites, proper to their wealth, for the slain kings and kinsmen.
The charioteers headed by <s>Indrasena</s>, and also <s>Sañjaya</s> and <s>Vidura</s>,
and <s>Yuyutsu</s>, at his command, went to perform their final rites.
Those great chariot-warriors, adorned with garlands, garments, and ornaments,
were placed upon the pyre fires, as if they were entering their own valor.
Then, from here and there, there arose from the gathered women,
who clung to one another's necks, a pitiful sound of weeping.
Then <s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s>, together with <s>Dhṛtarāṣṭra</s> and accompanied by his retinue,
followed by the royal women, went to bathe in the river.
When his mother had told him the story of <s>Karṇa</s>, whose birth had been hidden,
in sorrow he gave that brother a water-offering mixed with tears.

children.text: sa yathāvidhi bandhūnāṃ vidhāya svocitāṃ kriyām
children.translated_text: Having performed, according to rule, the proper rite for his kinsmen,
he ordered cloth pavilions to be set up for the rites of the royal women.
Then those kings' ladies, with straight, wide eyes, whose streams of eye-water surpassed their pearl necklaces,
went to the <s>Bhāgīrathī</s>, their broad and rounded hips resounding with the sweet girdles of graceful swans.
Having bowed to <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> and to <s>Nara</s>, the best of men,
and to the goddess <s>Sarasvatī</s> and <s>Vyāsa</s>, one should then proclaim victory.
While <s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s> stood on the bank of the heavenly river, having made the water-offering and completed the impurity rites,
sages beginning with <s>Nārada</s> came to see him.
When they had received seats and arghya-water and had been honored by the priest,
the divine sage, after asking the king about his well-being, spoke with affection.
"By good fortune, O king, you shine forth, safe and with your enemies slain;

children.text: diṣṭyā śalyādayo vīrā yātā vṛtrasamāḥ kṣayam ||
children.translated_text: by good fortune heroes such as <s>Śalya</s>, equals of <s>Vṛtra</s>, have gone to destruction.
I hope that, from delusion at separation from your kinsmen, you have not taken on a state fit for the timid,
one that destroys courage, and so fail to rejoice in victory."
When the divine sage had spoken thus, the son of <s>Dharma</s> sighed and said:
"What man like me could rejoice in this kingdom, which is like a cremation-ground?
Teachers, friends, sons, servants, relations, and kinsmen
have been slain by us, who are merely bodies left behind and who desired power.
Those dear people, for whose sake kings seek a kingdom cleared of thorns,

children.text: te hatāḥ svajanāḥ sarve gato niṣphalatāṃ śramaḥ ||
children.translated_text: have all been killed; our labor has come to fruitlessness.

children.text: idaṃ dahati me ceto yatkarṇo vinipātitaḥ
children.translated_text: This burns my mind: that <s>Karṇa</s> was brought down,

children.text: sa hi me kathitaḥ kuntyā bhrātā tapanasaṃbhavaḥ ||
children.translated_text: for he has been declared to me by <s>Kuntī</s> to be my brother, born from the Sun.
Long ago, the anger that arose in me toward him, going ahead as a change of feeling,
softened when I thought, 'His feet are like <s>Kuntī</s>'s.'
That uterine brother was slain by us, greedy for sovereignty.
Shame now on my kingdom, another name for hell.

children.text: asmadarthe raho mātrā yācitaḥ sa mahāyaśāḥ
children.translated_text: For our sake he, of great fame, was secretly entreated by our mother;
again and again he protected us when we had fallen into the range of death.
I wish to hear, venerable one, how his curse came about."

children.text: iti rājñā viṣaṇṇena pṛṣṭaḥ provāca nāradaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Questioned thus by the despondent king, <s>Nārada</s> spoke.
"Long ago, out of hatred for you, <s>Karṇa</s> begged <s>Bhāradvāja</s>

children.text: brahmāstraṃ tacca na dadau droṇo 'smai phalguṇapriyāt ||
children.translated_text: for the <s>brahmāstra</s> (Brahmā weapon), but <s>Droṇa</s> did not give it to him because of his love for <s>Phalguṇa</s>.
Grieved when he was told by him, 'This must be known by a brahmin,'
he quickly assumed the dress of a brahmin and went to the hermitage of <s>Jāmadagnya</s>.
Then, as a pupil of the descendant of <s>Bhṛgu</s>, seeking the <s>brahmāstra</s>,
the bowman wandered for a long time on the slopes of <s>Mahendra</s> mountain.
Once a certain brahmin, intensely angered because his sacrificial cow had been injured,
cursed him, who had incurred sin unknowingly.
'Because harm has been done by you, in delusion, to my sacrificial cow,
therefore, when you are engaged with your enemy, the earth will swallow your wheel.'

children.text: iti śaptaḥ sa vipreṇa dahyamāna ivāniśam
children.translated_text: Thus cursed by the brahmin, he burned inwardly as if day and night,
but after great effort he pleased <s>Rāma</s> and obtained the <s>brahmāstra</s>.
Then one day, when confidence had arisen, the descendant of <s>Bhṛgu</s>,
worn down by vows, placed his head in <s>Karṇa</s>'s lap and fell asleep.
Meanwhile a terrible, unbearable worm named <s>Alarka</s>,
thin, with sharp fangs, lips, and feet, bit <s>Karṇa</s>.
Afraid of waking his guru, he endured that pain as long as he could;
then, soaked by his blood, <s>Bhārgava</s> gave up his sleep.
Startled, and contracted at the touch of blood, he asked, 'What is this?'
Seeing <s>Rādheya</s> bitten, he beheld the creature's misshapen form.
The moment it was seen by <s>Rāma</s>, the worm was reduced to ashes,
and became a rākṣasa with a red neck and blazing eyes.
He said, 'Out of wantonness, desiring the wife of <s>Bhṛgu</s>,

children.text: gṛdhro nāma surārātiḥ śapto 'haṃ muninā purā ||
children.translated_text: I, an enemy of the gods named <s>Gṛdhra</s>, was once cursed by a sage.
Because of that curse I went to hell and entered this sinful womb, O lord,
which was to last until the sight of you; now that too has been exhausted.'

children.text: ityuktvā rākṣase yāte karṇaṃ papraccha bhārgavaḥ
children.translated_text: When the rākṣasa had spoken thus and gone away, <s>Bhārgava</s> questioned <s>Karṇa</s>:
'Who are you? Surely you are not a brahmin; you are a kṣatriya, able to bear sharp pain.'
Hearing this, <s>Karṇa</s>, alarmed, disclosed to him

children.text: kulaṃ nāma ca yenāśu taṃ śaśāpa ruṣā guruḥ ||
children.translated_text: his own lineage and name; because of that the guru quickly cursed him in anger:
'Because you obtained the <s>brahmāstra</s> under the disguise of a brahmin,
therefore, at your final crisis, this will come to destruction for you.'
Thus rejected by <s>Bhārgava</s>, <s>Karṇa</s> reached <s>Suyodhana</s>.
Through the friendship born from conflict with you, he was made lord over <s>Aṅga</s> by him.
Long ago the son of <s>Dhṛtarāṣṭra</s>, relying on the strength of his arms,
carried off the daughter of <s>Citrāṅgada</s>, the king of <s>Kaliṅga</s>.
At that svayaṃvara, after <s>Duryodhana</s> had gone ahead,
<s>Karṇa</s> alone, in pride, fought the enraged circle of kings.
After conquering all the kings, and even <s>Jarāsaṃdha</s>, that treasure of fame,
powerful in wrestling, he set him swinging in doubt.

children.text: jarāsaṃdho dadau tasmai mālinīṃ nagarīṃ jitaḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Jarāsaṃdha</s>, defeated, gave him the city of <s>Mālinī</s>,

children.text: anye ca tatyajurvīrā bhāgaṃ bhāgaṃ nareśvarāḥ ||
children.translated_text: and other heroic kings each abandoned a portion of tribute to him."
He had been deceived by <s>Surendra</s>, who took away his armor and earrings,

children.text: śaptaḥ pūrvaṃ dvijendreṇa guruṇā bhārgavena ca ||
children.translated_text: and had earlier been cursed by the chief Brahmin and by his <s>Bhārgava</s> teacher.
He was summoned by wise <s>Kuntī</s> and rejected by <s>Gāṅgeya</s>;

children.text: śalyena tejasaḥ śāntyai śrāvitaḥ paruṣā giraḥ ||
children.translated_text: and, to quiet his brilliance, <s>Śalya</s> made him hear harsh words.
The steadfast hero was slain through <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>'s strategy by the son of <s>Śakra</s>, with divine weapons;
otherwise, who could have killed that man of mighty valor in battle?
When <s>Nārada</s> had spoken thus, <s>Kuntī</s> addressed the grief-stricken son of <s>Dharma</s>,
firmly shaking off the pain she felt for her own son.
Even when the Sun urged him toward peace, he did not understand, because of fate's power;
he always hated you, and I myself neglected him.

children.text: yātaḥ sa sūryasadanaṃ saṃmukhaṃ samare hataḥ
children.translated_text: Slain face to face in battle, he has gone to the Sun's abode.
Do not grieve. Now enjoy the kingdom you have obtained, without distress.
But, as he reckoned the many virtues of <s>Karṇa</s>, he found no comfort,
and said, "Because our mother concealed him, our elder brother was unknown to us.
For that reason, from now on women will always be broken in steadiness.
There are livelihoods open to us through begging, or through fruits and roots.
How could we abandon those and bring about this dreadful destruction of all?
Out of greed, abandoning <s>dharma</s> (right order), we, senseless men, acted like beggars.
After reflecting on the conduct of our family, we have sold our path to heaven.
Ah, like dogs, we have brought about a dreadful destruction of all.
By petty men a vast quarrel was made, ending only in the wasting away of our bodies.
The ocean of worldly existence has the fierce sea-monster of separation from friends and kinsmen;
free from thirst, I shall cross it on the raft that is the abandonment of attachment.
Let heroic <s>Arjuna</s> protect the earth, out of regard for us.
I abandon this contemptible livelihood, made tasteless by toil."
When the anguished son of <s>Dharma</s> had spoken thus, <s>Dhanañjaya</s>
said, his eyes reddened with anger, looking at the ground for a moment:
"Ah indeed, for those cursed by the gods, even when sufferings end, the joys are excessive pains.
Therefore everyone grieves in every way, cheated by fate.
This <s>saṃnyāsa</s> (renunciation) of yours now will be a laughing-stock in assemblies of good men.
You longed for lost prosperity, and now you abandon prosperity once obtained;
you sink into unmanly acts, with conditions turned upside down.
<s>Saṃnyāsa</s> is called the laziness of procrastinators.
What else in the world is more shameful, or more censured by the wise?

children.text: yatsarvaṃ tyajati kṣipraṃ naraḥ kṣība ivāmbaram
children.translated_text: A man who at once gives up everything is like a drunkard throwing off his garment.
This unprecedented thing begun by you is worse than calamity.
We have never heard of a king who lives on alms.
O king, enjoy this royal fortune that has come to you in due order, without wavering.
Sacrifices, gifts, and the like are the acts only of wealthy, blessed men;

children.text: yathā hi śocyastyaktārtho na tathā tyaktajīvitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: for one who has abandoned wealth is more pitiable than one who has abandoned life.
A man who has lost his life is dead for a moment, but a poor man is always dead.
O king, now that you have won this earth, like <s>Māndhātṛ</s> or <s>Nahuṣa</s>,
perform sacrifices of many kinds, rich in gifts to the priests."
Thus addressed by the son of <s>Śakra</s>, the son of <s>Dharma</s> replied:
"You should listen to me, <s>Pārtha</s>, after giving up longing for vulgar pleasures.
Feeding on pieces of withered leaves, even-minded, tranquil toward what is dear and not dear,
a celibate in the forest among the wandering deer,
I, silent and with grasping fallen away, shall think of nothing at all with my mind.
I shall be without food, a sage, for the cutting off of worldly existence."
As the king was speaking thus, the son of the Wind said to him:

children.text: bata deva jaḍasyeva buddhiste durgrahe dṛḍhā
children.translated_text: "Alas, lord, like that of a dullard, your understanding is fixed on a bad resolution.

children.text: aghātayitvā pṛthivīṃ kiṃ naiṣā dhīstvayā kṛtā ||
children.translated_text: Why was this thought not formed by you before you caused the earth to be slaughtered?
What use is a water-drawing machine when the city has been burned by fire?
O king, you are not in old age; as a renouncer of everything, you do not look well.
You are like an <s>aśoka</s> tree in spring, suddenly with dry shoots.
This earth has been gained by staking life itself, lord, and by toil;
if you abandon it with contempt, what else can be said of that but delusion?
After shaking off the crushing press of obstacles and at last obtaining a treasure,

children.text: padā kṣipasi kiṃ rājangataṃ na prāpyate punaḥ
children.translated_text: why do you kick it with your foot, O king? What has gone is not obtained again.
After bringing back a beloved woman through those many sacrifices of life, though she is fleeting,

children.text: madhumatto yathā śete tathā tvaṃ kartumudyataḥ
children.translated_text: you are preparing to act like a man who lies down drunk on honey.
Your self has been deceived by <s>saṃnyāsa</s>; you ought not abandon your station.
If liberation belonged to those who abandon action, trees would be seen liberated, but they are not.

children.text: kiṃ vānyatpatitāḥ sarve tadaiva vyasane vayam ||
children.translated_text: What else is there? We all fell into calamity at that very moment,

children.text: yadaiva tvaṃ grāmakāmastvaṃ dhātrā jyeṣṭhaḥ kṛto 'si naḥ
children.translated_text: when the Creator made you, a lover of village life, our eldest.
Once in the forest you longed for the village; today, in the village, you are eager for the forest.

children.text: tiṣṭhatyaṅke na ca skandhe kaṣṭaṃ bāla ivāturaḥ
children.translated_text: Like a sick child, you do not stay on the lap or on the shoulder. It is painful.
Householders who possess true character and stand in their own duty are liberated;

children.text: vane kuraṅgamātaṅgā na tu dṛṣṭā divaṃ gatāḥ
children.translated_text: but deer and elephants in the forest have not been seen going to heaven."
When <s>Bhīmasena</s> had spoken thus, <s>Dhanañjaya</s> again said:
"O king, there is liberation at home for blessed men who eat the sacrificial remainder.
In the past, young Brahmin boys, whose beards had not yet appeared,
embraced dispassion before its time, went to the forest, and renounced.
Then <s>Puraṃdara</s>, taking the form of a bird and feeling compassion for them,
praised, within their hearing, householders who eat the sacrificial remainder.
Hearing the speech of that golden bird, those Brahmins
were delighted, and, foolish as they were, considered themselves eaters of the sacrificial remainder."

children.text: śakuniḥ so 'tha taiḥ pṛṣṭo jagāda vihasanniva ||
children.translated_text: Then the bird, questioned by them, spoke as if laughing:
Rough, emaciated, smeared with dirt, living painfully in the forest,
always having only suffering as your portion, you are not true eaters of remnants.
Householders who, evening and morning, divide food according to rule,
and eat what remains after servants and petitioners: they are the blessed eaters of remnants.
For them, through boundless merits, there are eternal worlds in heaven;
from the householder all āśramins live, as creatures live from the cloud.

children.text: evaṃ te bodhitā yuktvā khagarūpeṇa vajriṇā
children.translated_text: Thus instructed by <s>Vajrin</s> in the form of a bird,
the brahmins abandoned forest life and came to their own home.
You know the course of all dharmas and understand the truth of the teachers;
you too, O guardian of the earth, ought not to abandon your station in this way.
When <s>Arjuna</s> had spoken thus, the two sons of <s>Mādrī</s> then said:
Accept the kingdom without hardship, its thorns pulled out.
Victorious in empire and a performer of sacrifices, protect the people, lord of the earth.
When the two Yama-like twins had spoken thus, the dear, loving beloved,
<s>Draupadī</s>, sweet in speech, addressed the son of <s>Dharma</s>:
These heroic brothers of yours, radiant as gods and obedient to your command,

children.text: anutsāhena te paśya likhantyete mṛṣā bhuvam
children.translated_text: see, because of your lack of resolve, are drawing idle lines upon the ground.
That difficult deed which these men performed with strength in battle,
you should now make fruitful by taking up the share of kingship.
For them, downcast, sighing, and distressed that their efforts have proved fruitless,
show honor with affection, applauding their valor.
O king, whose conduct is not cowardly, enjoy the kingdom won by your own arms;

children.text: bhajasva vijayotthānāṃ na klībāḥ saṃpadāṃ padam
children.translated_text: cowards are not the seat of the fortunes that arise from victory.
When <s>Kṛṣṇā</s> had spoken thus, <s>Jiṣṇu</s> again addressed the king:
Kings go to heaven through the proper protection of the world;
subjects engage in their own dharmas through fear of the king's punishment.
Without punishment, people devour one another like fish.
Where punishment stands nearby, dark and red-eyed,
there the riches of dharma increase through the Vedas and sacrifices.
Whatever fruit belongs to sages of peaceful splendor through those various fitting austerities,
that same fruit belongs to the king, the brother of <s>Dharma</s>, who bears the rod of punishment.
Once, when <s>Janaka</s> had turned away from the kingdom and wished to go to the forest,
his wife, a speaker of dharma, spoke sweetly out of love:

children.text: rājanvane na mokṣo 'sti bandho nāsti gṛheṣu ca ||
children.translated_text: O king, liberation is not in the forest, nor is bondage in houses.
For discerning people engaged in their own duty, release is found there.
Shaven-headed men whose craving is unshaven, ochre-clad outside and stained within,
are called, by speakers of dharma in the world, hypocrites bearing the banner of dharma.
Therefore, even while you remain in the kingdom at all times,
the destruction of saṃsṛti can truly be attained by you, happy and unattached.
Thus addressed by his wife, the <s>Maithila</s> attained the state of one liberated while living;
though he had not abandoned the kingdom, he reached the supreme eternal abode.
When <s>Phalguṇa</s> had spoken thus, and when <s>Devasthāna</s> praised
the dharma of active life, the sage <s>Kṛṣṇa-Dvaipāyana</s> also said:
Proper protection of the people is your own dharma, lord of the earth.
For kings, going to the forest at the wrong time is a collapse of order.
Kings beginning with <s>Sudyumna</s> attained perfection by their own nature,
untouched by the hardships of austerity, through the proper bearing of punishment.
Long ago there were two sage brothers, learned in śruti and smṛti,
<s>Śaṅkha</s> and <s>Likhita</s>, whose vows were sharpened by right conduct.
Once, in his brother's hermitage, having himself taken from a tree,
<s>Likhita</s>, through delusion and as if from affection, ate fruits.
Coming up to him, <s>Śaṅkha</s>, distressed by fear of a fall from dharma, said:
Do you not know this is theft? Why eat another's fruit?

children.text: gaccha pāpaṃ kṛtaṃ bhrātaḥ svayaṃ rājñe nivedaya ||
children.translated_text: Go, brother; report the sin you have committed yourself to the king.
Thus addressed by him, <s>Likhita</s> went to <s>Sudyumna</s>, lord of the earth,
and, desiring punishment, himself reported that he had eaten the fruit.
The king said to him: Holy one, you of vast vows,
you are authorities on dharmas; pure one, go, with boons from me.
Although he was addressed in this way even by the king, again and again
he asked only for punishment from the lord of men, fearing a fall from good conduct.
Then the ruler of the earth ordered his hands to be cut off.

children.text: chinnahastaḥ sa ca yayau prahṛṣṭo bhrāturantikam ||
children.translated_text: And he, with hands cut off, went joyfully to his brother's side.
At his word, after bathing again in the river, with a pair of hands newly arisen,
he became, through ascetic power, one whose fever of latent fault was pacified.
<s>Sudyumna</s> too, lord of the people, through the proper bearing of punishment,
obtained worlds fit for austerity, he who was a treasure of fame.
Therefore, O king, standing in kṣatriya dharma, protect the people,

children.text: kṣayaṃ kālakṛtaṃ vīkṣya mā ca śoke manaḥ kṛthāḥ ||
children.translated_text: and seeing the destruction wrought by time, do not set your mind on grief.

children.text: bhūtvā bhūtvā pralīyante kālena kalitāḥ kila
children.translated_text: Again and again they come into being and dissolve, fashioned by time;
the worlds are caught in the meshes of time's portions, and this toil of becoming is strange.
It was said long ago, O king, by the discerning king <s>Senajit</s>:
In suffering one should make the mind firm, the remedy for the sickness of pain and grief.
For those who grieve and lack firmness, peace never arises anywhere.
From sufferings come sufferings, as men's wealth comes from wealth.

children.text: dṛṣṭvā jagati jantūnāṃ kāle kāle bhavābhavam
children.translated_text: Seeing the becoming and passing away of creatures in the world at every time,
what knower of time, what mind that knows truth, would grieve, as over fruits?
Once, when asked by <s>Janaka</s>, the brahmin <s>Aśmaka</s> said:
The discerning do not grieve over things that are by nature perishable.
Among stationary and moving beings no one is seen

children.text: śakto hyāyuṣi maryādāṃ yaḥ kālavihitāṃ bhavet ||
children.translated_text: able to overstep the limit on life that has been fixed by Time.
Wealth, life, the body, birth, and youth likewise
undergo many kinds of reversal of form through the variety of Time.
High things become low, and things joined together fall apart;
low places too become elevated in the course of Time.
Those of low lineage attain nobility, and the wealthy fall into poverty;
fools attain learning, and the fortunate likewise fall into misfortune.
Kings are seen to be short-lived, and poor men to live a hundred years;
experts in <s>rasāyana</s> (rejuvenation) are seen broken by old age.
The rich are tormented by disease, while the poor are free from illness;
knowers of <s>āyurveda</s> die while still young.
Fools are devoted to good conduct, and scholars are devoid of <s>dharma</s>;
such reversals, struck down by Time, indeed come to pass.
Even the gods, beginning with four-faced <s>Brahmā</s>, makers of the three worlds,

children.text: na hi kālakaṭākṣeṇa lakṣitaṃ rakṣituṃ kṣamāḥ ||
children.translated_text: are not able to protect one marked by the glance of Time.
For the prosperous and for those without wealth, for the wise and for the dull-minded,
the price in Time's market is the same, for it has no attachment.
For embodied beings, shaken by the wind of Time in the forest of becoming,
comings and goings constantly arise with one another, as for trees.
If what has met by chance also perishes by chance,

children.text: śokaḥ kiṃ tatra jantūnāṃ satataṃ hi gatāgatam ||
children.translated_text: what grief is there for living beings? There is always coming and going.

children.text: na viyogeṣu saṃtāpaḥ kāryaḥ kila vivekibhiḥ
children.translated_text: The wise should not make anguish over separations;
for in existence, things experience nonexistence and are destroyed in a moment.
Having related what had thus been said by <s>Aśmaka</s>, the great sage
fell silent when he saw <s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s>'s grief was deep.
Then, urged affectionately by <s>Arjuna</s>, the lotus-eyed one,
the blessed enemy of <s>Kaiṭabha</s> addressed the son of <s>Dharma</s>:
Do not uselessly make despondency, O king, drying up your body;
those slain heroes will not return because of grief.
Some go today, others in the morning, still others afterward, and yet others later;

children.text: sarve niḥsīmni saṃsāre yānti kaḥ kena śocyate ||
children.translated_text: all go in boundless <s>saṃsāra</s>. Who is to be grieved for by whom?
Surely everyone, through delusion, thinks himself imperishable,
since, though destruction stands before him, he himself is perishable and grieves for the lost.

children.text: te janāste prabhāvāśca tāśca prajvalitāḥ śriyaḥ
children.translated_text: Those people, those powers, and those blazing fortunes
have indeed been brought by Time, with ease, to being only a remnant in memory.
Once this blessed <s>Nārada</s>, consoling out of compassion
King <s>Sṛñjaya</s>, who was afflicted by grief for his son, said:
O king, why do you grieve for a son who reached his appointed limit and has gone?
The whole world, together with us, will not exist in the end.
King <s>Marutta</s>, guardian of the earth, went to death through Time;
at his sacrificial assembly the gods, together with <s>Indra</s>, were seated on earth.
For him <s>Pākaśāsana</s> rained down gold for a year,
and <s>Saṃvarta</s>, the brother of <s>Bṛhaspati</s>, was his officiating priest.
<s>Suhotra</s> too, lord of the earth, has become only the remainder of a tale;
by rains of gold he made the earth truly wealthy.
And King <s>Bṛhadratha</s>, foremost of chariot-warriors, has gone to his setting;

children.text: yasya yajñe surapatiḥ somaṃ pītvā mudaṃ yayau ||
children.translated_text: at his sacrifice the lord of the gods drank soma and rejoiced.
<s>Śibi Auśīnara</s> ruled the earth under one umbrella;
that foremost bearer among all givers has gone to being only fame.
With a thousand horse-sacrifices and a hundred <s>rājasūya</s> rites

children.text: īje yaḥ so 'pi bharataḥ kālena tridivaṃ gataḥ ||
children.translated_text: he sacrificed; that <s>Bharata</s> too went to heaven through Time.
And <s>Rāma</s>, son of <s>Daśaratha</s>, destroyer of the ten-necked one's lineage,
has reached the path of the end, his virtues sung by the gods.
King <s>Bhagīratha</s>, by whose austerity <s>Jāhnavī</s>
reached the head of <s>Śaṃkara</s>, departed by the will of Time.
That King <s>Dilīpa</s> too has attained the state of memory,
at whose golden sacrificial post the dwellers in heaven danced.
And <s>Māndhātā</s>, not womb-born, that all-conquering king,
has gone, whose lovely valor was admired by gods beginning with <s>Śakra</s>.
King <s>Yayāti</s> too came to destruction through Time,
the hero who in the battle of gods and demons slew the enemies of the immortals.
And King <s>Ambarīṣa</s> entered the body of fame,
whose unfading command kings bore like a garland.
King <s>Śaśabindu</s> too has taken refuge in the final state;
he had a hundred crores of sons, radiant like <s>Śakra</s>.
King <s>Gaya</s> has gone, he who gave a golden earth

children.text: pradadau yasya saṃkhyāṃ ca yajñānāṃ na pracakṣate ||
children.translated_text: and whose sacrifices they do not even state by number.
<s>Rantideva</s> too has departed; in his sacrifices, with the hides of animals

children.text: srutaiḥ pravartitā tena puṇyā carmaṇvatī nadī ||
children.translated_text: streaming, the holy river <s>Carmaṇvatī</s> was set flowing by him.

children.text: atītaḥ sa ca bhūpālaḥ sagaro yena sāgarāḥ
children.translated_text: And that King <s>Sagara</s> has passed, by whom the oceans
were made through sixty thousand sons who guarded the sacrificial horse.
And <s>Vainya</s>, who with the tip of his bow made the mountains separate,

children.text: so 'pi śakrādhipo rājā priyaṃ tatyāja vigraham ||
children.translated_text: that king, a lord over even <s>Śakra</s>, abandoned his dear body.

children.text: ete cānye ca bhūpālāḥ kālena kavalīkṛtāḥ
children.translated_text: These and other kings were swallowed by Time.

children.text: mā śucas tava madvākyātputraḥ sṛñjaya jīvatu ||
children.translated_text: Do not grieve; at my word, O <s>Sṛñjaya</s>, your son shall live.
Having said this, <s>Nārada</s> [turned to] the king's son, <s>Kanakaṣṭhīvin</s>...
After reviving him, that treasure of compassion made him live for a thousand years.
"How did that golden-spitting son of <s>Sṛñjaya</s> come to be?
Asked this by the son of <s>Dharma</s>, the four-armed one spoke again.
In the house of <s>Sṛñjaya</s>, king of the earth, <s>Nārada</s> and <s>Parvata</s>,
two divine seers wandering in the mortal world, were staying.
"Everything present in the heart must be told by each to the other": making this agreement,
the two remained there together, full of affection and attachment.
For service to them <s>Sṛñjaya</s> appointed his daughter, adorned with beauty,
the delicate <s>Sukumārī</s>, whose name was true to its meaning.
As that young girl, with eyes lovely as a doe's, was attending on them,
<s>Nārada</s>, gazing without blinking, became troubled by love.

children.text: taṃ tasya hṛdgataṃ bhāvaṃ gūhamānasya lajjayā
children.translated_text: Although he hid that feeling in his heart out of shame,
his sister's son <s>Parvata</s> quickly understood it with the eye of knowledge.
Angry at the breach of propriety, he then cursed his uncle:
"You will become the husband of this <s>Sukumārī</s> in the form of a monkey."

children.text: iti tena ruṣā śaptaḥ kopāttamapi nāradaḥ
children.translated_text: Thus cursed by him in anger, <s>Nārada</s>, angry too,
cursed his sister's son: "May you become one who does not reach heaven."
Then in time, when the maiden had been given by <s>Sṛñjaya</s>,
<s>Nārada</s> received her at the wedding and at once became such as he had been cursed to be.
She too, the faithful wife, having obtained <s>Nārada</s> as a husband in that form,
regarded him, with undivided mind, as a stream of nectar for her eyes.
When the turmoil of anger had subsided, they appeased their curses toward one another,

children.text: prītyā babhūvatuḥ svasthau tau parityajya vikriyām ||
children.translated_text: and, abandoning the alteration of form, the two became calm again through affection.
And <s>Sukumārī</s>, devoted to her husband, approached <s>Nārada</s>, who had put off the monkey form,
hesitantly, after she had learned that story only after a long time.

children.text: ataḥ śeṣāṃ kathāmeṣa svayaṃ vadatu nāradaḥ
children.translated_text: "Therefore let <s>Nārada</s> himself tell the rest of this story."
When <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> had said this and fallen silent, <s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s> questioned him.
Questioned by him, the sage said: "Thus I, accompanied by <s>Parvata</s>,
stayed in <s>Sṛñjaya</s>'s house and became well pleased.
Then, by our boon, a son was born to King <s>Sṛñjaya</s>,

children.text: yathārthaṃ kāñcanaṣṭhīvī na sehe taṃ śatakratuḥ ||
children.translated_text: the aptly named golden-spitter; <s>Śatakratu</s> could not endure him.
By chance, as that child was absorbed in play on the bank of the <s>Jāhnavī</s>,
the lord of the gods killed him with the thunderbolt in the form of a tiger.
Seeing his lotus-eyed son killed, <s>Sṛñjaya</s>
lamented, his mind overwhelmed by fainting from terrible distress.
Seeing that lord of the earth distraught and noisy with lamentation,
out of compassion I revived his son, the golden-spitter.
By my boon, after enjoying this earth for a thousand-year span of life,

children.text: kālena yātastridivaṃ sthāyino na hi dehinaḥ ||
children.translated_text: he went in time to heaven; embodied beings are not permanent."
When <s>Nārada</s> had told this, and <s>Vyāsa</s> too had repeatedly
instructed the grief-stricken son of <s>Dharma</s>, he spoke again:
"Shame on me, blinded by greed and fallen into this peril of sin,
by whom, through hope of enjoyments, the destruction of elders, kinsmen, and sons was brought about.

children.text: punaḥ punarimāṃ hutvā vahnau pātakinīṃ tanum
children.translated_text: Even if I cast this sinful body again and again into the fire,

children.text: kṣayaṃ yāsyati manye no na bhīṣmavadhapātakam ||
children.translated_text: I think the sin of killing <s>Bhīṣma</s> will not be destroyed."
To <s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s>, lamenting thus and seized by the fire of grief,
the sage, son of <s>Parāśara</s>, spoke for the stability of the world:
"For kings who live by battle, the killing of enemies is always <s>dharma</s> (duty).

children.text: kṛtvā kulocitaṃ karma mā viṣādaṃ vṛthā kṛthāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Having done the action proper to your lineage, do not grieve in vain.
By recitations, remorse, and powerful acts of <s>prāyaścitta</s> (expiation),
and by gifts and ablutions at sacred fords, there is release from sins.
But if, O king, you falsely suspect that you are stained by abandoning your own <s>dharma</s>,
then sacrifice with the horse sacrifice.
Rule the subjects with confidence, and also the women whose protectors have been slain;
look upon the maidens of those whose enemy-sons were killed as upon sons.

children.text: iti bruvāṇo bhagavānrājñā pṛṣṭo muniḥ punaḥ
children.translated_text: As the venerable sage was speaking thus, and was questioned again by the king,
he, whose agitation had become quiet, spoke of the pacification of all sins.
Through failure to perform good deeds and through the practice of condemned ones,
a man, coming to remorse, becomes fit for <s>prāyaścitta</s> (expiation).
A skull-bearer, going for twelve years uncovered and living on alms,
is freed at the end of the vow from the terrible fear of brahmin-slaying.
Sins equal to this, people say, embodied beings cross beyond
by sacrifices with abundant sacrificial fees and by gifts of a thousand cows.
The sin of liquor-drinkers is expiated by drinking liquor like fire;
one who has violated the guru's bed is freed by lying on a bed of flame-colored fire.
By throwing oneself from a precipice or into fire, and by the great departure,
and, for donors, by the gift of earth, a grave sin is destroyed.

children.text: prāyaścittaṃ na tu strīṇāṃ rajasā saṃvṛtā hitāḥ
children.translated_text: But for women there is no <s>prāyaścitta</s> (expiation); protected by menstruation,
they become pure in disposition, like rivers through a great flood.
Through deliberation over what may and may not be eaten, and through distinction between what should and should not be done,
this subtle confusion of <s>dharma</s>, proclaimed as prescribed and forbidden, arises.
Take delight in your own kingdom, accept the subjects as well,

children.text: gaccha śāntanavaṃ bhīṣmaṃ sa te dharmānpravakṣyati ||
children.translated_text: and go to <s>Bhīṣma</s>, son of <s>Śāntanu</s>; he will teach you the <s>dharmas</s>."
Thus addressed by <s>Dvaipāyana</s> and awakened by <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>,
he placed <s>Dhṛtarāṣṭra</s> before him and entered the city with his followers.
Honored by the subjects and sung by <s>Māgadha</s> bards,
he reached the capital and entered the beautiful assembly hall,
the brahmins who had come there in person, rich in abundant blessings.
He honored <s>Dhaumya</s>, setting him foremost as the chief among household priests.
Meanwhile a false ascetic, marked by a triple staff and wearing three crests,
a rākṣasa named <s>Cārvāka</s>, friend of <s>Duryodhana</s>, arrived.
He said to <s>Dharmaja</s>, "O king, I speak to you by command of the Brahmins:
what use is a kingdom to you, traitor to kinsmen and friends, your splendor ruined?"

children.text: iti bruvāṇe cārvāke viṣaṇṇe ca yudhiṣṭhire
children.translated_text: As <s>Cārvāka</s> spoke thus, and <s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s> grew dejected,
those Brahmins, filled with anger, came to know him through the eye of knowledge.
"This is the rākṣasa named <s>Cārvāka</s>, friend of <s>Duryodhana</s>."
Having said this, the twice-born made him ashes by a mere hūṃkāra.
When that night-roamer had been burned by the anger of the Brahmins,
<s>Śauri</s> spoke, laughing, as if scattering nectar.
"Invulnerable to all beings through a boon from <s>Brahmā</s>,
this night-roamer ascetic became fuel for the fire of Brahmin anger.
By good fortune that sinner has been slain by the splendor of the speakers of brahman."
When <s>Govinda</s> had spoken thus, a festival arose in the assembly.
Then the consecration of the son of <s>Dharma</s> took place by a divine rite,
like that of the god <s>Śatakratu</s> after <s>Vṛtra</s> had been slain.
On a seat broad as <s>Sumeru</s>, embraced by the fortune of victory,
he shone like the sun, lovely with the radiance of lamps and twilight.
First maintaining <s>Dhṛtarāṣṭra</s>, together with the women, as if he were a deity,
and installing the mighty-armed son of the Wind, <s>Bhīma</s>, as heir-apparent,
he appointed <s>Vidura</s> to affairs of counsel and <s>Dhanaṃjaya</s> to campaigns of conquest,
<s>Saṃjaya</s> to the supervision of expenditure, and <s>Nakula</s> to the protection of the army.
He appointed <s>Dhaumya</s> to Brahmin affairs and <s>Sahadeva</s> to attendance near him,
and he assigned the elder ministers to the appropriate duties.
Then, having praised <s>Hṛṣīkeśa</s>, the son of <s>Dharma</s>
gave <s>Duryodhana</s>'s residence, splendid with priceless jewels, to <s>Bhīma</s>.
The king gave <s>Duḥśāsana</s>'s house, surrounded by thousands of maidservants,
a mansion rich with jewels and gold, to <s>Arjuna</s>.
Having in this way distributed the row of <s>Kaurava</s> dwellings to the others too,
he brought about settled appeasement, standing by the judgment of the discus-armed one.

children.text: tato vidhāya bandhūnāṃ rājā śrāddhaṃ yathāvidhi
children.translated_text: Then the king performed the śrāddha for his kinsmen according to rule,
and for their sake he established meritorious works marked by water-stations, wells, and drinking places.
Then at dawn the king honored the son of <s>Ambikā</s>,

children.text: gāndhārīṃ svāṃ ca jananīṃ praṇamya racitāñjaliḥ ||
children.translated_text: and, bowing with joined hands to <s>Gāndhārī</s> and to his own mother,
he went with his attendants to see the lotus-eyed one, resting in <s>Arjuna</s>'s residence,
as <s>Vāsava</s> would go to see <s>Brahmā</s>.
Approaching him, dark as the sky and pervaded by the radiance of the <s>Kaustubha</s>,
with the splendor of the beginning of day made noble by the sun's rays,
seated on a golden seat vast as the peak of <s>Sumeru</s>,
as if enveloped by the circle of his own radiance, in a yellow garment,
the lord of the earth spoke to him, who was bowed in meditation on something,
as if scattering the nectar of joy at seeing him by the brightness of his teeth.
"Blessed lord, did your night pass comfortably,
with rows of bees playing in the lake of your yogic sleep?"
When <s>Kamalākānta</s>, absorbed in a certain meditation,
said nothing at all after being addressed thus, then the king spoke again:
"Ah, soul of all beings, you are indeed the object of meditation for seers of truth;
taking up stainless meditation, you fill us with wonder.
Is there welfare for the worlds?" As the king was saying this,
the one whose form is the universe slightly opened his eyes and addressed him:
"<s>Bhīṣma</s>, lying on the bed of arrows, has begun today to praise me.
I have gone in mind to him, who is honored by all the wise.

children.text: sa me bahumataḥ śrīmānyoginaṃ cintayāmi tam
children.translated_text: That glorious one is highly esteemed by me; I am thinking of that yogin.

children.text: ye māṃ smaranti satataṃ dehatyāge smarāmi tān ||
children.translated_text: Those who remember me constantly, I remember them at the abandonment of the body.
The sun has now almost entered its affection for the northern quarter;
this is the time for <s>Devavrata</s>, who seeks liberation, to release the body."
Hearing this, the son of <s>Dharma</s>, with joined hands turned by affection,
said, "Blessed lord, <s>Bhīṣma</s> deserves the sight of you.

children.text: tadehi sarve gacchāmastaṃ draṣṭuṃ tejasāṃ nidhim
children.translated_text: So come; let us all go to see that treasury of splendors.
He, the cutter of all doubts, will proclaim knowledge to me."
Thus addressed by <s>Dharmarāja</s>, <s>Hari</s>, together with <s>Phalguṇa</s>,
and with <s>Bhīma</s>, <s>Sātyaki</s>, and the others foremost among them, set out in a chariot.
At that moment <s>Bhīṣma</s>, surrounded by all the hosts of sages,

children.text: tuṣṭāva prayato dhyātvā viṣṇuṃ jiṣṇuṃ jagaddviṣām ||
children.translated_text: intent and meditating, praised <s>Viṣṇu</s>, victorious over the enemies of the world:
"Homage to <s>Hari</s>, the divine tree of nirvāṇa against the scorching desert of <s>saṃsāra</s>,
to <s>Hari</s>, the lion against the herd of elephant-like delusions.
