the jackal, clever only for his own interest, came near and spoke again:
In this world, now devoid of kinsmen, my mind has no confidence,
where men abandon a little son and go away as if he were a piece of wood.
An old man departs through fear for himself; a child is abandoned in a lonely place.
Who in this world should place trust in people devoted to their own interest?
So the two, the vulture and the jackal, emaciated by hunger, spoke for the sake of food:

children.text: divā gṛdhrasya bhojyaṃ yadrātrau gomāyukasya tat ||
children.translated_text: what was the vulture's food by day was the jackal's by night.
Meanwhile the blessed son of <s>Ambikā</s>,
wandering at his own will and granting boons, came there and revived that boy.

children.text: śatāyuṣaṃ skandavarātte yayuḥ prāpya taṃ sutam
children.translated_text: Receiving that son, endowed with a hundred-year life-span by <s>Skanda</s>'s boon, they went away;
and by the Lord's glance the vulture and the jackal also obtained welfare.
Thus, for the wise and resolute, whose nature is not dejection,
desired ends are suddenly accomplished by the Lord's command.
A weak man, relying on pride, should not make enmity with a strong one;
the great śalmali tree perished through rivalry with <s>Vāyu</s>.
Broad with spreading branches, a shelter for travelers scorched on the road,
there was a śalmali tree on a slope of <s>Himavat</s>, kissing the sky.

children.text: papraccha nāradaḥ prītyā taṃ yadṛcchāgato muniḥ
children.translated_text: The sage <s>Nārada</s>, arriving there by chance, asked it with delight:
Ah, surely your splendor of leaves, flowers, and fruits is dense and unbroken.

children.text: manye tava paraṃ mittraṃ vāyuryenāsi rakṣyase
children.translated_text: I think <s>Vāyu</s> is your supreme friend, by whom you are protected;
trees overwhelmed by his force split apart and fall.
Hearing this, the śalmali, handsome with its trunk and blinded by pride, said:

children.text: citraṃ mune na jānīṣe bale tulyo na me 'nilaḥ ||
children.translated_text: It is strange, sage, that you do not know: <s>Anila</s> is not equal to me in strength.
When that tree had spoken thus in boastfulness again and again,
<s>Nārada</s> went and reported just that to <s>Pavana</s>.
Agitated with anger at his words, the vast wind of destruction

children.text: śvo draṣṭāsīti taṃ vṛkṣaṃ samabhyetya tadābravīt ||
children.translated_text: came to that tree and said, 'Tomorrow you will see.'
Then during the night, out of terror, that intelligent śalmali reflected,
and of itself shed its branches before the storm of mighty force.
Then in the morning <s>Vāyu</s> came and saw
the śalmali broken by itself, covered with all its branches cut to pieces.

children.text: aho nu dhanyamantro 'si buddhyā tvaṃ rakṣitastaro
children.translated_text: Ah, tree, you have a fortunate counsel; you have been protected by your intelligence,
said <s>Vāyu</s>, and, his anger gone, he departed as he had come.

children.text: lobhe eva mahatpāpaṃ jñānameva paraṃ mahaḥ
children.translated_text: Greed alone is a great sin; knowledge alone is the supreme light.

children.text: dama eva parā śāntistapa eva paraṃ padam ||
children.translated_text: Self-restraint alone is the highest peace; austerity alone is the supreme state.
Truth alone is the highest merit; restraining anger is the better course.
Non-cruelty is the highest <s>dharma</s>; this is the essence of those who teach <s>dharma</s>.
For embodied beings, through the various expiations prescribed by <s>śruti</s> and <s>smṛti</s>,
through recitation, service at sacred fords, and gifts, sin is destroyed.

children.text: brahmahā dvādaśa samāḥ kapālāṅko vrataṃ caret
children.translated_text: A killer of a Brahmin should perform the vow for twelve years, marked with a skull;
a killer of an embryo, cut down by a sword face to face in battle, is released.
Those who have violated a guru's bed cross beyond sin when killed for the sake of Brahmins;
kings are released from all sins by the horse sacrifice.
In the teachings of the son of <s>Dharma</s>, in the incidental tale told by the mongoose,
then, when asked, <s>Bhīṣma</s> spoke of the origin of the sword.
In ancient times, when the world was afflicted by asuras, on a peak of <s>Himavat</s>,

children.text: svayaṃbhūr bhagavān khaḍgo dhātrā dhyātaḥ samāyayau ||
children.translated_text: the blessed sword itself came forth, meditated upon by the Creator.
Tall and dark like a blue lotus, surveying the worlds,
it came to be in the hand-tip of the three-eyed god through <s>Brahmā</s>'s word.

children.text: tena niṣkaṇṭakaṃ kṛtvā rudro raudreṇa tejasā
children.translated_text: With it <s>Rudra</s>, by his fierce splendor, made the world free of thorns,
and afterwards the moon-crested one became auspicious in form toward the world.

children.text: taṃ khaḍgaṃ lebhire bhūpā manuprabhṛtayaḥ kramāt
children.translated_text: Kings beginning with <s>Manu</s> obtained that sword in succession,
by the fall of whose edge embodied beings have no rebirth.

children.text: śrutveti mandiraṃ pārtho gatvā bhīṣmagiraḥ smaran
children.translated_text: Having heard this, <s>Pārtha</s> went to his house, remembering <s>Bhīṣma</s>'s words,
and held conversations with <s>Vidura</s>, who declared the whole essence of <s>dharma</s>.
Among them, with <s>Vidura</s> as the sixth, there arose various discussions,
resting on <s>dharma</s>, desire, and wealth, among men whose conduct was purely righteous.
Then <s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s> came again and asked <s>Bhīṣma</s>,

children.text: sauhārdaṃ kena na calediti pṛṣṭo 'bravīcca saḥ ||
children.translated_text: 'By what does friendship not waver?' Asked thus, he replied:
With grateful, good, honorable, noble, and unfailing people,
the affection of the virtuous does not perish, for they are wholly intent on receiving virtues.
One should avoid betrayers of friends, ingrates, and those of crooked intention.
I do not see, O king, any sin equal to ingratitude.
Proud, of impure conduct, devoid of Vedic teaching,
a man of the central country, dark-bodied, turned away from character and proper behavior,
there was formerly a polluted brahma-bandhu named <s>Gautama</s>.
Living attached to a Śabara woman on the frontiers and seeking wealth,
he wandered over the earth; separated from a caravan, he entered a forest.
In that place, shaded by moist trees and filled with cheerful tawny elephants,
he sat down for shade at the foot of a banyan tree.
There was a crane named <s>Nāḍījaṅgha</s>, swift and of excellent Buddhist-like vows;
seeing him destitute, and filled with compassion, he bent down and said:
I will burn away this sleepless poverty of yours, worthy of a brahmin.
Go from here to my friend <s>Virūpākṣa</s>, lord of the rākṣasas.

children.text: kārtikyāṃ sa hi dātṝṇāṃ dhuryo dāsyati te dhanam
children.translated_text: At the <s>Kārttikī</s> festival he, foremost among givers, will give you wealth,
when he has heard that you are mine. Hearing this from the compassionate one, he went there,
obtained abundant gold from him, and quickly returned.
Seeing the crane there, satisfied with his wealth, he thought:
This gold cannot be eaten in a forest where there is no trade.
So now I shall strike down this very crane, for he is very fat.
Having pondered for a long time in this way, that lowest of twice-born men, wanting provisions for the road,
bent under his load of gold, killed him as he slept, though his heart was guileless.
Then the rākṣasa king, distressed by his disappearance,
sent out a circle of spies in his suspicion and reached that brahmin.

children.text: hataṃ tena bakaṃ jñātvā nijagrāha tamutkaṭam
children.translated_text: Knowing that the crane had been killed by him, he seized that fierce man,
and the sky-going bird regained life through the foam of the heavenly river.
When <s>Nāḍījaṅgha</s> saw <s>Gautama</s>, struck down for his offense,
he revived that evildoer too; anger toward the low is not found in the good.
Thus was the conduct of the ungrateful <s>Gautama</s>: he killed one of excellent vows.

children.text: jaghāna pāpe pāpānāṃ niḥśaṅkaṃ ramate manaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Among sinners, the mind of sinners sports fearlessly in sin.
Thieves of deposits, killers of cows, women, teachers, and brahmins

children.text: dharmiṣṭhā iva yasyāgre sa kṛtaghno vicāryatām ||
children.translated_text: seem very righteous beside him; consider such a man the ungrateful one.
Then <s>Dharmarāja</s> asked the grandsire, knower of dharma:
How should one whose wealth and kin have been destroyed take refuge in dharma?

children.text: sa tena pṛṣṭaḥ provāca śṛṇu senajitaṃ nṛpam
children.translated_text: Questioned by him, he replied: Listen to King <s>Senajit</s>.
When that king was overwhelmed by grief for his son, a certain brahmin came to him, knew his state, and said:
All beings in this existence are born only for non-existence.
You too will in time be a cause for grief; how then do you grieve, O king?
If someone has come together with you by chance and has gone away by chance,
what is this deluded confusion over separation on the road of <s>saṃsāra</s>?
Attachment toward those seen for but a moment is born for the sorrow of embodied beings.

children.text: mamāyamiti mugdhānāṃ na sa teṣāṃ na tasya te ||
children.translated_text: For the foolish who say 'this is mine,' he is not theirs, nor are they his.
Beings grieve while desiring what is not obtained, and grieve over what is obtained when it is ill-fated;

children.text: naṣṭaṃ śocanti duḥkhārtā jantavaḥ sukhinaḥ kadā ||
children.translated_text: afflicted by pain, they grieve over what is lost. When are creatures happy?
The wise do not become attached to wealth, sons, or wives,

children.text: avaśyaṃ viprayogo hi taiḥ paraiśca nṛṇāṃ sadā ||
children.translated_text: for separation from them, as from others, is always inevitable for men.
Who would not think union with loved ones to be like nectar,
if, in separations, they were not terrible as poison and cutters of the vital parts?
Long ago the courtesan <s>Piṅgalā</s>, waiting for her lover who had given an assignation,
thought long on him when he did not come, and alone at night said to herself:
What use is he even if he comes, since he will bring sorrow in separation?
I shall turn to the beloved who is here within, undecaying and beyond grief.
Thus her anguish from that curse was calmed by the nectar of contentment,
and <s>Piṅgalā</s>, as if awakened, slept in the supreme abode.
What happiness is there while human life passes like a current?
Asked thus by <s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s>, the grandsire spoke again:
Long ago a brahmin father, questioned about this by his son <s>Medhāvin</s>,
said: Having completed study, one should be a celibate student and then a householder.
Having become free of debt to the ancestors through sons, and then drinking only air in the forest,
as a sage, equal toward friend and enemy, one goes to the supreme state.
Hearing that, the son said: All this action is blameless,

children.text: ślāghyāya śreyase karma yadi kālaḥ pratīkṣate ||
children.translated_text: leading to praiseworthy welfare, if Time will wait.
For those whose own tasks are unfinished, life is short and unsealed;
by the count of days and nights alone it flows away unseen.
This Time, who has counted everything, does not delay even for a moment for beings,
though entreated, like a caravan traveling very far.
A wise man should not delay even half a moment in his duties;
we do not know when or upon whom Death will fall.
Not out of affection, not out of compassion, not out of usefulness, not out of respect
can Time bear to wait for embodied beings whose tasks remain unfinished.

children.text: mṛtyunā yasya sauhārdaṃ yo na vettyāyuṣo 'vadhim
children.translated_text: Only speech such as 'I shall do this tomorrow' is fitting for one
who has friendship with Death and who does not know the limit of his life.
Ah, this negligence belongs to a world stupefied by delusion:
after seeing a child dead, an old man remains fearless.

children.text: nave vayasi bhogārhe naveṣu vibhaveṣu ca
children.translated_text: In fresh youth, when pleasures are fit to be enjoyed, amid new wealth,

children.text: navoḍheṣu ca dāreṣu hriyate mṛtyunā janaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and with newly married wives, a person is carried off by Death.
Therefore what is wholesome should be done first, for the pacification of <s>saṃsāra</s>,
for the conjunction of body and embodied self is unstable, rocking like a crossing wave.
Then, asked by <s>Dharmarāja</s> about the division of happiness and sorrow
among rich and poor people, the son of <s>Śantanu</s> spoke again:
Long ago a wise brahmin named <s>Śampāka</s> said:
People are exceedingly tormented by thirsting desire; contentment is a stream of nectar.
Unacquainted with fear, free from anxiety, able to sleep, and free from disease,
a poor man is always happy, performing his acts with whatever he has obtained.

children.text: sukhamāste sukhaṃ śete sukhaṃ ca pratibudhyate
children.translated_text: He sits happily, sleeps happily, and wakes happily,
content, free from toil, free from danger, and free from sickness.
But of a rich man, filled with arrogance, looking crookedly from a frown,
his complexion is pale and thin from worry over guarding the wealth stored in his jars.
For a thief, afraid of the king, who does evil for the sake of gain,
and for a man afflicted by the disease of indigestion, spitting and yet longing for food,
for one whose wife is dried up by greed and who shares in misery as its only fruit,
what talk of rivalry is there with those who always feed on the nectar of non-possession?
A wealthy man thinks himself equal to <s>Śakra</s> and <s>Vaiśravaṇa</s>
only so long as he is not seized by thieves or by the anger of kings.
When abundant wealth and well-furnished houses are passing away,
the painful cholera of sorrow belongs to the rich rather than to the poor.
When an undertaking has come to failure, what should a man eager for wealth do?
Asked this by the king, the son of <s>Śantanu</s> reflected and said,
Listen to the remedy for grief at a time when wealth has been lost.
Long ago there was a twice-born man named <s>Maṅki</s>, who repeatedly sought wealth,
but, though he made efforts, did not obtain it, because fate had turned away in disdain.
His resources exhausted, he then bought two bulls with what wealth remained,
and himself undertook ploughing in the field, having a large load to draw.
Meanwhile a broad-necked camel, awakened from broken sleep, rose up;
that great-bodied camel carried off the two bulls, hanging from its shoulder.
When he saw the two bulls hanging there through the lifting of the yoke,
suspended by that strong one, the twice-born man's son, stricken with grief, lamented:

children.text: aho nu citravarṇāṅkau mama vatsatarau priyau
children.translated_text: Ah, my dear young bulls, with limbs of variegated color!
The camel shines as it drags them, like two ornaments rich with jewels.
Having spoken thus, with a deep disposition toward <s>vairāgya</s> (dispassion) born of disenchantment,
he at once condemned craving, his fever of latent passion calmed.
Alas, craving is a source of humiliation for living beings and leads to misery;
deceived by it, all people grieve day and night.

children.text: alabdhaṃ vāñchatāṃ vittaṃ labdhaṃ ca parirakṣatām
children.translated_text: For men who desire wealth not yet obtained, who guard what has been obtained,

children.text: naṣṭaṃ ca śocatāṃ puṃsāṃ kadā duḥkhaṃ nivartate ||
children.translated_text: and who grieve over what has been lost, when does suffering ever cease?
Desire for objects is the root of calamity; contentment is the highest happiness.
To my mind, the desireless and the desirous are like a healthy man and a sick man.
A man with wealth is watched anxiously by the king, by a robber, and by his own people;
but a poor man, though called deficient, is not reckoned by the world in that way.
Therefore the minds of those who have abandoned desires, who are rich in the wealth of contentment,
are not overcome by loss, gain, expense, or toil.
This has been obtained, this has been lost, this I shall obtain again,
while embodied beings think only of this, their life grows old.

children.text: adhunā lobhamunmūlya spṛhāṃ dūre nirasya ca
children.translated_text: Now, uprooting greed and casting longing far away,
I shall become free from delusion, a sage to whom dear and unpleasant things are equal.

children.text: tyāgo hi hanti vyasanaṃ tathā hi janakaḥ purā
children.translated_text: For renunciation destroys misfortune; indeed, long ago <s>Janaka</s>,
even while his city was burning, did not undergo any alteration through grief.
Having reflected thus for a long time, <s>Maṅki</s>, his mind calmed by disenchantment,
abandoned the noose of hope and attained the supreme state.
After hearing this, the son of <s>Dharma</s> again addressed the son of <s>Śantanu</s>,
asking, How should a living being live free from sorrow?
He said: Listen, O king. Long ago <s>Prahlāda</s>, lord of the <s>Dānavas</s>,
spoke to a brahmin, ever blissful and wandering at will:
In this vast ocean of wealth, with hundreds of whirlpools of pleasure and pain,
how, brahmin, are you seen unspoiled and always content?

children.text: keyaṃ ślāghyatarā vṛttiḥ ko vāyaṃ vibhavo dhiyaḥ
children.translated_text: What is this most praiseworthy way of life? What is this power of understanding,
that, sporting and roaming in this world, you remain unattached and are not stained?
Asked thus by him, the broad-minded twice-born man replied,
I wander impartial toward all conditions, always satisfied.
Knowing all this to be the play of <s>māyā</s> (illusion), the bewilderment of <s>saṃsāra</s>,

children.text: kṣayodayeṣu bhūtānāṃ na duḥkhaṃ na sukhaṃ bhaje ||
children.translated_text: I partake of neither sorrow nor happiness amid the decline and rise of beings.

children.text: āyuṣāṃ vibhavānāṃ ca bhāvānāṃ ca svabhāvataḥ
children.translated_text: Seeing the insubstantiality, by nature, of lifespans, fortunes,
and states of being, I do not grieve over them and am free from pain.
Sometimes I enjoy various pleasures; at another time I am without food.
I may be naked, or clad in rags, or dressed in costly garments.
I may sleep on the earth with my arm for a pillow, or on a couch;
equal through tranquility and self-restraint, I maintain the <s>ājagara</s> vow.
Knowing the higher and lower nature of things, fixed like an anvil, free from longing,
having abandoned delusion, fear, and hatred, I practice the <s>ājagara</s> vow.
A python swallows whatever comes to it: a deer, a buffalo, an elephant;
when nothing comes, it maintains an untroubled, motionless state.
Taking up this python-like way of life, with a stainless disposition,
settled in clarity, I do not worry about gain and loss, happiness and unhappiness.
Having heard the brahmin say this, <s>Prahlāda</s>, his mind filled with wonder,
praised that state of his, the condition of one liberated while living.
After hearing this, the son of <s>Pāṇḍu</s> again addressed <s>Bhīṣma</s>:
Grandfather, of family, action, wealth, and understanding, which is best?
Asked thus by the king, the son of <s>Jāhnavī</s> replied,
Wisdom alone stands above, surpassing all virtues.
Long ago a merchant, swollen with the pride of wealth, was traveling in a carriage,
and on the road he knocked down the very thin sage <s>Kaśyapa</s>.
Thrown to the ground by him, whose cheeks bore swinging earrings,
he grieved over himself as poor and made a resolve to die.
To him, lying in the dust, wretched, and vowed to abandon his life,
<s>Śakra</s>, out of compassion, came in the form of a jackal to speak.
He said, 'Alas, surely no one in <s>saṃsāra</s> has contentment,
since, though your conduct is bright, O sage, you do not think highly of yourself.

children.text: dhanyā manuṣyāḥ saṃsāre yaiḥ svahastena bhujyate
children.translated_text: Blessed are human beings in <s>saṃsāra</s>, who eat with their own hands,
who relieve an itch and pull away insects, thorns, and the like.
Ah, you are a king among the meritorious, since you are born from a human womb;
and you are a brahmin and an ascetic, enviable, O <s>Kaśyapa</s>.

children.text: aho dhanyo 'si yannākhurna maṇḍūko na kukkuṭaḥ
children.translated_text: Ah, blessed you are, since you are not a mouse, not a frog, not a cock,

children.text: na pukkaso na cāṇḍālo na kuṣṭhī na jaḍo 'si vā ||
children.translated_text: not a <s>pukkasa</s>, not a <s>cāṇḍāla</s>, nor a leper or a dullard.
People are seen afflicted by long illnesses, fallen from one misery into a still greater misery;
look at those who grieve, having entered a dark birth.
You are a man with all limbs complete, free from the calamity of disease,
and you are a brahmin, joyful; who is more fortunate than you?
Through delusion do not set your mind on discontent in the hope of wealth;
even after attaining the status of <s>Indra</s>, a person desires superiority beyond that.
This thirst, through constant practice, grows among embodied beings;
like a cord made of entrails and sinews, when pulled it stretches to length.
Therefore, devoted to your own <s>dharma</s> (proper duty), born in a good family and worthy of regard,
you should not wish to die out of desire when you see another's wealth.
I became a false logician, maintaining arguments about smoke and fire;
hating the <s>Veda</s> and being an atheist, I have entered this sinful birth.
Although I have often become disgusted with this body, out of fear

children.text: na tyajāmi tanuṃ pāpā yonayaḥ santyato 'dhikāḥ ||
children.translated_text: I do not abandon the body; there are sinful births worse than this.
With this thought the lord of the gods made him free from sorrow,
and, after showing him his own form, went away to the abode of the thirty gods.
Hearing this, the son of <s>Kuntī</s> said, 'By whom was this world created?

children.text: jīvaśca kīdṛśo dehe sa ca yātaḥ kva tiṣṭhati ||
children.translated_text: And what is the living soul like in the body? Where does it go and where does it remain?'
<s>Bhīṣma</s> said, 'Once, on the peak of <s>Kailāsa</s>,
asked by the sage <s>Bhāradvāja</s>, <s>Bhṛgu</s> spoke this very answer.
For the mind-born <s>Prajāpati</s>, standing on the lotus of the earth,
space was this first creation, from <s>Viṣṇu</s>, who touched manifest form.
For trees and for human beings the five-element constitution is the same.
By him, in this great creation, manifold manifestations were made;
fire is joined with wind in the form of <s>prāṇa</s>, <s>apāna</s>, and the rest.
On the northern side of the <s>Himavat</s> there is a fruitful land free from disease;
those who do meritorious deeds go there, while those of opposite conduct go to the opposite condition.
Even here in this world the good and evil deeds of creatures are seen
through happiness, joy, wealth, and the like, and through poverty, distress, and pain.
Then the grandsire, asked by the king about right conduct, said:

children.text: prātaḥ prabuddho vijane malaṃ tyaktvā śuciḥ sadā ||
children.translated_text: One who wakes in the morning, voids excrement in a secluded place, and is always pure,

children.text: devapūjārato hotā dātā maunī ca bhojane
children.translated_text: devoted to worship of the gods, an offerer of oblations, a giver, silent while eating,
approaching his wife at the proper season, reverent toward elders, and patient,

children.text: yo naraḥ sa sadācāraḥ prāpnoti padamuttamam ||
children.translated_text: that man is one of right conduct and attains the highest state.
Again asked by the king, 'What is <s>adhyātma</s> (the inner self)?', the all-knowing
son of <s>Śantanu</s> spoke the truth, meditating in his heart on the eternal.
The knower of the field, connected with the three qualities in the field, with senses spread out like rays,
though unattached, appears as if attached, even when hidden and veiled.
One whose mind is unmoving like a lamp in a windless place, calm in understanding and even-minded,
silent, his senses effortlessly subdued, as if become a post, beholds him.
Through the restraint of outward activity and through the control of the mind,
through abandoning passion, grief, fear, and hatred, he is seen by the good.
The mind, unsteady as lightning and waves, roams, restless without ceasing;
for those who lack mastery it becomes bewildered like the wind.
When, by practice, the mind has become level like an ocean without waves,
and has gone to stillness, with every disturbance pacified,
then yogins, beyond light and darkness, see the eternal, auspicious <s>puruṣa</s>,
the supreme one who through meditation gives utter happiness.
Hearing this, the son of <s>Kuntī</s> addressed the grandsire:
What is the attainment of the fruits of sins like, and what are the destinies?
Asked thus by the king, the son of <s>Gaṅgā</s> spoke again:
For people, the attainment of results corresponds to their intention and is perishable.
For those moved by ego, seeking enjoyment, sovereignty, and pleasure,
and for sensual people, residence is only in hells, resembling their desire.
The various divine regions, where pārijāta creepers sway and the generous fragrance of mandāra flowers spreads,
where golden-lotus lakes are lovely and served by the lord of heaven,
easily reached by moving aerial cars, those regions of the gods,
all having fixed limits, are declared to be hell.
The beginningless and endless abode, free from the three qualities,
untouched by any fraction of time, is attained only by one without desire.
Long ago a disciplined brahmin, reciting the <s>Saṃhitā</s> and rid of lust and passion,
dwelt at the foot of the snow-bearing mountain.
After a thousand years had passed for that reciter of divine knowledge,
<s>Sāvitrī</s>, pleased, came herself and granted an increase of his recitation.
Then in time the blessed <s>Dharma</s> came to him and said,
'Abandon the body and come to a divine state with a divine form.'
Hearing that, he said, 'I will not abandon this body born together with me;

children.text: svargaspṛhā na me kācid dyaurmahī ca same mama ||
children.translated_text: I have no longing at all for heaven; heaven and earth are the same to me.

children.text: na vāñchā na ca me dveṣaḥ svarge 'pyastyavaśaṃ mayā
children.translated_text: I have no desire and no hatred; even heaven does not compel me.
If by all means I must go, then it will be with my body, and not otherwise.'

children.text: ityukte tena bhagavānyamo mṛtyuśca tāṃ bhuvam
children.translated_text: When this had been said by him, lord <s>Yama</s>, <s>Mṛtyu</s>, and <s>Kāla</s> came to that place,
and told the brahmin what <s>Dharma</s> had said.
At this moment the glorious king <s>Ikṣvāku</s>, lord of the earth,
came to that hermitage in the course of a pilgrimage to sacred fords.

children.text: sa taṃ jāpakamabhyetya babhāṣe tejasāṃ nidhim
children.translated_text: Approaching that jāpaka, that treasure-house of splendor,

children.text: gṛhāṇa me dhanaṃ vipra pātraṃ tvatsadṛśo 'sti kaḥ ||
children.translated_text: he said, 'Accept wealth from me, brahmin; who is a vessel worthy like you?'
Hearing this, the jāpaka said, 'I have turned away from such things, O king;
brahmins devoted to the <s>pravṛtti-dharma</s> (path of active duties) are fit vessels for accepting gifts.
Whatever you desire, I will give you at once, without delay.'
When the brahmin had spoken thus, the lord of the earth said,
'Give me the fruit of this japa that you have acquired.'
Addressed thus by the king, the brahmin replied to him, 'Take it.'
The king said, 'You are strong and unconquerable in battles of speech;
this fruit of japa, given by you, is of no use to me.'
Although the brahmin entreated him even once while he was speaking so,
the king did not take it, proud in the thought, 'I am a giver, a ruler.'
Meanwhile <s>Kāma</s> and <s>Krodha</s>, disputing with one another, came to him,
ugly and deformed in appearance, and gladly asked for judgment.
One said, 'The fruit of a cow must be given to this man; I give it.'

children.text: dattaṃ mayā punargrāhyaṃ netyuvāca tathā paraḥ ||
children.translated_text: The other then said, 'What has been given by me should not be taken back.'
After considering for a long time while the two were disputing,

children.text: uvāca dīyamānaṃ yo na gṛhṇāsi jito 'tha saḥ ||
children.translated_text: the king said, 'You who do not accept what is being given are thereby defeated.'

children.text: athābravīnnṛpaṃ viprastvaṃ na gṛhṇāsi kiṃ mama
children.translated_text: Then the brahmin said to the king, 'Why then do you not accept what is mine?
Or perhaps everyone is learned when giving instruction to others.'
When the jāpaka had spoken thus, the king looked at those two, <s>Kāma</s> and <s>Krodha</s>,
and, saying, 'It must be enjoyed together,' accepted the fruit.

children.text: tataḥ svarge sa vibudhe prāpte sa brahmaṇi svayam
children.translated_text: Then, when heaven among the gods had been reached, he himself, intent on <s>Brahman</s>,
entered the absorption of renunciation together with the king.
Placing the mind within the breath and gazing at the two nostrils,
he filled the inner sky, the ether extending six <s>kośas</s>, with radiance.
With his light fixed between the brows, opening the casket of <s>Brahman</s>,
he quickly rose beyond the sun, blazing with a splendor surpassing sun and fire.
That radiance of the brahmin and the king, arising from the opening in the palate,
entered <s>Brahmā</s> directly in the form of a span-sized person.
Asked by the king about the fruit of fitness for knowledge, of the Vedas and discipline,

children.text: phalaṃ svargaṃ ca bhūtānāṃ bhīṣmaḥ pṛṣṭo 'bravītpunaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and about heaven for beings, <s>Bhīṣma</s> spoke again.
In ancient times <s>Prajāpati</s> <s>Manu</s> told this to <s>Bṛhaspati</s>:
karma is marked by what is to be avoided and what is to be adopted, and by pleasure, pain, and the like.
Since there is pleasure and there is non-pleasure, activity is said to belong to karma;
knowledge is understood as free from pleasure and pain, and devoid of desire and passion.
Vedic action leads only to happiness, while action opposed to it leads to unhappiness;
acts such as giving shine when purified by disciplines of absorption and restraint.
Through the various fruits of karma, according to the different forms they take,
people sink into pleasures and pains, brought under the power of passion and delusion.
This <s>māyā</s> (cosmic illusion), which brings about the world's creation, continuance, and dissolution,
is made of the great elements, like a shadow appearing in space.
Though present after entering another body, it is not perceived because of delusion and the rest,
like fire always present inside wood that is covered with smoke.
As bracelet-ness and the like appear in gold, or a carved figure in wood,
so everything shines in the self alone; though existent, it remains as if nonexistent.

children.text: jñānena gṛhyate jñānaṃ gajeneva vane gajaḥ
children.translated_text: Knowledge is grasped by knowledge, as an elephant is caught by an elephant in the forest;
that alone knows its own course, as a serpent knows the feet of serpents.
Then the grandfather, asked by <s>Pārtha</s> about the <s>Vaiṣṇava</s> nature,
spoke what had been told by <s>Nārada</s> and others through the eyes of knowledge.
The blessed <s>Puṇḍarīkākṣa</s>, <s>Keśava</s>, the Lord, from the lotus of his navel
created the four-faced one and brought the whole world into being.
Having slain the demons headed by <s>Madhu</s>, he established everlasting order;
as <s>Saṃkarṣaṇa</s>, the destroyer of all, he assumes the state of <s>Rudra</s> at dissolution.
Thus he indeed is the cause of creation, maintenance, and destruction,
by whom, as <s>Varāha</s>, the earth was lifted up as if in the play of a lotus fiber.
<s>Vāsudeva</s> is the supreme abode, eternal, firm, and imperishable;
so the teacher explained to the disciple devoted to the <s>nivṛtti-dharma</s> (path of withdrawal).
Beings, deluded by the wondrous <s>māyā</s> of <s>Viṣṇu</s>,
seized by passion, hatred, and pride, come back and go away again and again.
Thus transmigrating beings, born from semen and blood, continue onward;
women, whose delusions are perilous in their consequences, bewilder them.
For women, so called, are the chains of the prison-house of <s>saṃsāra</s>,
the knotted ropes of attachment for passion, hatred, and despondency.
Or, through affection, beings made of lineage come to decay through sons born from their own limbs,
like moist fragments of skin through worms born from themselves.
Those celibates whose senses and desires are restrained are released from <s>saṃsāra</s>,
those in whom desire does not arise because root and seed have been scorched.
These channels that carry the mind bear what is born of imagination toward an abyss;

children.text: tacchuṣyati virāgeṇa yeṣāṃ te paramaṃ gatāḥ ||
children.translated_text: for those in whom that dries up through dispassion, they have reached the supreme state.
The thread of <s>tṛṣṇā</s> (craving), beginningless and endless, like fibers in lotus stalks, belongs to embodied beings;

children.text: sahajo 'ntaḥsthito hantuṃ niḥśeṣaṃ ca na śakyate ||
children.translated_text: it is innate and lodged within, and cannot be utterly destroyed.
By even and disciplined conduct, after seeing <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> in the heart,
shining like a purified sky, peace is attained by the peaceful.
Then, when the king asked, "How did <s>Janaka</s> attain liberation?"
<s>Devavrata</s>, being questioned, told the story of the lord of <s>Mithilā</s>.
In former times <s>Janaka</s>, who attended upon a hundred teachers,
had as his teacher one named <s>Pañcaśikha</s>, a <s>Kapila</s> devoted to brahman.
In the presence of those hundred teachers, he spoke this to the king,
his understanding intent on removing the transformations of insubstantial, flashing <s>saṃsāra</s>.
When the compulsion of birth has slipped away, though one is bound by action, one is without latent desire;
one has taken hold of all grasping as an unstable heap.
For those who make a severing at the root of the transformations of egoism,
the delusion of becoming is broken by even the slightest attentiveness.
"All this shines in me; I am established everywhere":
such alone is the noble conduct of good men who are beyond <s>saṃsāra</s>.
Truly, for those who end in decay and whose nature is old age and death,
the body gradually becomes fivefold through the weakening of the senses.
These five, beginning with sound, in which there is certainty about the real nature of things,

children.text: avyayaṃ paramaṃ cakraṃ buddhiśceti paraṃ mahat ||
children.translated_text: and the imperishable supreme wheel and intellect are the highest greatness.
For those who do not see correctly, these are otherwise, devoted to suffering;

children.text: tyāgā evaṃ paraṃ tattvaṃ muktānāṃ nyastakarmaṇām
children.translated_text: but for the liberated, who have laid down action, renunciations in this way are the supreme reality.
For those whose minds have gone astray falsely, delusions of the heart bear fruit.
Renunciation of substance destroys action; renunciation of enjoyment destroys the performance of vows;
renunciation of pleasure brings union with austerity, but renunciation of everything leads to peace.
That <s>kṣetrajña</s> (knower of the field), free from the three <s>guṇas</s>, is eternal and imperishable;

children.text: yairdṛṣṭaste na lipyante paṅke śaśikarā iva ||
children.translated_text: those by whom he is seen are not stained, like moonbeams in mud.
When the result is destroyed and contentment is enjoyed, and when merit and sin have dwindled,
the sages, unimpaired and shaped like the sky, behold the great principle.
Like a wandering deer its horn, or like an old snake its skin,
like a bird a shaken śāla tree, the sāttvika man releases bondage.

children.text: ityākarṇya vaco rājā janako mithilāṃ purā
children.translated_text: Having heard this speech, in former times king <s>Janaka</s>,
free from thirst and passion, did not know whether <s>Mithilā</s> was burned or unburned.
Asked by <s>Pārtha</s>, "What is happiness?" <s>Bhīṣma</s> again replied:
"Here and hereafter there is happiness for the restrained, who are rich in contentment.
Self-control is firmness, self-control is splendor, self-control is fame, self-control is delight;
for men devoted to self-control there is no such thing as an enemy.

children.text: kiṃ tapo vā na vetyetadupavāsādikaṃ vratam
children.translated_text: Asked again by the son of <s>Kuntī</s> whether this vow of fasting and the like was austerity or not,
the son of <s>Śantanu</s> spoke to him again.
A man who is always moderate in diet may be fasting even while eating;
for the fasting of fools is merely the drying up of the vital breaths.
A man always devoted to his own wife may be a celibate;
one who eats meat used in sacrifice may be one who abstains from meat.
He who always eats what remains after guests, brahmins, and servants
should be known as an eater of nectar; the gods are named eaters of nectar.

children.text: naraḥ karmaphale kartā kiṃ na vetti kṣamābhujā
children.translated_text: Does a man, the agent in the fruit of action, not know? Asked by the king of patience,
<s>Bhīṣma</s> said: "Long ago <s>Śakra</s> spoke to <s>Prahlāda</s>.
"You have fallen from your station, lord of daityas, and your kinsmen have been killed by me;
when there is cause for grief, how do you look composed and as if untroubled?"

children.text: śrutveti daityastaṃ prāha śakra kiṃ katthase vṛthā
children.translated_text: Hearing this, the daitya said to him, "<s>Śakra</s>, why do you boast in vain?
States of being are naturally fickle; human effort is without meaning.
The fool becomes foremost among the wise, the handsome man becomes without beauty,
and the careless become endowed with policy. What cause is there here?

children.text: na hi śokaḥ sukhabhraṃśe kartavyo vṛddhasevibhiḥ
children.translated_text: Those who attend upon elders should not grieve at the loss of happiness;
non-being may arise in being, for states are fragile as the bending of an eyebrow."
Having heard this, <s>Śakra</s> departed, because of that instruction in wisdom;
for good men, whose essence is understanding, rejoice and are free from hatred.
Then <s>Pārtha</s> asked the grandfather, "When the forest of kings' sovereignty
is burned by an untimely fire, what is firmness?" and he replied:
"When the daityas had fallen from kingship and <s>Śatakratu</s> had obtained lordship,

children.text: papraccha gatvā brahmāṇaṃ naṣṭe vairocane purā ||
children.translated_text: long ago he went and asked <s>Brahmā</s>, after <s>Vairocana</s> had been ruined:
"He who, overpowering the prosperity of the world-protectors with his own splendor,

children.text: yo babhūva jagannāthaḥ sa baliḥ kvādya vartate ||
children.translated_text: became lord of the world, where does that <s>Bali</s> dwell today?"
Asked thus by the lord of the gods, the lotus-born one said:

children.text: śūnyāgāre kharo bhūtvā bhraṣṭaiśvaryo baliḥ sthitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: "Having become a donkey in an empty house, <s>Bali</s>, bereft of sovereignty, remains."
Hearing this, the delighted <s>Śakra</s> quickly came to see him,
mounting <s>Airāvaṇa</s>, like a moving <s>Kailāsa</s>.
Going to the empty dwelling, he saw <s>Bali</s> in the form of a donkey,

children.text: tuṣāśinaṃ baliṃ ko vā vipadbhirnaiva pīḍyate ||
children.translated_text: eating husks. Who indeed is not afflicted by misfortunes?
Seeing him, the lord of the three worlds, who had become sole ruler, said:

children.text: tvamimāṃ gatimāpannaḥ kathaṃ śocyāṃ na śocasi ||
children.translated_text: "Having reached this pitiable condition, how do you not grieve?
Where is that umbrella, bright with the smile of <s>Lakṣmī</s>'s play? Where is the chowrie?
Where is that song of the apsarases, with bracelets swaying to the rhythm of their palms?
Where is that golden garland, given by <s>Brahmā</s>, on your crowned head,
by which, even at night, the quarters bore the beauty of young sunlight?

children.text: athavā yānti cetāṃsi mahatāṃ saha bhūtibhiḥ ||
children.translated_text: Or perhaps the minds of the great depart along with their powers.

children.text: api smarasi kiṃ daitya bhāsvatastava śāsanāt
children.translated_text: Do you remember, daitya, how, under your shining command,
the earth became one whose crops ripened without ploughing, rich in sacrificers?
And under your moon-white parasol during your procession,
thousands of <s>Gandharvas</s>, wearing golden garlands, danced?"
After hearing this speech of <s>Śakra</s>, who was mounted on <s>Airāvaṇa</s>,
<s>Bali</s>, deceived by <s>Vāmana</s>, spoke with his mind unconfused:
If <s>Lakṣmī</s>, unsteady like waves, comes and goes again,
why do enemies dance about, saying, "This has been done by us"?
Established in my own being, like an ocean without waves, I do not grieve,
seeing that fortunes, after a long time, have been reduced by Time to mere remnants of a story.
Because of the harshness of fate, prosperity must inevitably end in misfortune.
What perishable man would grieve for <s>Lakṣmī</s>, once she has been swallowed by Time?
This insurmountable Time expands everywhere.
Since my maintenance has been fashioned from husks, I have gone on to self-rule.
In this broad lotus-pond of <s>saṃsāra</s> (worldly existence), whose open petals are hopes,
the black bee of Time simply drinks the pollen of creatures.
By the command of that Time, so heavy with the swallowing of the world,
you too, <s>Śakra</s>, will come to the state of being only a memory.

children.text: kiṃ na viplāvayantyetā hariṇyaḥ śīghragāḥ kṣaṇam
children.translated_text: Do these rushing, swift fortunes not flood everything in a moment,
like rivers with swelling foam for white parasols and with waves?
Fickle <s>Lakṣmī</s> goes away; life flows off unnoticed.
When such is the nature of things, who like me would grieve?

children.text: āyuḥ kenākṣayaṃ labdhaṃ viyogaḥ kasya vā priyaḥ
children.translated_text: By whom has inexhaustible life been obtained? And to whom is separation dear?
In whom has fickle <s>Lakṣmī</s>, with her wandering glance, been seen firmly seated?
Through false, playful, restless unions, seen and then lost,
how many people have not been mocked by her, who goes to everyone?
Trees of pride, fragrant with the abundance of sovereignty, attended by bees of virtue, encircled by creepers of beloved women,
with flowers of fame in bloom and hopes filled with fruit, are all carried away by the great flood of Time, which scrapes everything bare.
As he was saying this, <s>Śakra</s> saw a woman of graceful form
emerging from his body; seeing her, he asked in astonishment:
Who are you, doe-eyed one, adorned with a playful peacock crest?
Why have you come out from the body of the lord of <s>Daityas</s>?
Hearing that, she said to <s>Śakra</s>: I have come to you,
leaving this man who has forgotten right conduct and whose ghee has been touched by leftovers.
I dwell in the water of the sharp edge of brave warriors' swords.
I am <s>Kamalā</s>, auspicious, purified by lotuses, dwelling in lotus-ponds.
Having said this, <s>Śrī</s>, taking her presence in earth, water, fire, and wind
with her four feet, approached the thousand-eyed <s>Śakra</s>.

children.text: śrīvihīnaṃ purā śakro namuciṃ nāma dānavam
children.translated_text: Long ago <s>Śakra</s> asked the <s>Dānava</s> named <s>Namuci</s>, bereft of fortune:
Why, <s>Dānava</s>, do you not grieve in this time of sorrow?
Asked thus, the <s>Daitya</s>, a ground of firmness like an unstirred ocean, replied:
Those who are ruined are destroyed by grief, and they give joy to their enemies.
For bodies burned by grief, where can prosperity sprout again?
Wisdom is destroyed by grief, and the destruction of wisdom leads to calamity.
For those whose minds are touched by grief and who are already ruined, whence can any rise come?
One experiences one's own karma, auspicious or inauspicious, when it ripens.
Enemies do not know the inner state of good men whose faces do not wither.
<s>Bali</s>, displaced from his own station when <s>Śakra</s> obtained prosperity,
when questioned again, spoke even in distress with his understanding unimpaired:
For heroes, victory and defeat are both inevitable in the holding of their ground.

children.text: karmāyattau na kartā tvaṃ kālaprāptamidaṃ bhaja ||
children.translated_text: They depend on karma; you are not the doer. Accept what has arrived through Time.

children.text: kālo na yāti yāsyanti sahasrāṇi bhavādṛśām
children.translated_text: Time does not pass away; thousands like you will pass away.

children.text: gantā tvamapi kālena kiṃ dhairyeṇa vikatthase ||
children.translated_text: You too will go by Time. Why boast of your firmness?
Even searching with subtle understanding, I do not see anything in the worlds
that is hard to obtain without effort and has not been licked by the tongue of Time.
World-rulers whose powers remain only as tales

children.text: śrūyante vihitāste te kiṃ vṛthā śakra mādyasi ||
children.translated_text: are heard to have been made so by Time; why, <s>Śakra</s>, do you exult in vain?
I am able by myself to defeat you, together with your retinue, deluded by pride;

children.text: kiṃtu na kṣamate kālo velevābdherbalaṃ mama ||
children.translated_text: but Time does not permit my strength, as the shore restrains the ocean.
Calamities come by Time, and prosperity comes by Time.
For men sealed by their own karma, what occasion is there here for grief?
Hearing this, the thousand-eyed one withdrew from rashness born of anger,

children.text: sa tamūce kālavaśaṃ tvaṃ yathāttha tathaiva tat ||
children.translated_text: and said to him: As you say that all is subject to Time, so indeed it is.
When the worlds become unrestrained and touched by <s>Kali</s>,

children.text: tadā tvaṃ dāruṇaiḥ pāśairmuktaḥ svāsthyaṃ gamiṣyasi ||
children.translated_text: then, released from terrible bonds, you will regain well-being.
Then, when asked by the king about the former form of the auspicious and the inauspicious,
<s>Bhīṣma</s> described the marks of destruction and rise among living beings.
Long ago, on the bank of the heavenly river, <s>Śakra</s>, accompanied by <s>Nārada</s>,
saw <s>Lakṣmī</s>, whose face was a blossoming lotus, and asked her:
Goddess, tell me truly the reason for your coming here.
Asked thus by great <s>Indra</s>, the lotus-eyed one replied:
<s>Śakra</s>, abandoning the <s>Daityas</s>, whose conduct was ruined and who had broken loose from restraint,

children.text: surāṇāṃ sadma sādhūnāṃ samprāptā tava cāntikam ||
children.translated_text: I have come to the abode of the gods and the good, and into your presence.
Formerly the <s>asuras</s> were adorned with good conduct.
They had bathed, maintained the sacrificial fires, were unconquered, and were honored by women.
They were generous, free from craving, patient, and looked upon ghee at dawn.
They did not eat curds and barley-meal at midnight or in the lap.
Their emission in love was not fruitless; therefore I adorned them.
But now, their boundaries of conduct destroyed, they are mad with arrogance and have been abandoned by me.

children.text: āyattāḥ patayaḥ strīṇāṃ śaṇṭīnām adya tatpare
children.translated_text: Today husbands are dependent on women and devoted to shrewish women.
They perform rising and similar services for them, and they speak loudly.
Young men, with rogues as counselors, the words of elders and their age...
These people, blinded by pride, mock others, their locks tossed about in contemptuous play.
They eat what has been prepared by unclean cooks who handle leftovers,
and, in hidden gardens, they are cut off from worshippers of the gods, servants, and their own people.
The women in their houses, absorbed in laughter and sport, do not even look at grain, milk, and food left uncovered,

children.text: gṛhe teṣāṃ na vīkṣante hāsakeliratāḥ striyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: or at ghee touched by their own leavings.
A man wears what is proper for women: hair-arrangements, garments, and ornaments;
and a woman assumes masculine conduct, gait, and speech.
Thus, having abandoned the dwelling of those sinners blinded by intoxication,
I have come near to you; O truthful one, my abode is with you.
Hope, faith, firmness, patience, beauty, right conduct, victory, and intelligence,
the eight goddesses, with me at their head, have come to you alone.

children.text: iti bruvāṇāṃ tāṃ śakraḥ prāpya prāyāttriviṣṭapam
children.translated_text: When she had spoken thus, <s>Śakra</s>, having met her, went back to <s>Triviṣṭapa</s>.
This is the first sign for men, bearing auspicious or inauspicious fruit.
Asked by the king about the state of brahman, the Grandsire spoke again:
In former times <s>Asita Devala</s> addressed <s>Jaigīṣavya</s>:
You are honored and reviled, equal toward all, with pleasant and unpleasant alike;
you are seen to have abandoned passion, fear, and hatred. For what reason is this?
Questioned thus by the chief sage, <s>Jaigīṣavya</s>, knower of independence,
said: This truth has arisen in me, whose mind is at peace.
Good people, full of contentment, whose confusions have been dispersed by discrimination born from the fire of knowledge,

children.text: na hṛṣyanti na śocanti santaḥ saṃtoṣanirbharāḥ ||
children.translated_text: neither rejoice nor grieve.

children.text: mānāvamānayostulyā na snigdhā na ca vairiṇaḥ
children.translated_text: They are equal in honor and dishonor, neither attached nor hostile;
nowhere do they think, 'This is mine,' or 'I belong to this.'
Those who touch secure happiness have no envy or attachment;
they wander fearless, completely freed from every bond,
awakened from things like dream and magic, and they attain the state of brahman.
Asked by the lord of the earth, 'Who is beloved and honored everywhere?',
<s>Bhīṣma</s> replied with what <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> had said to the king of the <s>Andhakas</s>:
There is only one person beloved and honored by all: <s>Nārada</s>,
who moves at will, is happy, diligent, and master of his senses.
His range is unobstructed; he is unattached, though associated with many;
he delights in play, beholds the world, and is free from desire and anger.
Hearing this, the son of <s>Pṛthā</s> also asked <s>Bhīṣma</s> about the origin of beings

children.text: kālasya ca gatiṃ bhīṣmo babhāṣe viśvatattvavit ||
children.translated_text: and the course of time; <s>Bhīṣma</s>, knower of the truth of the universe, explained it.
Long ago the blessed <s>Vyāsa</s>, questioned by <s>Śuka</s>, said this

children.text: sargasthitiṃ ca kālaṃ ca yacca kṛtyaṃ dvijanmanām ||
children.translated_text: about creation, duration, time, and the duties of twice-born men.
At the end of a thousand ages, the unmanifest becomes manifest;
brahman creates from sound the five elements, beginning with space and ending with earth.
When, in the later dissolution of that creation, through time only space remains,
space and the other elements pass into dissolution in what is called the unmanifest.
This is the brief account of creation; now hear the duty of twice-born men.
Consecrated by rites beginning with birth, one should become a student and then a householder.
Then, seeing the self by the self, one becomes a forest-dweller and afterward a renunciant.
The brahmanical duty has thus been stated; now the way of life of knowers is described.
With desire made indifferent and detached through disregard, with the self flickering like lightning,
seeing inwardly the supreme light, all-pervading like the wind,
dwelling alone in an empty place, equal-minded, one is dissolved in brahman.
By action one goes to <s>saṃsāra</s> (the cycle of rebirth); by knowledge one becomes free from <s>saṃsāra</s>.
With desire dissolved back into its own source and the mind blossoming with consciousness,
one rests always in one's own heart and enjoys the supreme nectar.

children.text: śrutveti bhīṣmaṃ papraccha ya ete pṛthivīśvarāḥ
children.translated_text: Hearing this, the <s>Pāṇḍava</s> asked <s>Bhīṣma</s>: These lords of the earth

children.text: yātā mṛtyuvaśaṃ teṣāṃ ko mṛtyuriti pāṇḍavaḥ ||
children.translated_text: who have gone under the power of death, what is Death for them?
<s>Bhīṣma</s> said: Long ago <s>Nārada</s> spoke to King <s>Anukampaka</s>,
who was afflicted by grief for his son and had come under the control of enemies.
Having created all this, <s>Vidhi</s> saw that creatures had grown numerous
as the world revolved, and he became angry.
When living beings were being burned by the blazing flame born from that anger,
the compassionate god <s>Tryambaka</s> entreated the four-faced one,
and, petitioned by <s>Śambhu</s>, the Creator withdrew that fire of wrath.
From the fire of anger that had been withdrawn, a lotus-eyed maiden
arose, dark as the sky and adorned with red garments.

children.text: uvāca tāṃ tato brahmā tvaṃ śanaiḥ saṃhara prajāḥ
children.translated_text: Then <s>Brahmā</s> said to her: Slowly withdraw the creatures,
for this earth, resting upon the waters, is sinking under its burden.

children.text: tacchrutvā dāruṇaṃ dhātuḥ kṛpayā netrajaṃ jalam
children.translated_text: Hearing that terrible command of the Creator, out of compassion she took in her hands

children.text: nijaṃ jagrāha pāṇibhyāṃ nindantī janma duḥkhitā ||
children.translated_text: the water born from her own eyes, sorrowful and condemning her birth.

children.text: kathaṃ tava sutā deva ghore karmaṇi madvidhā
children.translated_text: O god, how can a daughter of yours such as I be fit for this dreadful act?

children.text: yogyā bandhuviyuktānāṃ na sahe duḥkhināṃ giraḥ ||
children.translated_text: I cannot endure the cries of suffering people separated from their kin.

children.text: ityuktvā vipulaṃ cakre duṣkaraṃ vividhaṃ tapaḥ
children.translated_text: Having spoken thus, she performed vast, varied, and difficult austerity.
She was <s>Mṛtyu</s> (Death), compassionate and afraid of universal destruction.
The Creator granted her a boon: Your teardrops will become diseases

children.text: bhaviṣyanti janāntāya tvāṃ na jñāsyanti mohitāḥ ||
children.translated_text: for the ending of people; deluded, they will not recognize you.

children.text: iti mṛtyuḥ purā sṛṣṭvā brahmaṇā sarvasaṃhṛtiḥ
children.translated_text: Thus, long ago, <s>Mṛtyu</s>, the destruction of all, was created by <s>Brahmā</s>.

children.text: mā śucaḥ pṛthivīpāla sā hi kaṃ nopasarpati ||
children.translated_text: Do not grieve, O protector of the earth, for whom does she not approach?
Again asked by the son of <s>Dharma</s> about the truth of <s>dharma</s> (righteous order),

children.text: śaśaṃsa sāraṃ dharmasya satyaṃ parahitaṃ tathā ||
children.translated_text: the Grandsire declared the essence of <s>dharma</s>: truth, and likewise the welfare of others.

children.text: gatirdharmasya vividhā sūkṣmā jñātuṃ na śakyate
children.translated_text: The course of <s>dharma</s> is varied and subtle; it cannot be known easily.
For those whose reasoning is reversed, unrighteousness comes to be treated as <s>dharma</s>.
Formerly there was the sage <s>Jājali</s>, whose austerity was performed within the water;
because of their trust in him, birds had made nests in his matted locks.
Seeing the fledglings of the birds gradually grown on his head,
he became intoxicated with his own <s>dharma</s> (righteousness); then the rākṣasas said to him:
"Without having attained the equality of <s>Tulādhara</s>, why, O sage,
are you exulting here, ready to squander your abundant austerities?

children.text: iti śrutvā samanviṣya gatvā vārāṇasīṃ muniḥ
children.translated_text: Hearing this, the sage investigated, went to <s>Vārāṇasī</s>,
and then saw <s>Tulādhara</s>, who lived by selling meat.
Knowing by the eye of wisdom the reason for his arrival,
<s>Tulādhara</s> himself said, "O brahman, <s>dharma</s> is of the nature of the sky.
The path of <s>dharma</s> is reached by those who are not feared by any beings,
who give fearlessness to beings, who are unattached, and who are skilled in action.

children.text: ahiṃsā paramo yajñaḥ puṇyairyaṣṭuṃ sa śakyate
children.translated_text: Non-injury is the highest sacrifice; that sacrifice can be performed by the meritorious.
Behold the sin, for a paltry gain, from tormenting the lives of cows and other animals.
For those who have gained merit through sacrifice of the self, who resort only to the self as their sacred ford,
and who have abandoned pride and rivalry, their kinsmen do not grieve.
Thus that <s>Tulādhara</s> dispelled <s>Jājali</s>'s great delusion of pride,
and, established in unattached action, he went to the supreme state.

children.text: gītaṃ vicaravnunā pūrvaṃ dharme 'smin eva bhūbhujā
children.translated_text: This same teaching on <s>dharma</s> was formerly sung by the king <s>Vicaravnu</s>:
"Non-injury is the highest <s>dharma</s>, and sacrifice is without the ostentation of material wealth.
These men, ruled by desire and longing for reward, sacrifice with the lives of animals;
meat, fish, and honey and the like were contrived by cheats for the sake of enjoyment.
Animal sacrifice is accepted through greedy teachers of hypocrisy;

children.text: pūjyo hi bhagavānviṣṇuḥ so 'dbhiḥ puṣpaiśca tuṣyati ||
children.translated_text: for the blessed <s>Viṣṇu</s> is worthy of worship, and he is pleased with water and flowers.

children.text: glāniṃ śarīraṃ nāyāti yathā na maraṇaṃ bhavet
children.translated_text: One should undertake action in such a way that the body does not decline
and death does not occur, for the body is the instrument for <s>dharma</s>."
Asked by the king about judging what ought and ought not to be done,
<s>Pitāmaha</s> said, "There was a sage of the <s>Aṅgiras</s> line named <s>Cirakārī</s>.

children.text: ciraṃ vicārya karmāṇi sa karoti yadā tadā
children.translated_text: Because he performed actions only after reflecting for a long time,
fools mocked him as lazy and merely long-sighted.
Once, urged by his own father to kill his mother,
he pondered for a long time, his mind loosened on the swing of doubt.
'The guru's command cannot be transgressed, yet killing one's mother is unbearable';
thus, darkened by sorrow, he fell into uncertainty about <s>dharma</s>.
He remained intent on thought until his father himself,
overtaken by remorse, withdrew his own command.
By reflection <s>Cirakārī</s> thus saved both his mother

children.text: mātaraṃ guruvākyaṃ ca vimarśo hi śubhāspadam ||
children.translated_text: and the guru's word; reflection is indeed the abode of good."
"How should a king protect right conduct without oppressing people?"
Asked this by the king, the son of <s>Śantanu</s> spoke again:
"Long ago the wise <s>Dyumatsena</s>, king of the <s>Sālvas</s>,
spoke to his son named <s>Satyavān</s> after seeing condemned men greatly afflicted:
'O king, the course of <s>dharma</s> is subtle. Why are these robbers
restrained by you in just any way, because of the incapacity of the brahmins?
By the killing of one man alone, his wife, sons, and kinsmen,
many as they are, become as good as slain; therefore punishment must be considered carefully.'
Hearing this, <s>Dyumatsena</s> said, 'By not punishing those who deserve punishment,
a king casts his subjects into this fathomless great pit of fear.
Formerly people were lightly punished, gentle, and did little harm;
today, through the reversal of the age, they are unrestrained even by the penalty of death.'
Such was the exchange between the prince and the king

children.text: nivṛtte ca pravṛtte ca dharme dharmavidāṃ vara ||
children.translated_text: about <s>dharma</s> that withdraws and <s>dharma</s> that acts, O best of those who know <s>dharma</s>.

children.text: nivṛttaṃ ca pravṛttaṃ ca dharmaṃ pṛṣṭo 'tha bhūbhujā
children.translated_text: Then, asked by the king about withdrawn and active <s>dharma</s>,
the son of <s>Śantanu</s>, a seer, explained the truth of both.

children.text: nahuṣasya purā saure sattre gāṃ yūpasaṃgatām
children.translated_text: Long ago, at the solar sacrifice of <s>Nahuṣa</s>, seeing a cow fastened to the sacrificial post,
the brahmin yogin <s>Kapila</s>, who moved according to his own will, said:
'Alas, violence has been imagined as <s>dharma</s> by the wicked;
greedy men who long for the fruit of desire delight in injuring others.'
Hearing this, the brahmin <s>Syūmaraśmi</s> entered the cow there
and said, 'The authority of the Vedic word is not accepted by you.

children.text: yajeta dadyādityeṣā na śrutā kiṃ śrutiḥ smṛtiḥ
children.translated_text: Has this scripture, "One should sacrifice, one should give," not been heard by you?
The <s>dharma</s> marked by householdership is a limb of sacrifice and the support of all.'
Hearing this, <s>Kapila</s> said, 'A rite made of pure knowledge
alone carries one across darkness; a material sacrifice is bondage.'
Hearing this, <s>Syūmaraśmi</s> again spoke in favor of ritual action:
'Knowledge takes support in a reflection, as in a pure, shining jewel.'
Again the king asked, 'What is best among <s>dharma</s>, wealth, and desire?'
The son of <s>Śantanu</s>, skilled in the course of the three aims, replied:
'A certain brahmin, desiring wealth, worshipped the gods without result,
and for a long time devotedly served <s>Kuṇḍadhāra</s>, who possessed wisdom.
When he was pleased, the brahmin then saw in a dream, in the abode of <s>Vaiśravaṇa</s>,
<s>Maṇibhadra</s> distributing heaps of wealth as was fitting.
<s>Kuṇḍadhāra</s> approached him and made a request for the brahmin's sake.
Through the beneficial yogic power of <s>Kuṇḍadhāra</s>,
the brahmin became dispassionate toward boons, became righteous, and went to perform austerity.
Moving through the sky and possessing divine sight, he became accomplished through austerity.
Thus <s>dharma</s> is the essence of the three aims of life and gives auspicious fruit.'
Having heard of the residence in hell of kings attached to wealth and desire,

children.text: niśamya kuryātko nāma na dharmopārjane matim ||
children.translated_text: who indeed would not set his mind on the accumulation of <s>dharma</s>?
Non-injury is the highest <s>dharma</s>; dispassion is the teacher of knowledge;
complete renunciation is supreme peace, but for those given to desire everything is otherwise.
Long ago <s>Asita Devala</s>, questioned by <s>Nārada</s>, said:
"This body, consisting of eighteen elements, warm, and composed of the five elements,
again comes into union with the knower of the field, like a tree with a bird.
As long as the thread of latent impressions is not exhausted, even when separated, it is not released.
When action is cut off, free from dualities and devoid of merit and sin,

children.text: dehī dehaviyoge svaṃ brahma gacchati nirguṇaḥ ||
children.translated_text: the embodied one, at the separation from the body, goes to his own attributeless <s>Brahman</s>."
<s>Janaka</s>, whose net of latent impressions had been exhausted, said to <s>Māṇḍavya</s>:
"I alone am the foremost among the happy, without possessions,
for even when the city is burning, nothing of mine is burned.
For those scorched by the wind of <s>saṃsāra</s>, their minds faint with thirst,
the cloud of the nectar of contentment is the highest medicine.
With wealth, thirst increases, just as water increases with salt;
the grief of one whose thirst has increased grows like the horn of a cow.
Having abandoned that thirst, free from attachment and established in a state without pain,
with desire withdrawn like a turtle's limbs, moving by his own will, a man is liberated."
Through this speech of <s>Janaka</s>, <s>Māṇḍavya</s>, his worldly existence fallen away,
entered the firm, peaceful, disease-free radiance of <s>Brahman</s>.
A renouncer whose senses and desires are restrained, fearless and causing fearlessness,
though despised and cast off, though empty in conduct, and without support,

children.text: anirviṇṇaḥ prahṛṣṭaśca jñātā maunī ca mucyate
children.translated_text: not despondent, joyful, a knower, and silent, is liberated;
so said the wise <s>Hārīta</s>, who rests on purified knowledge.
Long ago <s>Vṛtra</s>, fallen from sovereignty, addressed <s>Śukra</s>, his teacher:
"For living beings, bound by karma and abiding in a body made of the five elements,
prosperities and adversities alike come in turn.
I am free from longing; I do not grieve; I resort to imperishable equanimity.
Now I shall not pass into passion, being colorless though in contact with colors."
Having spoken thus, the lord of demons learned from the sage
<s>Sanatkumāra</s>, who had come by chance, that <s>Viṣṇu</s> is the imperishable cause.

children.text: sa vijñāyācyutaṃ devaṃ prayayau paramāṃ gatim
children.translated_text: Knowing the god <s>Acyuta</s>, he went to the supreme goal.

children.text: so 'yaṃ nārāyaṇaḥ kṛṣṇaḥ saṃbandhī tava pāṇḍava ||
children.translated_text: This <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, is your kinsman, <s>Pāṇḍava</s>.

children.text: rājñā vṛtrakathāṃ pṛṣṭaḥ punaḥ prāha pitāmahaḥ
children.translated_text: Questioned by the king about the story of <s>Vṛtra</s>, the grandfather again said:
"Long ago, when the slayer of <s>Jambha</s> had been defeated by <s>Vṛtra</s> in battle,
he was instructed by <s>Vasiṣṭha</s>; bearing <s>Viṣṇu</s>'s power and the thunderbolt,
he slew that great-bodied one, who was bewildered by the fever of pride.
From the body of the slain <s>Vṛtra</s>, brahmahatyā came forth,
with loosened hair, emaciated, terrible, smeared with filth, and skull-bearing.
After searching everywhere for the fleeing thousand-eyed one for a long time,
she saw him and seized him by the throat, motionless, terrified, and trembling.
When the four-faced one saw him for a long time secretly overpowered by her,
out of compassion he begged Hatyā to release <s>Śakra</s>.
Restrained by <s>Brahmā</s>'s words, brahmahatyā
abandoned the lord of the gods, taking up a fourfold place of residence, terrible to behold.
He who does not carefully cast seeds and the like into a blazing fire,
he who cuts a tree at a sacred time, and he who desires a menstruating woman,
and he who throws phlegm, filth, and the like into water:
that man is himself a place for brahmahatyā, said <s>Svayambhū</s>.
Asked again about the origin of fever, <s>Bhīṣma</s> said to <s>Pārtha</s>:
"Long ago the blessed lord, husband of <s>Gaurī</s>, was standing on the peak of <s>Sumeru</s>,
and he heard of the sacrifice of <s>Dakṣa Prajāpati</s>, crowded with gods.
At <s>Gaurī</s>'s words, 'Are you then unworthy of a share in sacrifices?' <s>Hara</s>,
though uninvited, then formed the intention of destroying <s>Dakṣa</s>'s sacrifice.
From a drop of water of sweat on the forehead of that wrathful one, in an instant
Fever arose blazing, three-headed and copper-eyed.

children.text: brahmaṇā duḥsahaḥ so 'tha vinyastaḥ kila bhāgaśaḥ
children.translated_text: Since he was unbearable, <s>Brahmā</s> is said to have distributed him in portions

children.text: teṣu teṣūtkaṭo yatnādekaḥ ko nu saheta tam ||
children.translated_text: among various beings; who indeed could bear him whole, even with effort?
They say that this terrible one continually exists in many forms: heat in elephants' temples,
mineral pitch in mountains, the cast-off sheath in snakes, and blueness in waters;
labored breath in cows, barrenness in fields,
hoof-disease in horses, and eye-disease in cuckoos;

children.text: meṣeṣu pittabhedaṃ ca hikkāśvāsaṃ śukeṣu ca
children.translated_text: a disorder of bile in sheep, hiccup and asthma in parrots,
splitting of the crest in peacocks, and fatigue in lions;

children.text: janmanyante vivāhe ca manuṣyeṣu jvaraṃ tathā
children.translated_text: and in human beings fever at birth, at death, and at marriage.
Thus they declare him to be terrible, established in many ways and ever present.
Then <s>Rudra</s> created a fierce attendant named <s>Vīrabhadra</s>,
and also the goddess <s>Bhadrakālī</s>, like a flame of the fire of time.
The two went and shattered the sacrifice of <s>Prajāpati</s>, rich in offerings,
its limbs broken apart and scattered, after slaying it in the form of a deer.
Then <s>Dakṣa Prajāpati</s> praised the ancient destroyer of harm to the gods,
<s>Śaṃkara</s>, the deformed-eyed, many-eyed, three-eyed one, dear to the lord of <s>Yakṣas</s>,
the self of all, all-pervading, of every form, free from disease,
with divine names whose meanings were hidden.
"Homage to you as sacrifice, endowed with realization of the knowable truth,
to the bull-bannered one, denoted by <s>Oṃ</s> and consisting of all the Vedas,
to the one of unbounded form, all-pervading, whose form is the universe
Homage to him whose hands and heads are everywhere, the inner self of all.
Homage to the fierce one of exalted splendor, to <s>Śarva</s>, who is rich in greatness,
to <s>Rudra</s> of lofty fame, worthy of worship, who bears the moon.
Then, when the blessed three-eyed one, the destroyer of <s>Tripura</s>, was pleased,
<s>Dakṣa</s> obtained the fruit of a thousand sacrifices through that boon.
"How does the fear of death cease for those who have conquered the worlds?"
Asked thus by the king, the Grandfather replied.
"Long ago <s>Samaṅga</s>, knower of all truth, was asked by <s>Nārada</s>:
'Surely grief and death perish through conquest of the vital breaths and the senses.
What benefits the five senses is for satisfaction, and satisfaction produces arrogance;
arrogance always leads to downfall on the path of transmigration.
Free from passion and delusion, glad in myself, I move about unnoticed;
I am without grief and immortal. Therefore, <s>Nārada</s>, behold me.'
Asked by the king what good was certain according to scripture, he spoke again:
<s>Bhīṣma</s> related what <s>Nārada</s> had said to all-seeing <s>Gālava</s>.
"One should act for the welfare of beings and abandon egoism;
one should not proclaim one's own excellence in assemblies by blaming others.
One should avoid slander, greed, idleness, and wandering at night;
one should not be talkative from pride, nor pursue what pleases the senses.
One should not grieve over the loss of pleasure, nor desire what is hard to obtain;

children.text: jānannapi na kurvīta kauṭilyaṃ na ca viśvaset ||
children.translated_text: even when one knows, one should not act deceitfully, nor should one place trust in deceit.
One should set one's mind on the company of the good and dwell in the city of good conduct;
one should at once give up sin and not do what will bring remorse.
Asked how liberation comes gradually, <s>Bhīṣma</s> spoke again,
telling what <s>Ariṣṭanemi</s> had said to <s>Sagara</s> for liberation.
"The tree of worldly existence is encircled by the vine of hope and has its root bound by ignorance;

children.text: na hi pātayituṃ śaktaḥ sukhena bhavapādapam ||
children.translated_text: it cannot easily be made to fall.
Who is able to restrain his own affection, spoken of through a thousand births and born from habitual impressions,
for women, wealth, and kinsmen?
Having mounted lovely fortune, like a bee upon the lotus of women,

children.text: tyajeti viṣasaṃkāśaṃ ko nāma vacanaṃ pibet ||
children.translated_text: who indeed would drink the poison-like word, 'Give it up'?
Alas, in wealth, sons, and wives gained by themselves,
small-minded men sink down and perish, as if in the taste of honey.
Seeing the livelihood of children arranged separately by fate,
who would wear himself out by taking upon himself their maintenance?
For those who eat only a limited amount, what use are crores of accumulated lands?
When dead, you see nothing; why this grasping at everything?
Toward gold and a lump of earth, toward a couch and a bed of dust,

children.text: cīnāṃśuke valkale ca samānaḥ kila mucyate ||
children.translated_text: toward Chinese silk and bark-cloth alike, one who is equal is indeed liberated.
Considering everything to have an end and having attained supreme detachment,
standing apart from all states, a man truly becomes free from becoming.
Reckoning the wretched condition at the end, equal toward gold and stone,
a man without possessiveness is happily released by breaking the knot of ignorance.

children.text: atha śukrakathāṃ pṛṣṭo rājñā prāha suravrataḥ
children.translated_text: Then, asked by the king about the tale of <s>Śukra</s>, <s>Suravrata</s> said:
"Long ago <s>Śukra</s>, lord of yogins and son of <s>Bhṛgu</s>,
entered and pervaded the body of the lord of wealth, ruler of the <s>Guhyakas</s>.
He quickly took away abundant wealth; and the lord of wealth, distressed,
reported the robber's conduct to his friend <s>Pinākin</s>.
The enemy of <s>Tripura</s>, angered, seized the descendant of <s>Bhṛgu</s>,

children.text: papau sa codare śaṃbhorbabhrāma vipule ciram ||
children.translated_text: and drank him; and he wandered for a long time in the vast belly of <s>Śambhu</s>.
There, remaining inside, he was burned by the fire of <s>Rudra</s>'s concentration;
when all the channels were blocked, he praised the beloved goddess.

children.text: tataḥ sa śukradvāreṇa nirgataḥ śukratāṃ yayau
children.translated_text: Then he went out through the passage of semen and came to be <s>Śukra</s>;

children.text: satīsaṃrakṣito lebhe na ca vai pūrvavatsthitim ||
children.translated_text: protected by <s>Satī</s>, he did not regain his former condition.
Asked then what the highest good was, the Grandfather again said
what <s>Parāśara</s> had said long ago to the lord of <s>Videha</s>.
"For the man whose chariot of desire is restrained by the reins of tranquillity,

children.text: na caratyavaṭe tasya karmaṇo 'pi sukhaṃ sadā ||
children.translated_text: it does not travel into the pit of action; even in action he always has happiness.

children.text: ratyai bhogā vimūḍhānāṃ sā duḥkhāya viyoginām
children.translated_text: Enjoyments are for the delight of the deluded, but for those separated from them they lead to suffering;
for them this is only suffering, darkness for darkness, and bondage to a great darkness.
Among good people, when enjoyments are lost, there arises what is called detachment;
their detachment leads to austerity, and austerity to the calming of transmigration.
For those engaged in good conduct, following scripture,
with minds attached to their own proper action, prosperity comes of itself.
Long ago <s>Prajāpati</s>, in the form of a goose, was asked by a king and said:
"Anger is death for base beings when it has departed from their own happiness.

children.text: dagdhāḥ krodhena śocanti krodhāndhā nipatanti ca
children.translated_text: Burned by anger, they grieve; blinded by anger, they fall.
One who has conquered anger sleeps happily, with the bonds of passion and the rest overcome.
Asked what the imperishable is, <s>Bhīṣma</s> said to the lord of men
what blessed <s>Vasiṣṭha</s> had formerly said to <s>Janaka</s>:
"The fourteenfold creation, the qualities, actions, and injunctions:
one should know all this as perishable; the imperishable is the supreme state.
This conjunction of the imperishable and the perishable is the meeting of the embodied self and the body;
when the body's copper-like alloy is burned away, the imperishable is seen like gold.
Asked again, <s>Bhīṣma</s> said that the ancient teacher <s>Yājñavalkya</s>
taught his pupil <s>Janaka</s> the ascertainment of the supreme imperishable.
"It is to be approached through reflection on the self, and is the cause in the realm of beings;
free from the three qualities, imperishable, devoid of any object to be known."
The fearless disciplined ones behold that peaceful, eternal, fixed, undecaying reality, taught by <s>Sāṃkhya</s> and <s>Yoga</s>,
like an ocean without waves.
By the grace of the sun <s>Sarasvatī</s> entered my mouth;
through her I became a maker of sacred knowledge and took refuge in the essential state alone.
When the manifest has clearly dissolved into the twenty-fifth principle, the twenty-sixth is released;
so the lord of the Gandharvas instructed <s>Viśvāvasu</s>.

children.text: tiṣṭhangṛhe ko nu muktaḥ pārtheneti suravrataḥ
children.translated_text: When <s>Pārtha</s> asked, 'Who indeed is liberated while remaining at home?', <s>Suravrata</s>

children.text: pṛṣṭo babhāṣe sulabhā yadūce janakaṃ purā ||
children.translated_text: replied with what <s>Sulabhā</s> had once said to <s>Janaka</s>.
A liberated mendicant named <s>Sulabhā</s>, bearing the triple staff,
once went through the air to <s>Mithilā</s> to see <s>Janaka</s>.
She, slender-waisted, wearing beauty as the ornament of youth,
saw <s>Janaka</s>, lovely and graceful in form.
Seeing her, the <s>Maithila</s> king seemed to have his limbs sprinkled with a stream of nectar,
and he performed fitting honor for her with water for the feet, a seat, and the rest.

children.text: tataḥ sukhoṣitā tatra bhuktottaram upetya sā
children.translated_text: Then, after dwelling there comfortably and after eating, she approached him
in the assembly and, with her rays, made his inner self her own.
Entering him unnoticed through her lovely eyes,
she became inwardly united with him for a moment, like a sleeping river of nectar.
Then <s>Janaka</s>, his own state touched by her state, spoke,
as the brightness of his teeth made a liberated, qualityless garland of pearls.
Ah, moonlight upon the nectar-ocean of the mind, who are you, and whose are you?
From where have you come, flawless-limbed one, showering nectar upon the eyes?
I am a disciple of <s>Pañcaśikha</s>, a sage who knows the Veda of <s>Sāṃkhya</s>;
I am a king who has attained liberation, foremost among those who know the weapon of discernment.
Though I wear a crown and bracelets and possess umbrella, fan, and vehicle,
my desires are shaven away; I am a forest of tranquility, one who purifies mind and action.
In this skull-bowl of inward knowledge, scorched for me by <s>Pañcaśikha</s>,
nothing is born among the objects of sense, because of the power of the seed of knowledge.

children.text: naikāntavāsitā śāntyai na gehaṃ bandhanāya ca
children.translated_text: Dwelling wholly alone is not what brings peace, nor is a house what causes bondage;
liberation is prescribed everywhere for those whose minds are unstained.

children.text: antaḥpraveśaḥ kimayaṃ tvayā me yogataḥ kṛtaḥ
children.translated_text: What is this entry into me that you have made by yoga?
Because of distinctions of caste, lineage, stage of life, and the like, this is a confusion of boundaries.
If you wish to conquer us, then this pride of yours has shown itself;
and this too is a fault in your own teaching, that you touch others.

children.text: sarvāṅgasaṅgaṃ kuruṣe satī bhūtvā na lajjase
children.translated_text: Though you are a chaste woman, you make contact with every limb; are you not ashamed?

children.text: kāraṇaṃ brūhi subhage na mithyā vaktumarhasi ||
children.translated_text: Tell me the reason, fortunate one; you ought not speak falsely.
Questioned thus with extreme harshness, she did not waver from firmness;
one eyebrow was slightly raised, and her lips blossomed with a smile.

children.text: sā babhāṣe praviṣṭāpi chāyeva purataḥ sthitā
children.translated_text: Though she had entered him, she stood before him like a shadow and spoke:
Speaking, in an assembly of good people, a statement with no regard for what comes before or after,
and saying, 'I am liberated, yet I speak in distinctions' -- ah, king, you do not shine.

children.text: kāsi kasya kuto vā tvaṃ yadevamabhidhīyate
children.translated_text: 'Who are you? Whose are you? From where are you?' When this is said,
have you not heard, in that matter, of the material thing made of qualities, like a wooden puppet?
This manifest form, shaped by the thirty qualities and parts, has become manifest;
