children.text: saṃghātastattvacakrasya so 'yaṃ kasya na kasya vā ||
children.translated_text: this aggregate of the wheel of principles -- whose is it, and whose is it not?
Its stages beginning with the deposit of semen are not perceived all the way to old age;

children.text: dīpasyevārciṣo yātā yasya so 'yaṃ kutaḥ katham ||
children.translated_text: since they have passed like the flames of a lamp, how and from where is this the same person?
There is no true relation even with one's own limbs, just as with the worlds;
how much less in the self? Liberated one, do you not see the self as like a mere reflection?

children.text: vikalpaṃ pṛcchato naiṣā muktatā tava śobhate
children.translated_text: This liberated state of yours, while you ask in terms of distinctions, does not become you,
like a victory garland on an elephant shattered by the roar of battle.
As this boundless kingdom remains with you, I do not consider your liberation real,
any more than thirstlessness in a man scorched on a desert plain.
Royal fortunes toss men about with yak-tail fans and cover them with umbrellas,
and with billows of intoxication they carry away discernment.
'The armies have been slain; the prince has fallen again in battle' --
by such common misfortunes, kings alone are made miserable.

children.text: dhanaṃ kośe gajāḥ śāle svagṛheṣu ca mantriṇaḥ
children.translated_text: Wealth is in the treasury, elephants in the stable, and ministers in their own houses;
the queen has her part of the bed, but in the night you are alone.

children.text: akaṅkaṇam ahāraṃ ca śayyāyāṃ vartate vapuḥ
children.translated_text: On the bed the body lies without bracelet and without necklace;
with breath alone remaining, turned away, you run elsewhere in dream.
I am a mendicant with an empty dwelling; in this empty body of yours

children.text: nivasāmi kṣapāmekāṃ kā nu te nṛpate kṣatiḥ ||
children.translated_text: I dwell for one night. What harm is there to you, O king?
If I entered by yoga without touching your body,

children.text: tatkathaṃ nṛpate muktaḥ sparśaṃ vetsi sarāgavat ||
children.translated_text: then how, O king, though liberated, do you feel touch like one still possessed by passion?
If you fear mixture of castes, how can <s>Pañcaśikha</s> be your teacher?
What you said just now, lord of men, has therefore become vain.
'The seed of knowledge in me, unable to sprout, does not grow
among the objects of sense' -- king, you do not see that this was spoken by yourself.
We are all undivided, because both support and supported share one basis,

children.text: tarau latā tatra puṣpaṃ tasminṣaṭcaraṇā iva ||
children.translated_text: like a vine on a tree, a flower on that vine, and a bee in that flower.
But if you perceive separateness in every respect,
then, for one absolutely distinct, whose confusion with whom is there here?

children.text: sa tvaṃ pravṛttivimukho na ca prāpto nivṛttatām
children.translated_text: You have turned away from worldly engagement, but you have not attained withdrawal;

children.text: triśaṅkuriva madhyastho na divaṃ na bhuvaṃ śritaḥ ||
children.translated_text: like <s>Triśaṅku</s>, you stand in the middle, resting neither on heaven nor on earth.
Until you reach this firm conviction -- 'all this is not mine, or else I myself am all' --
how are you liberated, O king?
Thus, having grasped the meaning of the instruction through words easy to understand, the king

children.text: na hṛṣṭo nāpahṛṣṭaśca tūṣṇīṃ nabha ivābhavat ||
children.translated_text: was neither elated nor cast down, but became silent like the sky.
Asked by the king about the detachment of <s>Śuka</s>, <s>Bhīṣma</s> again said
what the sage, the son of <s>Parāśara</s>, had said to his son <s>Śuka</s>:
"Son, behold the wretched condition of the undiscerning, as they pass through worldly existence and death,
ending in cold and heat, sickness and death.
When life stands in this flower of a body like a bee,

children.text: capaleṣu ca bhāveṣu tāṭasthyaṃ putra nocitam ||
children.translated_text: and all states are unstable, my son, mere aloofness is not fitting.
A lifespan is only just as it has been written: a moment, a night, a day, and then it is gone;
for millions whose time has arrived, even a single muhūrta is hard to obtain.
Sunk in the honeyed film of latent impressions, brought on by the flavors of manifold states,

children.text: svayamutpādite magnaḥ kṣudraḥ ko nāma mucyate ||
children.translated_text: and produced by himself, what petty man indeed is set free?
Without satisfying the desires of their own minds, leaving wives, wealth, and sons behind,
creatures, alas, go away, dragged off by the serpent of Time.
The terrible forest of sword-leaves, the heated river <s>Vaitaraṇī</s>,
and burning cauldrons exist in the next world; there is no house and no kinsmen.
Before this youthfulness slips away unnoticed,
before you shrink with old age like a hide scorched by heat,
before you are overcome by hiccup and labored breath, with eyes like those of a dreamer,
and, whirling like a potter's wheel, you cannot see the ten directions,
before, after beholding the golden-colored earth in unrestrained freedom,
you go alone into long darkness, impenetrable even to a needle,
before you rejoice or cry out when assailed by good and evil,
be one awakened by samādhi, one from whom becoming has turned away.
Hearing this, <s>Śuka</s>, who had attained disillusionment, abandoned his own dwelling;
after taking leave of his parents, the yogin went away for the samādhi that is the highest good.
Then, hearing that good and bad deeds are the root of human beings' karma,
the grandsire, questioned by the king about the story of <s>Śuka</s>, spoke again:
Long ago, in a grove of karṇikāra trees on <s>Meru</s>, the moon-crested one,
<s>Hara</s>, tawny with the rays from the serpent-jewels of his necklace, sported.
There <s>Vyāsa</s>, the son of <s>Satyavatī</s>, intent on fierce austerity
and desiring a son, received from <s>Maheśvara</s> the boon, "I shall grant it."
Then, in time, that sage himself churned the fire-sticks for fire,
while looking at the apsaras <s>Ghṛtācī</s>, who was moving before him.

children.text: tasya śukraṃ papātāśu śukībhūtāṃ vilokya tām
children.translated_text: Seeing her quickly transformed into a female parrot, his semen fell at once;
though he had not united with her, there in the araṇi wood his son was born.
Born from the womb of the araṇi wood, he became <s>Śuka</s>, the son of <s>Vyāsa</s>,

children.text: śukraḥ kamaṇḍaluṃ yasmai dyauśca daṇḍājinaṃ dadau ||
children.translated_text: to whom <s>Śukra</s> gave a water-pot, and Heaven gave a staff and antelope-skin.
After studying the Vedas in manifest form and receiving instruction from <s>Bṛhaspati</s>,
through austerity and celibacy he became honored by the dwellers in heaven.

children.text: upadeśaṃ pituḥ prāpya tadgirā janakaṃ yayau
children.translated_text: Receiving instruction from his father and, at his word, he went to <s>Janaka</s>,
moving through the sky but going on foot, to see one skilled in the meaning of the dharma of liberation.
After crossing the regions of <s>Meru</s>, he entered <s>Mithilā</s>,
unangered though he was being stopped by gatekeepers who spoke harshly.
Having passed beyond the two outer courts of King <s>Janaka</s>,
the sage, admitted by the ministers, stood honored in the inner palace.
Then lovely women with lotus-eyes attended upon him there,
by whose nectar-like smiles Kāma lives, though burned by <s>Śiva</s>.
There, on a bed worthy of the best, the yogin, intent on meditation,

children.text: nināya rātriṃ prātaśca nṛpo draṣṭuṃ tamāyayau ||
children.translated_text: passed the night; in the morning the king came to see him.
Honored by <s>Janaka</s>, the son of his teacher <s>Vyāsa</s>
sat upon a jeweled seat and then asked the lord of <s>Mithilā</s>:
"I have been sent to you by my venerable father <s>Vyāsa</s>.
Tell me the stainless knowledge connected with a teacher's instruction."
<s>Janaka</s> said: "By rows of steps made of ritual acts,
one ascends, with purified mind, to the high, supreme, stainless abode.
When the thick mass of all conceptual display has been carried off by the wind of knowledge,
the sun of awakening is seen at the cessation of the night of the pairs of opposites.
Seeing everything in the self and that self everywhere,
the sage, freed from the three guṇas, moves without possessiveness.
For him whose stain has been cast off, whose mind is clear and unattached,
liberation has been won everywhere, as he touches the state of the doer of all.

children.text: spṛhāgranthiṃ puro muktvā tato rāgaṃ tataḥ śucam
children.translated_text: First loosing the knot of longing, then passion, and then grief,
through the abandonment of ego the yogin becomes filled with Brahman.
Having entered the state of being the inner self of all and assumed the state of omniscience,

children.text: yukto vimiśratāṃ yāti śaileṣu salileṣu ca ||
children.translated_text: the disciplined one comes to mingle among mountains and waters as well.
'I am' alone is worldly existence; 'I am not' alone is its destruction.
Thus, as the good contemplate, the thread of latent impressions is cut.
Having abandoned affection for phenomenal states, one should take up identification with the body;
and when identification with the body ceases, one should take up identification with the vital breath.
Having cast aside identification with the vital breath as well, one should take up universal egoity;
afterwards one should contemplate emptiness, by which one is dissolved in Brahman."
Hearing this and other lucid speech of the lord of <s>Mithilā</s>,
accomplished <s>Śuka</s> took leave of him and went to the snowy mountain.
Meanwhile the divine sage <s>Nārada</s> came to see
<s>Himācala</s>, a jeweled mansion charming with the dance of creepers,
with noble caves and waterfalls frequented by flocks of vidyādharas,
and with sweetly singing birds in bowers of golden lotus-ponds.
Then <s>Śuka</s> there his father and his disciples, full of humility,
Approaching him as he was teaching, he reported his own affair.
<s>Sumantu</s>, together with <s>Paila</s>, <s>Vaiśampāyana</s>, and <s>Jaimini</s>,
those disciples of <s>Vyāsa</s>, joyfully embraced <s>Śuka</s>.
Then once, when the leaders headed by <s>Vaiśampāyana</s>
had gone down to the earth after taking leave of their guru <s>Kṛṣṇadvaipāyana</s>,
<s>Śuka</s> alone remained there, intent on meditation,

children.text: adhīyānaḥ paraṃ brahma vyastaṃ vyāsena dhīmatā ||
children.translated_text: studying the supreme brahman as set forth by wise <s>Vyāsa</s>.

children.text: atha pravāti pavane kṛte cādhyayane śukaḥ
children.translated_text: Then, when the wind was blowing and the recitation had been performed, <s>Śuka</s>
heard those courses of the winds that had been taught by his guru.
The divine wind called <s>Samāna</s> has as its powerful son <s>Udāna</s>;
<s>Vyāna</s> is his son, and the famed <s>Apāna</s> is the son of that one.
Born from him is the one named <s>Prāṇa</s>; these have seven ordered movements,
and their many kinds of action are said to correspond to their names.
The wind of that form called <s>Pravaha</s> drives smoke and clouds onward;
the wind called <s>Āvaha</s> makes lightning flicker, O sage.
The one that carries water in clouds and impels the planets
should be known as <s>Udvaha</s>, devourer of all the oceans.
The bearer of the gods' aerial cars, the roaring one, is named <s>Saṃvaha</s>;
and the fifth wind, <s>Nivaha</s>, supports the waters of the heavenly <s>Gaṅgā</s>.
The sixth, remembered as <s>Parivaha</s>, fills the moon with nectar;
the last, the dreadful wind <s>Parāvaha</s>, is the end-maker of beings.

children.text: sa eva vāyurniḥśvāso vahatsveteṣu no paṭhet
children.translated_text: When that very wind, as breath, is moving in these, one should not recite.
When <s>Kṛṣṇadvaipāyana</s>, having said this, had gone to the heavenly <s>Gaṅgā</s>,
<s>Nārada</s>, out of affection, approached <s>Śuka</s> as he sat alone.
The son of <s>Vyāsa</s> bowed to him respectfully and, when he was comfortably seated,
asked him about welfare in this world; questioned by him, <s>Nārada</s> replied:
Knowledge, vision, austerity, truth, renunciation, attachment, pleasure and pain,

children.text: krodhaśca mṛtyurityetadyo vetti na sa śocati
children.translated_text: anger, and death: one who understands these does not grieve.
Non-injury is the abode of <s>dharma</s> (righteous order); longing is the dwelling-place of sorrow.
Abandonment of attachment is the state of liberation; habituation to enjoyments is the house of grief.
From those torment-making objects there arises, at separation, a great wasting away.
A good person should not brood over those things that are charming only at first sight;

children.text: bahu manyeta na dhanaṃ saṃtoṣaṃ śamamāsthitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: established in contentment and calm, he should not value wealth highly.
Considering the manifold variety of worldly existence to be full of many afflictions,

children.text: na vismayaṃ na saṃtāpaṃ vānurāgaṃ bhajeta ca ||
children.translated_text: he should cultivate neither amazement, nor anguish, nor attachment.
Lazy and procrastinating people are seen to be endowed with wealth,
while striving and capable people sometimes have no share of wealth anywhere.

children.text: anicchatāṃ saṃtatiṃ ca jāyante bahavaḥ sutāḥ
children.translated_text: Many sons are born to those who do not desire offspring,

children.text: labhante putrakāmāśca pātaṃ vā naiva vā sutam ||
children.translated_text: while those who long for a son obtain either a miscarriage or no son at all.
In that very belly where things hard to digest, once eaten, are quickly digested,
an embryo grows for ten months.
Men burned by disease perish though surrounded by hundreds of physicians,
while others, lying in the mud of the road, pass beyond their illnesses.
Wise men of handsome form are slaves to people bereft of beauty and intelligence.
Widows grieve in one place, and elsewhere men bereft of wives grieve likewise.
Reflecting with his mind on all this manifold illusion in its entirety,
a wise man should become hostile to the nature of becoming, and should not become attached.
Hearing what <s>Nārada</s> had thus said, the son of <s>Vyāsa</s>
meditated on the course of worldly existence and, from disenchantment, found no steadiness.
Resolved upon the effort of abandoning everything, he took leave of <s>Nārada</s>,
went to <s>Vyāsa</s> on the riverbank, and bowed, filled with joy.
Having humbly told him of his disenchantment, with all latent desire gone,
<s>Śuka</s> circumambulated his guru and rose to depart.
'Wait a moment, my son, until, with the nectar of seeing you,
I fully gladden my heart,' his father then said to him.

children.text: nirakṣepaḥ sa gatvātha samāruhya gireḥ śiraḥ
children.translated_text: Unhindered, he went on, climbed the summit of a mountain,

children.text: niḥśabdaḥ sa same deśe sarvajñaḥ samupāviśat ||
children.translated_text: and, silent and all-knowing, sat down on level ground.
By the very process of transcending, he loosened the bindings of the knots,
and fixed his radiance in the single essence of radiance, like gold in gold.

children.text: raviṃ vāyuṃ jalaṃ bhūmiṃ praviśya gaganaṃ tathā
children.translated_text: Entering the sun, wind, water, earth,
and likewise the sky, by the power that manifests the universe, he rested on emptiness and non-emptiness.
Laughing, he suddenly flew upward; though embodied, he was as if bodiless,
his limbs unattached like the wind, and he moved through the sky like <s>Vainateya</s>.
When he had attained the highest perfection, the women of gods and <s>Gandharvas</s>
and all the sky-roamers showered him with rains of flowers.
He said to all the deities, 'When my father searches for me
and calls out in distraction, all of you should give him an answer in the hermitage.'
Having said this, he quickly leapt beyond the eightfold darkness,

children.text: tyaktvā rajaḥ saptavidhaṃ sattvaṃ cotsṛjya kevalam ||
children.translated_text: abandoned the sevenfold passion, and cast off even pure lucidity.
As the three worlds trembled with falling meteors and burning horizons,

children.text: nirvyañjanaṃ nirguṇaṃ ca brāhmaṃ tejaḥ samāviśat ||
children.translated_text: he entered the brahman-radiance, without marks and without qualities.
As he went on, he split in two a vast, broad, two-peaked divine mountain,
though his limbs did not cling to it; then the gods themselves went there.
Then, on the bank of the <s>Mandākinī</s>, where golden lotuses shone,
charming with noble, blooming <s>Mandāra</s> and <s>Pārijāta</s> trees,
the women of the Thirty Gods were engaged in bathing-sport, with restless eyes,
with breasts like golden pitchers and full circles of thighs and hips,
unclothed, their slender waists lovely with dark lines of hair
Seeing <s>Śuka</s>, who was free from passion, they stood motionless with amazement.
They had cast off their bodices, while he had crossed beyond the bodice of desire;
they looked upon the lovely, one-pointed man without contracting or bending in embarrassment.
When he had passed beyond the regions of the wind, his son-loving father
<s>Vyāsa</s> came swiftly through the sky to search for him.
Hearing his father's cry, 'Alas, my son!', <s>Śuka</s>, having attained the state of the inner self of all
and being only pure consciousness, uttered the sound 'bhoḥ'.
By the sound of him whose form was emptiness, the mountains made an echo;
that very state of his became, as it were, the answering resonance of the earth-bearing mountains.

children.text: līne tataḥ pare dhāmni śuke tanayavatsalaḥ
children.translated_text: Then, when <s>Śuka</s> had dissolved into the supreme abode, his son-loving father
<s>Vyāsa</s> sat down on a golden slab on the bank of the heavenly river.
Seeing him, the <s>apsarases</s>, absorbed in water-play with one another,
placed garments on their bodies and, from modesty, became withdrawn.
Then <s>Śiva</s> himself approached him, that sun of knowledge though overcome by grief,
consoled him, and made him free from sorrow.

children.text: eka eva paro devaḥ ko vedya iti bhūbhujā
children.translated_text: Asked by the king, 'Who is the one supreme god to be known?',
the son of <s>Śantanu</s>, meditating on <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> in his heart, replied:
Long ago <s>Nārada</s> came to <s>Badaryāśrama</s> and asked the Lord,
<s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, for a vision; he spoke to him:
'Of <s>Viṣṇu</s>, whose form is unmanifest yet who has a fourfold manifest form,
<s>Nara</s> and I, O <s>Nārada</s>, are only the unfolding of his will.
That all-pervading Lord is always seen by those who follow one path, worship one deity, and hold one vow,
by disciplined men whose stains have been swept away by knowledge.
Go from here to <s>Śvetadvīpa</s> and see men who are forms of <s>Viṣṇu</s>, free from disease,
white, intent on meditation on <s>Viṣṇu</s>, and marked with the <s>Śrīvatsa</s> sign.'
Hearing this, the sage became fixed on him in thought and wholly devoted to him,

children.text: prayayau ca paraṃ draṣṭuṃ kāraṇaṃ viṣṇumavyayam ||
children.translated_text: and he set out to behold the supreme cause, imperishable <s>Viṣṇu</s>.
He had formerly been praised in <s>Śvetadvīpa</s> by the ascetics <s>Ekata</s>, <s>Dvita</s>, and <s>Trita</s>,
and by those seated at the Vastrayajña rite.
Reaching <s>Śvetadvīpa</s>, <s>Nārada</s> saw beautiful men
with the radiance of the moon, camphor, snow, and silver.
He bowed to them, and, while they honored him with minds established in purity,
he praised <s>Viṣṇu</s> with divine mantra-words, his hands joined in reverence:

children.text: oṃ jaya ajita avyaya aprameya ananta acyuta aparimita acala acintya apratihata abhava mahāvibhava niratiśaya nirañjana nirlepa niṣprapañca nirupama nirvikāra nirguṇa nityodita viśva viśvarūpa viśveśvara viśvasamuddharaṇa śuddhasūkṣma dhruva śāśvata śānta saṃvitsvarūpa paramānandamandira bhaktimandākinīmarāla svecchāśaktivyaktīkṛtanijaprasāra lakṣmīlatāvasanta madhuvadhūgaṇḍapāṇḍimaprada suramahiṣīvibhramavirāma ānandasyandarasendumaṇḍala akhaṇḍitaprasādamaṇḍitākhaṇḍala kaustubhaprabhāracitakamalākucakuṅkumabhaṅga apariṣvaṅgasaṅgamākulīkṛtasvarbhānubhāminīloka daṃṣṭrendukalālekhāyitavasudhābhirāmamahāvarāha hiraṇyakaśipukānanadavānala vāmanalīlāsaṃpadavāmanīkṛtasuraiśvarya caraṇanakhamayūkhāyitasvarvāhinīpravāha kṣatrakṣayādhvaroddīpitakuṭhārānala daśavadanavadanakandukavinodānandita kāliyakulakamalinīkuñjara rukmiṇīkapoladantapattrīkṛtapāñcajanyaprabhāpura vidrumadrumāyitakaiṭabharudhirāruṇorustambha brahmapadmapadmākaraturagamukhakhalīnakhanakhanāyamānasāmavedoccāra
children.translated_text: 'Om, victory to you, unconquered, imperishable, immeasurable, endless, unfailing, unlimited, unmoving, inconceivable, irresistible, unborn, of great glory, unsurpassed, stainless, untouched, beyond manifestation, incomparable, changeless, without qualities, eternally arisen, the universe, whose form is the universe, Lord of the universe, uplifter of the universe, pure, subtle, firm, everlasting, peaceful, whose own form is consciousness, abode of supreme bliss, swan upon the river <s>Mandākinī</s> of devotion, whose own expansion is made manifest by the power of free will, springtime to the creeper <s>Lakṣmī</s>, giver of pallor to the cheeks of the bride <s>Madhu</s>, repose of the amorous play of the wives of the gods, full moon of the flowing nectar of bliss, adorned with unbroken favor toward <s>Akhaṇḍala</s>, whose <s>Kaustubha</s> radiance marks <s>Kamala</s>'s breasts like saffron, who agitated the world of <s>Svarbhānu</s>'s shining women by the meeting of an embrace, great <s>Varāha</s>, lovely with the earth appearing as the line of a crescent moon on your tusk, forest fire to the forest of <s>Hiraṇyakaśipu</s>, whose play as <s>Vāmana</s> made small the lordship of the gods, whose toenail rays became the stream of the heavenly river, axe-fire kindled in the sacrifice of destroying kṣatriyas, delighted by play with the ball-like heads of the ten-faced one, elephant to the lotus-bed of <s>Kāliya</s>'s race, whose <s>Pāñcajanya</s> brilliance became a leaf-painting on <s>Rukmiṇī</s>'s cheek, whose thigh-pillars were reddened like coral trees by the blood of <s>Kaiṭabha</s>, and whose horse-faced bridle jingles with the recitation of the <s>Sāmaveda</s> in the lotus-lake of <s>Brahmā</s>'s lotus.'
With hundreds of such divine praises and with secret names,
he then saw the eternal one, made of light, in many colors.
Seeing that world-pervading one being praised by the white men

children.text: taṃ viśvavyāpinaṃ dṛṣṭvā kṛtakṛtyo yayau muniḥ ||
children.translated_text: with the mantra beginning 'Jitanta,' the sage, having accomplished his purpose, departed.
Thus no one other than <s>Nārada</s> saw that Lord.
He is the unmanifest, supreme <s>Viṣṇu</s>, the undecaying source of beings,
without beginning or end, pure, knowable, subtle, and stainless.
Having heard the dharma of withdrawal, the son of <s>Dharma</s>, seeking peace,
again asked about the dharma of those in the āśramas, and <s>Suravrata</s> spoke:
On the bank of the <s>Gaṅgā</s>, a certain brahmin of noble mind asked
a guest who had come to his house, 'What is foremost among all dharmas?'
'A great nāga named <s>Padma</s>, on the bank of the <s>Gomatī</s> in <s>Naimiṣa</s>,
knows that,' the guest, when questioned by the brahmin, replied.
Then, at that word, the brahmin went to the bank of the <s>Gomatī</s>,
but he did not see the serpent, who by his turn had gone to the chariot of the Sun.
Remaining there without food for several days, the brahmin

children.text: nāgaṃ dadarśa taṃ prāptaṃ dṛṣṭvā papraccha kautukam ||
children.translated_text: saw that nāga when he had arrived; on seeing him, he asked out of curiosity:
'Tell me first, O nāga: while you were stationed in the chariot of the Sun,
what wonder did you see in heaven? Afterwards you shall explain dharma.'
Hearing this, the nāga said, 'On the path of <s>Mārtaṇḍa</s>,

children.text: rathasya cakraṃ vāreṇa balena vahatā mayā ||
children.translated_text: as I carried the chariot wheel with my strength in my turn, I saw this:
upon the thousand ray-branches of the Sun, like birds,
stand gods, siddhas, and sages; that is the wonder.'

children.text: karairgṛhītvā tyajati payo bhūmau praviśya ca
children.translated_text: Taking the water in his hands, he lets it fall, and, entering the earth,
the Blessed One sees everything unseen; such was the wonder.
He broke through the disk of the sun and entered into its brilliance, as into light itself.
Long ago, by his power, he rose up from the mortal world at midday.
I saw that great being, and the sun took him by the hand.
He broke through the disk of the sun and entered into its brilliance, as into light itself.
Seeing radiance merged into radiance, we asked the day-maker,
'Who is this?' and the glorious sun, filled with joy, said:
'This perfected man lives by gleaning and has adopted the pigeon-like way of life.
He has gone to my abode; this too is a wonder.'
Hearing this from the serpent, the Brahmin became delighted, his face opened wide with joy,
for through the incidental tale he had obtained words of instruction bearing on his own purpose.

children.text: āmantrya pannagaṃ vipro vidhāya cyavanaṃ gurum
children.translated_text: Taking leave of the serpent and making <s>Cyavana</s> his teacher, the Brahmin
undertook the vow of gleaning and attained perfection, while the gods sang of him in heaven.
This was heard by <s>Nārada</s> from <s>Cyavana</s>, and from him by the foe of <s>Jambha</s>;
from <s>Śakra</s> it was heard by the <s>Vasus</s>, from them by me, and from me by you.
After hearing various teachings on tranquility, <s>Dharmarāja</s> addressed the grandsire,
overcome by grief and thinking of the destruction of his kinsmen:
'Ah, alas, in this world I am surely foremost among those who commit sin;
by fate I have been made the cause of the slaughter of all my own people.

children.text: jāyeta mādṛśaḥ ko 'nyaḥ sadṛśo mama duṣkṛtī
children.translated_text: What other evildoer like me could be born, equal to me,
who, grandfather, can look at you after having struck you down with arrows?
Blessed is <s>Suyodhana</s>, father; shame on me, abandoned by merit,

children.text: bandhūnāṃ tvatpradhānānāṃ yaḥ kṣaye sākṣitāṃ gataḥ ||
children.translated_text: who have become a witness to the destruction of my kinsmen, with you at their head.
In childhood, while playing in your lap, I rumpled your linen garment;

children.text: mlāpitaṃ rājyalubdhena sa eva nihato bhavān ||
children.translated_text: now that same you has been slain by me, greedy for kingdom.'
Hearing this from <s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s>, the son of <s>Śantanu</s>, wishing to speak,
said to him: 'Do not, my son, create a false pain of remorse.
This whole world is dependent, not master of itself;
the world, stamped by its own karma, necessarily obtains coming-to-be and passing-away.
Once in a forest a Brahmin woman named <s>Gautamī</s>, tenderly loving her son,

children.text: daṣṭaṃ dadarśa sarpeṇa gatāsuṃ kānane purā ||
children.translated_text: saw her little boy bitten by a serpent and deprived of life.
Seeing her tormented by grief for her son, a hunter named <s>Arjunaka</s>
bound that serpent, took it, came up to <s>Gautamī</s>, and said:

children.text: ayaṃ putrasya te hantā mayā baddho bhujaṅgamaḥ
children.translated_text: 'This snake is the killer of your son, and I have bound it.

children.text: brūhi yāvatkṣipāmyenaṃ vahnau śastreṇa hanmi vā ||
children.translated_text: Tell me at once whether I should throw it into the fire or kill it with a weapon.'
Hearing these words of the hunter, <s>Gautamī</s>, disturbed, replied:
'This poor serpent does not deserve death, for it acted without understanding.
All beings are finite, marked by the seal of an appointed limit;

children.text: upayānti svayaṃ mṛtyuṃ hantā kaścinna kasyacit ||
children.translated_text: of themselves they come to death. No one is the killer of anyone.

children.text: tasmādasminna kopo me kutaḥ kope 'pi nigrahaḥ
children.translated_text: Therefore I have no anger toward this one; even if there were anger, what punishment could there be?

children.text: jaḍa vyādha vimuñcainaṃ hataḥ kālena me sutaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Dull hunter, release it. My son was killed by Time.'
Though the hunter was told this repeatedly by her, when out of anger
he did not abandon his intention to kill the serpent, the miserable snake then said:

children.text: hato 'yaṃ mṛtyunā bālo yo māṃ preritavānsvayam
children.translated_text: 'This boy was killed by <s>Mṛtyu</s>, who himself impelled me.
Since I was not independent, what power did I have, except to transgress his command?'
When the serpent had spoken thus, the hunter again said:

children.text: kāraṇena tvayā sarpa nīto 'yaṃ mṛtyunā śiśuḥ ||
children.translated_text: 'Serpent, because of you this child has been brought to death by <s>Mṛtyu</s>.

children.text: na hi nāma svayaṃ kaścitkareṇākṛṣya mṛtyunā
children.translated_text: For surely no one is led away by <s>Mṛtyu</s>, pulling him with his own hand,

children.text: nīto bhavadvidhā yāvadyātāḥ sarpa na hetutām
children.translated_text: until creatures like you, serpent, become the cause.
Therefore you must certainly be killed, since you are the cause of the child's destruction.'
As the hunter repeatedly spoke thus in anger against the serpent,
<s>Mṛtyu</s> himself, not to be restrained, came near and addressed him:

children.text: nāhamasya śiśorhantā na cāyaṃ bhujago jaḍa
children.translated_text: 'I am not the killer of this child, nor is this serpent, dull man.
The impeller is the Blessed <s>Kāla</s>; at destruction he destroys everything.
Those states moving in the three worlds, fashioned by <s>Kāla</s>,
touch the path of nonbeing and come into being again and again.'
When <s>Mṛtyu</s> had spoken thus, <s>Kāla</s> himself came and said to him:
'Neither I, nor <s>Mṛtyu</s>, nor the serpent is master over the fall of the boy.
Through its own deeds this world obtains death and arising;
people move about by the threads of karma, as if made of machinery.

children.text: jāyate vardhate bhuṅkte prasūte modate punaḥ
children.translated_text: A creature is born, grows, eats, begets, and rejoices again;

children.text: jīryate kṣīyate vāpi na jantuḥ karmaṇā vinā ||
children.translated_text: it ages or declines only through karma, never without karma.'

children.text: iti kālena kathite sarpaṃ tatyāja lubdhakaḥ
children.translated_text: When <s>Kāla</s> had said this, the hunter released the serpent,

children.text: pṛthagyayuśca te sarve naṣṭaśokā ca gautamī ||
children.translated_text: and they all went their separate ways; <s>Gautamī</s> too was freed from grief.
Thus people perish only through deeds done by themselves;
do not grieve for the lords of the earth who have gone to death through karma.
Asked by the son of <s>Pāṇḍu</s>, 'By whom was <s>Mṛtyu</s> conquered
while living in the householder's stage according to dharma?' the son of <s>Śantanu</s> replied:
Long ago in <s>Māhiṣmatī</s> there was a king born in the line of <s>Ikṣvāku</s>,
glorious, named <s>Suyodhana</s>, comparable to <s>Smara</s>, <s>Indra</s>, and <s>Dhanada</s>.

children.text: taṃ narmadā nadī dṛṣṭvā snātaṃ kamalalocanam
children.translated_text: Seeing him, lotus-eyed, bathing, the river <s>Narmadā</s>,
stricken with desire, fell in love with his graceful, playful form.
On her the king begot a daughter, lotus-eyed,
lovely, named <s>Sudarśanā</s>, whose sight delighted the eyes.
When she had reached youth, the Blessed <s>Pāvaka</s>, seeing her,
overcome by love, asked the king for her, taking the form of a Brahmin.

children.text: nirdhanāvajñayā tasmai tāṃ yadā na dadau nṛpaḥ
children.translated_text: When, out of contempt for his poverty, the king would not give her to him,
then that fire in his sacrifice went out of sight in anger.
Then, appeased by the officiating priests through observance, the seven-flamed one

children.text: svapne jagāda taṃ mahyaṃ kanyaiṣā dīyatāmiti ||
children.translated_text: spoke to him in a dream: 'This maiden should be given to me.'
Then the king, delighted when he saw him in visible form as <s>Sudarśana</s>,
gave his daughter to him, obtaining his presence at the sacrifice.
Requested by that king, even today the fire-god
dwells constantly present in <s>Māhiṣmatī</s>, destroying all calamities.
Then from <s>Sudarśanā</s> there was born to <s>Vibhāvasu</s>
a beloved son named <s>Sudarśana</s>, a great ocean of jewel-like virtues.

children.text: sutā moghavato rājñaḥ kāntāṃ moghavatīṃ yuvā
children.translated_text: As a young man he obtained <s>Moghavatī</s>, the lovely daughter of King <s>Moghavat</s>,

children.text: sa lebhe kṣīṇavāṇasya navā śaktiṃ manobhuvaḥ ||
children.translated_text: like the new power of the love-god when his arrows had been spent.

children.text: tayā saha kurukṣetre gṛhī dharmapade sthitaḥ
children.translated_text: With her, as a householder in <s>Kurukṣetra</s>, established on the path of <s>dharma</s>,
he, a wish-granting tree for petitioners, then made an effort to conquer death.
'The wishes of those who ask must in every way be fulfilled without breaking affection,'
so he always instructed his wife, his partner in the discipline of <s>dharma</s>.
As he did not fall away from <s>dharma</s>, death was always watching for a flaw in him,
hidden on every side, yet he found no opening.
Then one day, when <s>Sudarśana</s> himself had gone for firewood,
a certain guest, a brahmin, came up and spoke to his wife:

children.text: ātithyaṃ kriyatāṃ subhru rājaputri mama tvayā
children.translated_text: 'Fair-browed one, let hospitality be shown to me by you, princess.

children.text: yadi dharmaḥ pramāṇaṃ te tanmāṃ bhaja sulocane ||
children.translated_text: If <s>dharma</s> is your authority, then embrace me, lovely-eyed one.'
Although she tried to dissuade him with other boons as he spoke thus,
the twice-born man said again and again, 'Apart from you I ask for nothing.'

children.text: dharmyaṃ tataḥ sā vacanaṃ smṛtvā bhartuḥ pativratā
children.translated_text: Then that chaste wife, remembering her husband's righteous command,
said, 'So be it,' and did everything the brahmin desired.
At that moment <s>Sudarśana</s> came to the doorway of the house
and, though full of longing, waited after calling his beloved, 'Come here!'

children.text: sā bhartrā sahasāhūtā na ca prāptā dvijāntikam
children.translated_text: Suddenly summoned by her husband, she did not come away from the brahmin's side;
her heart rocking like a swing, she stood for a moment overcome with shame.
Then from inside the house the brahmin addressed <s>Sudarśana</s>:
'This wife of yours has been obtained by me, a guest who asked, for pleasure.

children.text: prāptā nādyāpi śayanaṃ prāptaśca tvaṃ gṛhādhipaḥ
children.translated_text: She has not yet reached the bed, and you, master of the house, have arrived.
What do you think is proper here?' Having said this, he fell silent.
Meanwhile death, his body concealed, took up a club
and, saying 'I have found my chance,' became filled with joy.
Then <s>Sudarśana</s>, his mind unaltered, said to the brahmin:
'Brahmin, without hesitation and with my permission, take pleasure with my wife.'
When the son of Fire had spoken thus, a vast cry of 'Good! Good!'
suddenly arose from the dwellers in heaven in the sky.
The guest abandoned the form of a brahmin and, assuming a great form,
came up to <s>Sudarśana</s> with joy and spoke, a mass of splendor:
'I am <s>Dharma</s>. I came to your hermitage wishing to test you two as a couple,
and I have seen this unbroken strength of character in you both.

children.text: adhṛṣṭā tejasā ceyaṃ tvadbhāryā kena laṅghyate
children.translated_text: Unassailable by her splendor, by whom could this wife of yours be violated?
Dividing herself in two through yoga, she will become the river <s>Oghavatī</s>

children.text: bhaviṣyati kṣitau puṇyā nityaṃ tvāṃ cānuyāsyati ||
children.translated_text: on earth, holy, and she will also always follow you.'
Having spoken thus, <s>Dharma</s> disappeared, and death went away disappointed;

children.text: sa ca vīro divaṃ prāpa sabhāryaśca sudarśanaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and that hero <s>Sudarśana</s>, together with his wife, reached heaven.
Asked by <s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s> how <s>Viśvāmitra</s> obtained the difficult state of a brahmin,
the son of <s>Gaṅgā</s> again spoke as follows:
In ancient times the glorious <s>Gādhi</s> was the son of King <s>Kuśika</s>;
he had a daughter named <s>Satyavatī</s>, doe-eyed in beauty.
The best of sages, <s>Ṛcīka</s>, obtained her as a bride won by a bride-price,
with a thousand moon-bright horses having dark ears.
That sage, carefully honored by her, who was endowed with good conduct,
was pleased and, when asked for a boon, granted a son for her mother and for herself.
'You should embrace an aśvattha tree, and your mother an udumbara tree;
and, receiving the sacrificial porridge given by me, you will both have sons,' said the sage.
Having received such a boon, she joyfully reported it to her mother;

children.text: tadgirā vyatyayaṃ cakre vṛkṣayoḥ pāyase tathā ||
children.translated_text: at her mother's words she made an exchange in the trees and likewise in the porridge.
Knowing this, the sage, whose eye was knowledge, said to his wife:
'Your mother's son will be a brahmin; yours will have a kṣatriya nature.'

children.text: tacchrutvā duḥkhasaṃtaptā yayāce sā muniṃ punaḥ
children.translated_text: Hearing that, she was scorched with grief and again begged the sage,

children.text: kṣatrācārastu me pautro mā putra iti mūrchitā ||
children.translated_text: fainting as she said, 'Let my grandson, not my son, have kṣatriya conduct.'
When he said, 'So be it,' <s>Satyavatī</s> bore a son,
<s>Jamadagni</s>; and his son was <s>Rāma</s>, fit for a kṣatriya.
And in due time <s>Gādhi</s>'s wife gave birth to <s>Viśvāmitra</s>,
who, because of the exchange of the tree and the porridge, became foremost among brahmins.
Again questioned by the king about the virtue of compassion, <s>Suravrata</s>
said: 'In a forest long ago there was a tree with dense shade.
Struck by a hunter, killer of deer, with a poison-burnt arrow,
it dried up, as if touched by forest fires.
When all the birds had abandoned that fruitless tree and gone away,
one parrot alone remained there; the affection of the good is unwavering.
In that tree, harsh from the scorching of summer heat and bereft of fruit and flowers...

children.text: sthitaṃ tatra śukaṃ vīkṣya śakro 'bhyetya tamabravīt ||
children.translated_text: Seeing the parrot staying there, <s>Śakra</s> came up and said to him:
"When there are trees with clear shade, fruit, and other gifts, why, bereft of splendor,

children.text: kiṃ tvayāyaṃ śritaḥ śākhī tyaktvainaḥ cara nirvṛtaḥ ||
children.translated_text: have you taken shelter in this tree? Abandon it and live happily."
Then the parrot said to <s>Śakra</s>, "This is not fittingly said.
Among good people, companionship is the same in happiness and in sorrow.

children.text: yatroṣitaṃ ca bhuktaṃ ca vihṛtaṃ ca yathāsukham
children.translated_text: Where one has lived, eaten, and sported at ease,
good people do not flee from that place when its prosperity has been struck down by time."
Hearing this, <s>Maghavan</s>, out of satisfaction, with drops of nectar
suddenly made the tree crowded with bursting leaves, flowers, and fruit.

children.text: ānṛśaṃsyātsa ca śukaḥ prayayau paramāṃ gatim
children.translated_text: And because of his non-cruelty that parrot went to the highest state.
Thus there is no other virtue equal to kindness.
Asked by the king about fate together with human effort, <s>Bhīṣma</s> again said:
"The conjunction of both leads to success; the separation of these two is fruitless.

children.text: anuptabīje kṛṣṭe 'pi daivaṃ kṣetre karoti kim
children.translated_text: What does fate do in a field that has been ploughed, if seed has not been sown?

children.text: pauruṣaṃ karma puruṣairyathā yatra yadā kṛtam
children.translated_text: Whatever human effort is done by men, wherever and whenever,

children.text: tathā tatra tadābhyetya visaṃvādo na dṛśyate ||
children.translated_text: that very result comes there and then; no discrepancy is seen.
For givers, for those of meritorious conduct, for observers of vows, and for speakers of truth,
various kinds of blessedness are seen, through kingdoms, heaven, births, and prosperity."
Asked by <s>Pārtha</s>, "Who are to be honored?" the firm-in-vow son of the river-goddess said:
"The twice-born are always to be honored; they are the supreme refuge everywhere.
In a former birth, two men had become a monkey and a jackal.
Remembering their former births, the two friends saw each other in a cremation ground.
There the monkey, his mind troubled, affectionately said to the jackal,
'By what action have you reached the state of eating corpse-flesh?'

children.text: pratiśrutya mayā pūrvaṃ na vitīrṇaṃ dvijanmane
children.translated_text: 'In the past, though I had promised, I did not give what was due to a twice-born man.
Therefore I have fallen into a jackal's womb,' he said.
Asked this same thing by the jackal, the monkey answered:
'I disrespected Brahmins; therefore I have come to monkeyhood.'
By transgressing against Brahmins, people enter a dark condition.
Therefore those who desire welfare should honor Brahmins with their whole being."

children.text: asavarṇopadeṣṭāraḥ kiṃ na syuḥ śreyasāṃ padam
children.translated_text: Again asked by the king, "May not Brahmins who instruct those of lower caste be the seat of blessings?"

children.text: viprā iti punaḥ pṛṣṭo rājñā śāntanavo 'bravīt ||
children.translated_text: the son of <s>Śaṃtanu</s> said:

children.text: purā vane śūdramuner brahmarṣir abhavat sakhā
children.translated_text: "Long ago, in a forest, a <s>brahmarṣi</s> (Brahmin sage) became the friend of a Śūdra ascetic.
Once, requested by that Śūdra at a <s>śrāddha</s> (ancestral rite), he went to his hermitage.
In that man's ancestral rite, while instructing him about the offerings to gods and ancestors,
the sage said, 'First arrange this remaining sacred grass-seat.'
Then, after a long time, having worn out their bodies,
the two entered another birth in order to experience the residue of their karma.
That Śūdra became a king, and that <s>brahmarṣi</s> became his priest.
For that king the priest had lost knowledge and all memory had disappeared.
At auspicious and merit-invoking recitations among good men, the king, remembering his former birth,

children.text: sadā jahāsa taccāsau nṛpaṃ papraccha lajjitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: would always laugh; and that embarrassed priest asked the king about it.
When asked, with an oath demanded, the king privately told the priest
the reason for his laughter: 'In the past I was a Śūdra.
And you, a <s>brahmarṣi</s>, once gave instruction to me.
Because of that, though now worthy of reverence by the gods, you have attained this improper condition.'

children.text: śrutvaitatsahasā smṛtvā tapase sa yayau muniḥ
children.translated_text: Hearing this and suddenly remembering, the sage went away to perform austerities.
Thus the best of the twice-born should not become an instructor of those beneath him."
Asked by the king, "Who is the vessel of fortune?" the son of <s>Jāhnavī</s>

children.text: pṛṣṭaḥ prāha hareragre rukmiṇīṃ śrīḥ purābhyadhāt ||
children.translated_text: said that once, in the presence of <s>Hari</s>, <s>Śrī</s> spoke to <s>Rukmiṇī</s>:
"Among fortunate, bold, capable people whose deeds are radiant,

children.text: jitendriyeṣu vīreṣu prītyā me śāśvatī sthitiḥ ||
children.translated_text: among self-controlled heroes, my abiding presence is eternal and loving.
Those who are free from arrogance, greed, fear, wretchedness, and anger,
who are grateful and well-conducted, are always my pleasure-house.
I attend upon a woman who is devoted to her husband, not quarrelsome, not fickle, not over-curious,
whose utensils are not scattered about, and who has put away sleep.
I dwell among intoxicated lordly elephants, among horses and bulls,
among clusters of blooming lotuses, and among the rays of the autumn moon;
in rivers smiling with swans, in battles where kings shine forth,
in forests holy with sages, and in sacrifices."
Having heard this, the son of <s>Pāṇḍu</s> again asked <s>Bhīṣma</s>:

children.text: sparśādhikyaṃ kimu strīṇāṃ nṛṇāṃ vā saṃgameṣviti ||
children.translated_text: "In sexual unions, is the greater pleasure of touch found in women or in men?"
He said: "There was a sacrificing king named <s>Bhṛṅgāśva</s>,
who was like a constant springtime for the flowering creepers of fame.
He again performed an <s>agniṣṭut</s> sacrifice, hostile to the mighty one,
by which <s>Vāsava</s> came to enmity with him.
Once, desiring game, he was travelling through the forest on horseback,
when, bewildered by <s>Indra</s> and tormented by thirst, dear child, he lost his way.
Ahead he saw a broad lake, clear as crystal,
marked by the swing of restless waves, a pleasure-house of the cold-rayed moon.
After bathing in it at once and watering his horse,
he became a woman in form, with full hips and breasts.
Overcome by shame and sorrow, he went on horseback to his own city.
After reporting his own story, he appointed his hundred sons to the kingdom.
Then, in female form, abandoning the kingdom, he went to a deserted ascetic grove,
pondering within himself the perverse play of fate.
There an ascetic desired him, who had the form of a lovely woman.
Wherever there is a lotus pond, there the bees alight.
Therefore he begot a hundred mighty sons;
and, lovely in body, he was always exceedingly affectionate toward them.
Then he went to his earlier sons, born while he was male, and said:
'Let the earth be enjoyed together with those sons of mine born while I was female.'
At his word the two hundreds of sons came to be united,
and they enjoyed the earth, governed by unfaded fame and valor.
Meanwhile <s>Śatakratu</s>, approaching in the form of a brahmin,
produced the arising of strife by dividing the king's sons.
Then they, armed for battle against one another for the sake of the kingdom,

children.text: kṛtvā sainyakṣayaṃ ghoraṃ niḥśeṣāḥ pralayaṃ yayuḥ ||
children.translated_text: caused a terrible destruction of their armies and all met their end.
When the two hundreds of sons had gone to death in battle through division,
<s>Bhṛṅgāśva</s>, in a woman's form, lamented with a piteous sound.
Seeing him and hearing that tale, <s>Indra</s>, wearing a brahmin's body,
his anger gone, repeatedly spoke, smiling, out of compassion:
'I am <s>Śakra</s>; these sons of yours, who acted displeasingly toward me,

children.text: bheditā nādhunā vairamāpanne tvayi me nṛpa ||
children.translated_text: were split apart by me. Now, king, I have no hostility toward you in your distress.
Let one hundred of your sons live today by my boon,
whichever you wish: those born before from the male, or those from the female body.'
When the king of the gods had spoken thus, <s>Bhṛṅgāśva</s> asked him,
bowing his face, for life for the sons born from his womanhood.
<s>Surapati</s> said to him, 'How is it that you abandon the sons born from masculinity
and feel affection for the sons produced from womanhood?'
Questioned thus by <s>Maghavat</s>, the king in a woman's body said:
'Women alone are the abode of affection, tenderness, and love.
Hearing this, <s>Śakra</s> said, 'Let all your sons live;

children.text: strīrūpaṃ tu parityajya puruṣo bhava madvarāt ||
children.translated_text: but abandon your female form and become a man by my boon.'
Thus addressed, the king said, 'I will not give up womanhood;

children.text: strīṇāṃ sparśeṣu yā prītiḥ sā puṃbhirlabhyate kutaḥ ||
children.translated_text: for the pleasure that is in women's touches, how can it be obtained by men?
Having, by fate, experienced these two natures for a very long time,
this much alone I know: women are the vessel of pleasure.

children.text: kāmasya sāraṃ surataṃ ratasya sparśāmṛtaṃ tacca sulocanānām
children.translated_text: The essence of desire is lovemaking; the essence of lovemaking is the nectar of touch, and that belongs to the fair-eyed women.

children.text: sarvātmanā nirvṛtijīvaśūnyaṃ bhave bhave jīvitameva kāntāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Beloved women alone are life in birth after birth; without that, life is utterly empty of satisfaction and vitality.'
Hearing that he had spoken according to the truth, the lord of the gods
departed pleased, after reviving his two hundred sons.
Having heard this, the son of <s>Dharma</s> again said to the son of <s>Gaṅgā</s>:
'I wish to hear the greatness of the god who is enemy of <s>Tripura</s>.'
When asked thus by the king, the grandsire declared:
'<s>Keśava</s> is fit to speak of the greatness of the god of gods.

children.text: harireva haraṃ vetti haro vetti tathā harim
children.translated_text: <s>Hari</s> alone knows <s>Hara</s>, and <s>Hara</s> likewise knows <s>Hari</s>;
theirs is one form, which for a certain cause has taken on duality.'
When <s>Devavrata</s> had spoken thus, <s>Murāri</s>,
asked by the son of <s>Dharma</s>, reverently told of the power of the moon-crested one:

children.text: putrārthinī jāmbavatī priyā provāca māṃ purā
children.translated_text: 'Long ago my beloved <s>Jāmbavatī</s>, desiring a son, said to me:
"Lord, I wish from you to obtain a son like <s>Pradyumna</s>, suited to a son's virtues;
let this resolve of mine be fulfilled by you."
So addressed by that beloved, whose eyes were like those of a young deer,
I meditated for a moment and, desiring a son, went to undertake worshipful service.
Then, after ascending the mountain, to what was once a hermitage grove of sages,
I saw <s>Upamanyu</s>, a mass of splendors, in his own hermitage,
joyful, of advanced age, adorned by the boon of the bearer of <s>Pināka</s>,
blazing with various austerities, his body full of beauty,
with tranquil, lovely being that gave delight,
as he poured forth a stream of sweet, noble nectar of liberation.
Seeing him, I bowed; accepting the worship he performed,
I became filled with supreme bliss born from conversation with him.
He, whose eye was knowledge, spoke lovingly to me as I bowed:
'Having worshiped the god <s>Giriśa</s>, you will obtain a son equal to yourself.
Those conquerors of the three worlds, headed by <s>Sukeśi</s>, in ancient times,
are heard to have attained a station greater than <s>Śakra</s>'s through <s>Śaṃkara</s>'s boon.
Long ago, in this hermitage of my father, the great seer <s>Vyāghrapāda</s>,
after once tasting cow's milk, I asked my mother for it.
Because milk was not available, my mother then gave me a drink made from flour;
having drunk it and found it tasteless, I became tear-eyed with sorrow.

children.text: athābravīnmāṃ jananī vane putra payaḥ kutaḥ
children.translated_text: Then my mother said to me, "Son, whence is milk in the forest?
For without worshiping <s>Śrīkaṇṭha</s>, what is desired is never obtained anywhere."
Hearing my mother's words, I went to the ascetic grove;
with effort I performed severe austerity for a thousand years.
I would not ask from another, even for a boon bestowed by <s>Śakra</s> himself,
apart from the god <s>Dhūrjaṭi</s>, whose crest is the nectar-rayed moon.

children.text: tenālaṃ surarājyena kiṃ mokṣeṇāpi tena me
children.translated_text: Enough, then, with the sovereignty of the gods; what even is liberation to me,
if <s>Śaṃkara</s>, beloved through guileless devotion, is not the giver there?
When <s>Śakra</s> had been addressed many times in this way by me, who was devoted to <s>Bharga</s>,
he abandoned his Indra-form and became <s>Vṛṣabhadhvaja</s>.
Seeing the trident-bearing, matted-haired god, wearing the digit of the moon,
I became a torrent of tears flowing from overflowing bliss.

children.text: tataḥ stuto mayā śaṃbhurmahyaṃ kṣīrodadhiṃ dadau
children.translated_text: Then <s>Śaṃbhu</s>, praised by me, gave me an ocean of milk.
and in that hermitage, by my resolve, he established his presence near me.
Worship that boon-giving lord, the husband of <s>Pārvatī</s>, with ascetic practice,

children.text: labhasva tanayaṃ kṛṣṇa tasyātmā tvaṃ sa vā tava ||
children.translated_text: and obtain a son, <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>; he is your own self, and you are his.
Having spoken thus, <s>Upamanyu</s> initiated me into the ordinance of <s>Śiva</s>
and instructed me in the discipline of austerity, saying, 'Receive the secret.'
Then, with the mantra given by him and with austerity, concentrated in mind,
in time I saw the god who bears the crescent moon on his crest.
He was mounted on a mass of clouds in the sky, shining with the brightness of a hundred moons;
and seeing him, I bowed in welcome, praised him, and became filled with joy.
Then <s>Maheśvara</s>, after granting me the boons I desired,
disappeared, as if filling the ten directions with floods of nectar.
Then <s>Upamanyu</s> came to me, and, seeing me exalted and delighted, said:
'Listen, <s>Mādhava</s>, to the names of <s>Dhūrjaṭi</s> spoken by <s>Taṇḍi</s>.
Formerly a sage named <s>Taṇḍi</s>, with secret hymns sung by <s>Svayaṃbhū</s>,

children.text: trinetraṃ prayataṃ nāmnāṃ tuṣṭāva daśabhiḥ śataiḥ ||
children.translated_text: praised the three-eyed lord, with devotion, by ten hundreds of names.

children.text: sthāṇo sthirasthite śaṃbho śarva bhāno varaprada
children.translated_text: O <s>Sthāṇu</s>, O steadfastly established one, O <s>Śaṃbhu</s>, O <s>Śarva</s>, O radiant one, giver of boons,
O <s>Hara</s>, O <s>Rudra</s>, foe of <s>Smara</s>, O universe, O lord of the lord of the universe,
O <s>Bhava</s>, O <s>Bharga</s>, O auspicious refuge, beloved of <s>Bhavānī</s>, O lord,
O you whose crest-ornament is a fragment of the moon, O <s>Śiva</s>, O peaceful one, O <s>Maheśvara</s>,
homage to you, who bring about the creation, preservation, and destruction of the world,
whose forms are <s>Brahmā</s>, <s>Upendra</s>, and <s>Indra</s>, who are the three guṇas and the three forms.
With such divine words of praise and with names proclaimed by the Veda,
numbering a thousand, that sage praised the moon-crested lord.
After thus holding conversations with the sage concerning <s>Īśvara</s>,
I mounted <s>Garuḍa</s> and went to <s>Dvārakā</s>, filled with joy.
Then from <s>Jāmbavatī</s> a splendid son, a pearl of the lineage,
<s>Sāmba</s>, was born; you know his qualities, son of <s>Dharma</s>.':
Hearing this told by <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, the sages in <s>Bhīṣma</s>'s assembly
bowed in their minds to the blue-throated god.
'How are wives of men fickle and attended by companions?'
Asked again by the king, the son of <s>Jāhnavī</s> spoke:
Formerly the sage <s>Aṣṭāvakra</s>, wishing to marry <s>Sulocanā</s>,
saw a beautiful woman named <s>Suprabhā</s>, the daughter of the sage <s>Vadanya</s>.
Her exceedingly delicate form was like the moon, jasmine, and a fresh sprout;

children.text: sa tāmālokya sumukhīṃ yayāce sotsuko munim ||
children.translated_text: seeing that fair-faced woman, he eagerly asked the sage for her.
<s>Vadanya</s> said to him, 'Go to the broad northern quarter,
passing beyond the palace of <s>Kubera</s>, which is attended by <s>Bhava</s>.
When you have returned from there, I shall give you <s>Suprabhā</s>.'

children.text: ityuktaḥ sa vadanyena pratasthe tāṃ diśaṃ śanaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: So addressed by <s>Vadanya</s>, he set out slowly toward that quarter.
Then, crossing the <s>Himādri</s> and the great river <s>Bāhudā</s>,
and bathing in <s>Aśoka</s> and <s>Vimala</s>, he reached <s>Rudrāṇī</s>'s well.
Reaching the slope of <s>Kailāsa</s>, he saw the abode of the lord of wealth,
a grove of wish-granting vines shining on the banks of golden lotus-ponds.
Respectfully honored there by King <s>Vaiśravaṇa</s>,
he lived for more than a year in pleasure-houses made of jewels.
For a long time he gained great delight from the dances of apsarases
and the songs of gandharva women; then, taking leave of <s>Dhanada</s>, he departed.
Then, crossing the greatest mountains and descending to a level jewel-made ground,
he reached a grove of jewel-vines, dense with shade.
In that divine forest, cool with golden lotus-pools,
he saw a noble mansion whose frame was netted with gems and pearls.
Then he approached the front door of that beryl house
and said, hoping for shelter, 'I have arrived from afar as a guest.'
Then seven lotus-eyed maidens came out,
adorned with divine ornaments, and offered him hospitality.
Led by them into the house, bright with a seat of gold and jewels,
he saw on a jeweled couch an old woman wearing brilliant ornaments.
Receiving from that sweet-speaking woman the seat she indicated,
the sage, his fatigue gone, remained for a moment motionless with wonder.

children.text: dinānte so 'tha tāḥ prāha yāntu sarvāḥ svamālayam
children.translated_text: At the end of the day he said to them, 'Let all of you go to your own dwelling;
let only one, calm in heart, attend upon me.'
When the sage had spoken thus, all those beautiful-eyed women went away;
only one aged woman, clothed in moon-white garments, stayed there.
Then <s>Aṣṭāvakra</s> slept on a pleasingly soft bed,
with a canopy hung with garlands of mandāra blossoms and with a clean coverlet.
Then the old woman rose slowly from another bed
and quietly went to the bedside of the celibate sage.
Her body trembling, distressed, she climbed onto the bed
and, under the pretext of cold, tightly embraced the sage.
As she embraced him, he remained motionless like a piece of wood,
his mind fixed on the fear of embracing another's wife.
Then she, seeing him averse to touch, spoke sweetly out of affection:

children.text: uvāca bhogasaṃkalpabhaṅgaṃ mā me kṛthāḥ prabho ||
children.translated_text: 'Lord, do not frustrate my resolve for pleasure.
This jeweled mansion of mine, this lovely grove of jewel-vines,
is under your control; suddenly my mind takes delight in you.

children.text: na te doṣo 'sti matsaṅge tyājyā naiva tu yoṣitaḥ
children.translated_text: There is no fault for you in union with me; women should certainly not be rejected.

children.text: durgamaṃ nābhijānanti gaṇayanti na ca śramam ||
children.translated_text: They do not recognize what is hard to reach, and they do not count the effort;
women go only to men with the snare of passion.'
These women do not turn back out of regard for family, nor because of jealousy.
Among women <s>Makaradhvaja</s> has his advance entirely unobstructed.
The saying, 'A woman is faithful,' is merely a rumor; what talk can there be of her being attached to one man?
They go on to another man, as rivers go from hollow to hollow.
How can a woman driven by <s>Manmatha</s> resort to deliberation?
For them, even at the stake of life, the beloved nectar of lovemaking is dear.
Though she pleaded with him in this way, the sage did not welcome her.
On the next night too she addressed him in just the same way:
'Enjoy me, who have come of my own accord; my fever of love is unbearable.
For women, they say, restraint in desires for pleasure is death.'

children.text: ityuktvā nirvikāraṃ taṃ sā dṛṣṭvā punarabravīt ||
children.translated_text: Having said this, she saw that he remained unchanged, and spoke again:
'Know me to be the northern quarter. The conduct of women has been shown to you.

children.text: adhunā tāṃ vadanyasya gatvā prāpnuhi kanyakām ||
children.translated_text: Now go to <s>Vadanya</s> and obtain that maiden from him.'
Hearing this, the sage, amazed, took leave of her
and slowly returned to his own hermitage, having learned the conduct of women.
Then he went to <s>Vadanya</s> and reported that affair of women's conduct to him,
and by the rite of marriage he obtained <s>Suprabhā</s>, whom <s>Vadanya</s> gave to him.
Then, when asked about śrāddha according to rule, and also about the order of worthy and unworthy recipients,

children.text: rājñā gatiṃ ca tīrthaṃ ca pṛṣṭaḥ śāntanavo 'bravīt ||
children.translated_text: and about a king's destiny and tīrthas, <s>Śāntanava</s> spoke:
One should worship the gods in the forenoon, pure, dressed in white, with senses subdued,
adorned with auspicious ornaments and wearing a garland, with pure and pleasing enjoyments.
But the ancestral rite should be performed in the afternoon, with a carefully restrained mind,

children.text: teṣu teṣu ca kāleṣu deśeṣu ca yathāvidhi ||
children.translated_text: at the proper times and in the proper places, according to rule.
A śrāddha lacking the proper place, time, and other conditions, licked by dogs, with its savor fallen away,
or touched by insects, cocoons, or bones, is eaten by rākṣasas.
Madmen, the wretched, the one-eyed, lepers, husbands of low-caste women,
physicians, usurers, and those who live by singing, dancing, and the like,
those with deficient or excessive limbs, heavy men, sellers of sacred knowledge, liars,
those without sacred fires, eaters at public sacrificial sessions, kṣatriyas, and those who live from fields,
slanderers, those without vows, and those devoid of Vedic learning,
and also sceptics who destroy śrāddha, are brahmins always to be avoided.
For men who steal others' property and approach others' wives,
for breakers of vows, the greedy, and those who live by forbidden trade,
for those who cut off another's livelihood, friend, or husband,
and for those devoid of prescribed conduct, hell is an imperishable abode.
For those whose minds are full of compassion, who are generous, and who shower gifts on worthy recipients,
for the patient, for āśramins, and for makers of feeding houses, wells, and assembly halls,
for sacrificers, those purified by tīrthas, the learned, and speakers of truth,
and for those who abstain from wine and meat, the road to heaven is unobstructed.
Long ago, when asked by <s>Gautama</s>, the all-knowing sage <s>Aṅgiras</s>,
smiling, spoke of the merit of tīrthas through the discipline of austerity.
<s>Candrabhāgā</s>, <s>Vitastā</s>, and the rivers of <s>Kaśmīra</s>,
when visited, indeed grant men a destiny equal to that of sages.

children.text: bhāgīrathīṃ kauśikīṃ ca rāmaṇīṃ narmadāṃ tathā
children.translated_text: <s>Bhāgīrathī</s>, <s>Kauśikī</s>, <s>Rāmaṇī</s>, and <s>Narmadā</s>,

children.text: prayāgaṃ nandikuṇḍaṃ ca vipāśaṃ mānasaṃ saraḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Prayāga</s>, <s>Nandikuṇḍa</s>, <s>Vipāśā</s>, and <s>Mānasa</s> lake,
and other holy tīrthas: when a man with senses subdued reaches them,
as a giver who has fasted beforehand, he obtains the fruit of all tīrthas.
But <s>Gaṅgā</s> is called the foremost tīrtha among all tīrthas;
when even a mere bone is touched by her, men gain an imperishable path to heaven.

children.text: na te deśā na te śailā na te janapadāḥ kṣitau
children.translated_text: Those are not countries, those are not mountains, those are not districts on earth

children.text: patākā yasya puṇyasya jāhnavī na vibhāvyate ||
children.translated_text: where <s>Jāhnavī</s>, the banner of that merit, is not perceived.
What use are sacrifices full of danger? What use are austerities that bring fatigue,
if the bodies of the meritorious are purified by the water of <s>Jahnukanyā</s>?
She is a pearl-creeper of the sky's splendor, a garland on the crest of <s>Śrīkaṇṭha</s>;
for those into whose memory she has entered, she serves only to break all sins.
For those touched by <s>Gaṅgā</s>'s water, heaven itself is a small reward:
so a siddha who formerly lived by gleaning said when asked.
Having heard this spoken by <s>Aṅgiras</s>, <s>Gautama</s>, it is said,

children.text: smṛtvā vavande sānandaḥ puṇyāṃ mandākinīṃ muniḥ ||
children.translated_text: remembered and joyfully bowed to the holy <s>Mandākinī</s>.
When the king asked, 'How can brāhmaṇya be attained by a man?'

children.text: pṛṣṭo devavrataḥ prāha brāhmaṇyaṃ durlabhaṃ nṛpa ||
children.translated_text: <s>Devavrata</s> said, 'Brāhmaṇya is hard to obtain, O king.
At his father's command, for the sake of a sacrifice, a twice-born man named <s>Mataṅga</s>,
travelling in a vehicle, struck a donkey hard with a goad.

children.text: gardabhī vyathitaṃ dṛṣṭvā putraṃ duḥkhāduvāca tam
children.translated_text: Seeing her son in pain, the she-ass spoke to him in grief:
'There is no brāhmaṇya in this man; therefore, though born, he acts like a caṇḍāla.

children.text: vahainamiti tacchrutvā priyaḥ papraccha tāṃ punaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Carry him.' Hearing that, the beloved one questioned her again.

children.text: tayā niveditāṃ jātiṃ nijāṃ jñātvā sa duḥkhitaḥ
children.translated_text: When she told him his own birth, he understood it and became sorrowful;

children.text: meroḥ śṛṅgādiva śvabhre patito vilalāpa saḥ ||
children.translated_text: as if fallen from <s>Meru</s>'s peak into a chasm, he lamented.

children.text: pitre nivedya tatpāpaṃ mātuḥ sa tapase vanam
children.translated_text: After reporting that sin of his mother to his father, he went to the forest for austerity,
desiring brāhmaṇya, and remained like a post for a hundred years.
Even from <s>Śakra</s>, who came to him in person, he did not obtain brāhmaṇya.

children.text: tato gatvā gayāṃ cakre sahasrābdaṃ paraṃtapaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then, going to <s>Gayā</s>, he performed the highest austerity for a thousand years.
Again and again, by his austerity, he made the three worlds smoke, as it were;
from <s>Indra</s> he obtained divinity, but not the supreme brāhmaṇya.

children.text: chandodeva iti khyātaḥ sa mataṅgābhidhaḥ purā
children.translated_text: In ancient times that one named <s>Mataṅga</s> became famed as <s>Chandodeva</s>;
he became a sky-goer, honored by doe-eyed women and exceedingly dear to them.'
It is indeed heard that king <s>Vītahavya</s> attained Brahminhood.

children.text: tadvadeti punaḥ pṛṣṭo rājñā prāha pitāmahaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Again asked by the king, "Tell that also," the grandsire spoke.
In former times, by the sons of <s>Vītahavya</s>, the <s>Hehayas</s>, who were very powerful,
the king of <s>Kāśi</s>, named <s>Haryaśva</s>, was struck down in battle.
In time, his son too, again by those same men in combat,
<s>Sudeva</s> was struck down in the city of <s>Kāśi</s> by enemies who had found their mark.
His son also, <s>Divodāsa</s>, was defeated by those same men in war;
through the grace of <s>Bharadvāja</s> he obtained a son, <s>Pratardana</s>.
He, having gone against all the sons of <s>Vītahavya</s> in battle,
killed them, expert in supreme weapons and having gained <s>Bharadvāja</s>'s boon.
<s>Vītahavya</s>, his sons slain and his army and vehicles destroyed,
pursued by <s>Pratardana</s>, went for refuge to <s>Bhṛgu</s>.
Having reached <s>Bhṛgu</s>'s hermitage, intent on killing <s>Vītahavya</s>,
the proud <s>Pratardana</s> said to the sage, "Release this man."

children.text: tacchrutvā kṣatriyo neha kaścitsarve dvijā vayam
children.translated_text: Hearing that, <s>Bhṛgu</s>, afraid, said, "There is no Kṣatriya here; we are all twice-born,"
and then he trembled at the falsehood.
When <s>Pratardana</s> understood that his enemy had fallen away from the designation of Kṣatriya
and had departed, <s>Bhṛgu</s>, whose speech was truthful, made <s>Vītahavya</s> a Brahmin.

children.text: ke praṇamyā iti punaḥ pṛṣṭaḥ śāntanavo 'bravīt
children.translated_text: Again asked, "Who are to be bowed to?" the son of <s>Śaṃtanu</s> said:
Brahmins devoted to the <s>dharma</s> (religious duty) of their own work, free from violence and passion,
Brahmins alone, whose conduct and vows are pure, are to be bowed to,
by whose anger and favor there is the drying up and nourishing of kings.
The earth-gods are always to be honored; by their favor the sacrificial fire

children.text: havyaṃ kavyaṃ ca vahati kṛṣṇamityāha nāradaḥ ||
children.translated_text: carries the oblation to gods and ancestors, as <s>Nārada</s> said to <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>.

children.text: jaye balaṃ bhaye rakṣā bheṣajaṃ vyasanāmaye
children.translated_text: "May Brahmins be strength for you in victory, protection in fear, medicine in the illness of calamity,
and, in the next world, <s>Śakra</s>," so <s>Śambara</s> said.
Asked by the son of <s>Pāṇḍu</s> about the nature of women, naturally restless
and of minds hard to discern, the grandsire explained.
Once, when asked by <s>Nārada</s> about women's nature, the heavenly woman
named <s>Pañcacūlā</s>, trembling at a curse, spoke truthfully.

children.text: strī satī strīsvabhāvaṃ ca mādṛśī vaktumarhati
children.translated_text: "A woman, especially a true woman like me, is fit to speak of women and women's nature.
Afraid of your command, however, I shall speak in truth.
They cause friction and agitation, are anxious, and have turbid intentions;
intoxicated, they carry off one's body, like rivers carrying off low ground.

children.text: apyanviṣṭā na labhyante saṃtyaktā na tyajanti ca
children.translated_text: Even when sought they are not found; when abandoned they do not leave;
like latent dispositions in worldly existence, women are wholly devoted to delusion.
They laugh when sorrowful, and when delighted they grieve in contempt;

children.text: rāgiṇyo 'pi priyaṃ ghnanti ko hi tāṃ vetti yoṣitam ||
children.translated_text: even when passionate, they injure the beloved. Who indeed knows a woman?

children.text: na kulena na mānena na dhanena na sevayā
children.translated_text: Not through family, honor, wealth, or service
do women of fickle intention keep to proper bounds.

children.text: suveśaṃ subhagaṃ kāntaṃ tyaktvā paricitaṃ ciram
children.translated_text: Abandoning a well-dressed, fortunate, beloved man long familiar to them,
women at their own will take pleasure in one contemptible and never seen before.
If they are addressed sweetly, if they are looked at with a smile,

children.text: yantritāḥ svajanenāpi tadā sādhyā na yoṣitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: then women cannot be controlled, even by their own people.
Sometimes, from the failure to find suitors, or from suffering, poverty, and hardship,
chastity arises among women quite by chance.
Noble women look with longing upon courtesans
who sport joyfully in the laughter and intimacy of many men.
For women, desire grows precisely because of prohibition,
as for sick children toward other contacts and unwholesome things.
Desire, whose range is uncut, cannot make them endure steadiness;
when men are unavailable, women proceed with one another.
What wise man would ever trust women, cruel and attached for a moment,
like twilights, with faults always near at hand?
Compassion is never found in wicked people in any way,
nor lack of arrogance in the rich, nor straightforwardness in doe-eyed women.
Even good women, restrained by many kinds of hindrances,
on seeing a handsome man suddenly become moist with desire.
Long ago womankind was honorable and became an object of anxiety to the gods;
thereupon, entreated for the gods' sake, the creator made women by creating destructive spirits.
Women acquire modesty to increase men's curiosity,
and the vow of chastity is artificial, a means of winning the husband's trust.

children.text: nṛtyanti śocanti patanti yānti hasanti gāyanti vadanti yacca
children.translated_text: Whatever women do, whether they dance, grieve, fall, go, laugh, sing, or speak,
all that activity of women, like a dream, is made of illusion and altogether false."

children.text: tāḥ striyo lolamatayaḥ kathaṃ rakṣyā narairiti
children.translated_text: Again asked by <s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s>, "How are such women of unsteady mind to be guarded by men?"
the son of the river <s>Tripathagā</s> spoke again.
Once the sage <s>Devaśarman</s>, preparing to go for the sake of a sacrifice,
instructed his disciple <s>Vipula</s> about the very deceptive <s>Śatakratu</s>.

children.text: jñātvā ruciṃ śarīrāntaḥ praviśa tvaṃ samīravat
children.translated_text: Knowing <s>Ruci</s>, he entered within her body like the wind;
pressing her limbs with his own limbs, he remained there attentively.
Meanwhile <s>Sahasrākṣa</s>, seizing the opportunity, arrived.
He saw <s>Ruci</s>, lovely-eyed and again motionless,
with golden breasts and hips, like a golden doll.
Then, when <s>Ākhaṇḍala</s> approached, she became filled with desire,
but, restrained by <s>Vipula</s>, the lovely-eyed woman could not speak.
She was scattered with the flowers of laughter, with her restless locks as bees,
like a creeper standing without wind, with trembling hand-sprouts.
Seeing her, the astonished <s>Śakra</s>, sharply rebuked by <s>Vipula</s>, went away.
Then the sage <s>Devaśarman</s>, having returned, learned all that had happened.
After that, <s>Vipula</s> obtained boons from his pleased teacher,
and, his purpose fulfilled, wandered over the earth, honored by kings and Brahmins.
Meanwhile, invited by his wife's sister's husband, King <s>Ruciraṅga</s>,
she saw her sister in the house, adorned with flowers.
At her word, the disciple was sent by <s>Devaśarman</s> to fetch flowers,

children.text: dadarśa mithunaṃ ṣaṭ ca devinaḥ kitavān pathi ||
children.translated_text: and on the road he saw a pair, and six gamblers playing dice.
In their dispute he heard this oath: "May the one who departs from an agreement
attain the worlds earned by <s>Vipula</s>."
Hearing this, he was distressed; he approached his teacher and reported it,
fearing the sin of having touched the body of his teacher's wife.
The teacher said to him, "That pair is called day and night,

children.text: ṛtavaḥ ṣaṭ ca kitavāste nṛṇāṃ karmasākṣiṇaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and those six gamblers are the seasons; they are witnesses of men's deeds.

children.text: na śakyā rakṣituṃ nāryo rakṣitā ca tvayā ruciḥ
children.translated_text: Women cannot be guarded, yet <s>Ruci</s> was guarded by you.
What was proclaimed about you was false; therefore let the sin perish."

children.text: ityevaṃ rakṣitā pūrvaṃ vipulena guroḥ priyā
children.translated_text: Thus in ancient times the teacher's beloved wife was guarded by <s>Vipula</s>;
but no one is able to guard such women with restless eyes.
Then, asked by the king about the <s>vivāhadharma</s> (law of marriage), <s>Bhīṣma</s> spoke again:
"A maiden should be given to a man of good qualities, noble family, and excellent beauty.
A maiden given to an inferior man is like the <s>śruti</s> handed over to a Śūdra;
she burns both families. Therefore one should examine the suitable recipient.
From marriages not prescribed by <s>śāstra</s> arises mixture of castes,
and through unequal unions among men a family falls into misfortune."

children.text: darśane sahavāse ca satāṃ pṛṣṭo mahībhujā
children.translated_text: Asked by the king about the sight of good people, about living with them,

children.text: māhātmyaṃ ca gavāṃ bhīṣmaḥ sarvajñaḥ punarabravīt ||
children.translated_text: and about the greatness of cows, all-knowing <s>Bhīṣma</s> spoke again:
"Between the <s>Gaṅgā</s> and <s>Yamunā</s>, <s>Cyavana</s>, under a vow of remaining beneath the water,
stood for a very long time, a chief of sages, a great ascetic, motionless as a post.
Smelling the holy fragrance of that compassionate one,
fish clung to his limbs as if playfully forming bracelets.
Then, after a long time, fishermen drew up in a net
a vast mass of fish, and in its midst they saw the sage,
wrapped in stalks of waterweed, adorned with bracelets and garlands of shells,
tawny with green beard and matted hair, like a mass of radiant energy.

children.text: taṃ vīkṣya kampitāḥ sarve sahasā jālajīvinaḥ
children.translated_text: Seeing him, all the net-fishermen suddenly trembled,
and said to him, whose eyes were closed, 'Have mercy, venerable lord.'
Then, filled with compassion for the fish who had lived with him,
he looked at the <s>Niṣādas</s>, wishing to bless them with his glance, and said:
'Sell me, and let the water-dwellers be released by you.

children.text: dayitāḥ sahavāsānme matsyā yūyaṃ ca darśanāt ||
children.translated_text: The fish are dear to me because they lived with me, and you are dear because you have seen me.'
When the sage had said this, the fishermen quickly went to the king
and, trembling, reported their own affair to <s>Nahuṣa</s>.

children.text: tataḥ svayaṃ sa nṛpatiḥ pūjāmādāya satvaraḥ
children.translated_text: Then that king himself, quickly taking offerings of worship,
placed his priest before him and came to see <s>Cyavana</s>.
The sage saw <s>Nahuṣa</s>, who had bowed and stood with folded hands,
and urged him, 'Take me for a proper price.'
'To the fishermen I will give thousands, hundreds of crores of crores,
or half my kingdom, or even the kingdom,' said the king.
'This is not a fitting price for me; consider the matter together with the sages,'
the sage repeatedly told the king, out of compassion for the fishermen.
Then, as <s>Nahuṣa</s> stood dejected, face downcast and afraid of a curse,

children.text: gavi jāto dvijavaro babhāṣe dhīmatāṃ varaḥ ||
children.translated_text: a foremost Brahmin, born from a cow and best among the wise, spoke:
'Only a cow is the supreme equivalent price for this lord of sages.
Therefore, O king, purchase him with a cow and be at peace.'
When the Brahmin had said this, the lord of the earth rejoiced,
and, for the release of the mass of fish, bought the <s>Bhārgava</s> with a cow.
Then <s>Cyavana</s>, treasure of compassion, out of affection born from that sight,
accepted the cow from the fishermen, intent on their welfare.
When the cow had been duly accepted by the chief sage,
the fishermen and the fish, by the fall of his glance, went bodily to heaven.
Cows are the abode of nectar, pure, the mothers of <s>Rudra</s>;
by mere remembrance they indeed remove the sin of embodied beings.
When the king asked, 'How was a Brahmin born in the family of King <s>Kuśika</s>,
and a king in the line of <s>Bhṛgu</s>?', the one of divine vows replied:
'Long ago <s>Cyavana</s>, knower of future events and treasury of splendor,
was honored and stayed in the palace of King <s>Kuśika</s>.
When the king, together with his wife, had undertaken the vow of serving him,
the sage ate and then slept motionless for three periods of seven nights.
The king, fasting and accompanied by his wife,
quietly massaged his feet, anxious with fear of breaking his sleep.

children.text: tato muniḥ samutthāya maunī gatvā manojavaḥ
children.translated_text: Then the sage rose, silent, and went away with the speed of thought,
and disappeared on the road while the king and his wife followed him.
When he had vanished, the king, fasting and greatly faint,
fell down; then, after recovering for a moment, he entered his own house again.
The two spouses again saw him mute, still like a piece of wood;
while he slept on one side for twenty-one nights,
the two of them remained fasting, again massaging his feet.
Then, when he had awakened, with oil prepared through a hundred pourings, by the king...
When his bath had been carried out with devotion, the sage took his seat upon the throne.

children.text: tato nānāvidhaṃ bhojyaṃ rājayogyaṃ svayaṃ kṛtam
children.translated_text: Then the various kinds of food, fit for a king and prepared by himself,
which had been offered by the king together with his wife, the descendant of <s>Bhṛgu</s> burned up.
Again becoming invisible, and again making himself present before him,
the sage was amazed when he saw that king, together with his wife, unchanged.
Seeing the king, with his wife beside him, unaltered and without food,
he ordered him, 'Carry me in a war-chariot.'

children.text: ityuktvā dampatī dhṛtvā tau rathe vicacāra saḥ
children.translated_text: Having spoken thus, he yoked the couple and moved about in the chariot,
while they were sprinkled with blood produced by the blows of a three-spiked scourge.
