Then the sage, repeatedly bewildering them, showed them heaven,
beautiful with wondrous golden creepers and with the <s>Nandana</s> garden.
Through manifold, fleeting displays of illusion, seen and then lost,

children.text: muninā vihitairmohaṃ dampatī tau na jagmatuḥ ||
children.translated_text: fashioned by the sage, that couple did not fall into delusion.
Trembling, without food, and worn down by the fatigue of a long road,
they were released from the chariot after a long time by the excellent sage, who was pleased, and he said to them:
'I am pleased with the devotion of you two. Now accept a boon.
Your grandson, O king, will be a brahmin, a man of great austerity.
This hostility of the <s>Bhārgavas</s> has arisen with his descendants;
therefore I have afflicted you with the intention of cutting off the kṣatriyas.
By my word, O lord of the earth, be free from weariness, restored,
and blessed, together with your wife, as if filled with nectar.'
When he had spoken thus and disappeared, in the course of time, for that king,
there was born in his line the glorious <s>Viśvāmitra</s>, a treasury of austerity.
And how <s>Rāma</s> the <s>Bhārgava</s> was born and brought about the destruction of the kṣatriyas
through the power of <s>Ṛcīka</s>, that I have told before.
Hearing this, the ruler, fearing the sin of destroying the earth's kings,
asked again, and <s>Bhīṣma</s> told him the highest fruit of gifts.
Everything desired is obtained by austerity, by good conduct and self-restraint,
and by compassion, truth, and giving.
By giving a tawny cow, adorned and supplied with a bronze milking vessel,
a man obtains a reward equal to the gift of the earth.
A man who gives a sesame-cow goes to the world of the <s>Vasus</s>,
and one who gives a maiden and land reaches <s>Śakra</s>'s world and rejoices.
The gift of freedom from fear to living beings is remembered as the best of gifts,
and the gift of what one personally cherishes grants the fruit of all desires.
By the gift of gold, it is said, men's sin is destroyed.

children.text: sarvaṃ sūte vasumatī dhatte ca nikhilaṃ jagat
children.translated_text: The earth produces everything and supports the entire world;
therefore the giver of land should be known as giving everything, the best among donors.
Food is the life-breath of embodied beings; therefore the giver of food gives life.
<s>Nārada</s> said that in the world there is no gift equal to the gift of food.
They declare the gift of water to be nectar for living creatures,
for in the next world the lands are without shade and blazing with heat.
They praise the gift of sesame for the destruction of all sins.
Long ago, pleased, <s>Yama</s> urged a brahmin, 'Give sesame.'
Having given away all one's property except a brahmin's property, one crosses difficulties;
for the thorn of a brahmin's property is said to be a sharp fall for men.
Long ago in <s>Dvāravatī</s>, in a great well covered with shrubs and grass,
all the <s>Vṛṣṇis</s> saw a huge lizard.
When they were unable to lift him out and questioned him, he said softly,
'I am <s>Nṛga</s>, a king, brought to this condition by a brahmin's curse.
Long ago, after giving countless cows to brahmin householders,
and after giving crores of gold, I reached supreme bliss.
Then one day another brahmin saw, in a brahmin's house, a cow I had given,
and, thinking it was his own cow stolen by a thief, he seized it.

children.text: rājñā mameyaṃ prāgdattā hṛteyaṃ dasyunā paraḥ
children.translated_text: 'This was given to me earlier by the king; this was taken away by another robber.'
Disputing in this way, the two came to my assembly.
When I heard that affair, I repeatedly made requests to both of them,
earnestly and separately, with wealth, cows, servants, and horses.
Even so, one would not give up the cow, because he was guarding what he had received as a gift,
and the second, anxious with affection and fear, would not give up the cow born in his house.
Then, in time, I went to the abode of <s>Dharmarāja</s>,
and I heard of divine worlds, won for myself by many gifts.
But because of the misplacement of a brahmin's property,
<s>Yama</s> himself assigned me this lizard-state until the sight of <s>Śauri</s>.
As he was speaking thus, his sin was destroyed by <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>'s sight,

children.text: nṛgo jagāma tridivaṃ tyaktvā tāṃ kṛkalāsatām ||
children.translated_text: and <s>Nṛga</s> went to heaven, abandoning that lizard-state.
The great sage named <s>Nāsiketā</s>, son of the brahmarṣi <s>Uddālaka</s>,
gave up his breaths through his father's anger, struck down by his glance.

children.text: putraṃ nipatitaṃ dṛṣṭvā śāntakrodho muniḥ śanaiḥ
children.translated_text: Seeing his son fallen, the sage's anger grew calm, and slowly,
that treasury of mantras restored him to life out of compassion, with tearful eyes.

children.text: tataḥ svapnotthita iva prāptajīvo muneḥ sutaḥ
children.translated_text: Then the sage's son, alive again as if risen from sleep,
was questioned by his father and told everything he had seen in <s>Yama</s>'s dwelling.
In the hall of the king of the ancestors, splendid with hundreds of jewel pillars,
I received abundant honor, water for my feet, an arghya offering, and a seat.
There, in aerial cars shining with the brilliance of the sun and moon,
I saw meritorious men, radiant with bright ornaments and smiling.
Rivers of ghee, milk, nectar, and water were seen there by me,
with jewel-birds calling at the tops of bowers made of heaps of golden lotuses.
After I had seen celestial enjoyments, I asked <s>Vaivasvata</s> in wonder:
'For whom are these streams that carry nectar, to be possessed at will?'
<s>Yama</s> said, 'These rivers of milk and ghee belong to those who have given cows.
A man does not enjoy the supreme nectar without giving a cow.
If cows are unavailable, then, with water and sesame,
or with ghee, one should fashion a cow and give it with the intention of nectar.
In the world there is no other gift equal to <s>godāna</s> (the gift of a cow).
Thus the lord of the ancestors told me reverently, again and again.'
When <s>Nāsiketa</s> had spoken so, the sage, surrounded by hundreds of sages,
praised again and again the great merit of giving cows.
Surpassing all worlds, the world of cows shines forth;
where, truly, the splendors and joys of heaven make hell seem like nothing.
Those who give cows, bright with good deeds, go to <s>Goloka</s>.
So, when once questioned by <s>Śakra</s>, <s>Kamalāsana</s> said.
Foremost sages such as <s>Vasiṣṭha</s>, kings such as <s>Daśaratha</s>,
and the gods headed by <s>Śakra</s> declare nothing equal to cows.

children.text: nivāsārthaṃ purā gāvaḥ prārthitā bahuśaḥ śriyā
children.translated_text: Long ago, for a dwelling-place, the cows were repeatedly entreated by <s>Śrī</s>,
but, saying, 'You are fickle,' they did not grant her shelter.
Then <s>Lakṣmī</s> said, 'Rejected disrespectfully by you,

children.text: tyaktā nindyā bhaviṣyāmi tasmādyāce punaḥ punaḥ ||
children.translated_text: I shall become blameworthy; therefore I ask again and again.'
Then the cows, with disdain, assigned <s>Śrī</s> a place in cow-dung;

children.text: tasmādetāḥ paraṃ puṇyaṃ pavitraṃ nāstyataḥ param ||
children.translated_text: therefore these are supremely meritorious, and nothing is purer than that.
In the same way, the gift of gold burns away all sins of embodied beings,

children.text: tejo hi paramaṃ putra kāñcanaṃ jātavedasaḥ ||
children.translated_text: for gold, my son, is the supreme brilliance of <s>Jātavedas</s>.
Long ago, on the bank of the <s>Jāhnavī</s>, while offering <s>piṇḍa</s> at my father's <s>śrāddha</s>,
I saw the hand of <s>Śantanu</s> rise up, adorned with a jeweled bracelet.

children.text: piṇḍo mayā kuśeṣveva taṃ vilokya samarpitaḥ
children.translated_text: Seeing it, I placed the <s>piṇḍa</s> only upon the kuśa grass.

children.text: tuṣṭastadā me janakaḥ svapne provāca māmidam ||
children.translated_text: Then my father, pleased, spoke this to me in a dream:
'My son, by following the śāstra you have made me blessed as a son.

children.text: kanakaṃ dehi viprebhyo dānānāmuttamaṃ hi tat ||
children.translated_text: Give gold to Brahmins, for that is the best of gifts.

children.text: jāmadagnyaḥ purā rāmaḥ kṛtvā niḥkṣatriyaṃ jagat
children.translated_text: Long ago <s>Jāmadagnya Rāma</s>, after making the world devoid of Kṣatriyas,
was made by the sages to give gold; therefore he was freed from sin.
Long ago the gods, oppressed by <s>Tāraka</s>, entreated the moon-crested lord,
knowing the future story of <s>Skanda</s>'s birth.
Then the god, because of the interruption of his lovemaking, placed the energy of <s>Gaurīpati</s>
in the mouth of <s>Jātavedas</s>, and released that supreme splendor.
The splendid embryo was held by Fire for ten thousand years;

children.text: gaṅgāyāṃ nihitaḥ sāpi nidadhe taṃ girestaṭe ||
children.translated_text: placed in the <s>Gaṅgā</s>, she too deposited it on a mountain slope.
That blessed <s>Kārtikeya</s> was born as an infant in the reed thicket;
powerful for the gods, he became their general and the slayer of <s>Tāraka</s>.
That which first arose from <s>Jātavedas</s> at his birth,
by which the earth became rich in wealth, is called gold.
Then, asked by the king about the rule for <s>śrāddha</s>, the son of <s>Śantanu</s> said:
One should understand <s>śrāddha</s> as the gift of sesame, soaked in honey and ghee.
With black gram, fish, sheep, hare, goat, boar, and birds,
and also with the fresh meats of spotted deer, antelope, gayal, and buffalo,
in increasing order, month by month, up to a year,
those learned in sacred tradition say that the ancestors are satisfied at <s>śrāddhas</s>.
With the meat of the vādhrīṇasa they declare satisfaction for twelve years,
and with rhinoceros meat, tortoises, and kāla greens, satisfaction without end.

children.text: na teṣāṃ pitaraḥ śocyāstrayodaśyāṃ maghāsu ca
children.translated_text: Their ancestors need not be lamented for when <s>śrāddha</s> is performed on the thirteenth day, under the Maghās,

children.text: varṣāsu vihitaṃ śrāddhaṃ pāyase na sasarpiṣā ||
children.translated_text: and in the rainy season, with rice pudding together with ghee.
At the well of <s>Gayā</s>, under the banyan tree, or in the shade of an elephant,
and on holy days, they reckon <s>śrāddha</s> as endless.
For desired ends, one should prescribe <s>śrāddha</s> at the conjunctions of lunar days and nakṣatras.
A Brahmin of good conduct, whose body is without fault, deserves the <s>śrāddha</s>.
By the <s>Vaiśvadeva</s> rite and by a properly consecrated fire,
the <s>śrāddha</s> is protected by Brahmins, preceded by worship of <s>Viṣṇu</s>.
At a <s>śrāddha</s>, the three kinds of salt mixed with molasses are always forbidden,
as are cumin, asafoetida, sauviraka, onions, and garlic.
Asked by the lord of the earth about the distinction between givers and receivers,
the son of the heavenly river meditated and then spoke again:
Long ago, in a time ruined by drought, when the trees were burned up,
<s>Arundhatī</s>'s companions, the peaceful <s>Saptarṣis</s>, wandered on the earth.

children.text: dāsaḥ paśusakho nāma dāsī caṇḍā ca tadvadhūḥ
children.translated_text: A servant named <s>Paśusakha</s>, and his servant-wife <s>Caṇḍā</s>,
followed those very sages, tormented by hunger and thirst.

children.text: rājye surājñaḥ śaibyasya gatāsuṃ tanayaṃ tataḥ
children.translated_text: Then, in the kingdom of <s>Surājña Śaibya</s>, the sages, overcome by hunger,
set about cooking his dead son in a pot.
Then King <s>Vṛṣādarbhī</s>, comparable to <s>Vaiśravaṇa</s>, seeing
the sages agitated and sorrowful, spoke to them with folded hands:

children.text: yathecchaṃ gṛhyatāṃ mattaḥ sarvaṃ vā vividhaṃ vasu
children.translated_text: 'Take from me whatever you wish, every kind of various wealth.
Let this livelihood, which gives rise to disgust, be abandoned by you.'
When the king had spoken so, the bulls among sages replied:
'O king, a gift accepted from a king is terrible and destroys ascetic power.
For Brahmins like trees, once burned by the fire of accepting gifts,
and left only with sin and ignorance, how can there again be the fruit of merit?'

children.text: etaduktvā parityajya sthālīṃ te kānanaṃ yayuḥ
children.translated_text: Having said this, they abandoned the pot and went to the forest,
turning away from accepting gifts even at the price of the suffering of their lives.
Then in the forest <s>Vṛṣādarbhi</s> had his ministers make udumbara fruits
filled with gold, and threw them before those sages.
But the lordly sages, frightened, abandoned even those as if they were blazing
and went away, praising among themselves the holy disposition of contentment.
In anger at that, <s>Vṛṣādarbhi</s> at once offered an oblation into the fire
and, producing a fearsome <s>kṛtyā</s> (destructive rite-being), ordered her to destroy the sages.
Meanwhile those sages, wandering happily in the forest,
saw a stout wandering ascetic, <s>Śunaḥsakha</s>, companioned by a dog.
Seeing him, when <s>Arundhatī</s> asked about the cause of his plumpness,
the best of sages said, 'He is not occupied with rites, as we are.

children.text: agnihotraṃ na vedāśca śāstrakanthā na duḥsahā
children.translated_text: He has no agnihotra, no Vedas, no unbearable load of treatises,
no effort over all sorts of firewood, no wife, and no beggars.
This stout body of <s>Śunaḥsakha</s>, who goes about as he pleases
and dwells in happiness, grows because he is free from anxiety.'
After saying this, the sages, having become friendly with him in the forest,
saw a lotus pond rich with blooming lotuses and blue lotuses.
The fierce <s>yātudhānī</s> sent by <s>Vṛṣādarbhi</s>
said there to them as they sought lotus stalks, 'I am guarding this lotus pond.
State your own names, and then take the lotus fibers.
For those whose names are not known, there is no passage here in my presence.'
Hearing this, the sages, beginning with <s>Atri</s>, in order
declared their names to her with various hidden etymological explanations.
When she heard their names, whose letters and words were made puzzling by etymology,
the <s>kṛtyā</s>, left without an answer, did not obstruct them from taking the stalks.

children.text: śunaḥsakhoditaṃ nāma punaḥ papraccha sā yadā
children.translated_text: But when she again asked the name spoken by <s>Śunaḥsakha</s>,

children.text: tadā kruddhāstu daṇḍena vidadhustāṃ ca bhasmasāt ||
children.translated_text: then, angered, they reduced her to ashes with a staff.
Then the sages pulled up lotus fibers white as moonbeams,
set them on the bank, bathed, and performed the water rite.
Afterwards, rising up, exhausted and eager to eat the lotus stalks,
they did not see those stalks that had been placed on the bank of the pond.
Suspicious of one another, they made oaths in order,
for a sudden loss of what is desired is hard to bear even for great men.
'Let the one by whom our meal of lotus stalks was stolen be a vain cook, vain in conduct,
a false witness, a doer of forbidden acts, cruel, lustful, a thief, and devoid of the Veda.
Let him touch a cow and fire with his foot, and spit phlegm into water.
Let him approach another's wife, be a poisoner, a seller of soma,
and a slanderer, by whom our food of lotus stalks was taken.'
When the sages had spoken thus, <s>Śunaḥsakha</s> then said to them,
'May the one by whom our lotus stalks were taken elsewhere give a maiden

children.text: deyātsa kanyakāṃ yena hatānyatra bisāni naḥ
children.translated_text: to a sacrificer, a repository of the metres, pure, and celibate.'
Hearing this, the sages said, 'You have spoken what is desirable.
Surely it was you who took all our food of lotus stalks.'
As they were speaking in this way, <s>Śunaḥsakha</s> laughed and said,
'The theft of your lotus stalks here was indeed done by me, for your welfare.

children.text: sā ca kṛtyā hatā ghoro devo 'haṃ tridaśeśvaraḥ ||
children.translated_text: And that terrible <s>kṛtyā</s> has been slain; I am the god, the lord of the thirty gods.'
Having said this, the lord of heaven assumed his own form,
and with the seven seers went to heaven, adorned with rows of moving aerial cars.
Thus the conduct of those bright-minded men, who had turned away from accepting gifts
and were rich in contentment, shines with the ornament of freedom from greed.
Long ago the sages headed by <s>Kaśyapa</s> and kings such as <s>Nahuṣa</s>
set out for the sacred fords, placing <s>Śatakratu</s> before them.
Having bathed at holy tīrthas, they went to the <s>Puṣkarāhariṇī</s>,
and there the sage <s>Agastya</s> did not see his own lotus, which he had set down.
Then they in order made oaths concerning the grave sin,

children.text: indrastu prāha dhanyo 'stu sa hṛtaṃ yena puṣkaram ||
children.translated_text: but <s>Indra</s> said, 'Blessed is the one by whom the lotus was taken.'
When the king asked <s>Bhīṣma</s> about the gift of umbrellas and sandals,
he said, 'Here it is supreme merit, and hereafter it is regarded as protection.
Long ago <s>Jamadagni</s>, bow in hand, intent on target practice in the forest,
sent forth a row of arrows like the sun a garland of rays.
At her husband's command, fair-faced <s>Reṇukā</s> repeatedly
brought back the arrows released by him.
At midday he saw his wife fainted from the fatigue and torment

children.text: sa jāyāṃ vīkṣya madhyāhne kruddhaḥ sūryamudaikṣata ||
children.translated_text: caused by the fierce rays' spreading heat, and in anger he looked at the sun.
Then, as he was preparing to strike him in the sky with a formidable divine weapon,
the Sun came in fear with folded hands and appeased him.
When his anger had passed, the lord of day, to please him,
gave him an umbrella to ward off heat and a pair of sandals.
That gift of umbrellas and sandals is remembered as the highest among gifts,
since it calms the suffering of men in this world and the next.
The gift of ponds and wells is also meritorious and brings comfort to embodied beings,
for in the next world, scorched like a desert, water is said to be hard to obtain.
In the terrible, shoreless darkness of the next world, where there is no support,
light is hard to find; therefore a man should always give a lamp.
One who gives flowers, offerings, and incense satisfies all the worlds;
so <s>Śukra</s> once told the lord of the <s>Asuras</s> in another tale.
By giving flowers and incense, <s>Nahuṣa</s> became irresistible in heaven,
and, with his command unbroken, obtained the seat of <s>Ākhaṇḍala</s>.
But when, arrogant, he touched the best of sages with his foot, saying, 'Move on!',
then, after approaching <s>Agastya</s> in pride, he was cast down by <s>Bhṛgu</s>.
When he had the dreadful form of a great python, caused by the grasp of <s>Bhīma</s>'s arms,

children.text: araṇye bhavatā yasya śāpamokṣaḥ purā kṛtaḥ ||
children.translated_text: you once brought about his release from the curse in the forest.
Again asked by the king about the fate of those who steal a brahmin's property,
the son of <s>Śantanu</s> said, "O king, a brahmin's property is a dangerous poison indeed.
Long ago a certain prince, remembering his former birth and full of curiosity,
asked a caṇḍāla the cause of his low birth, and he too replied:
"Listen to the cause by which I reached the state of a caṇḍāla.
Long ago a brahmin's cows were stolen by powerful bandits.
Some of their dust fell on a sacrificial ground, into the soma itself,
and, having drunk that, the brahmins went to hell together with the consecrated sacrificer.
That dust fell into the alms-bowl of a brahmacārin,

children.text: tadreṇu tatsthitaṃ cānnaṃ mohānme bhakṣyatāṃ yayau ||
children.translated_text: and through delusion I came to eat that dust and the food that was there.
I was a learned brahmin, a brahmacārin with conquered senses;
by that act I have reached this condition. See the weight of a brahmin's property.
Having spoken thus, at the kṣatriya's word, for the sake of a brahmin, in the fire of battle,

children.text: hutvā śarīraṃ caṇḍālaḥ prāpa puṇyaṃ punargatim ||
children.translated_text: the caṇḍāla offered up his body and obtained a meritorious rebirth."
Asked by the king about the various destinies of those who do merit,
<s>Bhīṣma</s> said, "Because of the variety of karma, those are the worlds of embodied beings.
Long ago, in <s>Gautama</s>'s hermitage, a young elephant was raised
on the milk left from the oblation and on shoots of wild rice.
Then, in time, with bees clinging to his cheeks dark with rutting-fluid,
playful and languid, he became like a mountain.
Eating fuel-sticks, darbha grass, and fruit, guarding the hermitage of the deathless sage,

children.text: muneḥ putra iva prītyā sa babhūva mahāgajaḥ ||
children.translated_text: that great elephant became, in affection, like the sage's own son.

children.text: taṃ pravṛddhaṃ tathā nāgaṃ svayametya śatakratuḥ
children.translated_text: Then <s>Śatakratu</s> himself came and took away that grown elephant,
assuming the form of king <s>Dhṛtarāṣṭra</s>.

children.text: punaḥ punaryācyamāno muninā sa yadā nṛpaḥ
children.translated_text: When the king, though repeatedly entreated by the sage,

children.text: na tatyāja gajaṃ darpāttadā taṃ gautamo 'vadat ||
children.translated_text: did not give up the elephant because of pride, then <s>Gautama</s> said to him:
"When men, subjected to time, go there at the body's end,

children.text: nandanti śocantyathavā tatra dāsyasi me gajam ||
children.translated_text: where they rejoice or grieve, there you will give me my elephant.
Where sinful men are cut apart by those scowling servants
commanded by <s>Vaivasvata</s>, there you will give me my elephant.
Where the timid and the brave are equal, and likewise the weak and the strong,

children.text: yatra mugdhā vidagdhāśca tatra dāsyati me gajam ||
children.translated_text: where the simple and the clever are alike, there you will give me my elephant.

children.text: dhanadasya pure ramye merau vā nandane vane
children.translated_text: In the lovely city of the lord of wealth, or on <s>Meru</s>, or in <s>Nandana</s> grove,
or in the abode of the cool-rayed moon or of the thousand-rayed sun,
or in the world of <s>Varuṇa</s>, of the lord of the gods, of the <s>Surabhīs</s>, or of <s>Svayaṃbhu</s>,

children.text: loke vā dāsyasi gajaṃ na tatra balavānasi ||
children.translated_text: there too you will give the elephant; you will not be powerful there."
Hearing this, the king said, "Atheists go to hell;
men of mixed deeds go to the mansion of <s>Yama</s>.
Those devoted to vows and honoring guests go to the city of the lord of wealth;
sacrificers go to <s>Nandana</s>, and givers go to the orb of the soma.
Those devoted to Vedic recitation go to the world of the sun, and the disciplined servants of sacred fords,
those who are tranquil, go beyond saṃsāra to the supreme abode of <s>Svayaṃbhu</s>.

children.text: nāhaṃ kvacidgamiṣyāmi kva nu dāsyāmi te gajam ||
children.translated_text: I shall not go anywhere at all; where, then, shall I give you the elephant?"

children.text: ityuktvā kuñjaraṃ tasmai dattvā divyāṃ tathā gatim
children.translated_text: Having spoken thus, he gave him the elephant and also divine passage;

children.text: svaṃ vapurdarśayitvā ca hasannindro yayau divam ||
children.translated_text: then, showing his own form, <s>Indra</s> went laughing to heaven.
Long ago king <s>Bhagīratha</s>, still in his body, went to the world of <s>Brahmā</s>,
for he had given earth, cows, bulls, maidens, villages, and towns.
Men of good conduct, truthful, obedient to their elders,
devoted to honoring gurus and patient, become hundred-year-lived here.
The observances of those who practice fasting vows, according to lunar days, constellations, and conjunctions,
bestow divine fruits; so <s>Aṅgiras</s> declared long ago.
When the son of <s>Dharma</s> had heard this and was preparing again to ask, "Tell me the body's fate,"
then <s>Bṛhaspati</s> himself arrived.
Honored by the best of sages, by <s>Bhīṣma</s> and by <s>Vidura</s>,
and by <s>Dhṛtarāṣṭra</s> and <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, he occupied a seat bright with jewels.
<s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s>, having worshiped him and being directed by <s>Bhīṣma</s>'s instruction,
asked about conduct, saṃsāra, and the death of the body and of the embodied self.
Then the guru of the gods said, "The body is made of the five elements;
after abandoning it when it has gone fivefold, a man acts as if in a dream.
At the breaking of the body, the embodied self goes to a lightless, friendless place,
and, pierced by its latent impressions, knows each good and bad result.
Leaving the corpse behind like a snake its slough,
the creature, joined with dharma and adharma, goes like wind carrying fragrance.
After experiencing those several results, bodiless and resting on the eightfold subtle body produced by karma,
it comes into conjunction with the elements again, fallen once more through the channel of semen.
There it is again smeared by its variegated deeds, like something daubed with honey;
smeared, it wanders wheel-like among crores of animal wombs.

children.text: dattvā ca vipulaṃ dānaṃ modate puṇyavānsukhī
children.translated_text: Having given abundant gifts, the meritorious and happy man rejoices;
by nonviolence he goes to heaven, while through craving he undergoes hardship.
A fallen brahmin, after taking what is not his, becomes a donkey for a long time;

children.text: sūkaraḥ kṛkavākuśca jambukaḥ śvā sa jāyate ||
children.translated_text: he is born as a boar, a cock, a jackal, and a dog.

children.text: gurornikāraṃ kṛtvā ca bhavati śvā tato vṛkaḥ
children.translated_text: Having insulted his guru, he becomes a dog and then a wolf;
then, released from the whirl of hell, he becomes a dreadful donkey.
One who has harmed his parents becomes, in turn, a dog, a tortoise, and a porcupine,
then a snake and a slave, until the exhaustion of his karma.
One who hates her husband, having become a monkey, is then born as a mouse and also as a dog.
The taker of a deposit, after slowly wandering through hundreds of wombs for suffering,
is born as a contemptible worm in a mire thick with whirling filth.
One devoted to slandering others becomes a śārṅga bird; a betrayer of trust becomes a fish.
The evildoer becomes, in order, a deer, a goat, and then an insect.
A thief of crops becomes a mouse, a boar, and likewise a dog.
An adulterer enters various kinds of flesh-eating births.
A śūdra who goes to a brahmin's wife is born as a worm and a mouse.
An ungrateful man, struck violently by the servants of Time in the hells,
then becomes a worm and perishes within hundreds of wombs.
A man who kills an embryo becomes a worm twenty-one times.
A stealer of food becomes a fly, and a stealer of barley-food becomes a mouse.

children.text: cīrī ca lalanasteno dadhihartā tathā bakaḥ
children.translated_text: A stealer of a woman becomes a cīrī bird, and a stealer of curds likewise becomes a heron.
A stealer of color becomes a peacock, and a stealer of red cloth becomes a jīvajīvaka bird.
From stealing oil one becomes a pippala creature; from stealing fruit one becomes an ant.
From stealing sweet food one becomes a dhūka bird, and from stealing clothes a pigeon.
A stealer of fragrance becomes a musk-rat, and a concealer of the truth becomes a fish.
Thus, through those many and various evil deeds, with their strange ripenings,

children.text: tāṃ tāṃ tamomayīṃ yoniṃ saṃsaranti śarīriṇaḥ ||
children.translated_text: embodied beings pass through one after another womb made of darkness.
Such sins of men, without acts of expiation,

children.text: dānena kila śāmyanti dānaṃ hi paramā gatiḥ ||
children.translated_text: are said to be calmed by giving; for giving is the supreme goal.
Food alone is the highest life-breath of beings, the arising of nectar.
Therefore the gift of food is great, for in it the worthiness of the recipient is not reckoned.
The giver of food, showering nectar, is always born wealthy.
Prosperous, he gives food again, by the very inclination formed from former merit.
He again obtains sovereignty in this very play of the turning wheel.
In this revolving time, a meritorious man does not decline.
Having spoken thus, the blessed lord himself, worshiped by the great seers,
ascended to heaven, his orb of directions colored by radiance.
Asked about <s>dharma</s> marked by non-injury, which grants fearlessness to all beings,
<s>Śāntanava</s> again spoke to <s>Ajātaśatru</s>.
For men, abstention from eating meat is equal to hundreds of horse sacrifices.
For meat is born from the terrible sin of killing, and from nowhere else.
Meat arises only from flesh, and man is made of flesh.
In this <s>saṃsāra</s> of equal pain, how is one not ashamed while eating it?
Even when touched by a thorn, they undergo some strange alteration;
yet they eat the body of an animal cut apart by weapons.
At the destruction of the body, embodied beings feel intense fear and trembling.

children.text: dṛṣṭvā ko nāma māṃsebhyaḥ spṛhāṃ kuryādarākṣasaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Seeing this, who, unless he were a rākṣasa, would feel desire for meat?
One who does not eat meat is a friend of the world, granting fearlessness to living beings.
An ocean of merit and compassion, he goes to the fearless abode.
Non-injury is a sacrifice whose requisites are unobstructed, a sacred ford free from the fatigue of travel,
the highest vow, one that does not require giving up food.
Life-breaths are most dear to men; those by whom they are offered in the fire of battle,
tell me their fate, said the king; asked thus, <s>Bhīṣma</s> spoke again.
So it is: life-breaths are dear even to suffering embodied beings.
Who can suddenly give them up, except one possessed of courage?
When life is slipping away in every way, the timid, overcome by fear,
close their eyes fearfully even when only a blade of grass touches them.
Long ago, on the road, an insect fled in terror from a cart.
Seeing it, <s>Vyāsa</s>, whose eye was knowledge, smiled and asked:

children.text: asmin api śarīre te rakṣārthaṃ ko 'yamāgrahaḥ
children.translated_text: Even in this body of yours, what is this insistence on protecting it?
I think all this is only death for you, whose life is contemptible.
Hearing this speech of the sage, the insect replied to him:
There is nothing so dear to embodied beings as the body, lord.
Bound by love for my female insect, with my tiny insect daughters,
I have happiness in my house inside a hole, like <s>Śakra</s> in heaven.
The life-breaths are the abode of affection; who is able to give them up by himself?
They cannot be obtained even for a moment, not even with hundreds of <s>Meru</s> mountains.
I was a śūdra, and through many sins I have come to this insect womb;

children.text: pitroḥ śuśrūṣayā kiṃtu mune jātiṃ smarāmyaham ||
children.translated_text: yet by serving my parents, sage, I remember my former birth.
Hearing that, the blessed lord, ocean of compassion and creator of beings,

children.text: tasmai nṛpapadaṃ vyāso dadau janmāntare kramāt ||
children.translated_text: <s>Vyāsa</s> granted him, step by step in another birth, the rank of a king.

children.text: vipro 'tha tadgirā bhūtvā sa yayau paramāṃ gatim
children.translated_text: Then, becoming a brahmin through his word, he went to the supreme goal.
In calamities, the sight of great souls is a wish-fulfilling tree.
Therefore those by whom life-breaths, though exceedingly dear, were given up face to face in battle,
oceans of courage, rival the lord of the gods in the third heaven.
What is superior: knowledge, austerity, or giving?
Asked this by the king, <s>Jāhnavīsuta</s> spoke.
Long ago in <s>Vārāṇasī</s>, <s>Vyāsa</s> was invited by <s>Maitreya</s>.

children.text: bhuktvā prahṛṣṭaḥ provāca kathānte tapasāṃ nidhiḥ ||
children.translated_text: After eating, delighted, that treasury of austerities spoke at the end of the conversation:

children.text: tejaḥ paraṃ tapo nāma divyameva balaṃ tapaḥ
children.translated_text: Austerity is supreme radiance; austerity is indeed divine strength.

children.text: paśyanti santastapasā jñānaṃ hi tapasaḥ phalam ||
children.translated_text: The good see by austerity, for knowledge is the fruit of austerity.
In this existence, scorched by great delusion, when the three worlds are pervaded by it,
knowledge alone is the supreme eye, an unimpaired cause of insight for the world.
But, surpassing all this, giving alone is superior.

children.text: dānātparaṃ na saṃsāre dehināṃ śarma vidyate ||
children.translated_text: There is no happiness in <s>saṃsāra</s> for embodied beings higher than giving.
Through gifts of food, the meritorious have gone to the supreme state.
for the virtuous one, as the sage attained it with effortless ease.
Food is oblation, nectar, and life; the giver of it is a giver of life.
Having said this and taken leave of the sage, the best of sages departed.
Then, when the king asked the grandsire about the good conduct of women,
he said, 'For women, good conduct is always the vow of a faithful wife.'
Long ago <s>Kaikeyī</s>, named <s>Sumanā</s>,
asked <s>Śāṇḍilī</s>, who dwelt in the world of the gods and surpassed the immortals with her mass of blazing splendor:

children.text: subhage kena tapasā dānena caritena vā
children.translated_text: 'Blessed lady, by what austerity, gift, or conduct
do you shine in this heavenly aerial car like the embodied radiance of the sun?'
Asked this out of curiosity by her, <s>Śāṇḍilī</s> said:

children.text: nāhaṃ vratairna saṃnyāsairna dānena divaṃ śritā ||
children.translated_text: 'I did not reach heaven by vows, by renunciations, or by gifts.
My husband was always worshiped by me with devotion, like a deity.

children.text: na hi santaḥ praśaṃsanti tapaḥ strīṇāmataḥ param ||
children.translated_text: For the good do not praise any austerity higher than this for women.
In a courtyard, at the doorway, or in the palace, I was not one who gazed at the royal road,
nor, when my husband was abroad, was I without my vow.
Following my husband like a shadow, fearful when he was angry and seeking his welfare,
I became a faithful wife in mind, speech, and deed, and so reached heaven.'
Having said this, <s>Śāṇḍilī</s> departed; thereafter to lofty <s>Niṣadha</s>
there is no higher refuge for women than that vow of a faithful wife.

children.text: adhikaṃ prīyate kiṃ svit sāmnā dānena vā janaḥ
children.translated_text: 'By which is a person more pleased, by conciliation or by giving?'
Asked this by <s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s>, <s>Devavrata</s> again replied:

children.text: purā vane dvijaḥ kaścidgṛhīto rakṣasā balāt
children.translated_text: Long ago in a forest a certain twice-born man was seized by force by a rākṣasa.
Because he had no other means at all, he considered release through conciliatory speech.
The night-rover, ready to kill him and intending to deceive him, said:
'I am pale and weak. Tell me, why is this so?'
The Brahmin said to him, 'Surely your friends have gone far away from you,
and prosperity has been obtained by you without allies; therefore you are pale.
Or perhaps, though you honor your own people with effort,

children.text: viraktaḥ svajano yāsi tena vā pariśuṣyasi ||
children.translated_text: they are plainly estranged without cause; therefore you waste away.
Or plainly you see others, inferior to you in qualities, honored,
blessed with power and pride; therefore you are weak.

children.text: vyaktaṃ tyāgī daridro 'si guṇairnūnaṃ na pūjyase
children.translated_text: Clearly you are generous and poor, and surely you are not honored for your virtues.

children.text: prājñasya te na śṛṇvanti sādhurvā vañcyase khalaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: Or people do not listen to you though you are wise, or, being good, you are deceived by rogues.

children.text: mūrkho vā śāstrarasiko mānī hīnakulo 'si vā
children.translated_text: Or you are a fool fond of śāstra, proud, or of low family.

children.text: duḥkhaṃ svapiṣi manye 'haṃ cintayā hariṇaḥ kṛśaḥ ||
children.translated_text: I think you sleep unhappily; thin from worry, you are yellow-pale.'
Hearing these words of the Brahmin, which grasped his inner state, the night-rover

children.text: prītastatyāja taṃ sāmnā ko hi sāntvairna tuṣyati ||
children.translated_text: was pleased and let him go through conciliation; who is not satisfied by soothing words?
Then, asked by the king about the power of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, the son of <s>Śantanu</s> said:
Long ago sages came to see <s>Śauri</s>, who was engaged in austerity.
Then there they saw a great forest burned by fire issuing from the mouth of <s>Viṣṇu</s>,
and afterward restored by that very one with a glance.
Seeing that, they understood from <s>Nārada</s>'s mouth the supreme divine reality,
and, by his speech, the abode of <s>Viṣṇu</s>, whose mountain peaks had been scorched.
Then <s>Nārada</s>, skilled in telling many kinds of stories, was asked by the foe of <s>Kaiṭabha</s>
and, at the end of the tale, related what suited the occasion.

children.text: purā himagirau gaurī dhūrjaṭeḥ kila līlayā
children.translated_text: Long ago on <s>Himagiri</s>, <s>Gaurī</s>, in play, it is said,
covered <s>Dhūrjaṭi</s>'s eyes with her hands, and by that he became three-eyed.
By the fire born from his third eye that mountain became
one whose sky was encircled by flames from the burning masses of śāla trees and creepers.
Then, at <s>Gaurī</s>'s word, the moon-crested one by his glance
again made the mountain, <s>Gaurī</s>'s father, bright with smiling flowers, creepers, and trees.
There, eager with affection, the Blessed Lord was asked many kinds of stories
by the goddess, and at the end of the tale he stated the determination of dharma and artha:
the good conduct of those engaged in worldly action, born of the divisions of varṇa and āśrama,
and, for those who have withdrawn, the fruit born of action without attachment, namely nirvāṇa.
Then the goddess, asked by the moon-crested one about doe-eyed women,
described the meritorious conduct whose deity is the worship of a husband.
Then <s>Nīlakaṇṭha</s>, asked by all the lordly sages, said
that <s>Viṣṇu</s> is the supreme cause in the arising and dissolution of beings.
'<s>Hari</s>, the son of <s>Vasudeva</s>, will be born on earth,
descended as a partial incarnation and intent on destroying the enemies of the gods.

children.text: sa sūryaḥ sa ca śītāṃśuḥ so 'haṃ sa ca caturmukhaḥ
children.translated_text: He is the sun, he is the moon, he is I, and he is the four-faced one.
<s>Śauri</s>, the slayer of <s>Kaṃsa</s> and <s>Keśin</s>, consists of all the gods.
This too we have heard from <s>Īśvara</s> in the presence of <s>Umāpati</s>.'
Having heard this speech of the sage, <s>Keśava</s> came to <s>Dvārakā</s>
and obtained a son from <s>Rukmiṇī</s>, he who created the three worlds by his own will.
'Blessed are you, O king, for this mighty lord, beloved of <s>Kamalā</s>,
the jewel protecting the universe, marked by <s>Garuḍa</s>, is your guardian.'
When <s>Gāṅgeya</s> had told this and remained silent for a moment,
the son of <s>Dharma</s> spoke softly in the midst of the assembly of sages:
'What single deity is the supreme refuge and happiness for all embodied beings?
In whom is the universe established, and who, when praised, grants liberation?'
When <s>Dharmaputra</s> had said this, the son of <s>Jāhnavī</s> spoke,
having bowed in his mind to lotus-eyed <s>Viṣṇu</s>, free from affliction:
'<s>Viṣṇu</s>, the Blessed Infinite One, god of gods and lord of the world,
praised with the thousand names, is the giver of liberation, he whose banner bears <s>Garuḍa</s>.
The universe is established in him, and he is the supreme deity.

children.text: nāmnāṃ sahasraṃ munayo yasya gāyanti muktaye ||
children.translated_text: The sages sing the thousand names of him for liberation.'
The universe, <s>Viṣṇu</s>, the vaṣaṭ-call, whose nature is past, future, and present,
the lord, bearer of beings, creator of beings, and cutter-off of worldly becoming;
the master, the Person, the Ancient One, witness of the field and the knower of the field;
the earth, the self-born one, <s>Śaṃbhu</s>, the ordainer, the creator, and destiny;
<s>Hari</s>, <s>Hiraṇyagarbha</s>, the lord of <s>Śrī</s>, the maker of the universe;
<s>Vṛṣākapi</s>, the unfailing one, the thousand-eyed one, the lord of cows;
the thousand-headed <s>Viṣṇu</s>, the all-pervading one, whose essence is the praṇava: their hymn,
marked by a thousand names, is proclaimed to be the king of mantras.
Having spoken thus, with Vedic, divine names, both secondary and primary,
<s>Bhīṣma</s> praised the eternal god with a full thousand of names.
Having listened to this attentively and having bowed to <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, the son of <s>Dharma</s>
asked the son of the heavenly river about the power of the earth-gods, the Brahmins.
He said: 'Indeed, from fear of Brahmins devoted to brahman,

children.text: udeti somaḥ sūryaśca prayāti ca samīraṇaḥ ||
children.translated_text: the moon rises, the sun rises, and the wind moves.
Long ago, <s>Kārtavīrya</s>, maddened by the thousand arms obtained through <s>Dattātreya</s>'s boon,
was addressed by <s>Vāyu</s> as one who had conquered the three worlds:
"There is no one, O best of kings, stronger than Brahmins,

children.text: bhavādṛśā dṛśā yeṣāṃ bhavanti na bhavanti ca ||
children.translated_text: for people such as you exist and cease to exist by their very glance."
Long ago <s>Uttathya</s>, chosen by the daughter of <s>Soma</s>, rose up against the lord of aquatic beings;
in anger he drank up the waters that lord loved and carried off his beloved.
Long ago the Dānavas, who had conquered all gods and Gandharvas,
were slain by the gods, left without refuge, when <s>Agastya</s> drank the ocean.
In ancient times, in the gods' battle with the Daityas, when they were protected amid darkness,
the cool-rayed moon was created by <s>Atri</s>, and <s>Cyavana</s> defeated <s>Śakra</s>.
Hearing this greatness of Brahmins, the Haihaya king,
<s>Arjuna</s>, with undivided mind, worshiped the earth-gods constantly.

children.text: ataḥ paraṃ brāhmaṇānāṃ prabhāvaṃ keśavo vibhuḥ
children.translated_text: Beyond this, the mighty <s>Keśava</s> knows the power of Brahmins,
he from whose navel-lotus the four-faced one was created by his own will.'
When <s>Bhīṣma</s> had spoken thus, <s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s> asked <s>Hṛṣīkeśa</s>
about the greatness of Brahmins, and he, being questioned, said to him:
'Long ago, when <s>Raukmiṇeya</s> asked me about the power of twice-borns,
I told him that even the deities tremble because of their ascetic heat.
My son, with every effort always honor Brahmins;
by their anger and favor they make alive and they burn up.
Long ago <s>Durvāsas</s>, seeking shelter, with blazing eyes and hair,
dwelt in my house, while I served him with those various things dear to him.

children.text: sa bhuktvā pāyasaṃ taptamucchiṣṭena ruṣā jvalan
children.translated_text: After eating hot rice pudding, blazing with anger, he said to me, "Smear your limbs with the leftovers,"
and I did that out of fear.

children.text: rukmiṇīṃ sa rathe kṛtvā babhrāma bahuyojanam
children.translated_text: He put <s>Rukmiṇī</s> in a chariot and roamed for many yojanas,

children.text: nirvikāraṃ ca māṃ dṛṣṭvā tutoṣa paruṣāśrayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and when that harsh-tempered one saw me unchanged, he was pleased.
He said to me, "Your body, smeared with my leftovers, will become adamantine,

children.text: bhaviṣyati vinā pādau tau niliptau yatastvayā ||
children.translated_text: except for your feet, because those two were not smeared by you."'
After hearing this speech of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, <s>Pārtha</s> again from the son of <s>Śantanu</s>
heard the sin-destroying lineages of gods, kings, and seers:
<s>Kaṇva</s>, <s>Raibhya</s>, <s>Yavakrīta</s>, <s>Vasiṣṭha</s>, <s>Bhṛgu</s>, and <s>Kaśyapa</s>,
<s>Duḥṣyanta</s>, <s>Rāma</s>, <s>Nahuṣa</s>, <s>Alarka</s>, <s>Śveta</s>, and <s>Bhagīratha</s>.
Having recounted them, he remained silent for a moment in the soundless assembly;
then, at <s>Vyāsa</s>'s command, the godlike vow-keeper sent <s>Pārtha</s> to the city.
The son of <s>Kuntī</s>, together with <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, his brothers, and his followers,
set out for <s>Hastināpura</s>, placing <s>Dhṛtarāṣṭra</s> before him.
The generous <s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s>, honored by the gods, stayed there,
and, seeing that the northern course had arrived, returned again to the grandsire.
He came with his attendants to <s>Gāṅgeya</s>, who lay upon the arrows,
bowed down, announced, "I am the Pāṇḍava," and sat nearby.
In the assembly attended by the lords of sages, like another world of <s>Brahmā</s>,
when there was silent stillness and all were looking toward <s>Bhīṣma</s>'s face,
<s>Gāṅgeya</s> slowly opened his eyes, looked at the Pāṇḍavas with their followers,
and, skilled in speech, spoke gravely to the eldest Pāṇḍava:
'By good fortune you have arrived at the proper time, now that the sun has turned;
two months have passed for me as I lay on this bed of sharp arrows.
Having addressed you, my son, I now go to the eternal worlds.'
Having said this, the grandsire, an ocean of the milk of truth, with his neck turned slightly,
spoke to <s>Dhṛtarāṣṭra</s> in <s>Vidura</s>'s presence:
'O king, the eye made of knowledge is seen to remain unimpaired in you;

children.text: mā gamaḥ putraśokārtyā mohaṃ kālo hi durjayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: do not fall into delusion from the pain of grief for your sons, for time is hard to overcome.
Regard King <s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s>, who is compassionate, as your own son;
may the rest of this time pass for you, filled with contentment.'

children.text: etaduktvā hṛṣīkeśaṃ stutvā mūrdhnā praṇamya ca
children.translated_text: Having said this, he praised <s>Hṛṣīkeśa</s> and bowed with his head,
then said, 'Blessed lord, permit me to depart.'
Then, permitted by <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, <s>Bhīṣma</s>, like a waveless ocean,
remained for a moment, holding the support of his breath.
As he abandoned the outer body through the savor of inward contact,
all saw his limbs slowly becoming free of arrows, and they were filled with wonder.
He, with every inward attachment fallen away, with all the wheels burst open by the power of his own strength rising from the root where the mind rested within,
through the course of the central channel, impelled upward by breath spreading in expanding masses of quivering, star-bright radiance...
Having fixed his gaze, brighter than moon and sun, between his brows, while the life-swan rose from the charming lotus with delicate petals,
and marked by the streaming away of the whole activity of his senses, <s>Bhīṣma</s> at once became as if contemplating something beyond words.
Then a radiance, tawny like lightning and filled with hundreds of rays,

children.text: bhittvā bhīṣmasya mūrdhānaṃ viveśa vimalaṃ nabhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: split open <s>Bhīṣma</s>'s head and entered the stainless sky.
Then <s>Dharmarāja</s>, together with <s>Vidura</s>, himself prepared for him, with jeweled ornaments, garments, and flowers,
a heavenly conveyance.
<s>Yuyutsu</s> quickly took up his umbrella, white as his fame,
and <s>Bhīmasena</s> and <s>Arjuna</s> likewise took fly-whisks, white with purity.
Fanned by the women of the <s>Bharatas</s>, who were full of tears, with the breeze of palm-leaf fans,
he reached the pyre, prepared with sandalwood and agaru.
When <s>Gāṅgeya</s>, as though still alive, had merged into his vast splendor,
<s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s> and the others, their eyes filled with tears, performed the water rite.
There, on the bank of the <s>Mandākinī</s>, while the king and his followers were dejected,
<s>Jāhnavī</s> rose up from the midst of the water, her eyes filled with tears.
Distraught, grieving, and sorrowful, she was repeatedly looked upon by the deeply saddened supreme seers,
<s>Vyāsa</s>, <s>Nārada</s>, <s>Kaṇva</s>, and the others, and she spoke.
Alas, my son! You defeated even that <s>Rāma</s>, pupil of <s>Tripurārāti</s> and foe of kṣatriyas;

children.text: jetā tasyāpi rāmasya nihato 'si kathaṃ paraiḥ ||
children.translated_text: how have you now been slain by others?

children.text: aho nu tvayi kālena yāte 'staṃ yaśasāṃ nidhau
children.translated_text: Alas, now that you, a treasury of fame, have been brought to setting by Time,
this earth is to be pitied, empty and bereft of its jewel of heroes.

children.text: kā nāma jananī pāpā madvidhānyā bhaviṣyati
children.translated_text: What other sinful mother like me will there be,

children.text: nihataṃ tvādṛśaṃ putraṃ yā śrutvāpi na dīryate ||
children.translated_text: who, even after hearing that a son like you has been slain, does not split apart?

children.text: aho bata varākeṇa hato bhīṣmaḥ śikhaṇḍinā
children.translated_text: Ah, alas, <s>Bhīṣma</s> has been killed by wretched <s>Śikhaṇḍin</s>;
a furious lion, enemy of elephants, has been felled by a jackal.
As <s>Jahnukanyā</s> was speaking in this stream of lamentation, <s>Janārdana</s>,
slowly consoling her, spoke in a voice deep as thunderclouds.
Though you know the highest truth, and though you were witness to the curse of the <s>Vasus</s>,
how, goddess, are you deluded like an ordinary mother?
For <s>Śāntanava</s>, <s>Bhīṣma</s>, whose valor was like that of <s>Tripurāri</s>,
could not have been slain by <s>Śikhaṇḍin</s>'s power, apart from mighty Time.

children.text: sa yātaḥ paramaṃ dhāma svacchandanidhanaḥ svayam
children.translated_text: He has gone by himself to the supreme abode, choosing the time of his own death.

children.text: aśocyaṃ mā śucaḥ putraṃ ko 'nyo jāyeta tadvidhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Do not grieve for a son who is not to be grieved for; who else could be born like him?
Thus, slowly comforted by <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> together with <s>Vyāsa</s> and the others,
the <s>Mandākinī</s>, with fish and makaras streaming in her current, shone for a moment.
Then <s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s> and the others, with their followers, took leave of her,
and, overwhelmed with grief, turned back when the lord of day had gone to setting.
Having bowed to <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> and also to <s>Nara</s>, the best of men,
to the goddess <s>Sarasvatī</s> and to <s>Vyāsa</s>, one should then utter the <s>Jaya</s>.
When the sun that was <s>Bhīṣma</s> had set, leaving only the moonlight of his fame,
the son of <s>Dharma</s> fell, his lotus-face withered by grief.
While he was dejected with his kinsmen, overcome by delusion and fainting,
<s>Dhṛtarāṣṭra</s>, slowly restraining his grief, spoke to him.
Rise, protector of the earth; you ought not abandon courage.
You have heard from the sages the insubstantial course of <s>saṃsāra</s> (worldly existence).
This is not the occasion for grief, since you have not fallen from your own <s>dharma</s> (duty).
O ocean of the nectar of courage, protect your subjects like <s>Prajāpati</s> protecting creatures.
This present time is fit for me alone to be grieved over,

children.text: vidurasya giro yena na śrutāḥ sunayojjvalāḥ ||
children.translated_text: for by me the words of <s>Vidura</s>, shining with good policy, were not heard.
When <s>Dhṛtarāṣṭra</s> had spoken thus, <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> addressed the king:

children.text: mā śucaḥ kṣatradharmeṇa labdhāṃ bhuṅkṣva mahīmimām ||
children.translated_text: Do not grieve. Enjoy this earth, won in accordance with kṣatriya <s>dharma</s>.
For prosperities, dependent on courage, flee from those who are miserable.
Victorious king, perform sacrifice to remove the suspicion of sin.
By a properly performed <s>aśvamedha</s> (horse sacrifice), you have attained fitness for that.
Hearing this speech of the sage, he fixed his desire upon the sacrifice.
Thinking that the rite depended on wealth, he considered the royal treasury.
Then, eager for the great sacrifice, he summoned all the treasurers.

children.text: tebhyaḥ śuśrāva sarvasvaṃ kṣayitaṃ yudhi kauravaiḥ
children.translated_text: From them he heard that all the wealth had been exhausted by the <s>Kauravas</s> in the war.

children.text: aśvamedhe nirāśaṃ taṃ vijñāya draviṇaṃ vinā ||
children.translated_text: Recognizing that he despaired of the <s>aśvamedha</s> without resources,
<s>Vyāsa</s>, ocean of compassion, spoke as if cooling him.
On <s>Himācala</s> there remains the sacrificial surplus of King <s>Marutta</s>,
much gold; you will obtain it for the sake of the sacrifice.
Hearing this, the son of <s>Pāṇḍu</s> asked about the great sacrifice of King <s>Marutta</s>,
and the foremost sage told the story.
In the mighty lineage of <s>Manu</s>, a treasury of the fame of great men,
there was a glorious king named <s>Marutta</s> in the family of <s>Karandhama</s>.

children.text: tam indraḥ spardhate nityaṃ na sa śaknoti ceṣṭitaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Indra</s> was always competing with him, but could not surpass him by his efforts.

children.text: yadā tadā manyutapto rahaḥ prāha bṛhaspatim
children.translated_text: Then, burned by anger, he spoke in private to <s>Bṛhaspati</s>.
King <s>Karandhama</s> was one for whom your father officiated as priest.
In due order his son, <s>Marutta</s>, greater even in those virtues, is also yours to serve.
But because of the clash produced by his pride, I make this request of you:
you must not now go to the position of his officiating priest.
So entreated by <s>Maghavat</s>, <s>Bṛhaspati</s> said, 'So be it.'

children.text: adyaprabhṛti martyo me na yājya iti saṃvidā
children.translated_text: By agreement he declared, 'From this day forth no mortal shall be one for whom I officiate.'
Meanwhile King <s>Marutta</s>, resolved to undertake a vast sacrifice,
approached <s>Bṛhaspati</s>,
and earnestly requested him, saying, 'May you be my officiating priest.'
Constrained by his affection for <s>Śakra</s>, he did not give his assent;
rejected by his guru, the king went away with his face bent down in shame.
As he went, his resolve ruined, he saw <s>Nārada</s> on the road.

children.text: nārado 'pi tamālokya pṛṣṭvā śrutvā ca tatkathām ||
children.translated_text: <s>Nārada</s> too, seeing him, questioned him and heard his story.

children.text: uvāca tyaja saṃtāpaṃ mā rājanvimanā bhava
children.translated_text: He said, "Give up your distress; do not be downcast, O king.
There is a treasure of splendors named <s>Saṃvarta</s>, the younger brother of <s>Bṛhaspati</s>.
He is a lord of yogins, wandering at will; he stays in <s>Vārāṇasī</s>.

children.text: saṃvartaḥ sa parijñeyo vrajethāḥ śaraṇaṃ tu tam ||
children.translated_text: He should be recognized as <s>Saṃvarta</s>; go to him for refuge.
When he asks, 'By whom was I pointed out?', you should bow and say:
'<s>Nārada</s> told me that you were here.'
After telling him this, and gladdened, you should point to blazing <s>Jātavedas</s>
and, saying so, entreat him to be your officiating priest, O best of sacrificers."
When <s>Nārada</s> had spoken thus, the king was filled with joy.

children.text: taduktaṃ vidadhe sarvaṃ gatvā vārāṇasīṃ svayam ||
children.translated_text: Going himself to <s>Vārāṇasī</s>, he did everything that had been said by him.

children.text: saṃtyaktonmattarūpaṃ sa prāpya taṃ yājakaṃ nṛpaḥ
children.translated_text: The king reached that priest, who had assumed the form of a madman,
and, with his permission, then performed austerity on the slope of <s>Himagiri</s>.
Desiring wealth for the sacrifice, that king worshiped the god <s>Śaṃkara</s> with austerity
and obtained gold equal in mass to many <s>Meru</s>s.
Then, when the artisans had fashioned all the vessels out of gold,
the complete sacrificial equipment of the earth-ruling king was set in motion.
When <s>Bṛhaspati</s> learned of the incomparable prosperity at his sacrifice,
he became tormented and grew thin, because <s>Saṃvarta</s> was the priest.
Asked by <s>Śakra</s> the cause of his grief, with his mind withered,
he spoke of the splendor of <s>Marutta</s>'s sacrifice, troubled by rivalry with his brother.
Then <s>Śatakratu</s>, affectionate toward his guru, in order to please him,
summoned Fire and said, "Go to <s>Marutta</s>, the king.

children.text: gatvā madvacasā vācyaḥ sa ca rājā tvayā kratau
children.translated_text: Having gone, that king must be addressed by you in my words at the sacrifice,
so that, abandoning <s>Saṃvarta</s>, he may become one whose rite is performed by <s>Bṛhaspati</s>."
Thus ordered by the king of the gods, Fire went to the lord of men
and delivered <s>Śakra</s>'s message, but the king did not accept it.
Then, after he had returned, <s>Vajrī</s> urged him, "Go again,"
but <s>Pāvaka</s>, trembling with fear of <s>Saṃvarta</s>, said:

children.text: sa tatra brahmacārī māmūce saṃvartakaḥ krudhā
children.translated_text: "There that brahmacarin, <s>Saṃvarta</s>, a mass of fiery power, spoke to me in anger:
'I will curse you if you come back again.'
Hearing this, <s>Puraṃdara</s> said to him, "You are frightened."
Then the Fire, blazing with wrath as his oblation, replied to him:
"Ah, surely the fire of a Brahmin's anger, in the case of you, the lover of <s>Ahalyā</s>,
has been forgotten, O <s>Śakra</s>, through negligence, or anger, or delusion.
When <s>Cyavana</s>, in anger, created the great-fanged mighty demon <s>Mahādaṃṣṭra</s>

children.text: asṛjattvadvadhāyograṃ tadā dhairyaṃ kva te gatam ||
children.translated_text: for your destruction, where then did your courage go?
The rages of Brahmins are unbearable; they burn up the world in a moment."
When <s>Hutāśana</s> had spoken thus, <s>Śakra</s> could not say anything.
Again dispatched by <s>Indra</s>, the lord of the Gandharvas spoke to the king:

children.text: ūce guruṃ bhajasveti na ca rājā tamagrahīt ||
children.translated_text: "Accept the guru," but the king did not heed him.
Then <s>Vajrī</s> himself, enraged, roaring with a deep sound,
went through the sky to the king's sacrificial ground, surrounded by clouds.
Then, by the great power of <s>Saṃvarta</s>'s fierce brilliance,
the thunderbolt released by <s>Śatamanyu</s> entered into the clouds.
Then <s>Vṛtrahā</s>, helpless through the power of his mantra, was summoned
and came together with the thirty gods, Soma-drinkers entitled to sacrificial shares.
Then <s>Śatakratu</s>, honored by <s>Marutta</s> and his anger pacified,
devoted himself to service among the instruments of the sacrificial rite.
At his command all the gods became makers of the sacrificial supplies
for the earth-protecting king, subject to his order for a long time.
Thus, through <s>Saṃvarta</s>'s brilliance, the sacrifice of that king who had conquered <s>Indra</s>
and who rained gold reached completion without obstruction.
"With the wealth left over from that sacrifice, you, purified, should undertake
the great horse-sacrifice rite," said the lordly sage, and then he ceased.
Then, comforted by <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> and also by the sages and his brothers,
<s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s>, resolved on undertaking the horse sacrifice, regained firmness.
Then, when the son of <s>Dharma</s> set about examining the affairs of his subjects,
that whole circle of sages addressed him and disappeared.
Then in the garden of the assembly hall, lovely with golden jewel-creepers and blooming golden lotuses,

children.text: atha kṛṣṇau sabhodyāne svairaṃ prītyā vijahratuḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> and <s>Arjuna</s> roamed at ease in affection.
At the end of their conversation there, the beloved of <s>Subhadrā</s> said to the foe of <s>Kaṃsa</s>:
"Everything that was spoken by you at the beginning of the battle has been forgotten by me.
O knower of the supreme truth, please speak again that knowledge which was set forth."
Thus addressed by the son of <s>Pāṇḍu</s>, <s>Keśava</s> said, dejected:
"Ah, because of your inattention, that was not heard by you, foolish as you were.
It cannot be spoken again in that way; nevertheless, listen to this.
Long ago, a certain perfected one who had attained the state of <s>jīvanmukti</s> (liberation while alive)
was questioned by a Brahmin and, knowing the whole delusion of worldly existence, spoke.
In this unreal aggregate of beings, made from the five elements,
the <s>jīva</s> (individual soul), bound by the <s>guṇa</s>s, remains like a bird in a cage.
For embodied beings whose single essence is ego, who have forgotten the self,
the waning and arising of pleasure and pain revolve like a wheel.
At the end of the body, through contact with karma, creatures, by their good and evil deeds,
They attain star-like aerial cars, or else hells.
Then, when the enjoyment is exhausted, into a womb wrapped in the placenta
the self, in the form of semen, enters the womb suffused with blood.
As water is absorbed into the face of a mirror by the tips of breaths,
as the heat of a fire that has been blown out spreads through the sky,
or as the fragrance of a flower enters the midst of the wind,
as color passes into crystal that has a cleft,
so, with a movement difficult to perceive, the self runs into the embryo,
bearing its latent impression within, as the wind bears a touch of cold.
For one who is born, craving is born; for one who grows, it grows.

children.text: tṛṣṇātantur visasyeva śuṣyato na tu śuṣyati ||
children.translated_text: Like the fiber of a withering lotus, it does not wither away even as he withers.
Firmly resorting to detachment through discrimination and through contact with suffering,
one initiated into brahman is released by the mantra, 'I am not this.'
First he is extinguished with respect to states of being, and then with respect to the activities of their causes;
having reached the state without support, the yogin is absorbed in brahman.
Knowing the self as having hands and feet everywhere, as all-pervading and imperishable,
and knowing this true condition of becoming,
the siddha, having spoken thus to the Brahmin, suddenly vanished.
And hear this other matter, <s>Kaunteya</s>, attentively, for your welfare.
Once, in private, a certain Brahmin woman spoke to her husband:
'What goal shall I go to, I who am a virtuous woman, desireless and devoted to you?'
Asked thus by her, the Brahmin, with a smiling face, said to her:
'The fire named <s>Vaiśvānara</s>, they say, stands within embodied beings.
The senses, the mind, and the intellect are remembered as its seven flames;
its fuels are the sense-objects, and the seven enjoyers are also its priests.

children.text: tasminhate sarvamidaṃ jāyate ca punaḥ punaḥ ||
children.translated_text: When oblation is offered in that fire, all this is born again and again.
The senses always serve the mind, and the mind serves them;
through mutual assistance they delight in the conjunction with the body.
Long ago the seven deer that are the senses, beginning with mind and intellect,
were slain by the king, without reasoning, with arrows made of yoga.
For one whose senses are conquered, nothing here is his; yet all of this belongs to him alone.
'Objects belong to the object,' so <s>Janaka</s> said to the Brahmin.
Therefore, seeing all this with a mind free from attachment,
I, knowing the higher and the lower, have abandoned it for the pacification of the appearance of becoming.
Your goal too, fair lady, is always like my own state.
Know the fire of knowledge to be produced from the fire-stick of brahman.'
Hearing these words of her husband, the Brahmin woman, a seer of reality,
attained supreme mastery in the knowledge of the field and the knower of the field.
Having heard this, <s>Arjuna</s>, filled with wonder, spoke to <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>:

children.text: yogīndro brāhmaṇaḥ ko 'sau kvāste vā sā ca tadvadhūḥ ||
children.translated_text: 'Who was that Brahmin, lord of yogins, and where does he stay, and where is that wife of his?'
Thus addressed, the foe of <s>Kaiṭabha</s> again said to <s>Dhanaṃjaya</s>:
'Long ago, when asked by his disciple, an omniscient teacher spoke.
This story that cuts off becoming was heard by <s>Bṛhaspati</s> and the other lordly sages,
all-seeing seers, and was spoken by <s>Svayaṃbhū</s> himself.
For beings bound by the three guṇas and altered by distinctions of karma,
this state of living creatures, though slight, always comes to great extent.
This manifold creation, they say, has issued from ahaṃkāra (ego-making);

children.text: tasmin eva layaṃ yāti śvabhre puṣpacayo yathā ||
children.translated_text: it dissolves into that alone, as a heap of flowers falls into a pit.
Ahaṃkāra, through the habit of hundreds of former births, has become inwardly intimate;

children.text: ahaṃkāraḥ sa manaso līlayā kena bhedyate ||
children.translated_text: who can easily separate it from the mind?
Only by the thinning of ignorance, for one who has gradually renounced action,
when the dualities of conceptual construction cease, the light of knowledge arises.
Burning the poisonous tree of becoming with the blazing fire of knowledge,
one freed from every knot tastes the supreme nectar.

children.text: iti brahmoditaṃ jñānaṃ śiṣyāya guruṇā purā
children.translated_text: This knowledge, spoken by <s>Brahmā</s> long ago, was taught by the teacher to his disciple,
furnished with many illustrations, for the pacification of becoming.

children.text: ahameva guruḥ pārtha śiṣyaśca tvaṃ samo mama
children.translated_text: I myself am the teacher, <s>Pārtha</s>, and you are the disciple, equal to me.'
Having spoken this whole treasure of knowledge, <s>Janārdana</s> fell silent.

children.text: tato vihṛtya suciraṃ prītyā kṛṣṇaḥ kirīṭinā
children.translated_text: Then <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, after staying happily for a long time with <s>Kirīṭin</s>,
set his mind on going to <s>Dvārakā</s>, eager to see his kinsmen.

children.text: sa gatvā nṛpamāmantrya dhṛtarāṣṭraṃ ca sānugam
children.translated_text: He went and took leave of the king and of <s>Dhṛtarāṣṭra</s> with his attendants,

children.text: āśvāsya kṛṣṇāṃ kuntīṃ ca praṇamyādāya cānujām ||
children.translated_text: comforted <s>Kṛṣṇā</s> and <s>Kuntī</s>, bowed, and took his younger sister with him.
Making an agreement, 'I shall meet you again at the aśvamedha (horse sacrifice),'
<s>Garuḍadhvaja</s> departed, his chariot driven by <s>Dāruka</s>.
As he traveled with <s>Sātyaki</s> as his companion, coloring the faces of the quarters with his splendor,

children.text: uttaṅkaṃ tapasāṃ rāśim āluloke muniḥ pathi ||
children.translated_text: he saw on the road the sage <s>Uttaṅka</s>, a mass of austerity.

children.text: taṃ dṛṣṭvā sādaraṃ śauriḥ praṇamya racitāñjaliḥ
children.translated_text: Seeing him, <s>Śauri</s>, with respect, bowed with folded hands
and asked after the welfare of the hermitage-dwellers who were free from enmity.
<s>Uttaṅka</s> too, seeing <s>Hari</s> well and with affection, said:

children.text: ūce kaccittvayā sāmnā rakṣitaṃ bhārataṃ kulam ||
children.translated_text: 'Has the Bhārata clan been preserved by you through conciliation?
Are King <s>Duryodhana</s> and <s>Dharmaputra</s>, together with their followers,
settled without conflict, through your wisdom, in their ancestral station?'
Asked thus by <s>Uttaṅka</s>, <s>Govinda</s> replied to him:

children.text: bhāratānāṃ mune yatnaḥ paraḥ saṃdhau kṛto mayā ||
children.translated_text: 'O sage, the highest effort toward peace among the Bhāratas was made by me.
Though the <s>Kaurava</s> was repeatedly advised for his welfare by <s>Vidura</s> and others,

children.text: na jagrāha kṛtāntena daivena ca vimohitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: he did not accept it, deluded by death and by fate.
Through the obstinacy of the Kuru king, who followed <s>Rādheya</s>,

children.text: nihatāḥ pārthivāḥ sarve śeṣāḥ pañcaiva pāṇḍavāḥ ||
children.translated_text: all the kings were slain; only the five <s>Pāṇḍavas</s> remain.'
Having heard this, the sage, like blazing fire from anger,
said to him, with a distorted mind, 'They were brought down by you yourself.
Though you were able, O <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, since you, seeking <s>Pārtha</s>'s welfare,
neglected that dreadful destruction, therefore I give you a curse.'
When <s>Uttaṅka</s> had spoken thus, the slayer of <s>Kaiṭabha</s> replied:
'I know you, <s>Uttaṅka</s>, treasury of austerity, a mass of fiery power.

children.text: kiṃtu nārhasi kopena tīvraṃ kartuṃ tapovyayam
children.translated_text: But you ought not, through anger, to make a severe waste of your austerity;

children.text: tamo hi duḥsahaṃ ghoraṃ krodho mṛtyuḥ śarīriṇām ||
children.translated_text: for anger is unbearable, terrible darkness; it is death for embodied beings.
Even now your delusion is not destroyed; surely even now you do not see.

children.text: kiṃ na jānāsi māṃ sarvaṃ sarvavyāpinamavyayam ||
children.translated_text: Do you not know me as all, all-pervading and undecaying?
I am made of all gods, the maker, the universal self of the worlds.'
When the lotus-eyed one had said this, the sage, his anger calmed, said:

children.text: jāne tvāṃ kiṃtu taddivyaṃ draṣṭumicchāmi te vapuḥ
children.translated_text: 'I know you, but I wish to see that divine form of yours.'
Thus entreated by the lord of sages, through the play of manifesting the universe,
he showed that supreme lordly form, filled in its foremost consciousness with the radiance of power, in which <s>Druhiṇa</s>, <s>Rudra</s>, <s>Mahendra</s>, and the moon flashed forth as lines,
imperishable and beyond the three abodes; seeing it, the best of sages became free from delusion.
Then <s>Viṣṇu</s>, bowed to by <s>Uttaṅka</s> with hymns and devotion,
at that word of his again assumed that same gentle form of his.
'I shall make myself present to you everywhere through remembrance, O sage,'
and having said this and dismissed him, the one whose banner bears <s>Garuḍa</s> departed.
Then once, as that sage was thirsty for water while wandering in the deserts,
he saw a caṇḍāla, bow in hand, offering water.
Although that man repeatedly begged him, saying, 'Take it,' when the sage
<s>Uttaṅka</s> did not accept the impure water, he vanished then.
Then the Blessed Lord <s>Viṣṇu</s> himself came to him and said:

children.text: mune madvacasā śakraḥ sudhāṃ tvāṃ dātumāyayau ||
children.translated_text: 'O sage, at my word <s>Śakra</s> came to give you nectar.

children.text: jalado na sa cāṇḍālo mithyā śaṅkā tavābhavat
children.translated_text: He was a cloud-giver of water, not a caṇḍāla; your suspicion was false.

children.text: pratyākhyātaḥ sa yanmohānna tadyuktaṃ tvayā kṛtam ||
children.translated_text: Since he was rejected by you through delusion, that was not rightly done by you.
Now, through my boon, let this desert land of yours be filled
with streams of water containing nectar.' Having said this, <s>Hari</s> departed.
Thus that <s>Uttaṅka</s>, of great power and a treasury of fame,
obtained the rare sight of <s>Viṣṇu</s> together with his grace.

children.text: āsādya paramaṃ jñānaṃ yaḥ purā gurusevayā
children.translated_text: He was the one who formerly, having attained supreme knowledge through service to his guru,
went as a seeker of that teacher's fee to the palace of King <s>Pauṣya</s>.
Having obtained the beautiful earrings given by <s>Pauṣya</s>'s wife,
and seeing them stolen, he went to <s>Rasātala</s>, risking his life.
After conquering the serpents and recovering those jewel earrings there long ago,

children.text: yo dadau gurubhāryāyai kṛtakṛtyo babhūva ca ||
children.translated_text: he gave them to his guru's wife and became one who had accomplished his task.
When <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, giver of joy to the <s>Yādavas</s>, had gone to <s>Dvāravatī</s>,
<s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s>, together with his ministers, considered the business of the sacrifice.

children.text: sa gatvā sānujaḥ śailaṃ śrīkaṇṭhadayitaṃ śanaiḥ
children.translated_text: He went slowly with his younger brothers to the mountain beloved of <s>Śrīkaṇṭha</s>,
and by austerity propitiated <s>Rudra</s>, god of gods, bearer of <s>Pināka</s>.
With a ritual offering, according to rule, at an auspicious moment,
he worshiped the lord of the <s>Guhyakas</s> and <s>Maṇibhadra</s> with his followers.
When the fire had been satisfied by the sages, with <s>Dhaumya</s> as priest,
the illustrious son of <s>Pāṇḍu</s> obtained the treasure deposited by <s>Marutta</s>.
There were thousands of shining golden vessels, various in form and broad in size,
and hundreds of loads of jewels.

children.text: uṣṭrāṇāṃ śakaṭānāṃ ca hayānāṃ kariṇāṃ tathā
children.translated_text: By camels, carts, horses, and elephants alike,
he brought that wealth, ten lakhs in number, to <s>Hastināpura</s>.

children.text: mahiṣāṇāṃ kharāṇāṃ ca puruṣāṇāṃ gavāṃ tathā
children.translated_text: Of buffaloes, donkeys, men, and cattle too,

children.text: na babhūva tadā saṃkhyā vahatāṃ bhūri kāñcanam ||
children.translated_text: there was then no counting those who carried the abundant gold.
Then, when the king had taken the inexhaustible treasury and reached his own city,
<s>Madhusūdana</s> came, accompanied by all the <s>Vṛṣṇis</s>.
At that very time the wife of <s>Saubhadra</s> gave birth to a son,
burned by the weapon of <s>Droṇa</s>'s son and dead.
The festive cry of the women, 'A son has been born to <s>Uttarā</s>!',
became that very sound of weeping: 'He is lifeless, lifeless!'
When the child, whose limbs were tender like young coral shoots and buds,
was born lifeless, the mothers' company fainted from grief.

children.text: tataḥ kuntī subhadrā ca sametya karuṇānidhim
children.translated_text: Then <s>Kuntī</s> and <s>Subhadrā</s> approached the treasure of compassion
and spoke to the husband of <s>Rukmiṇī</s> with voices choked by tears:
'Of your dear sister's son <s>Abhimanyu</s>, an embodiment of fame,
the young son's young child has today been born without life.'
Hearing this, the Blessed Lord, creator of beings, softened with compassion,
<s>Śauri</s>, entered the birth chamber adorned with pitchers.
It was tawny with cloth gleaming like jewels, heaped with hundreds of shining herbs,
and guarded by mantras, physicians, fire, weapons, and missiles.
Then <s>Uttarā</s>, regaining consciousness after being sprinkled with cold water,
took the child in her lap and lamented before <s>Hari</s>.
Then <s>Śauri</s>, whose voice was deep as a rain cloud, spoke,
gently looking at the child with a glance that rained nectar:
'As truth, Brahmins, and dharma are dearer to me than anything else,
by that truth may this boy, freed today from the weapon, live.'
When <s>Mādhava</s> had spoken thus, that child, having regained life,
became like a lotus bud touched by rays of the sun.
Then at once a vast festival began in the city.
Even among the sky-goers there arose the cry, 'Well done, well done!'
Since this infant was born when the Kuru line had been exhausted,
'therefore let him be called by the name <s>Parīkṣit</s>,' said <s>Keśava</s> then.
Then, at <s>Vyāsa</s>'s command, a very wealthy provision fit for the king's sacrifice
was set in motion, rich in abundant jewels and full of many marvels.
Then, after releasing according to rule the dark sacrificial horse,
guarded by the son of <s>Pāṇḍu</s> himself, the wielder of the <s>Gāṇḍīva</s>,
the son of <s>Dharma</s> was consecrated at the end of the bright fortnight of <s>Caitra</s>,
wearing a golden garland, bearing a staff, shaven-headed, and wrapped in a black antelope skin.
Then, when the sacrificial horse reached the region of <s>Trigarta</s>,
a tumultuous battle arose between the princes and <s>Savyasācin</s>.
<s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s>'s command to him had been that the kings were not to be killed;

children.text: tāṃ smaran āvadhīdbhūpānsa vijigye tu kevalam ||
children.translated_text: remembering that, he did not slay the rulers, but only conquered them.
In battle he faced the heroic <s>Vajradatta</s>, son of <s>Bhagadatta</s>, lord of <s>Prāgjyotiṣa</s>,
and after three days defeated that fighter from elephant-back.
He fought for a long time with the <s>Saindhavas</s>, cruel warriors,
while <s>Pārtha</s> went on foot in battle against men stationed on chariots and elephants.
Then <s>Duḥśalā</s>, taking the infant grandson of <s>Jayadratha</s>,
approached <s>Savyasācin</s> and spoke with tear-filled eyes:
'Brother, when you arrived, merely on hearing your name,
my son, the son of <s>Jayadratha</s>, died, his heart shattered.
This boy is his son, my grandson, the son of your sister's son;
he must be protected by you in every way.' Having said this, the daughter of <s>Dhṛtarāṣṭra</s> wept.
Distressed, <s>Pārtha</s> consoled her, his eyes wet with tears,
and, condemning his own kṣatriya birth, went on following the horse.
Then King <s>Babhruvāhana</s>, her son, came out to meet the horse-guardian, the lord of white horses,
when he had reached the city of <s>Maṇipūra</s>.

children.text: pūjāmādāya tanayaṃ namraṃ dṛṣṭvā puraḥ sthitam
children.translated_text: Seeing his son, who had brought offerings of honor and stood bowed before him,
the son of <s>Śakra</s>, eager for battle, did not welcome him, though his hands were folded.

children.text: dṛṣṭvā māṃ sāyudhaṃ prāptaṃ sāmnā pratyudyato 'si kim
children.translated_text: 'Seeing me arrive armed, why have you come forward with conciliation?
Shame on you, no kṣatriya but a coward,' <s>Dhanaṃjaya</s> said to him.
At that moment a serpent woman split the earth and rose up,
and before her husband, the son of <s>Pāṇḍu</s>, she spoke to <s>Babhruvāhana</s>:
'This father of yours, fond of fine warriors, is pleased by battle.
For the high-spirited, the splendor of courage bears fruit in a lineage of heroes.'

children.text: ityuktaḥ sa tayā dhanvī rathaṃ hemaharidhvajam
children.translated_text: Thus addressed by her, the archer mounted a chariot with a golden, tawny banner,
fastened on his armor, and came to fight his father.
Then <s>Dhanaṃjaya</s>, pierced by him with hundreds of arrows and wearied,
was filled with delight and praised his valor.
The son of <s>Citrāṅgadā</s> cut down, before they could reach him, the iron arrows
released by the wielder of the <s>Gāṇḍīva</s>, heavy as thunderbolts, with his own shafts.
Then the son of <s>Śakra</s> tore apart his son's chariot,
patterned with golden leaves and vines, as the wind tears apart a garden.
Seeing his son chariotless and fighting without confusion,
<s>Vijaya</s> sent arrows slackened by only a slight effort.
Then <s>Babhruvāhana</s>, with a sharp feathered arrow in the heart,
struck the lord of white horses as if with a thunderbolt that splits mountains.
When <s>Arjuna</s>, invulnerable to all beings, had been slain by his son,

children.text: nādo babhūva gagane hā heti tridivaukasām ||
children.translated_text: a cry of 'Alas, alas!' arose in the sky from the dwellers in heaven.
Seeing his father fallen to the ground like <s>Śakra</s>'s banner,
<s>Arjuna</s>'s son fainted, blaming himself, and dropped his bow.
Then <s>Citrāṅgadā</s> came up and saw her husband slain by her son;
stricken with grief, the slender-waisted woman lamented:

children.text: aho bata cirādetya jāyāyā mama mandiram
children.translated_text: 'Alas, noble prince, after so long you have come to the house of your wife,
and you have received this hospitality from a son stronger than you.
Alas, ill-fated as I am, I see you, my husband long absent,

children.text: tvāṃ prāptaṃ nayanānandaṃ paśyāmi nihataṃ kṣitau ||
children.translated_text: who came as a joy to my eyes, now slain upon the ground.'
Having said this, she tightly embraced her husband, her voice choked with tears,
and <s>Citrāṅgadā</s>, together with <s>Ulūpī</s>, the Nāga maiden, fell upon the ground.
Then <s>Babhruvāhana</s>, regaining consciousness, grief-stricken and babbling,
made a vow to abandon his body, bent down by guilt.

children.text: tataḥ pradadhyau manasā nāgī saṃjīvanaṃ maṇim
children.translated_text: Then the Nāgī meditated in her mind upon the life-restoring jewel,
and, when summoned in thought by that faithful woman, it came from the world of the Nāgas.

children.text: spṛṣṭo 'tha hṛdaye tena jīvitaṃ prāpya phalguṇaḥ
children.translated_text: Touched by it on the heart, <s>Phalguṇa</s> regained life,

children.text: citrāṅgadā ca sahasā śokaṃ tyaktvā hriyaṃ yayau ||
