children.translated_text: and <s>Citrāṅgadā</s> at once cast off grief and felt shame.
Then, after reporting what had happened, <s>Ulūpī</s>, the serpent's daughter, spoke
to <s>Arjuna</s>, that ocean of firmness, as if he had just risen from sleep:
'This was the curse, given to you long ago by the <s>Vasus</s> because of the killing of <s>Bhīṣma</s>.

children.text: ko 'nyathā tvāṃ raṇe śakto jetuṃ nirjitadhūrjaṭim ||
children.translated_text: Otherwise who in battle could be able to conquer you, who conquered <s>Dhūrjaṭi</s>?
Out of affection for me, my father entreated them, and those <s>Vasus</s>
declared that this greatly radiant jewel would bring an end to your curse.'
Hearing this, <s>Pārtha</s> was amazed; then he gently consoled
the Nāgī and <s>Citrāṅgadā</s>, and accepted the honor offered by his son.
Then the heroic <s>Pāṇḍava</s> took leave of that beloved son,
and, following the horse, wandered over the earth girdled by the ocean.
After conquering the lord of <s>Magadha</s>, the grandson of <s>Jarāsaṃdha</s>,
and the <s>Vaṅgas</s>, <s>Puṇḍras</s>, <s>Kirātas</s>, southerners, and <s>Magadhas</s>,
He commanded them all, the <s>Gāndhāras</s>, the sons of <s>Subala</s>, and the striking royal princes,
that they should come to the king's sacrifice.
Then <s>Arjuna</s>, together with the horse that had turned back,
entered <s>Hastināpura</s> victorious, honored by the townspeople.
Then, when the sacrifice of the king who showered gold had begun according to rule,
crowded with hosts of sages, and when all the kings had arrived,
when King <s>Babhruvāhana</s> had arrived together with his mother,
and had been respectfully honored by the sons of <s>Pāṇḍu</s> out of love for <s>Phalguṇa</s>,
the son of <s>Satyavatī</s>, whose moment had been made by a divine consecration that burned up every sin,
himself performed the rites, those sacrificial actions.
There everything was golden, beginning with the piling of the bricks:
the posts, vessels, solid dishes, couches, houses, and gateways.
Divine seers, Siddhas, Gandharvas, and Kinnaras sang auspicious songs,
and companies of Apsarases danced in the intervals of the sacrifice's rites.
And when the herd of animals had been killed, the best Brahmins
took hold of the horse according to scripture, having enclosed <s>Pārṣatī</s>.
Then those officiating priests there, having drawn out the horse's omentum,
cooked it and presented the auspicious smoke to the <s>Pāṇḍavas</s>.
Then, with the rite complete in full, the lord of the earth
gave to <s>Vyāsa</s> as a priestly fee the earth whose girdle is the four oceans.
Afterward, at his word, the king gave a crore of crores of gold,
and again received the earth from the sage, who gave it back to the Brahmins.
Then, when the kings worthy of honor had been honored by the king
and dismissed, there arose an extraordinary great festival of the Brahmin assembly.
There were streams of honey, milk, and ghee,
and heaps of foods and sweet cakes shone like the family mountains.
As gold and jewels were being given by the king to the twice-born,
the ten directions shone, as though filled with rainbows.
<s>Dhṛtarāṣṭra</s> with <s>Vidura</s>, <s>Sañjaya</s>, and the sons of <s>Subala</s>
stood there like deities, being honored by the king.
Meanwhile, with one side beautifully golden, emerging from the mouth of a hole,
a quick-moving mongoose came to the sacrificial ground.
In a human voice he spoke, producing wonder among the people:

children.text: aho nu saktuprasthena na tulyo 'yaṃ mahāmakhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: 'Ah! This great sacrifice is not equal even to a prastha of saktu.

children.text: nūnaṃ dānakaṇaḥ śuddhaḥ kṛśo 'pi prathate nṛṇām
children.translated_text: Surely a pure particle of giving, even if meager, becomes famous among men;
surely the possession of much wealth is only the false pomp of a festival.'
As he was saying this, he was questioned by Brahmins filled with amazement,
and said, 'Hear, O twice-born, the greatness of the prastha of saktu.
Long ago in <s>Kurukṣetra</s> there was a Brahmin who lived by gleaning fallen grains,
lean, with a large family, whose only wealth was pure goodness.
Once, during a terrible famine, his livelihood was exhausted for a long time,
and after wandering with difficulty through a hundred fields, he obtained a prastha of saktu.
At home, having performed the necessary rite by the Vaiśvadeva procedure,
he set out to eat with his wife, when he saw a beggar.

children.text: kṣutparītaḥ kṣudhākrāntaṃ sa taṃ dṛṣṭvātithiṃ dvijaḥ
children.translated_text: Seeing that guest overcome by hunger and tormented by hunger, the Brahmin, himself oppressed by hunger,
gave him his own meal, his heart clear with contentment.
When, after eating that, the beggar's hunger was not appeased,

children.text: tadbhāryā tatsutaścāsmai tatsnuṣā ca dadau tadā ||
children.translated_text: then that Brahmin's wife, his son, and his daughter-in-law also gave their portions to him.
Then, satisfied by the meal of them all, that guest said:
'I am <s>Dharma</s>, pleased by your goodness. May great perfection be yours.'
Having said this, when he had disappeared, they all, whose conduct was praiseworthy,

children.text: saśarīrā divaṃ prāpuḥ sarve te ślāghyavṛttayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: went bodily to heaven in aerial cars bright as the sun.
Then I, a dweller in a hole, summoned by the scent of the saktu,
came to that ground of leftovers where that guest had eaten.
This one side of me, touched by the water from his vessel,
became golden and beautiful when I rolled there, as though bathed by merits.
For a very long time I had the thought, "How might my other side become golden?"
Therefore I came to you, O lord of the earth.
Though I have wandered here in the dining places of hundreds of thousands of Brahmins,

children.text: bhrāntasyāpi na saṃjātaḥ ko 'pi kānto lavastanau ||
children.translated_text: not even the smallest lovely particle has arisen on my body.
Therefore this sacrifice does not deserve equality with the prastha of saktu.'
Having said this, the mongoose of wonderful beauty vanished from sight.
Thus purity of intention is better than thousands of sacrifices;

children.text: manasaḥ kila vaimalyaṃ paraṃ brahma pracakṣate ||
children.translated_text: indeed they declare the supreme brahman to be the purity of the mind.
Long ago, during <s>Agastya</s>'s twelve-year sacrificial session,
the Brahmins told one another of a terrible drought to come.
Then <s>Agastya</s>, the great-minded treasury of austerity, abandoning sacrifice with materials,
performed a sacrifice of meditation with unwavering mind.
That very sacrifice, rich in wealth and attended by the all-knowing ones,
became the rite through which <s>Indra</s>, filled with joy, sent rain.
The sacrifice of the <s>Pāṇḍava</s>, whose goodness was pure, was superior;
but the mongoose, because of his own purpose, raised an objection there.
Long ago, wishing to test <s>Jamadagni</s>, <s>Krodha</s> himself, in the form of a dog,

children.text: pasparśa jihvayā śrāddhe dhṛtaṃ hi piṭhire payaḥ ||
children.translated_text: touched with his tongue the milk placed in the vessel at the śrāddha.
Recognizing, with the eye of knowledge, 'This is <s>Krodha</s>,'

children.text: na śaśāpa tato bhītaḥ krodhaḥ kampākulo 'bhavat ||
children.translated_text: the sage did not curse him; then <s>Krodha</s>, frightened, became full of trembling.

children.text: tataste pitaraḥ kruddhā yeṣāṃ śrāddhe dhṛtaṃ payaḥ
children.translated_text: Then the angry ancestors, in whose <s>śrāddha</s> milk had been taken,
uttered a long-lasting curse, by which his anger passed into the state of being a mongoose.
After telling the story of the insult at <s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s>'s sacrifice,
'You shall attain the end of the curse,' thus a limit was fixed for him by those very ancestors.
Thus the noble tree of conduct of the king, honored by all the rulers of men, richly nourished by the Brahmin folk and arrayed with flowers of goodness,
shone forth, full of clusters of auspicious fruit, rooted in the provisions of sacrifice, and having truth for its branches.
Having bowed to <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> and also to <s>Nara</s>, the best of men,
and to the goddess <s>Sarasvatī</s> and to <s>Vyāsa</s>, one should then proclaim the <s>Jaya</s>.
When King <s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s> ruled the earth beneath a single royal umbrella,
no cry born of distress was heard, and no beggar was seen.
When the fame of that hero of <s>dharma</s> had spread through the three worlds,
people became slow to occupy themselves with woven tales of <s>Rāghava</s> and the like.
<s>Dhṛtarāṣṭra</s>, together with <s>Vidura</s>, and faithful <s>Gāndhārī</s>

children.text: satataṃ daivataṃ tasya babhūvuḥ pratimāṃ vinā ||
children.translated_text: were always deities for him, without need of an image.
The king arranged cooks skilled in the variety of the six tastes,
and he himself inspected the cooks for <s>Dhṛtarāṣṭra</s>'s meal.
By his command, the sons of <s>Pāṇḍu</s> never gave an unpleasant reply to the aged Kuru,
even when he uttered improper words; all of them made no retort.
'The son of <s>Ambikā</s> eats every kind of food fit for a king,'
so he had it announced, but in secret he lived on fruit.
Alas, <s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s> did not perceive the detachment of that man,
who kept vows, recited prayers, slept on the ground, and had only his wife as companion.
As they lived in this way, full of mutual affection,

children.text: kāle pravāhini yayuḥ samāḥ pañcādhikā daśa ||
children.translated_text: fifteen years passed in the flowing course of time.
Then once, remembering the wicked acts of the <s>Kauravas</s>,
arrogant <s>Bhīma</s> loudly spoke at length of their slaughter.
Hearing that, <s>Dhṛtarāṣṭra</s>, whose anger was conquered and whose wife was his companion,
made as though he had heard nothing at all, and became eager for renunciation.
Then, because of his intense disenchantment, his mind turned away from the delusion of worldly existence,
and, desiring peace, it became adorned with detachment.
For those burned by hundreds of separations and feeding on the poison of humiliation,
the complete abandonment of everything is indeed happiness, a cascade of the nectar of nirvāṇa.
Eager for life in the forest, he approached <s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s>
and, emaciated by observances, spoke words that stirred self-restraint and quietude:
'O king, teacher of the orders of class and stage of life, O <s>Pārtha</s>, permit me.
To attain the condition proper to old age, I am going now to the ascetic grove.
This attachment to the taste of worldly pleasures, in men whose minds are devoted to them,
always increases like an undigested thirst.
Touch me with your body fragrant with merit, O son of <s>Dharma</s>.

children.text: svasti te pāhi pṛthivīṃ putravatpaśya ca prajāḥ ||
children.translated_text: May it be well with you; protect the earth, and look upon your subjects as sons.
Make the highest effort in acquiring treasury, fortresses, and military strength.
As guardian of your subjects, keep counsel secret, for the fortunes of kings are easily uprooted.
Having spoken thus, the old man, fasting and thin, smelled the king's head,
and with trembling body became eager to depart.
The king, his eyes filled with tears, begged him with folded hands:
'How can you possibly deserve to go to the forest, abandoning me?
I cannot bear to give up the satisfaction of serving your feet here.
For you, father, who are free from attachment, even this house is an ascetic grove.'

children.text: iti tenārthyamāno 'pi bubudhe na yadā sa tat
children.translated_text: But when, though entreated by him in this way, he did not accept it,
then the sage, the son of <s>Satyavatī</s>, himself came there.
He approached <s>Dharmarāja</s> and, clear-eyed with knowledge, said:
'Let this old king go, O ruler; let him go to the ascetic grove.
For minds that are fully mature, at the proper time detachment is the supreme fruit
of learning, age, wisdom, discrimination, and noble lineage.
When the hair is whitened by old age and interest in objects of sense has grown calm,
I think there is no ornament for embodied beings higher than the ascetic grove.'
When <s>Vyāsa</s> had spoken thus and disappeared, the sorrowing king
said, as if with difficulty, 'So be it,' and the foremost Kuru rejoiced.
He performed an excellent <s>śrāddha</s> for his elders, with <s>Bhīṣma</s> foremost,
and gave abundant, costly gifts approved by the Brahmins.
The sons of <s>Pāṇḍu</s> placed no obstacle before him as he gave,
but <s>Bhīma</s>, his eyes red with anger, spoke to <s>Dhanaṃjaya</s>:

children.text: kilbiṣaṃ yaiḥ kṛtaṃ ghoraṃ purāsmāsu bahucchalam
children.translated_text: 'Those by whom a terrible sin, full of deceit, was formerly done against us,

children.text: kauravāṇāṃ kathaṃ śrāddhe teṣāṃ vittavyayaṃ sahe ||
children.translated_text: how can I endure the spending of wealth at the <s>śrāddha</s> of those <s>Kauravas</s>?
Let wicked <s>Duryodhana</s> go to hell together with his younger brothers.
We ourselves shall perform <s>śrāddha</s> for the son of <s>Śaṃtanu</s>.'
Repeatedly restraining the son of the Wind as he spoke in this way,
<s>Śvetavāhana</s> said, 'This must not be said again.'
Then the king, the son of <s>Ambikā</s>, set out together with <s>Gāndhārī</s>,
with the son of <s>Gavalgana</s> as companion, having addressed the townspeople, and followed by <s>Vidura</s>.
Though she was earnestly entreated by her sons with tear-filled eyes and by her daughters-in-law,
<s>Kuntī</s>, following her brother-in-law, did not abandon her desire for the ascetic forest.
Then <s>Dhṛtarāṣṭra</s>, together with <s>Kuntī</s> and his younger brother,
entered a forest frequented by royal sages, his intention purified.
There he met <s>Śatayūpa</s>, foremost of royal sages,
and, wearing matted hair and bark garments, he practiced austerity for a long time together with his younger brother.
That man, emaciated by severe observances, the great sages such as <s>Nārada</s>...
They came to see him, who had reached the state of having accomplished his task and was worthy to be seen.
Those great chariot-warriors, accompanied by all the women of the <s>Bharatas</s>,
left their great fourfold army at the edge of the forest.
With white parasols and yak-tail fans set aside, going on foot,
they entered the ascetic grove frequented by <s>Dhṛtarāṣṭra</s>.
They bowed to the son of <s>Ambikā</s>, to their mother, and likewise to <s>Sañjaya</s>,
and, grief-stricken on seeing them reduced to sinews alone, they fell into a swoon.
<s>Dhṛtarāṣṭra</s> too, when the king had been announced by <s>Sañjaya</s>,

children.text: papraccha kuśalaṃ kośe paure janapade tathā ||
children.translated_text: asked after the welfare of the treasury, the townsmen, and the countryside.
Then <s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s>, after asking the aged <s>Kuru</s> about the growth of his austerity,

children.text: viduraḥ kveti papraccha sa ca pṛṣṭastamabravīt ||
children.translated_text: asked, 'Where is <s>Vidura</s>?' and, when questioned, he replied to him:
'Living on air, with limbs remaining only as bone, moving as he wills, and unclothed,

children.text: viduro 'sminvane putra dṛśyate na ca dṛśyate ||
children.translated_text: <s>Vidura</s>, my son, is seen and is not seen in this forest.'
When <s>Dhṛtarāṣṭra</s> had spoken thus, by chance there approached
<s>Vidura</s>, his limbs smeared with dust, emaciated, his face no larger than a bilva fruit.
Seeing the people in the hermitage, he was intent on fleeing,
and <s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s>, alone and with tear-filled eyes, ran after him.
<s>Vidura</s>, now visible and now invisible, through his disregard for him,
showed the equality that the passionless have toward grass and toward a king.
Taking shelter at the root of a tree, his body one of knowledge and seeming to blaze,
he was addressed by the king, who wished to speak with him: 'I am <s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s>.'
Silent, with unblinking eyes and his inner desire consumed, he looked at him,
and with his sight, breath, and senses he suddenly and quickly entered that very man.
When <s>Vidura</s> had left his body like a cast-off slough and entered him, the king,
abandoning his royal disposition, became filled with knowledge.
Then, when <s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s> set out to burn the body of <s>Kṣattṛ</s>,
sky-going perfected beings, accomplished in knowledge, restrained him there.
Then the king returned, reported all that to <s>Dhṛtarāṣṭra</s>,
and, free from grief, remained with his younger brothers near his mother.
Eating fruit and sleeping on the ground, he passed the night,
and in the morning gave jewels and gold to the Brahmins as they desired.
Having bowed to the foremost <s>Kuru</s>, who was seated with royal seers,
he saw the son of <s>Satyavatī</s>, a mass of splendor, who had arrived.
<s>Vyāsa</s> too honored the son of <s>Dharma</s>, who stood with folded hands,
and praised the venerable accomplishment of <s>Kṣattṛ</s> through the <s>yati-dharma</s> (discipline of ascetics).
Then, entreated by the aged kṣatriya, by <s>Gāndhārī</s>, and by <s>Pṛthā</s>,
<s>Vyāsa</s> showed all the kings, together with the <s>Kauravas</s>, who had gone to the other world,
to the women of the <s>Kurus</s> in the water of the heavenly river.
The virtuous women too followed them in aerial cars, abandoning their bodies.
Then the king, the son of <s>Dharma</s>, stayed there for a month in that place frequented by the Seven Seers,
and, urged by the aged <s>Kuru</s>, set out for the city.
Going with divisions of chariots, horses, and elephants, sighing again and again,
he entered the capital with difficulty, as though unwilling.
Then, while <s>Dharmarāja</s> was ruling the earth according to <s>dharma</s> (righteous order),
in the course of time the divine sage <s>Nārada</s> arrived.
Asked about the story of <s>Dhṛtarāṣṭra</s> and honored by the king,
he said, 'That royal seer, O king, has reached the supreme state.
For a year he lived on air, and for another year he abandoned food;
his face became like a ball, hard to recognize, and he was emaciated.
Then, desiring liberation, that sage, free from ritual action, gave up the sacred fires;
they too remained in the forest among the old trees.

children.text: tatra priyāsakho rājā kuntyā saha mahāmatiḥ
children.translated_text: There the wise king, with his dear companions and with <s>Kuntī</s>,

children.text: vanaṃ prajvalitaṃ dṛṣṭvā samādhiṃ vidadhe param ||
children.translated_text: seeing the forest ablaze, entered the highest <s>samādhi</s> (meditative absorption).
Unencompassed, yet all-encompassing, pure, with their activities fallen away by themselves,
and with the enclosure of the cosmic egg opened wide, they went to the supreme light.
Thus for them the tree of knowledge bore fruit: tranquility was its sprout,
complete renunciation its tender leaves, and the radiance of the heart its flower.

children.text: tato dāvāgninā tena dagdhāste bandhunā yathā
children.translated_text: Then they were burned by that forest fire, as though by a kinsman;
but <s>Sañjaya</s>, emaciated by vows, went to the snowy mountain.
Hearing this, the son of <s>Pāṇḍu</s> was filled with the fire of grief,

children.text: śuśoca sānujaḥ kuntīṃ sasutaṃ ca kurūdvaham ||
children.translated_text: and with his younger brothers he mourned <s>Kuntī</s> and the bearer of the <s>Kuru</s> line together with his son.

children.text: tataḥ prayāte devarṣau rājā kṛtvā jalakriyām
children.translated_text: Then, when the divine seer had departed, the king performed the water rite,
and, with them in mind, gave abundant and inexhaustible wealth.
After that, taking hold of courage and casting off the grief born in his body,
he meditated on the insubstantiality of worldly existence and took refuge in discernment.

children.text: bhāvāḥ svabhāvaviśarārava eva teṣu saktaṃ mano na virahe sahate 'nutāpam
children.translated_text: Beings are by nature fragile; when the mind is attached to them, it cannot bear remorse at separation.

children.text: tatsarvathā priyaviyogaviṣāhatānāṃ śāntyai sudhā tanubhṛtāṃ vipulo vivekaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Therefore, for embodied beings struck by the poison of separation from the dear, broad discernment is nectar for their peace.
Having bowed to <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> and to <s>Nara</s>, the best of men,
to the goddess <s>Sarasvatī</s> and to <s>Vyāsa</s>, one should then proclaim the <s>Jaya</s>.
When <s>Dharmarāja</s>, foremost among earth-bearing kings, was ruling the earth,
in the twenty-sixth year, illustrious sages went to <s>Dvārakā</s>.
Seeing them, with <s>Kauśika</s> at their head, the foremost <s>Vṛṣṇis</s>,
overwhelmed by delight and arrogance, dressed <s>Sāmba</s> in the guise of a bride and asked:

children.text: api putraḥ sutā vāsyā bhaviṣyati munīśvarāḥ
children.translated_text: 'Will a son or a daughter be born to this woman, O lords of sages?'
Hearing that, they said, 'From her there will arise the death of the clan.'
'A club called the <s>brahmadaṇḍa</s>.' Having said this, they vanished from sight.
Then <s>Sāmba</s> brought forth an iron club, compact and hard as a thunderbolt.
The one so named, out of fear, quickly ground it to powder and threw it into the ocean.
The omniscient foe of <s>Kaiṭabha</s>, knowing what had happened and understanding that the destruction of the <s>Vṛṣṇis</s> was near,
went away with delight in a pilgrimage to the sacred fords.
Then the discus, fierce as the blazing disk of the sun and hostile to the enemies of the gods,
and the chariot and golden banner suddenly disappeared.
Then, when the sun had the dimness of a cat and its orb was covered by headless trunks,
and when the wind blew, striking all the quarters in every direction,
a shaven-headed being with a misshapen face, in every house of the <s>Yādavas</s>,
showed his face and went away; though sought by speech, he was not seen.
In the houses, the cry of the mynah birds became the sound of a shrieking man,
and even the royal road was filled with the cries of vultures and jackals.
At that time there was also unnatural birth among the animals,
and in the treasuries bound with gold, the jewels split open of themselves.
Though these terrible portents had arisen, they were still without suspicion.

children.text: babhūvurvṛṣṇayo bhānti na hi nāśeṣu buddhayaḥ
children.translated_text: The <s>Vṛṣṇis</s> remained confident; for minds do not shine clearly at times of destruction.
Then, when <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> had reached <s>Prabhāsa</s>, the <s>Yādavas</s> and <s>Vṛṣṇis</s>
came to that very place and held a great festival.
There in the varied gardens they sported happily,
absorbed in the pleasures of song and dance, marked by the eye of Time.
Then, while the <s>Vṛṣṇi</s> clan was engaged in drinking sport,
a quarrel arose, bound up with battle, between <s>Śaineya</s> and <s>Kṛtavarman</s>.

children.text: hārdikyaṃ sātyakiḥ prāha suptahā sauptiko bhavān ||
children.translated_text: <s>Sātyaki</s> said to the <s>Hārdikya</s>, 'You are a killer of sleepers, a man of the night attack.'

children.text: sa tamūce tvayā prāyagato bhūriśravā hataḥ
children.translated_text: He replied to him, 'By you <s>Bhūriśravas</s>, who had gone to <s>Prāya</s>, was killed.'
From such a dispute a very terrible battle arose among them.
From the clusters of reeds that had earlier grown from that thunderbolt-club,
even grass there became a <s>brahmadaṇḍa</s>, swollen with maddened force,
suddenly turning into clubs for the destruction of the <s>Andhakas</s> and <s>Vṛṣṇis</s>.
The drinking ground that had been for them a festival for the eyes of women
became the dreadful banquet hall of Death's slaughter-feast.
When <s>Sāmba</s>, <s>Gada</s>, strong-armed <s>Cārudeṣṇa</s>, <s>Pradyumna</s>, <s>Kṛtavarman</s>,

children.text: aniruddhe ca śaineye nihate paśyato hareḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Aniruddha</s>, and <s>Śaineya</s> had been killed before <s>Hari</s>'s eyes,

children.text: vṛtte vṛṣṇikṣaye ghore strīśeṣā yādave kule ||
children.translated_text: and when the terrible destruction of the <s>Vṛṣṇis</s> had occurred, the <s>Yādava</s> clan had only women left.
<s>Dvārakā</s> seemed to weep with streams of tears from broken necklaces.
Then <s>Śauri</s>, overcome with grief, going to see <s>Haladhara</s>,
sent <s>Dāruka</s> to report that matter to <s>Savyasācin</s>.
Taking <s>Babhru</s> with him to protect the women from robbers, <s>Keśava</s>
went, took leave of his father, and approached the son of <s>Rohiṇī</s>.
Then <s>Madhusūdana</s> saw coming out of his mouth
a white serpent with a thousand heads, like a white mountain.
Then, together with serpents headed by <s>Vāsuki</s> who had come forward to meet him,
he saw him enter the ocean and again be honored by <s>Varuṇa</s>.
<s>Janārdana</s>, knower of the course of all beings, did not grieve.
For when existence comes to nonexistence, how can there be permanence among things?
When <s>Balabhadra</s> had joined the abode of <s>Ananta</s>, along with the forest,
the yogin entered it and slept, fixing the retention of his breath.
Him, absorbed in his own light, a hunter, mistaking him for a deer,
struck in the sole of the foot with a sharp-tipped arrow.
<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, taken for a black antelope, was struck by the hunter's arrow,
and entered the eternal supreme abode called <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>.
When <s>Govinda</s>, together with <s>Śrī</s>, had entered <s>Viṣṇu</s>,

children.text: viṣṇuṃ praviṣṭe govinde babhūva kṣubhitaṃ jagat
children.translated_text: while he was being honored by gods, perfected beings, seers, and gandharvas, the world was shaken.
Meanwhile, when <s>Dāruka</s> had reported the destruction of the <s>Yādavas</s>,

children.text: śokaṃ trāsaṃ ca dainyaṃ ca bhejire pāṇḍavāḥ param
children.translated_text: the <s>Pāṇḍavas</s> fell into extreme grief, terror, and misery.
Then, at <s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s>'s command, <s>Śvetavāhana</s>
went to <s>Dvārakā</s>, accompanied by <s>Dāruka</s> himself and faint with grief.
He reached the city of the <s>Yādavas</s>, like a lotus pond without lotuses,
bereft of the lion-like <s>Vṛṣṇis</s>, like a cave in the <s>Himālaya</s> bereft of lions.
Seeing it painfully touched by heaps of calamities and misfortunes,
he entered to see the grief-stricken father of the foe of <s>Kaṃsa</s>.
He was surrounded by the women of the <s>Vṛṣṇis</s>, loud with star-like lamentation.
There were sixteen thousand women, the wives of the lotus-lord.
Seeing the father of <s>Saubhadra</s>, bewildered and trembling with fear,
and seeing <s>Vasudeva</s> lying on the ground and lamenting, <s>Pārtha</s> too, overcome by grief,
fell down as if split by a thunderbolt.

children.text: kva rāmaḥ kva ca govindaḥ kva pradyumnaḥ kva sātyakiḥ
children.translated_text: 'Where is <s>Rāma</s>? Where is <s>Govinda</s>? Where is <s>Pradyumna</s>? Where is <s>Sātyaki</s>?
Ah, this power of Fate is hard to overcome,' said <s>Arjuna</s>.
Where formerly there was the dense sound of jewel bracelets, dancing, and song,
unceasing, with cascades of delight for the ears,
there itself <s>Bībhatsu</s>, hearing the sound of the <s>Vṛṣṇi</s> women weeping,
passed a night from which prosperity had entirely departed.

children.text: tataḥ prātaḥ priyasuto vasudevaḥ priyāṃ tanum
children.translated_text: Then in the morning <s>Vasudeva</s>, dear in his son, abandoned his dear body,
followed by the women headed by <s>Devakī</s>.
Then, overwhelmed by grief for all the foremost <s>Sāttvatas</s>,
<s>Pārtha</s> cremated their bodies and performed the water rite.
Then <s>Kuntī</s>'s son took <s>Vajra</s>, <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>'s grandson,
and the beloved women of the <s>Vṛṣṇis</s>, and set out with <s>Dāruka</s> following.
Then <s>Dvāravatī</s>, with the circling arms of swelling waves,
With a terrible loud laughter of conches, the ocean, abode of makaras, carried it away.
When the city of the <s>Vṛṣṇis</s> had quickly been destroyed by the ocean, as if from greed for its jewels,
the sorrowing people said, 'Everything follows the person.'
<s>Śvetavāhana</s>, taking the wives of the lion-like <s>Vṛṣṇis</s>,
set out for <s>Indraprastha</s> and reached a difficult, terrible forest.
There bandits, cowherds, strong men living by cattle,
saw the women of the <s>Sāttvatas</s>, fortunate heavenly women never seen before,
their garments massed with flashes of jewel-rays trembling like lightning,
and, overcome by greed, rose up to seize them by force.
Seeing those cowherds rushing upon them, armed with fierce clubs,
the bearer of the <s>Gāṇḍīva</s> bow angrily strung <s>Gāṇḍīva</s>.
Yet even he, destroyer of enemies, had been struck by the power of Time;
as his arrows failed, he had no strength at all to draw the bowstring.
The bow-staff was no longer obedient to him and brought him the deepest pain,
like a beautiful young bride belonging to an old and poor man.
As he was scorched by the fire of anger and knit his brows in vain,
his arrows became powerless, like servants of an undisciplined master.

children.text: te divyāstragaṇāḥ kvāpi jagmurutsṛjya taṃ mṛdhe
children.translated_text: Those hosts of divine missiles went somewhere else, abandoning him in battle,
disregarding the contact of the string, like rogues disregarding a penniless friend.
Deprived of his great shafts, he heaved deep sighs,
his face bent down in embarrassment, like a generous man whose treasury is exhausted.
Then, when <s>Pārtha</s> was helpless there because all his weapons had failed,
the senseless forest-dwellers carried off the women of the <s>Vṛṣṇi</s> citizens.
But toward the principal women they had no boldness;
how can a low, unworthy man have force against the most worthy?

children.text: taiḥ prasahya hṛte straiṇe bhagnamāno dhanaṃjayaḥ
children.translated_text: When the female company had been violently seized by them, <s>Dhanaṃjaya</s>, his pride broken,
set out, casting resentful glances at his own staff-like arms.
'Alas, powerful is the goddess Impermanence in this world!
Alas, the mastery of beings ends in utter worthlessness!
Alas, Time consumes all! Alas, the world has strange ripenings!'
So the people said in grief: '<s>Vijaya</s> has been conquered by cowherds.'
Fie on the wondrous fragility of the Creator,
whose sport of impermanent display brings about the delusion of bewilderment!
He by whom <s>Indra</s> and the others were shattered at <s>Khāṇḍava</s>,
he by whom the foe of <s>Tripura</s> was pleased in battle in the form of the <s>Kirāta</s>,

children.text: jitvā tamapi gopālā varākāḥ suhṛdaṃ hareḥ
children.translated_text: even him, the friend of <s>Hari</s>, wretched cowherds defeated,
and they carried off the wives of <s>Viṣṇu</s>. Fie on the irresistible force of Time!
Taking <s>Revatī</s>, <s>Rukmiṇī</s>, <s>Satyabhāmā</s>, and also <s>Jāmbavatī</s>,
as well as <s>Vajra</s>, the grandson of the enemy of <s>Kaṃsa</s>, and the other <s>Yadu</s> women,
<s>Phalguna</s>, grieving, entered <s>Indraprastha</s>,
surrounded on all sides by crowds of citizens with tears in their eyes.

children.text: rājye nidhāya tatraiva vajraṃ yāte dhanaṃjaye
children.translated_text: When <s>Dhanaṃjaya</s> had installed <s>Vajra</s> there in the kingdom,
the queens who followed <s>Satyabhāmā</s> entered the fire out of grief.
<s>Kirīṭī</s>, afflicted by separation from the <s>Vṛṣṇis</s>, went toward <s>Hastināpura</s>,
and in the forest he saw <s>Vyāsa</s>, who knew the higher and lower states of beings.
He told him of his terrible sorrow, the destruction of the <s>Vṛṣṇi</s> clan,
and his own defeat by cowherds on the road, though he had taken up his bow.
The sage, a treasury of knowledge, comforted him as he fainted and said to him:
'My son, all this is the unfolding of the sports of Time.
Understanding, powers, enjoyments, majesties, strengths, and virtues
are in every way brought by a fraction of Time to the state of being only a memory.
Surely sages would not set their minds on the abandonment of everything
if worldly existence did not have, as its single final flavor, its own end.'
Thus addressed by the sage, <s>Pārtha</s> went to <s>Hastināpura</s>,
thinking on the majesty of the lion of the <s>Vṛṣṇis</s> and deeply overwhelmed.
Having bowed to <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> and to <s>Nara</s>, the best of men,
and to the goddess <s>Sarasvatī</s> and <s>Vyāsa</s>, one should then proclaim the <s>Jaya</s>.
Then, after hearing of the destruction of the <s>Vṛṣṇis</s> from <s>Dhanaṃjaya</s>,
the son of <s>Dharma</s> sighed and said, 'Homage to mighty Time.'
Together with his brothers, he entered the yoga made by the renunciation of everything,
having given the kingdom of <s>Duryodhana</s> to <s>Yuyutsu</s>, who was worthy through his virtues.
He established <s>Parikṣit</s>, the son of <s>Abhimanyu</s>, in his own kingdom,
and, true to his command, instructed <s>Subhadrā</s> to protect him.
The knower of dharma entrusted him to the subjects and to the twice-born,

children.text: śrāddhaṃ vidhāya bandhubhyaḥ puṇyāmiṣṭiṃ ca naiṣṭhikīm ||
children.translated_text: performed the <s>śrāddha</s> for his kinsmen, and also a meritorious final <s>iṣṭi</s>.
He cast the sacred fires into the water and consoled the sorrowing citizens.
Taking leave of the goddess Earth, accompanied by his younger brothers and with <s>Draupadī</s> as companion,
<s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s>, joined to yoga and renouncing everything, set out.
Then the blessed Fire himself came together with them,
and from <s>Pārtha</s> he took <s>Gāṇḍīva</s> and the two inexhaustible great quivers.
One dog followed them, though it was carefully warded off.
Then they slowly reached the south-western direction.

children.text: dṛṣṭvā tatra samudreṇa bhṛtāṃ dvāravatīṃ jalaiḥ
children.translated_text: Seeing there <s>Dvāravatī</s> filled with the waters of the ocean,
they proceeded toward the northern quarter, having circumambulated the earth.
Crossing the <s>Himālaya</s>, they reached the sandy ocean,
and saw <s>Meru</s>, whose <s>Nandana</s> was embraced by lofty peaks.
On that road, without shelter and without support, hard to cross,
the daughter of <s>Drupada</s>, her body delicate as śirīṣa blossoms, fell.

children.text: tāṃ yātajīvitāṃ dṛṣṭvā bhīmaḥ prāha yudhiṣṭhiram
children.translated_text: Seeing that her life had departed, <s>Bhīma</s> said to <s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s>:
O king, this daughter of the king of <s>Pāñcāla</s> has fallen upon the ground.
Even after reflecting on it, I see no fault at all in her.
Why has she abandoned the discipline of austerity and come to death?
Hearing this, the son of <s>Dharma</s> spoke without turning his face back:
She always had an excessive partiality for <s>Arjuna</s>.
When the ruler had said this, <s>Sahadeva</s> fell to the ground.
When he had fallen, the king, questioned by <s>Bhīma</s>, spoke again:
This man, through pride in his wisdom, thought the world dull-witted.
When the son of <s>Dharma</s> had said this, <s>Nakula</s> fell upon the earth.
Then the king, questioned by <s>Bhīma</s>, spoke again while still going on:

children.text: rūpamānī smareṇāpi spardhāmeṣa na ca kṣamī ||
children.translated_text: This man was proud of his beauty, and could not bear rivalry even with <s>Smara</s>.
When the king, as he went on, had said this, <s>Dhanaṃjaya</s> fell.
Again, questioned by <s>Bhīma</s>, the lord of the earth said:
Proud of his heroism, this man acted slackly on the field of battle.
Saying this, the king went on, his understanding undiminished.
Then <s>Bhīma</s>, having fallen, said to him, 'I have fallen.'
He said, 'O <s>Bhīma</s>, you had pride in strength, and you ate much.'
Then he went on alone, followed only by a dog.
<s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s> saw <s>Indra</s> himself arriving in a chariot.
When <s>Śakra</s> said, 'O king, come to my city,' he replied:

children.text: śunā virahitaḥ svargaṃ saśarīro na kāmaye ||
children.translated_text: Without the dog I do not desire heaven in this very body.
The lord of the gods said to him, 'How can dogs have access to heaven?
Who other than you would say, "Let the dog mount the heavenly seat"?'
Then the king said to him, 'How could I endure abandoning one devoted to me?
For a cruel man who hates the devoted, how can there be access to heaven?
If I have any merit at all, O lord of the gods, then by that merit

children.text: yātu svargaṃ sadehaḥ svā nainaṃ tyaktuṃ samutsahe ||
children.translated_text: let this dog go bodily to heaven; I cannot bring myself to abandon him.
The good declare that abandoning one who is devoted is equal to killing a woman
and to stealing a Brahmin's property, containing the essence of every sin.'
When <s>Dharmarāja</s> had spoken thus, <s>Dharma</s> abandoned the form of a dog
and said to him, 'Son, I am pleased with this good conduct of yours.

children.text: dṛṣṭo 'si pāthaso hetoḥ purā dvaitavane mayā
children.translated_text: Long ago in the <s>Dvaita</s> forest, I tested you on account of water.

children.text: svasti te vraja bhūpāla saśarīraḥ surālayam ||
children.translated_text: May it be well with you. Go, O king, bodily to the abode of the gods.'
Thus instructed by his father, he mounted a broad, shining aerial car,
a stairway of merit, and entered the mansion of the gods.
Honored together by the gods and by sages such as <s>Nārada</s>,
he shone among the star-like royal sages like the sun.

children.text: tataḥ sa śakramavadadbhrātaro yatra me sthitāḥ
children.translated_text: Then he said to <s>Śakra</s>, 'Where my brothers are staying,

children.text: śyāmā ca yatra dayitā tatra vāso mamepsitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and where my beloved dark lady is, there is the dwelling I desire.'
The thousand-eyed god said to him, 'Do not fall into human feeling.
You have attained the supreme state, inaccessible even to royal sages.'
Though the son of <s>Dharma</s> was repeatedly addressed in this way with effort by the wielder of the thunderbolt,
he said again and again, 'I wish to reach my brothers.'
Having bowed to <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> and to <s>Nara</s>, the best of men,
to the goddess <s>Sarasvatī</s> and to <s>Vyāsa</s>, one should then proclaim the <s>Jaya</s>.
Then <s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s> saw the Kuru king, adorned with heavenly splendor,
brilliant with diadem and armlets, and resembling <s>Śakra</s>.

children.text: taṃ vīkṣya sānujaṃ tatra jātamanyuḥ śatakratum
children.translated_text: Seeing him there with his younger brothers, he grew angry and addressed <s>Śatakratu</s>:
'Blessings to the gods; let this salutation be for heaven.
Where wicked <s>Duryodhana</s>, the cause of the destruction of the earth,
shines on the highest seat, lofty on the summit of <s>Sumeru</s>,

children.text: na tatra mama vāso 'sti vrajāmyeṣa namo 'stu te
children.translated_text: there is no dwelling for me. I am going; homage to you.

children.text: yatra me bhrātaraḥ śūrāstatra vāso mamādhunā ||
children.translated_text: Where my heroic brothers are, there now is my dwelling.'
As the king was speaking thus, the gods then said to a divine messenger,
'Go toward his brothers,' addressing one swift as wind and mind.
Going at once by the path indicated by the divine messenger,
he saw dreadful beings dwelling in the interior of hell.
It was slippery with masses of hair, blood, flesh, gore, and fat,
strewn with many soaked corpses and crowded with worms.
It was surrounded everywhere by the beaks of crows, vultures, cranes, and owls,
and packed with hundreds of close-packed heaps, with no break in the stench of corpses.
Its banks were of heated sand, with saws, stones, and cooking tortures,
terrible with red oil, vats of fat, peaks, and silk-cotton trees.
It was frightening with razor-thorns, harsh spikes, and pillars of flame,
its sands filled with the foul pus of the heated <s>Vaitaraṇī</s>.
There men and women, cut by the sword-leaved forest, made cries.
There, in that dreadful thicket of darkness, the son of <s>Dharma</s> heard
the cry of sinners being boiled, a sound terrible enough to break courage:
'Stay here for a single moment, O king; do not turn back.
When we are touched by the cool winds of your merit, the darkness does not afflict us.
We are your Pāṇḍava brothers, beginning with <s>Bhīma</s>.

children.text: kṛṣṇā ceyaṃ varārohā mahiṣī vallabhā satī
children.translated_text: And this is <s>Kṛṣṇā</s>, the fair-hipped one, your dear and virtuous queen.'
Hearing that piteous speech, the king was as though split open by a thunderbolt.
He stood right there, unwavering, condemning the badly fashioned sport of fate.
He said, 'Alas, the judgment of the gods is ruined by lack of reflection,
since they have disregarded in this suffering these people devoted to <s>dharma</s> (righteousness).

children.text: ayaṃ mohaḥ prasādo vā viveko nāyamīdṛśaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Is this delusion, or is it favor? Discernment of this kind is no discernment.

children.text: vibudhānāṃ na jānanti ye dharmasya vyatikramam
children.translated_text: Those who do not recognize the gods' transgression of <s>dharma</s> (righteousness)--
is this confusion, a dream, or illusion? What is this?' Thus he thought.
Divine messenger, I do not know whose wicked behavior this is.

children.text: ihaivāhaṃ sthito gaccha na me svargeṇa kāraṇam ||
children.translated_text: I will remain right here. Go; I have no need of heaven.

children.text: pūjyante yatra durvṛttā viśasyante nu sādhavaḥ
children.translated_text: Where the wicked are honored and the good are slaughtered,
when <s>Dharmarāja</s> had spoken thus, the divine messenger went to the lord of the gods

children.text: gatvā vyajijñapatsarvaṃ sa ca tūṣṇīṃ samāyayau
children.translated_text: and reported everything; and he too came silently.

children.text: prāpte surādhipe tatra saha dharmādibhiḥ suraiḥ ||
children.translated_text: When the lord of the gods arrived there together with <s>Dharma</s> and the other gods,
nothing inauspicious was seen, and a holy wind blew.
Then the lord of the gods said to the despondent son of <s>Dharma</s>:
This is untrue; this was an illusion displayed here by me.
Such a sight must necessarily be seen by kings whose deeds are mixed.
Because of your contact with a trace of untruth in the killing of <s>Droṇa</s>,
come, see your own brothers established in their divine station,
and <s>Pāñcālī</s> in heavenly splendor, and your sons who have attained immortality.
When the king of the gods had spoken thus, <s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s>, freed from sorrow,
bathed, at <s>Dharma</s>'s word, in the heaven-Gaṅgā's water, bright as the sky,

children.text: utsṛjya mānuṣaṃ bhāvaṃ puṇyāṃ surasabhāṃ yayau ||
children.translated_text: and, casting off his human state, went to the holy assembly of the gods.
There, amid the graceful dancing of apsarases and gandharvas and kiṃnaras singing,
he saw his own younger brothers mounted upon their proper stations.

children.text: maṇḍale ca raveḥ karṇaṃ svayamindreṇa darśitam
children.translated_text: And he saw <s>Karṇa</s> in the disk of the sun, shown to him by <s>Indra</s> himself,
and <s>Abhimanyu</s>, whose lovely form surpassed <s>Manmatha</s>,
that son of <s>Soma</s> named <s>Varcas</s>, in the lunar sphere,
and King <s>Dhṛtarāṣṭra</s>, directly the king of the gandharvas,

children.text: vasuṃ śāntanavaṃ bhīṣmaṃ guruṃ droṇaṃ bṛhaspatim
children.translated_text: <s>Bhīṣma</s>, son of <s>Śantanu</s>, as a Vasu, and his teacher <s>Droṇa</s> as <s>Bṛhaspati</s>,
and <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, lord of the universe, bearing conch, discus, and mace.

children.text: yadaṃśā bhuvi ye jātāstāṃśca dṛṣṭvā tadāśrayān
children.translated_text: Seeing also those whose portions had been born on earth, now abiding in their own sources,
the son of <s>Dharma</s> attained everlasting bliss, worthy of reverence from the dwellers in <s>Nandana</s>,
a treasure-house of splendors, the station fit for <s>Hariścandra</s>.
Then, honored on every side by kings such as <s>Nahuṣa</s>, <s>Dilīpa</s>, <s>Dhundhumāra</s>, <s>Sagara</s>, <s>Bhagīratha</s>, <s>Rāma</s>, and <s>Kārtavīrya</s>,
that moon among kings, of bright conduct, shone resplendent.
Having heard in this way the story of the <s>Bhārata</s> recited by <s>Vaiśampāyana</s>,
<s>Janamejaya</s>, his snake sacrifice completed, became satisfied.
When this had been told by the Sūta to the inhabitants of <s>Naimiṣāraṇya</s>,
those headed by <s>Śaunaka</s>, hearing it, remained filled with joy.
Having bowed to <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, and to <s>Nara</s>, the best of men,
to the goddess <s>Sarasvatī</s> and to <s>Vyāsa</s>, one should then proclaim the victory.

children.text: muniḥ punātu vo vyāsaḥ sadā saṃnihitā sukhe
children.translated_text: May the sage <s>Vyāsa</s> purify you, ever present in blessing,
he whose pure, honey-sweet <s>Sarasvatī</s> flows in the three paths.
Asked again by <s>Śaunaka</s> in <s>Naimiṣa</s>, <s>Laumaharṣaṇi</s>
spoke of the wondrous manifestation on earth of the foe of <s>Kaiṭabha</s>.
Having heard the story of the <s>Bhārata</s>, the delighted <s>Janamejaya</s>
respectfully asked <s>Vaiśampāyana</s> about the Vaiṣṇava lineage.

children.text: sa pṛṣṭaḥ pṛthuvaṃśena pārthivena kathāṃ hareḥ
children.translated_text: Asked by the king descended from <s>Pṛthu</s>, he reverently bowed to the Lord,

children.text: jagāda jagatāṃ hetuṃ praṇamya prayataḥ prabhum ||
children.translated_text: the cause of the worlds, and told the story of <s>Hari</s>.
First the imperishable blessed <s>Viṣṇu</s> created the waters.

children.text: tāsu vīryaṃ narākhyāsu yena nārāyaṇaḥ smṛtaḥ ||
children.translated_text: In those, called naras, he placed his seed, whereby he is remembered as <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>.
Then there was a golden egg, in which <s>Prajāpati</s> was born.
He created the Prajāpatis headed by <s>Manu</s> and including <s>Kardama</s>,
and <s>Dakṣa</s>, through whose daughter's descendants all beings came to be.
He separately ordained kingdoms bearing names beginning with <s>Soma</s>.
Once there was a son of <s>Aṅga</s>, the Prajāpati of <s>Atri</s>'s lineage,
born from <s>Sunīthā</s>, daughter of <s>Mṛtyu</s>, a destroyer of established order.
There was a king named <s>Kharva</s>, impure in mind through sin,
like rebellion embodied, because his subjects had turned away from proper rule.
Though he was conciliated many times, when he did not come under control,
then the sages restrained that exceedingly powerful man and struck him down.
Those sages, filled with the fire of anger, churned his left thigh.
From it there arose a short black man, trembling with fear.
Told by <s>Atri</s>, "Sit down," he became the progenitor of the <s>Niṣādas</s>.
Then the sages churned the right hand of <s>Vena</s>.
From that lotus-hand, with copper-red finger-petals, there arose
glorious <s>Pṛthu</s>, broad-eyed, like the grandsire <s>Brahmā</s>.
His bow <s>Ājagava</s>, as he showered gold, shone forth
like a mass of his own flames, the radiance of a blazing fire.
By his favor <s>Vena</s> went to heaven; then <s>Vainya</s>, first of kings,
was approached by the oceans themselves and worshiped with jewels.
In water and on mountain, his passage met with no broken favor.
The newly arisen sūtas, māgadhas, and bards praised him.
For the livelihood of his subjects, the earth was commanded by that vigorous king.

children.text: bhītā dudrāva gaurbhūtvā dhanvī tāmādravatsa ca ||
children.translated_text: Frightened, she fled in the form of a cow; and he, bow in hand, ran after her.
She swiftly fled through all the worlds, as far as the world of <s>Brahmā</s>,
but, turning her face back, saw that same man behind her with weapon raised.
Seeing no refuge, she spoke to him with joined palms:

children.text: kopaṃ jahi mahīpāla yoṣitaṃ parirakṣa mām ||
children.translated_text: Abandon your anger, O guardian of the earth; protect me, a woman.

children.text: vinā dharitrīṃ tiṣṭhanti prajānātha kathaṃ prajāḥ
children.translated_text: Without the earth, O lord of subjects, how can subjects continue to exist?
Hearing this speech of the Earth, the king, his anger gone, said:
This undertaking of mine against you is for the sake of my subjects' livelihood.
For the protection of the lives of many, the killing of one is praised.
"Having expanded myself, I will support the creatures,

children.text: na cedvitare lokānāṃ vṛttiṃ putrī ca me bhava ||
children.translated_text: if you do not grant livelihood to the worlds; and become my daughter."
Thus commanded by the king, the bowed Earth said,

children.text: ahaṃ vṛttiṃ vidhāsyāmi prajānāṃ tvatsutā satī ||
children.translated_text: "I will provide livelihood for the creatures, while being your daughter.
Make the regions level, lord, for they are uneven with masses of rock;
then all this will come forth from me like milk that has flowed."
Hearing this, the widely famed <s>Pṛthu</s>
split apart the great heaps of stone with the tip of his bow, by which the earth became clearly level.

children.text: tataḥ sasyāni pṛthivīṃ svanāmāṅkāṃ dudoha saḥ
children.translated_text: Then he milked the earth, stamped with his own name, for crops,
making <s>Svāyaṃbhuva Manu</s> the calf and the hollow of his joined hands the vessel.

children.text: śrūyate munibhirdugdhā tapo brahma ca bhūḥ purā
children.translated_text: It is heard that in ancient times the earth was milked by sages for tapas and brahma,
with <s>Soma</s> as the calf, <s>Bṛhaspati</s> as the milker, and a golden vessel.
And this earth was milked by the ancestors for nectar in a silver vessel,
after taking <s>Yama</s> as the calf and <s>Antaka</s> as the milker.
By the serpents she was milked in a gourd vessel for strength-giving poison,

children.text: dhṛtarāṣṭraṃ ca dogdhāraṃ kṛtvā vatsaṃ ca takṣakam ||
children.translated_text: after making <s>Dhṛtarāṣṭra</s> the milker and <s>Takṣaka</s> the calf.
By the asuras the earth was milked in an iron vessel for māyā (illusionary power);
then <s>Prahlāda</s> was the calf, and the dānava <s>Madhu</s> was the milker.

children.text: yakṣairapi purā dugdhā vatsaṃ kṛtvā dhaneśvaram
children.translated_text: In ancient times she was also milked by the yakṣas, after making <s>Dhaneśvara</s> the calf,
for a fearsome milk that causes disappearance, in an unbaked vessel.
She was milked for blood by the rākṣasas, with <s>Sumālin</s> as the calf,
and she was milked for auspicious fragrances by the gandharvas and kinnaras in a lotus vessel.
By the mountains, after taking <s>Meru</s> as the milker in a mountain-vessel,
she was milked for hosts of jewels and herbs, after making <s>Himālaya</s> the calf.

children.text: vṛkṣaiḥ pālāśapātre ca dugdhā puṣpaṃ phalaṃ tataḥ
children.translated_text: By the trees she was then milked for flowers and fruit in a palāśa vessel;
at that time the śāla tree became the milker and the plakṣa tree became the calf.
Thus the earth is always the giver of all things, by the command of <s>Pṛthu</s>,
the victorious first king, whose deed was this wonder.
Hearing this story of <s>Vainya</s>, <s>Janamejaya</s> was amazed,
and asked the sage about the tale of the manvantaras; he too spoke.
"Formerly there was <s>Svāyaṃbhuva Manu</s>; then the seven seers
were <s>Marīci</s>, <s>Atri</s>, <s>Pulastya</s>, and others ... [text lost].
... and the gods were those called <s>Tuṣita</s>.
The third Manu was named <s>Auttama</s>; the seven seers then
were his sons of <s>Vasiṣṭha</s>, and the heavenly beings were the <s>Ṛbhus</s>.
The fourth Manu was <s>Tāmasa</s>, in whose interval the seven seers
were <s>Pṛthu</s>, <s>Gārgya</s>, and others, and the inhabitants of heaven were the <s>Sabhyas</s>.
The fifth Manu was <s>Raivata</s>; the seven seers then
were headed by <s>Vedabāhu</s>, and the gods were the <s>Abhūtarajases</s>.
Then the sixth Manu was <s>Cākṣuṣa</s>; in his interval
there were seven sages headed by <s>Bhṛgu</s>, and the immortals were called the <s>Lekhas</s>.
When these six, rich in sons, had passed away,
the glorious seventh Manu, <s>Vaivasvata</s>, now reigns today.
<s>Kaśyapa</s>, <s>Atri</s>, <s>Vasiṣṭha</s>, <s>Bhāradvāja</s>, then <s>Gautama</s>,
<s>Kauśika</s>, and <s>Jamadagni</s>: these seven are the great seers today.
The deities are the Aśvins, Rudras, Maruts, Vasus, and Ādityas,
and the sons of this Manu are kings headed by <s>Ikṣvāku</s>.
Then <s>Sāvarṇa</s> will be the future Manu; in his interval the seven seers
will be <s>Rāma</s>, <s>Vyāsa</s>, <s>Kṛpa</s>, <s>Ātreya</s>, <s>Drauṇi</s>, <s>Gālava</s>, and <s>Kāśyapa</s>.
Four future Manus called <s>Merusāvarṇa</s> will come after him,

children.text: teṣāṃ nava navāścānye te te saptarṣayaḥ kramāt ||
children.translated_text: and for them, in each case, the corresponding seven seers will be new ones in sequence.

children.text: rocyo nāma manuḥ ṣaṣṭho bhautyākhyaḥ saptamo manuḥ
children.translated_text: The sixth will be a Manu named <s>Rocya</s>, and the seventh a Manu called <s>Bhautya</s>;
these are the fourteen Manus, from whom the manvantaras proceed in order.
Seventy-one complete sets of four yugas, together with the additional portion,
are the measured limit of each of the manvantaras.
When those fourteen manvantaras have passed,
at the end of a kalpa the whole world dissolves within <s>Viṣṇu</s>.
And it comes into being again; thus it turns like a wheel.
Such is the beginningless and endless course marked by hundreds of thousands of kalpa-dissolutions.
Now, in this present interval of the present Manu, this <s>Vaivasvata</s>,
listen to the origin-story in connection with the <s>Harivaṃśa</s>.
The Āditya <s>Vivasvān</s>, born from <s>Kaśyapa</s>, a treasury of lights,
became fierce in form, a dreadful mass of streams of blazing radiance.
"Fortunately this one, while still in the egg, did not die from his own increased splendor";
because his father said this with affection, he became renowned as <s>Mārtaṇḍa</s>.
His beloved was named <s>Saṃjñā</s>, a lotus-pool of beauty,
the daughter of the Prajāpati <s>Tvaṣṭṛ</s>, maker of many marvels.
In her <s>Ravi</s> begot a son, <s>Śrāddhadeva Manu</s>,
and <s>Yama</s> and the daughter <s>Yamunā</s>, so named because they were twins.
Then <s>Saṃjñā</s>, though possessed of steadiness and courage, could not endure
that altered form of the sharp-rayed one, whose radiance was terrible, she herself like a moon-lotus of beauty.
She placed there her own shadow, equal in form and produced by the power of māyā,
and secretly from her husband went to her father's side.

children.text: patyuḥ samīpaṃ gaccheti nirastā tena māninā
children.translated_text: When that proud father dismissed her, saying, "Go to your husband's presence,"
she was ashamed, became a mare, and went to the northern <s>Kurus</s>.
Then, in <s>Chāyā</s>, who had the same appearance as <s>Saṃjñā</s>, another Manu named <s>Sāvarṇa</s>
was born as the son of <s>Ravi</s>, who did not know what had happened."
<s>Śanaiścara</s> was the second, and toward those two
<s>Chāyā</s>, out of maternal affection, showed greater love, not so toward the other two sons.

children.text: kṣamī jyeṣṭho manuḥ sehe tadyamastu na cakṣame
children.translated_text: The eldest, <s>Manu</s>, being patient, endured that; but <s>Yama</s> did not put up with it.
For once, in childhood and by fate, his mother had been struck by the boy.

children.text: sā taṃ śaśāpa kupitā caraṇāste patantviti
children.translated_text: Angered, she cursed him: 'May your feet fall off.'
Hearing that, the frightened <s>Bhāsvān</s>, in anger, was ready to curse her.
Going quickly to <s>Tvaṣṭṛ</s>'s house, he told the story concerning <s>Saṃjñā</s>.
'This splendor of yours is too fierce; virtuous <s>Saṃjñā</s> cannot bear it.

children.text: pracchannaṃ tatra vaḍavā vane carati śādvalam
children.translated_text: Hidden there, in the form of a mare, she grazes on grass in the forest.'
Learning this from <s>Tvaṣṭṛ</s>'s words, and being set by him upon a turning device,
he caused his own radiance to be pared down, eager for the sight of his beloved.

children.text: tejasā tena vidadhe tvaṣṭā cakraṃ sudarśanam ||
children.translated_text: With that radiance <s>Tvaṣṭṛ</s> made the <s>Sudarśana</s> discus,
an aid to the foe of <s>Kaiṭabha</s> in destroying the darkness of the demons.
Then the sun, lover of lotuses, the day-maker, taking on a lovely form,
went and saw his beloved in the forest in the form of a mare.
There, as she struggled, she was mounted by him in horse form,
but she kept her face turned away, afraid of contact with another male.
Then she discharged the seed of <s>Vivasvat</s> with a snort from her nostrils,
and from that were born the twin <s>Nāsatyas</s>, the two <s>Aśvins</s>.

children.text: atha saṃjñā parijñāya saumyaṃ devaṃ divākaram ||
children.translated_text: Then <s>Saṃjñā</s>, recognizing the gentle god, the day-maker,
assumed her own form and went home, following him.
<s>Manu</s> became a lord of creatures, and <s>Yama</s> became lord of the ancestors.
The two <s>Aśvins</s> became physicians of the gods, and <s>Yamunā</s> became a river.
The other <s>Manu</s>, son of <s>Savarṇā</s>, became a future lord of creatures.
Among the planets, slow-moving <s>Śanaiśvara</s> became the seventh.
<s>Ikṣvāku</s>, <s>Śibi</s>, <s>Śaryāti</s>, <s>Nābhāga</s>, and others were sons of <s>Manu</s>.
When they had been born, <s>Manu</s>, desiring a son, performed
a sacrifice to <s>Mitra</s> and <s>Varuṇa</s>; there a daughter of charming radiance was born to him,
named <s>Iḍā</s>, her garments brightened by the sparkle of shining jeweled ornaments.
Lotus-faced, she bowed to <s>Manu</s> and, obedient to his command,
went to the dwelling of <s>Mitra</s> and <s>Varuṇa</s>, saying, 'I am a portion of you.'
Approved by those two as a daughter suited to good conduct,
she received this boon: 'You shall become <s>Manu</s>'s son.'
Then, as she returned and walked with an elephant's gait,
she, doe-eyed, was seen by <s>Budha</s>, son of the Moon.
Through union with him she obtained <s>Purūravas</s> as her own son.
Abandoning her female form, she became a king named <s>Pradyumna</s>.
<s>Utkala</s>, <s>Vinatāśva</s>, and <s>Gaya</s> were his sons.
From <s>Ikṣvāku</s> was born <s>Vikukṣi</s>; his son was <s>Kakutstha</s>.
In that lineage was born <s>Kuvalāśva</s>, who, at <s>Uttaṅka</s>'s word,
struck down the dreadful great demon named <s>Dhundhu</s>, hidden within the sands,
by whose breaths the earth was being burned.
In the line of king <s>Kuvalāśva</s> was born <s>Trayyāruṇi</s>.
By him his son named <s>Satyavrata</s>, because of the abduction of citizens' daughters,
was cursed: 'You are an outcaste,' and, having fallen into that state, lived in the wilderness.
Meanwhile, during a terrible twelve-year period without rain,
<s>Viśvāmitra</s> abandoned his wife, together with her sons, on the ocean shore.

children.text: sāṃ madhyamaṃ gale baddhvā vikretuṃ prastutā sutam ||
children.translated_text: She, tying the middle son by the neck, was preparing to sell him,
but <s>Satyavrata</s>, out of compassion, stopped her and provided her livelihood.
That son of <s>Viśvāmitra</s>, because his neck had been bound, became <s>Gālava</s>.

children.text: sa tyāgādvāritaḥ kiṃ me na piteti purohite
children.translated_text: 'When I prevented that abandonment, what is he to me, if not a father?'
So prince <s>Satyavrata</s> became angry with the priest <s>Vasiṣṭha</s>.
Then, deluded by the curse, he killed his <s>Kāmadhenu</s> as she was wandering
and made her food for the sons of <s>Gādhi</s> and for himself.
Because he angered his father, killed the cow, and ate unsanctified food,
<s>Vasiṣṭha</s> made three spikes of curse fall upon him.
<s>Viśvāmitra</s> gave his father's station to that man, named <s>Triśaṅku</s>,
and became his officiating priest; by him he went bodily to heaven.

children.text: tasya putro hariścandro rājasūye rarāja yaḥ
children.translated_text: His son was <s>Hariścandra</s>, who shone at the <s>Rājasūya</s> sacrifice.
In that family was king <s>Sagara</s>, by whose sons the ocean was made.

children.text: mātuḥ sapatnīdattena jātaḥ saha gareṇa yaḥ
children.translated_text: He was born together with poison, given by his mother's co-wife.
Having conquered the border countries that had earlier harmed his father,
he deprived them of Vedic recitation and the vaṣaṭ-call and marked them with distinguishing signs.
Because their lives had been spared, he made the <s>Kāmbojas</s> have shaven heads.
He made the <s>Śakas</s> half-shaven, and the <s>Pāratas</s> loose-haired.
He assigned beard-marks to the <s>Pahlavas</s>, <s>Yavanas</s>, and others.
In his lineage was <s>Dilīpa</s>; his son was <s>Bhagīratha</s>.
On earth the river <s>Bhāgīrathī</s> attained the status of his daughter.
In his family was born king <s>Rāma</s>, son of <s>Daśaratha</s>.
From his son <s>Kuśa</s> there arose many lineages of royal seers.
This is the lineage of <s>Ikṣvāku</s>; from his brother <s>Nariṣyanta</s>,
the <s>Śakas</s> were born; <s>Ambarīṣa</s>, lord of the earth,
was the son of <s>Nābhāga</s>, and the sons of <s>Vṛṣṇi</s> were the <s>Vṛṣṇis</s>.
The sons of <s>Śibi</s> were bold in battle; <s>Śaryāti</s> had a daughter,
<s>Sukanyā</s>, who was married by <s>Cyavana</s>, and a son who was a border-king.

children.text: ravetī tasya tanayā sa purā sahitastayā ||
children.translated_text: <s>Revatī</s> was his daughter; long ago he, together with her,
went to <s>Brahmaloka</s> to hear music in <s>Brahmā</s>'s presence.
Then, after the time of many ages had passed like the smallest fraction of a moment,
returning, he saw his own city as <s>Dvārakā</s>, surrounded by the <s>Vṛṣṇis</s>.
untouched by the portion of Time because she had dwelt in <s>Brahmaloka</s>.
He gave <s>Revatī</s>, still a young maiden, to <s>Balabhadra</s>.
And after giving away his daughter, he went to a cave of <s>Meru</s> for austerity.
The sixth younger brother of <s>Ikṣvāku</s> was named <s>Riṣṭa</s>; his two sons
were Vaiśyas who attained Brahminhood through the discipline of austerity, stainless.
The seventh was <s>Karūṣa</s>; from <s>Kāruṣa</s> his sons were kings.
And the eighth, <s>Pṛthuka</s>, became a Śūdra because he killed his teacher and a cow.
These were the eight brothers of <s>Ikṣvāku</s>, sons of <s>Manu</s>.
Thus these were the lineage-bearers on earth of <s>Śrāddhadeva Manu</s>.
Asked by the king, in connection with <s>śrāddha</s> (ancestral rite), about the rule concerning the fathers,
the sage spoke; <s>Bhīṣma</s> said to <s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s> at the end of his question:
The fathers, honored in a <s>śrāddha</s> with three funeral cakes for three generations,
nourish living beings, even through their various states of rebirth, as deities.
When, at the time of <s>śrāddha</s>, I raised up a cake for my father <s>Śaṃtanu</s>,
there arose a hand, beautiful with bracelets and soft as a lotus.

children.text: taṃ vilokya mayā piṇḍe kuśeṣveva samarpite
children.translated_text: Seeing it, I nevertheless placed the cake upon the kuśa grass itself;
because I followed the action prescribed by scripture, my father was pleased by that.
Therefore I obtained the excellent boon of death at will.
Then, as <s>Mārkaṇḍeya</s>, instructed by him at that time, arrived,

children.text: apṛcchaṃ daivataṃ śrāddhaṃ phalaṃ ca pitṛyājinām
children.translated_text: I asked about the deities of <s>śrāddha</s> and the fruit for those who sacrifice to the fathers.
He said: While I was practicing austerity on the peak of <s>Meru</s>, I asked
<s>Sanatkumāra</s>, and the Blessed One, a treasury of splendors, told me this:
In former times <s>Brahmā</s>, seeing the gods and seeing that they sacrificed only for themselves,
bewildered them with a curse, saying, 'Why do these not sacrifice to me?'
All of them, their understanding lost, propitiated the lotus-born god.
At his command they asked their own sons about expiation.
Then, purified by expiations and by instruction in ritual action and knowledge,
and addressed by their own sons, on account of their venerable status, as 'Go, dear sons,'

children.text: ta ete pitaraḥ pūjyā devānāṃ tanayā api ||
children.translated_text: they became these fathers who are to be honored, even though they were sons of the gods.

children.text: yeṣāṃ śrāddhaṃ vinā prāhustridaśā niṣphalāḥ kriyāḥ
children.translated_text: The gods declare that without their <s>śrāddha</s> rites are fruitless;
in sacrifices lacking that, the Rākṣasas consume the fruit.
Therefore the fathers and the gods, the hosts of fathers as well, belong to one another.
By <s>śrāddha</s> <s>Soma</s> is strengthened, and he nourishes all creatures.
The fathers, pleased by <s>śrāddha</s>, everywhere strengthen for men their fathers and grandfathers,
even when they have entered animal wombs.
Four of their groups have form, and three groups are bodiless;
they are known as the nectar-eaters, the devotees of yoga, and the <s>Vairājas</s>.

children.text: menākhyā mānasī teṣāṃ kanyā himagireḥ priyā
children.translated_text: Their mind-born daughter, named <s>Menā</s>, was dear to <s>Himagiri</s>.
Her splendid son was <s>Maināka</s>, father of the great mountain <s>Krauñca</s>.
<s>Menā</s>'s daughters were three, and they performed austerity difficult to perform.
The eldest of them, named <s>Aparṇā</s>, was <s>Bhavānī</s>, beloved of <s>Bhava</s>.

children.text: u meti tapaso mātrā vāritābhūdumeti yā
children.translated_text: She whom her mother restrained from austerity by saying, 'U, do not,' became <s>Umā</s>.
The second, named <s>Ekaparṇā</s>, became the wife of the sage <s>Devala</s>.
And the third, <s>Ekapāṭalā</s>, became the wife of <s>Jaigīṣavya</s>.
The mind-born daughter of the fathers, the sons of <s>Marīci</s>,
was the excellent river named <s>Acchodā</s>, formerly flowing from lake <s>Acchoda</s>.
Not recognizing her father, she looked upon him with desire;
fallen from her state, she fell because of his curse, though an end was fixed by his grace.
In the twenty-eighth Dvāpara age she was born from a fish womb,

children.text: asūta yā sutaṃ vyāsaṃ gandhakālī parāśarāt
children.translated_text: as <s>Gandhakālī</s>, who bore the son <s>Vyāsa</s> by <s>Parāśara</s>.
The other fathers, the <s>Barhiṣads</s> in heaven, were sons of <s>Pulastya</s>.

children.text: mānasī kanyakā teṣāṃ pīvarī nāma yoginī
children.translated_text: Their mind-born maiden was a yoginī named <s>Pīvarī</s>.
In her, <s>Śuka</s>, son of <s>Vyāsa</s>, will beget children,

children.text: putrīṃ ca kṛtvā jananīṃ brahmadattasya bhūpateḥ
children.translated_text: and a daughter who will become the mother of king <s>Brahmadatta</s>.
These three hosts of fathers are bodiless because they have renounced ritual action.
Those who are worshiped and who prosper the <s>Somadevas</s>, <s>Mānavas</s>, and others
are embodied fathers called <s>Somapās</s>, other nectar-eaters.

children.text: teṣāṃ gaurmānasī kanyā yajante brāhmaṇāśca tām
children.translated_text: Their mind-born daughter is <s>Gauḥ</s>, and the Brahmins sacrifice to her.
Others, sons of <s>Aṅgiras</s>, are fathers devoid of faith.
The Kṣatriyas are their sacrificers, and they have a maiden named <s>Yaśodā</s>,
mother of king <s>Dilīpa</s>, performer of a thousand sacrifices.
The <s>Ājyapā</s> fathers are sons of <s>Kaśyapa Prajāpati</s>.

children.text: yajante tānsadā vaiśyā kanyā teṣāṃ ca mānasī ||
children.translated_text: Vaiśyas always sacrifice to them; their mind-born daughter
is named <s>Virajā</s>, mother of king <s>Yayāti</s>.

children.text: sukālā nāma pitaro vaśiṣṭhasya muneḥ sutāḥ ||
children.translated_text: The fathers named <s>Sukālas</s> were sons of the sage <s>Vasiṣṭha</s>.
They are to be honored only by Śūdras; their daughter is the river <s>Narmadā</s>,
beloved of <s>Kurukutsa</s>, whose son was king <s>Trasaddastu</s>.
These four embodied hosts of fathers are the deities of the social classes.
Age after age <s>Śrāddhadeva Manu</s> prescribed their worship.

children.text: rājataṃ rājatāṅkaṃ vā yātaṃ teṣāṃ svadhābhujām
children.translated_text: Silver, silver-marked, or obtained by silver is the implement for them, the eaters of <s>svadhā</s>.
In <s>śrāddha</s>, worship of <s>Soma</s> and Fire goes first.

children.text: ta ete pitaraḥ pūjyāḥ krodhahīnāḥ prasādinaḥ
children.translated_text: These fathers are to be honored; they are free from anger and gracious.
Devotion to them is a wish-fulfilling creeper of resolve and bears great fruit.
Brahmins who have fallen away through violation of <s>dharma</s> (righteous order), by worship of the fathers,
will come back to their own station; you will see all that at the sacrifice.
'Know for yourself the reality of <s>śrāddha</s>,' he said,
and <s>Sanatkumāra</s>, after giving me divine sight, disappeared.
Then I saw those seven Brahmins in <s>Kurukṣetra</s>, under the power of Time.

children.text: vāgduṣṭaḥ krodhano hiṃsraḥ piśunaḥ svasṭamaḥ kaviḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Vāgduṣṭa</s>, <s>Krodhana</s>, <s>Hiṃsra</s>, <s>Piśuna</s>, <s>Svasṭama</s>, and <s>Kavi</s>,
and <s>Pitṛvartin</s> were their names, men whose conduct matched their forms.
Then, long ago, those descendants of <s>Kauśika</s>, pupils of the teacher <s>Gārgya</s>,

children.text: prasthitāḥ pathi gāṃ mūḍhāḥ kṣudhārtā hantumudyayuḥ
children.translated_text: set out on the road and, foolish and afflicted by hunger, prepared to kill a cow.
Though they were restrained by <s>Kavi</s> and by <s>Svasṭama</s>,
they did not desist; then, in anger, <s>Pitṛvartin</s> said to them:
'In every way this act of yours is improper, blamed by all living beings.
If your resolve is obstinate, let this undertaking be preceded by a <s>śrāddha</s> (ancestral rite).'

children.text: etadākarṇya te sarve taduktaṃ cakrire vidhim ||
children.translated_text: Hearing this, they all performed the rite he had spoken of.
Then, in time, cursed because of that violence, they were born as hunters.
Among the <s>Daśārṇas</s>, abiding in their own work, they were devoted to truth and good conduct.

children.text: janmāntare śrāddhaphalālluptā teṣāṃ na tu smṛtiḥ
children.translated_text: Through the fruit of the <s>śrāddha</s> in another birth, their memory was not lost.
<s>Nirvairin</s>, <s>Nirvṛti</s>, <s>Kṣānta</s>, <s>Nirmanyu</s>, <s>Vaidhasa</s>, and <s>Kṛtin</s>,
and <s>Mātṛvartin</s> were those hunters, intent on serving their parents.
They cast away their bows while bringing water for their parents and gave up their lives.
Thereafter, on dark <s>Kālāñjana</s> mountain, in bowers filled with masses of flowering creepers,
they were born as deer, terrified, exhausted, and distressed, but remembering former births.
<s>Unmukha</s>, <s>Nityacakita</s>, <s>Stabdhavarṇa</s>, <s>Sulocana</s>,
<s>Ghasmara</s>, <s>Piṇḍita</s>, and <s>Nādī</s> were names suited to their behavior.
They were celibate, patient, and exiles from their former knowledge.
Having gone as wanderers to the slopes of <s>Meru</s>, they abandoned their lives.
Even today, on the paths going to <s>Meru</s>, rising from the slopes of <s>Kālāñjana</s>,
their rows of footprints are seen upon the golden peaks.
Then, on an island in the pure river, where the sand was washed by waves,
they became young <s>cakravāka</s> birds, observing celibacy.
<s>Nirmama</s>, <s>Niḥspṛha</s>, <s>Kṣānta</s>, <s>Nirvaira</s>, <s>Niṣpratigraha</s>,
<s>Nirvṛta</s>, and <s>Nibhṛta</s> were those bird-yogins.
There they were born as swans, devoted to asceticism and yoga,
in the water adorned with garlands of lotuses and blue lotuses blown open by gentle winds.
As they sported in the water, they saw a king named <s>Vibhrāja</s>,
who, with clusters of lotus-faced women, outshone the lake itself.
He had come by chance to drink in the creeper-grove near the bank.
Seeing him like <s>Indra</s>, the youngest bird
formed a desire for his kingdom, his mind carried away by that royal splendor.
And two birds had minds that followed his desire.

children.text: tataḥ kālena te sarve sārasā vyasavo 'bhavan
children.translated_text: Then, with time, all those cranes gave up their lives.
That forest and lake became connected with <s>Vibhrāja</s> and frequented by the king.
Then <s>Vibhrāja</s> had a son, a king named <s>Aṇuha</s>.

children.text: tasmai vitṝṇāṃ dauhitrīṃ putrīṃ vyāsasutaḥ śukaḥ ||
children.translated_text: To him <s>Śuka</s>, son of <s>Vyāsa</s>, gave the daughter of the <s>Vitṛs</s> as a granddaughter,
named <s>Kṛtvī</s>, the presiding deity of divine yogins.
From her that swan was born as a son, fallen from yoga and with memory destroyed.

children.text: brahmadatta iti khyātaḥ kāmpilye nagare nṛpaḥ
children.translated_text: He became famous as king <s>Brahmadatta</s> in the city of <s>Kāmpilya</s>.
Two kings, his ministers, were known by names including <s>Pāñcāla</s> and <s>Puṇḍarīka</s>.
They were the two swans whose yoga had been lost through desire, their minds following him.
But four rememberers of former births were born as fellow students.
The beloved wife of <s>Brahmadatta</s> was the daughter of the sage <s>Devala</s>.
She was named <s>Saṃnati</s>, proud and with eyes intoxicated like wine.
Once, in a forest where the wind swayed among creepers and tāla trees,
served by her, he wandered like the god of love with his lute.
He knew the cries of all living beings, and there, in a lover's quarrel,
he heard the many appeasing words of a male ant to his wife.
Hearing that, the king, whose beautiful cheek-plates trembled,
laughed, making it seem as if a pearl necklace were on his beloved's throat.
'Why has my lord suddenly laughed at me?' she thought, embarrassed.
The lotus-faced woman became like a lotus-bed at moonrise.
Though the king explained the wonder of the ants' speech,
she, resolved only on giving up her life, considered it false.
Troubled by the long anger of his beloved, the lord of the earth
observed a fast without food and, with purified mind, beheld <s>Viṣṇu</s>.
By <s>Hari</s>'s command, 'Your welfare will come in the morning,'
at dawn he mounted his chariot and entered the city with his ministers.
Meanwhile, their father, sent by those four twice-born men who remembered former births
with the instruction, 'Recite a verse to the king,' came to him.

children.text: sa samāsādya bhūpālaṃ sacivābhyāṃ saha sthitam
children.translated_text: Approaching the king as he stood together with his two ministers,
the Brahmin, his mind somehow eager, recited this to him:

children.text: sapta dāśā daśārṇeṣu girau kālāñjane mṛgāḥ
children.translated_text: 'Seven fishermen among the <s>Daśārṇas</s>, deer on <s>Kālāñjana</s> mountain,
<s>cakravāka</s> birds on the river-island, and swans on <s>Mānasa</s> lake,

children.text: vayaṃ te 'dya kurukṣetre jātā vedavido dvijāḥ
children.translated_text: we are those very ones, now born in <s>Kurukṣetra</s> as Brahmins who know the Veda.
We are going on a long road; why are you dispirited?'
Hearing this, the king recovered the self of yoga and memory, and his senses became motionless.

children.text: sacivābhyāṃ saha paraṃ dhāma tacca samāyayau ||
children.translated_text: Together with his two ministers he reached that supreme abode.
Thus, by the power of the <s>śrāddha</s>, after destroying that fierce sin,
the descendants of <s>Kauśika</s>, being yogins, went to the highest state.
By the command of <s>Śāntanu</s>, I heard this from <s>Mārkaṇḍeya</s>.
<s>Brahmadatta</s> had a son, king <s>Viśvaksena</s>.
His son was <s>Daṇḍasena</s>, and his son was <s>Bhallāṭa</s>,

children.text: yaḥ karṇena purā vīro digjaye vinipātitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: the hero who was formerly struck down by <s>Karṇa</s> during the conquest of the quarters.
<s>Bhallāṭa</s> had a son, the ill-governed <s>Janamejaya</s>.
Then his son <s>Ugrāyudha</s>, wicked in conduct and unrestrained,

children.text: tridivaṃ śantanau yāte hartuṃ satyavatīṃ balāt
children.translated_text: when <s>Śantanu</s> had gone to heaven, wished to carry off <s>Satyavatī</s> by force;
the evil man formed this intention, and therefore he was slain by me.
Thus <s>Bhīṣma</s> told the son of <s>Dharma</s> the fruit of <s>śrāddha</s>.
By <s>śrāddha</s> (ancestral offering) <s>Soma</s> is nourished, and the <s>Vṛṣṇis</s> are descendants of his line.
In ancient times the blessed <s>Atri</s>, silent and best of sages, practiced
motionless austerity for three thousand divine years.
Then, as he remained unwinking and celibate, his body
became lovely and made of divine nectar, like the ocean of milk.
Then from <s>Atri</s>'s two eyes flowed that nectar, streaming tenfold,
into the ten directions, filling the sky with radiance.
Enclosed with effort as an unbearable embryo by the ten directions,
it suddenly attained the state of <s>Soma</s> and fell shining upon the earth.
When he had fallen, and the three worlds had quickly trembled,
<s>Brahmā</s> placed him in a Veda-made chariot drawn by a thousand horses.
The best of sages and the gods praised him as he stood in the chariot, the sustainer of the three worlds,
for the increase of his splendor; by that splendor he became conqueror of all.
He performed austerity for a full hundred lotuses of years,
and through his radiance hosts of divine herbs and nectars arose.
Then, consecrated as king by <s>Brahmā</s>, lord of the Brāhmaṇas,
beloved of <s>Dakṣa</s>'s daughters, he shone at the <s>Rājasūya</s> sacrifice.
Served by gods, siddhas, seers, and gandharvas, lord of the three worlds,
he roamed through the worlds, swollen with insolence and unrestrained by fortune.

children.text: jahāra tarasā so 'tha tārāṃ nāma bṛhaspateḥ
children.translated_text: Then he violently carried off <s>Tārā</s>, the beloved wife of <s>Bṛhaspati</s>;
who is not overwhelmed by the arrogance born from prosperity?

children.text: tridaśairbodhyamāno 'pi na sa tatyāja tāṃ yadā
children.translated_text: When, though admonished by the gods, he did not give her up,
then <s>Śukra</s> and <s>Rudra</s> took <s>Bṛhaspati</s>'s side.
Then, when the dreadful war over <s>Tārā</s> had begun,
against the gods headed by <s>Rudra</s>, by the hero of snowy radiance,
the <s>brahmaśiras</s> weapon was released, cutting away the fame of the dwellers in heaven,
and it left their army with only a remnant, broken, crushed, and slain.
Then the terrified gods approached the lotus-born <s>Brahmā</s> and entreated him;

children.text: nirvāya sāmnā samaraṃ dadau jāyāṃ bṛhaspateḥ ||
children.translated_text: he ended the battle by conciliation and gave <s>Bṛhaspati</s>'s wife back.
When she came back pregnant, he, fierce with the poison of jealousy, said to her,
with her face lowered, 'You must not carry this embryo in my womb.'
Then she abandoned the embryo on a bed of reeds;
as soon as he was born, radiant <s>Budha</s> conquered the gods with his splendor.

children.text: pṛṣṭā tato 'yaṃ kasyeti devairnovāca sā yadā
children.translated_text: When the gods asked, 'Whose is this child?' and she did not answer,
then, questioned by <s>Viriñci</s>, she quickly said, 'It is <s>Candra</s>'s.'
That glorious son of the Moon, rising in opposition in the sky,
wise and a cooling fan, shone as a delight to the gods.
Then in time the cool-rayed Moon, his orb wasted by the loss of offerings,
burned by his violation of another's wife, went to <s>Atri</s> for refuge.
Out of paternal affection, <s>Atri</s> destroyed his sin with mantras,
and, freed from wasting disease, he shone again, restored to his own beauty.
Then from <s>Iḍā</s> was born <s>Budha</s>'s son, <s>Purūravas</s>,
whose beloved <s>Urvaśī</s> was famed through the worlds like glory itself.
By her he had six sons in the abode of the gods;
<s>Āyus</s> was the eldest, a king, and <s>Nahuṣa</s> was <s>Āyus</s>'s son.
<s>Raji</s> and the others, four in all, were his younger brothers in ancient times;
in the former war between gods and Asuras, when <s>Vajrapāṇi</s> sought help,
<s>Raji</s>, younger brother of <s>Nahuṣa</s>, was chosen with sovereignty in heaven as the wager.
After killing the heroic sons of <s>Diti</s>, he won the lordship of the gods as the agreed prize.
But, deceitfully addressed by <s>Śakra</s>, 'I am your son,' he gave it up.

children.text: atha kālena jayino rajeḥ putrā mahaujasaḥ ||
