children.translated_text: Then in time the victorious, very powerful sons of <s>Raji</s>
seized the kingdom of the king of the gods, won by their father's strength.
Then <s>Śakra</s>, deprived of his kingdom and even deprived of his share in sacrifices,
asked <s>Bṛhaspati</s> for a sacrificial cake no larger than a jujube.
Petitioned by him, whose lotus-like face was childish and whose mind was ruined,
<s>Bṛhaspati</s> brought bewilderment upon the minds of <s>Raji</s>'s sons.
Then, passionate and intoxicated, fallen away from the path of justice,
they became greatly arrogant, their valor and prowess destroyed.
By that means the wielder of the thunderbolt killed those hard-to-conquer men and regained his own station.
For the fortunes of the wicked are restless like leaping minnows.
<s>Nahuṣa</s>'s son was <s>Yayāti</s>, lord of the earth,
who with his excellent divine chariot conquered the world in six nights.
That best of chariots was later lost from his lineage because of a curse;
it was obtained by <s>Jarāsaṃdha</s> and then taken by the enemy of the Asuras.
From <s>Yayāti</s> and <s>Devayānī</s>, daughter of <s>Śukra</s>, were born
two sons, <s>Yadu</s> and <s>Turvasu</s>, approved by the good.
And from <s>Śarmiṣṭhā</s>, daughter of <s>Vṛṣaparvan</s>, there were three sons,
named <s>Druhyu</s>, <s>Anu</s>, and <s>Pūru</s>, who increased his lineage.

children.text: kāle 'tha vipule yāte yayātiḥ pravayāḥ sutān ||
children.translated_text: Then, after a long time had passed, aged <s>Yayāti</s>,
lord of the earth and still desirous, asked his sons for youth in exchange for old age,
old age, the row of claws of the lion Death, striking down the lotus of happiness.
When no one accepted that old age, then <s>Pūru</s> accepted it.
Therefore, after obtaining youth, <s>Yayāti</s> then cursed the others, beginning with <s>Yadu</s>,
so that their descendants would always be without kingship.
Then, wishing to see the far shore of pleasures, with a youthful body,
he sported in <s>Nandana</s> with <s>Viśvācī</s>, the heavenly woman.
Although the king long enjoyed the lotus-eyed woman,
when, with desire increasing, he did not come to the end of pleasures,

children.text: tadā rājyaṃ sutasyaiva purordatvā jarāṃ nijām ||
children.translated_text: then, having given the kingdom to his son <s>Puru</s>, he took back his own old age.
With dispassion arisen, he adopted a sage's vow and spoke these words:
'A wonder: this longing for enjoyment grows through the practice of enjoyment,
like submarine fire through the mass of surging waves of water.
Alas, the pollen-cloud of the lotus of vast saṃsāra
binds deluded men night after night, like bees, with affection.
Even in those who grow old, it does not age; even in those who perish, this perishable passion is not cast off.
Desire remains inside those who desire, like a worm inside trees.
Though forbidden by discipline and also disregarded by firmness,
passion blazes forth, ah, like fire covered with a cloth.'
Having reflected thus, restrained <s>Yayāti</s>, joined with ascetic practice,
by the rite proper to his family, came to exist only as the remnant of his fame.
When the very broad earth had come under the rule of <s>Puru</s>, son of <s>Yayāti</s>,
in the passage of time, after many generations, there arose a lord of the earth,
<s>Duṣyanta</s>, whose son was <s>Bharata</s>, founder of the <s>Bhārata</s> lineage.
In his stainless family you, <s>Janamejaya</s>, were born.
This <s>Paurava</s> lineage has already been related by me before.
But <s>Turvasu</s>'s lineage was great; in it <s>Karaṃdhama</s> was born.
His son was <s>Marutta</s>, to whom <s>Maheśvara</s> gave gold.
In his extensive lineage arose the <s>Pāṇḍyas</s>, <s>Caulas</s>, and <s>Keralas</s>.
But in the lineage of <s>Druhyu</s> was born a king named <s>Marutpati</s>.
He was killed by <s>Yauvanāśva</s> with difficulty in a long battle.
<s>Gāndhāra</s> was his son; in his lineage the <s>Turaṅgamas</s> were born.
In <s>Anu</s>'s lineage <s>Dharma</s> and others were born as kings of the borderlands.
But in the far-spread lineage of <s>Yadu</s>, the king who was son of <s>Kṛtavīrya</s>
was born as <s>Kārtavīryārjuna</s>, arrogant through his thousand arms.
The <s>Hehayas</s>, <s>Ānartas</s>, <s>Bhojas</s>, and the <s>Tālajaṅghas</s> and others were in his family.
In time, in that lineage, <s>Vṛṣa</s> was born; <s>Madhu</s> was the son of <s>Vṛṣa</s>.
<s>Vṛṣaṇa</s> was his son, in whose lineage were the <s>Sāgaras</s> and <s>Vṛṣṇis</s>.
<s>Andhaka</s> too arose in their line and became the founder of the <s>Andhaka</s> lineage.

children.text: bahuśākhe ca tadvaṃśe jāto krūraḥ sahasradaḥ ||
children.translated_text: And in that many-branched lineage were born <s>Akrūra</s> and <s>Sahasrada</s>.
In time, in the family of his paternal uncle, the glorious <s>Śūra</s> was born.
His son was <s>Vasudeva</s>, called <s>Ānakadundubhi</s>.
When he was born, a great sound of kettledrums arose in heaven.
His brother was named <s>Devabhāga</s>, and another was <s>Devaśravas</s>.

children.text: anādhṛṣṭiḥ kanavako vatsaḥ śyāmo vavṛñja saḥ
children.translated_text: There were also <s>Anādhṛṣṭi</s>, <s>Kanavaka</s>, <s>Vatsa</s>, <s>Śyāma</s>, and <s>Vavṛñja</s>.
<s>Pṛthukīrti</s>, <s>Pṛthā</s>, <s>Śrutadevī</s>, <s>Śrutaśravā</s>,
and <s>Rājādhidevī</s>: these five were daughters of <s>Śūra</s> and his younger sisters.
<s>Pṛthukīrti</s>'s son was king <s>Dantavakra</s>, a prince.
<s>Pṛthā</s>'s sons were <s>Dharmarāja</s>, <s>Bhīmasena</s>, and <s>Dhanaṃjaya</s>.
<s>Śrutaśravā</s>'s son was the mighty <s>Śiśupāla</s>,
who had formerly been that demon-king <s>Hiraṇyakaśipu</s>.
In the paternal-uncle line of <s>Śūra</s> there was <s>Śaineya</s>, <s>Satyaka</s>.
His son was <s>Sātyaki</s>, otherwise named <s>Yuyudhāna</s>.
There were also <s>Uddhava</s>, teacher of the wise, and <s>Śatrudeva</s> and others.
In the family of <s>Śatrudeva</s> was born <s>Ekalavya</s>, the <s>Niṣāda</s>.
To <s>Vatsāvat</s>, who was without a son, powerful <s>Vasudeva</s>,
<s>Śauri</s>, ritually gave with water his brave natural son <s>Kauśika</s>.
To sonless <s>Gaṇḍūṣaka</s>, <s>Hari</s> gave <s>Cārudoṣṇa</s> and others.

children.text: dve bhārye vasudevasya rohiṇī devakī tathā
children.translated_text: The two wives of <s>Vasudeva</s> were <s>Rohiṇī</s> and <s>Devakī</s>.
<s>Rāma</s>, <s>Sāraṇa</s>, <s>Durdama</s>, and <s>Subha</s> were sons of <s>Rohiṇī</s>.
<s>Śubhra</s>, <s>Piṇḍāraka</s>, and <s>Damana</s> too were those sons of the great-faced one.
And this younger sister <s>Subhadrā</s> became the wife of <s>Savyasācin</s>.
<s>Rāma</s>'s son by <s>Revatī</s> was named <s>Niṣadha</s>.
<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, son of <s>Devakī</s>, was the god, the destroyer of the <s>Dānavas</s>.
And <s>Vasudeva</s> had sons by his other wives:
<s>Bhoja</s>, <s>Upāsaṅga</s>, <s>Vijaya</s>, <s>Vṛṣadeva</s>, and <s>Gada</s>,
<s>Āśāvaha</s>, <s>Lomapāda</s>, <s>Kapila</s>, and <s>Vardhamānaka</s>,
<s>Pauṇḍra</s>, and the lord of the <s>Niṣādas</s>, men of fierce valor and prowess.
Meanwhile the sage <s>Gārgya</s>, subsisting on black iron,

children.text: cacāra dvādaśa samā brahmacārī paraṃ tapaḥ ||
children.translated_text: lived for twelve years as a celibate, practicing supreme austerity.
When the daughter of the <s>Trigarta</s> king tried him with playful seduction,
he did not move, iron-like, even though his intention was being drawn away.
He, burned by anger, begot on a cowherd's daughter, by <s>Rudra</s>'s command,
<s>Kālayavana</s>, a very Death to all rulers of the earth.
His chariot had dreadful horses whose foreparts had the form of bulls.
Taken as a son by the childless lord of the <s>Yavanas</s>,
he, seeking battle and maddened with pride, asked about the good warriors on earth.
Learning from <s>Nārada</s>'s words of the heroic <s>Vṛṣṇi</s>-<s>Yādavas</s>,
who dwelt in <s>Mathurā</s>, he rushed with an <s>akṣauhiṇī</s> to conquer them.
Attacked by <s>Kālayavana</s> and oppressed by <s>Jarāsaṃdha</s>,
the <s>Vṛṣṇis</s> abandoned <s>Mathurā</s> and made <s>Dvārakā</s> in the sea.
And from other branches of the lineage other <s>Yādavas</s> were born.
In the family of <s>Sātvata</s>, whose deeds were sung by the gods,
there was the sacrificer king <s>Devāvṛdha</s>; <s>Babhru</s> was his son.
Born from <s>Sarvarṇā</s> on the river <s>Āpagā</s>, he was a giver of many hundreds of thousands.
In that family arose heroic <s>Bhojas</s>, descended from <s>Śāntika</s>.
From <s>Andhaka</s> was born <s>Kukkura</s>; in that lineage too there was <s>Āhuka</s>,
a king suited to the Kṛta age, the founder of the <s>Vṛṣṇi</s> lineages.
<s>Devaka</s> and <s>Ugrasena</s> were his two sons. As for <s>Devaka</s>,
his sons were <s>Devavat</s> and the others, and his daughters were <s>Devakī</s> and the rest.
Those seven, mothers of heroes, were given to <s>Vasudeva</s>.
<s>Kaṃsa</s>, son of <s>Ugrasena</s>, was the elder brother of <s>Nyagrodha</s> and the others.

children.text: kaṃsā kaṃsavatī tanvī pālī kahvā ca kanyakāḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Kaṃsā</s>, <s>Kaṃsavatī</s>, <s>Tanvī</s>, <s>Pālī</s>, and <s>Kahvā</s> were the daughters.
In the <s>Bhoja</s> family of <s>Vidūratha</s> there was one named <s>Hṛdika</s>.
His sons were <s>Kṛtavarman</s> at their head, <s>Śatadhanvan</s>, and the rest.
In <s>Kroṣṭṛ</s>'s line were <s>Prasena</s>, <s>Satrājit</s>, and <s>Senajit</s>.

children.text: ityete bahavo vaṃśā viśrutā yādavā yadoḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus these were the many famous <s>Yādava</s> lineages sprung from <s>Yadu</s>.
At the settlement of <s>Dvāravatī</s> on the ocean shore, a flawless jewel,

children.text: divyaṃ syamantakaṃ nāma prasenaḥ kila labdhavān ||
children.translated_text: divine and named <s>Syamantaka</s>, had been obtained by <s>Prasena</s>.
That jewel poured forth gold and destroyed widespread famine.
Although capable and eager, <s>Śauri</s> did not take it from him.
In time <s>Prasena</s>, devoted to hunting and adorned with the jewel,
was suddenly slain in battle by a lion that carried off the jewel.
Then <s>Jāmbavān</s>, king of the bears, as that lion was going swiftly,
killed it, took the jewel, and, powerful as he was, entered a cave.
When the <s>Vṛṣṇis</s> and <s>Andhakas</s> saw <s>Prasena</s> slain in the lonely forest,
they suspected, 'All this was done by <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> out of greed for the jewel.'
<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, though pure in intention, went to search for that jewel;
for who could endure a false stain, a slander upon his fame?
He saw bloodstained <s>Prasena</s>, torn open by the lion,
and not far from him he saw the lion lying dead.
When he did not find the jewel, he recognized a trail indicating a bear,

children.text: guhāṃ praviśya gambhīraṃ dadarśa vipulaṃ bilam ||
children.translated_text: and, entering a cave, he saw a vast, deep cavern.

children.text: tatra dhātryā sa śuśrāva vacanaṃ bālasāntvane
children.translated_text: There he heard the nurse's words as she soothed a child:

children.text: tavaivāsau maṇiḥ putra mā rodīḥ sukumāraka ||
children.translated_text: 'The jewel is yours alone, my son; do not cry, tender child.'
Hearing this and understanding what had happened, he saw <s>Jāmbavān</s>.
Then <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> fought with him for twenty-one days.
<s>Jāmbavān</s>'s chest had been scored by weapons in the fierce battle with <s>Daśagrīva</s>.

children.text: jāmbavantaṃ vijityātha dattāṃ tena sutāṃ hariḥ ||
children.translated_text: After conquering <s>Jāmbavān</s>, <s>Hari</s> then received the daughter given by him,

children.text: bimbādharāṃ jāmbavatīṃ lebhe taṃ ca syamantakam
children.translated_text: <s>Jāmbavatī</s>, with bimba-red lips, and also that <s>Syamantaka</s>.
Then, coming to <s>Dvāravatī</s>, the noble-minded one brought the <s>Syamantaka</s>
and gave the jewel to <s>Satrājit</s> himself, the younger brother of <s>Prasena</s>.
<s>Satrājit</s> gave three daughters, headed by <s>Satyabhāmā</s>, to the enemy of <s>Mura</s>,
maidens like moonlight for the night-lotuses of desire.
After <s>Satrājit</s> was killed by the <s>Bhoja</s> <s>Śatadhanvan</s>,
<s>Akrūra</s> carried off the jewel by an agreement of mutual assistance.

children.text: satyabhāmā svayaṃ gatvā hate pitari duḥkhitā ||
children.translated_text: <s>Satyabhāmā</s>, grieving when her father had been killed, went herself,
while the <s>Pārthas</s> had been burned in the lac house by the sons of <s>Dhṛtarāṣṭra</s>,
and reached the wielder of <s>Śārṅga</s>, who was staying at <s>Vāraṇāvata</s>.
With tears she reported that her father had been killed by <s>Śatadhanvan</s>.
Then the one whose banner bears <s>Garuḍa</s> swiftly came to <s>Dvārakā</s>.
Going with <s>Rāma</s>, he fought with <s>Śatadhanvan</s>.
Though <s>Śatadhanvan</s> had given him the jewel, <s>Akrūra</s> did not aid him.

children.text: svārthakāle vyatīte hi dhūrtā no kasyacinnijāḥ
children.translated_text: For rogues, once the moment of self-interest has passed, belong to no one.
Quickly mounting a mare that could go a hundred yojanas,
<s>Śatadhanvan</s> fled at speed toward <s>Mithilā</s>.
The enemy of <s>Kaiṭabha</s> killed him, but did not obtain that jewel.
<s>Lāṅgalin</s>, angry with him, wrongly thought, 'The jewel has been concealed.'

children.text: na dvārakāṃ viśāmīti mithilāṃ vimukho yayau ||
children.translated_text: 'I will not enter <s>Dvārakā</s>,' he said, and, turning away, went to <s>Mithilā</s>.
There <s>Duryodhana</s> received instruction in the mace from him.
Then, after the <s>Vṛṣṇi</s> heroes who followed <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> came and placated him,
the illustrious <s>Halāyudha</s>, having learned the truth, came to <s>Dvārakā</s>.
<s>Akrūra</s> too, prospering through the jewel, performed many sacrifices and made many gifts.
Protected by the armor of consecration, he passed sixty years happily.
When the jewel had become somewhat known, and when he became afraid of <s>Rāma</s> and <s>Keśava</s>,
then, after <s>Akrūra</s> had gone away, <s>Pākaśāsana</s> did not rain.
For a long time <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> had previously ignored him, fearing a split among kinsmen.
But then, with the <s>Yādavas</s> afflicted by famine, he conciliated him and brought him back again.
When that lord of generosity arrived, the lord of heaven sent rain.

children.text: kālena yācitaḥ sāmnā kṛṣṇena sa dadau maṇim
children.translated_text: In time, when gently requested by <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, he gave the jewel.
For affection, <s>Akrūra</s> also gave him his lovely-eyed sister.
And <s>Keśava</s>, pleased by his humility and straightforwardness, gave the jewel
to <s>Akrūra</s> himself; for the limits of affection among the great are hard to grasp.
After hearing the lineage-list of the <s>Yādavas</s>, <s>Janamejaya</s>,
astonished at the birth of <s>Viṣṇu</s>, said to <s>Vaiśampāyana</s>:
'Ah, this great and unprecedented wonder appears to me:
How did the abode of the world, the teacher of all that moves and does not move, become a man?
He within whose belly-cavity the series of worlds lies at the end of a kalpa,
how did that creator of beings enter a human womb?
This universal form belongs to him, the inner self of all beings,
reflected in the mirror unfolded by mere will.'

children.text: iti pṛṣṭaḥ kṣitibhujā jagāda mudito muniḥ
children.translated_text: Thus asked by the king, the sage spoke with delight:
'Hear the wondrous birth of <s>Viṣṇu</s>, which cuts away the fear of birth,
by which, as the sacrificial Boar, with a body composed of the Veda and sacrifice...
having lifted up the earth, girdled by the four oceans.
The earth, dark as a blue lotus, shone on the tip of whose tusk,
like a young śevala creeper hidden among playful pools.
By whom, as a lion, with oyster-like nails white as conches,
the fame of <s>Hiraṇyakaśipu</s> was drunk away together with his life.
In the cage of saw-like claws, from the grinding of the bones of his chest,
whose anger in killing the Daitya became like the banner of the fire at the end of an age.
In whose stride across the three worlds, his foot became a banner of victory,
its fluttering white garment stirred by the flashing water of the <s>Gaṅgā</s>.
At first he was a dwarf, then tall, and after that immeasurable;
and he became the joy of the gods and the bewilderment of the enemies of the gods.
As he grew, the sun became an earring at his ear and a lotus at his navel,
and at his ankle it took the form of a jeweled anklet.
For the heavenly women gazing upward at that body,
the three folds were not seen, as if from fear of their destruction.
By the incarnation as <s>Dattātreya</s>, when righteous conduct was sinking,

children.text: vedānāṃ ca kṛtaṃ yena sthityai hastāvalambanam ||
children.translated_text: he gave a handhold for the stability of the <s>Vedas</s> as well.
Becoming embodied as <s>Jāmadagnya</s>, he cut away <s>Kārtavīrya</s>'s vigorous
thousand arms, lovely like clusters of lotus fibers.
On his axe, broken by the crushing of bones, he bore a garland of teeth,
as though it were a count of the times when the kṣatriyas were destroyed.
He gave to <s>Kaśyapa</s> the cow, the fertile earth, with her eastern limbs and lovely middle land,
with <s>Puṇḍra</s> forests and with her calf.
He became <s>Raghunandana</s>, ornament of the expanse of the world,
a hero, the mighty wind against the terrible clouds <s>Subāhu</s> and <s>Mārīca</s>.
The sound of whose bow, wandering through the seven worlds and filled with the agitation of the seven oceans,
belonged to the archer who pierced the seven tāla trees.
Even today the ocean, its shell-cases split open by the impact of the bridge,
with clearly visible pearls for teeth, speaks his fame.
By him, with the rays of his white fame resting on the tips of crowns,
the dust raised by <s>Indrajit</s>'s army was wiped from the guardians of the worlds.
As the heads of <s>Daśāsya</s> fell and sprang up again and again,
there arose a delightful illusion of easy ball-play.
To remove the burden of the earth, <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> was born in the <s>Vṛṣṇi</s> lineage,
the death of kings such as <s>Śiśupāla</s>, the breaker of Asuras.
On whose chest even <s>Ariṣṭa</s>'s defeat, the breaking of his horn,
was indicated by uneven scratch marks that could not cling there.
Whose foot, on the head of the serpent <s>Kāliya</s>, made with its bright nails
circles like hoods and rose up in rivalry with <s>Śeṣa</s>.
In the forest of <s>Bāṇa</s>'s arms, with blazing matted locks born from crushing cuts at the root-bones,
whose discus acted like a saw.
And he who, apparently as <s>Kalki</s>, son of <s>Viṣṇuyaśas</s>, will come at the end of the age,
a springtime of new fragrance for the garden-creeper of goodness and <s>dharma</s>.
Of him, whose power is wondrous, let this bright
deed be heard, able to wash away sin with the nectar of merit.

children.text: prabhāvaṃ tasya tattvena vaktuṃ ko nu pragalbhate
children.translated_text: Who indeed is bold enough to speak truly of his power,
where <s>Vācaspati</s> is mute, and the words of the lord of serpents are far away?
Long ago, after the killing of <s>Vṛtra</s>, in the battle called <s>Tārakāmaya</s>,
the gods went for refuge to <s>Viśvaksena</s>, <s>Janārdana</s>.

children.text: dattaṃ tenābhayaṃ teṣāṃ viṣame daityaje bhaye
children.translated_text: When he had given them fearlessness amid their perilous fear of the Daityas,
all the assembled Dānavas entered the battlefield.
<s>Maya</s>, treasure-house of magic, their leader, fierce in form,
shone mounted on a golden chariot drawn by a thousand bears.
<s>Tāra</s>, riding an iron chariot more than a krośa long,
equipped with a thousand sounds, appeared like fire born from smoke.
<s>Hayagrīva</s> mounted a chariot drawn by a thousand horses,
and <s>Tvaṣṭā</s> one yoked with rutting elephants and heavy as <s>Mandara</s>.
Heroes such as <s>Virocana</s> stood facing the battle;
that ocean of an army was vast as a mass of clouds at the end of an age.
Seeing it, the gods, reassured by <s>Viṣṇu</s>, rushed forward together;
at their front shone the Thousand-eyed one, mounted on <s>Airāvata</s>.
With the rays of his thunderbolt he displayed thousands of rainbows.
<s>Yama</s>, dark, riding a buffalo and wearing a great starry necklace,
stood like a blue mountain with waterfalls beneath a hanging cloud.
<s>Varuṇa</s>, with white horses, marked by jeweled garlands and radiant as the sun,
shone on his chariot like a jewel-peak risen upon <s>Kailāsa</s>.
Golden in aspect, with a golden chariot, wearing golden armlets,
<s>Dhanada</s> stole the splendor of <s>Meru</s> warmed by the sun's heat.
The moon-rayed one had horses white as slabs of ice and an icy weapon.
And <s>Vāyu</s>, cloud-borne, the life of embodied beings, stood there.
And the blessed god himself, the slayer of <s>Kaiṭabha</s>, came forward.
He bore the blazing discus, mace, <s>Śārṅga</s>, and <s>Nandana</s>, with <s>Garuḍa</s> as his banner.
In battle his discus shone, with Dānavas reflected in its edge,
as if whole hosts of enemies had entered within it and been slain on every side.
His serpent-slayer, the radiant vehicle, shone like <s>Meru</s> in a quiet blaze,
a stream that carried off the brilliance of his enemies.
With his wings blazing ever more intensely, the sky was covered,
as if by the twelve final suns gathered into one dense mass.
Mounted on him, <s>Hari</s>, adorned with the <s>Kaustubha</s>, shone resplendent.
joined with the submarine fire, like <s>Maināka</s>, source of jewels,
the <s>Rudras</s>, <s>Ādityas</s>, <s>Maruts</s>, <s>Viśvas</s>, <s>Sādhyas</s>, <s>Aśvins</s>, <s>Vasus</s>, and <s>Cāraṇas</s>
rose up together like billows from the ocean of the agitated army.
Then, with a sound like a shaken ocean, making the three worlds resound,
the battle-opening drum roared, deep with its booming noise.

children.text: petuḥ parasparaṃ teṣāṃ dehe tejasvināṃ prabhāḥ ||
children.translated_text: The radiances of those fiery warriors fell upon one another's bodies,
when battle had begun, like masses of golden arrows.
Flames sprang up from the heaps of weapons and missiles hurled by the hands of gods and Asuras,
and for a moment they made the tips of the banners seem to be yellow silk.
The Daityas moved about, their armor scratched by the tusks of the elephants of the gods,
smoking and aflame, like clouds filled with lightning.
Those divine elephants, their tusks bent against the broad chests of the Daityas,
thought even the great ancestral mountains as insubstantial as banks of sand.
Then, in the sky, pierced by weapons brandished by the arms of the Daityas,
the immortals quickly became motionless, as if painted in a picture.
That mighty magic of the Daityas was utterly irresistible;
for even <s>Yama</s>, as though bound by restraint, was checked when it came to their destruction.
<s>Vāyu</s> became as if lame, and the radiant Sun as if without light;

children.text: jayastu yudhi daityeṣu vahniḥ śīta ivābhavat
children.translated_text: and in battle against the Daityas, Fire became as if cold.
Then the thousand-eyed one, uprooting the Daitya-born magic with his thunderbolt,
again set the gods to fight the heroes headed by <s>Maya</s>.
As the Daityas, cut down by the thunderbolt of the thunderbolt-bearer, fell to earth,
all seven oceans became one through their heavy bodies.
Those Dānavas, like great elephants covered over,
fell wrapped in darkness, bewildered by <s>Surendra</s> and the enemies of the Dānavas.
Then <s>Maya</s>, rich in many illusions, made an illusion suited to the moment,
one filled with Aurva fire, solely for the destruction of the gods.
Born from the thigh, a child of Fire, produced by the resolve of the celibate sage,
the world-burning, time-formed, water-consuming fire, empowered by <s>Brahmā</s>'s boon,
the <s>Aurva</s> fire, formerly a boon-giver to <s>Hiraṇyakaśipu</s> through devotion,
blazed among the armies of the gods in that straitened battle.
Burned by <s>Aurva</s>, their bodies tangled in flames,
the gods thought that radiance and darkness had become one.
All the thirty gods, helpless under that mass of Aurva fire,
thought only of <s>Varuṇa</s> and the cool-rayed Moon as their refuge.
Then the Moon, directed by <s>Akhaṇḍala</s> and going with <s>Varuṇa</s> before him,
rose in battle against the Dānavas, hurling masses of ice.
Struck hard by those two with floods of frosty water,
the Dānavas became motionless, like wood and stone.

children.text: himasya mahatī śaktiḥ sā kāpi dahanātmikā ||
children.translated_text: Such was the great power of the snow, somehow fiery in nature,
by which a great breaking of the bones of the hosts of Dānavas occurred.
The army of the Dānavas, covered with thunderbolts of frost,
was indicated only by the passages of breath from their noses, without any clear divisions.
Knowing the exchange of illusions, <s>Maya</s>, for the success of his own people,
created a mountain-born illusion, dense with trees, weapons, and stones.
For the gods, hemmed in by trees and mountains, their weapons and armor split apart,
bewilderment yawned wide, except for the bearer of the discus and mace.
Then in a moment, ordered by him, and immediately empowered by his hand,
Fire and Wind entered together into the army of the Daityas.
After reducing the heaps of trees and stones to rows of ashes only,
and scattering them, blown up, through the directions, the two ranged over the front of battle.
Terrible with its beard kindled by flames fanned by the wind,
the smoke of the burning Daityas rose like Time.
From the wind heated by fire and from the fire driven onward by wind,
there arose a crackling roar, terrible as the shout of Death.
As their skins split and as their fats went 'chama-cham',
and as the great fastenings of their bones burst apart, there was a strange mingled tumult.
While the hosts of gods were victorious and the circle of Diti's sons was broken,
<s>Kālanemi</s> rose up, longing to swallow the three worlds.
With terrible mouths whose fang-tips were made clear by yawning, he filled the sky,
as if they had risen eagerly from the depths, each crying 'I first,' for the destruction of the world.
By the masses of his arms, like pillars of collyrium stone,
the quarters seemed wrapped in the coils of terrifying serpents.
With the high crest of his crown rubbing against the shell of the cosmic egg,
he created, with a net of smoke, the pomp of clouds of dissolution.
From the eyes of that hundred-faced one, flames went out into the directions,
and by his shadow the whole world became invisible for a moment.
By those dread circles, as if formed from clustered masses of death-night,
the ritual enclosures of his consecration to hurl the universe into destruction,
the quarters were lit by circles of blazing weapon-radiance.
Striking against every splendor and making all beings tremble,
he swept away the formations of clouds with the winds of his angry breaths.
Raising an arm whose shock struck against the shoulder of the wind,
he brought the sons of <s>Diti</s> back to life with a voice like the sound of a churned ocean.
Then, with the delighted Dānavas before him, their weapons raised,
the gods fought, their energy struck down by <s>Kālanemi</s>.
In that tumultuous clash of battle, destructive of life,
the great and dreadful body of <s>Kālanemi</s> grew larger.
The gods were encircled by flames vomited from the cavern of his mouth,
and were struck on every side by his arms, which had grown sideways and upward.
Struck down by that shower of weapons, their crests dragged away by his hands,
they fell from their chariots to the earth like men whose merit was exhausted, fallen from heavenly cars.
When <s>Śakra</s>'s crooked face was broken, when <s>Varuṇa</s> had become an object of pity,
when <s>Dhanada</s> had met destruction and <s>Śaśāṅka</s> feared eclipse,
with their weapons, standards, and parasols broken, and their chariots and elephants cut down,
the motionless Thirty-three gods stood powerless, like lamps by day.
What news could there be of a cold fire? The sun was only a mirror for the stars.

children.text: āsthā kiṃ niścale vāyau kiṃ yamena hataujasā ||
children.translated_text: What reliance was there on the wind when it was still? What use was <s>Yama</s> when his power was slain?

children.text: kimete mudritā rudrā vasavo vyasavo nu kim
children.translated_text: "Are these <s>Rudras</s> sealed shut? Or are the <s>Vasus</s> lifeless?"
Speaking thus with a roar, the sons of <s>Diti</s> rejoiced.
Then <s>Kālanemi</s>, having obtained victory and wounded the immortals,
stood in the office of the world-protectors, dividing his body in many ways.
Becoming water, he became all-pervading; becoming wind, he himself blew.
Taking the bodies of moon and sun, he made night and day.
As the self of all worlds, with fire as his mouth, he himself received the oblation;
he became composed of all the gods, desiring to conquer <s>Viṣṇu</s>.
Though lord of all the worlds and attended by all the hosts of gods,
he was not attended by the Veda, by <s>dharma</s> (righteous order), by compassion, by truth, or by fortune.
Then he saw the god who is first among gods, marked by <s>Garuḍa</s>,
who, through the play of delight in battle, ignored the crushing of the foremost troops.
He was adorned with the <s>Kaustubha</s>, beautiful with its garlands of radiance,
like a soft dark cloud made splendid by a flashing rainbow.
His arms shone with shoots formed by the wearing of jeweled armlets,
like other <s>Pārijāta</s> trees sprinkled with the nectar of necklace-light.
He was being borne by <s>Suparṇa</s>, charming with a golden luster,
as if by <s>Sumeru</s> embodied, afraid of lifting up <s>Mandara</s>.
He carried a mace whose golden armlets were marks recording the slaughter of demons,
as though it had been made from the heaviness of the greatest mountains.
His pair of thighs was surrounded by reddish rays like those of the young sun,
as if smeared with sprays of blood from the throats of <s>Madhu</s> and <s>Kaiṭabha</s>.
He was served by an expanse of conch-radiance, rippling with rows of jewels,
like the milk-ocean, wearied by the exertion of being his bed.
He was pervaded by circles of discus-light, red with blood leaping up from the forest of <s>Rāhu</s>'s neck,
like the sky pervaded by the rays of the sun.
"Ah, alas, this enemy of ours has come within range of our sight,
by whom the eyes of demon-women were brought to a stainless, collyrium-less state.
When he killed <s>Hiraṇyakaśipu</s> with the sharp sprouts of his nails,
this very slayer struck down our pearl-bright fame.
I shall kill him and wash the floor of the assembly, smeared with dust from <s>Nṛsiṃha</s>'s tread,
with the waters of tears of joy from the demons."
As he spoke thus contemptuously, the Lord, his lips white with a playful smile,
said, "I am intoxicated by the honey of arrogance that is about to fall."
Then the lord of the demons, terrifying and gaping wide with a loud laugh,
let fall a shower of weapons upon the god's breast with his massive arms.
Even <s>Suparṇa</s> was shaken by a mace of fierce speed;
by that blow, on the god's breast, even the unmoving one trembled for a moment.
Amazed, and stirred by anger, <s>Viṣṇu</s> then expanded,
with a thousand arms and feet and a thousand faces and eyes.
Taking up <s>Sudarśana</s>, clear and fearsome to enemies,
scattering golden sand with the outspread rays at its edge,
a razor-edged thunderbolt disk not blunted by heaps of demon bones,
he hurled that saw-cruel discus into the forest of the demon's faces.
Released from <s>Viṣṇu</s>'s arm, that terrible likeness of the sun,
spewing tongues of fire, cut off a hundred faces of the enemy.
With streams of flowing blood rising from his severed arms and faces,

children.text: na papāta ciraṃ daityo manyustabdha iva sthitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: the demon did not fall for a long time, but stood as if stiffened by wrath.
By the wind of <s>Tārkṣya</s>'s wings, which crushed the crests of the mountains,
the seven oceans leapt up, their waves embracing the sky.
Then all the demons everywhere were crushed by him whose hands and feet were everywhere,
by the universal form, and became only remnants in memory.
Then, when the wicked one had ceased and the practice of <s>dharma</s> had begun,
praised by the gods beginning with <s>Brahmā</s> and by the great seers,
<s>Hari</s>, having brought <s>Śakra</s> to his own station, went to <s>Brahmā</s>'s abode,
honored by perfected beings worthy of honor from the three worlds, whose selves were made of consciousness.
Then the Lord went to his own hermitage, illumined by his own radiance,
and in the ocean he entered yogic sleep beneath a lofty cloudlike coverlet.
Sleep slowly attended upon dark <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, lying on <s>Śeṣa</s>, thousand-faced,
like a garland of drunken bees attending a lotus-pond.
As he slept, his body, splendid in yellow silk, shone
as though heaped with masses of pollen from the lotus of <s>Brahmā</s> sprung from his navel.
Counting with his rosary the worldly stain of time,
he drew in and sent forth beings with the rosary-threads of his rows of breaths.
When he had fallen asleep, as fate brought on the southern course,
even Sleep became as if asleep, closed by a mass of darkness.
This sleep, marked by yawning, languor, and delusion, robbing men of the purpose of life,
was nevertheless purifying through contact with <s>Viṣṇu</s>, though it was a minor dissolution.

children.text: tato varṣasahasreṣu yāteṣu ca kṛte kate
children.translated_text: Then, when many thousands of years had passed in the Kṛta age,
when the Tretā had passed away and the Dvāpara had grown thin,
awakened by the breeze from the edge of the play-lotus of <s>Kamalā</s>
The gods, with <s>Pitāmaha</s> at their head and the thousand-eyed one foremost,
came together as one, intent upon the business of the world.
For a moment the hosts of sages, their hands like opened lotuses, praised him.
O god, while the three worlds are contained in you under the pretext of yogic sleep,

children.text: tvayi deva na jānīmaḥ kartvayaṃ suptasaṃvidā ||
children.translated_text: we do not know what is to be done by you, whose awareness is asleep.
Abandon sleep, the seal upon the acts of the three worlds, the bee resting on the lotus of your eyes,
like a garland of blue lotuses faded by enjoyment.
With your wide right eye, the birthplace of the sun,
make the worlds open like lotuses, O lord of the world.
With your left eye, pouring nectar that streams with the joy of moonrise,
revive all beings like night-lotuses, O soul of all beings.
O god, the gods await the glance of your favor.
Let this petition be heard, because the business of the worlds is weighty.
Hearing these words of the divine sages, his eyes clear from sleep,
with one half of his necklace resting where it had slipped aside, making a circle,
the god turned his neck and spoke to the gods, while with the rays of his teeth
he made, as it were, a cluster of lotus-fibers for the lotuses of their faces.
What is this gathering of the world-protectors, announcing counsel?
Surely the lands of the thirty gods have not been overrun by the lords of demons?
This radiance of your faces, surpassing heaps of opened lotuses,

children.text: iyaṃ vo vadanacchāyā na śaṃsati parābhavam ||
children.translated_text: with its filaments that are sprouts of light, does not indicate defeat.
And <s>Padmajanmā</s>, <s>Pitāmaha</s> himself, has come here;
therefore this beneficial matter for the worlds will not be a small one.
I am ready for your sake. Tell me now what must be done.
When the lord of gods had spoken thus, the four-faced one said:
You yourself know everything, all that is to be done, through yourself.

children.text: praśnājñāḥ kiṃtu bhavataḥ pareṇa na vilaṅghyate ||
children.translated_text: Yet a command in response to your question cannot be transgressed by another.

children.text: sahasraśīrṣaḥ śeṣo 'yaṃ vaktuṃ jānāti te stutim
children.translated_text: This thousand-headed <s>Śeṣa</s> knows how to utter your praise,

children.text: tavaiva bhāratī devī yadi vaiṣā sarasvatī ||
children.translated_text: if indeed that goddess <s>Sarasvatī</s> is your own speech.
When the fierce poisonous trees of the demons have been cut down by the saw of your discus,
the chariot of <s>dharma</s> in this world keeps its affection unbroken.
All the kings of the earth have prospered, following good conduct,
but through their abundant masses of forces the burden of the earth is great.
This is the earth's grave anxiety, from fear that she will sink:
because of the possible destruction of righteous kings, this undertaking has arisen.
Hearing this speech of <s>Prajāpati</s>, spoken for the good of creatures, the god
said, 'So be it,' and went together with the thirty gods to <s>Amarāvatī</s>.
Entering that city, rich in wish-granting trees and beautiful with jeweled mansions,
he occupied a splendid assembly hall gleaming with the radiance of lofty jeweled pillars.
There, when <s>Viṣṇu</s> was seated on a moonstone seat, like another milk-ocean,
the gods then obtained seats of gold and jewels.
At <s>Brahmā</s>'s word, when the door-keeper <s>Samīraṇa</s> stood there, staff in hand,
the assembly became silent like the milk-ocean asleep without wind.
Then, announced by name by the lotus-dweller himself,
she sat on the footstool before <s>Viṣṇu</s>, her face bent down.
Dark-hued, lotus-petal-eyed, her breasts dappled by the rays of her necklace,
the goddess Earth shone with the broken play of many jeweled lights.
Earth spoke, perfuming the divine fragrance of the lotus of her face,
and stealing the distress caused to tender creepers by swarms of bees:
O god, cherished by resting in the midst of the lotus of your feet,
I have never known the fatigue caused by the burden of the world.

children.text: lalanā kva nu nāmāhaṃ kva ceme kulabhūdharāḥ
children.translated_text: What am I, a mere woman, and what are these mountains of noble families?
This is the swelling strength of the support that comes from you.
Formerly, when I was sinking in the water as lightly as a lotus leaf,
you yourself, as the primeval boar, lifted me up on the tip of your tusk.
Formerly, when the world was one ocean, you churned up <s>Madhu</s> and <s>Kaiṭabha</s>,
and from their fat, made solid, you made me the earth.
When, in the time of <s>Bhārgava</s>, the warrior class was repeatedly destroyed in anger,
in time kings arose again in the lineage of <s>Manu</s>.
With the host of their excellent warriors, crowded with elephants and horses,
grown until there is no open space, I am oppressed by the burden.
Therefore give a moment's attention to some means for their destruction.
I have come for refuge to you, the refuge of the lords of the thirty gods.
Fire is the master of gold; the sharp-rayed sun is the master of cows.

children.text: tārakāṇāṃ guruḥ somaḥ sadā mama gururbhavān ||
children.translated_text: The moon is the master of the stars; you are always my master.
Hearing this speech of Earth, <s>Pitāmaha</s>, glanced at sideways by <s>Viṣṇu</s>,
understanding the truth of what she desired, spoke to the gods:
Let a descent in partial incarnations be made by you for the welfare of the earth.
This <s>Viṣṇu</s> himself is ready for an incarnation on the earth.
Long ago, while I was standing on the shore of the ocean with <s>Kaśyapa</s>,
the glorious ocean, adorned and accompanied by <s>Gaṅgā</s>, came to me.
When I was flooded by his waters, I angrily addressed him in his arrogance:
'Ho, you in royal guise, be <s>Śaṃtanu</s>'; as soon as he was thus addressed, he took on a body.
By my curse he was born as a lord of the earth named <s>Śaṃtanu</s>.
<s>Gaṅgā</s>, mother of the <s>Vasus</s>, followed him as his beloved.
In that lineage <s>Pāṇḍu</s> and <s>Dhṛtarāṣṭra</s> were born as kings on earth.
The portions of <s>Dharma</s>, <s>Anila</s>, <s>Indra</s>, and the <s>Aśvins</s> will come as the sons of <s>Pāṇḍu</s>.
Let the son of <s>Dhṛtarāṣṭra</s>, together with his younger brothers, be of the portion of <s>Kali</s>.

children.text: anyeṣu rājavaṃśeṣu bhavantu ca surāḥ pare ||
children.translated_text: And let the other gods be born in the other royal lineages.
<s>Rudra</s>, <s>Śiśirāṃśu</s>, the <s>Gandharvas</s>, serpents, and <s>Rākṣasas</s>,
in the terrible fire of battle produced by their mutual enmity,
may the dense forest of earthly kings go to destruction.
Having spoken to them thus, <s>Prajāpati</s> sent them forth to the earth,
and then the gods, ordered by him, descended to the earth in portions.
Meanwhile the blessed sage <s>Nārada</s>, a portion of <s>Hari</s>,
approached, making the directions golden-brown with his splendor.
He carried his curved vīṇā, as if the power of sound itself had taken form
within the narrow belly of the world; he knew the notes and was a treasury of meters.
A revealer of the secrets of the worlds, curious about the play of quarrel,
with his mass of matted hair bent down, he bowed to <s>Viṣṇu</s> and spoke:
Lord, by your command the lords of the gods have descended
among the lineages of kings on earth, but this effort is fruitless.
Against the wicked, against the arrogant great serpents and demons,
what power do the immortals have, even to touch them, without you, O supreme lord?

children.text: dānavā bhuvi saṃbhūtā bhavatā ye hatāḥ purā
children.translated_text: The Dānavas who were formerly slain by you have now been born on earth;
only you yourself, by descending, are able to destroy them at the root.
After killing the Dānava <s>Lavaṇa</s>, <s>Śatrughna</s>, the younger brother of <s>Rāghava</s>,

children.text: chittvā madhuvanaṃ cakre yāṃ purīṃ mathurāṃ purā ||
children.translated_text: cut down <s>Madhuvana</s> and formerly made the city <s>Mathurā</s> there.
In that city a king named <s>Kaṃsa</s> has now been born in the <s>Yadu</s> family;
he is that great Asura <s>Kālanemi</s>, whom you killed before.

children.text: hayagrīvādayo ye ca daityāḥ pūrvaṃ harāstvayā
children.translated_text: And those Daityas beginning with <s>Hayagrīva</s>, whom you destroyed before,
are now present on earth as <s>Keśin</s>, <s>Dhenuka</s>, <s>Ariṣṭa</s>, <s>Pralamba</s>, and others.
For their slaughter, Lord, undertake the effort yourself.
When <s>Nārada</s> had spoken thus, the Lord of the world said, So be it.
Asked by him about a birthplace suitable for the incarnation, the lotus-born <s>Brahmā</s> then said:
Listen, Lord, to who is the blessed father fitting for you.

children.text: yajñārthe yājñiyāṃ dhenuṃ purā putrasya kaśyapaḥ
children.translated_text: Long ago, for a sacrifice, <s>Kaśyapa</s> had a sacrificial cow;
<s>Aditi</s> and <s>Surabhi</s> were the beloved wives of that lord of creatures.
He has been born in the <s>Yādava</s> family as the greatly renowned <s>Vasudeva</s>;

children.text: devakī rohiṇī ceti te tasya dayite ubhe ||
children.translated_text: <s>Devakī</s> and <s>Rohiṇī</s> are his two beloved wives.
Taking the state of being his son, delighting in the play of cowherds,
showing deeds of utmost wonder, kill the Dānavas.

children.text: dhanyaḥ sa jagatāṃ vandyaḥ kasya vā na spṛhāpadam
children.translated_text: Blessed is he, honored by the worlds; for whom would he not be an object of longing,
when he hears you lisping the indistinct syllables, Father?
When <s>Hari</s> had accepted the words of the lotus-born one,
<s>Nārada</s>, a sower of division through curiosity and candor, went away.
Bound by his vow of wandering through the worlds with their varied suns,

children.text: sa mahīmetya mathurāṃ viveśa viṣadāṃ purīm ||
children.translated_text: he came to the earth and entered the splendid city <s>Mathurā</s>.
Seeing it, he was amazed: What is this family home of marvels,
this garden of all prosperities, this pleasure-grove of wish-granting creepers?
There he saw fierce <s>Kaṃsa</s>, seated on a throne among the kings,
newly powerful, terrible, the son of <s>Ugrasena</s>.
Honored by him, he entered that assembly, bright with jeweled thrones,
sat for a moment, and addressed that man proud of his strength:
<s>Kaṃsa</s>, while roaming through the worlds, I heard in the assembly of the gods
a counsel long pondered concerning the means of your death.

children.text: pituḥ svasuste devakyā yo garbho bhavitāṣṭamaḥ
children.translated_text: The eighth embryo that will be born from <s>Devakī</s>, your father's sister,

children.text: sānugasya sa te mṛtyurvihitaḥ śaṅkitaiḥ suraiḥ ||
children.translated_text: has been appointed by the fearful gods as death for you and your followers.
When the sage had said this and gone, <s>Kaṃsa</s>, breathing heavily as he sat in the assembly,
laughed, as if threatening the beauty of his enemies with his fangs.
Then he spoke to his ministers, his face unchanged even in boundless anger,
again and again looking up at the sky as if from envy of the gods:
Ah! This counsel of the heaven-dwellers has been told to us
by a foolish-minded sage whose nature is to divide.
Now I stand utterly opposed to the gods.
Let <s>Keśin</s> and the others, devoted to my purpose, roam the earth for destruction.
Let <s>Pralamba</s>, <s>Dhenuka</s>, <s>Ariṣṭa</s>, <s>Pūtanā</s>, <s>Kāliya</s>, and the rest,
through hatred of the gods, bring ruin upon the sacrificers in the world.
Let those always remain alert for the killing of <s>Devakī</s>'s embryos,
men and women loyal to me, with trustworthy reports.
Having said this to his ministers, <s>Kaṃsa</s> remained outwardly unchanged,
but inwardly he bore the burning of anxiety, unbearable as poison.
At that moment <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, who had fixed the time for protecting the world,
went to the underworld and saw those embryos born from <s>Kālanemi</s>.
Through fierce austerity they had formerly obtained a boon from the lotus-born <s>Brahmā</s>,
and <s>Hiraṇyakaśipu</s> cursed them as revilers of <s>Brahmā</s>:
Because you worshiped <s>Vidhi</s> while disregarding me,
therefore, first slain by your father, you shall die as embryos on earth.
Seeing them helpless under that curse, motionless beneath the waters,
seeing them asleep, the Lord spoke to Sleep embodied in her own form:
Cast these living beings yourself into the six wombs of <s>Devakī</s>.
There <s>Kaṃsa</s>, by his own design, will become their end.
But the seventh, the embryo in <s>Rohiṇī</s>, is to be removed by exchange;
after that I myself shall be the eighth embryo of <s>Devakī</s>.
In the cowherd settlement, <s>Yaśodā</s> by name is the wife of <s>Nanda Gopa</s>;
descend yourself into her womb at the same time as my birth.
In the eighth month, on the ninth day of the dark night, O doe-eyed one,
there the exchange will take place, since our births will be at the same time.
Then, when you have been struck violently upon a stone by <s>Kaṃsa</s>'s men,
O goddess, you will go to heaven, endowed with a divine body.

children.text: tatra tvaṃ śakrabhaginī bhūtvā pūjyā divaukasām
children.translated_text: There, having become the sister of <s>Śakra</s>, worshiped by the dwellers in heaven,
as <s>Durgā</s>, slayer of <s>Niśumbha</s> and <s>Śumbha</s>, you will make your seat on <s>Vindhya</s>.
Moon-faced, dark-bodied, lion-mounted, bearing a peacock-banner,
manifest and unmanifest, the supreme <s>śakti</s> (power), <s>Kālarātrī</s>, <s>Jayā</s>, and <s>Dhṛti</s>,
<s>Hrī</s>, <s>Śrī</s>, <s>Māyā</s>, <s>Mati</s>, <s>Puṣṭi</s>, the presiding divinity of the gods,

children.text: jananī vyāpinī kālī pārvatī dharaṇī prabhā ||
children.translated_text: the Mother, the all-pervading one, <s>Kālī</s>, <s>Pārvatī</s>, the Earth, and Radiance,
destroyer of all, terrible, auspicious, showering nectar,
<s>Navamī</s>, Presence, and giver of accomplishments: you will become all these.
Having instructed Sleep in this way, <s>Hari</s>, whose lotus-eyes were open from slumber,
meditated in his mind on that task, and the blessed Lord went to his own abode.

children.text: atha garbheṣu devakyāḥ ṣaṭsu kaṃsasya śāsanāt
children.translated_text: Then, when six embryos of <s>Devakī</s>, by <s>Kaṃsa</s>'s command,
had each in turn been killed by his cruel-acting servants,
and when the seventh too, called <s>Saṃkarṣaṇa</s>, had been drawn away and carried off,
into the womb-house of <s>Rohiṇī</s>, with her regarded as his own mother,
<s>Devakī</s> conceived the eighth embryo, the lord of the worlds,
by whom she became like daybreak when the sun is near.
Then, when the eighth month was complete, at midnight under <s>Abhijit</s>,
<s>Devakī</s> gave birth to <s>Viṣṇu</s>, as a fire-drill gives birth to flame.
At that very moment <s>Yaśodā</s> bore a daughter of pure radiance,
while the worlds were gladdened by the birth of <s>Acyuta</s>.
As the world trembled and the hosts of gods spoke auspicious words,
the quarters shone with showers of flowers, like the fame of <s>Hari</s>.
When the guards had been bewildered by Sleep, <s>Vasudeva</s>, his intention impelled by him,
secretly made the exchange of the two infants himself.
Having placed the son in the house of <s>Nandagopa</s> and taken that man's daughter,
fearful, he laid her down on <s>Devakī</s>'s birth-bed.
Then the guards, awakening and saying in wonder, 'This girl has been born,'
showed her to <s>Kaṃsa</s>, still wet with the waters of the womb.
Then, by his command, she was struck by them on the broad stone floor,
and, many-armed and bearing blazing weapons, she entered her own form like a flame of fire.
Adorned with a garland of stars as a necklace, with a moon-bright face,
she was the begetter of delusion in beings, like Night embodied.
She shone with earrings bright with the radiance of swan-like gems,
like the sky bearing the disks of moon and sun at setting and rising.
Adorned with peacock plumes and decorated with a peacock-banner,
dark, like the rainy season with <s>Śakra</s>'s bow and swollen clouds,
with a three-peaked crown laughing with many jewels,
her bound hair was adorned, like the earth possessing reddish mountains.
Accompanied by hosts of spirits, laughing again and again with a harsh sound,
tearing apart the darkness and threatening <s>Kaṃsa</s>, she said:
'<s>Kaṃsa</s>, when the time of <s>Kaṃsa</s>'s death has come, as you are dragged by your enemy,

children.text: vidārya jīvitaṃ dehe pāsyāmi tava śauṇitam ||
children.translated_text: I will tear the life from your body and drink your blood.'
Having said this, <s>Kātyāyanī</s> went to the desired region of heaven,
and the son of <s>Ugrasena</s>, ashamed that his effort had failed, trembled.

children.text: sa gatvā devakīṃ mūrdhnā praṇipatya prasādya ca
children.translated_text: He went to <s>Devakī</s>, bowed down with his head, conciliated her,

children.text: garbhāḥ kālena te mātaḥ kṣapitā ityabhāṣata ||
children.translated_text: and said, 'Mother, your embryos have been destroyed by Time.'
But the suspicious <s>Vasudeva</s> left <s>Rohiṇī</s>'s son,
of lovely moonlike brightness, in the houses of <s>Nandagopa</s> himself.
Having deposited the eldest infant, <s>Saṃkarṣaṇa</s>, with <s>Yaśodā</s>,
and while the affair of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> remained hidden, he became absorbed in anxious thought of him.
Then <s>Nandagopa</s>, urged by him who wished his son's welfare,
left terrible <s>Vṛndāvana</s>, infested with demons, thorns, and serpents,
and near the <s>Govardhana</s> forest, where the trees were tender by the <s>Yamunā</s>,
he made a cowherd settlement free from obstacles, surrounded by many cattle-stations.
There the <s>cātaka</s> birds were gladdened by the deep, dense roar of churning,
and the wind was filled with the aroma of ghee swirling from cooking.
The herds of cows, with calves hidden in inaccessible parts of the forest, lowed there,
and the deer stood motionless at the songs, sweet as cuckoos, of the cowherd women.
On the bank of the <s>Kālindī</s>, where children were swung by cane-creepers,
<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, emerald-bright, together with his moon-white brother,

children.text: vyavardhata vanodbhedaḥ sa gāṅga iva yāmunaḥ
children.translated_text: grew there like a forest sprout of the <s>Yamunā</s> beside one of the <s>Gaṅgā</s>.
Once, when he had fallen asleep beneath a cart, motionless and satisfied with breast-milk,
<s>Yaśodā</s> left him there and went to the <s>Yamunā</s>.
Then, waking, he softly tossed his hands and feet again and again,
and cried, as if marked by streams of milk through the gleam of his teeth.
Stretching his feet upward, his face opened wide by a yawn,
with one foot he overturned the cart and brought it down.
Meanwhile <s>Yaśodā</s> came near, her breasts flowing with milk,
and seeing the cart broken, she trembled, full of love for her son.
Taking up the unharmed child, she held him; alarmed, <s>Nanda</s> said this:
'By whom was this cart broken, without any blow from maddened bulls?'
When questioned in this way, the children said, 'By <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>.'

children.text: tataḥ kṛṣṇotsave loke supte niśi niśācarī
children.translated_text: Then, during the festival for <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, while the people slept at night,
a night-wandering woman named <s>Pūtanā</s> came by magic, her breasts streaming with milk.
Wishing for the infant's death, she placed her breast in his mouth,
and he drew it in and tore it away along with her life-breaths.
When she, roaring like a tiger, had been killed, there arose in fear
<s>Nandagopa</s>, together with his wife, became as if sinking and rising in an ocean.
Then, when the two of them had learned what had happened, they were filled with wonder and joy;

children.text: tau dampatī bahiḥ kaṃsabhayānno kaṃsabhayānno kiṃcidūcatuḥ ||
children.translated_text: yet because of fear of <s>Kaṃsa</s>, the married pair said nothing outside.
With slow placing of his feet, with soft goings and comings,
he who was capable of striding across the three worlds rained delight upon his kinsmen.
In time the two, <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> and <s>Saṃkarṣaṇa</s>, grew in the forest,
like two young lion-cubs filling out, as it were, with pride.
In their childish games, their bodies beautifully adorned, they shone,
as if they embraced and protected the earth, being able to lessen its burden.
Lovely, lotus-petal-eyed, with curling locks in motion,
with their smiles they seemed to make white pearl-strings upon their throats.
The body of each was foremost in equal beauty and sweetness;
for in the refuge of the great, surely, there is no opposition when the task is one.
There, when the god, protector of the three worlds, had willingly taken the form of a cowherd,
the dwellers in heaven came to envy the cowherds made blessed by his company.

children.text: dhartuṃ yadā yaśodā taṃ na śaśāka mahājavam
children.translated_text: When <s>Yaśodā</s> could not hold him, so swift was he,
the resolute woman then bound <s>Dāmodara</s> around the belly with a rope.
With force he dragged along the mortar tied by that rope,
and roamed in the forest, skillful in play and free from fatigue.
The cowherds were astonished at his dragging of the mortar,
though the world had not been astonished in him even at the firmness that supported Mandara.
On the bank of the <s>Yamunā</s> there were two great arjuna trees standing close together;
reaching them and getting between them, he pulled the mortar with force.
Uprooted by his strength, those two trees at once fell with a crash,
by which the waters of the <s>Yamunā</s> became deep and agitated with turmoil.
Seeing that, the cowherd boys, overwhelmed by fear and wonder,
went to <s>Yaśodā</s> and spoke in voices confused by agitation:
"Ah, careless woman, you were deluded by comfortable sleep;

children.text: pūjyau tau tava putrasya patitāvupari drumau ||
children.translated_text: those two venerable trees have fallen over your son.
Go and see the child, freed by fate from a great danger."
Hearing this, <s>Yaśodā</s>, as if drowned in sweat, went trembling.
When she saw her son between those two great trees,

children.text: saṃtrāsaṃ ca prasādaṃ ca vismayaṃ ca yayau kramāt ||
children.translated_text: she passed in turn through terror, relief, and amazement.
Then all the elder cowherds came together in alarm
and said, "By what divine powers have these two protectors of the settlement been felled?"
There was no thunderclap from clouds; in a cloudless sky, what question could there be of lightning?
No rutting elephant is here; why, then, this sudden destruction of the two trees?
While the circle of cowherds was speaking thus,
<s>Nanda</s> took up his son after releasing him, looking reproachfully at <s>Yaśodā</s>.
When <s>Nandagopa</s>, with his followers, had gone off blaming his own wife,
in every house there arose a strange, wondrous tale of the breaking of the trees.
Then the two, <s>Saṃkarṣaṇa</s> and <s>Acyuta</s>, with childhood somewhat loosened from them,
went about in the forest, dressed in blue and yellow garments and marked with side-locks.
With clusters of flowers worn as crests, they produced the illusion of fruit,
like two serpent-princes bearing foremost jewels as protective forehead marks.
Rich in fresh beauty from ornaments of peacock feathers,
they were streams of the nectar of loveliness, like two sons of the pārijāta tree.
Their natural voices were sweet with the soft notes of small flutes;
they seemed like two young kinnaras seated on the rocks of a lofty mountain.
They whirled skillfully with fine balls leaping upward,
and, charming with varied garlands, seemed like two sons of Vidyādharas.
Holding in their hands little play-bows marked like arrows,
the two heroes seemed to be <s>Rāghava</s> and <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s> come again into the forest.
As they played, noble in their delight, those lotus-eyed two
shone with the charm of youth now drawing somewhat near.
There, where the herbs and trees were sparse, faded by long enjoyment,
<s>Keśava</s>, eager for the pleasure of a fresh forest, did not find delight.
Creating fear in the cowherd settlement by means of hidden, illusory wolves,
he went to play near <s>Vṛndāvana</s>, beautiful with the <s>Kālindī</s>.
When the cowherd settlement had settled there, fearless and in a desirable refuge,
a certain enjoyment of the new forest arose among the cowherd clan.
Then the dark rainy season was seen, with newly risen clouds as breasts,
like a new bride of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, arranged for fresh delight.
With new rain-clouds in the sky, moving with the grace of young elephants,
it became like the rising smoke from the fire of Love in the minds of separated women.
Then the wind, as if fanning victorious King Love with fly-whisks,
was impelled by the sighs of thoughts belonging to women in separation.
On the earth the ketaka spikes were white like the smiles of beloved women,
like fragments of the moon scattered by the crushing of clouds.
Rows of cranes moved in the sky with its heavy thunder,
like masses of gleaming tusks of mighty elephants in the form of intoxicated clouds.
Between the clouds with <s>Śakra</s>'s bow and the forests with the dances of peacocks,
there arose, as it were, a rivalry of gathered splendor.
Bearing fresh, dark masses of tamāla trees and plantains washed by rain,
the earth shone like a young woman after an oily bath.
With leaping waves for movements, bends for brows, and laughter in heaps of foam,
she wandered in the <s>Yamunā</s> forest like an intoxicated youthful woman.
A certain garland-like brilliance of lightning shone among the clouds,
like a spray of heated jāmbūnada gold clinging to the summit of <s>Meru</s>.
Somewhere, flocks of royal swans, startled by the dark clouds, departed.
as if the beds of night-lotuses were searching for the moon, long lost.
In that season, heavy with the joyful fragrance of kadamba and kuṭaja blossoms,
in the time that was death for separated lovers, <s>Saṃkarṣaṇa</s> said to <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>:
Look, <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, the sky is filled with clouds that move about,
laughing with cranes like foam, as if with the waters of the <s>Yamunā</s>.
The dark body of the rain-clouds, marked by lightning as by a yellow garment,
and hung with a forest garland, shines just like yours.
Hearing these words of his elder brother, an ornament of affection, <s>Hari</s>,
adorned with play, longed for sport in the sweetly adorned forest.
Then, after a break in the rains, when everything seemed renewed,
one day <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> wandered in the forest without his brother.
Surrounded by cowherd boys, he came to a vast banyan tree,
which seemed to rise up to measure the sky with its mass of spreading arms.
It seemed to have risen out of curiosity to see the mountain peaks of the clans,
rich with <s>Vidyādharas</s> and inhabited by the gods.
It was the ornament of the earth, generous with good shade and fulfilling all hopes:
a tree named <s>Bhāṇḍīra</s>, like a palace of the forest goddesses.
Seeing that smooth, unfailing friend of delight, <s>Śauri</s>,
rejoiced and moved about beneath it, making amusement with song and music.
Then he saw the <s>Kālindī</s>, like a flood of rut-juice from the elephant of the world,
her moving, curling waves like the long braid of the earth.
She had a garland of stars made of foam and bubbles, fit for holy people,
and, entering the good shade of tāpiccha trees, seemed like night turned liquid.
She was marked by gleaming, swollen hoods, flashing wide as leaping śaphara fish,
like an army of serpents, her expanse of waves fragile and broken.
Her face was open lotuses, her eyes blooming blue lotuses,
her swelling breasts cakravāka birds; she was dark, with a swan-white smile.
She seemed like the jewel-mountain caverns melting under the heat of the fierce-rayed sun,
set flowing as emerald liquid roaring in whirlpools.
In one place she was still, as if asleep; in another she was wild, as if drunk;
elsewhere she seemed faint from the force of poison, as if bitten by a snake.
In one place she seemed afraid and hidden; in another, agitated and bewildered;
elsewhere, restless with strong coquettish motions, she seemed like a proud young woman.
Her waters were raised high by the jar-like breasts of cowherd women bathing in her,
and <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> rejoiced on seeing her, as if she were a charming young woman.
Then he saw a lake, dreadful and deep as the floor of the netherworld,
crowded with hundreds of terrible waves, crooked like the frown of black death.
It was stained with darkness, exceedingly fierce, and caused fear without reason;
everyone avoided it from afar, as they avoid a powerful wicked man.
As if with a blazing resolve, 'Even now the world has not been swallowed by me,'
it seemed to breathe without ceasing through waters that looked like rising smoke.
It was pervaded by terrible venomous serpents lying in hollows on the bank,
a lake bringing terror like its own realm, devoid of moon, sun, and stars.
After looking for a moment at that lake, impossible to disturb from afar, <s>Hari</s> thought:
In this lake lives that serpent named <s>Kāliya</s>, fierce with kālakūṭa poison,
dark in form and a source of fear to all living beings.
By his poisonous breaths this bank of the <s>Yamunā</s> has been polluted.
Maddened by excessive arrogance, he is intoxicated; here he deserves destruction.
My birth is chiefly for the destruction of evil-souled beings.
Having so reflected, from the edge of the lake he went to a young kadamba tree.
Tightening his waist-cloth, he climbed it and fell from the sky into the water.
At the swift descent of the roaring dark cloud that was <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>,
the churned water rose up with terrible crests of waves.
From the crash of billows that flew up like distant mountains,
there arose a dreadful clanging impact that seemed to strike the sky.
Then <s>Kāliya</s> appeared, dreadful with fire-belching poisonous hissing,
five-mouthed and red-eyed.
By his coil, like a mountain of collyrium, expanding on every side,
the blocked-up water rose and entered the sky.
In the ring of flame made by the blaze of his anger,
there quickly arose in the waters a dissolution that created the illusion of another submarine fire.
The streams of poisonous fire born from the grinding of his teeth
at once turned the rows of trees on the bank to ash.
Then <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, being encircled by the coils of the black serpent,
shone like a tamāla tree ringed round by the waters of the <s>Yamunā</s>.
When the cowherd boys saw <s>Govinda</s>, together with the serpent-lord's attendants,
surrounded on every side by venomous flames from the tips of his fangs,
they were terrified, came back to <s>Vraja</s>, and cried out, their balls fallen from their hands:
This <s>Dāmodara</s> has fallen into the terrible water of <s>Kāliya</s>!
Now he is wrapped by the serpent, dreadful as death and bristling with poison.

children.text: vacaḥ śrutvā yayuḥ sarve nandagopamukhā hradam ||
children.translated_text: Hearing this speech, all of them, with <s>Nandagopa</s> at their head, went to the lake.
When <s>Nandagopa</s>, stunned by fresh distress and his heart shaken by doubt,
was looking at the face of his son enveloped by the serpent,
and when the women were loud with high-pitched laments, torn open by <s>Yaśodā</s>'s grief,
they were exceedingly tormented, as if pervaded by the poisons of attachment.
Then, when <s>Saṃkarṣaṇa</s> had come to the bank, <s>Hari</s> was awakened by a mere sign from him.
With his arms he struck the serpent's terrible coil,
and, trampling it with his feet, <s>Hari</s> escaped from the bondage.
Bending down the circle of hoods, jeweled and blazing with fire,
<s>Madhusūdana</s> climbed onto the broad middle head.
Then he, the weighty teacher of all the moving and unmoving worlds,
crushed him with the placing of his feet, as if dancing gracefully.
Then, his pride fallen, his courage slipping away, and his fierce poison vomited forth,
he addressed <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, his syllables faltering as blood poured from him.
Terrified and helpless, I must be protected by you in every way.
This pitiable sign of folded hands is now my life-giving merit.
Hearing this, <s>Dāmodara</s> said to the lord of serpents:
This lake, with its inauspicious ways, may be used, but without you.
Therefore go to the ocean, if you wish to live.
There the mark of my foot on you will be protection against <s>Tārkṣya</s>.
When, at that command, the serpent had gone away at once with his followers,
the cowherds went off praising <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, filled with joyful wonder.
Then <s>Haladhara</s> and <s>Acyuta</s>, rich in playful sport, entered
a forest dark with broad tāla, hintāla, and tamāla trees.
Their minds were delighted and intoxicated by tasting the fruits of the tall palms,
and the two roamed there, intent on the bustle of boys' games.
Then a demon named <s>Dhenuka</s>, who dwelt in the Tāla forest, came near,
a donkey with a terrible mane, massive shoulders, and a hard-set frame.
Surrounded on every side by his huge-bodied donkey attendants,
the dense tāla grove seemed pervaded as if by rising smoke.
Then <s>Dhenuka</s>, in great anger, his eyes red as blood,
tore up the ground with his hooves, eager to kill <s>Rāma</s> and <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>.
As if summoning the demons who dwell in the underworld,
and as if striking with his brays, armed with teeth fierce as thunderbolts,
he rushed swiftly at <s>Saṃkarṣaṇa</s>, his tail wildly agitated,
like a troubled cloud, its single crest tossed by the wind, rushing against the moon.
Then, after attacking <s>Rauhiṇeya</s> with his teeth, while he remained unshaken,
he turned his face away, facing backward in order to strike a blow.
<s>Halāyudha</s> seized that assailant by those very two hooves
and hurled him onto the top of a palm tree, as if seeking fruit.
His great tree-like trunk was broken and his hard bones split apart,
and he fell lifeless to the ground along with the palm fruits.
Then, when he and his followers had been slain, and that donkey-like prowess destroyed,
that broad Tāla forest became accessible, free from obstruction.
Again, going to the <s>Bhāṇḍīra</s> forest, the two playful ones
played with the cowherd boys in games of paired wrestling and throwing down.
Then there came to those two one adorned with a crest of wild flowers,
a dānava named <s>Pralamba</s>, hidden by the deceitful disguise of cowherd dress.
Winning their confidence through games and delighting them again and again,
one day he carried off <s>Keśava</s>'s elder brother, who had mounted on his shoulder.
Having carried him away very swiftly, he revealed his own form,
and by it the quarters seemed, through fear, to be covered with a cloth of darkness.
On his head, shaped like the peak of a collyrium mountain and flashing brightly,
a crest-jewel shone tawny like a mass of forest-fire flames.
From his mouth there shone forth a row of smoky flames,
blue and yellow like a banner hanging from an archway of fangs.
On the demon's shoulder, rugged like a mass of dark mountain rock,
the son of <s>Rohiṇī</s> bore the appearance of an autumn cloud.
As he was quickly being carried away by him, having assumed a human condition,
<s>Keśava</s> reminded him from afar of his ancient form.
That form was the supreme radiance, lord of speech, facing every direction,
made of all the gods, true, endless, unborn, and imperishable.
Assuming his own vast strength, capable of bearing up the earth,
the slayer of <s>Dhenuka</s> struck <s>Pralamba</s> on the head with his fist.
From the fall of that fist, the frontal skull split open and burst apart,
and the demon's head sank into his body amid a scattered spray of blood.
When <s>Rāma</s> had slipped down from his shoulder, <s>Pralamba</s>'s mountain-vast body,
with its two arms hanging down, fell to the ground.
When <s>Pralamba</s> had thus been felled by mighty <s>Baladeva</s>,
and the four months of the rainy season had slowly passed there,
as the sacrificial festival approached, bringing joy filled with fresh eagerness,
preparations arose among the forest-dwellers.
Then autumn appeared, garlanded with the fragrance of saptacchada blossoms and ankleted with swans,
with the clear moon for her face and blooming blue lotuses for her eyes,
like a young woman invited to that great festival of <s>Vraja</s>,
her sky smiling with the beauty of white clouds.

children.text: tatra gopagirā jñātvā yāgaṃ kṛṣṇaṃ marutpateḥ
children.translated_text: There, learning from the cowherds' words of the sacrifice for the lord of the Maruts, <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>
spoke, as if sending forth <s>Pāñcajanya</s> through white smiles in his glances:

children.text: aho nu hāsyajananī mugdheyaṃ bhavatāṃ matiḥ
children.translated_text: Ah, this innocent thinking of yours is indeed laughable.

children.text: yāgaḥ śakrāya nārhe 'yaṃ gopā hi giridaivatāḥ ||
children.translated_text: This sacrifice to <s>Śakra</s> is not proper; cowherds have the mountain as their deity.
At his words, when the cowherds undertook the sacrifice to the mountain,
mountains of food were prepared, with great streams of ghee and milk.
At that sacrifice of Mount <s>Govardhana</s>, supplied with abundant food,
the earth seemed covered with snow by rice puddings covered with curds.
Adorned with peacock feathers and crowned with crests of flowers,
at that sacrifice the cowherds and the cows were beautifully decorated.
On the mountain summit, <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, the soul of the universe, with a supreme body
having the form of the mountain, ate all that had been offered by them.
<s>Kṛṣṇa</s> himself, together with the cowherds, bowed down to his own divine, great body,

children.text: praṇanāma svayaṃ kṛṣṇo gopaiḥ saha giriprabham ||
children.translated_text: which shone like the mountain and was noble with a smile of delight.
When that great festival had taken place, <s>Śatamanyu</s>, blazing with anger,
ordered terrible saṃvartaka clouds for the destruction of <s>Vraja</s>.
Urged on by him, they quickly came, dense as slabs of blue mountain rock,
and the thick clouds made the world overcast, as if with hundreds of nights of death.
With clouds like masses of split collyrium, powerful with thunder,

children.text: grastā ivoddhataiḥ kṣipraṃ nādṛśyanta diśo daśa ||
children.translated_text: the ten directions were quickly no longer seen, as though swallowed by those violent ones.
Then torrents shaped like elephant trunks, reeling with the fury of pillars,
fell upon the mountain, an utter overthrow of steadiness.
The descending outpourings of water, terrible as the loud laughter of Time,
shone like the waterfalls of black clouds that were themselves mountains.
Then there arose a flood of water, formed from masses of terrifying, far-spreading clouds,
restless with swelling, heavy waves.
Before the roaring cloud-demons, whose hair was tawny lightning,
the earth, covered with water, seemed to go somewhere else out of fear.
Those terrible clouds, controlled by <s>Śakra</s> and marked by blazing thunderbolts,
brought slaughter upon the cows through the fall of rain and lightning.
As they fell here and there, their eyes fixed on the paths,
the cows, overcome by terror and cold, suffered a dreadful destruction.
"This is the very beginning of the cosmic dissolution, terrible with the <s>Puṣkara</s> and <s>Āvarta</s> clouds,"
such was the thought of the frightened cowherds.
Seeing that terrible devastation, come near for the destruction of the cows,
<s>Govinda</s>, protector of the worlds, considered their protection for a moment.
"I shall forcibly uproot this lord of mountains, <s>Govardhana</s>,
and make it an umbrella, a vast shelter for the cows standing nearby."

children.text: iti dhyātvā dhiyaṃ dhīro nidadhe bhūdhare dṛśam
children.translated_text: Thinking thus, the steadfast wise one fixed his gaze on the mountain,
as though offering a garland of blooming lotuses to win its consent for the instant of uprooting.
Then at once the soul of the universe, endowed with great strength,
lifted the mountain with his two arms, while its roots, peaks, and slopes split apart.
The snakes of the uprooted mountain, hanging from its roots,
quickly appeared as if emerging from the netherworld, and became like a network of sinews.
With its waterfalls dammed by masses of crushed stones,
the quarters seemed wrapped in silk cloths of pale waves.
Covered with heaps of yellow orpiment dust, whirled about by gusts of wind
and cast down from that mountain, <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> shone as if clothed in yellow garments.
The clouds shaken off along its sides, as it sprang up for a moment,
gave sky-wanderers the illusion that the mountain was flapping wings.
When that mountain had become an umbrella through <s>Govinda</s>'s staff-like arm,
the rows of blooming garlands that slipped down on it created the semblance of hanging festoons.
"Today, after a very long time, we mountains have become free-moving;
O bearer of the thunderbolt, abandon your pride in having cut off the wings of mountains."
With the sounds of girdles and anklets from Vidyādhara women, doe-eyed and flying up in terror,
that mountain seemed to say this very thing.
With the roars of lions agitated as their ranges and resting places were overturned,
it seemed to threaten the powerful masses of dreadful clouds.
With leaders of elephant-herds thrown into confusion by the strain of being uprooted,
it shone in the sky as if with clouds struck down by the scraping of its crests.
With dust from clusters of flowers on its great branches whirling about,
it again and again made what seemed to be protective circles for the cows.
With wave-like pearl necklaces shaken loose from Siddha women who were falling in fright,
the mountain, standing in the sky, seemed to laugh at the mountains below.

children.text: taṃ dṛṣṭvā khecarāḥ prāhuḥ kimayaṃ girirutthitaḥ
children.translated_text: Seeing it, the skyfarers said, "What is this mountain that has risen up,
if it is not the beginning of dissolution, if it is not an untimely catastrophe?"
Then, at <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>'s command, the cowherds entered that broad earth-house made by the uprooted mountain,

children.text: vipulaṃ viviśuḥ śāntyai nikhilaiḥ saha godhanaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: for safety, together with all their wealth of cattle.
In that windless and waterless, very spacious slope of the mountain,
the cows and cowherds stood protected by the abode of the world.
Then, when seven nights had passed beneath the rain-covered sky, the lord of the Maruts,
ashamed that his undertaking had failed, went away together with the clouds.
Then the preceptor of the world, with mere play,
set that huge, high-peaked, heavy mountain back in its own place.
When that mountain had been held up for seven nights, the thousand-eyed one, bearing <s>Garuḍa</s> as his mark,
came in person, greatly astonished, to see him.
Descending from his divine elephant as if from a moving <s>Kailāsa</s>,
he saw <s>Madhusūdana</s> seated on a rock of <s>Govardhana</s>.
The heat of the sun was shaded by the wings of the invisible <s>Tārkṣya</s>,
and he filled the sky with a radiance that seemed beyond all reckoning.
He had the fine hue of a peacock's neck and garments bright as heated gold,
like a peak of a sapphire mountain touched by the warmth of early sunlight.
Seeing <s>Hari</s>, beloved of <s>Kamalā</s>, wearing the dress of a cowherd,
he inwardly congratulated himself on being thousand-eyed.
With masses of broad rays from the jewels of his crown, earrings, and armlets,
he seemed again and again to cast thousands of rainbows into the quarters.
Approaching <s>Keśava</s>, <s>Śakra</s> spoke words suited to affection,
as though filling the ten directions with nectar through the gleam of his teeth.
"This deed of yours is beyond the gods, O <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>; what wonder is there in that,
when even the smallest portion of your power is the refuge of all the worlds?
Above all the worlds stand the wish-granting cows;
by the command of those honored by the gods, and of <s>Brahmā</s> too, I..."
"I have come, O <s>Govinda</s>, to consecrate you in the desired kingship over the cows."

children.text: ityuktvā ratnakumbhena mūrdhni tasya dadau payaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Having spoken thus, he poured water from a jeweled jar upon his head.
After consecrating <s>Upendra</s>, <s>Indra</s> again and again propitiated him and said:

children.text: pālyastvayā sakhā bandhuḥ svasreyo janakasya yaḥ ||
children.translated_text: "You must protect your friend and kinsman, the son of your father's sister.
When you, O <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, destroyer of daityas, have killed <s>Keśin</s> and <s>Kaṃsa</s>,
that <s>Dhanaṃjaya</s>, with you as his ally, will conquer the earth."

children.text: iti praṇayino vācaṃ kṛṣṇaḥ śrutvā śacīpateḥ
children.translated_text: Hearing this affectionate speech of the lord of <s>Śacī</s>, <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>,
who knew the course of the <s>Bhārata</s> story, assented, saying, "So be it."
Having thus spoken privately with the slayer of the asura <s>Jambha</s>,
he went through the sky by a cloud split by <s>Airāvaṇa</s>'s trunk.
The cowherds, thinking that god in cowherd dress to be wondrous,

children.text: mudritā iva tacchaktyā mugdhā no kiṃcidūcire ||
children.translated_text: as if sealed by his power and bewildered, said nothing.
Then people drank in with their eyes that lotus-petal-eyed one,
all his childhood gone, full of the beauty of abundant youth.
On autumn nights, white with the smiles of the full moon,
he, dear to love, sported with women whose eyes stole the beauty of does.
Fond of fights between lustful bulls and of wrestling bouts,
he became charming through the impetuosity of heroic and erotic passion.
Those women became practiced in clever sayings, eager in adorning themselves,
astonishing in speech, and ready for amorous gestures.
An effort to imitate his sports, delight in hearing tales of him,
and joy in free conversation with him arose in some extraordinary way among the cowherd women.
For <s>Hari</s>'s delight, the faces of those innocent women,
with naturally smiling, quivering sprout-like lips, became especially dear.
That they were no longer under the control of their elders, though dependent on them, and had abandoned household duties,
and that they became hostile to their own people, was all the unfolding of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>'s face.
