Though bashful, the proud women showed manifest transformations of love;
though slender, they grew even thinner, their minds fixed on him.
"Why, friend, are you trembling, sweating, and suddenly fainting?
Surely you have not been bitten, heedless girl, by the serpent <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>?

children.text: nāyaṃ tava gṛhe mārgo mārgo 'yaṃ vijane vane
children.translated_text: This is not the path to your house; this is the path in the lonely forest,
to the play-house of the vāṇīra creepers on the bank of the <s>Yamunā</s>.
In that flower-grove, did the six-footed <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>
make a wound on your lip, so that your face is bent downward?
If the cowherd maidens sing of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>'s deeds,

children.text: tvaṃ na smarasi kiṃ mūḍhe srastaṃ śīlamivāṃśukam ||
children.translated_text: why do you not remember, foolish girl, your virtue fallen like your garment?
Drunk with pride, saying 'I am beloved of <s>Dāmodara</s>,' do you not see
that he is attached to trysts with hundreds of lovers and has many beloveds?

children.text: kiṃ nu nāma stanau tanvi sotkampau vinigūhase
children.translated_text: Why indeed, slender one, do you hide your breasts, which are trembling?
And what are you doing with your face, its cheeks marked with horripilation?
Here is a dark woman, blue as a blue lotus and smiling like a flower,
and <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> moves in secret; how can you go alone?"
Thus the cowherd women, fortunate in union, spoke among themselves with jealousy,
freely and resentfully, tormented by the arrows of love.
With fresh vañjula shoots torn by the fingernails of beloved women,
the forest became disordered, as if by arrows, in the passion of love-beds.
His beloveds, intoxicated and stirred by passion,
with lovely faces and rolling eyes, drank in his still lovelier face.
As they went helplessly to their assignations with <s>Keśava</s>,
their jealous glances fell upon the moon, fearing that it might see them.
When <s>Mādhava</s> was intent on the sweet, noble lovemaking of beautiful women,
<s>Manobhava</s> considered himself fruitful and blessed.

children.text: aho nu jayinī śaktiḥ samarasya smayakāriṇī
children.translated_text: "Ah, victorious indeed is the power of passion, producing pride in battle,
since its perfect loving course extends even to the preceptor of <s>Prajāpati</s>."
Then, once, while <s>Keśava</s> was rich in sports with women,
at the end of twilight there appeared a daitya in the form of a maddened bull.
<s>Ariṣṭa</s>, wicked in conduct, sharp-horned and red-eyed,
was black like a mass of darkness heaped together by moonbeams.
Terrible, frightening the bulls, with a roar deep as a kettledrum,
he was formidable with shoulders hard as slabs of blue mountain stone.
As his eyes were fixed on <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>'s belly, ready for a blow,
his pair of horns took on the likeness of the gateway of death.
<s>Acyuta</s> seized that fierce, pride-swollen attacker,
as a flatterer seizes a wicked fool newly come to power.
Seized by that strong younger brother of <s>Baladeva</s>,
he became bewildered, violently shaking and raising a cloth of dust with his tail.
As his face tossed and he made a dreadful bellow,
a broad mass of foam shone on his neck like a pearl necklace on a serpent-slayer.

children.text: tataḥ kaṇṭhaṃ nipīḍyāsya dhṛtvā mūrdhni padaṃ javāt
children.translated_text: Then, swiftly pressing his throat and placing his foot on his head,
<s>Hari</s> tore out one horn and struck him in the face.
Struck by the sharp horn, the dānava fell to the ground,
with a gurgling roar shaken by the outpouring of clotted blood.
When that <s>Ariṣṭa</s>, an ill omen to the dwellers in heaven, had been slain,
the power of the lord of <s>Mathurā</s> spread before the mountain-dwellers.
He thought of summoning the elder <s>Vṛṣṇi</s>s and the wise men, led by <s>Vasudeva</s>,
as well as his father <s>Ugrasena</s>, the <s>Dārdikya</s>s, <s>Akrūra</s>, and <s>Sātyaka</s>,
who were skilled in policy, for a decision;
at midnight, when the movement of people was silent and the servants had dispersed,
by the radiance of jeweled ornaments marked with reflections of lamps,
he seemed to reveal outwardly the flame of the hidden fire of his anxiety.
Then he spoke, after looking for a moment at the faces of the proud men,
relating, with a long sigh, this new humiliation at the hands of the enemy:
Before you, who are learned, famed for substance, and endowed with courage,
this torment of honor's decline is being pointed out.
Through heedlessness, or through arrogance, by our forgetting some small matter,
dust born from feet has been placed upon our crest-jewels.
You, who are versed in dignity and cannot endure equality even with the guru of the gods,

children.text: spardhayā bata lajjante yudhi vajrāyudhena ye ||
children.translated_text: and who, alas, are ashamed to rival <s>Vajrāyudha</s> in battle,
you are the ministers of that man, whose splendor rests upon his ministers;

children.text: tasya kā nāma gaṇanā gaṇanāthe 'pi jāyate ||
children.translated_text: what reckoning of him, indeed, can arise even for <s>Gaṇanātha</s>?
This is the ripening of an enemy's birth that was ignored with contempt,
by which even we have now been brought under the control of anxiety.
It is heard that <s>Nandagopa</s>'s child, whose deeds have grown great,
is, I suspect, a new and heavy terror causing alarm even among the daityas.
By placing his foot upon the head of the serpent <s>Kāliya</s>,

children.text: svarvīkṛtāni śūrāṇāṃ śirāṃsi ca yaśāṃsi ca ||
children.translated_text: he made both the heads and the fame of heroes reach heaven.
By him, together with his elder brother, <s>Pralamba</s>, <s>Ariṣṭa</s>, and <s>Dhenuka</s> were slain,
men for whom even <s>Śakra</s> was only an object of contempt in battle.
The mountain named <s>Govardhana</s> was held up by his hand for seven days;

children.text: smayāya durnimittāya nāśāya ca na kasya saḥ ||
children.translated_text: for whom was that not a cause of wonder, an evil omen, and destruction?

children.text: na jānīmaḥ sa kiṃ tāvadbhūtamatyadbhutaṃ kṣitau
children.translated_text: We do not know what sort of exceedingly marvelous being he is, arisen on earth,
by whom our prowess is being dragged downward.
Therefore this onset of calamity must be considered by you, wise heroes,
as an axe against the flowering creepers of fame.
And this was said before by <s>Nārada</s> himself, when he returned again:
'<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, the son of <s>Vasudeva</s>, is staying in <s>Nandagopa</s>'s house.
And that daughter of <s>Nandagopa</s>, whom you dashed against the stone,
went to the thickets of <s>Vindhya</s>, worshiped by <s>Pulinda</s>s and <s>Śabara</s>s.
She slew the two daityas <s>Niśumbha</s> and <s>Śumbha</s>, who possessed dense might;
the exchange of those two embryos had been arranged by <s>Vasudeva</s>.

children.text: kṛṣṇaḥ sa te bhayasthānamityuktvā nārado yayau
children.translated_text: '<s>Kṛṣṇa</s> is that source of fear for you.' Having said this, <s>Nārada</s> departed.

children.text: so 'yaṃ bandhuḥ kṛtaghno me vasudevaḥ sthito 'ntike ||
children.translated_text: This ungrateful kinsman of mine, <s>Vasudeva</s>, remains close at hand,
by whom our fame has been set upon a balance against the suspicion of destruction,
and the drops of whose sin are foul with the whirlpools of hell.
With what sin can that ungrateful, lowest man be compared?
This crooked serpent, filled with dreadful hālāhala poison,

children.text: dhṛtaḥ sarpo nijagṛhe yenāptaḥ satkule kaliḥ
children.translated_text: has been kept by me myself in my own house, through whom calamity has come into a good family.
This man with a falsely white beard, this dull enemy under the disguise of kinship,
<s>Vasudeva</s>, is always crooked; though fit for death, he has been protected.
Those expert in sound policy have declared that such men should be suspected in every way by kings.

children.text: ataḥ saṃcintyate ḍimbo na tu me gaṇanāspadam
children.translated_text: Therefore the boy is being considered, but he is not something that counts for me.
For the sacrificial fire of my true valor, massive enough to devour the world,
the cowherd child is not even a moth in the interval.
Or else, if he, together with his elder brother, behaves properly toward us,
what harm will there be? He will become a sharer in my enjoyments among my kinsmen.

children.text: akrūro madgirā yātu vrajaṃ dānapatiḥ svayam ||
children.translated_text: Let <s>Akrūra</s>, the lordly giver, go in person to <s>Vraja</s> at my command.
Having summoned those two through him, I wish to see the boys.
Let <s>Nandagopa</s> and the others, tribute-payers under my rule,
come to the bow-festival, ready to provide additional payments.
And those two, <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> and <s>Saṃkarṣaṇa</s>, who stir delight in heroes,

children.text: mallābhyāṃ yudhyamānau me raṅge prītatiṃ kariṣyataḥ
children.translated_text: while fighting with my two wrestlers in the arena, will give me pleasure.
When the divinely-sighted <s>Akrūra</s> heard what had been spoken by <s>Kaṃsa</s>,
that tiger of the <s>Yādava</s>s, eager for the sight of <s>Śauri</s>, set out.
When <s>Akrūra</s> had gone to the cowherd settlement, those aged bulls of the <s>Vṛṣṇi</s>s,
angered by the denunciation of <s>Vasudeva</s>, stood with downcast faces.
Then the grandfather <s>Andhaka</s>, like another grandsire,
a formidable and hard-to-overcome restrainer, addressed <s>Kaṃsa</s>:

children.text: vandhyāḥ kule 'pi satataṃ mayanye dhanyatarāḥ striyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: I think that women, even if barren in the family, are more blessed,

children.text: na kulaghnaḥ suto yāsāṃ kadācidapi jāyate
children.translated_text: if a son who destroys the family is never born to them.
Never upon tongues hard as thunderbolts, sharp, and cruel in action
does Fortune, tender as a lotus shoot and dwelling in nectar, remain.
Alas, after a long time the <s>Yādava</s>s and <s>Vṛṣṇi</s>s have come to a pitiable state,
since you, <s>Kaṃsa</s>, a boy who insults elders, are their leader.
What dull-minded, almost mad man speaks in such a way?
A son was somehow protected by his father, <s>Vasudeva</s>; what wonder is that?
Here there is nothing dearer to embodied beings than a son.
Son, ask your own father about the weight of affection for a son.
If a son, who is a rescue in the next world, has been protected by his father,

children.text: tasyāsya vācyatā keyaṃ yūyaṃ sarve 'pi putriṇaḥ
children.translated_text: what blame belongs to him? All of you too have sons.
The hero <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, <s>Vasudeva</s>'s son, younger brother of <s>Saṃkarṣaṇa</s>,
must by all means be conciliated by you with the thought that he is kin and beloved.

children.text: hitaṃ pathyaṃ ca me mohānna kariṣyasi cedvacaḥ ||
children.translated_text: If, out of delusion, you will not act on my beneficial and wholesome words,
then today this is the full limit of the power of your sovereignty.
Sequences of evil omens announcing destruction are being seen;
for you there is no better pacification of them than alliance with <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>.
Hearing <s>Andhaka</s>'s words, <s>Kaṃsa</s>, sighing and frowning,

children.text: nirjagāma tataḥ kaṃsaḥ parāṅmukha iva śriyaḥ
children.translated_text: then went out, as if turned away from Fortune.
As the aged <s>Vṛṣṇi</s>s were saying, 'This is not right,'
<s>Kaṃsa</s> at once commanded the white-bodied horse <s>Keśin</s>,
and that fierce dānava, sent by him to kill <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>,
went to the cowherd settlement on a day flooded with the blood-red light of terrible twilight,
his eyes filled, as it were, with blood from anger, as he breathed again and again.
His chest was joined to a long projecting muzzle, and his massive neck was bent down,
while the surface of the rocks was split by the blows of his hooves, hard as the essence of adamant.
His shoulders and neck were terrible with a wide-spread mane and crest of hair,
and with his neighing he seemed to strike against, and to drink in, the ten directions.
Blood dripped from his mouth, tasted from chewing flesh stripped of meat,
and his tail, curved and tossed up, had the shape of <s>Kṛtānta</s>'s yak-tail fan.
His mouth was gaping wide, and the circle of rays from his emerging teeth was plainly visible,
as if, as an eater of human flesh, he were casting heaps of bones into the quarters.
Pale in appearance, he rushed with speed upon <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>,
like a vast autumn cloud, driven by the wind, rushing upon a mountain.
Seeing <s>Keśin</s> before him with his forefeet raised high, <s>Keśava</s>,
though held back by the cowherds, ran at him in anger.
Struck powerfully on the chest by those two hooves, which had become like spears,
<s>Acyuta</s> did not tremble before that demon, dreadful with his terrible neighing roar.
By his bounds, the dust raised by the shaking of his mane
covered the quarters as if with hundreds of comets.
Against that assault, into the dreadful cavernous hollow of his mouth, <s>Hari</s>
placed his arm, doubled in size, as if putting something terrible into something terrible.
That arm of <s>Hari</s>, caught between <s>Keśin</s>'s teeth, shone
like a pārijāta tree in the ocean, surrounded by rows of foam.
Against the arm of <s>Mura</s>'s foe, firm as a stone pillar of the mountain that was <s>Keśin</s>,
the demon, his teeth broken, for a long time made the inside of his mouth suffer torment.
Streaming with sweat like water, with blood driven upward in torrents,
<s>Keśin</s>, his eyes rolled back, stood motionless, breathing hard.
When <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>'s arm swelled out between the two mounds of his cheeks,
that mouth split in two with the sharp crack of thick bones bursting.
His form crushed by the irresistible staff-like arm of <s>Dāmodara</s>,
the dreadful horse-demon fell, vomiting blood.

children.text: hate keśini kaṃsasya priye suhṛdi dānave
children.translated_text: When <s>Keśin</s>, the dānava dear to <s>Kaṃsa</s> as a beloved friend, was slain,
there arose throughout the worlds a certain great festival of joy and exultation.
The hidden sage <s>Nārada</s>, pleased, said to <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>,

children.text: sādhu mādhava niḥśalyaṃ tvāyā kṛtmidaṃ jagat ||
children.translated_text: 'Well done, <s>Mādhava</s>; by you this world has been made free of its thorn.
Because you have torn apart <s>Keśin</s>, you yourself will become known as <s>Keśava</s>.'
Having spoken thus, <s>Nārada</s> departed in joy to the direction he desired.
Then there appeared for <s>Śauri</s> a cluster of auspicious omens,
which foretold meeting with a kinsman equal to a father.
At the end of the day the lord of day went to the far side of <s>Meru</s>,
as if from respect to tell the wondrous tale of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>'s killing of <s>Keśin</s>.
Then the sky, naturally dark and variegated by twilight rays,
became charming like generous <s>Dāmodara</s> in his yellow garment.
The dark quarters, slowly pressed together by darkness, became
like cows with cowherds, milk dripping from the rays of the stars.
Then the moon, lord of night, arose as the <s>Pāñcajanya</s> of the ocean of the sky,
the jeweled mirror adorning the sports of night as a lovely woman.
With the rich essence of moonbeams, with the pleasure of divine beauty,
and with the removal of darkness, the sky shone as if with a necklace.
In the sky, white with nectar and dear to the eyes, a deep brilliance settled,
as if <s>Śauri</s>'s fame had taken refuge there under the guise of the moon's rays.
Delighting the peacocks with his chariot, rumbling like a cloud,
<s>Akrūra</s>, crest-jewel of the Vṛṣṇi heroes, arrived.
Reaching the house of <s>Nandagopa</s> in <s>Gokula</s>,
he saw lotus-eyed <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, the slayer of <s>Keśin</s>.
'This is that blessed enemy of <s>Kaiṭabha</s>, <s>Madhusūdana</s>,
born as the joy of the <s>Yādavas</s> to remove the burden of the earth.
He bears on his chest the mark of <s>Śrīvatsa</s>, fit for the <s>Kaustubha</s> jewel,
and worthy of the motionless embrace of the jar-like breasts of <s>Kamalā</s>.
With his cloud-dark body, raining nectar for the eyes,
he wears a pair of yellow garments lovely like a garland of lightning.
Because of him my mind dances, and my wide-spreading eyes
and my arms run forward, as if only to embrace him.'
Saying, 'Come, <s>Mādhava</s>, <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>,' filled with affection,

children.text: pūjito nandagopena kṛṣṇena ca viveśa saḥ ||
children.translated_text: he was honored by <s>Nandagopa</s> and by <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, and he entered.
Then, having received worship and a seat, he addressed <s>Acyuta</s> together with <s>Saṃkarṣaṇa</s>,
as though drinking in lotus-eyed <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> with his eyes.
'This calm and profound form of yours, showering the nectar of joy,
does not come within the range of the eyes of men who are not meritorious.
The lord of <s>Mathurā</s>, turned away from devotion to you through delusion, when he sees you arrived in the morning,
will become both one whose wish is fulfilled and one whose purpose is accomplished.
<s>Kaṃsa</s> wishes to see you; tomorrow you must go to his city.
Let the fortunate <s>Yādavas</s>, through the fullness of their merit, behold your body.
There, in the land of the bow-sacrifice of <s>Kaṃsa</s>, rich in stores of wealth,
let all the prosperous cowherds attend, bringing tribute.
This much alone is the abundant reason for my coming;
but this further little thing is said from affection for a kinsman.

children.text: vṛddhaḥ sa sukṛtī tatra putra putravatāṃ varaḥ
children.translated_text: There, my son, that aged and meritorious <s>Vasudeva</s>, best of those who have sons,
by seeing you, should obtain the fruit of his birth.'
For your sake the sharp arrows of <s>Kaṃsa</s>'s words are continually made into piercing sounds against him;
may he, noble one, obtain you, as the earth obtains Mount <s>Rohaṇa</s>.
Through fear of <s>Kaṃsa</s>, her breasts never drunk by her sons,
she constantly languishes at the name '<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>,' her breasts flowing with milk.
The tender sprout of her lower lip is greyed by sighs from hidden anxiety,
and she has fallen into a pallor of distress, with the weakness of love for her distant son held away.
Like <s>Kauśalyā</s> bereft of <s>Rāma</s>, the crest-jewel of his line,
come to her and cool her with a shower of the nectar of your sight.
Ah, fate is wholly like an innate thirst, like a companion shadow,
like an unexhausted latent impression.
For even the birth of you, skilled in uplifting the universe, crest-jewel of the protection of the world,
withers under anxious thought for the earth.
Your father, bent down by <s>Kaṃsa</s>'s rebukes, having obtained you at last,
O son worshiped by the three worlds, may he bear his head raised high in honor.
When the generous lord, full of affection and parental tenderness, had spoken thus,
he said, 'I shall do everything,' and his face became unchanged.
When <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> had consented to go, the moon seemed to grow wan
under the anxiety-heated sighs of the doe-eyed cowherd women.
The night, rich in floods of milk-like moonlight, seemed to have been milked dry,
and at morning, with the red of twilight, it appeared like a tawny cow.
Then, when the sun had become the jewel on the crest of the eastern mountain,
the sky took on the beauty of <s>Hari</s> with his blazing discus raised.
Then, with many carts filled by the delivery of tribute,
the chiefs of the cowherds set out to go, by <s>Kaṃsa</s>'s command.
<s>Akrūra</s>, <s>Rauhiṇeya</s>, <s>Acyuta</s>, and the others went by chariots,
as if being honored by the lofty lotus-eyes of the cowherd women.
Reaching the bank of the <s>Yamunā</s>, <s>Akrūra</s> said to <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>:
'In this lake, surrounded by serpents, O <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, is <s>Śeṣa</s>, lord of serpents.
Plunging in, O blessed one, I shall worship him with mantras as an eater of nectar.'
Having said this, he left the chariot in <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>'s care and plunged there.
Then, submerged, he saw in the underworld, marked by divine splendor,
the lord <s>Śeṣa</s>, thousand-headed, seated there.
He was adorned with garlands of golden lotuses and decked with every jewel,
having the appearance of a huge snowy mountain with a thousand peaks.
He was attended by all the serpent clans bowing before him,
clad in blue, bearing the palm-banner, holding the plough, and armed with the pestle.

children.text: utsaṅge tasya kṛṣṇaṃ ca śītāṃśoriva lāñchanam
children.translated_text: And in his lap, like the mark on the moon,
he saw <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> seated, and, amazed, he muttered the eternal brahman.
Thinking that <s>Rauhiṇeya</s> and <s>Acyuta</s> were those very two, he quickly rose up,
and seeing those very two standing on the chariot, he plunged again with reverence.
Again seeing them in the same way, he came up, his doubt cast off,
and when <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> asked him with a smile, he said, 'You alone are everything.'
At day's end <s>Akrūra</s> reached <s>Mathurā</s>, and inside his own house
he spoke freely to <s>Govinda</s>, fearing <s>Kaṃsa</s>'s wicked conduct:
'Dear one, you must not go now to <s>Vasudeva</s>'s house,

children.text: na ca rāmeṇa nitarāṃ kaṃsādāpnoti bhartsanām ||
children.translated_text: nor especially together with <s>Rāma</s>; he receives reproach from <s>Kaṃsa</s>.'
When the generous lord had spoken thus, <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> said with a smile:

children.text: satyaṃ tatra na gacchāvaḥ paśyāvaḥ kautukātpurīm ||
children.translated_text: 'True, we two shall not go there; out of curiosity we shall look at the city.'
Having said this, the high-spirited <s>Rāma</s> and <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> wandered about,
like two heroic <s>Vidyādharas</s> descended from aerial cars.
The two mighty-armed ones came upon the king's washerman
and asked for garments of lovely appearance, but that base man would not give them.
The younger brother of <s>Baladeva</s> killed that washerman,
arrogant with anger and pride and speaking cruelly, and took the garments by force.
A garland-maker woman, kindly and speaking with affection, herself brought garlands
and lovingly gave to the lord of fortune what bestowed fortune.
In a moment, playfully, <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> made her limbs clear and well formed,
turning her into a creeper of full beauty in the garden of youth.
Then, reaching the armory honored by daityas and dānavas,
the two saw a bow fit for heroic effort, solid as a stone pillar.
<s>Dāmodara</s> took that hard-to-bend bow and drew it with his two arms,
and broke it, with a spreading twang, as easily as a lotus-stalk fiber.
At that sound, which struck against the shoulders of the wind,
heaven roared as if split open, and the earth trembled.
The keeper of the armory too quickly reported the breaking of the bow
to <s>Kaṃsa</s>; though his mind shook, out of pride he made as if he had not heard.

children.text: bhagnaṃ kenāpi mallena śrutvā cāpaṃ nareśvaraḥ
children.translated_text: When the king heard that the bow had been broken by some wrestler,
he ordered a great festival of battle-spectacle for all the wrestlers.
Then, privately summoning the two wrestlers <s>Cāṇūra</s> and <s>Mauṣṭika</s>,
long kept in readiness, he made them prepared for the killing of <s>Muradviṣ</s>.
In private <s>Kaṃsa</s> spoke to the chief of the elephant stable, his minister for battle,
even in delusion possessed of some merit through his thought of <s>Śauri</s>:
'In the morning the son of <s>Vasudeva</s> will come to the great arena of the bow,
together with his elder brother, arrogant with pride; that mad one deserves death from me.
At the gate of the arena, you must station that thunderbolt-striking serpent-elephant,
<s>Kuvalayāpīḍa</s>, enraged and intent on killing him.
I shall indeed make <s>Vasudeva</s>, bereft of sons, without descendants,
and the kings of the <s>Andhakas</s> and <s>Yādavas</s>, concealed under the guise of kinship.
Long ago my mother, in her fertile season, from fresh curiosity...
He wandered on the flower-bright slopes of <s>Priyāsana</s> and the other hills.
There, the aśoka shoots were shaken by the play of gentle breezes,
and the bees were made tawny by the flashing pollen-filaments of bakula flowers.
In that forest, where charming birds hummed in bowers of massed creepers,
love's passion and delight were abundant, and <s>Smara</s> seemed to be revived.
There the lord of the dānavas, <s>Drumila</s>, husband of <s>Saurā</s>, saw her,
like a creeper of the wish-granting tree of desire, with breasts as its clusters of blossoms.

children.text: mayo yogīśvaraḥ so 'tha rūpaṃ kṛtvā piturmama
children.translated_text: Then that master of magic assumed the form of my father,
and, possessed by <s>Manmatha</s>, enjoyed that chaste woman, whose love was unrestrained.

children.text: tataḥ sā vṛttakartavyā śaṅkitā vīkṣya dānavam
children.translated_text: Afterwards, when the act had been done, she became suspicious on seeing the dānava;
grieving, 'I have been violated,' she angrily cursed the sinner.
'Evildoer, you will meet death in battle from one born in my husband's family,

children.text: ayaṃ ca mama garbhe 'dya tvayā yastanayo dhṛtaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and this son who has today been placed by you in my womb--'
Having said this, she slowly departed; so <s>Nārada</s> told me.
Therefore I am regarded as the son of the daitya-lord <s>Drumila</s>.

children.text: suto 'haṃ nograsenasya yādavā me na bāndhavāḥ
children.translated_text: I am not the son of <s>Ugrasena</s>; the <s>Yādavas</s> are not my kinsmen.
Indeed they are to be destroyed by me, while they wait upon <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>'s effort.
Having thus instructed his chief minister, even on that textually uncertain day,
he entered the arena, packed with assembled spectators, wearing a spotless garment.
There the sky was embraced by waves of rays from lofty jewels on the balconies,
and the place was crowded by the arrival of countless gathered feudatory lords.
There, surrounded by the heroes of the <s>Bhojas</s>, <s>Vṛṣṇis</s>, and <s>Andhakas</s>,
king <s>Kaṃsa</s>, broad-shouldered and seated on a golden throne, shone forth.
His splendor was variegated by rays from crown, earrings, armlets, and jewels,
and the edge of his turban was stirred by the ends of chowries held by women.
Then, at his command, insolent great wrestlers who had come from many lands
leapt up, skilled in the slapping of their arms.
Then the two heroes <s>Saṃkarṣaṇa</s> and <s>Acyuta</s>, dressed in blue and yellow garments,
white and dark like clouds, reached the gate of the arena.
There they again saw the elephant <s>Kuvalayāpīḍa</s>, huge in body and ready to attack,
a mighty elephant set in place because of its massive weight.
It was black as lampblack, terrifying like the coils of the lord of serpents,
as if it were a palace scorched by the massed flame of <s>Kālakūṭa</s> poison.
Driven on by its mahout with irresistible pride and force,
it faced battle, a beast whose tusk-blows had wounded mountains.
Again its terrible trunk was coiled and raised in a frightful circle,
making it look like <s>Antaka</s>, dreadful enough to swallow the three worlds.
<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, moving in circles on its left and right sides,
and, with speed, making it lean upon his own hand, bewildered it.
Then, shaken by blows, it reeled like a rolling mountain,
filling the sky with sprays from its heavy panting and trumpeting.
Because its tusk-strike had failed, it sank to the ground on its knees;
then, suddenly rising, it could not reach <s>Govinda</s>, quick in his deft and varied prowess.
Though it made every effort, as he moved even between its trunk, tusk-tips, and feet,
it did not attain him, like an unlucky man who cannot attain what he desires.
<s>Hari</s>, setting his foot on its face and giving it a powerful blow,
grasped with both hands the tusk, like a pillar of the battle-gateway.
As if uprooting the root of the lotus of <s>Kaṃsa</s>'s fortune from the elephant's face,
he killed it with that very sharp-pointed tusk-club.
Torn open by the blow of its own tusk and vomiting blood,
the elephant, streaming dung and urine, staggered like a mountain.
Its tail was dragged by <s>Rāma</s>, and its rider was killed by <s>Śauri</s>;
with its temples split by the tusk, that monstrous beast fell to the earth.
Having killed <s>Kuvalayāpīḍa</s>, and intent on ending the affliction of the world,
<s>Govinda</s> entered the arena, giving delight and wonder to the women.
His garment fluttered playfully, marked with splashes of the elephant's blood;

children.text: rūpaṃ tasya babhau raṅge meghasyeva savidyutaḥ ||
children.translated_text: his form shone in the arena like a cloud with lightning.
The elephant's tusk shone in the hand of the enemy of <s>Kāliya</s>,
like a ray of the eighth-day moon, bright with radiance in the sky.
Then, at <s>Kaṃsa</s>'s command, the strong wrestler from the <s>Andhra</s> country,
<s>Cāṇūra</s>, shaped like a mountain, fought with <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> there.
With knee-locks and arm-locks, with pushing and pulling,
and with crushing, slapping, and blows, the earth shook from the two of them.
'My son is pouring down nectar!' Thus, with eyes wet with tears of joy,
he was watched, tremblingly and with hope of victory, by <s>Vasudeva</s> and by his mother.
'Beloved of <s>Śrī</s>,' said the apsarases; 'destroyer of daityas,' said the sky-goers;
'Our kinsman,' said the cowherds with affection; 'a foremost hero,' said the <s>Yādavas</s>.
'What is this poor wrestler compared with him?' said <s>Saṃkarṣaṇa</s>;
as he was watched in this way as a man of strength, he filled the wrestlers with astonishment.
Then <s>Kaṃsa</s>, filled with anger, raised his broad arm
and stopped the sound of the instruments that were increasing <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>'s courage.
When the encouragement-music was stopped by <s>Kaṃsa</s> out of hatred for <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>,
the drums of the gods sounded in heaven with clear notes of celestial instruments.
When the seven seers cried, '<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, quickly kill the wrestler!',
a jewel from <s>Kaṃsa</s>'s crown fell, lighting up the sky.
Then, with wondrous prowess, he struck the wrestler, an incarnation of a daitya,
and with a fist-blow smashed his head and shattered his senses.
From his split forehead his two eyes, like lamps,
fell upon the ground, beautiful like a pair of stars.
Then, when that wrestler had fallen and all the other wrestlers had fallen with him,
there arose a sound born from the agitation of the arena, deep as a storm-tossed ocean.
Even <s>Saṃkarṣaṇa</s> seized a wrestler skilled in circular movements,

children.text: mauṣṭikaṃ nāma vikaṭaṃ tāmarākhyaṃ ca keśavaḥ ||
children.translated_text: the huge one named <s>Mauṣṭika</s>; and <s>Keśava</s> seized the one called <s>Tāmara</s>.
Having whirled <s>Tomala</s> in a life-ending circle, the destroyer of <s>Kāliya</s>

children.text: papāta bhuvi niṣpiṣya mauṣṭikaṃ ca halāyudhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: fell upon him and crushed him to the ground, while <s>Halāyudha</s> did the same to <s>Mauṣṭika</s>.
When those wrestlers, thorns to the dwellers in heaven, had been slain,
when the <s>Yādava</s> clan was amazed and the arena was thrown into turmoil,
and when the friends of <s>Vasudeva</s>'s wife seemed sprinkled with streams of nectar,
<s>Kaṃsa</s>, his brow terrible with frowns and his mind trembling, flew into rage.
As though, by his violent sighs, the fire of anger had reached the state of dissolution,
a dreadful fear appeared among all beings.
On the surface of his cheek a clear row of sweat-drops shone,
like a necklace of pearls reflected there, caught in his swinging earring.
As if checking the noise and uproar of the arena with the bend of his brows,
the lord of the earth spoke, after the people had been driven back by men with canes.

children.text: iyaṃ saralatā jātu jātā sārakṣayāya naḥ
children.translated_text: "This guilelessness of ours has surely arisen for the loss of our power.
How can a cowherd be seen among men famed for their strength?

children.text: jambukena hatāḥ siṃhā yadi tatkriyate 'tra kim
children.translated_text: If lions have been killed by a jackal, what is to be done here?
Let the cowherds be expelled from here, and let <s>Nandagopa</s> be bound.
And this <s>Vasudeva</s>, ruinous to his kinsmen and the basest of his family,
is to be placed in the mouth of destruction, together with the <s>Yādavas</s> of his own party."
At this command of the son of <s>Ugrasena</s>, fierce in valor,
those who followed his will rose up to do just as he had ordered.
Then the protector of the dwellers in heaven saw the cowherds overcome with fear,
and goddess <s>Devakī</s>, shaken by helplessness born of love for her son.
<s>Trivikrama</s> rushed up to the side of the golden throne,
and <s>Keśava</s> seized <s>Kaṃsa</s> by the hair among his swaying garlands.
When <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> suddenly fell before him, as if set down by the quarters, as if descended from the sky,
<s>Kaṃsa</s> thought that he was death itself.
As <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> dragged the king by his garlanded hair,
royal fortune seemed to lament through the jingling of broken ornaments.
With his face bent down, <s>Kaṃsa</s>, weighed down by <s>Śauri</s>,
looked upon the burden-oppressed earth, as though it had become the cause of his death.
His crown, a jeweled mountain where splendor sported beneath the sun of his face-sky,
fell, with a stream of loosened pearls like drops of tears.
Dragging him, while his pearl-strings, armlets, and earrings burst apart,
<s>Hari</s> cast <s>Kaṃsa</s> down from the great golden throne, as if from vast sovereignty itself.
His body, scraped against the red pavement, streamed with blood,
and <s>Hari</s> flung the lifeless <s>Kaṃsa</s> far away, his breath scattered.
He who had been unconquered by all kings and unbroken even in battle with the wielder of the thunderbolt,
when all beings saw him surely slain by <s>Śauri</s>,
a dreadful roar of tumult arose in the arena for a moment.
When <s>Kaṃsa</s>, crest-jewel of heroic lineages, had been slain by <s>Murāri</s>,
<s>Halāyudha</s> killed <s>Sunāman</s>, the younger brother of <s>Kaṃsa</s>.
Then the divine son of <s>Devakī</s>, worshipped by the gods,
bowed with overflowing joy to the lotus feet of <s>Vasudeva</s> and of his mother.
Hearing that <s>Kaṃsa</s> had suddenly been killed, the women of <s>Kaṃsa</s>'s household
came as though split open by an untimely fall of a thunderbolt.
They saw him lying on the ground, soiled with dust, like an elephant killed by a lion,
violently uprooted like a great tree by the wind.
Crying out with piercing lament, their necklaces and ornaments torn apart,
writhing on the ground, the doe-eyed women spoke thus:
"Alas, lord, flower-weapon of love skilled in the arts of women's play,
you whose fierce staff-like arms shattered circles of enemies in battle,
how have you turned away from your beloveds, who are the ground of love and affection,
and fallen asleep embracing the earth with your two arms, forgetting your regard for them?
How could death come to you unarmed, O hero, you who took the jewel of the lord of waters from <s>Jarāsaṃdha</s>
and wounded the <s>Yakṣa</s>?
O king, your chest was harshly scored by the tips of <s>Airāvaṇa</s>'s tusks;

children.text: vadhe tavāpi bhūpāla kathaṃ na kṣubhitaṃ jagat ||
children.translated_text: how did the world not tremble even at your death?
How is it that for you, lord of armies and king of kings,

children.text: nijaḥ paro vā saṃgrāme naiko 'pi nihataḥ puraḥ ||
children.translated_text: not one of your own men or an enemy was first slain in battle?
Raise your eyes, lord; look upon the women of your household.

children.text: iyaṃ kṛtakanidrā vā kopaḥ praṇayinīṣu vā ||
children.translated_text: Is this feigned sleep, or anger toward your lovers?
This is some pitiless road, the final journey of men,

children.text: panthāḥ pratīkṣyate kṣipraṃ na yatra dayito janaḥ ||
children.translated_text: where a beloved person does not quickly await one."
As the women of the inner apartments were lamenting thus, trembling,
<s>Kaṃsa</s>'s mother came suddenly, overwhelmed by grief.

children.text: utsaṅge sā śiraḥ kṛtvā putrasya kṣitiśāyinaḥ
children.translated_text: Placing the head of her son, who lay on the ground, in her lap,
she took up irresistible tears and mourned, speaking in pain:

children.text: aho nu tvāṃ nṛśaṃsena putra kālena nighnatā
children.translated_text: "Ah, son, by cruel Time, which has slain you,
your aged father's hope for a water-offering has been cut off.
Alone on a bed of dust, though fit for a costly couch,
how do you lie like an ordinary man, O lord of the earth?

children.text: jñātibhyo duḥsahaṃ puṃsāṃ jāyate nānyato bhayam
children.translated_text: For men an unbearable danger arises from kinsmen, not from anyone else:
seated in the assembly of the <s>Rākṣasas</s>, <s>Daśānana</s> truly said this.
The fortune that you won by your own arms was made common to your kinsmen;

children.text: lakṣmīḥ sa tvaṃ hataḥ putra jñātinā jñātivatsalaḥ ||
children.translated_text: such as you are slain by a kinsman, my son, though you were fond of your kin."
Having spoken thus, she addressed the aged king <s>Ugrasena</s>,
her husband, who was deeply stunned by the poison of grief for his son:
"This son of yours, O king, abandoned by his kinsmen,
Slain and alone like a thief, let him ask <s>Hari</s> for the funeral rite.
In this kingdom let the valiant <s>Bhoja</s> rule, or else mighty <s>Mādhava</s>.
This royal fortune, O king, always looks toward the faces of heroes.
Go, lord, and inform <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> in the assembly of the <s>Yādavas</s>:
'This <s>Kaṃsa</s>, lord of the earth, should be abandoned in the rites after death.'

children.text: kasya nāma hate vairaṃ prāṇaiḥ saṃśodhitāgasi
children.translated_text: Against whom, once he is slain and his offence is cleansed by his life, can enmity remain?

children.text: tyaktvā prayātaḥ sarvasvaṃ nottiṣṭhiti hataḥ punaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Having given up all his wealth, he has gone away; when slain, he does not rise again.
Hearing this, <s>Ugrasena</s>, like the sun reddened at twilight,
went to the house of <s>Vasudeva</s>, as if bitten in the throat by a snake.
With his kinsmen, his face bowed down, he saw <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>,
whose mind was troubled by remorseful thought over the death of his own kinsman.
<s>Ugrasena</s> said to him, 'Let what is proper be done by you;
protect the <s>Yādavas</s>, whose noble conduct has not withered.
At your command I shall perform <s>Kaṃsa</s>'s final rite,

children.text: datvā jalāñjaliṃ cāsya bhavāmi vipine muniḥ ||
children.translated_text: and, after offering him the handful of water, I shall become a sage in the forest.
When separation has come by the ordinance of fate, according to the discipline of yogins,
their splendor in forest after forest is fit only for tears.
Hearing that, the enemy of <s>Kaṃsa</s> said, 'This is true, and worthy of your family;

children.text: sadṛśaṃ tava bhūpāla śrutasya caritasya ca ||
children.translated_text: it is fitting for you, O king, for your learning and for your conduct.
This line dividing becoming and non-becoming is destiny,
as if imperishably written on the stone of a creature's forehead.
Do not grieve now over this event that cannot be turned back;

children.text: kāle kalitakālāgrā na hi muhyanti dhīdhanāḥ ||
children.translated_text: those rich in wisdom do not become bewildered when time has marked the limit of death.

children.text: satkriyāṃ bhajatāṃ kaṃso rājyaṃ ca bhajatāṃ bhavān
children.translated_text: Let <s>Kaṃsa</s> receive the proper rite, and let you receive the kingdom;

children.text: rājyārthino na hi vayaṃ na kaṃsastatkṛte hataḥ ||
children.translated_text: we do not seek kingship, nor was <s>Kaṃsa</s> slain for its sake.
If your mind is gracious toward us for the sake of the world's work,
then your own kingdom, for one who acts without deceit, must not be abandoned.
Having spoken thus, <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, ornament of the <s>Yadu</s> line, lowered his face,
and by force placed the aged man, who had turned away from sovereignty, on the royal seat.

children.text: tataḥ kaṃsasya rājārhe satkārye bandhubhiḥ kṛte
children.translated_text: Then, when the fitting royal honors for <s>Kaṃsa</s> had been performed by his kinsmen,
<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, together with his younger brother, stayed there, honored by the <s>Vṛṣṇis</s>.
Then the two went to the house of their guru <s>Sāṃdīpani</s>, a pupil of <s>Kaśyapa</s>,
having fulfilled the observance owed to a teacher, to the abode of the rule of all learning.
In divine missiles and in the sciences of sound, in the Vedas whose essence they understood,
and in faultless branches of knowledge and complete arts,
the two, mirrors of the jewel of genius, reached the farthest shore,
worshipping <s>Śiva</s> himself on festival days with steady reverence.
Then, when the guru was told by them, 'Let the teacher's fee be accepted,'
he said, 'By the power of you two, I wish to obtain
my son, who was carried off in the ocean by a <s>timi</s> fish during the pilgrimage to <s>Prabhāsa</s>.'
At the guru's words, <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, abiding by <s>Saṃkarṣaṇa</s>'s counsel,

children.text: gatvā jalanidhiṃ ghoraṃ mamajja mahasāṃ nidhiḥ ||
children.translated_text: went to the dreadful ocean and plunged into it, he who was himself a treasury of powers.
When he quickly said, 'Where is that son of my guru?',
the ocean, with joined palms, spoke to that lord of the worlds:

children.text: iha pañcajano nāma daityo vasati duḥsahaḥ
children.translated_text: 'Here dwells an unbearable daitya named <s>Pañcajana</s>;
in the form of a <s>timi</s> fish he carried off that son of <s>Sāṃdīpani</s>.'
At the ocean's words, the hero <s>Hari</s> slew <s>Pañcajana</s>

children.text: avāpa pāñcajanyākhyaṃ śaṅkhaṃ na tu guroḥ sutam ||
children.translated_text: and obtained the conch named <s>Pāñcajanya</s>, but not the guru's son.
Then, conquering <s>Vaivasvata</s> even in the city of the dead,
<s>Dāmodara</s> brought the son back in his body and gave him to the guru.
Then, arriving at <s>Mathurā</s>, skilled in weapons,
he, together with <s>Rāma</s>, filled all the <s>Yādavas</s> with wonder and joy.
Meanwhile, burning with the blazing fire of anger at <s>Kaṃsa</s>'s death,
and distressed on seeing his own daughters, <s>Kaṃsa</s>'s beloved wives, widowed,
mighty <s>Jarāsaṃdha</s>, lord of <s>Magadha</s>, came near,
under whose protection <s>Kaṃsa</s> had gained the kingdom after binding his father.
Other heroic kings who followed him also assembled,
the <s>Kārīṣa</s> king named <s>Dantavakra</s>, and <s>Śiśupāla</s>, lord of <s>Cedi</s>;

children.text: kaliṅgaḥ kauśikaḥ pauṇḍraḥ krātho rukmī sabhīṣmakaḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Kaliṅga</s>, <s>Kauśika</s>, <s>Pauṇḍra</s>, <s>Krātha</s>, <s>Rukmī</s> with <s>Bhīṣmaka</s>,
<s>Aṃśumān</s>, <s>Sālva</s>, and the kings of <s>Veṇudāri</s> and <s>Samudraga</s>;
the lords of <s>Trigarta</s>, <s>Suhya</s>, <s>Sauvīra</s>, <s>Śaibya</s>, <s>Pāṇḍya</s>, and <s>Videha</s>;
the rulers of <s>Kāśī</s>, <s>Kosala</s>, <s>Gandhāra</s>, <s>Kāśmīra</s>, the <s>Yavanas</s>, and others;
and the powerful kings headed by <s>Daśārma</s> and <s>Bhagadatta</s>.
Besieging <s>Mathurā</s>, they made every opening impassable with elephants.
Seeing those oceans of kings marked by the spreading foam of parasols and yak-tail fans,
the slayer of <s>Kāliya</s> judged that the time had come.
When <s>Mathurā</s> had been blockaded by the impetuous <s>Māgadha</s>
with twenty <s>akṣauhiṇī</s> armies, the <s>Vṛṣṇis</s> and <s>Yādavas</s> marched out.
Then, when battle began, the wielder of the plough, armed with his club,
and the enemy of <s>Kaṃsa</s>, bearing the bow <s>Śārṅga</s> and the mace <s>Kaumodakī</s>,
in two chariots whose banner-tops bore the palm tree and <s>Garuḍa</s>, and which were fitted with golden armor,
the two heroes entered the enemy army, thrown into confusion by battle.
There, as the bodies of elephant-lords were dragged down and crushed by <s>Rāma</s>'s club,
and as they fell together with chariots,
while the <s>Vṛṣṇis</s> fought against the valorous kings,
at the sound of <s>Muravairin</s>'s drawn <s>Śārṅga</s>,
the hearts of the demon-minded rulers trembled.
Made chariotless by <s>Jarāsaṃdha</s>'s showers of arrows, <s>Rāma</s> and <s>Keśava</s>
moved about on foot, the two heroes destroying excellent warriors.
In battle, when <s>Saṃkarṣaṇa</s> had crushed his chariot with his mace,
<s>Jarāsaṃdha</s>, mace in hand, rushed at him himself in anger.
In the terrible mace-fight of those two, powerful through excellent training and strength,
the sky became packed without a gap by gods who had come for the spectacle.
Under their swift blows, fit for pulverizing mountains,
their firm limbs, equal in steadiness, nevertheless trembled.
Then, when a dreadful, life-taking blow was being raised,
a voice from heaven spoke out to <s>Rāma</s> concerning <s>Jarāsaṃdha</s>:
'Enough of vain effort in battle, O slayer of <s>Dhenuka</s>;
this king is not to be killed by you; another destroyer has been born for him.'
Hearing this, <s>Rāma</s> stopped; and as the sun was setting,
there was a withdrawal of the two armies, whose noble heroes had been torn apart.
When the conquered <s>Jarāsaṃdha</s> had gone away and the <s>Vṛṣṇis</s> were free from obstruction,
<s>Rāma</s>, remembering his childhood games, once went to the cowherd settlement.
There <s>Govinda</s>'s elder brother, delighted and honored by the cowherds,
wandered in the lovely forest borders, bright with the beauty of flowers.
He sat at the foot of a kadamba tree smiling with blossoms,
as if fanned by it with its quivering leaf-buds as fly-whisks.
Joyful, eager for drink, and fair in form, he drank the divine <s>kādambarī</s> liquor
that had issued from the hollow of the kadamba, a wine made of flower nectar.
His face, its cheek-edges reddened by intoxication,
shone like the moon reddened by twilight, with earrings swaying playfully.
Then the goddess <s>Kādambarī</s>, adorned with divine garments and ornaments,
carrying a noble fragrance absorbed from dwelling among kadamba filaments,
her eyes reeling with intoxication like wavering lotuses,
served charming <s>Rāma</s>, who was sporting in delight, in embodied form.
And <s>Kānti</s>, his radiance, comparable to a beloved woman's face and bright as the cool-rayed moon,
approached joyfully and pleased him with words dear to him.
And <s>Śrī</s>, embodied and doe-eyed, gave him a garland of golden lotuses,
earrings splendid with rays, and a necklace.
Clad in blue and adorned with a golden garland, he shone
like <s>Kailāsa</s> with a raincloud clinging to it and lit by lightning.
His necklace, outshining the stars, gleamed royally,
like masses of foam from the Milk Ocean, or like the moon's stream of nectar.
Then, languid with intoxication and longing for the play of bathing,
he called from afar to the <s>Yamunā</s>, 'Come here!' with faltering syllables.
When that river disregarded his command and said nothing at all,

children.text: yadā tadā ruṣā rāmaḥ samutthāyādahe halam ||
children.translated_text: <s>Rāma</s> rose in anger and took up his plough.
With the tip of the plough he drew her, whose dark waters rolled restlessly,
like an angry proud woman with her braid loosened in agitation.
Her girdle, a row of swans confused by the turmoil, sounded again and again,
and in places she seemed to show rows of gooseflesh, with her water-garment slipping down.
In places she turned away, her face averted by the frown-like curve of her waves;
her broken necklace of foam was scattered with spray like pearls.
In places she was troubled as though grasping the silk cloth of her watery billows,
and in places her high breasts, the cakravāka birds, were covered by the hands of her waves.
In places she had noisy circles of birds bewildered by fear,
and her startled eyes were blooming blue lotuses made to dance by whirlpools.
In places, with the cooing cries of water-birds, she babbled as if sighing,
and in places she stumbled from the weariness of her hurried movement.
Dragged by the plough, that river became utterly bewildered,
and, brought into the midst of <s>Vṛndāvana</s>, then took visible bodily form.
Trembling, with folded hands, the <s>Yamunā</s> spoke to <s>Rāma</s>.
Her garment of water had slipped, and her movement was unsteady with trembling:
'The rivers will laugh at me with their foam near the ocean.
I wish to regain my own form, if you are gracious, O giver of honor;
for women are to be honored by great souls even when they have offended.'
Thus propitiated by her, doe-eyed like a young antelope,
<s>Rāma</s> desisted, watched by the inhabitants of Vraja who were seized with wonder.

children.text: tataḥ prāptaḥ sa mathurāṃ pūjitaḥ kāliyadviṣā
children.translated_text: Then he reached <s>Mathurā</s>, honored by the foe of <s>Kāliya</s>,
and, wearing divine garlands and garments, the glorious one brought joy to the <s>Yādavas</s>.
Then <s>Keśava</s> reflected on <s>Jarāsaṃdha</s>, who had gone away with his purpose broken,
yet was eager to return with that unbearable great army.
Seeing that <s>Mathurā</s> was far too small and that the <s>Yādavas</s> were increasing,
he consulted with the elders, beginning with <s>Ugrasena</s>.
He said, 'What we say here before you venerable elders
is a course of action strengthened by the deepest affection.
This is a certain celebrated and approved thought among those skilled in policy:
strategy must be considered, even when great heroes are present.
For us, through the mighty <s>Jarāsaṃdha</s>, there has arisen
a boundless, implacable fire of enmity, born from the severing of limbs.
Those kings of the earth, his followers, have become hostile;

children.text: jarāsaṃdhena sahitā ye na jeyāḥ surairapi ||
children.translated_text: joined with <s>Jarāsaṃdha</s>, they cannot be conquered even by the gods.
And that <s>Kālayavana</s>, with mlecchas, <s>Daradas</s>, <s>Cīnas</s>, and <s>Śakas</s> at his head,
has likewise oppressed our city by hemming it in with his forces.
Born from <s>Gārgya</s>'s fierce austerity, he is a conqueror of the three worlds,
a hero invulnerable to all beings by the boon of <s>Pinākin</s>.
At his blockade of our city, this river arose from the dung of his horses;
known in the world by the name <s>Aśvaśakṛt</s>, it spreads onward.

children.text: krameṇa vinipātānāṃ bhayaṃ te mahatāṃ dviṣām
children.translated_text: The fear of successive disasters from those great enemies
would not reach a fortified city merely through the rise of time and place.
Therefore, [let us resort to] <s>Dvāravatī</s>, a fortress garlanded with moats and ramparts...
'I wish to establish <s>Kuśasthalī</s> on the western ocean.'
When <s>Śauri</s> had said this, the chief men of the <s>Yadus</s> replied, 'So be it.'
For trust in words of benefit belongs to those whose future prosperity is auspicious.

children.text: kṛṣṇasarpaḥ tataḥ kṛṣṇaḥ kumbhe prakṣipya mudrite
children.translated_text: Then <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> put a black snake into a sealed jar,
and sent it to the lord of the <s>Yavanas</s>, declaring, 'I am unbearable.'
Seeing it, <s>Kālayavana</s> laughed, and with fierce ants
he sent the snake back devoured, saying that he was rich in troops.
Then, together with <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, all the <s>Yādavas</s> and <s>Vṛṣṇis</s>
left <s>Mathurā</s> and went to the city girdled by the ocean.
Then, surrounded by heroes and gleaming as if by gods,
the city shone with <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> as <s>Amarāvatī</s> shines with <s>Śakra</s>.
Then one day <s>Janārdana</s>, alone and going on foot,
set out, skilled in strategy, to draw <s>Kālayavana</s> away.
Seeing <s>Govinda</s> come, the delighted lord of the <s>Yavanas</s>
ran toward him, huge-bodied and terrible, like Time itself.
That enemy of the world, swift as thought and eager to seize <s>Janārdana</s>,
rushing on with speed, made the quarters tremble and quake in confusion.
Then steadfast <s>Acyuta</s>, whose course is inconceivable, entered a deep mountain cave,
vast in extent and like his own inscrutable <s>māyā</s> (power of illusion).
There was the king <s>Mucukunda</s>, son of <s>Māndhātṛ</s>,
who, in the war of gods and asuras, had brought about the destruction of <s>Śakra</s>'s enemies.

children.text: śrānto nidrāṃ varātprāpya vidadhe saṃvidaṃ suraiḥ
children.translated_text: Wearied, he had obtained sleep as a boon and had made an agreement with the gods:
'Whoever causes the end of my sleep shall go to ashes.'
As that king lay for a very long time upon a jewel couch,
<s>Govinda</s> sat down near his head in the cave.
Then the <s>Yavana</s> entered swiftly, breathing hard and blazing with anger,
and saw the royal sage asleep, mountain-like in form.
Seeing him with his face covered, <s>Kālayavana</s>, in anger,
thought, 'This is <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>,' and touched the king with his foot.
Then King <s>Mucukunda</s>, suddenly awakened by the foot,
reduced the one touching him to ashes with an eye fierce from pain.
When <s>Kālayavana</s> had been burned up, the king turned his face,
and, his eyes reddened by sleep, beheld the lotus-eyed one.
Seeing <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, of very small body, while he himself was like <s>Mandara</s>,
the lord of the earth understood that a vast span of time had passed.
When <s>Mucukunda</s> asked, 'Who are you?', <s>Keśava</s>
bowed with folded hands and related his own story.
Knowing that three ages had gone by, the lord of the earth, after his sleep,
and seeing that people had become short, only ankle-high,

children.text: na cakāra matiṃ rājye virase vigataspṛhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: took no thought for kingship; it had become tasteless, and he was free of desire.
When one's equals have passed away and the grounds of affection are empty,

children.text: jīrṇe jagati vicchāye sajane kā ratiḥ satām ||
children.translated_text: what delight can the good have in an aged, lusterless world, even among their own people?
That wise king went to a cavern of the <s>Himālaya</s> mountain for ascetic practice,
and ascended heaven, the proper ascent of those rich in merit.
Then <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> went to <s>Dvārakā</s>, made by <s>Viśvakarman</s>,
with golden gateways and ramparts, and jewel-studded towers and arches,
with moonlight fashioned from the spreading rays of spacious crystal mansions,
as if it had been built from the ocean of milk, pouring forth nectar,
with rows of beautiful faces reflected upon its jewel walls,
as if served by the moon after he had divided himself manyfold,
and entered that city, bright with pure radiance, attended by followers, and in constant festival,
taking with him all the army and wealth won from the <s>Yavana</s>.

children.text: tasyāṃ porajanaṃ sarvaṃ śaṅkho nāma nidhīśvaraḥ
children.translated_text: In that city, the lord of treasures named <s>Śaṅkha</s>
quickly filled all the townspeople with gold and jewels at <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>'s command.
The powerful son of <s>Devakī</s>, sending forth Wind himself,
brought the divine assembly hall called <s>Sudharmā</s> from heaven.
That city, guarded by excellent warriors, the <s>Vṛṣṇis</s>, <s>Sātvatas</s>, and <s>Yādavas</s>,
shone full of beauty, like <s>Meru</s> with lions in its caves.
As if given at the proper time by the ocean at <s>Hari</s>'s command,
that city, many yojanas in extent, became very splendid.
Meanwhile <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> heard of <s>Rukmiṇī</s>, the daughter

children.text: śuśrāva rukmiṇīṃ kṛṣmaḥ kanyāṃ rūpema viśrutām ||
children.translated_text: of the southern king <s>Bhīṣmaka</s>, famed for her beauty.
She too heard of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, the lotus-eyed enemy of <s>Kaṃsa</s>,
and in the minds of the two there arose something noble with the flavor of longing.
<s>Bhīṣmaka</s>'s son <s>Rukmī</s>, strong-armed and fierce in battle,

children.text: vīro bibharti yaḥ spardhāṃ bhuvi bhārgavabhīṣmayoḥ ||
children.translated_text: was a hero who maintained rivalry on earth with <s>Bhārgava</s> and <s>Bhīṣma</s>.

children.text: anujāṃ rukmiṇīṃ dṛptaḥ sa kṛṣmenārthitāṃ sadā
children.translated_text: Proudly, he would not give his younger sister <s>Rukmiṇī</s>, though <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> always sought her,
declaring from hatred, 'This man is a servant of <s>Kaṃsa</s>.'
Then, at <s>Jarāsaṃdha</s>'s word, King <s>Bhīṣmaka</s>
undertook to give his daughter to <s>Śiśupāla</s>, with his son's approval.
Then <s>Śiśupāla</s>, son of <s>Vasudeva</s>'s sister, came to that city
for the wedding procession, to which <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> and the other <s>Vṛṣṇi</s> heroes had been invited,
together with kings headed by <s>Dantavakra</s> and <s>Jarāsaṃdha</s>;
honored by <s>Bhīṣmaka</s>, he arrived for the wedding festival.
There <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> saw <s>Rukmiṇī</s>, moonlight to the eyes,
busy worshipping <s>Indrāṇī</s>, with eyes long like those of a black antelope,
fair-faced, graceful with beauty, her lower lip like a reddish sprout,
like <s>Lakṣmī</s> born together with the moon, nectar, and the divine tree.
Seeing that lotus-faced one, the springtime of Love's garden...
<s>Mādhava</s>, as though drenched with honey, pondered for a moment:
"This radiant stream of beauty, with foam blossoming like white garments,
is the life of the flower-bowed god, though he was burned by <s>Hara</s>'s roar.
This splendor must be modesty itself, rivaling lotuses; how could it belong to the moon?
The comparison for her happiness would be her own face, if seen in a mirror."
Thus thinking, <s>Vaikuṇṭha</s>, filled with longing and disturbed by <s>Manmatha</s>,
with his elder brother's consent, suddenly carried off the daughter of <s>Bhīṣmaka</s>.
When she had been carried away in that warrior's chariot, swift as the wind,
there arose a roar of the kings, deep with the agitation of their brave soldiers.

children.text: iyaṃ kṛṣṇena kṛṣṇena kanyā kanyā hṛtā hṛtā
children.translated_text: "This maiden, this maiden, has been taken, taken, by black <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>!"
Even as the kings said this, they seemed to fall into bewilderment.
Placing the unbearable burden upon the <s>Vṛṣṇis</s>, with <s>Rāma</s> at their head,
while the one whose banner bore <s>Tārkṣya</s> sped away, a terrible battle began.
With <s>Rāma</s>, <s>Sātyaki</s>, <s>Hārdikya</s>, <s>Gada</s>, <s>Akrūra</s>, and <s>Vidūratha</s>,
and with the <s>Yādavas</s> such as <s>Vakradeva</s>, <s>Sunakṣatra</s>, and <s>Sāraṇa</s>,
against the kings headed by <s>Śiśupāla</s> and <s>Jarāsaṃdha</s>, in the battle
for a moment it became like an untimely night, with arrows packed so densely that no gaps remained.
As enemies were being slain by mighty <s>Baladeva</s>,
and others by <s>Śiśupāla</s>, destruction came upon both armies.

children.text: atrāntare puro rājñāṃ skmī krodhāgninā jvalan
children.translated_text: Meanwhile, before the kings, <s>Rukmī</s>, blazing with the fire of anger,
armed and breathing like a stricken serpent, said to his father:
"Without killing <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, that defiled man of evil conduct,
I shall not return to my own city, fallen from a hero's vow."
Having spoken so, he mounted his chariot, followed by heroic kings,
and went forth, making the quarters resound, while the tips of his banners were tossed by his speed.
Seeing him coming from afar, the companion of <s>Rukmiṇī</s>, standing in his chariot,
<s>Hari</s> turned back and stood with his bow drawn up to his ear.
Then, swiftly, with dense black arrow-heads arrayed in ranks,
the lotus-beds of kings appeared to be covered over.
Then <s>Śauri</s>, being filled with arrows shot from <s>Rukmī</s>'s bow,
was covered with golden-feathered shafts like a mountain by the rays of the sun.
Quickly splitting with his arrows the inexhaustible, mutually flashing weapons
hurled by the kings, <s>Acyuta</s> shone as though dancing.
Then, swiftly, their parasols, chariots, and banners cut down by <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>'s arrows,
they became men with bows severed and hopes shattered.
Then <s>Śauri</s>, after cutting away all the weapons that poured forth divine missiles,
pierced <s>Rukmī</s>'s heart with three sharp iron arrows.
When he had fainted and fallen, and the circle of kings had fled,
<s>Śauri</s>, out of mercy and at <s>Rukmiṇī</s>'s words, spared <s>Rukmī</s>.
When <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> had gone to <s>Dvāravatī</s> and the <s>Vṛṣṇis</s> had turned back,

children.text: kuṇḍinākhyaṃ puraṃ rukmī praviveśa na lajjayā ||
children.translated_text: <s>Rukmī</s>, out of shame, did not enter the city called <s>Kuṇḍina</s>.
Having abandoned his city because of his vow, he founded another
city named <s>Bhojakaṭa</s>, reflecting on the breaking of his pride.
Taking <s>Rukmiṇī</s> as though she were the goddess of victory, and as fortune come in another bodily form,
the beloved of <s>Rukmiṇī</s> possessed her by the rite of marriage.
With her, lotus-eyed <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, she whose eyes were like blossoming blue lotuses,
made merry, his mind filled with a stream of nectar.
In her he begot ten sons, equal to the gods,
<s>Pradyumna</s>, <s>Cārudoṣṇa</s>, and the others, and also a daughter, <s>Cārumatī</s>.
Then the lord of the world obtained other beloved wives, creepers in the garden of loving affection,

children.text: anyā jagatpatiḥ patnīrmūrtā iva diśo daśa ||
children.translated_text: as if they were the ten directions embodied.

children.text: kālindī satyabhāmā ca satyā jāmbavatī tathā
children.translated_text: <s>Kālindī</s>, <s>Satyabhāmā</s>, <s>Satyā</s>, and <s>Jāmbavatī</s>,
<s>Mitravindā</s>, <s>Suśīlā</s>, <s>Lakṣmaṇā</s>, and the water-dwelling one,
<s>Sudantā</s> and <s>Rohiṇī</s>: these moon-faced women, ever

children.text: śyāmāḥ śyāmā iva prītyā bhejire śeṣaśāyinam ||
children.translated_text: dark and lovely, lovingly attended the one who lies on <s>Śeṣa</s>.
Sixteen thousand divine doe-eyed women
freely served <s>Hari</s>, the universal form, in the sports of <s>Kandarpa</s>.
Among them, for that lord, creator of the universe, there came to be
a class of sons numbering by the lakh, whose valor was able to destroy the enemies of the gods.
<s>Pradyumna</s>, <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>'s lotus-eyed son, obtained in a svayaṃvara
the maiden <s>Nārāyaṇī</s>, <s>Candrasenā</s>, a princess of <s>Vidarbha</s>.
By him, in her, was born a son, <s>Aniruddha</s>, radiant as the god of love,
whose beauty was the collyrium that brought wide-eyed women under the power of sight.
In time <s>Aniruddha</s>, together with the <s>Yādavas</s> and <s>Vṛṣṇis</s>,
went to obtain <s>Rukmī</s>'s beautiful-eyed granddaughter, <s>Rukmavatī</s>.
Then, while they were staying there with <s>Halāyudha</s> as their chief,
the southern kings formed an intention toward deceitful gambling.
Sitting in assembly and occupying jewel-seats, those kings
conspired together and challenged the one marked with the palm tree to play, as against a gambler.
Then, when a game of dice began with him, eager to produce a quarrel,
and stakes of crores of gold were being laid against one another,
by low cheats, though guileless, <s>Rāma</s> himself was repeatedly defeated.
Then undefeated <s>Rukmī</s>, laughing and rolling the dice, said to him:
"This ignorant weakling, though very rich, has been beaten. Ah!"
Hearing that, <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>'s elder brother, burning with anger and breathing hard, said:
"Ten thousand crores of gold is my stake."

children.text: ityukto halinā rukmī na kiṃcitpratyuvāca tam ||
children.translated_text: Thus addressed by the plough-bearer, <s>Rukmī</s> said nothing in reply to him.
Then, when the dice had been cast, he was defeated by <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>'s elder brother.
Making silence his pretext, he said, "I have not been defeated."
At that utterance from his tongue, when the wielder of the pestle grew angry,
a clear, bodiless voice issued from the sky:
"<s>Rukmī</s> has been defeated by <s>Rāma</s>, since he made the agreement in his mind;
for the disposition of the mind is the authority in all actions of embodied beings."

children.text: tacchrutvā na jito 'smīti vādinaṃ punareva tam
children.translated_text: Hearing this, when he again insisted, "I have not been defeated,"
the wielder of the pestle struck him down violently with the gaming board.
Proudly powerful <s>Bala</s> knocked out the teeth of the king of <s>Kaliṅga</s>,
and, uprooting an elephant-post, rushed upon the <s>Krathas</s> and <s>Kaiśikas</s>.
When the kings departed in terror of him, a foe like the fire of doom,
and <s>Rukmī</s>, lord of kings and equal to <s>Śakra</s> in valor, had been slain,
the <s>Vṛṣṇi</s> heroes went away slowly, as though filled with regret,
and <s>Acyuta</s>'s elder brother reported the whole affair to <s>Acyuta</s>.
Then <s>Madhusūdana</s> consoled <s>Rukmiṇī</s>, loud with lamentation,
and said nothing at all to <s>Halāyudha</s>, whose face was bent down.
Thus that <s>Rukmī</s>, like <s>Bhārgava</s>, not to be slain even by the gods,
was killed by the incarnation of <s>Śeṣa</s>, the palm-bannered one.

children.text: sāmbo nāma kadācittu jāmbavatyāṃ hareḥ sutaḥ
children.translated_text: Once <s>Sāmba</s>, son of <s>Hari</s> by <s>Jāmbavatī</s>,
went to <s>Hastināpura</s> to abduct <s>Duryodhana</s>'s daughter.
At that royal <s>svayaṃvara</s> (self-choice ceremony), because of anger over the abduction of the maiden,
the proud son of <s>Mādhava</s> was confined by the son of <s>Dhṛtarāṣṭra</s>.
Then wrathful <s>Halāyudha</s> came himself to set him free,
and set about violently breaking the city of the <s>Kaurava</s> king.
He set his plough on the rampart-bank, facing the bank of the <s>Gaṅgā</s>,
and by it the whole of <s>Hastināpura</s> suddenly began to shake.
Seeing the city, with its gates and watchtowers, reeling as it was dragged by the plough,
and about to be hurled into the <s>Gaṅgā</s>, they knew that <s>Halāyudha</s> was enraged.

children.text: duryodhanaḥ svaṃya gatvā praṇipatya prasādya ca
children.translated_text: <s>Duryodhana</s> went himself, bowed down, and appeased him;

children.text: sāmbaṃ muktvā gadāyuddhe prayayau tasya śiṣyatām ||
children.translated_text: then, after releasing <s>Sāmba</s>, he became his pupil in mace-fighting.
Such was the exceedingly marvelous strength of mighty <s>Baladeva</s>,
by whose two arms <s>Bhīma</s>, whose life-force equaled ten thousand elephants, was defeated.
Meanwhile a demon named <s>Naraka</s>, son of the earth,
carried off all the jewels and the women of the dwellers in heaven.
He stole the earrings of <s>Aditi</s> and initiated all beings into fear;

children.text: yudhi sehe na taṃ kaścitpravṛddhaṃ lokakaṇṭakam ||
children.translated_text: no one in battle could withstand him, grown into a thorn of the worlds.
Then one day, while <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> was seated with the <s>Vṛṣṇis</s>
in an assembly hall bright with many sapphire pillars and radiant jewel-thrones,
there appeared the sky, tawny with flashing masses of splendor,
like the radiance of golden dust from <s>Meru</s> crushed by the hooves of the sun's horses.
In the midst of it, the glorious lord of the gods gradually became clearly visible,
with streams of heavenly <s>Gaṅgā</s> water scattered by <s>Airāvaṇa</s>'s trunk.
He descended from heaven, attended by a moon-white parasol and fly-whisks,
and was surrounded by forests of ornament-rays like clusters of <s>Śakra</s>'s bow.
The <s>Vṛṣṇis</s>, headed by those named <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> and <s>Baladeva</s>,
rose suddenly and honored him with joy, wonder, and respect.
The thousand-eyed one quickly dismounted from the elephant and adorned a great seat;
looking affectionately at <s>Viṣṇu</s>, he spoke:
"Ah, blessed are the <s>Mādhavas</s> and <s>Vṛṣṇis</s>, praiseworthy for good conduct,
since you, like the sun to lotus-ponds, have risen visible among them.
You are the agent of the affairs of the worlds and the destroyer of the enemies of the gods;
I have come to you for the cutting off of calamity in the three worlds.

children.text: jaganti jagatāṃ nātha narako nāma bhūmijaḥ
children.translated_text: Lord of the worlds, a son of the earth named <s>Naraka</s>

children.text: bādhate kāmagaṃ yasya puraṃ prāgjyotiṣaṃ divi ||
children.translated_text: oppresses the worlds; his city <s>Prāgjyotiṣa</s> moves at will in the sky.
From the goddess <s>Aditi</s>, mother of the dwellers in heaven,
he violently stole her divine earrings, blazing with the brilliance of great suns.
Demons called <s>Hayagrīva</s> and <s>Nisunda</s>, hostile to the gods and relying on him,

children.text: kṣapayantyakṣayā bhāṃsi mahāṃsi ca yaśāṃsi naḥ ||
children.translated_text: are destroying our inexhaustible splendors and our great fame.
For the destruction of that son of the earth, who is like blind darkness,
you alone are able, like a sunrise mountain for the fierce sun of the discus.
This lord of birds, like our very wish,
will carry you to the place where that demon rests in his own city."
When <s>Śakra</s> had spoken thus and fallen silent, and <s>Murāri</s> had said, "So be it,"
<s>Garuḍa</s> appeared in the sky like a mass of lightning.
The discus-armed one mounted him at once, accompanied by <s>Satyabhāmā</s>,
while the lord of the gods mounted <s>Airāvaṇa</s>; they went by the path of the sky.

children.text: nākaṃ nākapatau yāte hariḥ prāgjyotiṣaṃ puram
children.translated_text: When the lord of heaven had gone to heaven, <s>Hari</s>, going to the city <s>Prāgjyotiṣa</s>,
cut through six thousand nooses in the demon's dwelling.
He killed <s>Mura</s> with his servants, ministers, sons, and kinsmen,
and <s>Nisunda</s>, after splitting apart masses of stones and heaps of thunderbolts;

children.text: hayagrīvaṃ ca yo varṣasahasraṃ yuyudhe suraiḥ
children.translated_text: also <s>Hayagrīva</s>, who had fought the gods for a thousand years,
and wicked <s>Virūpākṣa</s> in <s>Alakā</s>, together with his followers;
and likewise five-handed <s>Tāra</s> in the midst of the <s>Lohitagaṅgā</s>.
After killing them, he reached the swift-moving city <s>Prāgjyotiṣa</s>,
and slaughtered eight hundred thousand demons of dense power.
Then a terrible battle arose between <s>Naraka</s> and the slayer of <s>Madhu</s>,
great, terrifying to all beings, and shaking the worlds.
Then the discus-armed one, in anger, with his shining discus,

children.text: cakre cakreṇa narakaṃ dvidhā cakrāyudhaḥ krudhā ||
children.translated_text: whose edge was like a saw and whose nave was adamantine, cut <s>Naraka</s> in two.
When the earth-born one had fallen to the ground, shaped like a huge mountain,
burned by the fire-stream of the discus, together with his city and palace,

children.text: putraśokākulā devī chatraṃ ca pradadau mahī
children.translated_text: the goddess <s>Mahī</s>, distraught with grief for her son, gave the umbrella,
and the earrings, to the foe of <s>Kaiṭabha</s>, for the protection of his subjects.
Then <s>Hari</s>, from that city whose whole wealth of the lord of gods and of <s>Dhanada</s> had been plundered,
brought away the heap of jewels and departed from that city.
The great umbrella of the lord of waters, which had been taken by <s>Naraka</s>,
marked with a hundred thousand streams, the <s>Dāśārha</s> took from there as well.
The maidens of the <s>Gandharvas</s>, gods, and <s>Kinnaras</s>, imprisoned by him,
had been placed on a jewel mountain; <s>Madhusūdana</s> saw them there.
They were thrilled by waves of nectarous joy from the sight of <s>Govinda</s>;
raising the jewel mountain, the one whose banner is <s>Tārkṣya</s> led them away.

children.text: sa dṛṣṭvā divi deveśaṃ pūjitastena sādaram
children.translated_text: Having seen the lord of gods in heaven and been respectfully honored by him,
he looked with joy upon <s>Satyabhāmā</s>, who had been honored by <s>Śacī</s>.
Then the destroyer of demons, together with <s>Śakra</s>, bowed to the goddess <s>Aditi</s>,
the mother of the gods, and gave her the divine earrings.
He saw the <s>Pārijāta</s>, ornament of <s>Nandana</s>, ever granting all desires,
born from nectar, noble as though it were a lord.
Seeing that tree, a kinsman to the joy of the eyes, <s>Mādhava</s> himself
uprooted it and quickly carried it off; the slayer of <s>Vṛtra</s> allowed it.
Going through the sky with <s>Satyabhāmā</s> as his companion and with the <s>Pārijāta</s>,
mounted on <s>Suparṇa</s>, he became like wonder itself embodied.
By crowds of <s>Vidyādhara</s> women, filled with amazement and joy,
and eager with curiosity, he was as if drunk in again and again by their eyes.
Reaching <s>Dvārakā</s>, he released the lord of birds,
and saw it further adorned, by <s>Śakra</s>'s command, with varied embellishments,
wonderful, crowded with jeweled inner palaces fashioned by <s>Viśvakarman</s>,
with networks of swaying golden creepers and with jeweled and golden peaks,
protected on every side by mountains with spacious caves and waterfalls.
That city, surrounded on every side by mountains, the hero entered, honored by the <s>Vṛṣṇis</s> and <s>Yādavas</s>.
He bowed to the powerful goddess, his sister, standing between her brothers,
and, praised by <s>Nārada</s> himself for exploits made noble by victory,
<s>Hari</s> sported for a long time with women whose eyes stole the grace of deer.
Now <s>Pradyumna</s>, who was born as <s>Hari</s>'s son from <s>Rukmiṇī</s>,
was carried off from the birthing chamber by a demon named <s>Śambara</s>.
As a child he grew up in that demon's city, called <s>Okṣumatī</s>,
and little by little, through affection, was made one who had crossed to the far shore of every magical weapon.
Learning the story of his own abduction from the words of that beloved woman,
he killed in a great battle the one who knew all forms of magic.

children.text: taṃ kālaśambaraṃ ghoraṃ sābhilāṣāṃ ca tadvadhūm
children.translated_text: That terrible <s>Kālaśambara</s> he slew, and that demon's wife, filled with desire,
who had made her request, the lover swiftly took as his beloved <s>Māyāvatī</s>.
Carrying her away by the path of the sky and reaching <s>Dvārakā</s>,
he bowed, filled with overflowing joy, to his father, the beloved of <s>Rukmiṇī</s>.
He, the glorious incarnation of <s>Smara</s>, the bewilderer of <s>Śambara</s>,

children.text: sa babhūva paraṃ vīraḥ kārṣṇilokeṣu viśrutaḥ
children.translated_text: became a supreme hero, famed among the people of <s>Kārṣṇa</s>'s line,
and sons of <s>Mādhava</s> equal to him, headed by <s>Sāmba</s>, were renowned.
Kings came to see that astonishing splendor of <s>Hari</s> with his sons,
desired even by the thirty gods and hard to find on earth.
Those rulers of men from many lands, headed by <s>Duryodhana</s>,
were surrounded by eighteen <s>akṣauhiṇīs</s> of heroes.
Encircling Mount <s>Raivataka</s>, all of them, full of wonder,
stood in the secluded and lovely grounds near <s>Dvārakā</s>.
Then the blessed <s>Hari</s> went out with all the clans of the <s>Vṛṣṇis</s>,
honoring all those lords of the earth in due order.
When they were seated on thrones, the illustrious one took a great jeweled seat,
like a treasury of radiances upon the crest of Mount <s>Rohaṇa</s>.
Royal splendor, born from a forest of kingly lotuses and ringing with the anklets of bards,
seemed to embrace <s>Govinda</s>, smiling with umbrellas and yak-tail fans.
<s>Nārada</s> came to see him seated in the assembly of kings,
and said, 'O god, blessed are you, the wonder of the dwellers in heaven.'
When <s>Nārada</s> was answered by him, 'I am so together with the <s>dakṣiṇās</s>,'
the kings, filled with curiosity, asked, 'What is this?'
Urged respectfully by <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, 'Let it be told,' he spoke:
'Once, while I was bathing three times daily on the bank of the heavenly river,
I saw a turtle of wondrous form and said, "Blessed am I."
It said, "The wondrous <s>Gaṅgā</s> is blessed, resorted to by such as us."

children.text: dhanyāsīti mayā sāpi pṛṣṭā māṃ pratyabhāṣata ||
children.translated_text: When I asked her too, "Are you blessed?" she replied to me:
"More wondrous and blessed is the ocean, lord of all rivers."

children.text: pṛṣṭaḥ so 'pi mayā prāha mattaḥ kṣitiriyaṃ varā ||
children.translated_text: Questioned by me, he too said, "This earth is better than I."
She too said, "More wondrous are the mountains, by whom I am upheld."
They too said, "The lotus-born creator of the worlds is wondrous."
Asked by me, he too said, "The <s>Vedas</s> are greater than every wonder."
They too said, "Wondrous are the sacrifices, for whose sake we stand."
Questioned by me, they too said, "Our wondrous goal is <s>Viṣṇu</s>,
true, eternal, holy, who receives the all-offering."
Hearing this, I came and questioned <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> with great curiosity,
and the lord said this to me: "I am so together with the <s>dakṣiṇās</s>."'
When <s>Nārada</s> had spoken thus and departed, the circle of kings was astonished.
After he had gone and received proper honors, <s>Hari</s> entered his own city.
Once <s>Keśava</s> himself was consecrated for a great sacrifice,
when a distressed Brahmin came to him and begged, "Protect me!"

children.text: brūhi kiṃ te bhayamiti brāhmaṇaḥ śauriṇoditaḥ
children.translated_text: When <s>Śauri</s> said, "Tell me, what fear do you have?" the Brahmin
said, "I am luckless: three sons, each as soon as he was born,

children.text: hṛtāḥ kenāpi bhūtena caturthaṃ parirakṣa me
children.translated_text: have been carried off by some being; protect the fourth for me.
When the Brahmin said, "This is my wife's time of delivery,"
<s>Viṣṇu</s> assigned <s>Arjuna</s>, together with the <s>Vṛṣṇi</s> heroes, to guard him.
The bowman of <s>Gāṇḍīva</s> quickly reached the Brahmin's dwelling,
and, surrounding the quarters with the <s>Vṛṣṇis</s>, stood ready for the act of protection.
Then at midnight, when the Brahmin woman had delivered, amid ill omens,
a cry arose among the people: "The son has been taken! Taken!"
Hearing the distressed cry of the women and the piteous sound of the infant,
<s>Pārtha</s>, <s>Sātyaki</s>, and the others filled the sky with arrows.
When their efforts had proved vain and they had been reviled by the Brahmin,
they were ashamed and departed; hearing what had happened, <s>Acyuta</s>
took a chariot yoked with <s>Śaibya</s> and <s>Sugrīva</s>, with <s>Arjuna</s> as charioteer,
and <s>Garuḍadhvaja</s> set out, the ocean granting him a path.
Swift as thought, he crossed the ocean whose waters had become still,
while on the way <s>Meru</s>, <s>Kailāsa</s>, and other chief mountains bowed and gave him passage.
Then, with his discus tearing up the dense, rock-like darkness,
he reached a stainless expanse of sky and a radiance in the form of a man.

children.text: avicchinnaṃ jagadvyāpi dṛṣṭvā tyaktvā ca taṃ ratham
children.translated_text: Seeing it unbroken and pervading the world, and abandoning that chariot,
<s>Hari</s> entered that brilliance, like a thousand suns, and came out after a moment.
From that very place he took the four sons and gave them
to the Brahmin, whose heart was filled with joy and wonder.
Then <s>Kaiṭabhāri</s>, having reached <s>Dvārakā</s> with <s>Kirīṭin</s>,
was asked about that extraordinary wonder, and he, an ocean of marvels, said:
"Those mountains, that darkness, and that exceedingly brilliant radiance
were myself alone, the cause of the world's birth, continuance, and destruction.
By that radiant great-souled one, who desired a meeting with me,
the Brahmin's sons were taken and then handed back."
Meanwhile a great Asura named <s>Bāṇa</s>, son of <s>Baḍeḥauleḥjh</s> in the corrupt reading,

children.text: jahāra surasaṃghānāṃ tejāṃsi ca yaśāṃsi ca ||
children.translated_text: carried off the splendors and the fame of the hosts of gods.
Then the blessed <s>Bhava</s>, fond of his devotees, became pleased with him;

children.text: āsthāne yasya sa gaṇaḥ sabhyatāṃ satataṃ yayau ||
children.translated_text: in his court <s>Bāṇa</s>, as an attendant, constantly attained a seat in the assembly.
He was a pillar of a thousand arms, by whom the valor of the immortals was checked,
and he reduced even <s>Trivikrama</s>'s attained fame to dwarfishness.
That hero, longing for battle, once questioned <s>Tripurāntaka</s>,
having conquered everything, with folded hands drawn close by affection:
"Long forgetful of battle, O Blessed One, in war I desire
the scratching away of the battle-itch of these staff-like arms."
