Laughing, the god <s>Śūlapāṇi</s>, fittingly mindful of those arms, said to him:
"You will have a battle, signaled by the breaking of your banner."
Hearing this bold promise, and filled with joy, mighty
<s>Bāṇa</s> went to his own palace and reported it to his minister.
Then <s>Kumbhāṇḍa</s>, his minister and the best of the wise, said to him:
"Ah, this eagerness of yours for battle, O king, is without fruit.
The fortune of the three worlds has been obtained; all the gods have been conquered.
What use is war? Even for the mighty, victory and defeat are fickle."

children.text: iti vādini kumbhāṇḍe bāṇe ca samarotsuke
children.translated_text: While <s>Kumbhāṇḍa</s> was speaking thus and <s>Bāṇa</s> was eager for battle,
his banner, lofty like a play-mountain of demonic splendor, fell.
When that banner had fallen, proclaiming the destruction of the Dānavas,
and terrible ill omens had appeared everywhere,
<s>Bāṇa</s> was overcome with delight and indulged in drinking and sport,
while <s>Kumbhāṇḍa</s>, the eye of policy, had his heart scorched by anxiety.
Once, in <s>Bāṇa</s>'s city, in a grove flowering in every season,
the crescent-crested <s>Śiva</s> sported with the daughter of the mountain.
With troops of <s>Gandharvas</s> and <s>Apsarases</s>, absorbed in the arts of song and dance,
attending him, the lord's amorous grace shone brightly.
There, for laughter, a divine performer named <s>Citralekhā</s>
performed a dance according to rule in order to serve <s>Pārvatī</s>'s husband.
Through playful joking and amusement, with various mocking imitations,
performed by the <s>Apsarases</s>, <s>Bhava</s>'s beloved laughed.
There <s>Uṣā</s>, <s>Bāṇa</s>'s blue-lotus-eyed daughter,
saw the sportive play of <s>Śiva</s> and <s>Pārvatī</s>, a festival of the immortals.

children.text: tāṃ vīkṣya sādarāṃ devī babhāṣe lalitānanām
children.translated_text: Seeing her attentive, the goddess addressed the lovely-faced girl:
"<s>Uṣā</s>, you too will be absorbed in play with a beloved.

children.text: vaiśākhe harmyasaktāyā dvādaśyāṃ niśi yena te
children.translated_text: In <s>Vaiśākha</s>, on the twelfth night, while you are in the palace,

children.text: bhavitā saṃgamaḥ svapne sa te prāgjātivallabhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: the man with whom you will have union in a dream is your beloved from a former birth."
Thus addressed by <s>Bhavānī</s>, <s>Bāṇa</s>'s devout daughter
went to the inner apartments, her lotus eyes opened wide with joy.
As if asked, "What is this?" by her jingling jeweled ornaments,
with her hand laid on her trembling locks and her face bent down in bashfulness,
she was questioned by her friend <s>Citralekhā</s>, daughter of <s>Kumbhāṇḍa</s>:
"From where has fear arisen for you? Why do you tremble like a creeper?
After all, you are the daughter of <s>Bāṇa</s>, who causes fear to <s>Jambhāri</s>."

children.text: ityuṣā sahasā sakhyā pṛṣṭā tāṃ pratyabhāṣata ||
children.translated_text: Thus suddenly questioned by her friend, <s>Uṣā</s> answered her.
making, with collyrium-like tears, a shadow like a blemish on your moon-face,

children.text: kathaṃ nu dūṣitā nāma pūjyāsi janamāninī ||
children.translated_text: how indeed are you to be called defiled, you who are venerable and honored by people?
Could I ever endure life, chaste though I am, with my family stained?
As she was noisy with such lamentation, her friends spoke to that friend with joy:
Women of good families are not defiled by union in a dream, foolish girl.

children.text: kiṃ na smarasi yadgauryā sūcitaṃ kelikānane
children.translated_text: Do you not remember what <s>Gaurī</s> indicated in the pleasure grove:
'In a dream, timid one, your beloved will be the thief of your heart'?
Thus freely reminded at once by <s>Citralekhā</s>,
she joyfully meditated on her beloved, a nectar-rayed moon for the mind.
In her some strange, fresh flavor of longing grew,
by which the powerful fire of love suddenly blazed up.
Seeing her, with her petal-like lower lip grey from continual sighs,
<s>Citralekhā</s> spoke to her friend, like a creeper wilted by heat:
Friend, what is this delusion of curiosity about an undrawn picture?
Passion for a person seen in a dream is a crest-ornament made from one's own flowers.
It is obtaining a reflection in a mirror; it is asking the stars for the moon.
And eagerness for one seen in a dream, girl, is a childish desire.

children.text: na jānīmaḥ sa kaḥ kvāste kathaṃ vā kena labhyate
children.translated_text: We do not know who he is, where he stays, or how and by whom he may be obtained.
Surely your meeting with him must come about by itself.
Or else, the forms of gods, <s>Gandharvas</s>, <s>Kinnaras</s>, serpents, and <s>Rākṣasas</s>,
and of the kings who dwell within the three worlds,
I will draw without distinction on the edge of a cloth by my art, friend,

children.text: darśayāmi tava kṣipraṃ tato jānīhi vallabham ||
children.translated_text: and quickly show them to you; then recognize your beloved.
Having said this, within seven nights, after drawing them all on a cloth,
<s>Citralekhā</s>, able to reproduce everything for her friend, painted them.
Looking at the divine, serpent, royal, and human figures placed on the painted cloth,
she saw, among the heroes of the <s>Vṛṣṇis</s>, one handsome like <s>Govinda</s>.
Looking at that <s>Aniruddha</s>, filled with wonder and joy,
<s>Uṣā</s> said, 'This is he, the thief of my maidenly vow.'
Friend, who is this handsome lotus-eyed man with mighty arms,

children.text: prasahyāpahṛtaṃ yena dhairyaṃ me manasā saha ||
children.translated_text: by whom my courage has been forcibly carried off together with my mind?
Hearing this, <s>Citralekhā</s> said with a lovely smile:
Friend, this is the son's son of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, enemy of <s>Mura</s>.
He is the hero <s>Aniruddha</s>, the beloved of your heart pointed out by the goddess.
Surely this <s>Kāma</s> has come in a dream to seek pleasure with you.
By his valor in battles, while gods and demons look on in wonder,
excellent warriors, together with their kinsmen's hopes, are made small.
Hearing this, possessed by love and with her eyes fixed on the image,
<s>Uṣā</s> said, 'Without my beloved I cannot bear to live.

children.text: yadi ter'tho mama prāṇairyadi te 'haṃ priyā sakhī
children.translated_text: If my life has any value to you, if I am a dear friend to you,

children.text: tadanena kuru kṣipraṃ kāntena mama saṃgamam ||
children.translated_text: then quickly bring about my union with this beloved.'
To her, speaking thus again and again, <s>Citralekhā</s> said:
Just as your father's <s>Śoṇitapura</s> is guarded by good warriors,
so too <s>Dvārakā</s> is protected by the heroic <s>Vṛṣṇis</s>,
and, ringed with formidable watchtowers, it is inaccessible even to another.

children.text: tataḥ sakhi kathaṃ nāma vīraṃ te jīviteśvaram
children.translated_text: Therefore, friend, how could any woman ever be bold enough
to seize by force and carry off the hero who is lord of your life?
Even so, for your sake, I shall go, leading the way through the sky.
But success, ordained by the goddess, rests in your fortune, friend.
Having said this, she quickly entered the sky, with the rays of her jeweled ornaments
making the quarters variegated like <s>Indra</s>'s bow, as the splendor of a cloud does.
In a moment, swiftly setting out from <s>Bāṇa</s>'s city at the third watch,
she reached <s>Dvārakā</s> in an instant, its beauty mocking <s>Kailāsa</s>.
There, while the sky shone with the radiance of broad rows of great jewels,
she entered <s>Aniruddha</s>'s palace with her form unseen.
There she saw <s>Aniruddha</s>, surrounded by beloved women with fawn-like eyes,
his movements graceful with the sport of the god of love,
his brilliance mottled by the sidelong glances of affectionate young women,
as if he were <s>Smara</s> with a petal stuck from the blow of <s>Rati</s>'s ear-lotus.
He was marked with leaf-creepers made by breasts pressed close in the embraces of women,
and was covered with flowers from their braids, like another <s>Pārijāta</s> tree.
Seeing him, noble in valor and lovely in the form of erotic grace,
<s>Citralekhā</s>, seized with sudden alarm, thought for a moment:
Ah, I have set out upon this great undertaking, full of uncertainty,

children.text: kārye priyasakhīprītyā premṇi vā kiṃ vicintyate ||
children.translated_text: out of affection for my dear friend; yet in love, what is to be considered?

children.text: iti dhyātvā muhurvīrā sā tamovidyayā puraḥ
children.translated_text: Having reflected thus again and again, that heroine, with the magic of darkness before her,
covered the whole company of women and in an instant carried away [the text here is corrupt, apparently <s>Pradyumna</s>'s son, <s>Aniruddha</s>].
Like the power of resolve, swift-moving through her <s>māyā</s> (magic illusion),
she entered <s>Śoṇitapura</s> and went to her friend who was in the palace.
<s>Uṣā</s>, too, troubled by hundreds of hopes of obtaining her beloved,
suddenly saw her dear one, whom her friend had brought through the sky.
As if at once flooded with nectar, confused by joy, modesty, and fear,

children.text: kiṃ karomīti saṃbhrāntā kampamānā lateva sā ||
children.translated_text: she trembled like a creeper, bewildered and thinking, 'What shall I do?'
Having entered an indescribable state, her jeweled ornaments tinkling,
that delighted woman took her beloved and
entered a secret chamber, her eyes restless, afraid of people passing by,
with her girdle slipped, as though it had left her by itself from fear of <s>Bāṇa</s>.
There, with a splendid crown of <s>mandāra</s> flowers and swinging earrings,
with a beautiful necklace of very bright strings of pearls, he shone like the lord of stars.
Through him, a preceptor in initiation into love, radiant with all the splendor of <s>Smara</s>,
<s>Uṣā</s> remembered the wealth of <s>Rati</s>'s good fortune in union.
Through him, a preceptor in initiation into love, radiant with all the splendor of <s>Smara</s>,
<s>Uṣā</s> remembered the wealth of <s>Rati</s>'s good fortune in union.

children.text: aniruddho 'pi tāṃ prāpya vallabhāṃ bhuvi durlabhām
children.translated_text: <s>Aniruddha</s> too, having obtained her as his beloved, hard to obtain on earth,
thought himself a vessel for the riches of <s>Smara</s>'s empire.
As <s>Pradyumna</s>'s son secretly delighted with her there,
he was recognized by many signs by the guards of the maiden's inner apartments.
At the command of <s>Bāṇa</s>, the son of <s>Bali</s>, angry at the dishonor of his daughter,
terrible servants came to kill the descendant of <s>Pradyumna</s>.
Seeing them, their mouths made hideous by tusks and terrifying with fierce, knitted brows,
and seeing their dreadful swords and bows drawn, the hero <s>Aniruddha</s>
rose up with valor unrestrained at the beginning of battle,
and, raising a door-bar, rushed at them like a lion at deer.
Under the glance of his beloved, the body of that treasury of heroism
shone with the ardor of heroic love, as if he were <s>Manmatha</s> embodied.
Taking on his chest the shower of weapons hurled by them as if it were a garland of flowers,
he, roaring deeply, killed the demon soldiers.
Struck by his blows, their dreadful bodies broken,
the survivors fled in fear to where battle-fierce <s>Bāṇa</s> was.
"Why has this panic come upon men who witnessed the destruction of <s>Purandara</s>'s city,
a panic that produces bewilderment through anger and is fit for cowards?
Show regard for valor, the springtime for the blossoms of fame;
this fear is indeed unbearable, a thunderbolt falling on the mountain of pride."

children.text: vacobhiriti vīrāṇāṃ te bāṇasya ca śāsanāt
children.translated_text: With these words from the heroes, and at <s>Bāṇa</s>'s command,
they again rushed upon <s>Aniruddha</s> with a very great army.
With golden armor fastened on and many kinds of weapons blazing,
they were like moving great mountains with forests of shining herbs at night.
The grandson of the discus-armed one's son fought in battle with those enraged warriors,
while looking at his beloved, whose hand was set upon her trembling breasts.

children.text: ādāya tatsamutsṛṣṭaṃ khaḍgaṃ carma ca bhāsvaram
children.translated_text: Taking up the sword and shining shield that they had hurled at him,

children.text: maṇḍalāni caranvīraḥ sa cakarta raṇe ripūn ||
children.translated_text: the hero moved in circles and cut down his enemies in battle.
With their heads, shoulders, arms, knees, bellies, and waists cut off by him,
they fell like great clouds churned by the wind at the end of an age.
When the demon army had fled, its chariots and elephants shattered,
<s>Bāṇa</s> himself appeared, turning back the ocean of his forces.
With the reins entrusted to <s>Kumbhāṇḍa</s>, with a radiant team of a thousand horses,
with a dreadfully rumbling chariot, radiant with a thousand horses,
he was joined to that dreadfully rumbling chariot by the crusher of the gods.
He was formidable with the finest blazing weapons whirling from his thousand arms,
like a mountain whose peak is covered by fierce serpents with jeweled hoods.
With a sun-colored crown adorned by matted locks of jewel-flame,
and with white bands seeming to laugh aloud, he seemed to threaten all brilliance.
With fierce splendor raised by earrings like the disk of the sun,
and with a face terrible from frowning, he frightened the three worlds.
He was rippled by a starry necklace broad as the rays of the moon,
like a dark rain-cloud pouring forth wide cascades.
Adorned with beard and hair of heated-gold hue,
he seemed aflame from the tips of his teeth ground together in anger.
As he came rushing on, roaring, "Stand! Stand!" with the sound of the flood at dissolution,
the son of <s>Pradyumna</s> did not tremble.
By the unbroken nets of arrows released from the forest of <s>Bāṇa</s>'s arms,
he became covered, like the sun by undivided clouds.
Their furious battle became a cause for remembering the battles of <s>Hari</s>, <s>Hara</s>, and <s>Hiraṇyākṣa</s>,
and it shook the worlds with its own shaking.
Then <s>Aniruddha</s>, moving swiftly, cut through the succession of <s>Bāṇa</s>'s arrows with his sword,
and cut off the pole of his chariot.
Then the lord of demons hurled at him a flame-filled spear,
marked as if with a red strip, like a serpent-bride.
Taking in his hand that very spear, resembling the fang of Death, the steadfast one,
the <s>Dāśārha</s> of wondrous valor, sent it back at the lord of demons.

children.text: bāṇasya bhittvā sā dehaṃ viveśa dharaṇītalam
children.translated_text: After piercing <s>Bāṇa</s>'s body, it entered the surface of the earth.
Seeing <s>Bāṇa</s> split open by the spear, <s>Kumbhāṇḍa</s> said to him:
"Resort to magic and fight; if this man is neglected, he is hard to conquer.
In gambling and in battle, certain victory belongs to those who use illusion."
At <s>Kumbhāṇḍa</s>'s words, <s>Bāṇa</s> took up a bewildering magic,
terrible and dark, and suddenly disappeared.
Invisible, from the sky, with arrows in the form of serpents,
fierce with poison, he made that hero's limbs bound fast.
Surrounded by serpents blazing with the flames of quivering hood-jewels,
he shone with mottled color, like a sandalwood tree.
When <s>Aniruddha</s>, bound by the serpent-noose, remained steadfast and unshaken in mind,
the lord of demons formed the intention of killing him.
"This man is somehow of great power; being unknown, he does not deserve death."
At <s>Kumbhāṇḍa</s>'s words, the son of <s>Bali</s> stopped.
Meanwhile, in the inner palace of <s>Dvārakā</s>,
the loud cry arose: "<s>Aniruddha</s> has been carried off by someone!"
There the doe-eyed women, repeatedly helpless from fainting and terrified,
the beloveds of <s>Aniruddha</s>, lamented, overwhelmed by grief.
Then, in the assembly of the foremost <s>Vṛṣṇis</s>, in the presence of the enemy of <s>Kaiṭabha</s>,
A very great assembly was formed of those summoned by the sound of the kettledrum.
Then, like the seven oceans motionless in a windless calm,
they saw <s>Acyuta</s>, their eyes filled with tears, stilled by anxiety.
When the circle of the <s>Yādavas</s> was silent, overcome by the poison of grief and bewilderment,
wise <s>Vipṛthu</s> spoke to <s>Viṣṇu</s>, the conqueror of the enemies of the gods:
"What is this, even in you, O blessed lord, giver of fearlessness to the worlds,
this new spread of anguish from an inconceivable and great sorrow?
For surely in minds noble and deep as the great ocean,
there are no floods of joy and grief amid pleasures and pains.
If even you, O god, O <s>Acyuta</s>, are thus tormented by anxiety,
then now the course of courage, without any support, has stumbled.
<s>Jambhasūdana</s> has entrusted the protection of the three worlds to your arm,
and lies content in the joy of pleasure, embracing <s>Śacī</s>'s breasts."
Hearing what he had said, <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, in a deep and measured way,
set forth his speech, like a cloud to the swan-flocks of his enemies' fame:
"Contempt from another, through insult, makes a place in the heart
of the self-respecting, truly, like ignorance in embodied beings.
Today the foot of the <s>Yadu</s> clan has, by some arrogant-minded person,
been cast upon its head, covered with the mud of the road.
When <s>Aniruddha</s> has been carried off, our prowess, once considered foremost among kings,
has become fit only to be the object of mocking talk.
Since this wounding insult was inflicted by someone unknown,
what shall we do, striking the sky with punishments fierce as anger?
Let spies range everywhere, moving outside and inside,
swiftly, by <s>Āhuka</s>'s command, in order to discover <s>Aniruddha</s>."
When the enemy of <s>Kaṃsa</s> had spoken thus, the divine seer <s>Nārada</s>
appeared there, a treasury of splendors, skilled in the play of quarrels.
Seeing the lord of the world stilled by anxiety, he thought:
"Ah, the ocean has been disturbed by the leaping of a little minnow."
As he was considering this, <s>Janārdana</s> performed worship for him,
with water for the feet and a seat first; and he, being honored, spoke:

children.text: aho bata vimoho vaḥ pratipakṣaḥ parākrame
children.translated_text: "Ah, your bewilderment is indeed seen as an adversary to prowess;
therefore learn what has happened to <s>Aniruddha</s>.
For <s>Aniruddha</s>, with mighty <s>Bāṇa</s>, son of <s>Bali</s>,
there has occurred a festival of battle, terrifying with weapons and missiles set in motion.
O <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, your grandson <s>Aniruddha</s> has been carried off by the daughter of the daitya lord;

children.text: manye muhyati yāṃ dṛṣṭvā smaro 'pi smarapīḍitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: I think even <s>Smara</s>, seeing her, would be pierced by love.
She is <s>Uṣā</s> by name, lotus-eyed, the daughter, a lotus-pond of beauty,
of thousand-armed <s>Bāṇa</s>, son of <s>Bali</s>, enemy of the gods.
When he learned that his daughter had a lover, the delight of her heart, acting at will,

children.text: dṛṣṭvā ca durjayaṃ yuddhe babandha phaṇimaṇḍalaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: and saw that he was hard to conquer in battle, he bound him with coils of serpents.
Therefore from here you must go to <s>Bāṇa</s>'s <s>Śoṇitapura</s>, rising to the height of the sky,

children.text: gantavyaṃ bhavatā yoddhuṃ sāmasādhyā na dānavāḥ ||
children.translated_text: to fight; demons are not to be subdued by conciliation.
That land of immortals is hard to cross; you should go mounted on <s>Tārkṣya</s>,
where <s>Bāṇa</s>, by name an arrow in the hearts of the gods, is a thunderbolt to his foes."
When the divine seer had spoken thus and departed, the god <s>Madhusūdana</s>
came equally under the sway of joy, wonder, and anger.
Then the blessed one whose banner is <s>Garuḍa</s> meditated on <s>Garuḍa</s>,
and he, once meditated upon, suddenly appeared, like a spotless sun.
The soul of the universe mounted him with the ease of ascending a palace,
glorious, with <s>Baladeva</s> as his companion and followed by <s>Rukmiṇī</s>'s son.
The lord shone, clear and dark, adorned with the <s>Kaustubha</s>,
overpowering the brilliance of the sky when the sun had descended into its midst.
The abundant arm-trees of his four-armed form shone forth,
leafed by the radiance of the discus and blossoming with the rays of <s>Pāñcajanya</s>.
As he traveled, charming with his yellow garment tossed by the wind,
he made the sky golden with wheels of light from <s>Tārkṣya</s>'s wings.
Reflected in all the jewels of his ornaments, as though they had come out of curiosity,
were the fluttering turban-sprouts turned back along the edge of the sky, and with them he was attended.
Clusters of mandāra blossoms cast from the lotus-hands of women of the gods and <s>Vidyādharas</s>
became for him the semblance of strings of garlands.
When heroic <s>Aniruddha</s>, together with <s>Uṣā</s>, was confined in battle
by serpent-nooses in his own city by mighty <s>Bāṇa</s>,

children.text: durgasaṃtāriṇīṃ durgāṃ tadā sa śaraṇaṃ gataḥ
children.translated_text: then he took refuge in <s>Durgā</s>, who carries one across difficulties,
the sister of <s>Mahendra</s> and <s>Upendra</s>, and praised her with divine names:
"I praise the goddess, moonlight to the mass of darkness that is the power of <s>Kaṃsa</s> and the demons,
whose face is like the full moon, able to bewilder the wicked;
terrifying with a net of blazing trident-rays, graceful in form,
like a sandalwood creeper with fierce, writhing poisonous serpents;
dark, adorned with a necklace, her foot placed on the buffalo,
like the <s>Yamunā</s>, with <s>Kāliya</s>'s pool, smiling with foam;
with a dark sword-creeper in her hand, to which coils of serpents cling,
like a lotus plant with a swarm of bees rising from the heart of a single lotus;
served by mottled peacock-feather ornaments with blackish splendor,
like the rainy season by clouds flashing with rainbows;
eager for pure movement with her terrible locks spread wide,
like a dark aloe creeper sprung from a peak of <s>Himādri</s>;
<s>Sarasvatī</s>, the royal swan dwelling in the minds of lordly poets,
with varied, sweet, and noble sound and a beautiful sequence of words;
intent on quenching the burning heat of the desert of <s>saṃsāra</s>.
streaming in waves with the nectar of the bliss of consciousness in which all is one;
whose majestic onset has the profound play of the tumultuous burden of battle,
before whom the immortals were imagined as fearful at the cries of <s>Niśumbha</s> and <s>Śumbha</s>;
the unfailing twilight, dwelling on <s>Vindhyādri</s>, the younger sister of <s>Vāsava</s>,
marked with a crest of moon-fragments and adorned with a garland of heads;
dark as a grove of blossoming blue lotuses, with eyes like blossoming blue lotuses,
with a deep hollow of a navel and breasts like the temples of elephants;
the blessed <s>Kātyāyanī</s>, fierce <s>Caṇḍā</s>, <s>Cāmuṇḍā</s>, crusher of enemies,
<s>Śarvāṇī</s>, Night, <s>Śarvā</s>, served by siddhas and gandharvas;
the terrible one who draws in Time, eager for the village of the three worlds,
whose crest is adorned with a garland made from the skeleton of lotus-seated <s>Brahmā</s>;
auspicious, bestower of auspiciousness, tranquil, beloved of <s>Śiva</s>, hundred-faced,
three-eyed, gentle-faced, shining with the proud brilliance of the enemy of <s>Madana</s>;
clothed in a garment like the swelling foam of the nectar-ocean, with a jeweled girdle,
tawny with rays from the golden mountain and the citron held in her hand;
with a rosary whose beads are revolving star-jewels,
with a skull-bowl in her hand, a whole cosmic egg filled with the nectar-ocean;
with the clear expanded sky as her mirror, bright with the light of consciousness,
wearing necklaces, armlets, and bracelets made of the great serpent-lords of <s>Śeṣa</s>'s race;
with the disks of moon and sun smiling with stars as pearls,
radiant with a crown whose turrets are lordly three-peaked jewel-mountains;
adorned with a white turban like the tossing waves of the heavenly river,
assuming the appearance of a peacock parasol, like a raincloud bearing <s>Indra</s>'s bow;
like a female bee fond of drinking the dense nectar of the heart-lotus, whose stalk is the lotus-fiber of the navel curled at the tip of its root;
I take refuge in the Mother, the mother of all that is to be known, perceptible through the ever-arisen power of sound.
Thus praised with devotion by the son of <s>Pradyumna</s>,
the blessed ten-armed <s>Durgā</s> made herself present before him in person.
With a hand shining like a lotus
she burst apart his terrible serpent-cage, hard to pierce and like a rampart of adamant;
then, repeatedly followed on every side by her own swelling splendors,
she entered the sky, as if drawing away the life-breaths of the daitya lords.
Meanwhile the blessed one of great speed, whose banner is <s>Garuḍa</s>,
reached <s>Bāṇa</s>'s <s>Śoṇitapura</s>, which was guarded by fire.
The destroyer of <s>Kāliya</s> became eight-armed and terrible in form,
bearing conch, discus, mace, lotus, arrow, bow, sword, and shield.
And <s>Halāyudha</s> became like a snowy mountain,
vast with a thousand peaks, with a thousand bodies and faces.
And <s>Pradyumna</s> became equal to <s>Sanatkumāra</s>;
as they assumed those vast forms, the earth trembled.
With the mass of the ocean stilled after being churned by the blasts of wind from <s>Tārkṣya</s>'s wings,
there arose a strange agitation of the worlds, as at the beginning of dissolution.
Then <s>Halāyudha</s>, filled with wonder, said to <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>:
"Why have we suddenly become golden in radiance?"
The one whose standard is <s>Tārkṣya</s> said to him: "The fire that guards <s>Bāṇa</s>'s city,
the <s>āhavanīya</s> fire here, has risen up angrily before us.
By its brilliance the world appears like an untimely twilight;
now this task will depend upon <s>Suparṇa</s>."
When <s>Śauri</s> had said this, <s>Tārkṣya</s>, shaking the ocean by the beating of his wings,
took up the <s>Gaṅgā</s> and brought the Fire-god to calm.
Then, tangled with flame-locks shaped like spreading peaks,
other terrible fires, attendants of <s>Rudra</s>, rose up.
In their midst <s>Aṅgiras</s>, adorned with the blaze of a flaming trident,
shone like <s>Sumeru</s> marked by the disk of the sun.
With his crescent-shaped arrow <s>Hari</s> cut off
the fierce trident as it was about to strike him, like adverse fate cutting off a desired aim.
Struck down by <s>Śauri</s> with that broad-fletched great missile,
he who had felled enemies fell, burned like fire by fire.
Then, when the thicket of fire was broken and <s>Bāṇa</s>'s army was thrown into confusion,
<s>Janārdana</s> blew his <s>Pāñcajanya</s>, pure as his own fame.
At its great sound, crushing masses of wind,
there was a harsh roar as though the expanse of the worlds were colliding.
Then, entering <s>Bāṇa</s>'s city, the one whose banner is <s>Garuḍa</s>
encountered a great ocean of daityas, agitated and arrayed for battle.
<s>Hari</s> covered that boundless army with fire-weapons sharpened on stone,
making it madder-red, as if with bound cloths for men condemned to death.
Then, swiftly, from delight in battle, descending from <s>Garutmān</s>,
the hero armed with the plough fought with the enemies of the gods.
In that demon-house dark like spotless tamāla trees, he shone
like <s>Airāvaṇa</s> moving through the sky in a dense dark cloud.
Then, dragged by <s>Saṃkarṣaṇa</s>'s plough and struck by the crash of his mace,
all the dānavas fell like mountains split by the thunderbolt.
Having descended from the back of <s>Suparṇa</s>, <s>Acyuta</s>, together with <s>Pradyumna</s>,
carried off the birds of the daityas' lives with a net of arrows.
Tormented by the fierce beak and talons

children.text: kṣapitāḥ pakṣirājena kṣaṇaṃ śarma na lebhire ||
children.translated_text: and by the wing-beats of the king of birds, they found no comfort even for a moment.
Then, bearing ashes as his weapon, three-faced, three-crested, three-footed,
with reddish eyes rolling in sleep, yawning and sluggish himself,
with harsh hairs bristling from cold, resembling a makara,
<s>Jvara</s> appeared grey, withered by dizziness and exhaustion.
He challenged <s>Rauhiṇeya</s>, who moved in wondrous circles,
and, his body trembling with anger, set his mind on destroying him.
Resembling ash and a seizure, he hurled an unbearable force at him,
by which <s>Rāma</s>'s fair chest was covered in an instant.
Ash, blazing as it rose from that chest and falling on a slope of <s>Meru</s>,
suddenly burned a broad peak, crackling loudly as it flamed.
With all his limbs blazing from the remaining ash and his memory gone,
<s>Tālaketu</s>, staggering in his gait, looked utterly like a drunk man.

children.text: so 'bravītkṛṣṇa kṛṣṇāhaṃ pradīpto na labhe dhṛtim
children.translated_text: He said, "<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, I am burning and cannot keep my composure;
I see the whole world whirling like a potter's wheel."
Then the wielder of the <s>Śārṅga</s> bow approached <s>Halāyudha</s>, who was speaking thus,
and, embracing him to calm the ash, seized <s>Jvara</s> by his power.

children.text: sa tena samare ghore samākrāntaḥ krudhā jvalan
children.translated_text: Overpowered by him in the dreadful battle, blazing with anger,
<s>Jvara</s> hurled with his fists ash tangled with masses of flame.
For a moment <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> too blazed, but in that very instant his fire was calmed;
though struck equally by him with three arms, <s>Acyuta</s> did not tremble.
That dreadful battle between <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> and <s>Jvara</s>, roaring like thunderbolts,
became terrifying to all beings and made their hair stand on end.
The gleams of golden ornaments on <s>Jvara</s>'s body
seemed like flames issuing out under the pressure of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>'s massive arms.

children.text: nipīḍya nibiḍaṃ dorbhiḥ kṣitau kṣipattaḥ sa śauriṇā
children.translated_text: Crushed tightly by <s>Śauri</s>'s arms and cast down upon the earth,
he quickly entered his body unseen, like the wind.
Possessed by him, panting, yawning, dizzy, sleepy, languid, and stumbling,
the lord of beings for a moment became shaken by a strange and wondrous disorder.
Ah, indeed, the irresistible power inherent in a thing is weighty,
since even the lord of the world underwent alteration through contact with fever.
<s>Kṛṣṇa</s> then produced a dreadful Vaiṣṇava <s>Jvara</s>, one that removed the earlier fever,
and by that <s>Jvara</s> the former <s>Jvara</s> quickly became fever-stricken in turn.
Just as the foe of <s>Kāliya</s>, angry himself, was preparing to kill him,
a voice with a dreadful sound rang out from the sky:
"Blessed lord, this <s>Jvara</s>, an attendant of <s>Rudra</s>, must be protected."
Hearing this, <s>Madhusūdana</s> at once desisted from killing him.
<s>Jvara</s>, tormented by the <s>Viṣṇu-Jvara</s>, spoke to him with folded hands:
"O lord of the universe, out of compassion for me, withdraw your own <s>Jvara</s>."

children.text: mādhavena tu tadvākyātsaṃhṛte ca nije jvare
children.translated_text: When <s>Mādhava</s>, at his words, had withdrawn his own <s>Jvara</s>,
<s>Jvara</s>, with <s>Śarva</s> before him, joyfully bowed to <s>Hari</s>.

children.text: kiṃ te priyaṃ karomīti vādinaṃ hṛṣṭamānasam
children.translated_text: When he, delighted in mind, said, "What dear thing may I do for you?"
the enemy of <s>Madhu</s> addressed him in words sweet with favor:
"Those men absorbed in me who bow to me and remember

children.text: ye manmayāḥ saṃsmaranti santu te vijvarā narāḥ ||
children.translated_text: this battle of ours, fought with arms as weapons, shall be free from fever.
Meditated on as three-footed, armed with ash, three-headed, and tear-eyed,
your form shall give embodied beings the happiness of affection.
May the ancient seers, without beginning or end, the teachers, the lesser and the greatest,
and <s>Aniruddha</s>, <s>Pradyumna</s>, <s>Bala</s>, and <s>Keśava</s> destroy fevers."

children.text: ityuktaḥ śauriṇā prītyā tathetyāha hari jvaraḥ
children.translated_text: Thus addressed with affection by <s>Śauri</s>, <s>Hari</s>'s <s>Jvara</s> said, "So be it,"
speaking with folded hands bent in reverence before the jewel of his crest.
"I was fashioned by <s>Hara</s>, the destroyer of <s>Tripura</s>;

children.text: jitastvāyā dānavakānanāgre prasahya yuddhe tava kiṃ karomi ||
children.translated_text: conquered by you, O subduer of <s>Kāliya</s>, by force in battle before the forest of demons, what can I do for you?"
After <s>Śarva</s>'s <s>Jvara</s> had thus withdrawn first from the battlefield,
<s>Hari</s>, mounting <s>Tārkṣya</s>, fought on with his son and elder brother.
Pierced by <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>'s arrows and restrained by regard for their master's honor,

children.text: mānino daityasubhaṭā na tasthurna yayuḥ kṣaṇam ||
children.translated_text: the proud Daitya warriors neither stood their ground nor fled for a moment.
Then, their formation broken and their chariots and elephants shattered,
the Daityas, torn apart by <s>Dāmodara</s>, abandoned the battle and fled.
Driven off by <s>Hari</s>, like deer by a lion,

children.text: nadīvegā iva gatāḥ pratīpaṃ na samāyayuḥ ||
children.translated_text: they went like river-currents and did not return against the stream.
"Why have you gone, selling fame firm until the destruction of an age

children.text: vikrīya kiṃ gatā yūyaṃ mṛtyuḥ sarvatra dehinām ||
children.translated_text: for lives lighter than blades of grass? Death is everywhere for embodied beings.
How have you been struck down by fear, that thunderbolt against the mountain of honor,
that forest fire to the creeper of fame, that dark smoke against propriety?"

children.text: iti bāṇena bahuśaḥ kumbhāṇḍena ca māninā
children.translated_text: Though <s>Bāṇa</s> and the proud <s>Kumbhāṇḍa</s>

children.text: nivāryamāṇā api te jagmureva diśo daśa ||
children.translated_text: tried again and again to stop them with such words, they still went off in all ten directions.
Then, on the battlefield, the blessed <s>Rudra</s>, destroyer of <s>Bhaga</s>'s eye,
the god <s>Pinākin</s>, together with <s>Guha</s>, came himself to fight.
With broad masses of bodily rays smiling like heaps of frost,
the lord of the world seemed to make it adorned with abundant sacred ash.
With circles of moving bracelets, armlets, earrings, and serpents,
he seemed rippled by curls from the smoke of the fire of <s>Tripura</s>.
With wheels of radiance from his throat he seemed to create dark bodices for the wives of the quarters,
like <s>Puṣkarāvartaka</s> clouds, attendants at the beginning of dissolution.
The crescent moon sprouted from his tightly bound mass of matted hair,
and he had the appearance of a turban fashioned from the foaming river of the immortals.
On a radiant chariot yoked with <s>Nandin</s> and with lions,
he covered the sky like an embodied mass of the fire of anger.
Seeing <s>Hara</s>, accompanied by noble <s>Kumāra</s>, victor over <s>Tāraka</s>,

children.text: harirālokya niṣkampaḥ sajjaṃ cakre nijaṃ dhanuḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Hari</s>, unshaken, made his own bow ready.
When the enraged <s>Khaṇḍaparaśu</s> himself was in the tumult of battle,
embodied beings began to suspect that an untimely dissolution of the world had begun.
Then <s>Bharga</s> filled <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> with golden shafts,
like many tongues of fire flung up from his third eye.
Surrounded by those fierce missiles, loosed from fierce arms and made distinct by their speed,
he seemed encircled by the serpents of that one's bracelets, snapped loose by the drawing of the bowstring.
Then <s>Janārdana</s> released the rain-missile, terrible with a thousand streams of arrows,
strengthened by flashing and thundering roars, as an auspicious counter for <s>Rudra</s>.
Covered by that destructive missile, the foe of <s>Tripura</s>
deployed the fire-missile, terrifying the three worlds.
Encircled by rings of flame, <s>Garuḍadhvaja</s>, together with his elder brother,
took on the splendor of a lion confined in a golden cage.
When that missile had been brought to rest by <s>Murāri</s> with the water-missile,
<s>Trilocana</s> fought with <s>Paiśāca</s>, <s>Raudra</s>, and <s>Āṅgirasa</s> weapons.
Quickly warding off those missiles with solar, wind, and Indra weapons,
he, shaken by anger, set upon the string an arrow that could bring even <s>Tripurāntaka</s> to an end.
When the enemy of <s>Andhaka</s> had at length brought that arrow into union with the bow,
<s>Hari</s> made him, overcome with yawning, helpless by means of a yawning weapon.
At the terrible repeated yawning produced by the dreadful sound of <s>Śārṅga</s>

children.text: jṛmbhite bhairave bhīmaṃ bhayaṃ bhūtāni lebhire ||
children.translated_text: and of <s>Pāñcajanya</s>, beings obtained a fearful terror.
Then, on a broad and swift chariot driven by the son of <s>Kumbhāṇḍa</s>,
angry <s>Guha</s> advanced against <s>Rāma</s>, <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, and <s>Pradyumna</s>.
Struck by them with wind, fire, and rain missiles,
he, with blazing nets of weapons, produced an illusion that threw the world into agitation.
Six-faced <s>Ṣaṇmukha</s> too, surrounded by those various gold-feathered shafts, shone
as if he had lovingly returned to the reed-thicket, the field of his birth.
<s>Tārakāntaka</s> discharged the dread <s>Brahmaśiras</s> weapon,
and the mountains, kindled by its flames, attained the condition of <s>Sumeru</s>.
When that fire of the weapon spread forth, disturbing everything as if consecrated for universal destruction,
<s>Hari</s> took up his discus.
That terrible orb, as fierce as the sun and destructive of all weapons,
fastened to the staff of <s>Hari</s>'s arm, stole away the brilliance of the missile-fire.
When the power of that weapon had been cut away by the saw of the discus-rays,
<s>Guha</s> seized the cruel spear that split <s>Krauñca</s> mountain.
It was adorned with a row of shining gems like the teeth of Death,
and decorated with a red band resembling drops of <s>Tāraka</s>'s blood.
<s>Kārttikeya</s> hurled that spear, ringing with clusters of bells,
shrieking as if hungry and eager to devour the three worlds.
Blazing and dreadful, with eyebrows, hair, and beard like clouds bright at their edges,
it made the sky the outstretched tongue in the face of great <s>Mahākāla</s>.
"Blessing, blessing to <s>Acyuta</s>!" the gods cried in heaven,
as that spear, facing <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, shone swiftly like lightning.
Struck by <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>'s hūṃkāra, it became fruitless against him,
like a hope fixed by a simpleton upon one whose crooked mind has been discovered.
Then the discus-bearing one, gathering a circle of wrath,

children.text: guhaṃ vīkṣya kaṭākṣeṇa tadvadhe vidadhe matim ||
children.translated_text: looked at <s>Guha</s> with a sidelong glance and resolved to kill him.
A dark woman, naked, with loosened hair and red eyes,
stood before him to protect <s>Kumāra</s>, as if <s>Śakti</s> embodied.
Though the foe of <s>Kāliya</s> angrily kept saying, "Go away, go away,"
and repeatedly tried to stop her, she did not withdraw.
Meanwhile, with armies whose firm, deep sounds were like the roar of thunderclouds,
and whose cries rose loud and shrill, <s>Bāṇa</s> himself came into view.
Mounted on the back of <s>Kumāra</s>'s peacock, he shone
like a mass of dark clouds rising over the slope of a collyrium mountain.
Approaching <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, empowered by the strength of his many arms, he said:
"Now that your destruction is near, alas, you flare up like a lamp.
Killed by me here in a foreign land, unknown to your friends,
bereft of kinsmen, you will surely abandon life with difficulty."
When <s>Bāṇa</s> had spoken thus from pride, the one marked by <s>Garuḍa</s>
smiled and said, "Surely you are a hero only in boasting."
Then, filled by <s>Murāri</s> with showers of sharp arrows,
he released a succession of dreadful weapons from his thousand arms.
The sky, filled with masses resembling sparks from that fire,
took on the splendor of a jeweled floor sprinkled with gold dust.
Then <s>Bāṇa</s> took up the weapon of <s>Hiraṇyakaśipu</s>,
from fear of which the quarters seemed to flee somewhere, covered in darkness.
When the courtyard of the sky was filled with clusters of weapons arisen from it,
even the wind had no passage there, much less sky-going beings.
When that weapon had been checked by <s>Hari</s> with the rain-missile,
a shower of arrows released from the forest of <s>Bāṇa</s>'s arms rose up.
In the battle the peacock and <s>Garuḍa</s>, armed with beaks and claws,
again and again seemed to be a blue mountain and the mountain of the gods mingled together.
Then the peacock, thrown into confusion by blows from the tips of <s>Tārkṣya</s>'s wings,
was struck on the head and fell like a mountain.
When the lord of demons had been struck down, <s>Nandin</s>, sent by the foe of <s>Tripura</s>,
took up the <s>Raudra</s> chariot and again stood ready in battle.
Proud <s>Bāṇa</s>, quickly mounting it and disturbed by the poison of wrath,
brought about world-destruction with the great <s>Brahmaśiras</s> weapon.
Then the thousand-spoked discus, the destruction of the enemies of the gods,
Having raised a weapon that swallowed the demons' missiles, <s>Hari</s> rushed upon the lord of demons.
Again <s>Kālī</s>, dark and lotus-eyed, having cast off her garment,
stood before him to protect <s>Bāṇa</s> when his life was in danger.
Seeing her, <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> said, "O <s>Bāṇa</s>, how can a woman be protection for you?
In times of peril this is not fitting for a hero's vow."
Having spoken thus, <s>Hari</s> closed his eyes, avoided the woman,
and at once released his discus, hard to behold with its circle of radiance.
Whirling invisibly and bewilderingly again and again in the forest of <s>Bāṇa</s>'s arms,
the discus became like a saw, cruel with its mass of full fire.
In a moment <s>Bāṇa</s> became like a tree whose many arm-branches had been cut off at the root,
with torrents of blood streaming out violently.
Seeing <s>Madhusūdana</s> poised to cut off <s>Bāṇa</s>'s neck,
the blessed <s>Bharga</s>, together with <s>Guha</s>, approached, bowed, and said:
"O <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, I know you as the cause of the creation, maintenance, and destruction of the world.
Even so, we have some attachment to taking the demon's side.
My devotee is indeed your devotee; under your great protection he must be preserved.
I myself am you, a form of <s>Brahman</s> joined with the three <s>guṇa</s>s.
Therefore <s>Bāṇa</s>, who has taken refuge in me alone, must now be protected by you."
Thus addressed by <s>Hara</s>, <s>Hari</s> said, "So be it," and spared him.
Then, after taking leave of the Three-eyed One, when the bearer of <s>Garuḍa</s> on his banner had departed,
<s>Nandin</s>, troubled with anxiety, spoke to <s>Bāṇa</s>, whose arms had been cut off behind him:

children.text: aho bata na jānīmaḥ kiyatī bhavitavyatā
children.translated_text: "Ah, alas, we do not know how great destiny can be.
<s>Bāṇa</s> has come into danger of death even though the Three-eyed One was on his side.
O <s>Bāṇa</s>, though your arms are severed, propitiate the lord here by dancing,
namely <s>Bhava</s>, the boon-giver skilled in cutting away the fear of worldly existence, my friend."
Thus addressed by <s>Nandin</s>, <s>Bāṇa</s>, long-practiced in steps,
danced, and through that the blessed <s>Bhava</s> became a giver of boons to him.
By <s>Īśvara</s>'s boon <s>Bāṇa</s> became immortal, free from pain, splendid,
honored with his pair of arms, and became <s>Mahākāla</s>, foremost of the <s>gaṇa</s>s.
Then, when the lord of <s>Pārvatī</s> suddenly disappeared with his hosts,
<s>Śoṇitapura</s> became empty, abandoned by the demon folk.
Joyfully taking <s>Aniruddha</s>, together with <s>Uṣā</s>, from the palace of <s>Bāṇa</s>'s inner apartments,
the bearer of <s>Garuḍa</s> on his banner departed.
As he went, with the quarters made tawny by the rays from <s>Tārkṣya</s>'s wings,
the lovely-eyed one remembered the words of <s>Satyabhāmā</s>:
"There are divine cows of <s>Bāṇa</s>, whose milk is like heavenly nectar.

children.text: tā madarthaṃ tvayā deva hartavyā iti sasmitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Those, lord, must be carried off by you for my sake," she had said with a smile.
Just as he set out to seize them while they were grazing on the shore of the ocean,
all of them swiftly entered the abode of <s>Varuṇa</s>.
Then, when the ocean was agitated by the fierce wind from <s>Suparṇa</s>'s wings,
the army of <s>Varuṇa</s> advanced terribly with floods of thousands of chariots.
When the ocean of that army was split apart by the mass of <s>Murāri</s>'s arrows,
the angry <s>Varuṇa</s> himself rose up, with a jeweled parasol.
Pouring down divine weapons in battle, <s>Varuṇa</s> was being burned by <s>Śauri</s> with the <s>Vaiṣṇava</s> missile,
and with joined palms he addressed him:
"I am your own primordial form at the creation of the world, O lord of the world.

children.text: kṣantumarhasi me deva jahi kopaṃ tamomayam ||
children.translated_text: You should forgive me, lord; abandon this anger born of darkness.

children.text: nyāsīkṛtaṃ godhanaṃ ca bāṇena parirakṣa me
children.translated_text: And protect for me the herd of cows deposited in trust by <s>Bāṇa</s>."
Thus addressed by him, the blessed lord was pleased and went away through the sky.
Praised by the hosts of gods, he came near <s>Dvārakā</s>,
and, placing <s>Pāñcajanya</s> to his own mouth, filled it with sound.
At its deep resonance, like the smooth rumbling of clouds,
there arose an extraordinary festival of joy among the peacock-like heroes of the <s>Vṛṣṇi</s>s.
Entering <s>Dvārakā</s>, the lord was worshiped by all the <s>Yādava</s>s.
Afterwards, having dismissed <s>Indra</s> with his attendants, after due honor had been received,
and also <s>Garuḍa</s>, he was eager with loving affection for his beloved.
Satisfied by the complete destruction of the enemies of the gods, he sported at ease.
<s>Vaiśampāyana</s> spoke thus to King <s>Janamejaya</s>.

children.text: iti tasya vacaḥ śrutvā punaḥ papraccha śaunakaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Hearing his speech, <s>Śaunaka</s> asked again:
"All the earlier lineages of King <s>Janamejaya</s> have been heard.
I wish to hear from you, O <s>Sūta</s>, the lineage of his descendants."
Asked thus, <s>Sūta</s> spoke of those born from <s>Janamejaya</s>:
"There was King <s>Candrāpīḍa</s>, and <s>Sūryāpīḍa</s>, who attained liberation.
<s>Satyakarṇa</s>, son of <s>Candrapīḍa</s>, was the eldest of a hundred brothers.
His son, named <s>Śvetakarṇa</s>, entered upon the Great Departure.

children.text: taṃ jāyā mālinī nāma sagarbhānuyayau satī
children.translated_text: His wife, named <s>Mālinī</s>, a faithful woman, followed him while pregnant.
The prince, born from her afterwards, was abandoned in a mountain cave.
He cried, and out of compassion for him rainclouds appeared.
On the mountain he was taken up by two sons of sages, one on either side.
Known as <s>Ajapārśva</s>, he became the best of sacrificers.
Through his many sons and grandsons the lineage of <s>Pūru</s> was increased.
Even though, as <s>Yayāti</s> said, the earth might become bereft of sun and planets,
it will never at any time become bereft of the lineage of <s>Pūru</s>."
When King <s>Janamejaya</s>, in the preliminary worships for the <s>Bhārata</s>,
had heard the rule of gifts and asked, the disciple of <s>Vyāsa</s> spoke again:
"In the <s>Ādiparvan</s> one should give honeyed milk-rice to Brahmins.
In the <s>Sabhāparvan</s> one should perform satisfaction-rites with cakes and sweetmeats.
In the <s>Āraṇyaka</s> one should offer roots and fruits, and in the <s>Virāṭa</s> one should present cloth."
One should give varied food, drink, and cooked rice for the <s>Udyoga</s> and <s>Bhīṣma</s> parvans.
In the <s>Droṇa</s> parvan one should give weapons, and in the <s>Karṇa</s> parvan pure cooked rice;
in the <s>Śalya</s> parvan, cakes and the like, together with modakas and rice cooked with molasses.
In the <s>Gadāyuddha</s> one should give rice mixed with mung beans, and in the <s>Strī</s> parvan ornaments;
then ghee-rice and, in the corruptly transmitted item here, sacrificial food in the <s>Śānti</s> parvan.
In the <s>Aśvamedha</s> parvan one should give sacrificial food as desired, and likewise in the <s>Āśrama</s> section;
in the <s>Mausala</s> parvan perfumes, garlands, and the like, and in the one called <s>Prasthāna</s> a pair of sandals.
In the <s>Svarga</s> parvan one should give edible things and the like, but in the <s>Harivaṃśa</s> milk-rice.
At the end of the <s>Bhārata</s>, taking up the book, one should perform the worship of <s>Sarasvatī</s>.
A giver of gold, free from anxious thought, is fit for the fruit of all sacrifices.
Having heard this worship of the parvans, <s>Śaunaka</s> again asked:

children.text: sarvasatre nivṛtte tu rakṣite takṣake tathā
children.translated_text: "When the full satra had ended and <s>Takṣaka</s> had been protected,
what then, O <s>Sūta</s>, did that king <s>Janamejaya</s> do?"
<s>Sūta</s> said: Then the king, together with learned ministers and household priests,
deliberated and gathered the complete equipment for an <s>aśvamedha</s>.
Then the blessed sage came, made of divine knowledge,
the glorious <s>Vyāsa</s>, treasury of Vedic learning and treasure-house of true austerity.
The king worshiped him as he sat on a very costly seat, bowed down,
and asked, filled with the joy of tasting the nectar of the <s>Bhārata</s>:
"Blessed one, through the royal consecration a great destruction of kṣatriyas was brought about.

children.text: sa kathaṃ pāṇḍuputrāṇāṃ bhavatā na nivāritaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Why was that not prevented by you for the sons of <s>Pāṇḍu</s>?"
Asked thus by the king, the sage spoke, while with the rays of his teeth
he showed rows of filaments in the lotus of his mouth, where <s>Sarasvatī</s> dwelt:
"Since that destruction of kṣatriyas was inevitable, how could we have power over it?
And who regards as beneficial what is driven on by fate?
This battering wind of the coming and going of creatures attached to becoming
expands with all its force as destiny itself.
The arrival of good and evil fruits, though natural, stands in front;
like the line of the brow placed on the forehead, by whom is it seen with his own eye?
For those men, hemmed in by Time, their understanding became resolute and firm in decision.
For the blessed <s>Kāla</s> (Time), all-devouring, consumes everything.
If what is assigned by fate for embodied beings could be overstepped by words,

children.text: tatsattramapyaśvamedhaṃ mā kṛthā vighnado hi saḥ ||
children.translated_text: then do not perform even that satra, the <s>aśvamedha</s>, for he will be an obstruction-maker.
Hearing, out of hostility, of your three hundred sacrifices, <s>Śatakratu</s>
will enter the sacrificial horse and, blinded by passion, will violate your wife.
From then onward, when the stain of <s>Kali</s> has grown in this world,
even the mere mention of great sacrifices will become remote.
Some <s>Kāśyapi</s>, a commander named <s>Audbhida</s>, in the realm of <s>Kali</s>,
a capable brahmin, will again bring back the <s>aśvamedha</s>.

children.text: iti śrutvā viṣṇṇena muniḥ pṛṣṭo mahībhujā
children.translated_text: Hearing this, the dejected ruler of the earth asked the sage,
and he, whose eye was knowledge, described the signs of the end of the age:
"When discussion of the practices of varṇa and āśrama becomes inverted in the world, contrary to what ascetics desire,
that will be the youth of the ending of the age.
Men will become slack in marks of affection, devoid of truth and good conduct,
wearing hair and dress in strange ways, without proper turbans and garments.
Bandits will act like kings, and kings will behave like bandits;
all will give assistance to <s>Kali</s> in the decline of dharma.
Cooked food will be sold in the world, and twice-born men will sell the Veda;
when the age has waned, housewives will sell their sexual favor.
<s>Śūdras</s> will become makers of instruction and performers of brahmanical initiation;
and brahmins will again be treated with contempt by the word 'bhoḥ'.
Shaven-headed, wearing ochre garments, and deforming many vows,
<s>Śūdras</s>, after driving brahmins away, will accept gifts.
When beauty of form, charm, sweetness, and good adornment have declined,
women will be shameless, using their hair as ornament.
All will be scholars of their own doctrines, undiscerning seekers of liberation,
born in good families but desiring results without effort.
There will be cheaters of those ignorant of cheating, and thieves of thieves;
what more need be said? Kings will become stealers of wives.
With many women and few men, taking refuge near the <s>Himavat</s>,
the world, its children set upon its shoulders, will wander crying 'hā hā'.
Hypocrisy will be purity; crooked deceitfulness, skill; violence, heroism; livelihood, the injuring of others;

children.text: tarkaḥ śāstraṃ nāstikatvaṃ ca bodhaḥ śaucācāratyāga evāśu muktiḥ ||
children.translated_text: sophistry will be scripture, atheism knowledge, and abandoning purity and proper conduct will soon be liberation.
When the world has thus been thrown into confusion by the sins of <s>Kali</s>,
then, again through the ripening of time, the dharma of the <s>Kṛta</s> age will arise."
Then, when the sage, the sun of knowledge, had quickly disappeared,
the king's splendid <s>aśvamedha</s> sacrifice took place.
At that sacrifice <s>Śatakratu</s>, entering the horse and the king's wife <s>Vapuṣṭamā</s>,
violated her, unwilling as she was, under the power of desire.
Through the word of the adhvaryu, the king became filled with the poison of anger,
and cursed uncontrolled <s>Śakra</s> by forbidding him a share in sacrifices.
Casting all brahmins resentfully out of his own realm,
he entered the wives' chamber with unshaken body and said:
"Let this crooked-flowing channel of mud be expelled,
falling down with banks troubled by restless waves of sin.
Defiled in conduct, she is not fit to remain in my house,
for by her a mass of clouds has been made over the full moon of my fame.

children.text: svādu nāśnanti saṃtaptā na ca rātriṣu śerate
children.translated_text: Those who are tormented do not eat sweet things, nor do they sleep at night,

children.text: śalyaṃ marmāntare yeṣāṃ gṛhe bhāryā hi dūṣitā ||
children.translated_text: when a defiled wife in the house is a thorn in their innermost vital spot."
When the king had spoken thus, the lord of the Gandharvas himself,
<s>Viśvāvasu</s>, came to him and, out of friendship, said this:
"O king, this <s>Rambhā</s>, your bride, is a divine courtesan.
Her body, though pure, was violated by the lord of the gods in this sacrifice.
Out of fear of your power, fear of the brahmins, hatred, and desire,
this obstruction to your rite was ordained by <s>Śakra</s>, under divine command.

children.text: viprebhyo mā krudhaḥ patnīṃ mā tyākṣīḥ śuddhamānasām
children.translated_text: Do not be angry with the brahmins; do not abandon your wife, whose mind is pure.
For a secret touch upon one who did not consent is like the visible touch of a limb.
The birth-place of men, the furrow of the earth, naturally belongs to women;
though impure, it assumes purity. Do not kill the brahmins in vain."
Thus instructed by the king of the Gandharvas,
<s>Janamejaya</s>, his anger calmed, reflected and accepted it, saying, "So be it."
Having heard the deeds of <s>Viṣṇu</s> as recounted by <s>Vaiśampāyana</s>,
the king again asked about the manifestation as the Boar.
Asked by him with humility, after bowing to <s>Hari</s>, the sage
brought forth the divine, sin-removing majesty of <s>Viṣṇu</s>.
When a thousand yugas had been completed and <s>Brahmā</s>'s day had ceased,
the fiery-seeded, three-headed, self-existent god <s>Vṛṣākapi</s>,
having burned the whole world with his flames, together with its mountains and oceans,
the one <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, containing the three worlds in his womb, lies asleep.
He, containing the universe within himself, first emitted a golden egg.
Split above and below, it opened out in the eight directions.
It became the field of the three worlds, reaching down to the earth and crowned by the sky,
the womb of <s>Hiraṇyagarbha</s>, as the expounders of <s>brahman</s> call it.
In that clear water stood <s>Sumeru</s>, the golden mountain;
the earth sank there, pressed down by hundreds of great mountains.
Unable to bear all living beings, through the power of <s>Viṣṇu</s>,
the submerged earth went to <s>Vaikuṇṭha</s> for refuge, like a cow.
Then <s>Hari</s> fashioned a body, the Boar, resolute in raising up the bearer of the world,
a destroyer of the wicked, lofty as a mountain.
It had the hue of a mass of split collyrium and a cluster of rays from its auspicious tusks,
like the moon emerging from a mass of dark rain-clouds.
With tawny brows, beard, and hair, its face reddened the sky,
as if it were the peak of a blue mountain tinged with the pollen of golden lotuses.
He entered the floor of <s>Pātāla</s>, its interior dark with palmyras and tamālas,
while the broken-moon pieces of his tusks split apart the circle of darkness.

children.text: mantrātmā veda yajñāṅgaḥ sa varāho mahākṛtiḥ
children.translated_text: That great-bodied Boar, whose essence was mantra and whose limbs were the Vedas and the sacrifice,
raised the earth on the tip of his tusk like a little creeper of moss.
She, fastened on the edge of his tusk, with eyes like blue lotuses,
shone like the dark disk of the cool-rayed moon marked by a line of stain.
The abode of the world, having lifted up the earth, established the stability of the universe,
and arranged the mountains according to the division of the quarters.
After setting in place mountains shaped like conches, discs, and maces,
he created from his mouth the first god, the man <s>Prajāpati</s>.
When that one stood before him and respectfully asked, "What shall I do?"
the womb of the universe said, "Divide yourself," and disappeared.
Then, as he pondered, arising from the sky of consciousness,
the sound "Om" came forth, filling the three worlds.
Then arose the <s>vaṣaṭkāra</s> (sacrificial exclamation), and likewise the great utterances,

children.text: vedamātā ca sāvitrī vedaiḥ saha sanātanaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: and <s>Sāvitrī</s>, mother of the Veda, together with the eternal Vedas.
The seven ancient great seers, royal swans dwelling in <s>Prajāpati</s>'s pure mind,
were born, worthy of reverence by the world.
And <s>Dakṣa</s>, who was <s>Prajāpati</s>, arose from his right thumb;
his daughters, the maidens, obtained <s>Dharma</s>, the Moon, <s>Manu</s>, and <s>Kaśyapa</s> as husbands.
From them came this creation of the universe, a lineage including gods and Asuras.
<s>Aditi</s> bore gods from <s>Kaśyapa</s>, and <s>Diti</s> bore Daityas.
Once, taking refuge with <s>Hiraṇyākṣa</s>, lord of the sons of <s>Diti</s>,
the winged mountains caused upheaval in the world by their movement.
When <s>Śakra</s> set out to cut off their wings, <s>Hiraṇyākṣa</s>, siding with them,
brought about a terrible battle with the gods.
In that battle, made fearful by the convulsion of beings from the hurling of great weapons,
<s>Hiraṇyākṣa</s> conquered the gods in a fight that shook the worlds.
When the gods had lost their courage, the blessed Boar, whose body was like a mountain,
came himself, eager to slay the Daitya,
and the discus-bearer blew his conch with a mouth made terrible by tusks.
By its sound, which made the sphere of the cosmic egg whirl,
the great sacrifice for destroying the arrogant Daityas seemed to resound with <s>oṃkāra</s>.
Then <s>Hiraṇyākṣa</s> came forward and, with a spear that was like a messenger of destruction for his enemies,
struck the lord of the gods in the chest, roaring like a cloud.
The blessed lord, seeing with ease the Daitya's wondrous valor,
sent forth <s>Sudarśana</s>, the thousand-spoked discus that destroys foes.
When the Daitya mountain's noble head had been made into a peak by it,
and he had fallen to the ground, the shattered Dānavas fled to the quarters.
When brave <s>Hiraṇyākṣa</s>, crest-jewel of the enemies of the Thirty Gods, had been killed,
the gods, upheld by the Great Boar, returned to their own place.

With the darkness of the mighty Daitya pierced apart like the depths of a split collyrium mountain by his tusks, and with his conch and discus flashing more beautifully than the broad path of moon, sun, and stars...

children.text: pāyānnaḥ śeṣaśīrṣākramaṇasamuditairvyāptakāyaḥ phaṇāgraiḥ kṣubhyatkṣīrābdhiphenairiva maṇiśabalairmandarābho varāhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: May <s>Varāha</s> protect us: his body was covered by the expanded tips of the hoods raised from treading on <s>Śeṣa</s>'s heads, like <s>Mandara</s> mountain variegated with jewels, as if by the foam of the churning milk-ocean.
Long ago, in the <s>Kṛta</s> age, the glorious <s>Hiraṇyakaśipu</s>, son of <s>Kaśyapa</s> and <s>Diti</s>,
performed austerity for ten thousand years and more.
By <s>Brahmā</s>'s boon he became immune to gods, gandharvas, kinnaras, serpents, and rākṣasas,
and also to all weapons.
Having attained an equal station, he arrogantly overran the three worlds,
and the hero made all the women of the gods like wives whose husbands are away.
Then the gods, terrified and shattered, their splendor dimmed by the fire of his might,
their lives resting on <s>Brahmā</s>'s word, sought refuge in the imperishable god.
He, the giver of boons and source of beings, granted them fearlessness,
and fashioned a great body of <s>Narasiṃha</s>, accompanied by the syllable <s>oṃ</s>.
He became one who seemed to consume the mass of radiance of a blazing golden mountain,
making mountains small by the forceful impact of his swift feet.
He was covered with quivering sheaths of horripilation shaped like coral sprouts,
as if with sparks produced from the cruel fire of anger.
He was adorned with arms like golden pillars in the mansion of majesty,
marked with the conch, discus, mace, and lotus.
With the splendor of chowries from the raised ears of the elephant of Death,
he made the sky seem to laugh aloud with masses of rays from his nails.
His mane clung to the peaks of shoulders raised like the summits of <s>Meru</s>,
terrible, like fans kindling the dreadful fire of Time.
With the rows of rays from his fangs made clear by his yawning,
he seemed repeatedly to point out the circle of lotus-stalks belonging to the sun-lotus.
With fierce rays from his tawny, terrible eyes he made an untimely twilight,
blood-red and announcing the destruction of hundreds of arrogant daityas.
His high expanse of forehead was frightful with the bending of his tawny brows,
like a great twilight cloud flashing with hosts of stars and lightning.
Going to the dwelling of the daityas, like the fire of dissolution,
he saw <s>Hiraṇyakaśipu</s>'s hall, radiant like a thousand suns.
It stood on the head of the three worlds, shining like a golden garland,
with trees generous in divine jewel-fruits and flowers of every season.
Its jeweled pavement reflected the lotus-faces of lovely women,
and in it the glorious lord of the daityas shone with powerful brilliance.
On the broad lap of a wide jeweled throne, he was like the thousand-rayed sun at sunrise.
On his broad chest a garland of golden lotuses shone,
like a line of suns at the end of an age on the slope of a golden mountain.
The command, "The guardians of the worlds are forbidden to stand here,"
seemed for a moment to be written in the directions by the rays of his jeweled earrings.
With the lights of the crest-jewels of his high crown, brilliant like rainbows,
he repeatedly seemed to make a burden of jewels for the peacock of the sky.
He was served by hosts of siddhas, gandharvas, kinnaras, and apsarases.
He bore a shining turban, like masses of foam from the ocean of universal sovereignty.
There, with chowries gently waved by the hands of women of heaven,
royal fortune seemed to laugh in a rippling white garment.
Then the sky appeared terrible with emissions that burned the quarters,
filled with blood dripping from wounds by some [lacunose text].
Then a lion appeared, glorious, with the form of a man,
a god, crusher of the enemies of the gods, tawny like a hundred fires.
Seeing him, who brought about a new consecration of trembling in their hearts,
the sons of <s>Diti</s>, distressed with wonder, looked at one another's faces.
When the courtyard of the daitya audience-hall was in uproar with the question, "Who is this?",
wise <s>Prahlāda</s>, son of <s>Hiraṇyakaśipu</s>, spoke.
"This is some god made of all the gods, a treasury of radiance,

children.text: yena naḥ sthagitānīva cetāṃsi ca vacāṃsi ca ||
children.translated_text: by whom our thoughts and words seem to have been obstructed.

children.text: sa evāyaṃ hiraṇyākṣo yena nītaḥ pramāthinā
children.translated_text: This is that very impetuous one by whom <s>Hiraṇyākṣa</s> was carried off
to become the banner-cloth on the high shoulder of skull-bearing <s>Kāla</s>."
As <s>Prahlāda</s> was speaking thus, <s>Hiraṇyakaśipu</s>, his face crooked with a frown,
said to the daityas, "Seize him."
Then those bull-like dānavas, headed by <s>Vipraciti</s>,
terrible and blazing in their armor, all surrounded him.
The shower of weapons released by them, tangled in a network of flames,
the unmoving god received like a garland of red flowers.
Though covered by arrows, fierce with tips like flames and as if by his own radiance,
with a mere glance he made them like grass thrown by the wind.
Roaring with the sound of storm-clouds at dissolution, he shook them off,
and shattered the hall, which cried out as its people were thrown into agitation.
Then, when the circle of daityas was suddenly destroyed by his energy,
<s>Hiraṇyakaśipu</s> himself rose up in anger, biting his lip.
Hurling a mass of missiles, he threw a dreadful club,

children.text: kālacakraṃ triśūlaṃ ca kaṅkālaṃ musalaṃ tathā ||
children.translated_text: the wheel of Time, a trident, a skull-weapon, and likewise a mace.
He threw the <s>Brahmāstra</s>, the thunderbolt, the <s>Tvāṣṭra</s> weapon, a spear, the <s>Pāśupata</s> weapon, and a plough,
a most terrible club of Time and the embodied weapon of Death.
Even while being covered by these, the man-lion did not tremble,
though surrounded by daityas with faces of many creatures, formed from dreadful illusion.
Then <s>Hiraṇyakaśipu</s>, blinded by anger and huge in body,
created a convulsion of the worlds, by which the worlds trembled.
The earth, with its rival towns, capitals, islands, cities, and dominions,
shook, garlanded with rivers and rich in mountains.
Then the god drew the young daitya near, placed him on his lap, fierce in battle,
and tore open his chest with his harsh nails, terrible as thunderbolts.
From the lotus of the daitya's heart there issued sprays of blood,
like flames of fire produced by the crushing saw of his nails.
When the heroic lord of daityas, foremost among the proud, had been slain,
the gods regained their own splendor, as directed by <s>Nṛhari</s>.
Praised by <s>Brahmā</s> and the others, and fit to be meditated on by those who seek the path of liberation,
<s>Hari</s> then went to the northern shore of the milk ocean.
Those nail-shells of the god whose body was a lion, reddened by sprays of blood, terrible with the garment of the daitya, and streaming from openings in twilight clouds,
are victorious as moon-rays cooling the clusters of lotus-like faces of the wives of the enemies of the gods.
<s>Prahlāda</s>, crest-jewel of the daityas, was the son of <s>Hiraṇyakaśipu</s>;
the hero <s>Virocana</s>, enemy of the gods, was the son of <s>Prahlāda</s>.
<s>Bali</s>, son of <s>Virocana</s>, conqueror of the three worlds,
was himself installed by the hosts of daityas in <s>Śakra</s>'s office as universal emperor.
He set out to conquer the thirty gods with forces spreading through the three worlds,
while the sky was struck by the clangor of the bells on troops of rutting elephants.
With chariots swelling like cities, with elephants like kings of mountains,
and with horses swift as the wind, the sky was filled by him.
With <s>Svarbhānu</s>, <s>Vindana</s>, <s>Muci</s>, <s>Prahlāda</s>, <s>Bala</s>, <s>Śambara</s>,
<s>Jambha</s>, <s>Kumbhodara</s>, <s>Ugrākṣa</s>, <s>Tārakākṣa</s>, and <s>Virocana</s>,
with <s>Vipracitti</s>, <s>Hayagrīva</s>, <s>Maya</s>, and other chief enemies of the gods,
he was surrounded by crores upon crores of them, with blazing banners and armor.
With circles of white turbans, parasols, and yak-tail fans,
he made the sky look like the milk ocean, swollen with broad rows of foam.
<s>Śakra</s> too, together with the guardians of the worlds and supported by crores of the thirty gods,
made the quarters tawny with circles of crooked, blazing rays.
Then the fierce war-drum of the armies of the gods and asuras was beaten,
deep as the sound of clouds at the end of the world.
Then, as bodies were bristling with flames from the clash of weapons and missiles,
in the fire of anger, with swords as sacrificial posts, blood as ghee, and bows as ladles,
<s>Bali</s> shone as one consecrated in that great sacrifice of battle.
On one side by <s>Śakra</s>, the Sun, and Fire, and on the other by <s>Bāṇāsura</s> and the rest,
when darkness was made by arrows, there was a dreadful destruction of the two armies.
Then the gods, torn by the daityas' missiles and swords,
fled in fear to the quarters, agitated by shame as they tried only to save their bodies.
When <s>Śakra</s> had gone with his wheel broken, when Fire was seeking concealment,
when Wind had stopped fighting, and when <s>Yama</s> had taken up quietude,
the heroic <s>Bali</s>, lord of the three worlds, ruled the thirty gods,
placing his command on the heads of all the lords of the worlds without exception.
When the sovereignty of the gods had become a mere tale, and the rich kingdom belonged to the enemies of the gods,
the gods, at <s>Brahmā</s>'s word, went to <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> for protection.
The blessed, all-pervading lord, whose form is unmanifest, entreated by the gods,
entered through yoga into <s>Aditi</s>'s womb for a thousand years.
Then that <s>Viṣṇu</s>, son of <s>Kaśyapa</s>, dark and having the form of a dwarf,
was born, the eldest of the world, a child best among the dwellers in heaven.
Meanwhile wise <s>Bali</s>, consecrated for an <s>aśvamedha</s> (horse sacrifice),
became, for supplicants, a wish-granting tree that gave all desired things.
The god himself, a friend of <s>Bṛhaspati</s>, went to his sacrificial ground
and entered, with three tufts, a crown, a parasol, and a staff.
Seeing him dark, lotus-petal-eyed, with moving, curling locks,

children.text: taṃ lāvaṇyamayaṃ vīkṣaaya yayau niścalatāṃ baḍiḥauliḥjh ||
children.translated_text: and made of beauty, <s>Bali</s> became motionless.
Approaching the lord of daityas, the great-souled one in dwarf form
spoke in a sweet and noble voice, as though raining nectar:
"There were sacrifices of great <s>Indra</s>, of <s>Kubera</s>, of the Moon, of <s>Varuṇa</s>,
and of <s>Brahmā</s>; and now your sacrifice too shines forth.
Among sacrifices this <s>aśvamedha</s> is the best, just as you are among embodied beings."
Hearing these words of <s>Vāmana</s>, pure-souled <s>Bali</s> replied:

children.text: idaṃ te darśanaṃ sādho prīṇāti mama mānasam
children.translated_text: "This sight of you, holy sir, delights my mind.

children.text: śrotraśuktisudhādhārā vāṇī te kasya na priyā ||
children.translated_text: To whom would your speech, a stream of nectar for the shell of the ear, not be dear?

children.text: dadāni kiṃ te 'bhimataṃ tvādṛśāṃ hi mahātmanām
children.translated_text: What desired thing shall I give you? For to great souls such as you,
even the body is not something that should be withheld, much less wealth sought from outside."
When <s>Bali</s> had spoken thus with affection, <s>Vāmana</s> answered,
again and again making the sky seem washed with milk by the gleam of his teeth:
"Let three steps be given by you to me for the sake of my teacher.

children.text: ataḥ paraṃ bhavatprītiṃ bahu manye priyaṃvada ||
children.translated_text: Beyond that, O pleasant speaker, I value your affection highly."
Hearing this, astonished in mind, <s>Bali</s> said with a smile:
"I am <s>Bali</s> the giver, and you are a supplicant; how can only three steps be given?

children.text: dayitaṃ bahumānaṃ me yatheṣṭaṃ gṛhyatāṃ mune
children.translated_text: My beloved honor is dear to me; take whatever you wish, O sage.
Even the earth, with its oceans and lordly mountains, producer of jewels, is too little for you."
Even though this was being said, when <s>Hari</s> asked for nothing more,
then <s>Bali</s>, his face bent down in embarrassment, gave the water into his hand.
Then the god, the all-pervading lord made of all the gods, began to grow,

children.text: vyāpa padbhyāṃ vasumatīṃ śirasā ca divaṃ kṣaṇāt ||
children.translated_text: and in an instant he covered the earth with his feet and heaven with his head.
As he kept growing and set about taking possession of the three worlds,
his staff-like foot, moving through the mid-region, became the measuring rod of the cosmic egg.
"This universe is fully enough for me; the two steps are not completed."
Thus he spoke, as it were, with the sounds of mountains rolling as they trembled.
That which previously had been a jewel upon his diadem, when it had obtained the state of a pearl,

children.text: vaktre smitāṃśucakraṃ ca śanaiḥ śaṅkho 'pi vakṣasi ||
children.translated_text: and the conch, gradually a circle of rays from his smile, was also upon his breast.
That very moon in the sky, belonging to him who made the supreme stride,
quickly became, on the garland about his thighs, a white-lotus wreath.
When <s>Brahmā</s> washed his lotus feet with waters,
the <s>Jāhnavī</s> arose in the world, a garland upon the mass of <s>Hara</s>'s matted hair.
Thus, after striding over the three worlds and taking them from the lord of the Daityas in an instant,
he assigned him residence in the nether region called <s>Sutala</s>.
Ah, how vast as the great ocean was the strength in mighty <s>Bali</s>,
by whom the remainder of his gift was made pure through the binding of his own body.
Amazed, delighted, ashamed, and trembling as well,
the gods, gandharvas, siddhas, cāraṇas, and kiṃnaras became.
After slaying the host of Diti's sons, he arranged a livelihood for <s>Bali</s>.
Oblations offered and gifts given without faith, and likewise śrāddha offered to one unlearned in scripture,
sacrifice and the like performed without mantras, without vows, and without dakṣiṇā,
and whatever else was without proper rule, all that <s>Hari</s> gave to him.
Then, having installed the gods in their own stations, each in his proper place,
he assigned to the lord of the gods his shining sovereignty, like a garland.

children.text: iti te caritaṃ puṇyaṃ devasya kamalāpateḥ
children.translated_text: Thus this holy deed of the god, the lord of <s>Kamalā</s>,
has been told in connection with his manifestation, removing sin.

May the utterly wondrous form of the blessed lord bring peace to all our afflictions: with streams of radiance from the tips of his toenails, produced in the play of striding over the three worlds, it creates on the crown of the cosmic egg the sport of the celestial river spread out like a victory-garland,
while the orb of the sun, attached to his navel as it moves through the region resembling the lotus sprung from <s>Brahmā</s>'s seat, shines forth.
Thus, in the <s>Bhāratamañjarī</s> composed by <s>Kṣemendra</s>, the <s>Harivaṃśa</s> is complete.
There was a Kashmiri named <s>Prakāśendra</s>, a repository of virtues,
a wish-granting tree in fulfilling the aims of multitudes of various petitioners.
Brahmins, satisfied by his complete generosity, always said to him,
'You are <s>Indra</s> himself; only your virtue of radiance is greater.'
For him, whose noble fortunes full of blessings were like <s>Meru</s>,
there was in his house an unrestricted feeding-hall for the twice-born.
At a solar eclipse, after giving three black antelope skins along with three lakhs,
for a moment he was ashamed, his face bent down, thinking, 'I am giving too little.'
At <s>Svayaṃbhūśaṃbhuvijaya</s>, after establishing the deities,
and giving a quarter of a crore to temples, brahmins, monasteries, and the like,
he worshipped <s>Śarva</s> himself, streams of tears flowing,
embraced him firmly there with both arms, and passed away on that very spot.
His son, named <s>Kṣemendra</s>, through honoring learned men,
attained in gatherings of poets the worthiness of having his name mentioned.
From <s>Abhinavagupta</s>, jewel among chief teachers, who unfolded learning,
an ocean of understanding called by that name, he heard the science of literature.
By the dust of the lotus feet of the venerable Bhāgavata teacher <s>Soma</s>,
he, devoted to <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, attained supreme blessedness.
Once a brahmin named <s>Rāmayaśas</s> came to him and requested,
with noble intention, 'Make a condensed account of the story of the Bhārata.'
He said to him, 'I will indeed do it. Before this, as my own prior deed,
the delighted son of <s>Satyavatī</s>, treasure of knowledge, granted it in a dream.'
Having bowed to that boon-giver, I am ready for what you desire.
Having spoken thus, he praised the form of the sage seen in the dream:
Homage to you who bear tawny matted locks like a mass of flames of the fire of knowledge,
to dark <s>Kṛṣṇadvaipāyana</s>, whose greatness is not dark.
Homage to you whose complexion is variegated by the brilliance of a radiant beard,
whose splendor has arisen from the pollen of the lotus-feet of <s>Vāgīśvarī</s> at your mouth.
Homage to you whose evening meditation has drunk in the splendor of the sun,
whose eyes are like lamps cutting through the darkness of the three worlds.
Homage to you, thousand-branched tree of the grove of dharma,
bearing flowers grounded in goodness and fruit that is nirvāṇa.
Homage to you who wear the black antelope skin and dwell in the joy of awakening,
as though pervaded by a swarm of bees longing for the fragrance of merit.
Homage to you, shining with rays of a brahminical cord shaped like a digit of the moon,
as though resorted to by the radiance of swans dwelling in lotuses touched by the sun.
Homage to you, full river of knowledge, complete moon of the ocean of śāstra,
essence of nectar's sap, creator of the activity of poets.
Homage to <s>Vyāsa</s>, dwelling-place of truth, delighting in his own manifestation,
the abode of austerities, remover of the toil of saṃsāra.
Having thus composed the eight verses to <s>Vyāsa</s>, he made the <s>Mahābhāratamañjarī</s>,
a river whose waves pour forth the nectar of delight for the wise.
Ah, how wondrous is this clearness of the poet's <s>Sarasvatī</s>,

children.text: sadyo malinatā vaktre khalānāṃ jāyate yayā ||
children.translated_text: by which defilement at once arises on the faces of the wicked.
On the surface of the mirror of my speech, the directional elephant that is the <s>Mahābhārata</s>,
though complete in all its limbs, is seen as if measurable by the fist.

children.text: ratnodāracatuḥsamudraraśanāṃ bhuktvā bhuvaṃ kauravo bhagnoruḥ patitaḥ sa niṣparijane jīvanvṛkairbhakṣitaḥ
children.translated_text: Having enjoyed the earth girdled by four oceans rich in jewels, the Kaurava, with thighs broken, fell without attendants and, while still alive, was eaten by wolves.

children.text: gaupairviśvajayī jitaḥ sa vijayaḥ kakṣaiḥ kṣitā vṛṣṇayastasmātsarvamidaṃ vicārya suciraṃ śāntyai mano dīyatām ||
children.translated_text: The world-conquering <s>Vijaya</s> was conquered by cowherds, and the <s>Vṛṣṇis</s> were destroyed by reeds; therefore, after considering all this for a very long time, let the mind be given to peace.
May the bodily radiances of <s>Śauri</s> protect you: they steal the lovely brilliance of blossoming blue lotuses and resemble rows of bees eager for the pollen of his own navel-lotus;

children.text: yāḥ kurvanti śaśāṅkabimbaviṣade lakṣmīmukhābje muhuḥ kastūrīrasapattrabhaṅgasubhagā lakṣmīmukhābje muhaḥ kastūrīrasapattrabhaṅgasubhagā lakṣmīprabhāvibhramam ||
children.translated_text: those radiances, again and again, upon <s>Lakṣmī</s>'s face-lotus, clear as the disk of the moon, create the illusion of <s>Lakṣmī</s>'s splendor, charming like leaf-patterns painted with liquid musk.
This <s>Kṣemendra</s>, sprinkled as though with holy water from the sacred bathing-place of the story of <s>Viṣṇu</s>,
though his talk is only ordinary, has today attained the rank of lord among poets.
